misner-sharp-1964-mass-function.name: Misner-Sharp mass function and the tt Einstein equation dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho in areal-radius form (dl = dr/sqrt(1-2m/r)); base of certify.py's 'ansatz-free THEOREM'

source.located: C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964), 'Relativistic equations for adiabatic, spherically symmetric gravitational collapse'. There is no arXiv copy. Read through S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', Phys. Rev. D 53, 1938 (1996), arXiv gr-qc/9408002v2, which restates MS exactly: eq.(4) E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)); eq.(27) 1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda}(r')^2 - rdot^2, 'which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4]'; eq.(31)-(33) the MS perfect-fluid setting, E' = 4 pi r^2 rho r', and E = int_0 4 pi r^2 rho r' dchi 'if Sigma has a regular centre'; eq.(28a) general matter, E' = 4 pi r^2 (T00 r' - T01 rdot). Cross-read: Maeda & Nozawa arXiv 0709.1199 eq.(2.7), whose ref.[6] is Misner-Sharp 1964.

misner-sharp-1964-mass-function.published_statement: Hayward's restatement of MS (gr-qc/9408002 p.4, eq.4; p.12, eq.27): 'The Misner-Sharp spherically symmetric gravitational energy ... may be defined in units G = 1 by E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr))'; 'Note that E is an invariant.' In MS's own comoving form, 1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda}(r')^2 - rdot^2. MS perfect fluid (eq.32a-33): E' = 4 pi r^2 rho r', and with a regular centre E(chi) = int_0^chi 4 pi r^2 rho r' dchi. General matter (eq.28a): E' = 4 pi r^2 (T00 r' - T01 rdot). Proposition 1: 'A metric sphere is trapped iff E > r/2, marginal iff E = r/2, untrapped iff E < r/2.' Regular centre: g^{-1}(dr,dr) - 1 = O(r^2), 'Then E = O(r^3) at a regular centre.' Proposition 6: the dominant energy condition on an untrapped spatial hypersurface with a regular centre gives E >= 0.
published_hypotheses: spherical symmetry (Hayward p.2: 'assumed implicitly in the Propositions')
r is the areal radius, r = sqrt(A/4pi); E is defined on metric spheres from r and g^{ab} d_a r d_b r, with no coordinate choice needed
units G = c = 1
for dE/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho: the Einstein equations G = 8 pi T with no cosmological constant (Hayward eq.10-11; per Maeda-Nozawa, the mass generalised to include Lambda is a different function)
MS 1964 original setting: a time-dependent perfect fluid in comoving coordinates, adiabatic collapse
for E as a volume integral of rho: a regular centre (E = O(r^3), so E(0) = 0)
for positivity (not used by the tree): dominant energy condition, an untrapped hypersurface and a regular centre
hypothesis_drift: BROADENED, and supported: MS's perfect fluid in comoving coordinates becomes, at certify.py:113-121, arbitrary static matter in areal coordinates. Re-derived here (C2): G^t_t = -2m'/r^2 exactly, for any Phi and any anisotropic T, so m' = 4 pi r^2 rho. This agrees with Hayward eq.(28a) at T01 = 0. No harm.

ADDED and named: 'static' (certify.py:181, THEOREM_SCOPE at certify.py:386). The hypothesis is load-bearing. C5 shows that open FRW dust on its comoving slice has E = (4pi/3) rho R^3 > 0 while dl/dR = 1/cosh(chi) < 1, so distance contracts with a positive MS mass once rdot != 0. The tree's scope restriction is correct and necessary.

UNSTATED: general relativity. In Gauss-Bonnet or Lovelock gravity the mass is a generalised one (Maeda-Nozawa eq.2.7). In 4D GR the Gauss-Bonnet term is topological, so there is no drift for the tree's scope.

C2: G^t_t = -2m'/r^2 with no Phi dependence; with Lambda, m' gains Lambda r^2/2. C3: z3 finds the negation of [r>0, 1-2m/r>0 => (g_rr<1 <=> m<0)] unsatisfiable; the vacuity guard is satisfiable. No measured quantity enters, so there is no datum they could have lacked that would change the conclusion. What came later is generality, not data. Hayward (1996) showed the definition is an invariant for any spherically symmetric matter, static or dynamic. Maeda-Nozawa (2008) tied its form to 4D GR with Lambda = 0. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: both uses the tree makes re-derive exactly (C1-C3). The incompleteness found is not a data gap: the static hypothesis is load-bearing (C5), the areal-coordinate hypothesis is unstated and is dropped at the conformastatic use site (C6), and Lambda is unstated. None of these moves a recorded verdict.

birkhoff-theorem.name: Birkhoff's (Jebsen-Birkhoff) theorem: a spherically symmetric vacuum (Ricci = 0) region is locally part of maximally extended Schwarzschild (mass parameter M of any sign; M = 0 is Minkowski)

source.located: J.T. Jebsen, Ark. Mat. Astr. Fys. 15 nr.18 (1921), and G.D. Birkhoff, Relativity and Modern Physics (Harvard 1923) p.253. Neither is on arXiv. Read through: H.-J. Schmidt gr-qc/9709071 pp.1-2, 8-9, 14-16; Goswami & Ellis arXiv:1101.4520 pp.1, 3-4, eqs.(42)-(54); Deser & Franklin gr-qc/0408067 eqs.(22)-(26); Johansen & Ravndal physics/0508163 pp.1-3 (history); Ghosh, Mishra & Chowdhury arXiv:2411.09193 pp.1-2 (restated hypotheses and the regular-centre corollary).
source.via: The 1921 and 1923 originals are NAMED-NOT-READ. The theorem was READ as restated and re-proved in gr-qc/9709071 (coordinate-free proof), 1101.4520 (covariant 1+1+2 proof with both branches written out) and gr-qc/0408067 (Weyl-method proof, where dm/dt = 0 comes from the g_tr variation). All five restatements give the same content.

birkhoff-theorem.published_statement: Schmidt gr-qc/9709071 p.2: 'every spherically symmetric vacuum solution of Einstein's general relativity theory is part of the Schwarzschild solution; therefore, the solution possesses a four-dimensional isometry group, at least locally ... the popular formulation "every spherically symmetric vacuum solution is static" is misleading, because inside the horizon, the Schwarzschild black hole is not static.' Goswami-Ellis 1101.4520 p.1: 'it must be either locally static or spatially homogeneous'. p.4: 'Any C^2 solution of Einstein's equations in empty space, which is of the class LRS-II in an open set S, is locally equivalent to part of maximally extended Schwarzschild solution in S', with a static branch at eq.(51) (r > 2m) and a spatially homogeneous branch at eq.(54) (r < 2m). Deser-Franklin eqs.(24)-(26): b = b(t), a = 1 - 2m(t)/r, dm/dt = 0. Ghosh et al. p.1: 'along with the regularity of the spacetime at the centre, it implies that the metric inside an empty spherical cavity must be the Minkowski'.
published_hypotheses: Einstein's GR field equations. The theorem fails generically in theories with a scalar or helicity-0 degree of freedom (Goswami-Ellis p.1; Ghosh et al. p.2)
vacuum, R_ab = 0, with Lambda = 0 for the Schwarzschild form. With Lambda the class is Schwarzschild-(A)dS, plus products of constant-curvature 2-spaces when Lambda > 0 (Schmidt p.8 and footnote 3)
exact spherical symmetry: SO(3) orbits (Goswami-Ellis generalise this to LRS-II)
local: the theorem holds on an open set, 'independent of boundary conditions at infinity' (Goswami-Ellis p.1), and asymptotic flatness is not assumed
C^2 regularity (Goswami-Ellis p.4). Ghosh et al. p.2 cite Bergmann-Cahen-Komar 1965 for weakening this to C^0 piecewise-differentiable; that source is NAMED-NOT-READ

time dependence is not assumed. Staticity is a conclusion, and holds only where the extra Killing field is timelike (r > 2M); where r < 2M the region is spatially homogeneous (Schmidt p.2; Goswami-Ellis eqs.(51) and (54))
the mass m is an integration constant of either sign. A flat cavity needs the extra hypothesis of a regular centre (Ghosh et al. p.1)
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED, at foliation.py:48-51, :186-187 and V9 :708-709. The file calls the generalised-PG Schwarzschild 'STATIC' and says 'Gamma > 1 AT EVERY AREAL RADIUS'. But that chart is non-degenerate at every R > 0 (det of the (tau,R) block = -1/(1+2E), B5b), so it also covers R <= 2M. There |d_tau|^2 = -(1-2M/R)/(1+2E) >= 0 and no Killing combination is timelike (B5a, B5d, B5e), so that region is not static (Schmidt p.2; Goswami-Ellis eq.54). 'Static' holds on R > 2M only. foliation.py itself names the trapped region at :165-168 and :856, so the drift is in the witness's wording. The conclusion at :194-195 ('whole Schwarzschild EXTERIOR ... in a static spacetime') needs only R > 2M and survives.

UNCOMPUTED STEP, closed here. foliation.py:186 infers 'Ricci = 0 => Schwarzschild => static' without exhibiting the isometry. This audit exhibits it: t = tau/sqrt(1+2E) + F(R), with F' = -sqrt(2M/R+2E)/(sqrt(1+2E)(1-2M/R)), on f != 0 (B4c). d_tau is Killing and hypersurface-orthogonal (B5c). The step is right in substance; it was only missing.

DROPPED, at wall.py:179-181 and wall.py:664-666 ('a spherical shell's interior is exactly flat by BIRKHOFF at any compactness whatever'). Two hypotheses are missing: an empty cavity, and a regular centre. The regular centre forces M_in = 0, because the Kretschmann scalar is 48 M^2/r^6 (B6a-c; Ghosh et al. p.1). The tree's own device breaks the unqualified wording: stability.py:18-19 is a spherical shell whose interior is Schwarzschild with M_in = -m, which is not flat (B7). The object wall.py actually describes (the balloon with an empty cavity, :176-179) meets both hypotheses, so the conclusion at wall.py:183-187 is unchanged.

DROPPED in all four owners, immaterial at the tree's scales: Lambda = 0. With Lambda > 0 (Planck 2018: Omega_Lambda = 0.6847) the class is Schwarzschild-de Sitter (B9a). An empty regular cavity is then de Sitter, with Kretschmann 8 Lambda^2/3 (B9b), so 'EXACTLY flat' at wall.py:179-180 is strictly false. The departure at R = 4478 m is Lambda R^2/3 = 7.3e-46 (B9c).

DROPPED in all four owners: the GR field equations are an unnamed hypothesis. Birkhoff fails in general when a scalar or helicity-0 mode is present (1101.4520 p.1; 2411.09193 pp.2 and 4). The tree works in GR throughout, so this is a missing name, not a wrong use.

STRONGER THAN NEEDED, harmless, at linstab.py:209-210: P2 assumes 'static vacuum on both sides'. Staticity follows from Birkhoff and need not be assumed: f_in = 1 + 2m/R > 0 at every R, so there is no horizon and d_t is timelike everywhere (B7a). What P3 (linstab.py:211-212) actually needs is that M stays constant in each vacuum region while the shell moves (B1c, B2b-c). That holds, and the file does not name it.

ADDED beyond the theorem, but named elsewhere in the tree. stability.py:18-21 treats the core as a 'Schwarzschild point mass -m', and linstab specthm R8 has 'M_in = -m down to r = 0'. Birkhoff covers only the vacuum annulus and says nothing about r = 0, which here is a curvature singularity (B7b). The junction (stability.py:132-135; B8) uses f_in at r = R only, so it holds for any core of mass -m. The point-mass idealisation is already named as R8's m(0) != 0.

rederivation.outcome: 30/30 PASS. B1, areal chart: G_tr = (2/r) b_t; G_tt e^{-2A} r^2 = d/dr[r(1-e^{-2B})], giving a first integral 2M of either sign; G_rr fixes A_r = -B_r uniquely; G_thth then vanishes, so the solution is Schwarzschild. B2, covariant double-null form (covers trapped regions too): m_u = (1/2) R^2 e^{-2s}(R_u G_uv - R_v G_uu), and similarly for m_v, so vacuum implies m is constant. B3: with Lambda = 0, constant r is not vacuum (G_uv = e^{2s}/r0^2), and a null grad r forces m = r/2, which contradicts dm = 0. B4: foliation.py V7/V8 recomputed, and an explicit isometry to Schwarzschild found. B5: d_tau is timelike iff R > 2M; the chart covers every R > 0; the norm is +1/2 at R = M and -1/6 at R = 3M. B6: Kretschmann = 48 M^2/r^6; the centre is regular iff M = 0, and then Riemann = 0. B7: M_in = -m gives no horizon and a singular centre. B8: sigma(R,-m,0) > 0. B9: the Lambda case solves the field equations, the empty cavity has Kretschmann 8 Lambda^2/3, and Lambda R^2/3 = 7.29e-46.

later_literature.what: Coordinate-free proof. Corrects the popular wording 'every spherically symmetric vacuum solution is static': it is not static inside the horizon. Extends to any dimension and signature. With Lambda > 0, product spaces are also spherically symmetric Einstein spaces.

Two branches: locally static (r > 2m, eq.51) or spatially homogeneous (r < 2m, eq.54). Proves an 'almost Birkhoff' result for open sets away from the horizon. Fails for non-vacuum and for scalar-tensor theories; holds for electrovac and with Lambda.

later_literature.what: Holds on the Einstein branch of quadratic and higher-curvature gravity, and fails generally when a helicity-0 mode is present. A flat empty cavity needs a regular centre. C^2 can be weakened.
The g_tr variation gives dm/dt = 0, i.e. no monopole radiation. Credits Jebsen 1921.
History: Jebsen 1921 was first, then Birkhoff 1923, Alexandrow 1923 and Eiesland 1925.
Birkhoff with a cosmological constant (cited as ref.[18] in 2411.09193).

birkhoff-theorem.lacked_data: Jebsen and Birkhoff had no data to lack. The theorem uses no measured quantity, every later proof (1997, 2004, 2011, 2024) gives the same content, and the re-derivation here agrees (30/30). Two later developments bear on it, and neither moves a tree conclusion. (1) Lambda: unknown in 1923, measured positive since 1998. With Lambda > 0 the class is Schwarzschild-de Sitter and an empty regular cavity is de Sitter, so 'exactly flat' is strictly false. The departure at the tree's largest shell (R = 4478 m) is 7.3e-46. (2) Whether GR is the right theory: Birkhoff fails generically when a scalar or helicity-0 mode is present. That is a hypothesis about the theory, not a datum the authors lacked, and the tree assumes GR throughout. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the theorem has been re-proved covariantly, coordinate-free and in 1+1+2 form with no change of content. The one known correction is to how it is quoted (static only outside the horizon), and foliation.py's wording falls on the wrong side of that correction.
birkhoff-theorem.grade_evidence: The theorem stands as published: re-derived 30/30 in sympy, including the covariant double-null form and the degenerate branches. The tree uses it on a larger class than the theorem gives in two places. (a) foliation.py:48-51 and :186-187 call a chart covering every R > 0 'STATIC' (B5b), but the extra Killing field is timelike only at R > 2M (B5a, B5d; Schmidt p.2; Goswami-Ellis eq.54). (b) wall.py:179-181 and :664-666 say a shell's interior is flat by Birkhoff without the empty-cavity and regular-centre hypotheses, and the tree's own device violates them (stability.py:18-19, M_in = -m; B6, B7). All owners also leave Lambda = 0 unnamed (B9). Every conclusion resting on these uses survives once the hypothesis is named: the foliation witness needs only R > 2M; wall.py's balloon has an empty regular cavity; linstab and stability use Birkhoff only on the vacuum neighbourhoods of the shell, where M is constant and the region is static (B1c, B2, B7a); and Lambda's effect is 7.3e-46. Nothing is WRONG, and no datum moves a conclusion.
birkhoff-theorem.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS, if foliation.py limited 'STATIC' to R > 2M and wall.py stated 'empty cavity, regular centre (M_in = 0), Lambda = 0'. DATA-DEPENDENT, only if a tree conclusion depended on flatness at the ~1e-45 level at R ~ 4.5 km, or on shells near the de Sitter radius (~1.7e26 m). WRONG, if someone exhibited a C^2, Lambda = 0, spherically symmetric GR vacuum that is not locally Schwarzschild; none exists (B1-B3 and all five restatements read).

ltb-energy-function.name: Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi energy function: Gamma^2 = 1 + 2E; E > 0 unbound (hyperbolic) shell

source.located: Lemaitre 1933 (Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles A 53, 51), Tolman 1934 (PNAS 20, 169), Bondi 1947 (MNRAS 107, 410) have no arXiv copies. Read through restatements: (i) Bolejko, Celerier & Krasinski, arXiv:1102.1449v2 (CQG 28, 164002, 2011), eq.(15) ds^2 = dt^2 - R_r^2/(1+2E) dr^2 - R^2 dOmega^2; eq.(16) R_t^2 = 2E + 2M/R + Lambda R^2/3; p.4: 'The sign of k(r) determines the type of evolution when Lambda = 0', with (-k,Phi)->(2E,R) on p.6; eq.(11) is the pressure (Lemaitre-model) form. (ii) Lasky, Lun & Burston, gr-qc/0606003, eqs.(29)-(30) in the 1+E convention; fn.2 p.13: 'E(R) < 0 is the bound case and E(R) > 0 is the unbound case'. (iii) Lasky & Lun, gr-qc/0606055 (PRD 74, 084013), eq.(27): L_n E proportional to P', so E(t,r) is not conserved when there is a pressure gradient; p.5 attaches the unbound/bound labels in the pressure case.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1102.1449, gr-qc/0606003, gr-qc/0606055, 0911.0241 and 1807.06209. Lemaitre 1933, Tolman 1934 and Bondi 1947 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ.

ltb-energy-function.published_statement: Bolejko-Celerier-Krasinski (1102.1449) eqs.(15)-(16): for dust (p = 0, g_00 scaled to 1) the metric is ds^2 = dt^2 - R_r^2/(1+2E(r)) dr^2 - R^2 dOmega^2, with R_t^2 = 2E + 2M/R + (Lambda/3)R^2, where E(r) and M(r) are arbitrary. 'Because the pressure is zero, the mass does not depend on time.' Evolution type 'when Lambda = 0': E < 0 recollapses (elliptic, bound); E > 0 expands or collapses forever (hyperbolic, unbound); E = 0 is the intermediate case (parabolic, marginally bound). Lasky-Lun-Burston fn.2: 'E(R) < 0 is the bound case and E(R) > 0 is the unbound case'. Lorentzian signature needs E > -1 in their 1+E convention. It follows that Gamma = e^{-Lambda_metric} R' = sqrt(1+2E), so Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E.
published_hypotheses: spherical symmetry
dust: perfect fluid with p = 0 (1102.1449 p.2; eq.(15) is derived 'When p_,r = 0')
comoving geodesic flow with lapse = 1 (gr-qc/0606003 eqs.(11)-(12))
no radial energy flux (G_tr = 0 in comoving coordinates)

Lambda = 0 for the sign-of-E bound/marginal/unbound classification (1102.1449 p.4); with Lambda the threshold becomes E_lim = -(3M)^{2/3} Lambda^{1/3} (0911.0241 eq.15, in their convention where their E equals 2E here)
1 + 2E > 0 (Lorentzian signature)
R' > 0 away from necks and shell crossings (positive root in e^Lambda = R'/sqrt(1+2E))

gr-qc/9510071.name: Ford & Roman, QI with Casimir: constant negative density incompatible unless tau_0 <~ 0.46 L

source.located: L.H. Ford & T.A. Roman, 'Quantum field theory constrains traversable wormhole geometries', arXiv:gr-qc/9510071v1 (31 Oct 1995); Phys. Rev. D 53, 5496 (1996). Sec. 2 pp.4-6 eqs. (1),(3)-(9); Sec. 4.5 pp.18-19 eqs. (85)-(88); Sec. 6.
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content fullText=true on gr-qc/9510071 (arXiv v1). Sec. 1-2, 4.5, 6 and the references were read verbatim. Sec. 3-5 (wormhole algebra) was grepped only, because it is not used. The journal version PRD 53, 5496 was NOT read. Eq.(1) is proven in Ref.[13] (gr-qc/9410043), which was not re-read; it is restated identically in gr-qc/9607003 eq.(17), which was read.

gr-qc/9510071.published_statement: Sec. 2 p.5: 'Here one has a constant negative energy density, which would not be possible if Eq. (1) holds for all tau_0. However, if we impose some restrictions on the allowable values of tau_0, then the inequality does in fact still apply. Let us consider a massless scalar field with periodicity of length L in the z-direction ... observer moving with velocity v ... <T_mn u^m u^n> = -(pi^2/(45 L^4))(1+3v^2)gamma^2 (3) ... tau_0 <= (3L/2pi)(5/6)^(1/4)[(1+3v^2)gamma^2]^(-1/4) (5). Thus for the special case of a static observer (v = 0), we must have tau_0 <= (3L/2pi)(5/6)^(1/4) ~ 0.46 L (6).' ... 'g(1/sqrt3) = (3/2pi)(5/8)^(1/4) ~ 0.42 (9). Thus if we restrict tau_0 < 0.42 l_1 [l_1 = L/gamma], then the Minkowski space quantum inequality also holds in the compactified spacetime.' Eq.(1): (tau_0/pi) int <T_mn u^m u^n> dtau/(tau^2+tau_0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 tau_0^4) for all tau_0. It is proven for a free, massless, minimally coupled scalar field in Minkowski spacetime without boundaries.
published_hypotheses: H1 Eq.(1) is proven only for a free, massless, minimally coupled, real scalar field in boundaryless Minkowski spacetime, for an inertial observer, with Lorentzian sampling. Sec. 6: 'strictly derived only for a massless, minimally coupled scalar field'.
H2 The Casimir illustration is a massless scalar with PERIODIC identification of length L (compactified, no plates), in its vacuum. The coefficient is taken as pi^2/45 (eq. 3).
H3 The 0.46 L figure is for a STATIC observer (v=0). For arbitrary v the cap is tau_0 < 0.42 l_1, with l_1 = L/gamma.

H4 Applying Eq.(1) in curved or bounded spacetime is an ARGUED premise ('the basic premise of this paper'). It requires tau_0 small compared with the curvature radii and the distance to boundaries. The Casimir case illustrates that premise; it is not a theorem.
H5 Semiclassical: <T_mn> is a renormalised expectation value and fluctuations are ignored. No closed timelike curves.
H6 Plates appear only in Sec. 4.5 (the MTY wormhole), where the rule is carried over heuristically: tau_0 = f s, with 'a reasonable choice of f ... f ~ 0.1'.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED in the canonical gloss, not in the bounds.py prose: the canonical entry lists the hypothesis 'Casimir plates separated by L'. The source's eqs. (3)-(9) are for a periodic identification with no plates. bounds.py:67-70 says only 'a constant negative Casimir density' and is faithful here. The authors themselves later restate the example as plates (gr-qc/9607003 p.2-3), so the gloss has author precedent. But 0.46 L is the periodic scalar's number. For constant plate densities the analogous cap is 1.085 L; that is computed here (C8) and is not in the source.

DROPPED at bounds.py:67-70: the field content. Eq.(1), and so the 0.46 cap, are for one free massless minimally coupled real scalar only.

WEAKENED at bounds.py:67-68: 'Ford & Roman say the same from the other side', i.e. that Casimir does not saturate the QI, as Fewster finds. The source says nothing about saturation. It shows the constant density exceeds Eq.(1) above the cap and equals it exactly at the cap: the cap is defined by equality, so the bound is saturated there by construction. Below the cap the fraction of the bound is (tau_0/tau_max)^4: 0.23 % at the source's own f = 0.1, 9 % at L/4. Non-saturation follows only if tau_0 is taken well below the cap (H4, H6). gr-qc/9510071.lacked_data: In 1995 the authors lacked three things, all found later. (i) The sharper Lorentzian constant (Fewster-Eveson 1998, 9/64): with it the cap falls from 0.456 L to 0.279 L, or 0.332 L with the matched coefficient. (ii) Exact QIs in the compactified or bounded spacetime itself (Pfenning-Ford, Fewster-Teo). These are measured relative to the static vacuum and need no cap for the Casimir vacuum. (iii) A rigorous derivation of the small-tau_0 premise (Pfenning eq. 3.54), which later confirmed it. None of these reverses the qualitative conclusion: a constant negative density violates the flat-space Eq.(1) for all tau_0 and satisfies it only below a fraction of L. They do move the number 0.46, and they show the rescue is specific to using the flat-space bound. A separate point, not a matter of missing data: eq.(3)'s pi^2/45 computes to twice the one-real-scalar value, and with matched field content the cap is 0.54 L. So M's hypothesis holds in a narrow sense: the printed number is not robust, moving by factors of 0.61 to 1.19. It does not hold in the sense of a wrong conclusion: nothing here refutes the qualitative statement the tree quotes. Whether Casimir 'saturates' the QI in the sense bounds.py needs rests on Fewster 1208.5399, which is audited separately.
gr-qc/9510071.grade_evidence: (a) The words quoted at bounds.py:68-70 match arXiv v1 Sec. 2 p.5 verbatim (READ). (b) From the paper's own eq.(3) the numbers re-derive exactly: 0.456190 L and 0.424533 (checks C2-C4 pass). (c) The result holds on a smaller class than the tree's use carries. It is for a periodic massless minimally coupled real scalar, not plates (plates are added by the canonical gloss). It is for a static observer; over all v the cap is 0.42 L/gamma, which bounds.py:70 drops. It is for the flat-space QI only, so 'only by capping' is not true of the exact bounded-space QIs. (d) 'Say the same' (non-saturation) is the tree's inference. The density equals the bound at the cap by construction, and it is far below the bound only for tau_0 well below the cap (0.23 % at the source's own f = 0.1). (e) DISCREPANCY, not refutation: eq.(3)'s pi^2/45 is twice the computed pi^2/90, which moves the cap to 0.5425 L. The qualitative conclusion survives. The journal version was not read. The grade is not WRONG (no counterexample), not DATA-DEPENDENT (no measured input) and not OPEN (read and checked).
gr-qc/9510071.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade would become STANDS if bounds.py:70 stated the scope (static observer, periodic massless scalar, flat-space QI, or quoted 0.42 l_1) and the journal version PRD 53, 5496 printed pi^2/90 or 0.54 L. It would also become STANDS if some explanation of pi^2/45 (e.g. a complex field) matched Eq.(1)'s field content. WRONG would need a constant negative density that satisfies Eq.(1) for all tau_0. That is impossible: the sampled constant does not depend on tau_0 while the bound goes to 0 (C1). If the journal confirms pi^2/45 for one real scalar, the discrepancy stays as recorded and the grade stays NARROWED.

frw-metric-k-minus1-and-k0.published_statement: (Baumann 0907.5424 eq.1-3, 106; Ellis & van Elst gr-qc/9812046 eq.104-105) Assume space is homogeneous and isotropic (isotropic about every point), and use coordinates comoving with the matter (u^a = delta^a_0, t the comoving observers' proper time, slicing orthogonal to the threading). Then the metric is ds^2 = -dt^2 + a^2(t)[dchi^2 + S_k(chi)^2 dOmega^2], with S_k = sinh chi for k = -1 (open), chi for k = 0 (flat) and sin chi for k = +1. Equivalently it is a^2[dr^2/(1 - k r^2) + r^2 dOmega^2] with r = S_k(chi). The t = const 3-spaces have constant curvature, with 3-Ricci scalar 6k/a^2. With a perfect-fluid source the Einstein equations give H^2 = (8 pi G/3) rho - k/a^2 and addot/a = -(4 pi G/3)(rho + 3p) (Baumann eq.110-111; Ellis eq.106-107).
published_hypotheses: GR in 4 dimensions. The metric form is pure geometry; the Friedmann equations need the Einstein equations.
Spatial homogeneity and isotropy, with isotropy about every point (Baumann fn.1: a space isotropic everywhere is homogeneous; Ellis eq.103).
Matter-comoving coordinates: u^a = delta^a_0, u_a = -grad t, zero shift, t = proper time of the fundamental observers, slicing orthogonal to the threading (Ellis eq.104; Baumann eq.1 and p.45).
The fundamental flow is geodesic, shear-free and irrotational (Ellis eq.103: udot = sigma = omega = 0).
The source is a perfect fluid (Ellis sec.4; Baumann eq.19-20), and non-empty models assume mu + p > 0 (Ellis sec.5.2). This is a MATTER hypothesis, not a consequence of the metric.
k is normalised to -1, 0, +1, with the curvature scale carried by a (Ellis 4.1 item 2).
Simple (simply connected) topology for the global chart ranges (Baumann Problem 1; Ellis 4.1 notes other topologies). This is global only; no local statement depends on it.

geroch-1973-huisken-ilmanen-2001-imcf.name: Geroch monotonicity / Huisken-Ilmanen: Hawking mass non-decreasing under inverse mean curvature flow when R >= 0; proof of the Riemannian Penrose inequality

source.located: R. Geroch, 'Energy extraction', Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. 224 (1973) 108-117 (no arXiv copy); P.S. Jang & R.M. Wald, J. Math. Phys. 18 (1977) 41; G. Huisken & T. Ilmanen, 'The inverse mean curvature flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality', J. Differential Geom. 59 (2001) 353-437. HI has no arXiv copy: alphaXiv resolved its title twice to an unrelated paper, Kroener arXiv:1211.5046, which only cites HI as ref.[13]. All three are read through exact restatements. (1) M. Mars, 'Present status of the Penrose inequality', arXiv:0906.5566: sec.1 p.3; sec.2.4 pp.10-11, eqs.(13),(17),(18); sec.5.3 pp.21-23, eqs.(35)-(37); sec.5.4 p.23; sec.6 p.43. (2) S. Hirsch, arXiv:2210.12237v4: sec.1 p.1; sec.2.1 pp.3-4, eq.(6); sec.4.1 p.12. (3) Bi & Zhu, arXiv:2605.00680v2, p.2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0906.5566, 2210.12237 and 2605.00680. Geroch 1973, Jang-Wald 1977 and Huisken-Ilmanen 2001 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ. HI's own weak 'Geroch Monotonicity Formula' (sec.5) and their connectedness lemma (sec.4) were not read here; they are known only as Mars restates them.

geroch-1973-huisken-ilmanen-2001-imcf.published_statement: Mars 0906.5566 p.21: 'the Geroch mass (17) (with C = 0) is monotonically increasing if the surfaces are moved by inverse mean curvature (i.e. p e^psi = 1) provided the scalar curvature of (Sigma, gamma) is non-negative ... its value on any connected, topologically S^2 minimal surface is M_G = sqrt(|S|/(16 pi)) ... lim M_G(S_r) = M_ADM.' Eq.(17): M_G(S) = sqrt(|S|/16pi)(chi(S)/2 - (1/16pi) int (p^2 + 4C/3)), where 'chi(S) = 2 for a connected surface with spherical topology'. Geroch mass equals Hawking mass on time-symmetric data. Weak flow (p.22): across a jump 'the Geroch mass is non-decreasing provided the Euler characteristic of the surface does not decrease'; 'The example with two spheres in Euclidean space shows that this cannot be true in general'; therefore 'a connected component S_i of the outermost minimal surface must be chosen as initial surface. The Penrose inequality proven by Huisken and Ilmanen is ... M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi) (37)', with Schwarzschild rigidity. Hirsch p.1: HI 'proved the Riemannian Penrose inequality for connected horizons'. Hirsch p.3, for (M,g) asymptotically flat, 3-dimensional, complete, R >= 0: 'd_t m_H(Sigma_t) >= 0 where m_H = sqrt(|Sigma|/16pi)(1 - (1/16pi) int H^2)'.
published_hypotheses: A 3-dimensional Riemannian setting: in GR, a time-symmetric initial data set (k = 0), where the Geroch mass equals the Hawking mass (Mars p.10-11)
Scalar curvature R >= 0
The flowing surface is connected (Euler characteristic chi <= 2); the Hawking-mass normalisation '1 - ...' presumes chi = 2 (Mars eqs.(13),(17), p.22; Hirsch p.1 'connected horizons')

Either a smooth IMCF with H > 0 (Geroch/Jang-Wald; the flow generically becomes singular), or the Huisken-Ilmanen weak level-set, outer-area-minimising flow, whose monotonicity needs the Euler characteristic not to drop across jumps. HI guarantee this for an S^2 leaf outside the outermost minimal surface in an asymptotically euclidean 3-manifold (Mars p.22)

For the Riemannian Penrose inequality: (M,g) is complete and asymptotically flat, and the flow starts from a connected component of the outermost minimal surface. What is proved is M_ADM >= max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi) (Mars eq.37). The full inequality is Bray 2001, and the general non-time-symmetric Penrose inequality is still open
Dimension 3: Gauss-Bonnet is what cancels the constant term

geroch-1973-huisken-ilmanen-2001-imcf.lacked_data: No physical datum was missing, because this is mathematics. What Geroch (1973) and Jang-Wald (1977) lacked was a mathematical input: an existence theory for IMCF through its singularities. Mars p.3 and p.21: the flow 'generically develops singularities and therefore the argument could not be made rigorous at the time'. So their argument was incomplete in M's sense. When the missing piece arrived (the HI 2001 weak flow), the conclusion was confirmed, not reversed, with one narrowing: the jump analysis forced the flow to start from a connected component, which gives max_i sqrt(|S_i|/16pi). Bray later completed the full inequality by another method. Evidence against 'wrong': the identity re-derives symbolically (A), matches an exact computation on a non-round surface (C), and reproduces Misner-Sharp monotonicity (B). Evidence that the tree quotes it incompletely: the tree's R >= 0-only statement is refuted by the two-sphere example (D). That hypothesis was in the literature all along; the tree dropped it. The tree's claim at overturn.py:151-152 that nobody has settled the question either way is a claim of absence that one discovery call cannot settle, so it stays OPEN. One further observation, recorded and not repaired: m_H < 0 on a non-round surface in flat space (C3; Willmore). So m_H >= 0 off round spheres (overturn.py:149-150) is a stronger requirement than its spherical analogue.
geroch-1973-huisken-ilmanen-2001-imcf.grade_evidence: The published result stands as published. The monotonicity identity re-derives symbolically (A1-A3), matches an exact computation on a non-round surface to 18 digits (C2), and reduces to m' >= 0, equivalently R >= 0, in spherical symmetry (B1-B4). Schwarzschild is the equality case (E). Mars, Hirsch and Bi-Zhu restate it consistently, and nothing read contradicts it. The grade is NARROWED because the tree (overturn.py:138-140; CLAIMS.md:2640-2641 and 3109-3111) keeps only R >= 0 and drops connectedness of the flowing surface. Without connectedness the statement is false: two disjoint spheres in flat space have decreasing m_H (D1-D2). The tree also drops the weak-flow setting, and slightly overstates that IMCF 'proved the RPI': it proved max_i over connected components, and Bray 2001 proved the rest. Effect on the tree's verdict: none. overturn L1 is graded OPEN and uses Geroch/HI only as the nearest candidate tool, not as a premise.
geroch-1973-huisken-ilmanen-2001-imcf.what_would_change_the_grade: It becomes STANDS if the tree restates the result with connected leaves (chi <= 2) and, for the weak flow, a start from a connected component of the outermost minimal surface in a complete asymptotically flat manifold, and says the flow proved the RPI for a connected horizon, with Bray 2001 for the general case. It becomes WRONG only if someone produces a counterexample to HI's weak monotonicity under its own hypotheses; none is known in the literature read here.

1005.0031-eq58.published_statement: p.14: 'as Deutsch and Candelas [61] showed many years ago, in the neighborhood of a curved surface for conformally invariant theories, <T^{mu nu}> diverges as eps^-3 ... with a coefficient proportional to the sum of the principal curvatures of the surface ... for the case of a sphere, the leading surface divergence has the form, for conformal fields, for r = a + eps, eps -> 0, <T^{mu nu}> = (A/eps^3) diag[2/a, 0, a, a sin^2 theta] (58) [as the text layer renders it] ... A = 1/720 pi^2 for a scalar field satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions, or A = 1/60 pi^2 for the electromagnetic field satisfying perfect conductor boundary conditions. Note that (58) is properly traceless. ... The corresponding quadratic divergence in the stress corresponds to the absence of the cubic divergence in <T^rr>.' p.15 caution: 'the local vacuum-fluctuation energy density is to a large extent meaningless ... the coefficients of the divergent terms depend on the regularization scheme.'
published_hypotheses: H1: the field is conformally invariant (a conformal scalar with xi = 1/6, or the Maxwell field).
H2: the boundary is ideal: Dirichlet for the scalar, PERFECT CONDUCTOR for EM (n x E = 0, n.B = 0).
H3: the surface is smooth and closed; for (58) it is a sphere of radius a.
H4: the point is EXTERIOR, r = a + eps; the equation is stated for this side only.
H5: leading asymptotic order only, eps -> 0 (eps << a); eq. (57) carries eps^-2 and eps^-1 corrections T^(2), T^(1).
H6: flat (Minkowski) background; the quantity is the vacuum expectation value of the renormalised, bulk-subtracted stress tensor.

H7 (Milton's own caution, p.15): the local near-surface density depends on the regularisation and on the choice of stress tensor, and is 'to a large extent meaningless' except in how it couples to gravity (p.3 calls gravity 'the exception').

But what moved was an input, not a theorem, and the move lies inside the band tested. The ~3 sigma lattice-phenomenology tension that remains is attributed in the 2024-2026 literature to lattice excited-state contamination, a gap in method rather than missing experimental data. It is unresolved at the physical point.

source.located: C. Barcelo & M. Visser, 'Scalar fields, energy conditions, and traversable wormholes', arXiv:gr-qc/0003025v2 (14 Jul 2000; dated 7 March 2000), Class. Quant. Grav. 17 (2000) 3843-3864. Sect. 2.1 eqs.(2.1)-(2.3) pp.3-4 (kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N), action, T_eff); sect. 2.3 eqs.(2.7)-(2.11) and cases 1-3, pp.5-6; sect. 4 p.16 ('~ m_p/sqrt(xi)', footnotes 4-5); sect. 5 eq.(5.51) p.19 (physical Newton constant).

gr-qc/0003025-anec-cases.published_statement: BV pp.5-6, sect. 2.3: I = INT [T_eff]_mn k^m k^n dl (2.7) = INT kappa/(kappa - xi phi^2)[(dphi/dl)^2 - 2 xi d/dl(phi dphi/dl)] dl (2.8) = INT kappa[kappa - xi(1-4xi)phi^2]/(kappa - xi phi^2)^2 (dphi/dl)^2 dl - {2 xi kappa phi phi'/(kappa - xi phi^2)}|_{l1}^{l2} (2.10). 'We start by considering a complete null geodesic and assuming sufficiently smooth asymptotic behaviour. Then the boundary terms from asymptotic infinity can be neglected...' (2.11). '1. If xi < 0 ... the integrand ... is itself guaranteed positive so ANEC is satisfied. 2. If xi > 0, but we have (phi)^2 < kappa/xi, then again there are no places on the geodesic where kappa = xi[phi(l)]^2. Furthermore the integrand appearing above is again positive and ANEC is satisfied. 3. Finally, if xi > 0, and we have at least some places where (phi)^2 > kappa/xi ... The boundary terms can no longer be neglected and potentially can contribute -- typically making negative and infinite contributions ... (If xi in (0,1/4) then it is possible to have (phi)^2 > kappa/[xi(1-4xi)] and so make the integrand negative.) In short: there is definitely the possibility of ANEC violations under these conditions.' p.3: 'kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N)', S = 1/2 INT sqrt(-g) kappa R + INT sqrt(-g)(-1/2(dphi)^2 - V - 1/2 xi R phi^2). p.16: 'the scalar field has to reach absolute values above ~ m_p/sqrt(xi), where m_p is the Planck mass.'
published_hypotheses: A classical (not quantised) single real scalar, action (2.1), signature (-,+,+,+), with conformal coupling at xi = +1/6 in this convention (effective gravitational coefficient kappa - xi phi^2).

Later came the Higgs discovery and the measured bound |xi| < 2.6e15 (1211.0281), an unchanged CODATA G, a G_F refined at the 0.1-ppm level, and FFK 2023's independent re-derivation. gaussian-mills-ratio.name: Mills-ratio bounds for the Gaussian tail: phi(z)/z (1 - 1/z^2) <= P <= phi(z)/z

source.located: Classic: R.D. Gordon (1941), Ann. Math. Stat. 12, 364-366 (upper phi/x, lower phi/(x+1/x), x>0). The tree's exact pair (1/z - 1/z^3) < M(z) < 1/z is the K=1,2 truncation of the alternating Laplace series. Read at source in (i) L. Duembgen, arXiv:1012.2063v3 (Bern TR 76, Dec 2010), p.2 eq.(2) with the Gordon restatement, and p.4 sec.2 (proof of the k=0 case); (ii) T. Buric, N. Elezovic, L. Mihokovic, arXiv:2607.26636v1 (29 Jul 2026), p.7 Proposition 3.3 (two-sided envelope).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1012.2063 (all 24 pages) and 2607.26636 (all 13 pages). Gordon 1941 has no arXiv copy, so it is NAMED-NOT-READ; Duembgen p.2 restates it exactly. The tree's specific lower bound phi(1/z - 1/z^3) is stated verbatim as Prop. 3.3 of 2607.26636 with K=2.

gaussian-mills-ratio.published_statement: Duembgen 1012.2063 p.2: 'for integers k >= 0 and arbitrary x > 0, (2) 1-Phi(x) < phi(x)/h_k(x) if k is even, > if k is odd. In particular, phi(x)/(x+1/x) < 1-Phi(x) < phi(x)/x, which was first established by Gordon (1941).' Buric-Elezovic-Mihokovic 2607.26636 p.7 Prop. 3.3: 'For z = x+t > 0 and every K >= 1, M(z) = sum_{k=0}^{K-1} (-1)^k (2k-1)!!/z^{2k+1} + r_K, sgn r_K = (-1)^K, |r_K| < (2K-1)!!/z^{2K+1}, so the even and odd partial sums bracket M from below and above', where M = (1-Phi)/phi. K=1 gives M < 1/z and K=2 gives M > 1/z - 1/z^3. That is exactly the tree's pair, with strict inequalities.
published_hypotheses: Standard normal: phi(x) = exp(-x^2/2)/sqrt(2 pi) and Phi its distribution function (centred, unit variance). Any N(0, s^2) reduces to it through z = D/s.
x > 0 (Gordon; Duembgen eq.(2)) or z > 0 (Prop. 3.3). There is no other hypothesis, and the bounds are strict.
The lower bound 1/z - 1/z^3 says something only for z > 1; it is non-positive for z <= 1.

no-cloning-theorem.name: No-cloning theorem (Wootters-Zurek / Dieks 1982)

source.located: W.K. Wootters & W.H. Zurek, Nature 299, 802 (1982), and D. Dieks, Phys. Lett. 92A, 271 (1982). Neither is on arXiv. Read through Scarani, Iblisdir, Gisin, Acin, 'Quantum cloning', Rev. Mod. Phys. 77, 1225 (2005), arXiv:quant-ph/0511088: p.3 Sec. I.B gives the statement and the linearity proof 'following the work of Wootters and Zurek (1982)'; pp.3-4 Sec. I.C gives the history (Herbert's FLASH, WZ, Dieks, Milonni-Hardies, Mandel); p.4 covers Barnum et al. 1996 and Buzek-Hillery F=5/6; p.30 covers teleportation. Ahn-Myers-Ralph-Mann arXiv:1207.6062 p.2 restates the WZ content independently.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on quant-ph/0511088 (pp.1-4, 7, 30, 32) and on 1207.6062 (pp.1-5). The WZ and Dieks originals are NAMED-NOT-READ. Dieks' own proof is not restated word for word anywhere read here.

no-cloning-theorem.published_statement: As restated in Scarani et al. 2005, p.3: 'No-cloning theorem: No quantum operation exists that can duplicate perfectly an arbitrary quantum state.' The proof assumes |psi>|R>|M> -U-> |psi>|psi>|M(psi)>. For orthogonal |0>,|1>, linearity forces (a|0>+b|1>)|R>|M> -> a|00>|M(0)>+b|11>|M(1)>, which is not a product of two copies. 'So (2) may hold for states of an orthonormal basis, but cannot hold for all states ... using only the linearity of quantum transformations following the work of Wootters and Zurek (1982).' Scope, p.2: cloning 'can be done perfectly and with probability 1 if and only if a basis to which psi belongs is known'.
published_hypotheses: H1 LINEARITY: the evolution is a linear trace-preserving CP map. By Kraus's theorem this is a unitary on system plus ancilla with the ancilla traced out (Scarani p.3). Ahn et al. p.2 add that it holds 'if chronology is respected': Deutsch's CTC model makes the induced map nonlinear.
H2 PERFECT copying: fidelity exactly 1 with probability 1. Imperfect cloning is allowed (Buzek-Hillery F=5/6), and so is probabilistic exact cloning (Scarani p.2).
H3 ARBITRARY input: the set to be copied contains two distinct non-orthogonal states. A known orthonormal basis can be cloned.
H4 pure states in WZ. Barnum et al. 1996 extend it to non-commuting mixed states (no-broadcasting).
H5 standard Hilbert-space quantum mechanics, with the blank |R> and the machine |M> fixed independently of psi.

no-cloning-theorem.lacked_data: In 1982, WZ and Dieks had linearity as a postulate, Herbert's FLASH proposal as the trigger, and no experimental bound on nonlinearity. Teleportation (1993), no-broadcasting (1996) and optimal cloning (1996) came later. The later data are (a) nonlinearity bounds, all null (Polkovnikov 2022 READ, |eps_gamma| < 4.7e-11; Bollinger 1989 NAMED-NOT-READ); (b) optimal approximate cloning, which shows the theorem is sharp only for perfect copies; and (c) Deutsch-CTC models, contested, under which cloning is possible. None of this moves the theorem. It follows from linearity in two lines, re-derived here exactly (C1-C3), and every later test is consistent with H1. What the later work does show is that the conclusion is exactly as strong as H1, and the one route in the literature by which H1 fails, CTCs, is one this board keeps open (O3). So M's suspicion is not borne out for the theorem itself. It is borne out only in the narrow sense that the tree uses the result without naming the hypothesis it depends on, in a setting where that hypothesis is live.

Its statement and proof are re-derived exactly in sympy (C1-C3; linsolve returns EmptySet for any linear cloner on {|0>,|1>,|+>}). transit.py's number is correct when computed from the protocol rather than hard-coded (C4: Alice's pair is a psi-free Bell state, each qubit is I/2, S = 1 bit, fidelity at B is 1). No moved datum moves it. The grade is NARROWED under the rule's clause 'a hypothesis the tree drops'. Every tree site (transit.py:30-33, :231-232, :343; specthm.py R11 :1206-1209; ledger.py M-S1A-P5 :1360-1366; index3.py:1364) omits H1 (linear, chronology-respecting evolution) and H2 (perfect copies only). The board holds CTCs open (latticectc.py:109 O3_CLOSED = False), and CTCs are the one setting in the literature read here where the theorem is circumvented (Ahn et al. 1207.6062, itself contested by Bennett et al. 2009). Within the class the tree actually runs, teleportation in linear chronology-respecting QM, its use is correct. Two further discrepancies are recorded, not counted as refutations: the 'enforced by the protocol' wording reverses the source's direction (Scarani p.30), and the entropy at transit.py:230/:342 is taken of a literal I/2, so that selftest line cannot fail.
no-cloning-theorem.what_would_change_the_grade: To reach STANDS: the tree names H1 (linear, chronology-respecting evolution, no Deutsch CTC) and H2 (perfect copies only; approximate cloning at F = 5/6 allowed) at the no-cloning sites and in R11, and confines IT_IS_A_MOVE_NOT_A_COPY to that class. To reach WRONG: a non-null nonlinearity result, or an accepted resolution of the Deutsch-CTC dispute that places the tree's teleportation in a CTC region. Neither exists. OPEN does not apply, because the result is fully checkable here.

density-of-rationals.name: Every nonempty open real interval contains a rational (Archimedean property)

source.located: Classical result (Eudoxus/Archimedes; modern form in e.g. Rudin PMA Thm 1.20), with no arXiv original. Read through J. F. Hall, arXiv:1101.5652 (2011): Def 2.1, Prop 2.4, Ex 2.7, Lemma 3.4, Thms 3.5/3.8/3.11, Ex 3.9. Also J. Propp, arXiv:1204.4483v4 (2013): property (2) p.5, sec.3 p.7, sec.4 p.9. Also Z. Murray, arXiv:2205.08354 (2022) pp.10-11 and 15, where the Archimedean property and density of Q are machine-checked in Agda.
source.via: Rudin / Eudoxus-Archimedes are NAMED-NOT-READ. The Archimedean property was READ verbatim in 1101.5652 Def 2.1 and 1204.4483 (2). Density was READ as stated in 1101.5652 ('Q is dense in every Archimedean field', pp.10-11) and in 2205.08354 pp.10-11 (verified constructively in Agda). Neither restating paper prints density as a numbered theorem with its own proof, so it is re-derived here in z3.

density-of-rationals.published_statement: arXiv:1101.5652 Def 2.1: 'A totally ordered field (ring) K is Archimedean if for every x in K, there exists n in N such that |x| < n.' arXiv:1204.4483 (2): 'For every x in R there exists n in N_R with n > x. Equivalently, for every x in R with x > 0 there exists n in N_R with 1/n < x.' 1101.5652 pp.10-11: 'the rationals are dense in any Archimedean field' / 'Q is dense in every Archimedean field'. Ex 2.7: 'The fields R, Q, C are all Archimedean fields'. Lemma 3.10: a Dedekind complete field is Archimedean. Together these give: for real a < b there is p/q with a < p/q < b.
published_hypotheses: the field is a totally ordered ARCHIMEDEAN field (1101.5652 Def 2.1). R qualifies (Ex 2.7; Lemma 3.10; 1204.4483 p.9)
the interval is nonempty and open: a < b strictly
it fails without the Archimedean hypothesis: in R(omega)/R(eps), (0, eps) holds no positive rational (1204.4483 p.7; 1101.5652 Ex 3.9)
it still holds constructively for Bishop reals (2205.08354 pp.10-11)

squeezed-vacuum-negative-local-energy.published_statement: EGJ 1965, as restated (Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 Thm 3.2, read by a prior stage): 'Let A in A(O) be a self-adjoint local operator of a QFT such that <psi|A psi> >= 0 for all psi in the domain of A. Suppose <Omega|A Omega> = 0. Then A == 0.' Fewster math-ph/0501073 p.2: 'the energy density in any Wightman field theory necessarily admits negative expectation values (unless it is trivial).' Explicit form, KF 1993 Eq.(3.22), in the shape the tree transcribes at fluctuation.py:259 and re-derived here as A1. Take one plane-wave mode of a free massless scalar in a box of volume V, normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum, in the squeezed vacuum S(r e^{i theta})|0>. Then <:T00:> = 2K sinh r [sinh r + cosh r cos(2(k.x - omega t) + theta)], with K = hbar omega/(2V). It is negative wherever cos(...) < -tanh r.
published_hypotheses: P1 Free field. KF uses a massless scalar; one EM plane-wave mode has the same form because :E^2: = :B^2: for such a mode (KF K2).
P2 Flat (Minkowski) background (KF K1).
P3 The energy density is the EXPECTATION VALUE of T00, normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum, so the vacuum is the zero of energy (EGJ H3, KF K3).
P4 The pointwise value exists. This needs a Hadamard state, and a finite-mode Bogoliubov transform of the vacuum is one (EGJ restatement H6).
P5 The explicit form is for a single box-normalised mode. EGJ itself is generic: it asserts only that SOME state has a negative expectation value.
P6 EGJ gives nonpositivity only. Unboundedness at a point needs an extra scaling hypothesis. This key does not use it.

The tree's own fluctuation.py:90-91 already records this.

(iii) 'Gone' means the negative regions leave at c together with the positive energy that outweighs them; nothing is annihilated.

A single-mode squeezed vacuum of a free massless field has a negative expectation value of the normal-ordered energy density on part of every cycle, for every r > 0. This is re-derived symbolically (A1, B1-B2) with independent Fock controls (A2, C1). It is consistent with EGJ nonpositivity and with the KF (3.22) shape at fluctuation.py:259. (1) 'Genuinely negative at a point' is an expectation value with Delta' = 2 (C1). (2) The negative phase is a minority, and positive energy in the same wave outweighs it (B4-B5). (3) The dip has a floor of -hbar omega/(2V) per mode (B3). (4) 'Gone at c' needs free massless propagation in vacuum and single-pass generation (D1-D2). The status word MEASURED on S3 (ledger.py:1553) holds only through the identification in E1. Nothing here is WRONG. published_hypotheses: Not read at source. These hypotheses belong to the calculation as re-derived here and to the tree's READ restatement. None is quoted from 't Hooft.
H-SEMI: semiclassical, leading order in g^2, one-instanton (dilute-gas) saddle, weak coupling. Carried in RS96-inst ('semiclassical exponent', massform.py:1094).
H-T0: zero energy and zero temperature, vacuum-to-vacuum tunnelling (RS96-T0, massform.py:1071-1077).
H-CHIRAL: only left-handed SU(2) doublets carry zero modes, index 2T(R)Q (rederive D1-D2).

mass-energy-equivalence.published_statement: Not quoted verbatim, because the source could not be read here. The standard content of Einstein 1905 is: if a body gives off energy L as radiation, its mass decreases by L/c^2, and the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content. It was derived with a two-pulse thought experiment and printed to second order in v/c (K0 - K1 = (1/2)(L/c^2) v^2). The absolute statement E0 = M c^2, for the total rest energy of a closed system, is the later form due to Laue 1911 and Klein 1918. Both forms were re-derived here in sympy (script Parts A and B), and this audit relies on that re-derivation.
published_hypotheses: Special relativity: the Lorentz transformation of the energy of plane light waves (relativistic Doppler shift).
Energy is conserved in both inertial frames.

The body's kinetic energy is identified with the Newtonian, O(v^2), kinetic energy. This is the only approximation in the 1905 argument (script A3/A5). With K = (gamma-1) m c^2 the result is exact at every v (A4).
The 1905 form fixes only differences, Delta m = Delta E / c^2. The 1905 argument does not fix an additive constant in E.

The later absolute form assumes (E/c, p) is a four-vector, which forces the constant to 0 (script B1/C1). For an extended body it also needs a closed system in equilibrium, i.e. Laue's condition that stresses integrate to zero, so that its energy-momentum is a four-vector.
The equivalence is not a conversion mechanism. Releasing all of M c^2 needs a separate process, such as annihilation or black-hole evaporation, which the result does not assert.

Full conversion of the payload's rest energy into a terminal flash is not part of E = M c^2; the tree takes it from the folder's chain. E = M c^2 alone does not say a device's store must supply M c^2; the payload's own mass could supply a black hole's mass. The owner attributes this to the document ('its own premise'), so it is a scope note, not drift.

With K = (gamma-1) m c^2 it gives dm = L/c^2 at every v; with the Newtonian K it holds only as v->0. So the 1905 approximation lies entirely in the kinetic-energy identification. Part B: the four-vector law forces the additive constant C = 0, so the absolute rest energy is M c^2, and E^2 - p^2c^2 = M^2c^4. Part C: z3 finds any C != 0 UNSAT for gamma in (1,100), and the vacuity guard is SAT. Part D reproduces the tree's figures through its own functions (warpfolder imported read-only, bytecode writing off): 8.98755e18 J at 100 kg (printed 8.98e18, +8.4e-4); 4.4938e20 J at 5000 kg (printed 4.49e20, +8.4e-4); 8.98755e21 J at 1e5 kg against a printed 8.98e22 (factor 9.9916); 2148 Mt; a store of 1250 + 235.62 = 1485.62 J; shortfall 6.0497e15, i.e. 15.7817 orders. Part E: no current datum moves any of these. warpfolder.py --selftest still passes, and git status on research/warp-drive is clean.

mass-energy-equivalence.lacked_data: In 1905 Einstein had no test at all; he proposed radium salts. The data he lacked came later: mass defects in nuclear reactions (1930s), full conversion in pair annihilation, and the direct test at (-1.4 +- 4.4)e-7 (Rainville 2005, NAMED-NOT-READ). Every later datum agrees with the relation, and none disagrees at its stated precision. Computed consequence for the tree: moving the relation across its full 3-sigma band shifts the shortfall by less than 1e-6 in log10 and leaves the 1e5 kg row's slipped decade at a factor of 9.99 (script E1, E2). The weakness that did exist was in the 1905 derivation: an O(v^2) approximation and, as Ives argued, a disputed step. The exact relativistic re-derivation (A4) and the four-vector argument (B1, C1) close it. So M's hypothesis was tested and is not borne out for this result: having the missing data does not change the conclusion. The one thing that does not follow from E = M c^2 is that all of M c^2 is released as a 'flash' and that a device must supply it. That is the folder's premise, and the owner names it as such.
mass-energy-equivalence.grade_evidence: The statement as the tree uses it (the absolute rest energy M c^2 of a closed body at rest, in special relativity) is re-derived exactly here, with sympy (A1-A5, B1-B2) and z3 (C1 UNSAT, with a SAT vacuity guard in C2). Every figure the tree prints from it is reproduced through the tree's own functions (D0-D7). The only disagreement is the folder document's 1e5 kg cell: 8.98e22 printed against 8.98755e21 computed, a factor of 9.9916. The owner correctly records this as the document's internal inconsistency, and no datum can reconcile it (E3). c is SI-exact, and the empirical test band moves nothing (E1, E2). The hypotheses the tree adds (full conversion, and that the store must supply M c^2) are named by the owner as the folder's premise (warpfolder.py:55-57 and the canonical hypotheses). The hypothesis it drops (closed system, binding energy) is harmless at 1.5e-25 (E4). This caveat goes with the grade: the 1905 paper, Laue/Klein and Rainville 2005 were NOT READ in this stage, because the alphaXiv quota was exhausted and arXiv is egress-blocked. STANDS rests on computation within special relativity, not on a reading, and the published_statement is not a verbatim quotation.
mass-energy-equivalence.what_would_change_the_grade: Three things could change it. (1) A reading of the 1905 paper that shows a hypothesis missing from the list above. None is expected, since the re-derivation reproduces the paper's printed O(v^2) result. (2) A direct test that disagrees with E = M c^2 at roughly 1e-6 or more. None is known here. (3) A reading of the folder documents showing that they do not premise full conversion or a store-supplied M c^2. That would change the shortfall framing, which is the owner's claim about the folder and lies outside this external result, not this grade.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS. No script can re-derive the measurement, and the paper was not read. What was machine-checked is the closed form behind the step warpfolder.py files as NOT-ADJUDICATED. (A) sympy proves the identity F = (1/48pi)(p''/p')^2 - (1/24pi) d/du(p''/p') for the 1+1D Fulling-Davies flux F = (1/24pi)[(3/2)(p''/p')^2 - p'''/p']. The flux formula itself was recalled, not read. So for any motion that starts and ends inertial, the total emitted energy is (1/48pi) Int (p''/p')^2 du, which is never negative. (B) Numeric oscillating burst p = u + 0.05 sin(3u) exp(-u^2/16), with p' >= 0.859: min F = -2.041e-2, negative on 50% of the grid. The total is +3.549451e-3 and matches the closed form to 10 digits. The negative part, -4.157e-2, is 11.7 times the net. The negative flux is transient and always outweighed in total; it is not a static negative density. (C) The tree's frequency gap shifts by 1.04 decades between 1 and 11 GHz, and its verdict does not change.

minkowski-plane-wave-mode-normalisation.published_statement: Not read at source this stage. Per the DOCKET 62 transcription (not re-read): F&T (2.3) reads 'f_lambda(t,x) = U_lambda(x) exp(-i omega_lambda t), a complete orthonormal set of positive-frequency solutions'. In Minkowski space (Sec. 3), U_k = e^{ik.x}/[(2pi)^n 2 w_k]^{1/2}, and (3.2) = -(1/2) INT d^n k/(2pi)^n w_k |fhat^{1/2}|^2, with the dw measure transcribed as INT_0^oo dw. The textbook content, computed here rather than quoted: this is the unique normalisation that makes {U_k e^{-i w_k t}} Klein-Gordon-orthonormal to delta^n(k-k') and gives the canonical commutator [phi, pi] = i delta^n.
published_hypotheses: flat Minkowski spacetime, n spatial dimensions, |g_tt| = 1 (ultrastatic)
free real scalar, minimally coupled, mass mu >= 0, dispersion w_k = sqrt(k^2 + mu^2) > 0

modes orthonormal in the Klein-Gordon inner product, with continuum (delta^n(k-k')) normalisation and Lebesgue measure d^n k. Plane waves are not square-integrable, so orthonormality is distributional
completeness of the positive-frequency set, with the Fock vacuum built on it (the static/Minkowski vacuum)
IR: the Fock construction needs INT d^n k/(2 w_k) to be locally finite near k = 0, i.e. mu > 0 or n >= 2 (it fails for massless n = 1)
hypothesis_drift: NONE THAT MOVES A RESULT. The tree's 'standard Klein-Gordon normalisation with factor 2 w_k' (canonical.json; fewsterteo.py:27, 464) is the KG-orthonormal normalisation, computed here (C1).

n: the tree's docstring and canonical hypotheses say n = 3 (fewsterteo.py:464 'n = 3 coordinates'), but prefactor_route2 keeps n SYMBOLIC in the normalisation while differentiating in 3 coordinates (fewsterteo.py:467-472). Harmless: |U_k|^2 is x-independent for every n, and C1/C2/C4/C5 run with n symbolic. The tree does not state the IR hypothesis (mu > 0 or n >= 2); it is satisfied at n = 3 and carries no weight there.

The dispersion relation is DROPPED in the tree's route 2: omega_k is a free positive symbol and w^2 = k^2 + mu^2 is never imposed (fewsterteo.py:468). This is harmless for route 2, because grad^2|U_k|^2 = 0 whatever w is. The direct (2.10) -> (3.2) check (C4 here) does need the relation, and with it the factor 2 is forced without using (2.12).

The tree leaves the distributional (delta) normalisation implicit (fewsterteo.py:27-28, 464). F&T's 'orthonormal' (2.3, per transcription) uses the same convention. The labelling convention does not matter: SUM_lambda |U_lambda|^2 is the coincidence Wightman function, which completeness plus KG orthonormality fix whatever labelling F&T use (C3 matches the Hadamard coefficient 1/(4 pi^2 sigma)). So the combination route 2 feeds into (2.12) cannot depend on F&T's labelling.

DISCREPANCY IN THE TRANSCRIPTION CHAIN (recorded, not repaired, and NOT a finding against F&T). The DOCKET 62 transcription gives (2.10) as '-(1/2) INT_0^inf dw ...' and (5.6) as '-(1/(16 pi^3)) INT u^4 |fhat^{1/2}|^2'. With these modes, the transcribed (3.2) reduces (massless, n = 3) to -(1/(16 pi^2)) INT u^4 |fhat^{1/2}|^2 (C6a), which is one factor of pi away from the transcribed (5.6). The 1/(16 pi^3) form is the one that gives the tree's 9/64 against Ford-Roman's -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4) (C6b); 1/(16 pi^2) would give 9 pi/64 (C6c). So a 1/pi (for example INT dw/pi, or an fhat convention) is missing from the transcribed (2.10)/(3.2), not from the modes. fewsterteo.py:30-31 prints (3.2) without its dw measure, so the tree file itself does not show the inconsistency. The factor is common to (2.12) and (3.2), so route 2's P (a ratio) is unaffected, and so is route 1 (the ratio of the (2.10) and (2.12) brackets). It must not be quoted as an error of F&T until (2.10)/(3.2) are read at source.

dominant-energy-condition.lacked_data: The DEC is a definition that Hawking & Ellis (1973) posited for classical matter. No numerical datum enters it, so no measured input could have moved. What came later is evidence about whether real matter obeys it: quantum fields violate every pointwise condition (Casimir-type negative energy density), and per Kontou-Sanders 2020 (abstract only) some simple classical fields do too. So M's hypothesis holds in one sense: the 1973 authors lacked the results that narrow the DEC as a law of nature. Having them changes nothing here, and the evidence runs both ways. (a) axial.py's theorem assumes no energy condition (:190; B3 shows the identity is pure geometry), so u < 0 somewhere stands whatever matter exists. (b) concentric.py uses the DEC only contrapositively, to show its own core cannot satisfy it. sturm-comparison-theorem.published_statement: NOT QUOTED (source unreadable here). Standard modern form, re-derived symbolically in rederive/sturm-comparison-theorem.py [1]: if u'' + q u = 0 and v'' + m v = 0 on [a,b] with q >= m (a.e.), and v has consecutive zeros at a and b (b - a = pi/sqrt(m) for constant m > 0), then every non-trivial u has a zero in the CLOSED interval [a,b]; a zero only at an endpoint requires q = m a.e. on [a,b] and u a multiple of v. Proof: W = u'v - uv' has W' = (m - q) u v <= 0 if u > 0 on (a,b), while W(a) = -sqrt(m) u(a) <= 0 and W(b) = +sqrt(m) u(b) >= 0.
published_hypotheses: (S1) scalar, linear, second-order equation u'' + q u = 0 (self-adjoint form; (p u')' + q u = 0, p > 0, in the Sturm-Picone form)
(S2) q real, at least piecewise continuous / L^1_loc (Sturm 1836 assumed continuity; the L^1_loc extension is later -- stated from the re-derivation, not read)
(S3) comparison q >= m pointwise (a.e.) on the whole contiguous interval [a, a + pi/sqrt(m)]
(S4) conclusion: a zero in the CLOSED interval; strictly inside unless q = m a.e. and u is proportional to the comparison solution
(S5) SUFFICIENT only: nothing in the theorem says a zero requires q >= m (necessity is Lyapunov's separate inequality)

(C) Numerically, on 40 random 3-momenta, the minimum eigenvalue is about -6e-15 at xi = 0 (positive type), -1.81e-2 at xi = 1e-3, -3.05 at xi = 1/6, -4.60 at xi = 1/4, and -1.40 at m = 1, xi = 1/6. gr-qc/9304008-claim-after-3.8.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result, and the re-derivation is the evidence. The claim is a closed-form statement about a single-mode Fock expectation value with NO empirical input; K_00 cancels (C3). Kuo & Ford already had everything needed in 1993: the commutator, the box mode, the state (2.15) and the definition (3.2). Their own ingredients are enough to show the claim fails, because every combination of their printed (2.16) and (3.7) with the exact expressions gives Delta < 1 on rho < 0 (C7). The error is algebraic and enters at (3.8); C9 shows it is consistent with an unsquared factor. The sentence itself is a valid corollary of that wrong (3.8) (C8). No missing datum explains the error, and no new datum would change it. On the other side of the question, whether the error matters for the physics KF drew: it does not overturn their qualitative conclusion. The exact bound on rho < 0 is 1/3 < Delta < 1 (C6), so the fluctuations are still of order unity. sachs-weyl-shear-focusing.published_statement: Gao & Wald 2000 p.7 (READ): the Jacobi matrix obeys d^2A/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu (11), with A|_p = 0 and dA/dlambda|_p = delta. 'q will be conjugate to p if and only if det A = 0 at q.' With G = sqrt(det A) (12): 'G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b] (13), where sigma_ab denotes the shear of the congruence of null geodesics emanating from p.' Kar & SenGupta eq (17): dTheta/dlambda + Theta^2/2 + sigma^2 - omega^2 = -R_ab k^a k^b, attributed to Sachs 1961. Olum 1998: 'The generic condition holds whenever there is any normal matter or any transverse tidal force anywhere on P ... From the generic condition, sigma cannot vanish everywhere, thus WEC implies theta < 0.' Gao & Wald p.9: under NEC + null generic condition + null geodesic completeness, 'every null geodesic in M contains a pair of conjugate points'.

No later measurement can move it, so M's hypothesis has nothing to act on for this result, and the evidence is that the statement holds symbolically with no numerical input. What 1961-2000 did not address is the NEC-violating regime: the theorems that turn shear focusing into conjugate points (Hawking-Ellis via Gao-Wald p.9, and Olum) assume NEC/WEC. That is a boundary of scope, not a gap in data, and computing across it (S5) shows the boundary matters: with q <= -|w| there is no conjugate point. Negative mass is prescribed in the tree, not observed, and the result holds for negative-mass Schwarzschild as a vacuum metric regardless.

dust-shell-radial-instability-textbook.name: A pressureless (dust) thin shell with flat interior and Schwarzschild exterior is radially unstable (used as the validation fixture)

source.located: The tree names no source: stability.py:48 says 'as a dust shell must be' and stability.py:246 says 'as it must be'. The published result it relies on is the radial stability of a static thin shell with a Minkowski interior and a Schwarzschild exterior. That is Brady, Louko & Poisson, PRD 44, 1891 (1991), which is pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ. I read it through its exact reproduction in Ishak & Lake, arXiv:gr-qc/0108058v2, using eq (5) (Lake's potential), eq (7) (transparency), eqs (15)-(19) (the V''>0 criterion), sec. III.B and Fig. 2 ('R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0' at P'/sigma' = 1). The V''>0 criterion and the definition beta^2 = dp/dsigma come from Poisson & Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/9506083v1, eqs (13), (23) and (28). The adiabatic-index form comes from LeMaitre & Poisson, Am. J. Phys. 87, 961 (2019), NAMED-NOT-READ, via its restatement in Pitre-Schneider-Poisson arXiv:2604.05980v1 sec. X ('radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2'). The equation of motion for a genuine dust shell comes from Barcelo & Jaramillo arXiv:1112.5265v1, eqs (2)-(4).
source.via: alphaXiv page text. The alphaXiv quota ran out during this stage: answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers all returned 'quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses arxiv.org directly with a 403. I therefore read the verbatim alphaXiv page text that earlier calls in this same workflow had returned and cached under scratchpad d67/src/casmag/all/: gr-qc_0108058v2.txt (md5 26cf595d...), gr-qc_9506083v1.txt (1e67535c...), 1112.5265v1.txt (af75e731...) and 2604.05980v1.txt (9916ebc7...). BLP 1991 and LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 are known only through restatements. No source read states the fixture's exact claim (V''<0 at beta^2 = 0) word for word; I computed it in closed form from the formalism the sources give.

dust-shell-radial-instability-textbook.published_statement: No source read states the result in the tree's words. What the sources do state: (i) Ishak-Lake eq (5): 'Rdot^2 = eps + ([m]/M)^2 - 2 eps mbar/R + (M/2R)^2 ... applies to both shells and wormholes', with stability meaning V''>0 (15). Sec. III.B gives Brady-Louko-Poisson's shell around a black hole: 'R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0 and R/m+ ~ 3 as m- -> m+' at P'/sigma' = 1. (ii) Poisson-Visser after eq (28): 'for V''(a0) > 0 ... stable, while for V''(a0) < 0 perturbations can grow (at least until the nonlinear regime is reached)'. (iii) PSP sec. X, restating LeMaitre-Poisson: such shells are 'radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2' (Newtonian). (iv) Barcelo-Jaramillo eq (4): a dust shell (p = 0) with a Minkowski interior obeys M = sqrt(1+adot^2) M0 - M0^2/(2a), with M0 constant. COMPUTED HERE: V''(R0) = [2 beta^2 (3s+1)s^2 + (s-1)(3s^2+2s+1)/2]/(s^2 R0^2), where s = sqrt(1-2M/R0). At beta^2 = 0 this is -(1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(2 s^2 R0^2) < 0 for every 0 < M/R0 < 1/2. Equivalently, Gamma_crit = (3s^2+2s+1)/(4s^2) >= 3/2.
published_hypotheses: A thin shell (Israel/Lanczos surface layer): timelike and spherically symmetric.
Vacuum on both sides: Minkowski inside (m- = 0), Schwarzschild outside with m+ = M > 0.
Transparency, with static embeddings near the shell (Ishak-Lake eqs 6 and 12, and dc/dr = 0).
Static equilibrium at R0 > 2M with V = V' = 0. This needs the Lanczos surface pressure p0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R0 s) > 0.
Linearised perturbations with l = 0 only. V''<0 means perturbations grow only 'until the nonlinear regime' (PV).
Barotropic matter described by beta^2 = P'/sigma', with PV's caveat that there is 'no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound' (sec. IV).
Gamma form: Gamma = d ln p / d ln sigma at fixed entropy (PSP eq 10.17). LeMaitre-Poisson use a different density convention.
Genuine dust (BJ): p == 0 exactly, so M0 = 4 pi a^2 rho stays constant.
hypothesis_drift: The label 'dust' for beta^2 = 0 (stability.py:48, stability.py:246, and stability.py:65 for the device). The code (stability.py:167-176, p = p0 + beta2 (sigma - sigma0)) computes a static shell whose Lanczos pressure p0 > 0 is held constant. That shell has zero pressure response, but it is not pressureless. A genuine dust shell has no static configuration at all: V = V' = 0 cannot be satisfied (checked with sympy and z3), and BJ eq (4) gives a_ddot = -(2Ma + M0^2)/(4a^3) < 0 at every instant. stability.py:45 ('no pressure response') and stability.py:241 ('at beta^2 = 0') state the hypothesis correctly. This is a discrepancy of wording, not of content. The canonical entry's name, 'pressureless (dust)', carries the same misnomer.
No source is given (stability.py:48, 246): the expected sign is simply asserted. It is now tied to BLP 1991 via Ishak-Lake, to LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 via PSP, and to the closed form computed here.

The tree tests three compactness values (M/R = 0.01, 0.1, 0.2 at stability.py:47-49 and 246-247). z3 proves the result for all 0 < M/R < 1/2. This strengthens the claim rather than cutting against the tree.

What the fixture does not check (stability.py:44 against stability.py:62-65). The fixture pins only the sign of V'' at beta^2 = 0. The device verdict also depends on the sign of the beta^2 coefficient, which the fixture never exercises. This audit closes that gap: the coefficient 2(3s+1)s^2 is positive (z3), and the tree's beta2_crit(ordinary) reproduces the exact values +0.003823 / +0.046477 / +0.122892 and Ishak-Lake's 2.37.

Hypotheses not restated at the validation (stability.py:39-50): vacuum on both sides, transparency, linearity, and beta not being a sound speed. They are carried by the Poisson-Visser machinery named at stability.py:39-42, and none of them changes the fixture's conclusion.

The evidence runs against M's hypothesis for this result: an independent closed-form re-derivation matches the tree's numbers, the published 2.37 (BLP via Ishak-Lake) and the Newtonian Gamma = 3/2 (LeMaitre-Poisson via PSP). What could change the physics is the model's assumptions, not data, and each is named: the thin-shell idealisation, beta treated as a sound speed (PV sec. IV), linearity, and l = 0 only. On the last, PSP 2026 found more instability (all l >= 2), not less. The one inaccuracy found is the tree's own word 'dust' for beta^2 = 0, which is a labelling discrepancy, not a flaw in the outside result.

Under these, V''(R0) = -(1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(2s^2R0^2) < 0, and z3 proves it for every 0 < M/R < 1/2, where the tree samples only three points. 2604.05980-radial-gamma1.published_statement: p.9: 'If we follow M(sigma) along the equilibrium sequence, taking into account that dp = Gamma(p/sigma) dsigma and dmu = [(mu + p)/sigma] dsigma, we find that dM/dsigma >= 0 whenever Gamma >= Gamma_1, where Gamma_1 := 3/2 + 4(p/mu) + 4(p/mu)^2 (3.16a) = (1 + 2 sqrt(F) + 3F)/(4F) (3.16b) = (4 - 6C + 2 sqrt(1 - 2C))/(4(1 - 2C)) (3.16c), where C := M/R ... Gamma_1 = 3/2 + C + 7/4 C^2 + O(C^3) (3.17). The point along the sequence at which dM/dsigma = 0 is the configuration of maximum mass ... and this point also marks the onset of a radial instability -- the shell becomes dynamically unstable against time-dependent, spherically-symmetric perturbations [34].' Footnote 1: 'The criterion appears to be different from the one given in Eq. (34) of Ref. [34] ... In Ref. [34] it was defined as d ln p/d ln mu, whereas it is d ln p/d ln sigma here.' p.7: 'Gamma := (sigma/p) dp/dsigma (2.6) ... The first law then implies that dp = Gamma p/(mu + p) dmu (2.7).' p.37: 'It is known [34] that these equilibrium configurations are radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2.'
published_hypotheses: The shell is infinitesimally thin and traces a timelike hypersurface. The unperturbed state is static and spherically symmetric (p.2, p.7).
Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild outside, vacuum on both sides (p.7).
The shell matter is a perfect fluid with isotropic surface pressure, Eq (2.2).
The equations of state are barotropic, mu = sigma + eps(sigma) and p = p(sigma), Eq (2.4). Here sigma is the areal rest-mass density and mu the areal energy density.
The fluid is isentropic and obeys the first law dmu = (mu+p)/sigma dsigma, Eq (2.5). Eq (2.7) rests on this.
Gamma := d ln p/d ln sigma, taken in the rest-mass density, Eq (2.6). In general it depends on sigma.
Israel junction conditions, Eq (2.10), in general relativity.

The criterion is a turning-point criterion: dM/dsigma >= 0 along the equilibrium sequence. The paper does not derive that this point is where dynamical radial instability begins; it cites Ref [34] for that. It also assumes the sequence starts stable at low sigma (p.9).
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION (a discrepancy, not a content error). wall.py:112 attributes the (3.16c) form to '(LeMaitre-Poisson 2019)', and wall.py:445 says 'LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 / Pitre et al Eq (3.16c)'. casimir-anec-violation-curved.published_statement: Graham & Olum 0705.3193, abstract: ANEC 'is violated by quantum fields in curved spacetime.' p.2: 'In flat space, this condition has been found to be obeyed ... [by] a Casimir plate with a hole [2]. The latter result has been generalized to arbitrary Casimir systems, as long as the geodesic does not intersect or asymptotically approach the plates [3]. However, a quantum scalar field in a spacetime compactified in one spatial dimension or in a Schwarzschild spacetime around a black hole violates ANEC [4].' Sec. II p.3: the compactified case is 'very much analogous to the Casimir effect. ANEC is violated on any geodesic that does not remain at constant z. However, no such geodesic is achronal.' In Schwarzschild (Boulware vacuum), 'every complete geodesic ... is chronal.' Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007, abstract: 'the ANEC holds in flat space with boundaries, as in the Casimir effect, for geodesics which stay a finite distance away from the boundary.' p.2: the plate system is not expected to violate ANEC 'because geodesics parallel to the plates do not violate the NEC, while any other geodesic eventually intersects the plate material.' p.3: 'ANEC may be violated in general curved spacetimes', and it is violated in flat space with a periodic identification 'along any null geodesic which winds around the compact direction ... essentially the Casimir system without the plates.' Sec. IV, eq.(24): <T_ab> = (pi^2/90L^4) diag(-1,1,1,-3), and 'null geodesics which wind round the cylinder are not achronal.' Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.34: the parallel-plate Casimir state violates the pointwise conditions and the AWEC, 'However it has be[en] shown to obey the ANEC [123, 16].'
published_hypotheses: H1 Unrestricted ANEC: the integral runs over a COMPLETE, affinely parametrised null geodesic, and chronal geodesics are allowed (0705.3193 eq.1; gr-qc/0609007 eq.1).
H2 Free quantum TEST fields on a FIXED background. Semiclassical self-consistency is not imposed.

H3 The violating systems as published: (a) Minkowski space periodically identified in one direction. This is FLAT with nontrivial topology, 'the Casimir system without the plates', and the violation is on WINDING geodesics, which are chronal. (b) Schwarzschild in the Boulware vacuum, where every complete geodesic is chronal. (c) Urban-Olum: a conformally flat 4D spacetime, violated on ACHRONAL geodesics. (d) Visser: the class of spacetimes with a nonzero scale anomaly.

H4 The Casimir PLATE system OBEYS ANEC for geodesics a finite distance from the plates. This is FOP's theorem, for the minimally coupled free scalar and under their tubular-neighbourhood conditions. The plate with a hole also obeys ANEC.
H5 The status is explicit calculation, not a theorem that ANEC fails on every curved background.
