casimir-anec-violation-curved.lacked_data: The evidence here runs against M's hypothesis. The result rests on no measured datum: its inputs are computed QFT constants (pi^2/720, pi^2/90, the anomaly coefficient), and the conclusions the tree uses are signs, so no later measurement can move them. What the earliest work lacked was later calculation, and that moved in both directions. First, the plate system was shown to OBEY ANEC (Graham-Olum 2005; Fewster-Olum-Pfenning 2007). The tree has not taken this in, and the resulting mistake is the tree's, not the outside literature's. Second, violations on curved backgrounds were extended to ACHRONAL geodesics for test fields (Urban-Olum 2010), which strengthens the headline the tree quotes. Neither changes the tree's working conclusion that violating ANEC is not by itself a disqualification. What they change is which system is the counterexample, and why it escapes achronal ANEC.
casimir-anec-violation-curved.grade_evidence: The HEADLINE stands on sources READ: 'ANEC in curved spacetime is false in general, so violating it is not by itself a disqualification'. Those sources are G&O 0705.3193 (abstract and Sec. II, Schwarzschild/Boulware), FOP p.3, Visser gr-qc/9409043 p.1, and Urban-Olum 0910.5925 (achronal case; eq.42 evaluates to -2.116e-7). The tree drops one qualifier: these are test fields on fixed backgrounds. The NAMED COUNTEREXAMPLE is contradicted as worded. The tree says 'a geodesic between the plates violates it' and 'Casimir escapes because the geodesic between the plates is not achronal'. Against that, the sources say the plate system OBEYS ANEC (FOP abstract and p.2; G&O p.2; KS p.34). Computation here agrees: T_kk = 0 on every parallel geodesic (EM, and a scalar of any mass, any xi, Dirichlet or Neumann); every other geodesic hits a plate; and every null line between plates is achronal (z3). The Casimir-type counterexample that does exist is the plate-free compactified Minkowski space. Its violating geodesics wind and are chronal (covering interval -L^2), and it is flat, not curved. So the result holds for a smaller, different class than the tree states: the headline holds, and the example holds only as the compactified vacuum. The plate wording at anecscope.py:26, :33-34, :167 and obstruct.py:164-165 is a computed discrepancy, and it is recorded, not repaired. It is not graded WRONG overall because nothing resting on it moves. obstruct.py's ANEC row and index3 ANEC-RELOCATES use only 'violating ANEC is not a disqualification', and the curved counterexamples READ here carry that. The tree's escape mechanism (chronality, 'same as GJW', anecscope.py:109) is exactly the compactified-Casimir mechanism. It is not graded STANDS because the example as used is contradicted.

Also: 'The subtracted term, -Q^2/(2r), corresponds precisely to the classical electrostatic energy of the electric field stored in the exterior region'. Hayward gr-qc/9408002 p.4: 'A central point p will be called regular if g^{-1}(dr,dr) - 1 = O(r^2) ... Then E = O(r^3) at a regular centre'. Prop 6, p.9: 'If the dominant energy condition holds on an untrapped spatial hypersurface with regular centre, then E >= 0'. p.9: 'Note that the energy can be negative if the above assumptions do not hold.'

gr-qc/9805003.name: Olum, 'Superluminal travel requires negative energies' (gr-qc/9805003v2; PRL 81, 3567 (1998)): a causal path P satisfying Condition 1, with the generic condition on P, forces WEC violation at some point of P

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/9805003v2 (14 Oct 1998; dated August 1998), K.D. Olum, Institute of Cosmology, Tufts. The journal ref PRL 81, 3567 is as cited by Visser-Bassett-Liberati gr-qc/9810026 ref.[7]. The PRL typeset version was NOT read.

gr-qc/9805003.published_statement: Abstract: 'I propose a definition of superluminal travel which requires that the path to be traveled reach a destination surface at an earlier time than any neighboring path. With this definition (and assuming the generic condition) I prove that superluminal travel requires weak-energy-condition violation.' p.4 Condition 1: 'There exist 2-surfaces Sigma_A around A and Sigma_B around B such that (i) if p in Sigma_A then a spacelike geodesic lying in Sigma_A connects A to p, and similarly for Sigma_B, and (ii) if p in Sigma_A and q in Sigma_B then q is in the causal future of p only if p = A and q = B.' p.6: 'any spacetime that admits superluminal travel on some path P (and thus, according to our definition, that satisfies Condition 1) and that satisfies the generic condition on P, must also violate the weak energy condition at some point of P.' p.6: 'The present theorem rules out the existence, rather than construction, of superluminal travel, unless there is weak energy condition violation ... the WEC violation must occur along the path to be traveled.' p.6: 'Does this theorem mean that superluminal travel is impossible? No, because the weak energy condition is not obeyed by systems of quantum fields.' A separate, earlier result on p.3 covers the Fig.2 case: S is flat except a region t>t0 inside a spatial box; P is causal from (t1,x1) to (t2,x2) with t2-t1 < x2-x1; S has no singularities and the modified region obeys the generic condition. Then, by Tipler's and Hawking's theorems, 'WEC must be violated somewhere in S'. That location is NOT on P.
published_hypotheses: H1 Condition 1 is the DEFINITION of superluminal: 2-surfaces Sigma_A and Sigma_B, each made of spacelike geodesics through A (resp. B), and no point of Sigma_B lies in the causal future of any point of Sigma_A except B from A. It compares P with NEIGHBOURING paths in ONE spacetime. There is no reference geometry.
H2 the generic condition on P: K_[a R_b]cd[e K_f] K^c K^d != 0 somewhere on P.

H3 (unwritten in the paper, used at Eq.(3)) Einstein's equations: 'If the weak energy condition is satisfied, then R_ab K^a K^b >= 0'. That step needs only the NEC, so the proof actually yields NEC violation on P, which is stronger than the stated WEC violation.
H4 (implicit) a classical, smooth, 4-dimensional Lorentzian geometry with classical T_ab. The paper itself names quantum fields as the escape.
H5 P actually reaches B.
NOT assumed (checked by reading the proof): staticity, any symmetry, sphericity, asymptotic flatness, a foliation, a reference metric.
The author's own caveat (p.4): Condition 1 'might not be sufficient' for superluminal travel. This does no harm to a necessity claim.
One proof step is argued informally (p.5): that there is no focal point to Sigma_A at B. It was not re-proved or machine-checked here. Recorded, not graded.

frw-open-contraction.published_statement: As restated in Enqvist 0709.2044 eq.(2.2) and (2.9): FRW is the LTB metric ds^2 = -dt^2 + A'^2/(1-k(r)) dr^2 + A^2 dOmega^2 with A = a(t) r and k(r) = k r^2, in coordinates that move with the matter, with t the fluid's proper time. So, in the comoving gauge (Escriva 2504.05813 eq.2.3-2.5), Gamma = R'/B = sqrt(1 - k r^2) = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R), with M = 4 pi rho R^3/3 on the FLRW background (Escriva eq.3.3, Hayward eq.33). Gamma > 1 exactly when k < 0 at r > 0, and Gamma = 1 exactly when k = 0. For dust, rho + p = rho.
published_hypotheses: GR in 4D, with spherical symmetry about the chosen centre
homogeneous isotropic perfect fluid, T = (rho+p) u u + p g (Escriva eq.2.1); Enqvist eq.2.3 narrows this to dust + rho_Lambda
comoving slicing and threading: t is the fluid's proper time and the shift is zero (Escriva p.3; Enqvist p.3-4)
k(r) = k r^2 with k(r) < 1, the FRW limit of LTB (Enqvist eq.2.9)
a regular centre for M = int 4 pi R^2 rho dR (Hayward eq.33, Escriva eq.2.4)
rho > 0 is an assumption about the matter, not a consequence of k < 0: rho = 3(adot^2 + k)/(8 pi a^2)
the NEC contraction is rho + p; it equals rho only when p = 0 (dust) and, if rho is read off the Einstein tensor, only when Lambda = 0

friedmann-equation-open-dust.published_statement: As Enqvist 0709.2044 restates it, in the FRW limit A = a(t) r, k(r) = k r^2, F = F0 r^3, with G = c = 1: adot^2 = F0/a + (8 pi/3) rho_Lambda a^2 - k (eq.2.12), with F0 = 8 pi rho_M a^3/3 (eq.2.13). The pressure equation for dust is adot^2 + 2 a addot + k = 8 pi rho_Lambda a^2 (eq.2.11). For k = -1 and rho_Lambda = 0 this gives adot^2 = C/a + 1 with C = 8 pi rho a^3/3, and addot = -C/(2a^2). These are exactly the relations at nonstatic.py:460-462.
published_hypotheses: general relativity, G_mu_nu = 8 pi G T_mu_nu (Enqvist p.4)
homogeneity and isotropy: FRW as the limit A -> a r, k(r) -> k r^2 of LTB (Enqvist eq.2.2, p.4)
comoving coordinates with t = proper time of the fluid and zero shift (Enqvist p.3)
source = pressureless dust plus optional vacuum energy rho_Lambda (Enqvist eq.2.3); the tree sets rho_Lambda = 0
F(r) non-negative (Enqvist p.5), i.e. C >= 0; the strict witness needs C > 0
k(r) < 1 (Enqvist p.4), which k(r) = -r^2 satisfies
a > 0: the solution a = (C/2)(cosh eta - 1), t = (C/2)(sinh eta - eta) starts at a = 0 with rho -> infinity, so its domain is t in (0, infinity) (checked here, C9)

LAMBDA = 0 carries the tree's IDENTITY but not its SIGN (nonstatic.py:465-467, 663-664). With dust + Lambda the null contraction is still 3C/(8 pi a^3) = rho_matter. But rho = 3(adot^2-1)/(8 pi a^2), read off G_tt, becomes rho_m + Lambda/(8 pi), so the checked 'NEC - rho = 0' would read -Lambda/(8 pi) (C4). This is recorded as a named hypothesis, not as a drift.

The open-dust spacetime exists only for t in (0, infinity). It is past-singular: a -> 0, rho -> infinity and R = 8 pi rho -> infinity as t -> 0+ (C9). 'For all time' is true on the spacetime's domain but does not mean all t in R, and the spacetime is past-incomplete. Burwig-Easson 2510.13971 is consistent with this: a null-complete open FRW with bounded curvature has I_ANEC < 0, and open dust has rho + p > 0. Named qualifier: 'for all t > 0 of a past-singular solution'. It does not refute D10, which is a pointwise claim.

For a perfect fluid T_ab k^a k^b = (rho + p)(u.k)^2 for EVERY null k (C10), so the NEC is strictly satisfied in every direction and in every slicing. The tree states its claim more narrowly than it holds, and makes no WEC, DEC or SEC claim.

epstein-glaser-jaffe-1965.name: Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe (1965): the energy density in Wightman QFT cannot be positive. The tree uses it as "no pointwise lower bound on rho(x)".

source.located: H. Epstein, V. Glaser, A. Jaffe, 'Nonpositivity of the energy density in quantized field theories', Nuovo Cim. 36 (1965) 1016-1022. It is not on arXiv. Read through: C.J. Fewster, math-ph/0501073, pp.2-3 and Appendix A pp.10-12; C.J. Fewster, arXiv:1208.5399, pp.7-9 and 11; E.-A. Kontou & K. Sanders, arXiv:2003.01815, pp.17-18 (Thm 3.1, 3.2) and p.22; L.H. Ford & T.A. Roman, gr-qc/9607003, p.2 and ref.[2] on p.16; D. Cadamuro, arXiv:1912.11102, pp.2-5.
source.via: The 1965 original is NAMED-NOT-READ. Its theorem is READ as restated with proof in three places: Fewster math-ph/0501073 p.2, Kontou-Sanders Thm 3.2 and Fewster 1208.5399 p.8. Whether the 1965 paper also states unboundedness cannot be settled here. Ford-Roman credit EGJ (their ref.[2]) with the 'unboundedly negative at a point' fact. Fewster and Kontou-Sanders credit EGJ only with nonpositivity and derive unboundedness separately.

epstein-glaser-jaffe-1965.published_statement:
Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.18, Thm 3.2, verbatim: "Let A in A(O) be a self-adjoint local operator of a QFT such that <psi|A psi> >= 0 for all psi in the domain of A. Suppose <Omega|A Omega> = 0. Then A == 0." From p.17: EGJ "proved that non-positivity is necessary for any (non-vanishing) Wightman field in Minkowski space with vanishing vacuum expectation values."

Fewster math-ph/0501073 p.2: "Epstein, Glaser and Jaffe proved that the energy density in any Wightman field theory necessarily admits negative expectation values (unless it is trivial)."

Unboundedness is a separate result. Fewster math-ph/0501073 p.3: "IF we may assume that the vacuum admits a nontrivial scaling limit for T with positive canonical dimension ... the expectation value of T at a point (if it exists) is unbounded from below" (proof in Appendix A, eq.36). For free fields, Fewster 1208.5399 p.8: "By a scaling argument [18] ... the expectation value of :Phi^2: at a point is unbounded from below as the state varies among Hadamard states."

Ford-Roman gr-qc/9607003 p.2: "the energy density may be unboundedly negative at a spacetime point ... This fact has been known for quite sometime [2]", where [2] is EGJ.
published_hypotheses: H1 Wightman framework in Minkowski space: Hilbert space, dense invariant domain, vacuum Omega, and the field as an operator-valued distribution T(f).
H2 Reeh-Schlieder property: no nonzero local observable annihilates the vacuum.
H3 Vanishing vacuum expectation value <Omega|T(f)Omega> = 0. If it is nonzero, the theorem applies to T(f) - <T(f)>_Omega.
H4 The field is nontrivial.

H5 Needed for UNBOUNDEDNESS only, not part of EGJ: the vacuum has a nontrivial scaling limit with positive canonical dimension (Fewster math-ph/0501073 App. A), or, for free fields, the explicit scaling argument over Hadamard states.
H6 Needed for 'at a point': the pointwise expectation value exists ('if it exists', Fewster p.3). For free fields this means Hadamard states.
hypothesis_drift: Added conclusion and dropped hypothesis at bounds.py:232-233: 'F1 POINTWISE rho(x) ... NO lower bound exists (Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe)'. As restated, EGJ proves nonpositivity only. Getting to 'no lower bound' needs H5 and H6, and the site names neither. Check C3 in the rederivation shows an observable that is nonpositive but still bounded below.
The same drift at achievable.py:320-321: 'no pointwise cap on |rho| exists at all (Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe 1965 ...)'.

Quote-attribution discrepancy at achievable.py:199-203 and 321 (a discrepancy, not a refutation). The first line of gr-qc/9607003 is quoted correctly, but that line carries no citation. EGJ is cited as [2] on the third sentence, and gr-qc/9607003 does not quote EGJ. Crediting EGJ with 'unboundedly' is Ford-Roman's attribution; Fewster and Kontou-Sanders do not make it.

Hypotheses H1-H3 dropped at bounds.py:232-233, which states only 'pointwise energy density in QFT'. Minkowski space and zero vacuum expectation value are not named. In curved spacetime or with boundaries the statement is about the difference from a reference state.
No drift toward a stronger use: the tree does not cite EGJ against the time-averaged (F2) or ball (F3) functionals. For F3 it cites Ford-Helfer-Roman, not EGJ.

rederivation.outcome:
All 13 checks PASS, exit 0.
- C1a (sympy, general 2x2) and C1c (numeric, 2000 random positive semidefinite matrices, 0 violations): the EGJ core step. Positivity plus zero vacuum expectation forces A Omega = 0. C1b holds by construction and is only a sanity check.
- C2a-c (sympy): Fewster math-ph/0501073 eqs.(3)-(5) re-derived exactly. <psi_a|A psi_a> = zeta sin2a + eta(1-cos2a), with minimum eta - sqrt(eta^2+zeta^2) < 0.

- C5: a Lorentzian time average damps the cross term by exp(-2 omega t0). The same state family then has a finite worst case, -0.022040 at V = t0 = 1.

later_literature.what: Credits EGJ with nonpositivity in any Wightman theory. Proves unboundedness at a point only under an extra hypothesis: a scaling limit with positive canonical dimension (App. A). Says the density is unbounded 'in many models', not in all.
Makes the same split: EGJ gives loss of positivity, and a free-field scaling argument gives pointwise unboundedness.
Thm 3.2 restates EGJ with its Reeh-Schlieder proof. p.22 cites pointwise unboundedness as known without crediting EGJ.
In interacting integrable models (Ising, sinh-Gordon), even one-particle states can have negative energy density. Nothing here restores a pointwise lower bound.

later_literature.what: Credits EGJ with the 'unboundedly negative' fact, while the later reviews credit EGJ only with nonpositivity. What is contested is the attribution, not the physics.

epstein-glaser-jaffe-1965.lacked_data:
EGJ is a theorem derived from axioms (Wightman, Reeh-Schlieder, zero vacuum expectation value) and uses no numerical input. No measured value, then or now, can move it, which is why data_at_publication is empty. Casimir and squeezed-light evidence is consistent with the theorem, but the theorem does not need it.

What the 1965 authors lacked was mathematical, not data. They did not have the scaling-limit theory (Fredenhagen-Haag 1987) that turns nonpositivity into pointwise unboundedness, or the quantum-inequality programme that separates the pointwise functional from the worldline one. That later work narrows what EGJ alone can be cited for and supplies unboundedness under H5. It overturns nothing.

Evidence for M's hypothesis on this result: none, since there is no datum and no counterexample. Evidence against it: checks C1-C2 reproduce the theorem from its hypotheses, and C4 reproduces pointwise unboundedness for the free field the board uses.
epstein-glaser-jaffe-1965.grade_evidence:
The theorem itself stands: C1 and C2 re-derive it, and no later work contradicts it.

The tree uses it for more than it proves. bounds.py:232-233 and achievable.py:320-321 cite EGJ for 'no lower bound / no pointwise cap at all'. The restatements credit EGJ only with nonpositivity. Unboundedness needs the dropped hypotheses H5 and H6, and C3 shows nonpositivity alone does not imply it.

On the class the board actually uses (free fields in Minkowski space, Hadamard states), the tree's conclusion is true: C4 shows the pointwise minimum goes to -infinity.

Ledger W1 and the F1/F2/F3 separation are unaffected. W1 rests on Ford-Roman being a time average at one point, which is true whether or not a pointwise cap exists.

For theories with no positive-dimension scaling limit, nothing read here establishes unboundedness. That class is OPEN, not refuted.

The 'first line' attribution to Ford-Roman is a citation discrepancy. It is recorded, not repaired.
epstein-glaser-jaffe-1965.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS, either of two things: reading the 1965 paper and finding unboundedness proved from the Wightman axioms alone, or the owner sites citing EGJ for nonpositivity and Fewster math-ph/0501073 or the free-field scaling argument for unboundedness.

To WRONG: a finite pointwise lower bound on <T00(x)> for a free field in Hadamard states. C4 rules this out.

1005.0031-properly-traceless.name: Milton: the renormalised EM stress tensor in a source-free cavity is 'properly traceless'

source.located: K. A. Milton, 'Local and Global Casimir Energies: Divergences, Renormalization, and the Coupling to Gravity', arXiv:1005.0031v1 [hep-th], 30 Apr 2010. The phrase is at p.15 line 1, about eq. (58) on p.14. Eq. (58) restates Deutsch & Candelas, Phys. Rev. D 20, 3063 (1979), ref. [61]; DC is pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ. DC's construction was read through its restatement in Miao & Chu, arXiv:1706.09652v3 (2018), eqs. (1.1)-(1.3b) and Tables 1-2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1005.0031 (pp.1, 4, 6, 11-15, 25, 27-28, 30, 39-41, 49, 52) and on 1706.09652 (pp.1-18). In the repo I read tolman.py:170-185, 290-311, 600-630, 950-962, 1125-1140 and 2520-2540. Milton's sentence was read directly. DC 1979, the calculation it comes from, was read only through Milton and Miao-Chu.

1005.0031-properly-traceless.published_statement: Milton 1005.0031 p.14: 'as Deutsch and Candelas [61] showed many years ago, in the neighborhood of a curved surface for conformally invariant theories, <T_mu nu> diverges as eps^-3 ... <T_mu nu> ~ eps^-3 T(3) + eps^-2 T(2) + eps^-1 T(1) (57) ... for the case of a sphere, the leading surface divergence has the form, for conformal fields, for r = a + eps, eps -> 0, <T_mu nu> = (A/eps^3) diag(2/a, 0, a, a sin^2 theta) (58) ... A = 1/720 pi^2 for a scalar field satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions, or A = 1/60 pi^2 for the electromagnetic field satisfying perfect conductor boundary conditions.' p.15: 'Note that (58) is properly traceless. The cubic divergence in the energy density near the surface translates into the quadratic divergence in the energy found for a conducting ball ... the absence of the cubic divergence in <T_rr>.' p.13: for flat surfaces and conformal theories 'those divergences are not present', with Brown-Maclay (49) and the wedge (50)-(52), both traceless. p.15 caution: 'the local vacuum-fluctuation energy density is to a large extent meaningless. It is the global energy, or the force between distinct bodies, that has an unambiguous value.'
published_hypotheses: The claim covers only the LEADING eps^-3 surface divergence of <T_mu nu>. Eq. (57) also has T(2) eps^-2 and T(1) eps^-1 terms, which Milton does not show.
It applies near a curved surface. Eq. (58) is the sphere case, evaluated at r = a + eps (outside the sphere), with eps -> 0.
The field theory is conformally invariant: the conformal scalar (xi = 1/6) or electromagnetism in 4D.
Boundary conditions are ideal: Dirichlet for the scalar, perfect conductor for EM. The value A_EM = 1/(60 pi^2) holds for perfect-conductor boundary conditions.
The background spacetime is flat.
Renormalisation subtracts the no-boundary (Minkowski) value. The local tensor is ambiguous up to the choice of improvement term.

In DC's construction, which Miao-Chu 1706.09652 eq. (1.2) makes explicit, tracelessness (lim <T^i_i> = O(1)) and conservation are IMPOSED on the divergent parts before the coefficient tensors are solved for. 'Properly traceless' is therefore a consistency property of the construction, not an independent finding.
hypothesis_drift: STRENGTHENED from leading order to exact. tolman.py:308-310 reads Milton as saying 'the flat-space trace is exactly zero' for 'the renormalised EM stress tensor in a source-free cavity'. Milton's sentence (p.15) covers only eq. (58), the eps^-3 leading term near a sphere. Computed (rederive B2): if eq. (58) is taken with the metric at r = a + eps, its trace is 2A(-2a + 3eps)/(a^3 eps^2), which tends to -4A/(a^2 eps^2). Only T(2) cancels this, and Milton does not show T(2). The tree's exact claim is still true, by a route computed here that is not Milton's sentence. A1/A2: the Maxwell tensor is traceless as an algebraic identity, for any F and for the symmetric point-split bilinear. C7: the covariant DC/Miao-Chu form is traceless at every r. This is a discrepancy in what the citation covers, not a refutation.

SIDE CHANGED from exterior to interior. Eq. (58) is stated 'for r = a + eps', outside the sphere. tolman.py:606-613 uses it inside the cavity, with eps = a - r. The move is justified by DC's dependence on curvature, restated covariantly in Miao-Chu eq. (1.3a): kbar changes sign across the surface and Tr kbar^2 does not. Computed (rederive D1-D5): inside, u = -2A hbar c/(a eps^3) and p_r = -A hbar c/(a^2 eps^2), and conservation cancels at eps^-3 on both sides. These are exactly the values at tolman.py:609-610. The drift is real, but the tree's use inside the cavity is correct.

DROPPED from this entry's hypothesis list (tolman.py:306-311): PERFECT-CONDUCTOR boundary conditions. They are needed for A_EM = 1/(60 pi^2) and for the eps^-3 profile; Milton p.14 eq. (55) shows that a plasma-model mirror changes the profile. They are NOT needed for tracelessness in the vacuum region, since A1/A2 hold for any mirror. The tree names real mirrors elsewhere (DOCKET 54; the Sopova-Ford K term at tolman.py:1138-1140), so the drop is local to this entry.
DROPPED: 'conformal field' and 'leading order in eps' are not named at tolman.py:306-311. 'No trace anomaly' is named (tolman.py:311, 959-961).

UNNAMED SCOPE CAUTION. Milton p.15 calls the local near-wall stress tensor 'to a large extent meaningless', but tolman.py:600-613 builds its positive-control profile from that local eps^-3 term. Miao-Chu (pp.1, 9) argue the divergence is physical in a true BCFT, while recording DC's view that in a Casimir setup with space on both sides it is an artefact of perfect-conductor boundary conditions. The literature is contested on this point. It is not a fault in the tree's algebra.

FLAT SPACE versus the tree's full-GR embedding. tolman.py joins the flat-space tensor to full GR (V8). In curved spacetime the trace is the Weyl anomaly (Miao-Chu eq. 2.12, Maxwell c = 1/10, a = 31/180). The tree names both 'flat-space' and the anomaly (tolman.py:309, 959-961). An order-of-magnitude ESTIMATE (rederive F; the box-R term is not included) puts the curvature-squared anomaly against |u| at about 6e-90 at eps = 1 fm and 6e-108 at 1 nm, for a = 1 um. This is an estimate, not a bound.

(58), A = 1/60 pi^2 for EM, and 'properly traceless' are all verbatim on pp.14-15. Miao-Chu Table 1 now corroborates the value independently, so the status can move from RECOVERED/SINGLE-SOURCE to READ.

anec-definition.published_statement: Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.28: 'An averaged energy condition is a condition that requires a contraction of the stress tensor of a theory, averaged over a suitable spacetime region, to be non-negative ... Although one could consider many spacetime regions to average over, our discussion will only consider averages along causal geodesics, which is also the most common choice in the literature.' 'For the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) we consider null geodesics gamma with affine parameter lambda. The ANEC then requires that INT_{-inf}^{inf} dlambda T_ab(gamma(lambda)) gamma'^a gamma'^b >= 0 (83) for all inextendible null geodesics when the integral is absolutely convergent. An even weaker condition is the achronal averaged null energy condition (AANEC), which requires the same inequality only for all achronal inextendible null geodesics.' AWEC (81) is the same over inextendible timelike geodesics with proper time. p.29: extensions to non-absolutely-convergent integrals are 'not unique' (Verch (84), Wald-Yurtsever (85)). Table 4: 'tau is an affine parameter along the geodesic'. p.28: T_ab is the classical stress tensor or a renormalised expectation value. Graham-Olum 0705.3193 eq. (1): INT_gamma T_ab k^a k^b over a complete null geodesic with tangent k^a. K&S p.35: Klinkhammer 'showed that negative results can be obtained by integrating along curves which are not geodesics'.
published_hypotheses: H1 CURVE: an inextendible (complete) NULL GEODESIC (K&S eq. 83, Table 4; Graham-Olum eq. 1). Not an arbitrary null curve: Klinkhammer found negative results along non-geodesic curves (K&S p.35).

H2 PARAMETER: integral taken with respect to an AFFINE parameter, contracting the affine tangent. A constant affine rescaling changes the value by a positive factor and leaves only the sign invariant (Burwig-Easson (A9)); 'The factor 1/a(t) is not a convention, but rather the affine weighting' (p.5).
H3 INTEGRAND: T_ab gamma'^a gamma'^b, not rho; for a perfect fluid T_kk = (rho+p)(u.k)^2 (Burwig-Easson (A14)-(A16)).
H4 CONVERGENCE: absolutely convergent integrals; extensions non-unique (K&S p.29).
H5 STRESS TENSOR: classical or renormalised quantum expectation value (K&S p.28); the definition makes no QFT assumption, the theorems do (separate audit).
H6 ACHRONALITY: not part of ANEC; it defines AANEC. Self-consistency is a further strengthening (Graham-Olum Condition 1).

H7 SCOPE OF 'AVERAGED': K&S define averaging over 'a suitable spacetime region', with causal geodesics as the common choice (p.28). DSNEC (2111.05772 p.3) averages over two null directions, a 2D region.
hypothesis_drift: WIDENED -- overturn.py:167 'Every averaged energy condition bounds a WORLDLINE integral: int_line rho dl.' K&S p.28 define averaged conditions over 'a suitable spacetime region' and restrict to causal geodesics by convention. DSNEC (2111.05772 p.3, eq. 54) averages over two null directions and recovers ANEC only as a limit. 'Every' holds for the four conditions of K&S Table 4 (AWEC, ASEC, ANEC, AANEC), not for the family. A null geodesic is also not an observer's worldline.

SUBSTITUTED INTEGRAND (an unstated hypothesis ADDED) -- overturn.py:167 and :191 integrate rho, not T_ab k^a k^b. Computed (Part A): for a static perfect fluid in flat space with k = (1,1,0,0), T_kk = rho + P, and straight null lines are affine with dlambda = dx. So the chord integral equals the flat-space ANEC integral exactly when INT P dl = 0 (dust), and not otherwise. The owner does flag 'ANEC-analogue' (overturn.py:191) and two scope limits (overturn.py:209-213: not a field-equation solution; straight chords, not geodesics), but not the zero-pressure hypothesis.

QUALIFIER DROPPED -- overturn.py:217-218 'ANEC does not forbid this -- it is satisfied and it is not even the right shape of constraint' and overturn.py:660 'Neither the positive mass theorem nor ANEC is doing the work' drop the 'analogue' qualifier of :191 and the dust hypothesis. The conclusion at overturn.py:226 ('Two of the three famous obstructions are not obstructions here') rests on these lines. The chord arithmetic itself is re-derived exactly.

CONTEXT (same passage) -- overturn.py:219-221 contrasts ANEC with Ford-Roman inequalities 'over a sampling region rather than an average along a line'. Those QIs are themselves sampled along timelike worldlines (FFK 2111.05772 p.4: 'Most of these results are for averages over timelike curves'). The operative difference is finite sampling width against a complete line, not region against line.

AFFINE PARAMETER DROPPED -- anec.py:39 states ANEC as 'INTEGRAL <T_kk> dl >= 0', and anec.py:41-48 and 124-126 compute INT T_kk dx with k^t = 1 (k = (1, v+1, 0, 0), anec.py:98-103). Computed (Part C3): on y = 0 the conserved k_t = -(1+v) varies, so k is not affine. The affine tangent is K = k/(1+v) with K^x = 1, so dlambda = dx and the ANEC integral is INT T_kk/(1+v)^2 dx = -0.052410, against anec.py's -0.080665. achronal.py's own affine integrator gives -0.052410 identically. The sign is kept; the magnitude is 35% smaller.

Along a non-affine parameter even the sign is not guaranteed (a toy integral goes from +1/2 to -1/2 under a positive weight). Where checked, the sign survives: y = 0 affine, and y0 = 0.3 on the true geodesic.

later_literature.what: Fixes the definition: inextendible null geodesic, affine parameter, absolute convergence, AANEC as the achronal restriction. Averaging is 'over a suitable spacetime region', with geodesics as the common choice. Records Klinkhammer's negative results along non-geodesic curves.
Self-consistent achronal ANEC (Condition 1): only complete achronal null geodesics, and only in self-consistent semiclassical solutions. The definition in eq. (1) is the same as K&S.

Contradicts only the tree's generalisation at overturn.py:167. DSNEC averages null energy over two null directions (a 2D region) and has a finite bound; SNEC's bound is UV-divergent; ANEC is recovered as a limit (eq. 54). The ANEC definition itself is confirmed (eq. 3).

The affine weighting is load-bearing: in FRW the affine ANEC is INT (rho+p)/a dt, 'not merely ... the coordinate-time integral of rho + p'. Only the sign survives a constant affine rescaling, and T_kk = (rho+p)(u.k)^2. These are the two points where the tree's uses drift.

anec-definition.lacked_data: The ANEC is a DEFINITION (Tipler 1978, Borde 1987, Klinkhammer 1991, as restated by K&S 2020). Its statement contains no measured quantity, so no datum the originators lacked can move it. K&S eq. (83) and Table 4 carry no empirical input. Every later change was conceptual, not driven by data: achronality (Wald-Yurtsever 1991, Graham-Olum 2007), self-consistency (Penrose-Sorkin-Woolgar 1993, Graham-Olum 2007), non-unique lim-inf extensions (K&S p.29), and spacetime-region smearing (DSNEC 2021). None of these alters the definition; the last shows that 'averaged energy condition' is wider than 'worldline integral'. What was missing here is on the tree's side, not the authors': anec.py lacked the affine normalisation and, off-axis, the geodesic; overturn.py lacked the pressure term. Supplying them (computed here) leaves every sign the tree asserts unchanged. It changes the magnitudes: -0.0807 becomes -0.0524 at y = 0, and -0.0946 becomes -0.0603 at y0 = 0.3 on the true geodesic. For this result M's hypothesis is not supported: no external datum moved, and nothing in the published definition is inaccurate or incomplete as published.
anec-definition.grade_evidence: The published definition (K&S 2003.01815 eq. 83) stands as read and needs no data. The tree uses it on a wider class than it covers, in three computed ways. (1) overturn.py:167 'every averaged energy condition bounds a worldline integral' holds for the four conditions in K&S Table 4, not for the family (K&S p.28 'suitable spacetime region'; DSNEC 2111.05772 averages over two null directions). (2) overturn.py's straight-chord INT rho dl equals the flat-space ANEC integral only for zero-pressure matter (T_kk = rho + P, Part A). That hypothesis is not named at overturn.py:209-213, and the 'analogue' qualifier is dropped at overturn.py:217-218 and :660. (3) anec.py's INT T_kk dx is not the ANEC integral. On y = 0 it is non-affine (affine value -0.052410 against -0.080665, Part C3, confirmed by achronal.py's integrator). For y != 0 the lines are not geodesics (|A^y| = 0.60 at y = 0.3, Part C2). So the magnitudes at index3.py:381 are not ANEC values. The grade is not WRONG because no sign the tree asserts is refuted: the y = 0 affine ANEC and the y0 = 0.3 true-geodesic ANEC are both negative, and the chord arithmetic is exact. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT because no measured datum enters.
anec-definition.what_would_change_the_grade: To reach STANDS: overturn.py would name the zero-pressure hypothesis at the chord claim and restrict 'every averaged energy condition' to the causal-geodesic conditions. anec.py and index3.py would quote the affine geodesic integral (-0.0524 at y = 0, or achronal.py's geodesic values) and state the sign, not the coordinate-line magnitudes, as the ANEC finding. To reach WRONG, one of two things would have to be shown, and neither was found here. The first is an affine, geodesic ANEC integral of the tree's configuration that comes out non-negative where the tree asserts a violation. The second is an equation of state for the two-zone profile under which the true null-geodesic ANEC is negative where the tree says 'satisfied'. Reading Tipler 1978, Borde 1987 or Klinkhammer 1991 directly could refine the attribution only, not the definition.

clock-accuracy-1e-18.published_statement: Godun et al. 2014 (1407.0164v2 p.1): 'we present the first direct measurement of the ratio between the E3 and E2 optical transition frequencies in 171Yb+, with fractional uncertainty 3 x 10^-16'; p.3: 'nu_E3/nu_E2 = 0.932 829 404 530 964 65(31)'; Table I TOTAL for the ratio 3.36e-16 (systematic subtotal 3.29e-16, statistical 0.68e-16, dominated by the residual quadrupole shift of E2, 2.97e-16). p.4: 'Dependence on mu-dot arises through the nuclear magnetic moment and is negligible for optical transitions (the sensitivity coefficient B_E3 = B_E2 = 0).' The tree's '1e-18' has no published source: address.py:37-39 says only 'heading below 1e-18'; excite.py:397-400 declares CLOCK_ACCURACY_FIXTURE = 1e-18 an ORDER.
published_hypotheses: Godun: a single 171Yb+ ion, E3 and E2 interrogated interleaved on ~100 ms timescale, so gravitational redshift and time dilation are common-mode in the RATIO (p.2)
Godun: ac Stark shift of E3 removed by extrapolation between two probe powers, assuming constant beam pointing over the ~3 s cycle and a known power ratio kappa (sigma_kappa/kappa = 2e-4) (p.2)
Godun: quadrupole shift averaged out by three nominally orthogonal field directions; residual set by non-orthogonality, simulated (p.2)
Godun: BBR shift from experimental differential polarizabilities at 294.5 +- 2 K (p.2)
Godun: the constraints on alpha-dot and mu-dot assume local position invariance and linear time variation (p.4)
Godun: B_E3 = B_E2 = 0 is 'negligible', not zero -- dependence on mu only through the nuclear magnetic moment (p.4)

Current literature (2512.07346 p.8; 2512.21428 p.2): a stated systematic uncertainty is 'validated' only by a comparison; the roadmap criteria are <= 2e-18 evaluated and <= 5e-18 agreement; repeatability below 1e-17 'remains an outstanding issue for clock comparisons' (2512.21428 p.4)

A transported comparison is a different measurement; the best transportable figure seen is 2.1e-18 systematic (2507.14030, abstract snippet only). ADDED, carried unflagged to a different kind of clock: address.py:1161-1178 and 1537-1551 apply the same 1e-18 to a Th-229 NUCLEAR clock (eps_detectable_th229(1e-18, ...)), giving eps_det = 2.86e-24 and 'EIGHT ORDERS BETTER' (address.py:286). The READ state of Th-229 (2406.18719 p.8) is nu_Th/nu_Sr = 4.707 072 615 078(5) = 1.06e-12, 'Systematic uncertainty of this frequency ratio will be explored in future studies.' The fixture sits six orders past the measured nuclear state; the tree labels Flambaum's COEFFICIENT an ORDER (address.py:292-293) but not the ACCURACY applied to it. At the READ precision eps_det(Th-229) = 3.04e-18, worse than the electronic courier at the fixture.

WEAKENED qualifier: address.py:37-38 calls the optical/optical ratio 'the sharpest measurement in physics'; the nearest source wording (2512.21428 p.2) is 'the most precise measurements of any physical quantity (other than symmetry tests, e.g. [27])' -- the tree drops 'other than symmetry tests'.

LITERAL SCOPE: address.py:37-39 says an optical-to-optical frequency RATIO is 'heading below 1e-18'. As of the READ literature no inter-species optical ratio is below 1e-18 (best 2.2e-18, Al+/Sr, 2512.21428; 2.9e-18 Sr+/Yb+, 2603.23446). The tree's own (not external) 'coefficient exactly 1' (excite.py:397-401, address.py:252, 740-742) is exact only for an infinite-mass nucleus: with the reduced-mass Rydberg it is 1 - x(1-f)/(1+x), x = m_e/M (sympy, section G): 1 - 5.1e-4 (hydrogen, H2), 1 - 5.9e-6 (87Sr, H2). Recorded as a discrepancy in the tree's wording, not a refutation; it moves eps_det by at most 0.051%.

gr-qc/0003025-wormhole-branch.published_statement: Abstract: 'Among these classical solutions we find an entire branch of traversable wormholes for every xi > 0 ... For these traversable wormholes to exist we demonstrate that the scalar field must reach trans-Planckian values somewhere in the geometry.' Sect. 4 (p.16): 'In all these solutions the scalar field has to reach absolute values above ~ m_p/sqrt(xi), where m_p is the Planck mass. That is, either the scalar field acquires trans-Planckian values or the curvature coupling constant xi must become disturbingly large.' The exact form: the wormholes are the chi = pi/3 subfamily. They are continued through Phi = -1/sqrt(6 xi), where Phi = phi/sqrt(6 kappa), which is the surface phi^2 = kappa/xi with kappa = 1/(8 pi G) (eqs. 3.17, 4.41-4.43). Supporting ANEC analysis, eq. (2.11): if xi < 0, or if xi > 0 with phi^2 < kappa/xi everywhere, then 'ANEC is satisfied'. If phi^2 > kappa/xi somewhere, there is only 'the possibility of ANEC violations'.
published_hypotheses: Classical GR plus one real scalar, with action (2.1) carrying the term -(1/2) xi R phi^2. Signature (-+++), kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N)
MASSLESS, V = 0, for every exact solution. BV state that adding a Higgs mass 'results in analytically intractable equations'
Static and spherically symmetric configurations only
xi > 0 in BV's sign convention, where conformal coupling is xi = +1/6
The wormholes lie only in the chi = pi/3 subfamily, generated from the Fisher/JNW minimal solution by the Bekenstein conformal map (3.17)
For 0 < xi <= 1/6 there is an extra condition on the integration constant: Phi_+ > exp(-sqrt((1-6xi)/(6xi)) pi/2), eq. (4.43), or its twin (3.39). There is no such condition for xi > 1/6
Traversable is meant geometrically: two asymptotically flat regions, with no horizon and no naked singularity
The ANEC argument assumes a complete null geodesic with smooth asymptotics, so boundary terms at infinity vanish. V drops out of the null contraction
Stability is NOT addressed (footnote 5). The effective Newton constant changes sign between the two mouths (eqs. 4.47, 5.51)
'~ m_p/sqrt(xi)' is an order-of-magnitude statement. The exact threshold is sqrt(kappa/xi)

later_literature.what: They re-derive BV's branch, with the same existence condition, and prove it unstable for ANY xi > 0 under spherically symmetric perturbations. The cause is a -1/(4x^2) well at the sphere where f = 0, which gives unbounded growth rates. They assume V = 0 and a static background.

They prove there is no static or dynamic wormhole in any scalar-tensor theory where f > 0 everywhere and the scalar is not a ghost. This holds for any potential and without symmetry assumptions. For f = kappa - xi phi^2, the condition f > 0 is exactly BV's gate condition, so the refusal is confirmed on a larger class than BV's. They also find that wormholes with an f < 0 region are generically unstable, with the remote mouth in an antigravitating region.
Read to check the tree's comparison, not because it bears on BV. Their conformal coupling is at xi = -1/6 (footnote 1), so their xi ~ 1.7e4 has the opposite sign to BV's xi.
Later work uses the BV solutions as given (geodesics, orbit stability). The sweep found no refutation.

gr-qc/0003025-wormhole-branch.lacked_data: In 2000 BV had no Higgs discovery ('we do not (currently) have direct proof'), no stability analysis, no Higgs-inflation xi and only a weaker PPN bound. Everything that came later was checked against the result. The gate depends on no measured datum except G. It is a closed-form identity (checks C1-C5), and Bronnikov-Starobinsky later extended it to any potential and any symmetry, so later data cannot move it. The existence of the branch is unchanged as mathematics, but later work narrows its physical standing: it is unstable, and one mouth has negative G_eff. The measured Higgs mass cuts against M's hypothesis here. It confirms the Higgs has a potential, which puts it outside BV's V = 0 class. Whether a Higgs-sourced branch exists with the measured potential is OPEN; it was not computed here. The one datum the tree compares against, Higgs-inflation xi, turns out when read at source to lie on BV's no-wormhole side. The part of the result the refusal rests on needs no data and has been strengthened, not weakened, by later work.
gr-qc/0003025-wormhole-branch.grade_evidence: BV's statement and the quoted text are READ verbatim. Every closed-form step of the gate re-derives (20 of 20 checks, sympy and z3), and no datum moves it: xi_required is stable to 5e-5. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree uses the result on a larger class than BV proved. BV's existence result covers a massless, static, spherically symmetric scalar. higgs.py:15-17 and 128 apply it to the Higgs, which has a potential, and BV themselves call that case 'analytically intractable'. The canonical list also omits 'massless'. This does NOT move the tree's verdict, which refuses. The gate does not depend on the potential (C2, C3), and gr-qc/0612032 extends it further. The 'escape' is narrowed again by gr-qc/0201083, which finds it unstable for every xi > 0. Separately, the tree's '28 orders below' at higgs.py:150-151 compares across opposite sign conventions: in BV's convention Higgs inflation sits at xi = -1.76e4, where there is no ANEC violation at all. That strengthens the refusal and is recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation. Nothing here is WRONG.

It would also become STANDS if a wormhole branch were exhibited for the Higgs potential, by numerically integrating the static nonminimal system with V = lambda(phi^2 - v^2)^2/4. kuo-ford-1993-measure.published_statement: (3.2) 'Delta(x) = | (<:T00^2(x):> - <:T00(x):>^2) / <:T00^2(x):> | . The local energy density fluctuations are small when Delta << 1, which we take to be a measure of the validity of the semiclassical theory. Note that we have used normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state to define the various operators.' (3.43), in the Casimir section III.C with rho = <:T00:>_C: 'Delta' = (<:T00^2(x):> - rho^2)/rho^2 = (1/8)[(rho+xi1+xi2+xi3)^2 + ...], xi_i = p_i/rho'. As printed, the bracket's leading term reads rho; for the stated normalisation it must be 1. (3.44) 'Delta' = Delta/(1-Delta), Delta = Delta'/(1+Delta') ... an equivalent measure'. (3.45) 'Delta' >= 1/2, Delta >= 1/3 ... this bound is independent of the details of the geometry of the boundaries'; for the periodic case Delta' = 6, Delta = 6/7. Sec. V: 'The generalization of this analysis to curved spacetime backgrounds will require a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such spacetimes, which has not yet been developed. ... If we were to average fields over finite space or time intervals, then we could define a quantity similar to Delta without invoking normal ordering ... [this] introduces an arbitrary length or time scale into the problem.'
published_hypotheses: K1 Flat (Minkowski) background: 'restricted to a flat spacetime background' (Sec. V).
K2 Free massless, minimally coupled scalar field, Lagrangian (2.1).
K3 Normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state, for both <:T00:> and <:T00^2:>.
K4 Coincidence limit of the 00 component of (3.1). The measure is POINTWISE: KF reject averaging in Sec. V because it introduces an arbitrary scale.

K5 For (3.43)/(3.45): Wick's theorem under the stated condition phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0 (the Minkowski and Casimir vacua, i.e. pure vacuum-like quasifree states), with a diagonal two-point matrix (only the G_AA^2 terms appear in (3.40)).
K6 rho != 0. (3.44) tacitly needs <:T00^2:> >= rho^2 > 0; KF do not state this.
K7 The curved-space remark is time-indexed: 'has not yet been developed' as of 1993.

source.located: Classic: sqrt 2 is irrational (Euclid, Elements X, and the Pythagorean/Aristotle tradition). It has no arXiv copy, so the original is NAMED-NOT-READ. That gives Tennenbaum's descent proof from the 1950s and cites Conway & Shipman, Math. Intelligencer 35(3):2-7, 2013, which is not on arXiv (NAMED-NOT-READ). The tree's consequence 'causal but not stably causal' was checked against Minguzzi & Sanchez, arXiv:gr-qc/0609119v3: Def. 3.52 p.37, Prop. 3.54 p.37, and Thm. 3.56 p.38, which states that stable causality is equivalent to having a time function (Hawking 1968).

irrationality-sqrt2-degenerate-span.published_statement: arXiv:2508.08267 p.5, restating Tennenbaum: 'By the Carpets Theorem, the uncarpeted area (2 squares) equals the doubly carpeted area (1 square). Because these squares have integer side lengths, this "smallest" case is not the smallest, leading to a contradiction, implying sqrt 2 is irrational.' p.2 says the proof 'hinges only on the well-ordering axiom of positive integers and on the Carpets Theorem'. The algebra behind it (re-derived here): if a^2 = 2b^2 with a, b positive integers, then (2b-a)^2 = 2(a-b)^2 with 0 < a-b < b, which contradicts minimality. Stable causality, gr-qc/0609119 Def. 3.52: '(M,g) is stably causal if ... (i) There exists g~ such that g < g~ and g~ is causal'. Thm 3.56: stably causal <=> admits a time function <=> admits a temporal function.
published_hypotheses: a and b are positive integers, and the positive integers are well-ordered, so a smallest counterexample exists
The Carpets Theorem. Algebraically this is the identity (2b-a)^2 - 2(a-b)^2 = 2b^2 - a^2
The consequence the tree uses: for integers (m,n) != (0,0), m s + n = 0 exactly when s = -n/m is rational
Stable causality (Minguzzi-Sanchez Def 3.52): some Lorentzian metric g~ with strictly wider cones is causal. This means any such g~, not only translation-invariant ones

source.located: Bennett, Brassard, Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres, Wootters, PRL 70, 1895 (1993) [teleportation; no arXiv copy]; Bennett, Bernstein, Popescu, Schumacher, PRA 53, 2046 (1996), quant-ph/9511030 [ebit consumption, non-increase of expected entanglement under local operations, asymptotic reversibility for pure states]; Nielsen, PRL 83, 436 (1999), quant-ph/9811053 [exact single-copy pure-state LOCC conversion iff majorization]; Horodecki^4, RMP 81, 865 (2009), quant-ph/0702225 [restates the 1993 protocol in eqs. entanglement-consumed-locc-monotonicity.published_statement: BBPS 1996 (quant-ph/9511030) p.2: 'In [4] [Bennett et al. 1993] ... it is shown that the consumption of one shared ebit, together with the transmission of a two-bit classical message, can be substituted for the transmission of one qubit.' p.6: 'neither the measurement of k nor any other local processing by one or both parties can increase the expected entropy of entanglement ... though Alice and Bob cannot by local actions increase their expected entanglement, they can gamble with it.' Abstract and p.16: concentration and dilution 'asymptotically conserve entropy of entanglement' for PURE states; for mixed states reversibility was unknown in 1996. p.15: teleportation 'has the effect of destroying the entanglement between A and C while creating the desired entangled state'. Horodecki review p.57 eq. (150): 'Monotonicity under LOCC: Entanglement cannot increase under local operations and classical communication', E(Lambda(rho)) <= E(rho). p.51: 'In bipartite states we cannot transform separable state into entangled one by LOCC at all'. p.11: after teleportation 'Alice has just one of the Bell states ... no information about the state |q> is left with her.' Nielsen 1999 Thm 1: |psi> -> |phi> by LOCC iff lambda_psi is majorized by lambda_phi (exact, deterministic, single copy, pure states).
published_hypotheses: Teleportation (1993, as restated): an UNKNOWN qubit, one maximally entangled pair shared in advance, a Bell-basis measurement by Alice, two classical bits sent, a Pauli correction by Bob; fidelity 1 on every outcome
Ebit accounting (BBPS): pure states; entropy of entanglement as the measure; 'consumption of one ebit' refers to faithful transmission of an arbitrary qubit

Monotonicity (BBPS p.6; Horodecki eq. 150): operations restricted to LOCC. The strong form holds only ON AVERAGE over outcomes, since a single outcome can exceed the starting value (the 'gamble'). The axiom is the state-level form E(Lambda(rho)) <= E(rho)
Conservation/reversibility (BBPS abstract, p.16): ASYMPTOTIC (n -> infinity), PURE states only, vanishing error
Nielsen 1999: exact, deterministic, single-copy, pure-state LOCC conversions ('We do not consider approximate transformations')

The sources state a NON-INCREASE (monotonicity) law, not conservation. Computed (rederive part C): for a pure input qubit, entanglement across the Alice|Bob cut goes 1 -> 0, because Alice's leftover Bell pair on AA' is local to her. Only when the teleported qubit is itself half of a pair R-A does it stay 1 -> 1, moved to R-B by entanglement swapping. The literature has conservation only asymptotically for pure states (BBPS) or with an entanglement battery (2405.10599); in general it is irreversible (2111.02438). entanglement-consumed-locc-monotonicity.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. The results are theorems of finite-dimensional quantum mechanics under the LOCC restriction, and no measured datum enters them, so the 1993/1996 authors lacked no datum that could move the conclusion. What came later is mathematics, not data. (i) Nielsen 1999 turned the exact single-copy statement into a theorem; it confirms the result and is used here. (ii) Irreversibility for mixed states (Vidal-Cirac, as cited in 2111.02438; Lami-Regula) shows that no general 'conservation' of entanglement exists. That bears on the tree's wording, not on consumption. (iii) Battery and catalysis frameworks (2405.10599) recover a conservation-like law only by allowing operations beyond LOCC. Evidence either way: nothing later leaves 'exact teleportation of an unknown qubit through one ebit leaves zero shared entanglement, and LOCC cannot restore it' anything but intact, and nothing supports the word 'conservation' outside the asymptotic pure-state or battery settings. The premise that could fail is the LOCC restriction itself, since a quantum channel would restore entanglement. That is a hypothesis of the theorem, not a datum.
entanglement-consumed-locc-monotonicity.grade_evidence: The theorem the tree needs stands and is re-derived here. Exact (F = 1), deterministic teleportation of an arbitrary qubit through one pure ebit leaves exactly 0 shared entanglement on every outcome (sympy factorisation). Exact teleportation needs a maximal channel and consumes all of it (z3 over Nielsen's majorization theorem: unsat at residual dimensions 2-4, vacuity guard sat). LOCC cannot re-entangle the resulting product state (Horodecki p.51; numeric check). The declared constants 1.0 and 0.0 agree with the computation. The grade is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree uses the result on a larger class than the sources support. (1) transit.py:27-28 and :221-222 say 'you could not keep it open if you wanted to' without the exact-fidelity hypothesis; computed, at F = 2/3 the pair survives intact. specthm.py:1186-1187 records that R11's fidelity is not yet fixed while specthm.py:1209 binds CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE on it. (2) transit.py drops the unknown-state hypothesis that specthm.py:1188-1190 and :1212 keep, and ledger.py M-S1A-P5 (:1357-1365) quotes the flag with no hypothesis. ism-density-1-per-cc.published_statement:
Ferriere 2001 p.5: 'in the vicinity of the Sun, its density varies from ~1.5e-26 g cm^-3 in the hot medium to ~2e-20 - 2e-18 g cm^-3 in the densest molecular regions, with an average of about 2.7e-24 g cm^-3 ... This mass density ... corresponds to approximately one hydrogen atom per cubic centimeter.'

Ferriere Table I gives n as the TRUE density of H nuclei near the Sun: molecular 1e2-1e6; cold atomic 20-50; WARM ATOMIC 0.2-0.5; warm ionized 0.2-0.5; hot ionized ~0.0065 cm^-3. Mass densities include 70.4% H, 28.1% He and 1.5% heavier elements, with rho = 1.42 m_P n (Fig.2 caption).

Crawford 2011 Table 4:
- CHISM: n_HI 0.19+-0.04, n_e 0.07+-0.02, n_Htot 0.26+-0.05.
- LIC: n_HI >= 0.09, n_e 0.12+-0.04.
- G cloud (alpha Cen): n_HI >= 0.10.
- Conservative Icarus design range: n_Htot 0.15-0.43, n_e 0.05-0.21.
- Local Bubble: n_Htot ~ n_e 0.005-0.04.

Crawford's conclusion (2): 'assume the lowest likely density if considering braking devices which rely on transferring momentum ... to the surrounding medium (such as magsails)'.

CODATA 2022: m_p = 1.672 621 925 95(52)e-27 kg.
published_hypotheses: Ferriere's ~1 H/cm^3 is a SPACE AVERAGE near the Galactic midplane at the solar circle, smoothed over all phases (including molecular clouds at 1e2-1e6 cm^-3). It is not the density of any one phase.
Ferriere's mass density includes He and metals: rho = 1.42 m_P n_H.
The WNM's TRUE density is 0.2-0.5 cm^-3 (Ferriere Table I), from comparing 21-cm emission with absorption (Dickey & Lockman 1990; Kulkarni & Heiles 1987).

Local-cloud densities (Crawford; Frisch-Mueller) come from UV absorption columns toward nearby stars plus in-situ heliospheric neutral and pickup-ion data. N(HI)/distance is a rigorous LOWER limit. The Sun sits in or near the LIC; alpha Cen A/B sit in the G cloud.

Momentum-braking devices (magsails) couple only to the IONISED component: n_p 0.05-0.20 cm^-3 in the warm local clouds and ~0.005 in the Local Bubble (Gros 2017 sec.2.1-2.2; Crawford sec.3 and conclusion 3).
The target star may lie in Local Bubble material, n ~ 0.005 cm^-3, rather than in a cloud (Crawford conclusion 3).

ism-density-1-per-cc.lacked_data:
Tested M's hypothesis. The tree cites no source, so what its authors had is the textbook ~1 H/cm^3 average. Ferriere 2001 already qualifies that figure in the same paragraph: it is an all-phase average, and the WNM is 0.2-0.5.

What a user of 1 cm^-3 most plausibly lacked are the LOCAL measurements, all available since 2008:
- UV absorption columns toward alpha Cen and other nearby stars (Redfield & Linsky 2008, via Crawford Table 4);
- in-situ pickup-ion and neutral-He densities at the heliosphere (Bzowski et al. 2008; Slavin & Frisch 2008);
- CII* electron densities (Redfield & Falcon 2008).

These data change one conclusion. On the ion density the magsail floor rises 4.8-200x, so 'inside 810 AU, comfortably within a target system' does not hold, and on the tree's drag law a Local-Bubble target cannot be reached by ISM braking at all.

Evidence the other way: every lower density only strengthens stock.py's conclusion ('the diffuse medium is the one that fails'), and the space-averaged number is not wrong; Ferriere's value stands. Nothing here shows earlier physicists were wrong. The external result is intact; the tree applied it to a narrower situation than the one it describes.

svz-1978.published_statement: As Hill-Solon 1409.8290 eq. (39) restates it (READ by the sibling audit): <O'_Q>/m_N = (1/(3 beta_0^(nf))){2 - 2 lambda} + (alpha_s^(nf+1)(mu_Q)/pi)(1/(3 beta_0^(nf)))^2 {57/2 - 321 lambda/2 + 8 n_f} + O(alpha_s^2). At n_f = 3 its O(alpha_s^0) term is SVZ's f_TQ = (2/27)(1 - lambda), with lambda = sum over u, d, s of f_Tq. Eq. (101): 'the leading-order alpha_s result is well-known from Ref. [81]', which is SVZ. EOS as the tree quotes it (massform.py:1353-1354): 'f_N/m_N = sum_{q=u,d,s} f_Tq alpha_3q/m_q + (2/27) f_TG sum_{q=c,b,t} alpha_3q/m_q ... f_TG = 1 - sum_{q=u,d,s} f_Tq (12)'.
published_hypotheses: Leading order in alpha_s. The heavy-quark theorem is m_Q QbarQ -> -(2/3)(alpha_s/8pi) G^2, which equals -(alpha_s/12pi) G^2, with the one-loop beta coefficient b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3 (Hill-Solon eq. (39) at O(alpha_s^0); eq. (101)).
Heavy-quark limit: m_Q >> Lambda_QCD, with power corrections O(1/m_Q) dropped. Hill-Solon do not estimate O(1/m_c).
Three light flavours u, d, s define f_TG = 1 - sum over u, d, s of f_Tq (EOS eq. (12) as quoted). c, b and t are decoupled in sequence.

The result is a forward nucleon matrix element of the QCD trace, m_N = <N|theta^mu_mu|N>, in QCD only. It is a coupling (the Higgs-nucleon scalar coupling), not a partition of the mass: the source context is Higgs-nucleon interaction and dark-matter scattering.

svz-1978.lacked_data:
What SVZ (1978) lacked: (i) higher-order QCD coefficients, namely decoupling to O(alpha_s^3) (Chetyrkin-Kniehl-Steinhauser 1997) and the f_Q series (Hill-Solon 2014); (ii) any non-perturbative charm matrix element (lattice f_Tc from 2012 on, including ETM 19's 107(22) MeV); (iii) precise light sigma terms (FLAG 2024, whose two averages are still 2.7 sigma apart). EOS (2008) lacked (ii) and the Hill-Solon series.

Does having them change the conclusion? The leading-order relation is a correct leading-order theorem: it is re-derived here from the anomaly and the matching, and no counterexample exists. Going beyond leading order raises each f_TQ by 2-9% and the coupling sum by 3.3% (2+1+1) and 3.8% (2+1), and it breaks the exact (1 - f_l) factorisation. The lattice charm value sits 2.05 sigma above leading order. So the new data narrow the relation's exactness to its leading-order, heavy-quark-limit class but do not refute it.

No conclusion the tree rests on it moves. The coupling rows are CONTESTED and never added to the READ rows (massform.py:354-356). Every coupling-row central value stays below one half: 0.3066 becomes 0.3169, and the all-rows reading 0.3090 becomes 0.3193. For this result M's hypothesis holds in its weak form (the authors lacked data that moves the numbers) and fails in its strong form (nothing here makes the relation wrong).

klinkhamer-manton-1984.published_statement: As restated in Rubakov-Shaposhnikov eq. (2.11) and quoted at massform.py:1104-1107 (not re-read this run): "E_sph = (2 m_W / alpha_W) B(m_H/m_W), where m_H is the mass of the Higgs boson. The function B(m_H/m_W) has been evaluated numerically [32]; it varies from 1.56 to 2.72 as m_H/m_W varies from zero to infinity. So, the height of the barrier in the electroweak theory is of order 10 TeV." Reference [32] is Klinkhamer & Manton, PRD 30, 2212.
published_hypotheses: Classical field theory at tree level: a static solution of the classical Yang-Mills-Higgs equations, with no loop or quantum corrections.
Bosonic sector only: an SU(2) gauge field plus one Higgs doublet; fermions are ignored.
theta_W = 0 (pure SU(2), with the U(1)_Y field dropped). This is KM's setting as it is generally restated; the RS96 sentence the tree quotes does not state it.
A static, spherically symmetric (hedgehog) ansatz with two radial profiles f(xi) and h(xi), where xi = g v r and f(0)=h(0)=0, f(inf)=h(inf)=1.
Potential V = lambda(Phi^+Phi - v^2/2)^2, so the one free parameter is lambda/g^2 = (m_H/m_W)^2/8. m_H was unknown in 1984, which is why the result is a function B rather than a number.
Reading the sphaleron energy as the barrier height assumes the sphaleron is the lowest saddle. That holds below the bisphaleron onset at large m_H, but the quoted sentence does not say so.

klinkhamer-manton-1984.lacked_data: In 1984 KM lacked m_H, which stayed unknown until 2012. They absorbed that by design, giving B as a function of m_H/m_W. They also lacked a precise m_W (the W was found in 1983) and a percent-level sin^2 theta_W, and set theta_W = 0. m_t did not matter at tree level. With today's data, the measured m_H puts B at the computed 1.9163, which gives E_sph = 9.083 TeV. That lies inside the bracket and agrees with the two measured-m_H values the tree READ (9.08 and 9.11). Every current m_W, the contested CDF 2022 value included, moves E_sph by at most 0.30%, and theta_W != 0 moves it by about -1%. So for this result the evidence runs against M's hypothesis: no datum the authors lacked moves the conclusion that E_sph is 9-10 TeV, about 3.2e3 times the rest energy of 3 baryons. What did turn up is a computed numerical discrepancy in the endpoint values (1.56/2.72 against 1.520/2.706). It touches only the unphysical limits m_H -> 0 and m_H -> infinity, and it is not a data gap.

gklm-eq38.published_statement: GKLM p.12: 'Assuming that light travels on the brane with speed c while a bulk field propagates with speed c+Delta c, the velocity bound (6) directly translates to Delta c/c = gamma - 1 (38)'. Bound (6), p.2: 'bulk causality: |x'| <= gamma t' ... The bulk bound is generically saturated at late times (large t')'. The datum quoted beside it is GW170817/GRB 170817A [17]: '-3 x 10^-15 <= Delta c/c <= +7 x 10^-16 (39)'. The hedge, word for word: 'If we entertain the possibility that these are bulk degrees of freedom, the bounds on brane velocity become very strict.' Here 'these' means the SN1987A antineutrinos and the gravitational waves of the preceding sentences. GKLM print no numerical bound on beta.
published_hypotheses: H1 flat bulk: d-dimensional Minkowski space with ONE spatial dimension compactified on a circle, z ~ z + 2 pi R (eq. 1, M4 x S1). No bulk curvature and no warping.

H2 the brane is a test hyperplane at z' = 0 moving at constant beta purely along the compact direction (z = beta t in the preferred frame; eqs. 2-4). It is untilted, spanning all non-compact directions, and its induced metric is exactly Minkowski.

H3 the observer is at rest in the brane frame (t', x'), with no velocity along the brane relative to the preferred frame. This is GKLP's B = 0; GKLP 2208.09014 eq. 20 says: 'For B = 0, this reduces to the result v = gamma found in [1]'.
H4 light is confined to the brane and travels at c there ('Assuming that light travels on the brane with speed c').
H5 the messenger is a bulk field that propagates causally in the bulk (free and linear; a Green's-function analysis).
H6 late times or high momentum: bound (6) is 'generically saturated at late times', and KK modes reach v_g -> gamma only as |k'| -> infinity (eq. 37).
H7 whether neutrinos or gravitons ARE bulk degrees of freedom is entertained, not asserted ('If we entertain the possibility').
H8 brane-localized matter 'would presumably respect' worldvolume Lorentz symmetry (p.3). This is a presumption, not a theorem.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H3 (B = 0). At branelink.py:60-62, :172 (BETA_BOUND_CONDITIONAL_ON = 'the graviton being a bulk degree of freedom'), :170 (GW170817_BOUNDS = "beta (the brane's speed through S^1), not B") and :303 (BETA_MAX '# conditional on a bulk graviton'), the beta bound carries the bulk-graviton condition only. GKLM's eq. (38) is the B = 0 case. When B != 0, GKLP eq. (22) makes the GW excess d*F(B, direction), so GW170817 bounds a combination that depends on B and on direction, not beta alone. COMPUTED (rederive C7): at the tree's own CMB-dipole B (Gamma-1 = 7.6161e-7), beta lies in [3.7370e-8, 3.7463e-8], a +-0.12% spread that does not matter. At the tree's own escape value B = 0.999387630, the backward-held beta is 2.1380e-6, which is 57.1x BETA_MAX. The tree's escape function b_for_saving (branelink.py:275-281, 'backward excess held at d') already includes this B-dependence. So this is a missing condition in the stated bound, not a numerical error at B = 0.

DROPPED the 'untilted' part of H2, at branelink.py:60-62 ('brane moving through S^1 at beta'). Polychronakos arXiv:2210.11497 eq. (5.3) gives c_phi = 1 + (alpha cos phi + beta)^2/2. For a tilt-like brane (|beta| < alpha) some direction has c_phi = 1 (rederive C8b), so a single GW event need not bound beta. In his words: 'unless we happen to live in a tiltlike braneworld and the relative position of the binary star happened to be quite close to the direction phi_o'.

NOT NAMED at the owner sites: H4 (light confined to the brane, travelling at c). branelink.py:60-62 and :83-86 name only the graviton's status, while GKLM state H4 explicitly as the premise of eq. (38).

NOT NAMED: H1 (flat bulk, a single S^1, a test brane, no backreaction) and H5 (a free linear bulk field). branelink.py:60-62 applies eq. (38) to 'the graviton' without the flat M4 x S1 and test-brane scope that GKLM derive it on.

WEAKENED, BUT HARMLESS: H6. The tree writes '=' (branelink.py:61-62), as GKLM do, although GKLM derive it from a bound that is saturated at late times. RE-DERIVED (C2, C3): for the massless zero mode, omega' = gamma|k'| holds EXACTLY at every k. The image-envelope front deficit at 26 Mpc is at most 7.7e-54 even for R = 1 mm, so for GW170817 the '=' is exact far below the size of the datum. It is recorded as a named hypothesis and does not move the conclusion.

INHERITED BUT NOT NAMED: the 7e-16 carries its own hypotheses (1710.05834 Sec. 4.1): the GW peak and the first photons were emitted simultaneously, so no photons came before the merger, and D = 26 Mpc, the lower end of the 90% GW distance interval. branelink.py:60-62, through manyc.py:68-69 (GW170817_BOUND_HI = +7e-16), carries the number but not these conditions.

GKLM p.3 say only that brane-localized matter 'would presumably respect' the would-be Lorentz symmetry. Kabat & Nomura arXiv:2309.05759 show that bulk loops with non-zero winding generate UV-finite Lorentz-violating terms in the brane effective action, and branelink.py:96-97 itself computes such a loop-induced SME coefficient (|c| <= 6.37e-64). gklm-eq38.lacked_data:
What GKLM had in July 2022: the GW170817/GRB 170817A bound as published in 2017 (26 Mpc, 0-10 s window), the SN1987A neutrino bounds, and no measurement of any observer velocity B along the brane.

What came later, or was not used:
(a) The tighter host distance, about 40.7 Mpc (Cantiello 2018, NAMED-NOT-READ). It predates GKLM, who simply quoted LVC's conservative figure. It TIGHTENS the bound to d = 4.15e-16 and beta = 2.88e-8, so it cannot weaken the tree's conclusion.
(b) GKLP's dependence on B and Polychronakos's dependence on tilt. These are theory, not data. They show that the single-event bound on beta holds only for B = 0 and zero tilt, and the tree names neither condition.
(c) I read no second GW-GRB event, so the one 2017 emission-time assumption behind 7e-16 still stands. An exotic emission window changes the figure 54x in d (7.4x in beta).

M's hypothesis, tested for this result: eq. (38) did not suffer from missing data. It is a kinematic identity, and I re-derived it exactly for the massless zero mode. The one datum that moved did so in the conservative direction and does not change the conclusion. What the literature lacked then and still lacks is B (and any tilt). The tree already names B as unmeasured for O7; it also conditions BETA_MAX. Evidence on both sides is recorded, and nothing in the data refutes eq. (38).
gklm-eq38.grade_evidence:
Eq. (38) as published is exact, and I re-derived it with sympy (26/26 PASS). The image-envelope front reaches |x'| = gamma t' with a computed deficit of at most 7.7e-54 at GW170817 distances, and for the massless zero mode omega' = gamma|k'| holds exactly at every frequency. The tree's 50-digit beta = 3.74165738677e-08, 1/beta = 26726124.1912 and 93.80654 ns all reproduce. The 7e-16 datum reproduces from 1710.05834 (6.50e-16, rounded up). The hedge is quoted word for word.

The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree applies the result to a wider class than GKLM derive it for. branelink.py:170/172/303 state beta <= 3.74e-8 on the condition of a bulk graviton alone, which drops two of GKLM's hypotheses:
- B = 0, GKLM's frame. With GKLP eq. 22 the bound depends on B and on direction: it is 57.1x looser at the tree's own escape value B = 0.999387630, and only +-0.12% different at the CMB-dipole B.
- An untilted brane. Polychronakos eq. 5.3 lets a tilt-like brane escape a single-event bound.

The inherited 7e-16 also carries the emission-window assumption of 1710.05834 without naming it; an exotic window changes d 54x. The later distance datum tightens the bound rather than loosening it.

Separately, 'Delta c/c = 0 identically' for brane-confined gravity (branelink.py:85-86) holds at tree level only (Kabat-Nomura, and the tree's own 6.37e-64). That is a wording discrepancy, not a refutation. Nothing is WRONG: no counterexample to eq. (38) under its hypotheses exists or was found.
gklm-eq38.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names B = 0 (or the B- and direction-dependent form it already uses in b_for_saving) and zero tilt as conditions of BETA_MAX and BETA_BOUND_CONDITIONAL_ON, and names the 7e-16's emission-window and 26 Mpc assumptions. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a second GW-EM event, or an accepted emission model such as photons before the merger, that moves the GW-photon speed bound upward. To WRONG: only a demonstration that the massless bulk zero mode on a uniformly moving, untilted test brane in flat M4 x S1 does not travel at gamma on the brane; the re-derivation (C3c) shows that it does. To OPEN: not applicable, since the source was read and the identity is checkable.

gr-qc/9701064.published_statement: p.4: 'An accurate analytic approximation to the exact numerically calculated scalar field stress energy tensor was developed in Ref. [18] [AHS] ... <T^nu_mu>_analytic = (T)_0 + (xi-1/6)(T)_1 + (xi-1/6)^2 (T)_2 + (T)_log (4) ... we find that the semiclassical Einstein equations for a conformally coupled scalar (xi = 1/6) are as follows (K^2 = 1/(5760 pi))'. These are eqs. (5) tt, (6) ll and (7) thth, each with LHS = G^mu_nu of metric (2) and RHS = K^2[non-log bracket + ln f (log bracket)]. On p.5 the text layer reads '+16 f'^2 f''/f^3' in the tt log bracket and '-4 f'^2 r'^2/(f^2 r)' in the ll log bracket. p.6: the ll equation 'is actually a constraint'. The throat conditions are r(0)>0, r'(0)=0, r''(0)>=0, f(0)>0, f'(0)=0 and f''(0)>=0, with optional r'''(0)=f'''(0)=0. 'Writing out the ll-equation (6) at the point l = 0 ... yields an algebraic quartic equation for the throat radius': -4 (f''(0)/f(0))^2 [1+ln f(0)] r(0)^4 + 32 (f''(0) r''(0)/f(0)) [1+(1/2)ln f(0)] r(0)^3 + [K^-2 - 16 r''(0)^2 ln f(0)] r(0)^2 + 16 ln f(0) = 0 (8), 'where we have used only that r'(0) = f'(0) = 0 ... independent of the values assigned to the third derivatives'. p.7: 'taking f(0) = f''(0) = 1, r''(0) = 0 and xi = 1/6 yields r(0) ~ 67 l_P'. Eq. (9): '-1 <= ln f(0) < 0; f'(0)=f''(0)=f'''(0)=0; r(0) = sqrt(-16 K^2 ln f(0)); r'(0)=r''(0)=r'''(0)=0'. The paper plots 'a particular numerical solution for ln f(0) = -2/3' with throat 'r(0) ~ 0.02 l_P'. Footnote [20]: 'We have also set the scalar mass and temperature to zero: m = kappa = 0. In this case, the arbitrary renormalization scale parameter mu appearing in (T)_log can be absorbed into the definition of f.'
published_hypotheses: H1: static spherically symmetric metric in proper-distance gauge, ds^2 = -f(l)dt^2 + dl^2 + r^2(l) dOmega^2 (eq. (2), p.4), with f(0) > 0 (p.6).
H2: semiclassical Einstein equation G_mu^nu = 8 pi <T_mu^nu> (eqs. (1), (3)), in units hbar = c = G = 1 with MTW signs (footnote [19]).

H3: <T> is not the exact expectation value. It is the Anderson-Hiscock-Samuel analytic approximation, eq. (4), which HPS call 'accurate' (p.4). AHS left (T)_log in curvature form and HPS worked it out (p.4).
H4: a single conformally coupled scalar, xi = 1/6, massless and at zero temperature, m = kappa = 0 (footnote [20]).
H5: the arbitrary renormalization scale mu is 'absorbed into the definition of f' (footnote [20]), so the normalization of f, and with it the value of ln f(0), carries mu.
H7: eq. (9) data. -1 <= ln f(0) < 0, the first to third derivatives of f and r are all zero at l=0, and r(0) comes from (8). The plotted solution has ln f(0) = -2/3 (p.7).

gr-qc/9406053#kinematic-possibility.published_statement: Abstract: 'No assumption is made about the dimension of spacetime. First, it is stressed that topology change is kinematically possible; i.e., if a field equation is not imposed, it is possible to construct topology-changing spacetimes with non-singular Lorentz metrics. Simple 2-dimensional examples of this are shown.' Sec. III.C: 'if n is odd, there is a spacetime that interpolates between them if and only if chi(S1) = chi(S2) ... If n = 2, then again examples of topology change can be constructed ... if n is even and is greater than 2, then there is always an interpolating spacetime ... Thus, kinematically, though there are some constraints, a large variety of topology-changing closed universes exist. In particular, as Misner has pointed out, since any two closed 3-manifolds are cobordant, there is at this stage no barrier whatsoever to four-dimensional topology change.' Sec. III.D: 'The only Lorentzian cobordisms in two dimensions are the torus and the Klein bottle, the cylinder and the Moebius strip ... The spacetimes of fig. 6b and fig. 6c are explicit examples of Lorentzian topology change.' Fig. 6b is S1 u S1 -> empty (universe pair-annihilation). Fig. 6c, due to Sorkin, is S1 -> empty (self-annihilation). Reversing V gives the reverse transitions. Sec. IX: 'non-singular topology-changing spacetimes in two dimensions (albeit with closed timelike curves)'. Sec. III.E, restating Geroch: 'any two externally Euclidean spaces can be connected by an interpolating externally Lorentzian spacetime'.
published_hypotheses: No field equation imposed: the claim is kinematical ('if a field equation is not imposed').
Classical evolution: spacelike S1 and S2 are joined by a connected interpolating manifold M (Sec. I.A, II.A). S1 or S2 may be empty, which is creation or annihilation of the universe.
The Lorentz metric is smooth and non-degenerate ('non-singular') on all of M, built from a smooth, nowhere-vanishing vector field V (Sec. II.B).
The metric is time-oriented (Sec. II.A). Dropping this changes the kinematics: in odd dimensions the RS rule is then no longer required (Sec. VII).
M is not required to be foliable. With a foliation, topology cannot change without cuts or holes (Sec. I.A, corollary to Theorem 1).

Existence conditions (Reinhart, Sorkin). For even n, chi(M) = 0, which Misner connected sums can arrange when n > 2. For odd n, chi(S1) = chi(S2), the RS rule; in n = 3 it forbids every non-identity oriented closed transition. For n = 2, only the torus, the Klein bottle, the cylinder and the Moebius strip qualify.
The price is stated beside the existence claim: the 2D examples carry CTCs (Sec. IX), and Theorem 1 forces a CTC in any causally compact interpolating spacetime whose topology changes.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED QUALIFIER. create.py:51-53 and specthm.py:1156-1157 state 'topology change is kinematically possible' without the source's 'though there are some constraints' (Sec. III.C). Those constraints are the RS rule in odd n, which forbids every non-identity oriented transition in n = 3 (K7), and the restriction to the four chi = 0 cobordisms in n = 2 (K6a). Read existentially, the tree's sentence matches the abstract, which is equally unconditional. It is harmless in n = 4, where the source says 'no barrier whatsoever' (K8).

SCOPE OF THE CITED EVIDENCE. create.py:52 ('Borde exhibits 2-dimensional examples. So it is not forbidden outright') sits under CREATE, 'bring a throat into existence' (create.py:41-42), and specthm.py:1146 applies it to throat creation. Borde's 2D examples are universe pair-annihilation (S1 u S1 -> empty) and self-annihilation (S1 -> empty), with their reverses; neither creates a throat in an existing space. K6b enumerates every compact, non-singular, time-oriented 2D Lorentzian cobordism and finds no change between two non-empty surfaces of different topology. The trousers has chi = -1 (K5c). The throat case is supported in the same paper by its n = 4 statements (Misner, K8: S^3 -> S^2xS^1) and by Geroch's externally Lorentzian result (III.E, restated, Geroch NAMED-NOT-READ). The conclusion is supported; the example named is not the case that supports it.

gr-qc/9406053#kinematic-possibility.lacked_data: Tested and not supported, in either direction. The claim is a mathematical existence statement with no empirical input. What was available in 1994 already sufficed: cobordism theory, Reinhart, Sorkin, and Misner/Geroch in 4D. Here it is checked by construction rather than trusted. K3 and K4 build both 2D examples explicitly as smooth, non-degenerate, time-oriented metrics with spacelike boundaries and finite curvature. K8 checks the 4D throat-creation chi step. Later work extends the result rather than overturning it. Degenerate Morse metrics widen the kinematic class (Dowker-Surya 1998; Garcia-Heveling 2022), and an explicit non-degenerate 4D wormhole nucleation with CTCs has been built (Pisana et al. 2025). A later datum or theorem could only restrict the dynamics, which is Theorem 3 and a separate ledger key; it cannot remove an existence claim shown by explicit example. M's hypothesis does expose a scope point, not an error: the tree cites the 2D examples, which are universe creation or annihilation and provably cannot be throat creation (K6b). The 4D support for the throat case is in the same paper.
