1208.5399-sec1.3.published_statement: p.13: 'Consider a region between Casimir plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime and an inertial trajectory parallel to the plates. Let l be the distance from this trajectory to the nearest plate in the t = 0 surface. Then no experiment conducted along the trajectory in a time interval of less than 2l can possibly know about the existence of the plates; it should be as if the experiment was conducted in Minkowski space. In particular the quantum energy inequalities apply, and [as the energy density is supposed constant along the trajectory] (4) gives an a priori bound T00 >= -C/(2l)^4 ~ -3.17/(2l)^4 = -0.20/l^4. By comparison, the known value of the Casimir energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field is T00 = -pi^2/(1140 L^4) - (pi^2/(48 L^4))(3 - 2cos^2(pi z/L))/cos^4(pi z/L) which ranges between 3-7% of the bound as z varies in [-L/2, L/2].' p.14: the a priori bound 'also applies to all stationary (Hadamard) states of the system ... There remains an interesting question as to why the Casimir energy density is a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound.' Eq.(4), p.11: rho >= -C/tau^4, 'C ~ 3.17'. It comes from Eq.(3) on p.10, of which Fewster says 'The bound is known not to be optimal.'

P2 ideal plates at z = +-L/2 with (Dirichlet) boundary conditions in otherwise flat spacetime. The quoted density is the Dirichlet one, re-derived here from the Dirichlet image sum (B1-B4)
P3 inertial trajectory parallel to the plates at distance l from the nearer plate
P4 the energy density is constant along the trajectory (stationary state), so Eq.(4) applies with tau = 2l
P5 causal/locality argument: a measurement lasting less than 2l cannot detect the plates, so the Minkowski QEI applies (basis: local covariance, ref [31], NAMED-NOT-READ)

1208.5399-sec1.3.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. Fewster (2012) needed no empirical datum. The result is the ratio of a closed-form vacuum density (from the Dirichlet image sum, known since the 1970s) to a derived bound whose constant is mathematical. Every input he used re-derives here. The only defect is a misprint (1140 for 1440), which moves the midpoint from 6.76% to 6.70% and leaves '3-7%' intact. So on Fewster's own statement, nothing he lacked changes his conclusion (evidence: script B4, B5, C1-C5). What WAS lacking then, and is not supplied by anything read here, is the SHARP 4D QEI constant. Eq.(3) is 'known not to be optimal', and a sharp constant can only raise the ratio (C_s <= C implies ratio >= 3-7%). Saturation at the midpoint would need C_s = C/14.9. That missing quantity does not touch Fewster's sentence. It DOES bear on the tree's stronger reading ('Casimir does not saturate the QEI', 'three per cent is not a wall'), and only in the direction against the tree. The other datum the tree implies, a measured Casimir energy density, does not exist: experiments measure force (docket audit casimir-force-measurements.json). Real, dispersive plates move the density away from saturation, not toward it (Sopova-Ford, READ in that audit).
1208.5399-sec1.3.grade_evidence: Fewster's statement re-derives. C = 3.16986 (A1-A4), his minimal-coupling term matches exactly (B4), and the ratio falls monotonically from 6.70% at the midpoint (6.76% on his printed 1140) to 16/mu_1^4 = 3.196% at the plates (C1-C5), so '3-7%' holds. The 1140 is a misprint (B5): a discrepancy, not a refutation. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree uses the result more widely than the source in four named places. (i) 'REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT' (achievable.py:205; bounds.py:341, 418): it is a calculation, and no measurement enters. (ii) 'Casimir' is used without qualification (achievable.py:205-214, ledger.py:1998-2001) for a result about a Dirichlet minimally coupled scalar. (iii) 'Saturation is not 3 %' (achievable.py:213) is measured against a bound Fewster calls non-optimal; against the sharp bound, saturation needs C_s = C/14.9, which is OPEN. (iv) The withdrawn claim names the FORD-ROMAN bound, and in Ford-Roman's own capped form (gr-qc/9510071, READ in the docket) the Casimir density meets that bound with equality at the cap. It is not WRONG: there is no counterexample to the published statement, and the tree was right to withdraw 'Casimir saturates it' as an established fact, since that was never shown. jacobi-raychaudhuri-ricci-focusing.published_statement: Gao & Wald (2000) restate Raychaudhuri and Sachs, citing Flanagan-Marolf-Wald. Take the null geodesic congruence from a point p, with affine parameter lambda. The Jacobi matrix A obeys d^2A/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta (eq.11). With G = sqrt(det A) (eq.12), 'the Raychaudhuri equation yields G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]' (eq.13). Conjugate points are the zeros of G. Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 get them from two hypotheses together: the NEC R_ab k^a k^b >= 0, and the null generic condition k_[a R_b]cd[e k_f] k^c k^d != 0, which the Weyl tensor alone can satisfy. The general null Raychaudhuri equation, re-derived here and consistent with Freivogel-Krommydas 1807.03808 eq.(39) up to normalisation, is dtheta/dlambda = -theta^2/2 - sigma_ab sigma^ab + omega_ab omega^ab - R_ab k^a k^b. In GR (Lobo 0909.5539 p.3; Wall 1007.1493 eq.29), R_ab k^a k^b = 8 pi G T_ab k^a k^b, and positive R_kk ensures focusing within a finite affine parameter. The published results give SUFFICIENT conditions for focusing and conjugate points. None of the restatements read says that a conjugate point REQUIRES R_kk > 0.
published_hypotheses: H1: a null geodesic congruence with an affine parameter. The 1/2 in eq.(13) is 1/(n-2) with n = 4; see rederive A1-A3 in the gr-qc_0007021 audit.
H2: the congruence is twist-free (hypersurface-orthogonal), for example the congruence from a point (A|p = 0), so omega_ab = 0. Otherwise +omega^2 enters with a defocusing sign.
H3: four spacetime dimensions, for the 1/2 in eq.(13) and in theta^2/2.

H4: Einstein's equation (classical GR), which turns R_kk into 8 pi G T_kk/c^4. The trace term and any cosmological constant drop out because g_ab k^a k^b = 0. In modified gravity the condition falls on an effective T instead (Lobo 0909.5539 p.3).

H5: for a theorem that a conjugate point exists, the NEC R_kk >= 0 PLUS either initial convergence or the null generic condition, and enough affine extent (Gao-Wald Lemma 1 and Theorem 1; Hawking-Ellis 4.4.5 named, not read).

H6: the shear term sigma_ab sigma^ab >= 0 is sourced by the Weyl tensor through the Sachs/Jacobi equation, and it can produce a conjugate point on its own. The null generic condition can be met in vacuum.

(physics the tree uses) The Sturm threshold applies to a stretch of length l. 'Below nuclear density' compares density only. It does not ask whether a region at that density and of length l can exist.

nuclear-density-pressure.lacked_data: This does not support M's hypothesis for this result. '~1e35 Pa' has no outside author, so no earlier physicist lacked any data here. The saturation density has been known to about 5% for decades, and the tree already holds a value of the right order (2.3e17 kg/m^3) in three other files. The conclusion needs only n0 > 0.064 fm^-3, which is 2.5x below every quoted value, so it is insensitive to any plausible datum. The discrepancy is inside the tree: its own number overstates nuclear energy density about 4x and disagrees with its own constant by 4.84x, which inflates the printed margin from x2.5 to x10.5. The neutron-star sentence is missing an assumption about the shape of the region, not a datum.
nuclear-density-pressure.grade_evidence: The verdict tkk(100 km) = 9.505e33 Pa < nuclear density was re-derived as TRUE three ways: against the tree's 1e35, against eps0 for every n0 from 0.145 to 0.170, and against the tree's own 2.3e17 kg/m^3. It would flip only for n0 < 0.0643 fm^-3. It is not STANDS for two reasons. First, the figure as used, '~1e35 Pa', overstates nuclear energy density about 4x (4.23x at n0 = 0.16, and 4.84x against the tree's own constant). That is a discrepancy, not a refutation, but it makes the margin x2.2-2.6 rather than x10.5 and puts the crossover near 63 km rather than 31 km. Second, the tree drops two assumptions, now named: w = 1 with p ~ 0, and a long rather than ball-shaped seating region for the neutron-star sentence (a uniform ball has compactness pi^2/6 > 1 for every l). It is not WRONG, because no plausible datum gives a counterexample. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no moved datum moves the conclusion. Caveat: n0 was not read at source here, so the grade rests on the parameter scan and the tree's own constant.

IV.A (Hadamard states, eqs (54)-(60)) pp.15-17; small sampling domain, eq. (66), p.17; eqs (61)-(71) pp.17-18; Theorem IV.1 / eq. (72) and 'holds for any value of the coupling constant' p.18; non-triviality (73)-(74) and 'we do not expect it to be optimal' p.19. Published as SciPost Phys. 16 (2024) 119. 2309.10848-thmiv.1.published_statement: p.18: 'Theorem IV.1. Let f be any real-valued test function compactly supported in a small sampling domain. Let l^mu be a null vector field defined in the neighbourhood of support of f. Then, for all Hadamard states psi  <:rho_n:(f^2)>_psi >= -2 INT_D d^n alpha/(2pi)^n ((Q x Q)W_0)_kappa(fbar_alpha, f_alpha) - xi <:phi^2:(Q[f])>_psi, (72) where W_0 is the two-point function of the reference Hadamard state psi_0 and Q = l^mu nabla_mu.' The definitions it uses: (69b) Q[f] = nabla_mu nabla_nu(l^mu l^nu f^2) + (1/2) R_mn l^mu l^nu f^2; (71) f_alpha(x) = e^{i alpha x} f(x); D is the set of covectors satisfying (66). p.18: 'unlike those two inequalities [FO energy density, FK effective energy density], the QEI derived holds for any value of the coupling constant xi.' p.19: the bound is non-trivial in the sense of (74), and 'as this bound is derived by discarding positive terms we do not expect it to be optimal.' The left side is a DIFFERENCE: <:T_mn:>_psi = <T^ren>_psi - <T^ren>_psi0, eqs (59) and (65).
published_hypotheses: P1: (M,g) is globally hyperbolic and time-oriented, in n dimensions. The QFT lives on a FIXED background (algebraic quantization, p.15).
P2: a free real scalar field with mass m and real coupling xi, obeying (box_g + m^2 + xi R)phi = 0 (10), with box_g := -g^mn nabla nabla (p.5). Conventions (-,+,+,+), MTW (+,+,+) (p.5).
P3: psi and the reference state psi_0 are Hadamard (p.16, (54)). W_0 is the two-point function of psi_0. The left side is normal-ordered relative to psi_0, (59) and (65).

P4: f is real-valued, smooth and compactly supported in a SMALL SAMPLING DOMAIN. That is an open subset inside a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood, covered by one hyperbolic chart: d/dx^0 is future-pointing and timelike, and c|u_0| >= sqrt(sum_j u_j^2) for every causal covector (66) (p.17, following Fewster-Smith [20]).
P5: l^mu is a null vector field defined in a neighbourhood of supp f (p.18).
P6: the Leibniz rule for Wick powers (Hollands-Wald axiom 10), in the form (62)-(63) (p.17). This is an assumed renormalization prescription, not something derived.
P7: the point-split operator rho_hat_n = l.nabla (x) l.nabla is symmetric and of positive type, which gives (70) (p.18, citing [7] and [20]).
Scope: any real xi (p.18). The bound is not optimal (p.19).

C1: tested on a generic time-dependent 4-metric diag(-a,b,c,c)(t,x) with explicit functions, phi = sin(t+2x) + xt/3, xi = 3/10, m = 7/10. The off-shell Noether identity nabla^m T_mn + E d_n phi = 0, with E = g^ab nabla nabla phi - m^2 phi - xi R phi (the Euler-Lagrange expression of action (7)), holds for FFKP eq.(9) to 2e-165. It FAILS with the eq.(12) Ricci sign (residual 0.356). C2: FFKP's own steps (10) and (11) take (9) to (12) term by term, except for the Ricci term: (9) - (12) = 2 xi R_mn phi^2 exactly, a sign discrepancy in (12)/(13). C3: for T_ll = (1-2xi)A - 2xi B + k xi R_ll phi^2, the Leibniz/integration-by-parts step (62)-(63) gives a Ricci coefficient of -k in Q[f]. That is -1 from eq.(9), +1 from eq.(13) as printed, and +2 from eq.(61) as extracted. The printed (64)/(69b)/(72) carry +1/2, which matches none of them. Identity (63) is verified as a total divergence. C4: on HPS, g(l,l) = 0 exactly. 2309.10848-thmiv.1.lacked_data: Thm IV.1 is a mathematical theorem with no empirical input, so M's hypothesis in its data form does not apply: no measured datum enters (72) and none has moved. What the authors lacked, and nobody has yet, is the input needed to evaluate it on a particular curved background: W_0 of a reference Hadamard state and <:phi^2:>_psi on HPS. That absence is exactly why the tree's verdict is OPEN, and Kontou 2024 (Sec. 5.2) names the same gap. The one defect found is not a missing datum but an internal inconsistency in the v1 derivation, between eq.(9) and eqs.(12)/(13)/(61)/(64). The Ricci coefficient in Q[f] is printed as +1/2, while the conserved stress tensor of the paper's own action gives -1 (C1-C3). Why it plausibly went unnoticed: it cannot show up in any application FFKP make (Minkowski DSNEC/SNEC, (75)-(93), where R_mn = 0). Why it matters for the tree: on HPS, R_ll = -226800 pi^2 l^2 != 0 on any open supp f (C4b). Why it should not be over-read: no state violating the printed bound is exhibited (the bound is not sharp, p.19); the SciPost version is unread and may be corrected; and fixing the coefficient changes no verdict the tree draws from the theorem.
2309.10848-thmiv.1.grade_evidence: What the tree uses 'in form' STANDS. Any real xi (p.18, word for word), the small sampling domain, the null l, and the DIFFERENCE structure (59) were all read at source and re-checked (C4a, C4d). The printed right side does NOT carry over to the class the tree uses. The v1 derivation supports a Ricci coefficient of +1/2 in Q[f] only where R_mn l^m l^n = 0 on supp f, or where xi = 0. Eq.(9), shown here to be the conserved stress tensor of action (7) (C1a, residual 2e-165), leads to -1 instead. Eqs.(12), (13) and (61) as printed are inconsistent both with (9) and with each other (C1b, C2, C3). HPS's throat neighbourhood lies outside that class (R_ll = -226800 pi^2 l^2, C4b), and qeihps.py:99 copies the +1/2. This is a discrepancy in v1, recorded and not repaired. It is not a refutation: there is no counterexample state, and the journal version is unread, so it must not be quoted as an error in SciPost Phys. 16, 119 until that version is read. Consequence for the tree: none on its verdicts. VERDICT_APPLICABLE_QEI stays OPEN and KONTOU_REQUESTED_TEST_ON_HPS stays 'applies in form, not evaluable', because the blocking inputs (W_0 and <:phi^2:> on HPS, and HPS's state being Hadamard) are untouched. Only the Q[f] display at qeihps.py:99 carries a coefficient that the source's own eq.(9) does not support.
2309.10848-thmiv.1.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS, by any of three routes. First: reading SciPost Phys. 16 (2024) 119 or a v2 and finding (12)/(13)/(69b) corrected to the -1 that follows from (9); the theorem would then stand as the tree uses it, and qeihps.py:99 would be a stale copy. Second: a convention under which (9) and (12) both hold; given (10)/(11) none exists (C2). Third: an error in C1 (re-run the script; it uses exact differentiation evaluated at 30 digits). To WRONG: an explicit Hadamard state on a background with R_ll != 0 on supp f that violates the printed (72). flanagan-wald-1996.published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We study a free, linear, massless scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling in the context of perturbation theory about the flat spacetime/vacuum solution, and we modify the perturbed semiclassical equations by the "reduction of order" procedure to eliminate spurious solutions. We also restrict attention to the limit in which the lengthscales determined by the state and metric are much larger than the Planck length. At first order in the metric and state perturbations, and for pure states of the scalar field, we find that the ANEC integral vanishes ... For mixed states, the ANEC integral can be negative. However, we prove that if we average the ANEC integral transverse to the geodesic, using a suitable Planck scale smearing function, a strictly positive result is obtained in all cases except for the trivial flat spacetime/vacuum solution. Similar results hold for pure states at second order in perturbation theory, when we additionally specialize to the situation where incoming classical gravitational radiation does not dominate the first order metric perturbation. These results suggest ... that if traversable wormholes do exist as self-consistent solutions of the semiclassical equations, they cannot be macroscopic but must be "Planck scale".' Sec. I C (p.5): 'a one-parameter family (with parameter denoted by eps) of spacetimes (M, g_ab(eps)) and quantum states satisfying Eq. (1.1) [G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab>], with the spacetime reducing to Minkowski spacetime and the quantum state reducing to the vacuum state when eps = 0'; eqs (1.6)-(1.7) expand the state and the metric to O(eps^2) + O(eps^3). Sec. V (p.27): positivity of ANEC 'to order eps^2 ... actually fails ... Nevertheless, we do obtain a positivity result involving a transversely smeared version of the ANEC integral.' FW's OWN statement of semiclassical gravity's domain (p.2): objects that 'always lie outside the domain of validity of the semiclassical theory, either because the curvature scales are Planckian somewhere in the corresponding spacetimes, or because the quantum fluctuations in the stress tensor are comparable to its expected value.' p.4: 'we will be forced to resort to perturbation theory about the trivial solution'. p.5: 'the behavior of solutions in semiclassical gravity -- within the domain of validity of that theory -- may be qualitatively similar to classical solutions.'
published_hypotheses: H1 matter: a single free, linear (non-self-interacting), massless scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling xi (abstract; p.3; p.5)
H2 self-consistency: G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab> (eq. 1.1), whose only source is the quantum field's <T_ab>, with no classical matter
H3 one-parameter family reducing to Minkowski + vacuum at eps = 0 (p.5); results through O(eps^2), O(eps^3) dropped (eqs 1.6-1.7); no remainder estimate on the pages read
H4 reduction of order applied to the perturbed semiclassical equations (abstract; p.27 eqs 4.20, 4.23)
H5 long wavelengths: lengthscales >> Planck length (alpha >> 1; unknown corrections O((ln alpha)^2/alpha^6) in eq. 4.23)
H6 Hadamard 2-point distributions with positivity; in-data at J^- under 'suitable asymptotic conditions' (p.5)
H7 the second-order pure-state result also needs incoming classical gravitational radiation not to dominate h^(1); <T^(2)[h1,h1]> is not evaluated and approximate eq. (3.59) is used (p.27)
H8 complete achronal null geodesic; the conclusion is TRANSVERSELY SMEARED ANEC (Planck-scale smearing), and unsmeared ANEC fails
H9 globally hyperbolic spacetime (p.3)

lemaitre-poisson-2019-gamma1.published_statement: As restated in arXiv:2604.05980 Sec. III (READ): 'we find that dM/dsigma >= 0 whenever Gamma >= Gamma_1, where Gamma_1 := 3/2 + 4(p/mu) + 4(p/mu)^2 (3.16a) = (1+2 sqrt F+3F)/(4F) (3.16b) = (4 - 6C + 2 sqrt(1-2C))/(4(1-2C)) (3.16c), where C := M/R ... The point along the sequence at which dM/dsigma = 0 is the configuration of maximum mass ... and this point also marks the onset of a radial instability ... [34]'. Footnote 1: 'The criterion appears to be different from the one given in Eq. (34) of Ref. [34]. The reason has to do with inequivalent definitions of the adiabatic index. In Ref. [34] it was defined as d ln p/d ln mu, whereas it is d ln p/d ln sigma here.' Sec. X: 'It is known [34] that these equilibrium configurations are radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2' (Newtonian). So the restating source credits LP2019 with two things: (i) the theorem that maximum mass marks the onset of radial dynamical instability, and (ii) a criterion written in the d ln p/d ln mu convention (their Eq 34). The expression (3.16c) that the tree quotes is Pitre et al.'s form, written in the rest-mass convention.
published_hypotheses: H1 the shell is infinitesimally thin, static and spherically symmetric, matched by Israel junction conditions
H2 Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild of mass M outside
H3 the surface matter is a perfect fluid (rest-mass density sigma, energy density mu, pressure p)
H4 barotropic and isentropic: mu = sigma + eps(sigma), p = p(sigma), dmu = (mu+p)/sigma dsigma
H5 Gamma := d ln p/d ln sigma in the rest-mass convention (Pitre Eq 2.6); LP2019 Eq (34) uses d ln p/d ln mu instead
H6 the criterion is derived as the turning-point condition dM/dsigma >= 0; reading it as dynamical radial stability is credited to LP2019
H7 radial perturbations only; l >= 2 modes are unstable (2604.05980) and this threshold does not cover them
H8 the sequence starts at low sigma with Gamma > Gamma_1
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION DRIFT (a discrepancy, not a refutation): the tree credits the expression (3.16c) to LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 at wall.py:112 ('(LeMaitre-Poisson 2019)'), wall.py:444, research/README.md:1081, paper/CLAIMS.md:9016 (row S3) and index3.py:1820. Footnote 1 of the restating paper (READ) says LP's Eq (34) has a different form because it uses d ln p/d ln mu. The expression belongs to Pitre et al. Computed here: in LP's convention the same threshold is (3s^2+2s+1)/(s(3s+1)) = 3/2 + 5C/8 + 33C^2/32 + ..., which is Gamma_1*mu/(mu+p). The ratio to (3.16c) is 1.0295 at C=0.1 and 1.3090 at C=0.4. This form is PREDICTED from the physics, not read.
CONVENTION: kept, not dropped. wall.py:113 uses d ln p/d ln sigma in the rest-mass density, and wall.py:114-115 uses Eq (2.7), Gamma = beta^2 (mu+p)/p. This is the right convention for (3.16c).

It was confirmed here to hold identically.

gr-qc/9304008-eq3.18-3.23.published_statement:
Verbatim from the v1 text layer, pp.7-8. Conventions: |alpha,zeta> = D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> (3.9); alpha = s e^{i gamma} (3.12); zeta = r e^{i delta} (3.13); S+ a S = a cosh r - a+ e^{i delta} sinh r (3.16).

(3.18): '<alpha,zeta|:T_ab(x):|alpha,zeta> = 2K_ab{sinh r cosh r cos(2theta+delta) + sinh^2 r + s^2[1 - cos 2(theta+gamma)]}'.

(3.19): '<alpha,zeta|:T_ab(x)T_mn(x):|alpha,zeta> = 2K_ab K_mn ( s^4[cos 4(theta+gamma) - 4 cos 2(theta+gamma) + 3] + 3s^2{2 sinh r cosh r[2 cos(2theta+delta+2gamma) - cos(4theta+delta+2gamma)] + 4 sinh^2 r(cos 2gamma - cos 2theta) - cos(delta+2gamma)} + 3 sinh^2 r[cosh^2 r cos(4theta+2delta) + 3 - 4 cos 2theta] )'.

(3.22): 'In a squeezed vacuum, alpha = 0, we may also take delta = 0 ... <:T_ab(x):> = 2K_ab sinh r[cosh r cos(2theta) + sinh r].'

(3.23): 'For the case delta = 0 and alpha = 0 ... <:T_ab T_mn:> = 2K_ab K_mn sinh^2 r[2 cosh^2 r cos 4theta - 8 sinh r cosh r cos 2theta + 3(sinh^2 r + cosh^2 r)]. As required, for the vacuum state (r = 0) this quantity vanishes.'

p.9: 'numerical evaluation of Delta using Eqs. (3.2), (3.18), and (3.19) ... By the point that the state is sufficiently squeezed to have rho = <:T00:> < 0, we always have that Delta is at least of order unity.'
published_hypotheses: H1: a massless, minimally coupled free scalar in FLAT (Minkowski) spacetime, with the bilinear stress tensor (2.11). A single plane-wave box mode k, with (2.12)-(2.14): T[f,f] = -K e^{2i theta}, T[f,f*] = T[f*,f] = K, theta = k.x.
H2: the single-mode squeezed coherent state D(alpha)S(zeta)|0>, with KF's operator conventions (3.10)-(3.17): alpha = s e^{i gamma}, zeta = r e^{i delta}, S+ a S = a cosh r - a+ e^{i delta} sinh r.

H3: normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum for BOTH <:T:> and the quartic <:T T:>. See KF p.5 and (3.3)-(3.6): 'The effect of the normal ordering has been to remove the contribution of the n = 0 term from the diagonal part.'
H4: the coincidence limit x -> y and the purely temporal component, for Delta (3.2).
H5: squeezed vacuum means alpha = 0, and delta = 0 'as this is simply a choice of phase' ((3.22), (3.23)).

The tree's hypotheses are KF's H2 and H5, with w = e^{i delta} and g = e^{2i gamma}: 'single-mode squeezed coherent state, s = sinh r, c = cosh r, phases w, g' and 'squeezed vacuum = alpha 0, w = 1'. fluctuation.py:241-260 transcribes (3.18), (3.19), (3.22) and (3.23) term by term. This audit transcribed them independently (rederive C1-C2) and reached the same four verdicts.

C7 shows that the one plausible alternative reading of H3, <:T::T:> minus its vacuum value, does not reproduce the print either.

With the exact <:T00^2:>, at KF's own Fig.1/2 parameters (gamma = delta = 0, theta = pi/2), the point r = 1/2, s^2 = (1-e^{-1})/8 has rho/K = -0.316060 and Delta = 0 exactly; the Fock-space control agrees. M's hypothesis does not apply to this result, and the re-derivation is the evidence.

(3.18)-(3.23) are closed-form expectation values with no empirical input. Everything needed was in Kuo & Ford's hands in 1993: the commutator, their own (3.14)-(3.17), and the normal-ordering rule they state in (3.3)-(3.6). Their (3.18) and (3.22), derived from exactly those inputs, are exact (C1). The defect in (3.19) and (3.23) is algebraic, or typographical in v1. The consequences differ by case. For the squeezed VACUUM, the exact Delta is 2/3 wherever rho != 0 (C4), so KF's reading survives there. For the squeezed COHERENT family, their p.9 claim (rho < 0 always carries Delta of order unity) fails on a curve where Delta = 0 exactly (C8), at the parameters of their own Figs. 1-2. What KF lacked was a correct (3.19) and a closed-form check, not data. Whether PRD 47, 4510 prints corrected forms is NAMED-NOT-READ.

expansion-scalar-3h-flrw.published_statement: Ellis & van Elst eq.(11): 'nabla_a u_b = - u_a udot_b + (1/3) Theta h_ab + sigma_ab + omega_ab, where the trace Theta = tilde-nabla_a u^a is the rate of volume expansion scalar of the fluid (with H = Theta/3 the Hubble scalar)'. Eq.(25): 'Sdot/S = (1/3) Theta, so the volume of a fluid element varies as S^3.' Eq.(104), FLRW: 'Matter-comoving local coordinates can be found so that ds^2 = -dt^2 + S^2(t)(dr^2 + f^2(r) dOmega^2), u^a = delta^a_0 ... Sdot/S = (1/3) Theta, characterising S(t) as the scale factor for distances between any pair of fundamental observers.' Kar-SenGupta eq.(10): for u = d/dt in FLRW 'the shear and rotation are identically zero. The expansion is given as Theta = 3 adot/a'.
published_hypotheses: H1: u^a is a unit timelike vector field (eq.(4)), the 4-velocity of a chosen congruence. Theta is defined relative to that u^a ('of the fluid'; 'fundamental observers').
H2: Theta = 3H with H = Sdot/S requires FLRW geometry: perfect fluid with udot = sigma = omega = 0 everywhere (eq.(103)), and u^a the matter-comoving congruence u^a = delta^a_0 (eq.(104)).
H3: Theta is the fractional rate of change of a fluid element's volume along u (eq.(25)); Theta = 0 iff that volume is constant.
H4 (implicit): three spatial dimensions. The 1/3 in eq.(11) is 1/dim of the rest space (h^a_a = 3, eq.(5)).
H5 (application, not part of the identity): the real universe is FLRW only on large (homogeneity) scales. The lectures treat 'almost-FLRW' as an assumption to be justified.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED at obstruct.py:270-277 (row EXPANSION-IS-A-RELABELLING): 'the universe has theta = 3 H_0 ... theta is coordinate-invariant, so no relabelling moves it'. The row drops the congruence qualifier that permute.py:26 carries ('3H for a comoving congruence'), and the FLRW qualifier. Theta is a scalar of the pair (g,u), and rederive E shows this. The static Killing congruence of de Sitter (which is flat FLRW with a = e^{Ht}; pullback verified) has Theta = 0 exactly, at the same events where the comoving congruence has 3H. A tilted congruence in matter-FLRW has Theta != 3H. This does not refute 'no relabelling moves it': a diffeomorphism carries (g,u) with it, so Theta moves as a scalar (rederive C). What it does mean is that 'the universe has theta = 3H_0' is a claim about the fundamental-observer congruence, and choosing that congruence is a physical choice.

DROPPED at permute.py:26-33 and at the scorecard, permute.py:504-506 ('the expansion is a permutation: FALSIFIED'): the scale-of-validity hypothesis H5. The matter congruence has theta ~ 0 inside bound structures (sibling audit bound-systems-do-not-expand.json; arXiv:0911.0241, READ). So the falsification holds for the large-scale fundamental-observer flow, not for every sub-volume. The tree states it without qualification.

ADDED (the tree's own modelling, not from the source) at permute.py:200-202: a 'permutation of a closed index' is modelled as a measure-preserving flow, with theta hardcoded to 0.0. The external identity supplies only the conditional 'volume-preserving => theta = 0' (eq.(25)). That a Rubik-type rearrangement is such a flow is a declaration in the tree, not a computation. Recorded, not repaired.

Implicit at permute.py:196 ('Three, exactly -- one for each spatial direction'): correct only for isotropic expansion in 3 spatial dimensions (theta = nH; for anisotropic flows theta = H1+H2+H3). Not load-bearing.

expansion-scalar-3h-flrw.lacked_data: The identity is kinematic: differential geometry of a chosen congruence on an FLRW metric, with no measured input. No missing datum can falsify it, and it was re-derived here for all three k and in four coordinate systems. What 1998-era authors lacked was the value of H0 (45-80 km/s/Mpc) and knowledge of the Hubble tension. Current values (67.36, 68.51, 73.04) move the printed theta by up to 8.4% but never toward zero, so the tree's conclusion that theta != 0 for the cosmic matter flow is unaffected. The evidence therefore runs against M's hypothesis for this result: no moved datum reaches the conclusion. Where 'incomplete' does apply, the gap is not in the authors' data but in the tree's scope. The identity holds for the fundamental-observer congruence of an exact FLRW metric, and the real matter flow has theta ~ 0 in bound structures (arXiv:0911.0241). One non-load-bearing discrepancy is recorded. The cached text of gr-qc/9812046v5 p.23 reads 'Hubble time 1/H0 of about 1.8 x 10^9' for H0 ~ 50, while 1/(50 km/s/Mpc) = 19.56 Gyr. This may be a superscript lost in extraction and must not be quoted as an error until the typeset PDF is read.
expansion-scalar-3h-flrw.grade_evidence: The external identity itself stands exactly. Ellis-van Elst eq.(11), (25) and (104) were re-derived in sympy: Theta = 3H for the comoving FLRW congruence for k = 0 and +-1, unchanged under every coordinate change tried (including a generic nonlinear one), and Theta = 0 iff the flow preserves volume. No moved datum takes theta to zero. The grade is NARROWED because the tree's use drops two hypotheses. (1) obstruct.py:270-277 drops 'comoving congruence'; rederive E exhibits a congruence in flat-FLRW de Sitter (the static Killing observers) with Theta = 0 exactly. (2) permute.py:26-33 and 504-506 assert 'the universe has theta = 3H_0' and 'THE UNIVERSE IS NOT A PERMUTATION' without the homogeneity-scale hypothesis, while the matter flow has theta ~ 0 in bound structures. Neither drop reverses the verdict for the large-scale fundamental-observer flow: no relabelling moves theta, and changing the congruence changes the observer family rather than relabelling it. The step 'permutation = measure-preserving flow' (hardcoded 0.0 at permute.py:200-202) is the tree's own declaration, not part of the external result.
expansion-scalar-3h-flrw.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the obstruct.py row names 'the comoving (fundamental-observer) congruence of FLRW'; permute.py names the homogeneity-scale hypothesis (theta = 3H for the cosmic-scale matter flow, ~0 inside bound structures); and the word 'Measured' becomes 'Planck-LCDM fit'. To WRONG: a computed coordinate transformation that changes the comoving congruence's nabla.u at a fixed event (none exists, since the divergence of a vector field is a scalar), or an FLRW solution whose comoving congruence has Theta != 3 adot/a. To DATA-DEPENDENT: only if the verdict rested on theta's numerical value rather than on theta != 0, and it does not.

self-consistent-achronal-anec-open-ninet.published_statement: G&O 0705.3193v2 p.2: 'Condition 1 (self-consistent achronal ANEC) There is no self-consistent solution in semiclassical gravity in which ANEC is violated on a complete, achronal null geodesic. We conjecture that all semiclassical systems obey self-consistent achronal ANEC.' p.3: '...such a proof will have to await future work.' Abstract: 'free of known violations'. Later status, READ: Kontou-Sanders 2020 (l.4559) calls it a 'conjecture ... advanced by Graham and Olum'. DSNEC 2111.05772 p.5: 'no known counterexamples to self-consistent achronal ANEC in the semi-classical regime'. Kontou 2024 p.2: 'free of counterexamples in semiclassical gravity'. Iizuka et al. 2025 p.64: 'all holographic proofs of ANEC are performed on a fixed background. It remains an open question whether the self-consistent ANEC can be shown by using the holographic semiclassical Einstein equations'. Dorau-Much 2026 p.2: 'no violations of this condition are currently known'. Fliss 2026 p.45: the GSL implies achronal ANEC (Wall), but 'the status of the generalized second law ... is still uncertain'.
published_hypotheses: H1 SELF-CONSISTENCY: Einstein's equation holds with the full stress tensor, meaning classical matter plus the induced quantum <T_ab> (G&O p.2). A test field on a fixed background does not qualify.

H2 SEMICLASSICAL REGIME: 'Condition 1 should be expected to hold only in cases where the curvature is well below the Planck scale' (G&O p.3). This is what excludes the classical Barcelo-Visser violations and the scale-anomaly violation.
H3 COMPLETE null geodesic (G&O p.2).
H4 ACHRONAL geodesic: no two of its points are joined by a timelike path (G&O p.2). This excludes the compactified-Minkowski and Schwarzschild/Boulware violations.
Condition 1 states no spacetime dimension. G&O p.2 credit the 1+1 massless-scalar case as proved by Wald-Yurtsever.

The consequences (Lemma 1, topological censorship, no-CTC) also need the null generic condition, plus theorem-specific global hypotheses: asymptotic flatness, global hyperbolicity, simple connectivity, partial asymptotic predictability (G&O Sec. IV; Kontou 2024 Thm 2).
The status claim 'open' is a statement about the literature and has no hypotheses of its own.

self-consistent-achronal-anec-open-ninet.lacked_data: G&O had no experimental datum to lack: the conjecture is about semiclassical QFT, and its evidence is computed <T_kk>. Later work, READ, does not overturn it. Urban-Olum 2010's fixed-background violation supports G&O's choice to require self-consistency. Wall 2010 and the free-field GSL proofs give partial, conditional support. The holographic proofs are all on fixed backgrounds. Wall's point about quantised-graviton shear is a genuine incompleteness found later, but it affects the consequences G&O draw (the no-wormhole and no-CTC theorems), not the status of Condition 1. It would cut in M's direction, but no source quantifies it for a macroscopic geometry, so it must not be quoted as an opening. No source READ, up to Fliss 2026, reports a counterexample or a general proof. M's hypothesis is not borne out for this result: the defects found are discrepancies, not refutations. They are the tree's dropped semiclassical qualifier, the 19-year count being a lower bound, and G&O's printed footnote form.

G&O restrict Condition 1 to curvature well below the Planck scale (p.3), and anecscope.py:34-36/170-171 and every sibling site describe the conjecture without that restriction. gr-qc/9702026.lacked_data: (1) In 1997 there was no proven curved-spacetime QI for a non-static metric; the authors called the exact treatment 'exceptionally difficult' and used the flat QI at short sampling. Fewster & Smith and then Kontou & Olum (1410.0665, READ) later proved the flat form plus small first-order Ricci corrections, of size ~alpha^2 = 0.01 at alpha = 0.1. This is evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: the one gap the authors named was later closed in their favour, to first order. (2) Cosmological masses have moved, but E/M_gal stays within 2.3-4.4e20 and 'roughly ten orders' stays at 9.7 against baryons: no change. (3) Van Den Broeck 1999 (READ) and Bobrick & Martire 2021 (READ) are later constructions, not data. They narrow the ~1e62 kg energy to the spherical Alcubierre shape at R = 100 m and leave the wall bound untouched. Non-minimal coupling (0708.2450, named) has no state-independent QEI, which narrows H1. (4) The paper's arithmetic, not missing data: two printed figures do not follow from its own formulas (6.2e70 L_P, 1.94x high; -400 M_sun, 514x low). These are recorded discrepancies; the qualitative conclusions stand. Net: no datum the authors lacked moves their conclusion within H1-H10; later work narrows the class it applies to.

gr-qc/0007021.published_statement: THEOREM 1 (p.6): 'Let (M,g_ab) be a null geodesically complete spacetime satisfying the null energy condition (2) and the null generic condition (see eq.(9)). Then given any compact region K in M, there exists another compact region K' containing K such that if q,p not in K' and q in J+(p) - I+(p), then any causal curve gamma connecting p to q cannot intersect the region K.' The authors' own gloss (pp.5, 10): 'the theorem suggests that "time advance" is not possible, although it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation, since the theorem gives little control over the size of the region K''. THEOREM 2 (pp.12-13): given a timelike conformal boundary, NEC + null generic, a strongly causal closure and compact causal diamonds, any causal curve from p to a point on the boundary of A(p) lies entirely in the boundary. The paper reads this (p.14) as light through an asymptotically AdS spacetime 'always being "delayed" relative to propagation through anti-de Sitter spacetime itself', and the comparison is well defined only because the boundary geometry is held fixed. EQ.(13) (p.7): with A from eq.(11) and G = sqrt(det A) (eq.12), 'G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]'. INTRODUCTION (pp.2-4): the Visser-Bassett-Liberati result h_ab k^a k^b >= 0 'is highly gauge dependent'. Eqs.(6)-(8) give a pure gauge that 'opens out the light cones everywhere', so 'we can reverse the conclusions of [3] in any compact region'. The paper also says 'there is no natural way to choose a flat background for a curved spacetime'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Thm 1, Thm 2, Lemma 1) null energy condition R_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for all null k (eq.2), stated on Ricci, not on T_ab; Thm 2 footnote 3 says Borde's averaged condition can replace it
H2 (Thm 1, Thm 2) null generic condition: every null geodesic contains a point with k_[a R_b]cd[e k_f] k^c k^d != 0 (eq.9)
H3 (Thm 1) null geodesic completeness; footnote 1 (Galloway): H1+H2+H3 can be replaced by 'M contains no null line'

H4 (Thm 1) the conclusion holds only for p,q outside a compact K' that the theorem does not bound; it is an asymptotic statement about fastest null geodesics and makes no comparison with any reference geometry

H5 (Thm 2) conformal embedding with a timelike boundary (asymptotically AdS prototype), strong causality of the closure, compact J+(p)∩J-(q); the delay is measured against boundary null geodesics with the boundary geometry fixed
H6 (all) connected, smooth, time-oriented, paracompact, any dimension; no staticity, symmetry or asymptotic flatness assumed
H7 (eq.13) a twist-free null congruence from a point with affine parameter; the Raychaudhuri equation is quoted from ref [10] (hep-th/9908070), not derived
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 and H3 (and Galloway's no-null-line replacement). driven.py:116-118 states Theorem 1 as 'the NEC makes Shapiro always a delay, never an advance', and foliation.py:237-239 says 'with the NEC, never an advance'. The theorem needs NEC, null generic and null geodesic completeness together. Machine-checked (rederive F1): on the radial null rays that foliation.py:305-313 times (10M->100M), the null generic quantity is exactly 0 at r = 3, 10, 50 and 100 M, because radial is a principal null direction of Schwarzschild. Schwarzschild is also null-incomplete. So the example the tree attaches the theorem to lies outside its hypotheses.

ADDED a comparison with a reference geometry. foliation.py:235-239 (D4 'arrives EARLIER than in the reference geometry ... REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE ... Gao & Wald') and foliation.py:613-614 do this. Theorem 1 makes no such comparison, and the paper's stated aim (p.4) is theorems that 'do not require a comparison with Minkowski spacetime'. Its only reference comparison is Theorem 2, which needs a fixed timelike conformal boundary (asymptotically AdS), not an asymptotically flat corridor.

INVERTED the paper's position on the companion citation. foliation.py:314-317 says 'Gao & Wald and Visser-Bassett-Liberati say the sign of that excess is forced by the NEC', and driven.py:116-118 groups the two. Gao-Wald argue that the VBL result is gauge dependent and can be reversed in any compact region (eqs.6-8, machine-checked as rederive E1/E2). They say nothing that forces the sign of the Schwarzschild Killing-time excess, and they cite Penrose's theorem that Schwarzschild cannot be identified with Minkowski with its cones inside Minkowski's.

WEAKENED the authors' own caveat. The tree calls Theorem 1 'standing' (driven.py:116) and 'stronger' than D4 (foliation.py:237, 614), but the authors write 'it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation' (pp.5, 10).
HELD: 'no staticity' (driven.py:116-117, foliation.py:316-317) is correct (H6).

HELD for eq.(13) as used: composite.py:18-20 quotes it verbatim with the right equation number, and composite.py:36-40 evolves a 2x2 screen in 4D, which is exactly where eq.(13) is an identity (rederive A2, C1).

OWNER READING, NOT GAO-WALD: composite.py:24-29 ('Weyl focusing ... sign-blind ... exactly as hard') is not in the paper. In the straight-ray Born approximation T(-M) is T(M) with the transverse axes swapped, so the conjugate points coincide exactly (55.8658 for both signs; rederive C2). composite.py's own docstring records 55.16 against 56.52, 2.47% apart, so 'exactly as hard' (composite.py:28) holds only to first order in M. The selftest's 0.05 tolerance (composite.py:359-360) already allows for this.

SOURCE DISCREPANCY, not drift: read literally (A the full n x n matrix, 'any dimension'), eq.(13) is not an identity. det A = lambda^2 det A_perp (B2), and in flat space G''=2>0 while the right-hand side is 0 (B1). The coefficient 1/2 holds only for n=4 (A3). The correct object is G=(det A_perp)^(1/(n-2)) with coefficient 1/(n-2) (A1). Lemma 1's proof survives with that object. This is recorded as a notational discrepancy, not an error in the result.

later_literature.what: Remark (ii): positive mass does not imply non-negative time delay. A non-negative bulk-versus-boundary delay follows from null genericity, null geodesic completeness and the NEC via the focusing theorem, so those are exactly the load-bearing hypotheses the tree drops. The negative-mass AdS soliton still has a strictly positive delay, so the sign of the mass does not fix the sign of the delay.

Rigidity: under the NEC in 4D, or staticity, or stationarity, an asymptotically AdS spacetime with zero boundary-to-boundary delay is AdS; Prop. 5.4 gives the asymptotically flat analogue. Remark 5.3(2): spacetimes that approach negative-mass Schwarzschild violate energy conditions and fail the null boundary Penrose property, so composite.py's negative-mass regime lies outside this whole family of theorems.

gr-qc/0007021.lacked_data: The theorems take no empirical input, so no datum the authors lacked can move them. Cassini's roughly 50x improvement over Viking (Will, arXiv:1403.7377, READ) confirms GR's solar delay but is not an input. What came later was mathematics, and it strengthened or extended the result: Galloway's no-null-line version (footnote 1), Page-Surya-Woolgar 2002, which confirms that generic + completeness + NEC is the route to a non-negative delay, and Paternain-Woolgar 2026 on rigidity. The gap sits on the tree's side. It cites Theorem 1 for 'the NEC alone gives no advance against a reference geometry, Schwarzschild radial transit included', which the paper does not claim. The paper itself shows the main obstacle to that claim: there is no invariant reference identification, and the VBL result can be reversed by a gauge choice. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: every step that can be checked here re-derives (eq.7, eq.8, eq.13 in 4D). The one discrepancy (the literal n x n reading of eqs.11-13, and the 1/2 in 'any dimension') is notational and leaves the proof valid.
gr-qc/0007021.grade_evidence: The source stands as published. It was read in full; eqs.7-8 and eq.13 in 4D were machine-checked; no counterexample was found; the one discrepancy is notational. The tree's use is narrowed. (a) driven.py:116-118 and foliation.py:237-239, 314-317 and 613-614 drop the null generic condition and null geodesic completeness, and add a reference-geometry comparison the theorem does not make. Their Schwarzschild radial example (foliation.py:305-317) fails the null generic hypothesis at every sampled point (F1) and is null-incomplete. The paper also argues against the VBL flat-comparison reading that the tree pairs it with (eqs.6-8, E1/E2). (b) composite.py's use of eq.(13) is inside the valid domain (4D, 2x2 screen; A2, C1) and stands. Its 'sign-blind' claim is the owner's first-order reading, confirmed at O(M) (C2), and is not a claim of Gao-Wald. Neither (a) nor (b) refutes the paper. But the tree's 'standing ... never an advance' cannot be attributed to gr-qc/0007021 as written.
gr-qc/0007021.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS for the foliation/driven use would need the citation restated with Theorem 1's real hypotheses (NEC + null generic + null geodesic completeness, or no null line) and its real conclusion (fastest null geodesics between far events avoid any compact set). It would also need 'Shapiro always a delay' and the reference comparison dropped, or else Theorem 2 cited only for asymptotically AdS spacetimes with fixed boundary geometry. The sign of the Schwarzschild excess would need a different source. WRONG would need a spacetime satisfying H1-H3 in which a fastest null geodesic between arbitrarily far p,q enters a fixed compact K; none is known, and the proof re-checks. OPEN does not apply, since the paper was read in full.

null-energy-condition.published_statement: NEC: 'T_ab k^a k^b >= 0' for a null vector k [every null k] (Kontou-Sanders eq 26; Martin-Moruno-Visser eq 2.6 'for any null vector k^a'). 'For a perfect fluid the condition becomes rho + P >= 0' (K&S p.10); type I: 'NEC rho + p_i >= 0' (MM&V p.6). 'The NEC is the weakest of the four main pointwise energy conditions' (K&S p.11). Maxwell/Proca: energy density a sum of squares (K&S eq 36), 'Thus the WEC holds and hence also the NEC ... the DEC also holds, even off-shell' (K&S p.15, Table 2). Minimally coupled scalar with V independent of g: DEC hence NEC hold (K&S p.14). Non-minimally coupled scalar (xi != 0): T_kk = (1-2xi)(k.grad phi)^2 + xi G_kk phi^2 - 2 xi phi (k.grad)^2 phi can be made negative, 'the NEC is violated' (K&S eq 39, p.15); Minkowski test field phi = sin(mt): T_kk = m^2(1-2xi) at t=0, 2 xi m^2 at t = pi/2m (K&S eq 32, p.14). 'all pointwise energy conditions are systematically violated by quantum fields and also by some rather simple classical fields' (K&S abstract).
published_hypotheses: definition, not theorem: quantifies over EVERY null vector at a point; 'holds' needs every null k, 'fails' needs one
4D Lorentzian (M,g), signature (-,+,+,+); physical form T_kk equals geometric form R_kk/8pi only under the Einstein equation (K&S Table 1)
effective form rho + p_i >= 0 requires Hawking-Ellis type I (MM&V p.6); with an energy flux (T_0i != 0 in the frame) the general-direction form is MM&V eq 2.22-2.24, not the two diagonal sums

NEC-satisfying CLASSES as published: minimally coupled scalar with metric-independent potential (K&S p.14), Maxwell/Proca (p.15), perfect fluids with rho + P >= 0; NOT: non-minimally coupled scalar (xi != 0) classically (K&S p.15, 17; MM&V p.10), Galileon / kinetic-braiding theories (Rubakov 1305.2614), and quantum states of any Wightman field (Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe, K&S p.17)

later_literature.what: NEC violation implies instability for isotropic or purely subluminal systems (incl. relativistic fluids/solids); stable NEC violators exist only with anisotropic background and superluminal modes.
Kinetic-braiding / Galileon theories violate the NEC classically, stably, subluminally, ghost-free within GR (eq 22, 27, 28): 'classical matter satisfies NEC' needs canonical kinetic terms.
Non-minimal scalar violates NEC off- and on-shell; Maxwell/Proca and minimal scalars satisfy it off-shell; QFT violates all pointwise conditions.
NEC validity on a Cauchy surface does not propagate for test fields; not used by the tree (dust witness certified for all t in closed form).
Optimal-transport / low-regularity / static-spherical reformulations; none changes the pointwise definition used for smooth metrics.

null-energy-condition.lacked_data: The NEC is a DEFINITION (Hawking-Ellis 1973): no datum enters it, no later measurement can move it, and the re-derivation agrees. What arrived later bears on the companion belief 'ordinary / classical matter satisfies the NEC': Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe (QFT violates positivity), classical non-minimal scalar violation (K&S sec 2.3, eq 32/39, re-derived here), stable subluminal Galileon violation (Rubakov 1305.2614), and Dubovsky et al's instability theorem for isotropic/subluminal violators. Later work therefore NARROWS the NEC-satisfying class, in M's sense of 'incomplete'; but evidence the other way is equally firm: for the classes the tree actually computes on (open dust, Maxwell electrovac, perfect-fluid neutron-star comparison) the NEC holds exactly and no verdict in rests_on_it moves. anec-klinkhammer-wald-yurtsever.published_statement: As restated, since the 1991 papers are not on arXiv. Fewster-Roman gr-qc/0209036 p.9, eq. (II.35): the ANEC, int dlambda <:T_ab:l^a l^b>_omega(gamma(lambda)) >= 0, was "established by Klinkhammer [21] at least for a dense set of states in the Fock space of the Minkowski vacuum, and by Wald and Yurtsever [22] for a large subclass of Hadamard states". Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007 p.2: "In n-dimensional Minkowski space, the ANEC was proved for the scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling for a dense set of states in the Fock space of the Minkowski vacuum [Klinkhammer]; namely, all finite linear combinations of finite particle-number states of bounded momentum ... [Wald-Yurtsever] establishes the ANEC in four-dimensional Minkowski space for a restricted class of Hadamard states of the minimally coupled scalar field ... In general globally hyperbolic two-dimensional spacetimes, [W-Y] established the ANEC on complete achronal null geodesics for the minimally coupled free scalar field. This holds for arbitrary Hadamard states in the massless case, and a restricted class of Hadamard states for nonzero mass." Kontou-Sanders p.36: "In four dimensions, Wald and Yurtsever argued that the ANEC cannot hold for all states of a massless field in all spacetimes." Visser gr-qc/9409043 p.1: "it is now realised that in general the ANEC must fail. See the 'note added in proof' on page 415 of [W-Y]". W-Y's form of the condition (Kontou-Sanders eq. 85) is a lim inf over widening C^1_0 test-function windows. The titles are "General proof of the averaged null energy condition for a massless scalar field in two-dimensional curved space-time" (W-Y) and "Averaged energy conditions for free scalar fields in flat space-times" (Klinkhammer). Fewster-Roman pp.9-10 show that their own states obey ANEC: phi -> 0 (II.37) and psi -> 2 pi f(0) int u^2 C(u,u) du >= 0 (II.38).
published_hypotheses: H1 FIELD: a free scalar field. Klinkhammer: massless or massive, any curvature coupling xi. W-Y: minimally coupled in 4D Minkowski, massless in the 2D curved general proof. The electromagnetic field came later (Folacci 1992).

H2 BACKGROUND: Klinkhammer: n-dimensional Minkowski space. W-Y: 4D Minkowski (restricted class of states) and globally hyperbolic 2D curved spacetime (general proof). Neither proves a 4D curved result, and W-Y's note added in proof says ANEC fails for generic perturbations of Minkowski in 4D.

H3 STATES: Klinkhammer: a dense set in the Minkowski-vacuum Fock space, namely finite combinations of finite-particle states of bounded momentum. W-Y: a large or restricted subclass of Hadamard states in 4D Minkowski; all Hadamard states for the massless field in 2D.

H4 GEODESIC: a complete, affinely parametrised null geodesic. It must be achronal in the 2D curved theorem; in Minkowski every null geodesic is achronal. Klinkhammer gives negative results along non-geodesic curves and along chronal geodesics in compactified flat space.

H5 FORMULATION: either a lim inf over widening test-function windows (W-Y) or an absolutely convergent integral, with <T_ab> normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, so the vacuum gives 0 by construction.
H6 TEST FIELD: no back-reaction; the semiclassical Einstein equation is not imposed.

geodesic-slicing-existence.name: Existence of geodesic (Gaussian normal, Phi = 0) slicing

source.located: Gaussian normal coordinates / geodesic slicing, classically G. Darmois (1927), Wald, General Relativity (1984) sec 3.3 and Lemma 9.2.1, and Smarr & York, PRD 17, 2529 (1978). None of these has an arXiv copy. Read in E. Gourgoulhon, '3+1 formalism and bases of numerical relativity', arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): sec 3.3.3 eq (3.18), sec 4.4.2 pp.61-62, sec 9.2.1 pp.152-153.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/0703035. The review states the result itself, so it is the source read. Darmois 1927, Wald 1984 and Smarr-York 1978 are NAMED-NOT-READ (cited there as refs [105], [265], [247]). A title search for Smarr-York returned an unrelated paper (2107.06551) that only cites it.

geodesic-slicing-existence.published_statement: Gourgoulhon gr-qc/0703035 pp.61-62: 'we set N = 1 (4.75), beta = 0 (4.76) in some neighbourhood [of] a given hypersurface Sigma_0 ... Such coordinates are called Gaussian normal coordinates. The foliation away from Sigma_0 selected by the choice (4.75) of the lapse function is called a geodesic slicing ... the worldlines of the Eulerian observers are geodesics ... g = -dt^2 + gamma_ij dx^i dx^j. In general it is not possible to get a Gaussian normal coordinate system that covers all M. This results from the well known tendencies of timelike geodesics without vorticity ... to focus and eventually cross ... (cf. Lemma 9.2.1 in [Wald]). However ... provided that the neighbourhood is small enough, this is always possible.' Eq (3.18): a = D ln N, so N = 1 means geodesic observers. Sec 9.2.1 p.152: 'this type of foliation can become pathological within a finite range of t'. The geodesic slicing from the t_S = 0 Schwarzschild slice 'hits the singularity at t = [pi] m'.
published_hypotheses: a smooth spacelike hypersurface Sigma_0 is GIVEN; the slicing is generated by the geodesics normal to THAT Sigma_0 (p.62)
LOCAL: exists only 'in some neighbourhood' of Sigma_0 'small enough', i.e. until the normal geodesics focus or cross; not global in general (p.62, p.152; Wald Lemma 9.2.1 / Raychaudhuri)
lapse and shift are free gauge choices that leave the physical solution g unchanged; 'the only things to avoid are coordinate singularities' (p.61)
globally hyperbolic spacetime, so that a foliation exists at all (sec 3.2, p.39)
hypothesis_drift: LOCALITY DROPPED. nonstatic.py:87 says 'in geodesic slicing (Phi = 0, always available)'. The source says it is available only 'in some neighbourhood ... small enough' and 'In general it is not possible ... that covers all M' (p.62). Two exact counter-cases are computed here. (D) Flat space: the geodesic slicing normal to t = -sqrt(tau0^2+r^2) sends every normal through the origin at proper time tau0. That is a caustic with T_ab = 0, the time-reverse of the tree's own Milne witness. (E) Schwarzschild: the slicing from t_S = 0 reaches R = 0 at the throat at tau = pi m. The canonical entry's hypothesis list carries this locality; the owner's prose does not.

ADDED HYPOTHESIS: A NEW FOLIATION UNLESS D_r Phi = 0. This is not stated at nonstatic.py:86-89. Check B: the Eulerian acceleration is a_rhat = e^-Lambda Phi' (Gourgoulhon 3.18). Relabelling t shifts Phi by ln f', one number per slice, so Phi can be set to 0 on the same slices only where Phi' = 0 (z3 unsat otherwise). Otherwise geodesic slicing uses different slices, and W is a slice component: the tree says so itself at nonstatic.py:209-218. Check C: under a radial boost of the normal, W' = g(W+vU); only W^2-U^2 is invariant. The two Minkowski witnesses (nonstatic.py:448-449) are both Phi = 0 slicings of the same spacetime, with W = 1 and W = cosh chi. So 'D_t W = 4 pi R j, W constant exactly when j = 0' (nonstatic.py:87-88) is exact, but for the W and j of the geodesic congruence. These agree with the corridor's original W only on the initial slice. 'No flux ... to keep a corridor open' (nonstatic.py:88-89) holds only in that sense. foliation.py:337-347 independently re-reads E = R dGamma as a gauge price.

SPHERICAL SYMMETRY PRESERVED (canonical hypothesis 2). This holds when Sigma_0 is SO(3)-invariant, since the normal geodesics are then radial. It is argued by symmetry, not machine-checked, and it is not a drift. Every witness the tree actually runs is spherical with Phi = 0 (nonstatic.py:448-451).

IMPLICIT U = 0 CONDITION IN THE BUILD-ENERGY USE (nonstatic.py:178-183, '(R held fixed)', E = R Delta W). E = R Delta W is exact only if R stays fixed along the geodesic observer on the boundary sphere, i.e. U = 0. Under that reading, the tree's own MS-t and EV-W at Phi = 0 give m = R(1-W^2)/2, and EV-U then needs p_r = (W^2-1)/(8 pi R^2). At Delta W = 1 the enclosed Misner-Sharp mass is -3R/2 = -4.08e13 M_sun for the Proxima span (check F). This is a discrepancy with nonstatic.py:195-197 ('positive energy to be passed through a boundary, which is a change in KIND'), and it is consistent with the tree's own anchor lemma (nonstatic.py:113-119). It is a finding about the tree's use, conditional on the U = 0 reading, not about the external theorem. Nothing was repaired.

quant-ph/0504143.published_statement: quant-ph/0504143 eq. (15): 'the asymptotic form of T_xx near the boundary z = 0 is one half the corresponding expression for U in this limit, which was found in Ref. [14]: T_xx ~ (1/2) U ~ (sqrt2 omega_p/(128 pi)) (1/z^3), as z -> 0.' Units: Lorentz-Heaviside, hbar = c = 1. The origin is quant-ph/0204125 eq. So sqrt2/(128 pi) is the coefficient of the TRANSVERSE pressure T_xx, and U's coefficient is twice it. casimir-1948-parallel-plates.published_statement: As restated in quant-ph/0106045 p.25, eqs 2.36-2.37: for two perfectly conducting parallel plates of area S -> oo at separation a, the renormalised vacuum energy is E0ren(a) = -(c hbar pi^2/(720 a^3)) S, with the Minkowski contribution in the gap subtracted. The force is F(a) = -dE/da = -(pi^2/240)(hbar c/a^4) S. Mostepanenko 2021 pp.1-2: 'two parallel, electrically neutral ideal metal plates at zero temperature ... F_IM(a) = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4) ... E_IM(a) = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3). This is the Casimir energy per unit area.' The LOCAL energy density is not Casimir's 1948 statement but Brown-Maclay 1969. Sopova-Ford p.1 restates it: 'for perfectly conducting plates, one has a constant negative vacuum energy density'. Their eq (52) gives U = -pi^2/(720 a^4) in the limit omega_p -> oo.
published_hypotheses: Perfect conductors: E_t|S = H_n|S = 0 on both plates (review eq 2.27). Review p.154: 'valid only for perfect conductors of infinitely high conductivity ... for sufficiently high frequency any metal becomes transparent'.
Infinite plane-parallel plates, S -> oo (review eq 2.29).
Zero temperature (Mostepanenko 2021 p.1). Review p.79: the thermal effect is negligible for a << hbar c/(k_B T).
A free quantised EM field in the gap with two polarisations, renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski vacuum in the same volume (review eq 2.33).

For the local density (Brown-Maclay via Sopova-Ford) perfect conductivity is again assumed. A dispersive wall adds a positive position-dependent term that diverges at the interface. The midpoint density is then negative only for omega_p a > ~99, i.e. a > 1.3 um at 14.8 eV (Sopova-Ford eqs 50-51).

Real metals reach the ideal limit only for a >> lambda_p; the perturbation expansion is valid for a >= lambda_p (review pp.155-156). Below a few nm the Casimir force is the non-retarded van der Waals force, F = -H/(6 pi a^3) (Mostepanenko 2021 p.2; review eq 4.27).

casimir-1948-parallel-plates.lacked_data:
Casimir (1948) lacked any measurement: Sparnaay's 1958 attempt was only 'not contradicting', and the parallel-plate test at 15% came in 2002. He also lacked the optical response of real plates, which Lifshitz supplied in 1956. Having these data does not change his conclusion within its hypotheses. The ideal coefficient is re-derived exactly here, and the 2002 coefficient agrees at -0.45 sigma. The Drude/plasma puzzle concerns few-percent real-material corrections, not the ideal limit.

What the later data do change is the domain. The formula is the a >> lambda_p limit, and the tree uses it at 10 nm, 1 nm, 0.1 nm and 0.37 l_P. There the plasma-model interaction energy is 11%, 1.3% and 0.13% of the ideal value, and the midpoint local density is positive.

So M's hypothesis holds here in a form that does not help the device. The missing data narrow where the formula applies but do not make it wrong, and every correction lowers |rho| and enlarges the shortfall. The energy density itself has never been observed (Sopova-Ford p.16), so calling it 'MEASURED' is a status-word discrepancy, not a refutation.
casimir-1948-parallel-plates.grade_evidence:
The result as published STANDS on its own hypotheses. Script sections A-C re-derive it symbolically, the tree's numbers reproduce (D), no datum has moved (E), and the only parallel-plate measurement read agrees (pull -0.45 sigma).

The tree's use covers a larger class than the result does:
(1) It drops the perfect-conductor condition a >> lambda_p and evaluates the formula at 10 nm, 1 nm and 0.1 nm (achievable.py:124-141, 532-547; candidates.py:129-135). There the plasma-model Lifshitz result is 0.111, 0.0130 and 0.00132 of the ideal energy.
(2) It calls the energy density MEASURED (achievable.py:31, 417-419; candidates.py:73-74). Only the force is measured: 0.5-3 um for parallel plates, above ~120 nm for sphere-plate.
(3) Its KIND pass (candidates.py:78) holds only for a >~ 1.3 um in Al. At the gaps it prices, the plasma-model midpoint density is positive (G).

It is not WRONG, because there is no counterexample to the published result. Every narrowing lowers the available |rho|, so the tree's refusals stand unchanged or stronger. Its numbers are ideal-plate upper bounds, not physical Casimir values.
casimir-1948-parallel-plates.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: the owners limit the use to ideal plates, relabel the density as an inferred ideal-plate QFT value (the force is what is MEASURED), and present the nm rows as upper bounds. 1205.6497.published_statement: Conclusions (printed p.27): 'We find that, for M_h = 125 GeV, lambda(M_Pl) = -0.014+-0.006, see eq. (64). The exact vanishing of lambda(M_Pl) is excluded at 2 sigma. Moreover, the smallness of beta_lambda at high energy implies that lambda remains negative in a relatively large energy range. Indeed, we find that, for M_h = 125 GeV, the instability scale develops at 10^{11+-1} GeV. Quantum tunneling is sufficiently slow to ensure at least metastability of the EW vacuum, see fig. 5. ... beta_lambda ... vanishes at a scale of about 3 x 10^17 GeV.' Sec. 1 (printed p.2): 'M_h [GeV] > 129.4 + 1.4((M_t - 173.1)/0.7) - 0.5((alpha_s(M_Z) - 0.1184)/0.0007) +- 1.0_th (2). Combining in quadrature the theoretical uncertainty with the experimental errors on M_t and alpha_s we get M_h > 129.4 +- 1.8 GeV (3). From this result we conclude that vacuum stability of the SM up to the Planck scale is excluded at 2 sigma (98% C.L. one sided) for M_h < 126 GeV.' Fig. 4 caption: 'The instability scale Lambda_I at which the SM potential becomes negative ... 1 sigma bands in M_t = 173.1 +- 0.6 GeV, alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1184 +- 0.0007, M_h = 125.66 +- 0.34 GeV ... The theoretical error is not shown and corresponds to a +-1 GeV uncertainty in M_h.'
published_hypotheses: The Standard Model alone, extrapolated to the Planck scale. The paper says it 'ignores possible new (unknown) UV threshold effects occurring near the Planck scale' (printed p.27). No new physics, and gravity is not included.

Lambda_I is defined as the field value where the two-loop RG-improved potential V_eff = lambda_eff(h) h^4/4 turns negative (eq. 51, Fig. 4). The paper names no gauge and does not discuss the gauge dependence of this value.

gr-qc/9305017.name: Topological censorship (Friedman-Schleich-Witt): a traversable wormhole requires ANEC violation

source.located: J.L. Friedman, K. Schleich, D.M. Witt, 'Topological Censorship', PRL 71 1486 (1993), arXiv:gr-qc/9305017v2 (9 Jun 1995). Pages used: the abstract; p.3 (ANEC definition and Theorem 1); pp.4-5 (Lemmas 1-2 and their proofs); pp.5-7 (proof of Theorem 1 and the Penrose-Sorkin-Woolgar alternate proof); pp.8-9 (the withdrawn v1 Theorem 2, which fell to Burnett gr-qc/9504012, and the semiclassical remark).
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) on arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9305017: the whole v2 text was read. Also read at source for comparison: Galloway-Schleich-Witt-Woolgar gr-qc/9902061 pp.1, 3-6, 8-11 (Thm 2.1, Thm 2.2 and the remark after them); Graham-Olum 0705.3193 pp.1-8 (whole paper); Schleich-Witt gr-qc/9903061 pp.1-12 (whole). Galloway CQG 12 L99 (1995), Borde CQG 4 343 (1987) and Tipler PRD 17 2521 (1978) are NAMED-NOT-READ; they are known here only through the GSWW, FSW and Graham-Olum restatements.

gr-qc/9305017.published_statement: FSW v2 p.3 defines ANEC this way: 'A spacetime satisfies ANEC if the integral of T_ab k^a k^b is nonnegative along every inextendible null geodesic with affine parameter lambda and corresponding tangent k^a.' The theorem reads: 'Theorem 1. If an asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic spacetime (M, g_ab) satisfies the averaged null energy condition, then every causal curve from J- to J+ is deformable to gamma_0 rel J.' Here gamma_0 is a timelike curve from J- to J+ lying in a simply connected neighbourhood of J. The abstract states the theorem with the pointwise null energy condition instead. The Lemma 2 proof (p.5) says: 'ANEC and theta < 0 imply that every outward null geodesic from the outer trapped surface T has a conjugate point within finite affine parameter length.' On p.8 the authors add that 'any energy condition which implies that outward directed null congruences with theta < 0 have conjugate points will suffice', and they leave the semiclassical case open (citing Wald-Yurtsever). On p.4 they note: 'If the Poincare conjecture is false, the theorem does not prevent one from probing fake 3-spheres.'
published_hypotheses: H1 asymptotic flatness: there is a conformal completion with Omega vanishing on J and a nonvanishing null gradient. J = J+ U J-, each part S^2 x R with complete null generators; completeness in the future direction is not required (p.2).
H2 global hyperbolicity: M = D(Sigma) for a Cauchy surface Sigma (p.2).
H3 ANEC on EVERY inextendible null geodesic: INT T_ab k^a k^b dlambda >= 0 (p.3). The abstract states the pointwise NEC instead.
H4 (implicit) the Einstein equations hold, so a condition on T_ab is a condition on R_ab k^a k^b. GSWW gr-qc/9902061 p.8 makes this explicit.

H5 (implicit in the proof) the conjugate-point step needs the integral along the HALF-geodesic that starts on the trapped surface. Galloway 1995 and GSWW Thm 2.1(iii) state the condition in that form: INT_0^inf Ric >= 0 along every future-complete null geodesic. GSWW call it 'a modified form of the ANEC'.
H6 the source is classical: FSW treat semiclassical validity as a question, not a result.
The theorem is about ACTIVE censorship only, i.e. causal curves from J- to J+. Passive detection is allowed, as in the RP^3 geon. The v1 Theorem 2 is withdrawn in v2 as false.
The fake-3-sphere caveat depends on the Poincare conjecture, which was open in 1993-95.
hypothesis_drift: higgs.py:124 ('A WORMHOLE NEEDS ANEC, by topological censorship') drops H1 (asymptotic flatness) and H2 (global hyperbolicity). It names no form of the energy condition: FSW's whole-line H3, the half-line H5 that the proof actually needs, or whole-line ANEC plus the null generic condition. It also leaves H4 unstated. In its own context (the nonminimal xi phi^2 R coupling, Barcelo-Visser) the condition that enters the proof is on the effective R_kk, which is what Barcelo-Visser eq. (2.6) computes, so this omission changes nothing there. The contrapositive only puts the ANEC failure on SOME null geodesic, not specifically on the radial throat geodesic that Barcelo-Visser integrate. The higgs.py conclusion rests on Barcelo-Visser, read at source, not on FSW.

anecscope.py:32-33 ('what the topological-censorship and no-wormhole results actually use') and anecscope.py:170 ('what topological censorship actually uses') attribute achronal ANEC to FSW, but FSW's H3 covers every inextendible null geodesic, not only achronal ones. (a) The spacetime must be simply connected, so it only rules out wormholes between different asymptotically flat regions, not wormholes back into the same region (p.5). (A) sympy: with R_kk = 0 and theta0 < 0, theta = theta0/(1 + theta0 lam/2) solves the equation exactly (residual 0), with the focal point at 2/|theta0|. (B) 400 out of 400 random profiles satisfying the half-line condition focus before 2/|theta0| (largest ratio 0.981). This is sampling, not a proof. (C) The inference step of FSW Lemma 2, as FSW word it, fails. Take theta = -c e^{-lam} for lam >= 0. This needs R_kk = -c e^{-lam} - (c^2/2) e^{-2lam}, whose half-line integral is -c(c+4)/4 < 0. A continuous branch for lam < 0 with K = 3c^2/8 + c + delta/2 makes the whole-line integral equal to delta >= 0. The congruence starting at the trapped surface (theta0 < 0) never focuses (RK4 run out to lam = 60). z3 confirms this for every c > 0 (the negation is unsat). This is a gap in one step of the written proof, not a counterexample to Theorem 1. The half-line form (Galloway; GSWW Thm 2.1(iii)) closes it, and so does whole-line ANEC plus the generic condition. (D) A Minkowski null line has ANEC integral 0 and does not focus, so non-strict ANEC alone cannot rule out a null line; that route needs the generic condition. (E) z3: if 0 < d < L, the through-throat path is chronal, and if L <= d it is not (both negations unsat). So Ford's same-universe wormhole lies outside the achronal version.

gr-qc/9305017.lacked_data: (1) The Poincare conjecture, proved 2002-03 (NAMED-NOT-READ here). It removes FSW's own fake-3-sphere caveat, and Theorem 1 never depended on it, so it extends the result without moving it. (2) The right form of the energy condition for the Lemma 2 step. FSW's H3 is over whole geodesics, and check C builds a profile where the whole-line integral is >= 0 but the trapped congruence never focuses. Galloway (1995) supplied the half-line form, and GSWW, which includes two of the original authors, adopted it. This is evidence FOR M's suspicion that a published statement was incomplete. But the repair keeps the conclusion: no counterexample to the corrected theorem is known, and none is shown here. (3) Semiclassical data. FSW already knew that ANEC fails for quantum fields (Wald-Yurtsever) and left that case open. Later results change how far the theorem applies to quantum matter, not whether it is true as a conditional; self-consistent achronal ANEC is still unproven. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the conclusion has been re-proved under several alternative hypotheses (half-line ANEC; whole-line ANEC plus generic; achronal ANEC plus simple connectivity plus generic; timelike scri; weak cosmic censorship in place of global hyperbolicity), and no measured datum enters it. Net: incomplete as published in one hypothesis, not wrong.
gr-qc/9305017.grade_evidence: (i) The source against its own proof: FSW define ANEC over whole inextendible geodesics (p.3), but Lemma 2 needs the half-line integral. Check C shows the step fails from the whole-line form alone (sympy + z3, exit 0). thermal-state-kms-hadamard.published_statement: (A) Sahlmann-Verch 2000, Thm 5.1: 'Let omega in P and let omega_2 be the two-point distribution of omega. Suppose that WF(omega_2^(P)) = empty = WF(omega_2(P)), and suppose also that the symmetric part or the anti-symmetric part of the two-point distribution is smooth at causal separation. Then it holds that WF(omega_2) subset R.' Here P is the set of finite convex combinations of ground states or KMS states at beta > 0, taken for the flow of an everywhere-timelike Killing field on a globally hyperbolic stationary spacetime. From p.23: 'for the canonically quantized scalar Klein-Gordon field, WF(omega_2) subset R implies WF(omega_2) = R and thus the two-point function of every strictly passive state is of Hadamard form' (citing Radzikowski). On quasifreeness SV say only (p.19) that ground and KMS states 'turn out to be quasifree in examples'. (B) Sanders 2013, Thm 6.2, stated for V > 0: '(i) There exists a unique extremal C^1 beta-KMS state with vanishing one-point function ... (ii) [it] is quasi-free, regular ... (iv) Any D^2 beta-KMS state is Hadamard ... (v) Any extremal beta-KMS state ... is of the form eta*_rho omega_0 for some gauge transformation of the second kind'. (C) Khavkine-Moretti Def. 15 and Thm 9(b): a two-point function is Hadamard when it differs locally from the Hadamard parametrix by a smooth function, and two Hadamard two-point functions differ by a C^infinity function.
published_hypotheses: SV Thm 5.1: the spacetime is globally hyperbolic and stationary, and the flow is generated by an everywhere TIMELIKE, future-pointing Killing field
SV Thm 5.1: the state is strictly passive, i.e. a finite convex sum of ground states or KMS states with beta_i > 0 (beta = 0 excluded)
SV Thm 5.1: omega_2 is a distribution and a bisolution up to C^infinity
SV Thm 5.1: the symmetric or the antisymmetric part of omega_2 is smooth at causal (spacelike) separation

SV p.23 / Radzikowski: passing from WF subset R to Hadamard form is done for the CCR scalar Klein-Gordon field. Khavkine-Moretti Thm 9 states it for any m^2 and xi in d = 4, and their Remark 23 records a gap in Radzikowski's original proof, filled by Sahlmann-Verch 2001 and by Khavkine-Moretti
SV: quasifreeness is not derived; they say only 'quasifree in examples'
Sanders Thm 6.2 requires V > 0, which in Minkowski means m > 0; the massless field is outside the theorem. Its uniqueness holds only among extremal C^1 KMS states WITH VANISHING ONE-POINT FUNCTION
PSV 1806.02124: a KMS state taken along a flow that is spacelike at x is not Hadamard at x

godel-1949-ctc-metric.name: Goedel 1949: an exact Lorentzian (Einstein) solution containing closed timelike curves

source.located: K. Goedel, Rev. Mod. Phys. 21, 447 (1949), which has no arXiv copy. It is restated exactly in: Kajari-Walser-Schleich-Delgado arXiv:gr-qc/0404032 Sec.3.1 eq.(15), with the field-equation relations after eq.(18); Buser-Kajari-Schleich arXiv:1303.4651 eq.(1), Sec.2.1 and Sec.5 p.27; Verma-Aluri-Mota-Obukhov arXiv:2506.00860 eq.(1) (misprinted there); Luminet arXiv:2101.08592 pp.1-6.

godel-1949-ctc-metric.published_statement: As restated: 'in 1949 Kurt Goedel derived an exact solution of Einstein's field equations, in which a homogeneous mass distribution rotates around every point in space. This solution shows rather unusual properties such as closed time like world-lines' (gr-qc/0404032 p.2). Line element (gr-qc/0404032 eq.15): ds^2/(4a^2) = dt^2 - dr^2 - (sinh^2 r - sinh^4 r) dphi^2 - dz^2 + 2 sqrt2 sinh^2 r dphi dt. It solves R_mn - g R/2 = kappa T + Lambda g for a perfect fluid with kappa(rho + p/c^2) = 1/(a^2 c^2) and kappa p = Lambda + 1/(2a^2); for dust, Lambda = -1/(2a^2). 'a homogeneous solution with trivial topology R^4 yet contains CTCs through every point' (hep-th/0209114 p.3). 'infinite, non-expanding ... matter rotates relative to the compass of inertia with the angular velocity 2(pi G rho)^(1/2)' (2101.08592 p.1).
published_hypotheses: Einstein's field equations with a cosmological constant: R_mn - g R/2 = kappa T + Lambda g
Source: pressure-free perfect fluid (dust) with rho > 0 and comoving u = d_t, and Lambda = -1/(2a^2) < 0 ('pressureless dust balanced by a negative cosmological constant', hep-th/0209114 p.13)
Stationary and spatially homogeneous (five Killing vectors), not static, not isotropic; non-expanding, shear-free, rigidly rotating with Omega_G = c/(sqrt2 a)
Manifold R^4 with trivial topology: the CTCs do not come from an identification
Four spacetime dimensions
The CTCs are not geodesics: 'a proper acceleration has to be applied' (1303.4651 p.27)
Goedel did not offer it as a model of our universe, since it has no redshift (1303.4651 p.3)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED DIMENSION, supplied by a trivial construction rather than by Goedel (latticectc.py:82-83, "there exists a 5D Lorentzian metric containing a CTC -- Goedel 1949"). Goedel's solution is 4D. The 5D statement follows at once: Goedel x R, with a flat fifth direction, is Lorentzian and carries the same CTC (E5a). An exact 5D Goedel analogue in minimal supergravity also exists (hep-th/0209114 eq.3.29; E5c, E5e). The attribution is loose; the statement is true.

WEAKENED: the owner at latticectc.py:82-83 takes only the bare existence of a Lorentzian metric with a CTC. That needs neither Goedel nor any field equation: flat space with a periodic time already has one (2101.08592 p.4; E7; the causal-lattice case of D21). So 'never in doubt' is accurate for the statement as used. Goedel's actual content is stronger: an exact Einstein solution on R^4, with positive-density dust and CTCs through every point (E1, E2, E3).

THE LABEL UNDERSTATES THE SOURCE (latticectc.py:141-144, CODIM1_CTC_REFUSAL '... NEC-violating on the CTC slice -- Goedel-class, not a braneworld'; mirrored at LEDGER.md:44 and :117). The refused metric has no field equation and violates the NEC (latticectc.py:76-86), so it falls below Goedel's class rather than inside it. This is a discrepancy of description, and it strengthens the refusal's 'adds nothing': a NEC-satisfying 5D CTC metric already exists (E5b, Goedel x R, with the stress tensor read off its own Einstein tensor; E5c/E5c'', GGHPR with a Maxwell source).
