godel-1949-ctc-metric.lacked_data: In 1949 Goedel lacked the CMB and every vorticity limit built on it, the causal-structure machinery (Hawking-Ellis 1973; chronology protection 1992), brane and higher-dimensional frameworks, and string corrections. He did have Hubble's expansion, and he said himself that his model lacks it. On the evidence here, having the later data does not change the conclusion, and the evidence runs both ways. For stability: the result is closed-form and uses no data, it is re-derived exactly (E1, E3), and the CTC survives the brane generalisation at effective-equation level (Barrow-Tsagas, E6). Against physical relevance: observation disfavours global rotation (limits cited, NOT read), and some Goedel-type solutions with extra sources avoid CTCs. Those are different solutions, though, and they bear on whether nature realises Goedel's universe, which the tree never claims. The tree uses only 'a Lorentzian metric with a CTC exists'. It contains the closed timelike circle at r > ln(1+sqrt2), on a regular axis (E3c-f), and by transitivity such a curve passes through every point (E2b). The 5D version holds via Goedel x R (E5a) and via the exact GGHPR solution (E5c, E5e). No datum enters. Four discrepancies are recorded, none repaired, and none moves the grade. (1) 5D is a trivial corollary of Goedel, not his statement. (2) The label 'Goedel-class' at :144 understates Goedel: his source satisfies NEC and WEC (E4) and solves the field equations, so the refused NEC-violating metric with no field equation falls below his class. That strengthens the refusal. (3) 2506.00860 eq.(1) misprints the metric, which is degenerate as printed (E1a'). bell-pair-entanglement-entropy.published_statement: quant-ph/9511030 p.4: 'The entanglement of a partly-entangled pure state can be naturally parameterized by its entropy of entanglement, defined as the von Neumann entropy of either rho_A or rho_B, or equivalently as the Shannon entropy of the squares of the Schmidt coefficients. E = -Tr rho_A log2 rho_A = -Tr rho_B log2 rho_B = -sum_i c_i^2 log2 c_i^2. (4) ... The quantity E ... ranges from zero for a product state (eg theta = 0) to 1 ebit for a maximally entangled pair of two-state particles (eg theta = pi/4).' p.2: 'the consumption of one shared ebit, together with the transmission of a two-bit classical message, can be substituted for the transmission of one qubit.' p.6: 'neither the measurement of k nor any other local processing by one or both parties can increase the expected entropy of entanglement'. p.16: 'entropy of entanglement is a good entanglement measure for pure states ... No similarly simple entanglement measure is known for mixed states.'
published_hypotheses: H1 The bipartite state Psi(A,B) is PURE (eq. (2)). For mixed states, S(rho_A) and S(rho_B) are not the entanglement (p.16, counterexample of classically correlated spins).
H2 The bipartition is fixed, and E is the entropy of either reduced state. The two entropies are equal for pure states by the Schmidt decomposition (eq. (3)).
H3 The logarithm is base 2 and the unit is the ebit (eq. (4), p.2).
H4 'Maximally entangled' means all Schmidt coefficients are equal. For d=2 that gives exactly 1 ebit, and in general log2 d (p.4).
H5 The operational meaning (concentration yield and dilution cost) is asymptotic under LOCC. The value E itself is a closed-form function of a single copy.
H6 Under LOCC the expected E does not increase (p.6). This is a monotone. Conservation holds only asymptotically, for reversible pure-state concentration and dilution (abstract, p.16).
hypothesis_drift: KEPT: transit.py:78-85 (entropy2) computes -sum l log2 l over the eigenvalues of the 2x2 reduced state. At transit.py:315 it is applied to ptrace_first(rho_from(BELL)), where BELL=(|00>+|11>)/sqrt2 is defined at transit.py:90. That state is pure with equal Schmidt weights, so H1-H4 are kept.

NOT STATED AT SITE (purity, H1): transit.py:138 'CHANNEL_BITS_BEFORE = 1.0 # entanglement entropy of a Bell pair' carries no purity qualifier; the hypothesis is named only in the canonical entry. For a mixed channel, S(rho_B)=1 bit for every Werner weight p, including the separable range p<=1/3 (rederive C7). This matters only if R11 (specthm.py:1168; LEDGER.md:177) is applied to a physical, imperfect channel.

Rederive C6 shows the ebit is TRANSFERRED to a reference R, never multiplied, and that is what forces one pair per transit. This is a discrepancy of wording, not a refutation.

bell-pair-entanglement-entropy.lacked_data: Nothing the 1995 authors lacked bears on this result. E(Bell)=1 ebit is a definition (eq. (4)) evaluated on an exactly specified state and depends on no measured quantity; sympy reproduces it exactly. Later work (quant-ph/0702225 pp.65-67) added the uniqueness theorem and showed that all operational measures agree on pure states, which strengthens the result rather than moving it. Data could matter only outside the result as published. A physical Bell pair is never exactly pure, and for a mixed channel S(rho_B) stays at 1 bit while the entanglement falls (C7). So a future use of transit.py's constant for a real channel (R11) would need the channel's measured state and a mixed-state measure. kodama-1980-mass-flux.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002 App. B, pp.19-20: 'Kodama introduced vectors k and j which may be defined, up to orientation, by k = curl r (B1) and g(j) = -T(k) (B2) where the curl refers to the two-dimensional quotient space-time. It follows that g(k,k) = 2E/r - 1 (B3) ... k is spatial in trapped regions and causal otherwise ... Fixing the orientation so that k and j are future-causal for untrapped spheres ... (B4a,b). Thus k is tangent to the constant-r hypersurfaces (B5a) ... 4 pi r^2 j = curl E (B6) ... both k and j are covariantly conserved (B7) ... By Gauss' law, any such conserved current u has a charge ... independent of Sigma (with fixed boundaries) ... Q_j = INT *T(k,v) = INT_0 E' dzeta = E (B8b). The charge Q_j is the definition of energy of Kodama [53].' Abreu-Visser 1004.1456 pp.3-4: k^a = eps_perp^{ab} nabla_b r (24); nabla_a k^a = 0 (30); J^a = G^{ab} k_b with nabla_a J^a = 0 (31), 'a purely geometrical statement ... not related to the Bianchi identities'; J^a = -(2/r^2) eps_perp^{ab} nabla_b m (39). Sec. IX: the fixed-r flux taken without the W factor integrates to the Brown-York energy U = r0(1 - sqrt(1-2m/r0)) (81).
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry: a warped product of a (1+1) Lorentzian base with round 2-spheres, areal radius r > 0 (Hayward p.2; Abreu-Visser eq.1; Kinoshita eq.15).
Four spacetime dimensions for the classic statement (Kinoshita generalises to D dimensions).

Conservation of k and of J = G.k is a geometric identity that uses no field equation (Abreu-Visser eq.31; Kinoshita p.6). Reading J as an energy current, with its charge as matter energy, needs G = 8 pi T (Kinoshita p.1; Hayward B2 uses T).
No cosmological constant, for the charge to equal the Misner-Sharp mass of matter (Kinoshita eq.23).

Orientation fixed so that k and j are future-causal on untrapped spheres; k is timelike only where the sphere is untrapped. Normalisation |k|^2 = |1 - 2m/r| (Hayward B3; Abreu-Visser eq.56). The Kodama energy depends on this normalisation.
Hayward's (B8b), as written, integrates from a regular centre. The charge between two spheres is the difference of E by Gauss' law and needs no centre.
Units G = c = 1.

Without it the integral is E = R(W_1 - 1) (formation.py:135), which is minus the Brown-York energy of Abreu-Visser eq.81 (C7k-l) and is not -m_1 (vacuity guard C7j). The tree keeps E and K separate and correctly labels K as the Kodama one.

The tree's number m_1(R_s+) - m_1(R_s-) is exactly the Kodama charge between the two spheres that bound the shell (Gauss' law, C5). The value 2.00010e-02 was reproduced independently (C8b).

In Planck units, kappa^-1 is the squared value of the reduced Planck mass M_P, and thus b1 is much larger than the remaining renormalisation constants. Hence ... gamma~ ~= -b0/b1 = -16 pi G alpha~^S_1 m^4 and it does not depend on the choice of alpha~^S_3 and xi. Thus, the effective Hubble parameter of the predicted de Sitter spacetime reads H = sqrt(-gamma~), and hence we obtain the following value of the cosmological constant in Planck units according to the (semiclassical) Friedmann equations Lambda = 3 Omega_Lambda H^2 = 6 Omega_Lambda alpha~^S_1 (m/M_P)^4 M_P^2 ... nmc-classical-nec-violation.published_statement: Barcelo-Visser abstract (p.1): 'We demonstrate that a non-minimally coupled scalar field with a positive curvature coupling xi > 0 can easily violate all the standard energy conditions, up to and including the averaged null energy condition (ANEC).' Sec. 2.2 (p.5), eq. (2.6): 'G_mn k^m k^n = (1/kappa)[T^eff]_mn k^m k^n = [phi'^2 - xi (phi^2)''] / (kappa - xi phi^2) >= 0. This condition is clearly satisfied by minimally coupled scalars. However, for xi != 0 it can be violated in a number of ways: For xi < 0 any local minimum of phi^2 violates the NEC while for xi > 0 and |phi| small, [meaning |phi| < (kappa/xi)^(1/2)], any local maximum of phi^2 violates the NEC. Finally for xi > 0 and |phi| large ... any local minimum of phi^2 violates the NEC.' Also p.5: the NEC 'is the weakest pointwise energy condition, that is, when it is violated the WEC and SEC are violated too.' FFKPS sec. I (p.3): 'delta L = xi R phi^2 allow violations of the NEC even at the classical level'; 'At the classical level, the effective NEC can be violated by non-minimal coupling of either sign ... However, the effective ANEC ... is satisfied' (under their EFT field-range assumption); 'non-minimal coupling can be eliminated by a combined conformal transformation and field redefinition ... to the Einstein frame, where the NEC is obeyed.' FO 0708.2450 p.1: the classical stress-energy tensor 'does not satisfy the weak energy condition (WEC) at non-minimal coupling, i.e., xi != 0'.
published_hypotheses: BV: a classical (unquantised) real scalar field; the analysis is 'completely classical' (p.5)
BV: action (2.1) with -1/2 xi R phi^2 in the matter Lagrangian, mostly-plus signature, kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N), four dimensions
BV: the energy conditions are imposed on the EFFECTIVE stress tensor T^eff (2.3), i.e. on the Einstein tensor of the metric g in (2.1) (Jordan frame). This requires kappa - xi phi^2 != 0
BV: pointwise conditions along an affinely parametrised geodesic. The NEC statement does not depend on V
BV: the statement is EXISTENTIAL: the NEC 'can be violated' at configurations meeting the sign condition, not at every configuration
BV: the NEC can be violated for any xi != 0, of either sign. 'All standard energy conditions up to ANEC' is claimed for xi > 0, and violating ANEC needs |phi| > (kappa/xi)^(1/2)
FFKPS: the violation is of the 'effective NEC' in the Jordan frame; the Einstein-frame metric obeys the NEC

gr-qc/9607003-sec4-curved.published_statement: p.11 (Sec. 4), verbatim: 'Note that in Minkowski spacetime, our bounds hold for an arbitrary choice of the sampling time, t0. Recently we argued that such bounds should also hold in a curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries, if the sampling time is restricted to be much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]. An explicit example of the validity of this assumption has been given in Ref. [24]. There a QI is derived in the static closed and open Robertson-Walker universe models. For a choice of sampling time which is small compared to the local radius of curvature, the QI reduces to our flat spacetime bound.' pp.2-3 (Sec. 1), verbatim: 'These inequalities were derived for Minkowski spacetime, in the absence of boundaries. However, we recently argued [23] that if one is willing to restrict the choice of sampling time, then the bound should also hold in curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries. For example, we proved that the inequality Eq. (1) holds in the case of the Casimir effect for sampling times much smaller than the distance between the plates. ... Quantum inequalities in particular curved spacetimes, which reduce to Eq. (1) in the short sampling time limit, are given in Ref. [24].'

geroch-1967-topology-change.published_statement: Geroch, as restated in 2505.02210 Thm III.2: 'Let W be a compact spacetime whose boundary is the disjoint union of two compact spacelike 3-manifolds, Sigma_i and Sigma_f. If W has no CTCs, then Sigma_i and Sigma_f are diffeomorphic, and, furthermore, W is topologically equivalent to Sigma_i x [0,1].' Def. 6 there defines a spacetime as a 4-manifold 'together with an everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric'. Borde Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' Borde: 'By "causality violation" it is meant that there is at least one closed timelike curve.' Borde sec. IX: 'Neither Geroch's original theorem, nor its mild generalization in section IV, assume anything about the energy-momentum tensor, or indeed about a field equation - the results are purely kinematical.'
published_hypotheses: M (W) is an interpolating manifold: connected, smooth, Hausdorff and paracompact, with boundary S1 u S2. In Borde's generalisation the boundary may also include T, a compact timelike tube [Borde sec. II.A]

A smooth Lorentz metric that is non-degenerate everywhere on M, with S1 and S2 spacelike. T, if present, is timelike, with a timelike field tangent to it whose integral curves run from S1 to S2 [Borde II.A; 2505.02210 Def. 6]
Time-oriented, or time-orientable [Borde Thm 1 '(time-oriented)'; 2505.02210 Def. 6]. Borde secs. VII and IX: a non-time-orientable metric avoids the CTC only when one of the boundaries is empty

Geroch: W is compact, with compact (closed) spacelike boundary components. This is the closed-universe case; Borde reports that Geroch also covers the externally Lorentzian case. Borde: M is causally compact (the closure of I(p) is compact for every p), which a compact M satisfies trivially
Geroch, as restated in 2505.02210, is in dimension 4 (3-manifold slices). Borde's Theorem 1 assumes nothing about dimension
No energy condition, no field equation and no geodesic-completeness assumption
The conclusion is a CTC somewhere in M, the interpolating region. Nothing locates it more precisely

What was missing in 2023 is a calculation, not data: a DSNEC for curved spacetime. The literature read says it was still missing in 2024 (Kontou: 'This work has not been done yet') and in May 2026 (Fliss gives only the flat restatement). Evidence for M: a curved DSNEC could in principle reach HPS's throat, so the refusal depends on the current state of the field and is not a no-go theorem. Evidence against: a DSNEC built perturbatively in curvature would be controlled by the ratio of sampling length to curvature radius. HPS's curvature radius is 0.0243 l_P, and the Kretschmann radius is <= r_0/sqrt2 at any throat. The sampling length would then be sub-Planckian, outside the semiclassical regime that Freivogel-Krommydas require. So the refusal does not rest on missing data. sturm-liouville-self-adjointness.published_statement: NOT QUOTED (source unreadable here). The standard form, re-derived in the script: for L[u] = (p u')' + q u with p > 0 and q real (piecewise continuous / L^1_loc), the Lagrange identity v L[u] - u L[v] = d/dx[p (v u' - u v')] holds. So L with Dirichlet conditions u(a) = u(b) = 0 is (formally) self-adjoint, and the Wronskian p W is constant on solutions. Sturm separation (1836): the zeros of two linearly independent real solutions strictly interlace. Oscillation: the number of zeros in (a,b) of the solution with u(a) = 0 equals the number of Dirichlet eigenvalues of -L below 0, and the Dirichlet spectrum is invariant under x -> a + b - x. The in-tree 'reversal theorem' (06ee6bf:transit.py:50-54), quoted: 'Let u'' + q u = 0 with u(0) = u(L) = 0. Define the path read from the far end, q~(x) = q(L - x). Then v(x) := u(L - x) satisfies v'' + q~ v = 0 with v(0) = u(L) = 0 and v(L) = u(0) = 0. The SAME pair is conjugate. QED'.
published_hypotheses: (H1) scalar, linear, second order, in self-adjoint (Sturm-Liouville) form (p u')' + q u = 0 with p > 0 -- here p = 1, no first-derivative term
(H2) q real and piecewise continuous / L^1_loc (Sturm assumed continuity; L^1_loc via Caratheodory solutions is the later extension -- stated from the re-derivation, not read)

(H3) q a FIXED function of the affine parameter, independent of the solution's initial data (for the Jacobi equation: Ricci-only scalar focusing, or the full matrix Jacobi equation with a SYMMETRIC tidal matrix T)
(H4) self-adjointness is with respect to Dirichlet conditions at both ends of the interval; separation and oscillation need only real coefficients and a sign-definite Wronskian
(H5) 'reading from the far end' = the SAME segment with the affine parameter reversed (lambda -> L - lambda); R_ab k^a k^b is even in k, so q is reflected, not changed
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED LEMMA (proof route), seatindex.py:105-107 and :354. The fold c -> L - l - c is justified by 'transit.py's reversal theorem', but that theorem (06ee6bf:transit.py:50-54) is TWO-ENDED: it maps a conjugate pair (0, L) to itself. seats() (seatindex.py:144-156) is ONE-ENDED: u(0)=0, u'(0)=1, 'does u vanish in (0, L]?'. The missing step is Sturm separation: u0 has a zero in (0,L] iff the solution vanishing at L has a zero in [0,L). It is proved here by z3 [3] and confirmed exactly on 3,960 profiles [4]. The CONCLUSION is true; the cited justification is incomplete. For the same reason the canonical hypothesis 'Dirichlet conditions at both ends of [0, L]' is not the fold's hypothesis: admission has Dirichlet at 0 only.

conjugate-point-not-achronal.name: Causal-structure result: past a point conjugate to p along a null geodesic, the geodesic is no longer achronal (a timelike curve p -> r exists); contrapositive: an achronal null geodesic has no pair of conjugate points (Hawking-Ellis 1973 Prop. 4.5.12; Wald 1984 Thm 9.3.8; Penrose 1972)

source.located: Hawking & Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time (CUP 1973), Proposition 4.5.12. The proposition number comes from 2408.00154 (line 581 of the extracted text: 'achronal null geodesics cannot have conjugate points (Proposition 4.5.12 in Ref. [43])', where [43] = Hawking & Ellis) and from 2010.05086 (line 1281: 'null geodesic ... without conjugate points ([9] Proposition 4.5.12)', where [9] = Hawking & Ellis). The deformation form is Wald 1984 Sec. 9.3, as Gao & Wald gr-qc/0007021 use it. The book has no arXiv copy.
source.via: Hawking-Ellis and Wald are NAMED-NOT-READ. The restatements were READ as arXiv full text cached in this docket's src/casmag/all. Every alphaXiv call in this stage returned 'assistant quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses arxiv.org, so nothing could be fetched fresh. Gao & Wald gr-qc/0007021v2 (2000), definition: 'points p, q along a geodesic gamma are said to be conjugate if there exists a Jacobi field which vanishes at both p and q. Equivalently ... q will be conjugate to p if and only if det A = 0 at q'. Proof of their Thm 1: 'q in J+(p) - I+(p) ... Then gamma must be a null geodesic that does not contain any pair of conjugate points lying between p and q'. Proof of their Thm 2: 'lambda must contain a pair of conjugate points. Therefore ... lambda also can be deformed to be a timelike curve in M with the endpoints p and r fixed. Thus r in I+(p)'. Graham & Olum 0705.3193v2 p.3: 'every complete null geodesic that obeys ANEC has a pair of conjugate points [9] and thus is chronal [10 = Hawking-Ellis]'. Galloway math/9909158 p.16: 'an inextendible null geodesic is a null line iff it is achronal ... null lines ... must be free of conjugate points'. Also read: Cameron 2010.05086v2, and de Aguiar Alves & Landulfo 2408.00154v2 (Corollary 3). Osorio Morales & Santillan 2004.12523v4 was read only in part: the extracted text is missing its Proposition 1.

conjugate-point-not-achronal.published_statement: Hawking-Ellis Prop. 4.5.12 as restated by 2408.00154, 2010.05086 and Galloway math/9909158: an achronal null geodesic contains no pair of conjugate points. The equivalent form in Gao-Wald gr-qc/0007021 (from Wald Sec. 9.3 and HE): suppose a null geodesic gamma from p to r contains a pair of conjugate points lying between p and r, with the first conjugate point strictly before r. Then gamma can be deformed, endpoints fixed, into a timelike curve, so r is in I+(p). A point q in J+(p) - I+(p) is reached only by a null geodesic with no conjugate points between p and q. Two points are conjugate when a nonzero Jacobi field vanishes at both, i.e. det A = 0 with A(p) = 0, A'(p) = 1.

H2 gamma is an affinely parametrised null geodesic segment from p to r lying in the spacetime

anderson-molina-paris-mottola-kontou-val.published_statement:
AMM abstract (p.1): 'The criterion proposed is that solutions to the semi-classical Einstein equations should be stable to linearized perturbations, in the sense that no gauge invariant perturbation should become unbounded in time.'

AMM Sec. III (p.10): 'A necessary condition for the validity of the large N semi-classical equations of motion (2.9) is that the linear response equations (3.4) should have no solutions with finite non-singular initial data for which any linearized gauge invariant scalar quantity grows without bound.'

AMM Sec. II (p.7): 'we should regard the Planck scale as the physical UV cutoff which defines the extreme limit of possible validity of semi-classical gravity, and ... confine our attention to only those predictions of the theory which involve length scales l much greater than the Planck length.' The large-N solution is 'the exact solution of this equation without any perturbative re-expansion of G[g]'.

AMM Sec. V (p.13): the condition is 'necessary, though perhaps not a sufficient'. Flat space is stable 'provided we restrict ourselves to solutions with 4 G_N |k^2| << O(1)'.

AMM p.14: 'Further important and interesting examples to which the criterion may be applied are solutions with event horizons, such as Schwarzschild and de Sitter spacetimes ... In the Hartle-Hawking state one can construct a static solution to the semi-classical equations (2.9) that is quite close to the classical one near the horizon.'

Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 p.35: 'known violations of the AANEC involve Planck length distances, where the validity of QFT in curved spacetimes and/or semiclassical quantum gravity is doubtful ... Violations at Planck scale are allowed, because they probably lie outside the range of validity of the semiclassical Einstein equation.'

Kontou 2405.05963 p.19, on the Hochberg-Popov-Sushkov (HPS) self-consistent wormhole: 'The throat of the wormhole derived is of Planck length or up to the order 10^2 l_pl, so it is doubtful that it can be considered in the regime of the semiclassical approximation. However, it would be of interest to examine that wormhole solution using one of the QEIs for the nonminimally coupled fields ... to determine its exact validity.'

On the pages read, none of the three states a threshold on a metric-perturbation amplitude eps (or h) beyond which semiclassical gravity stops applying.
published_hypotheses: AMM H1: the background g solves the renormalised large-N semiclassical equations (2.9); the linear response (3.4) is the first variation about that solution (pp.8-9)
AMM H2: large N with N G finite, in the state |in>. A failed test means the approximation is 'not valid for that particular geometry, at least not for that particular state' (p.13)
AMM H3: validity is judged at length scales l >> l_Pl, i.e. 4 G_N |k^2| << O(1) (pp.7, 13), with the fourth-order coefficients of order 1
AMM H4: the criterion is necessary, not sufficient (p.13)
AMM H5: the allowed gauge transformations are those of (3.11); a growing one is excluded if the action (2.7) is not invariant under it (p.10)
Kontou-Sanders: the Planck-scale exclusion is hedged as 'probably', 'doubtful' and 'questionable'. It is a judgement, not a theorem
Kontou 2024: the stated reason for doubt is the HPS throat scale (1 to 10^2 l_P), and the exact validity is left to a future test with QEIs for non-minimally coupled (NMC) fields
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION DRIFT, AMM (substantive). throatmass.py:68-72, carried into ledger.py:1684-1685 and LEDGER.md:204 ('the corridor is EXPELLED rather than refuted'), credits AMM with the claim that 'eps ~ 1 lies outside semiclassical gravity's domain'. On the pages read, AMM draw the domain's edge in two places: length scales approaching l_Pl (p.7, and p.13's 4 G_N|k^2| << O(1)), and a growing gauge-invariant linear-response mode about a self-consistent solution (p.10). AMM call their large-N solution non-perturbative (p.7). On p.14 they name Schwarzschild horizons and the Hartle-Hawking static solution as places to apply the criterion, and h = 2M/r = 1 exactly at a horizon (rederive C3). So AMM treat an h = 1 geometry as inside their framework, not outside it.

ATTRIBUTION DRIFT, Kontou (substantive). The same site credits 'Kontou' with the eps ~ 1 claim. Kontou-Sanders pp.2 and 35 put the doubtful region at Planck-length distances. Kontou 2024 p.19 doubts HPS because its throat is 1 to 10^2 l_P, and p.25 calls a Planck-size throat the 'quantum gravity regime'. Both criteria are length scales, not metric amplitudes. The corridor has h = 1/2 at a free scale b; at a = 1 m it is 6.19e34 l_P.

DROPPED: AMM's criterion is a test that can pass or fail, and a failure names something: a growing gauge-invariant mode, which means 'the quantum fluctuations of the geometry should be included' (p.13). throatmass.py:71-72 ('an expulsion names nothing') and EXPULSION_WORSE_THAN_NO_GO (throatmass.py:163) leave this out. In addition, linstab.py records that AMM's criterion cannot yet be evaluated on the corridor, because no self-consistent solution is in hand (AMM_NEEDS_A_SOLUTION).

DROPPED: AMM's large-N setting (H2), 'for that particular state' (p.13), and 'necessary, not sufficient' (H4). This site applies nothing else of AMM, so these drops cause no over-claim beyond the attribution.

WEAKENED (hedge dropped): Kontou-Sanders say 'probably' and 'doubtful'; Kontou 2024 says 'doubtful' and asks for a test 'to determine its exact validity'. The tree's wording 'are right that ... lies outside' reads as a firm boundary; the conditional 'If' keeps only part of the hedge.

ADDED: the parameter eps. It is Flanagan-Wald's family parameter, graded in its own audit. Neither AMM nor Kontou uses a parameter of that kind. Grouping all three authors under one 'eps ~ 1' criterion is the tree's own construction.

POSSIBLE SOURCE OF THE CONFLATION (a reading, not claimed as the tree's intent): AMM pp.2-3 restate Kuo-Ford's fluctuation-to-mean ratio, which is 'of order unity' in many states including the Casimir vacuum. That is a '~1' breakdown measure, but it is a ratio of stress-tensor fluctuations, not a metric amplitude, and AMM criticise it as coordinate dependent. Kuo-Ford 1993 is NAMED-NOT-READ.

anderson-molina-paris-mottola-kontou-val.lacked_data:
What AMM had in 2002 was a criterion and a single evaluation (Minkowski, free scalar, vacuum). They had no evaluation on any curved self-consistent background and list Schwarzschild and de Sitter as future work (p.14).

What came later is GMMPS 2604.01047, which contests the flat-space verdict itself by tying it to renormalisation constants that AMM took to be of order 1. That moves AMM's stability result, which is now contested. It does not move the part the tree uses: AMM's domain boundary is set by length scale plus a stability test, and no later datum turns it into an eps threshold.

Kontou's data (the 1997 HPS throat scale and l_P) have not moved. No measured datum enters any of the three conclusions.

The data that are still missing, curved-background linear response and the renormalisation constants, would be needed to decide whether the corridor passes AMM's test. They would not supply the tree's antecedent. On this result, M's hypothesis finds no data gap that changes the conclusion.
anderson-molina-paris-mottola-kontou-val.grade_evidence:
The statements were read at source in the banked arXiv text layers. The tree's sentence at throatmass.py:68-72 credits AMM and Kontou with 'eps ~ 1 lies outside semiclassical gravity's domain'. The sources state a smaller, different restriction: length scales near the Planck length (AMM pp.7 and 13; Kontou-Sanders p.35, hedged 'probably'; Kontou 2024 p.19, 'doubtful' for 1 to 10^2 l_P throats), plus AMM's linear-stability test. AMM also apply their criterion to h = 1 horizons (p.14).

Computed: h is absent from AMM's condition. At h = 1/2 the curvature in Planck units is 2e-139 at r = 1 m. z3 shows that eps ~ 1 and Planckian curvature are independent.

So the sources expel a configuration only at Planck scale, which is a smaller class than eps ~ 1. At macroscopic scales the corridor is not expelled by what they state, and AMM's test remains undecided (linstab.py).

Not WRONG: nothing in the sources is refuted, and the tree's sentence is conditional. This is an attribution discrepancy, recorded and not repaired. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum has moved. Not OPEN: the texts were read. The residual uncertainty is which Kontou work the tree meant.
anderson-molina-paris-mottola-kontou-val.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade would move to STANDS if an unread passage (AMM Appendix B, Fewster-Kontou 2108.12668, or whatever Kontou work the tree intended) states that semiclassical gravity fails at eps ~ 1 regardless of scale. It would also move to STANDS if the tree limited the conditional to Planck-scale corridors of a few l_P, where the re-derivation gives 4G|k^2| between 0.24 and 4. The grade would move to OPEN if the tree meant a Kontou source that cannot be read here. It would move to WRONG only if the tree asserted the attribution unconditionally while a source states the contrary.

earnshaw-1842-theorem.published_statement: NOT QUOTED FROM SOURCE, because the source cannot be read here. The only wording available is a search-engine summary from WebSearch, which is not a reading: 'a collection of point charges cannot be maintained in a stable stationary equilibrium configuration solely by the electrostatic interaction of the charges', applying 'to classical inverse-square law forces (electric and gravitational)'. It is recorded here as the conventional modern form and flagged as unread. Nothing in the grade rests on it; the grade rests on the re-derivation.
published_hypotheses: These were NOT read at source. Each item below is a hypothesis the re-derivation shows the conclusion needs, not a quotation.

H1: the only forces come from a potential whose kernel is EXACTLY 1/r, i.e. the force is exactly inverse-square. S6a shows Lap r^-(1+d) = d(1+d) r^-(3+d), which vanishes only at d = 0. S6b shows a Yukawa kernel is not harmonic.
H2: the fields are static, the frame is inertial, and there are no velocity-dependent or time-dependent forces.

H3: the bodies are point particles, so only translational degrees of freedom count. For extended rigid bodies the translational conclusion survives by superposition; rotational equilibria are not covered.
H4: there are no induced or response sources (no polarisable or diamagnetic media). The charges or masses are fixed.
H5: the potential is evaluated away from the sources (r != 0).

H6: 'stable' means Lyapunov stable. The step from 'the potential has no minimum' to 'unstable' needs one of two things. If the Hessian is non-zero, the instability is exponential (S3, S4). If the Hessian is zero but the potential is not constant, it needs the Chetaev-Kozlov instability theorem, which is NAMED-NOT-READ; S5 gives numerical evidence.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKER ARGUMENT, CONCLUSION INTACT (stability.py:114-119; chain.py:141-150; paper/CLAIMS.md:988-991; obstruct.py:236-239). The tree argues: harmonic, therefore no strict minimum of U = m phi, therefore no stable equilibrium. It handles negative masses with 'negating m flips U = m phi, and -phi is harmonic too' (chain.py:148-149). The minimum-of-U criterion (Lagrange-Dirichlet) assumes the kinetic energy is POSITIVE-DEFINITE. The tree's own negmass.py case breaks that assumption. For a Bondi negative mass (inertial mass = passive mass < 0) the equation of motion is a = -grad phi whatever m is, so U = m phi is the wrong function and its minimum criterion runs backwards. The CONCLUSION still holds for every sign pattern. The linearisation K = M^-1 Hess U is traceless, because it is a sum of traceless diagonal blocks, but it is NOT symmetric. A traceless matrix cannot have an all-real-positive spectrum, so some mode grows exponentially unless the spectrum is {0}. S4 shows this for 7 free mixed-sign static equilibria: trace about 1e-17, all 7 K non-symmetric, growth rates 0.097 to 7.48. This is a flaw in the argument, not a refutation.

MISSING STEP (stability.py:116-117, 'a harmonic function has no strict minimum and NO static configuration is stably in equilibrium'). 'No minimum' does not by itself imply 'unstable'; the converse of Lagrange-Dirichlet is not a general theorem. For harmonic potentials the gap closes in two cases. Case 1, non-zero Hessian: a traceless symmetric matrix has a negative eigenvalue, so growth is exponential; in S3 all 93 equilibria found are saddles. Case 2, zero Hessian with a non-constant potential: the leading Taylor form is a non-zero harmonic polynomial with zero spherical mean (S2, k = 1..6), so there is no minimum, and instability then follows from the Chetaev-Kozlov theorem, which is NAMED-NOT-READ. Numerically (S5), for phi = x^3 - 3xy^2 a particle released at rest at 1e-3 leaves r < 0.5 at t = 92.1. The tree states neither step. chain.py:336 correctly names the escape as 'Hessian identically zero', meaning a constant potential, not a Hessian that is zero at one point.

UNDERSTATED, NOT OVERSTATED (stability.py:116). 'No strict minimum' is weaker than the truth. S2 shows a harmonic function has no local minimum of any kind, strict or not, unless it is locally constant. This SUPPORTS the tree's claim that 'the one escape Earnshaw permits is the DEGENERATE case, constant potential' (stability.py:118-119).

UNSTATED ASSUMPTION INSIDE THE WORD 'NEWTONIAN' (stability.py:120-123, 'the Newtonian CEILING' and 'a non-gravitational channel'). The ceiling needs a kernel that is EXACTLY 1/r (H1). Lee et al. 2020 (arXiv:2002.11761) test for an added Yukawa term, V_N[1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)], and motivate it from GRAVITATIONAL physics (dilaton, heavy graviton, extra dimensions), not only from non-gravitational channels. Any such term makes the potential inside the shell non-constant. S6c gives phi_in = -alpha G M lambda e^{-R/lambda} sinh(r/lambda)/(R r). S6e gives the curvature at the centre as -alpha G M e^{-R/lambda}/(3 R lambda^2), which is restoring only if alpha*M_shell < 0. The tree's list of escapes names 'a non-gravitational channel' and 'GR' but not a gravitational term that departs from 1/r. Taking 'Newtonian gravity' as the stated hypothesis, the tree's statement is exact.

THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES THE PREMISE AND REPORTS THE CONSEQUENCE (chain.py:323-326, has_strict_minimum). The check returns relative_laplacian > 1e-9. It measures harmonicity at one point and reports 'no strict minimum' as what the theorem then implies. Its docstring says this openly. This is not a fault; S2-S5 supply the step from the premise to the consequence.

SCOPE (stability.py:117, 'NO static configuration ... any placement'). The theorem covers point sources and translational stability only (H3). The tree applies it to a core inside an extended shell. By superposition, the core's potential energy as a function of its displacement is still harmonic; inside a uniform 1/r shell it is constant (S6d). The application is therefore within scope.

ATTRIBUTION (stability.py:114, 'CLOSED IN NEWTONIAN GRAVITY BY chain.py'). The owner credits a peer file with the closure, and chain.py:132-162 carries the argument. paper/CLAIMS.md:1001 labels it 'PROVEN ... Earnshaw from the traceless Hessian'. The traceless Hessian proves harmonicity only. To call the instability PROVEN also needs the S2/S4 steps, plus Chetaev-Kozlov in the degenerate case.

data_at_publication.quantity: The exponent of the force law, i.e. whether it is exactly 1/r^2. This is premise H1, and the whole theorem rests on it.
data_at_publication.value_then: In 1842 the law was taken as exactly inverse-square, by assumption. The experimental bounds available to Earnshaw (Cavendish and Coulomb for electricity, planetary motion for gravity) are NAMED-NOT-READ.
data_at_publication.value_now: Lee, Adelberger, Cook, Fleischer, Heckel, arXiv:2002.11761v1 (2020). Read from the local cache src/casmag/all/2002.11761v1.txt (md5 622a98c0aca3ad072ad15ea81a23d00f), lines 20-23 and 564-565: 'Newtonian gravity gave an excellent fit to our data, limiting with 95% confidence any gravitational-strength Yukawa interactions to ranges < 38.6 um'. The Yukawa form is V(r) = V_N(r)[1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)] (lines 51-54), and the data cover separations from 52 um to 3.0 mm. Bounds on |alpha| < 1 at longer lambda (their Fig. 5 cites previous works) are NAMED-NOT-READ.
data_at_publication.source_now: arXiv:2002.11761, read from the local cache of an earlier alphaXiv extraction; the alphaXiv quota was exceeded at this stage.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: NO, as long as the stated hypothesis 'Newtonian gravity' holds. Computed in S6: a Yukawa term breaks harmonicity, since Lap e^{-r/L}/r = e^{-r/L}/(L^2 r). It turns the neutral seat into a restoring one (alpha*M < 0) or an anti-restoring one (alpha*M > 0). The stiffness relative to the Newtonian scale GM/R^3 is |alpha|(R/lambda)^2 e^{-R/lambda}/3. At the bound read here (lambda = 38.6 um, |alpha| = 1) it is 10^-11242.8 for R = 1 m, 10^-8.9 for R = 1 mm and 10^-0.8 for R = 0.1 mm. So for any macroscopic device the deviation the data still allow at gravitational strength changes nothing. Only a sub-millimetre device, or a short-range term stronger than gravity (|alpha| > 1 at lambda < 38.6 um, not read here), could move the conclusion. Either would be outside 'Newtonian', and the tree's escape clause covers that only as 'non-gravitational'.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0) across 17 checks. S1 (sympy): tr Hess(1/r) = 0 exactly, and the Laplacian of three point sources with SYMBOLIC strengths and positions is 0, so any signs are covered. S2 (sympy): for k = 1..6, the homogeneous harmonic polynomials in R^3 form a space of dimension 2k+1, and every one has exactly zero spherical mean, so each takes negative values. Hence a non-constant harmonic function has no local minimum, strict or not. S3 (numeric): 93 equilibria of a test particle among 2-5 fixed sources with random signs were found; all 93 are saddles (eigenvalues of both signs), with max |tr H|/scale = 1.5e-15. S4 (numeric): 7 static equilibria of FREE collinear mixed-sign Bondi 3-body systems. The masses come from the null vector of the antisymmetric coupling matrix, and the residual acceleration is 0. In all 7 the linearisation is traceless (|tr| <= 2e-17) and non-symmetric, and every one has an exponentially growing mode (rates 0.097 to 7.483). So Earnshaw's conclusion holds for any signs, even where the tree's potential-minimum argument does not apply. S5 (numeric): at the degenerate critical point of phi = x^3 - 3xy^2 (zero Hessian, not constant), a particle released at rest leaves the point (t_exit = 92.1). S6 (sympy): Lap r^-(1+d) = d(1+d) r^-(3+d), and the Laplacian of a Yukawa kernel is non-zero. An exact integral gives the Yukawa potential inside a shell as phi_in = -alpha G M lambda e^{-R/lambda} sinh(r/lambda)/(R r). Its Newtonian limit is the constant -GM/R, which reproduces the tree's degenerate seat. The curvature at the centre is -alpha G M e^{-R/lambda}/(3 R lambda^2).

earnshaw-1842-theorem.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. Earnshaw's theorem is a theorem, not a measurement. Given its premise, a static and exactly harmonic potential of fixed sources (i.e. exactly 1/r), the conclusion is re-derived exactly here and needs no datum. The only empirical input is the premise itself: that the force law is EXACTLY inverse-square. In 1842 that was an assumption. Two things came later. (a) Laboratory tests of gravity's 1/r^2 law; the tightest one read here, Lee et al. 2020, finds no gravitational-strength Yukawa term at lambda >= 38.6 um (95% CL). (b) General relativity, where static stability is a different question; the tree keeps the GR version NOT-RUN. Would having these data change the conclusion? Computed evidence on each side. For 'no change': the Yukawa stiffness the data still allow inside a shell, at |alpha| = 1, is 10^-11242.8 of the Newtonian scale for a 1 m shell and 10^-8.9 for a 1 mm shell (S6). The Newtonian ceiling therefore survives to any precision that matters for a macroscopic device. Against 'no change': the data leave room at lambda < 38.6 um, and for |alpha| > 1 there. In that region a shell smaller than 0.1 mm would feel a Yukawa stiffness of about 10^-0.8 of the Newtonian scale, and of EITHER sign (restoring only if alpha*M_shell < 0). The ceiling would then not be a ceiling. That region lies outside 'Newtonian gravity', the tree's stated hypothesis, so it does not falsify the tree's statement. But the tree's escape list ('GR, time dependence, or a non-gravitational channel') leaves out a gravitational term that departs from 1/r, which is how Lee et al. themselves frame the dilaton and heavy-graviton possibilities. No datum that Earnshaw lacked overturns the theorem.
earnshaw-1842-theorem.grade_evidence: The mathematical content the tree uses is re-derived in full here; the re-derivation passes all 17 checks. (1) The potential of point sources of any signs is harmonic (S1, exact). (2) A non-constant harmonic function has no local minimum at all (S2, exact, k = 1..6). So the only case with a minimum is the constant potential, which is exactly the tree's 'one escape ... the DEGENERATE case' (stability.py:118-119). (3) Every equilibrium among fixed sources of random signs is a saddle (S3, 93/93). (4) Free mixed-sign Bondi static equilibria are exponentially unstable (S4, 7/7). (5) A particle leaves the degenerate zero-Hessian critical point (S5). (6) The Newtonian potential inside the shell is the constant -GM/R (S6d). While the stated hypothesis 'Newtonian gravity' holds, no datum that has moved changes the conclusion (S6: 10^-11242.8 at R = 1 m). Two flaws in the tree's argument are recorded, not repaired, and neither is a refutation. First, the tree's minimum-of-U argument assumes positive inertia, which the tree's own negative-mass case violates; the traceless-K argument rescues the conclusion (S4). Second, 'no minimum, therefore unstable' is stated without the zero-Hessian step (Chetaev-Kozlov, NAMED-NOT-READ; numerical evidence in S5). CAVEAT ON THE GRADE: Earnshaw 1842 and every restatement are NAMED-NOT-READ, because the alphaXiv quota was exceeded and arXiv and Wikipedia are egress-blocked. STANDS therefore certifies the statement as the tree uses it, by re-derivation. It does not certify the attribution to Earnshaw or that the tree matches his own hypotheses.
earnshaw-1842-theorem.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED in either of two cases. (a) Earnshaw's paper or a reliable restatement, once read, states a hypothesis the tree drops that the re-derivation did not surface, e.g. a restriction to like-sign sources or to positive inertia that the published proof actually needs. (b) The degenerate zero-Hessian case turns out NOT to be covered by the Chetaev-Kozlov instability theorem for some harmonic potential. DATA-DEPENDENT if the device's scale were set below about 0.1 mm. There, a gravitational-strength Yukawa term at lambda < 38.6 um, which is still allowed, would give a stiffness of order the Newtonian scale and of either sign. WRONG only if a counterexample is shown. One would be a static equilibrium of a test particle in an exactly 1/r field of fixed sources (any signs) whose linearisation is stable. Another would be a free mixed-sign point configuration whose linearisation K is non-zero, has its spectrum in [0, inf), and has bounded solutions. S3 and S4 found neither, and tr K = 0 rules both out by construction. OPEN would apply only if the re-derivation were withdrawn.

higgs-yukawa-static-sourcing.published_statement: Brax-Burrage 2101.10693 eq.(4) is a simplified SM with a real Higgs h and one Dirac fermion. The fermion term is -lambda_psi h psibar psi. The paper states: 'we replace psibar psi -> <psibar psi> = n_psi where n_psi is the number density of the medium. After identifying the mass of the fermions as m_psi = lambda_psi v, the equations of motion ... become ... box h + mu^2(phi) h - lambda h^3 - rho/v = 0 (10)', with mu^2 = lambda v^2 (eq.7). In the linear static case (eqs.(56),(58)), the perturbations outside a constant-density sphere are 'decreasing exponential functions' B e^{-sqrt(y)(r-R_0)}/(sqrt(y) r). Footnote 2 says: 'the Higgs field should couple to alpha rho in (10). We ignore this alpha coefficient.' Shi 1908.02159 p.1 gives '<phi> ~ +-v - f<psibar psi>/u^2' in the perturbative regime, significant only at rho ~ v^2 u^2 ~ 1e29 kg/m^3. Cline 1306.4710 eq.(11) gives 'sum_{c,b,t} f_q = (2/9)(1 - sum_{u,d,s} f_q)' (SVZ) and a Higgs-nucleon coupling f_N m_N/v with f_N = 0.30 +- 0.01.
published_hypotheses: Tree-level classical field equation of a real scalar with quartic (Mexican-hat) self-coupling. One Dirac fermion stands in for the SM (Brax-Burrage p.5).
psibar psi is replaced by its medium expectation value and identified with the number density n, i.e. nonrelativistic matter (Brax-Burrage p.5).
Linear perturbation theory about the vacuum, requiring a source density that is not too high (Brax-Burrage p.14; Shi 1908.02159: the shift matters only at rho ~ v^2 u^2).
Static configuration, constant-density source, decay at infinity, continuity at the surface (Brax-Burrage eqs.(54)-(58)).
Perturbative branch: Shi 2107.04206 shows the static solution is not unique beyond a size-dependent critical source (the 1210 phase).
For nucleons the coupling is alpha*rho = f_N m_N/v, with f_N from the SVZ heavy-quark relation at leading order in alpha_s plus the u, d AND s sigma terms (Cline eq.(11)).
hypothesis_drift: No drift on the field equation. address.py:138 '(nabla^2 - m_h^2) dphi = (m_psi/v) n' is exactly Brax-Burrage eq.(10) linearised (sympy residual 0) and matches Shi's shift. The uniform solution at address.py:140 re-derives. Only m_h^2 enters, so the unmeasured trilinear does not.

Weakened qualifier 'EXACT' (address.py:140, :145; source_to_field_ratio docstring at address.py:674-678). The law is exact only as the linear, tree-level, uniform statement. The exact uniform solution for the SM shape is rho = 8|V_min| eps(1+eps)(1+eps/2), so the exact source/field ratio is 4(1+eps)/(eps(2+eps)), not 8/(eps(2+eps)^2). The two differ by 1.3e-15 at eps_det and by a factor of 3 at the eps_0 = 1 of address.py:166. This is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

Dropped at the formula: psibar psi -> n, the nonrelativistic identification (address.py:137-142 uses the mass density rho). The tree knows the relativistic form, the (mc^2/E)^2 lemma at address.py:244-250. For a free Fermi gas at n0, rho_s/rho_B = 0.9774 (-2.3%).

Coupling hypothesis (address.py:104, :143). For a Higgs field displacement, the READ literature supports H1 = SVZ (Cline eqs.(11)-(13), f_N = 0.30). H2 (f = S) has no READ support as a Higgs-nucleon coupling. The one exception is Brax-Burrage footnote 2, which says the gluon part is uncoupled, contrary to SVZ; that is recorded as a discrepancy in the reading source. The tree refuses to choose (address.py:460).
Dropped (sibling sigma-term-scan): EPS_NUCLEAR (address.py:943) uses S = 0.06, which counts u and d only. SVZ sums over u, d and s. At S = 0.09, eps = -3.55e-13, 433x eps_det(H1).
Weakened (siblings dlnlambdaqcd-dlnv-2-9, svz-1978): the 2/9 is leading order in alpha_s and in the heavy-quark limit. Beyond LO, f = 0.2818 at S = 0.06 (+4.8%).

Unnamed hypothesis: that the perturbative branch is the unique static solution. The tree's criterion is eps << 1 (address.py:166, 297-303). Shi 2107.04206 p.15 puts the nonperturbative boundary at rho_c ~ 8.8e11 kg/m^3 for a 1 m sphere with the tree's H1 f, where eps ~ 1e-18. The boundary is far away for EPS_NUCLEAR (margin 4.7e8) and for the atom-scale courier (margin 4.5e9). It is relevant to the 1 m sources of address.py sections 6 and 9. It is contested for the SM, because Shi's model is a toy.

Weakened (sibling yukawa-green-function, re-shown in R7): the multiplicative form '[1 + O((lambda_h/L)^2)]' at address.py:181 fails where J = 0 but dphi != 0. The absolute form |dphi + J/m^2| <= |J''|/m^4 holds.

Discrepancy (sibling address-domination-theorem, re-shown in R3): address.py:164 and :697-722 start the exterior tail at eps_0. For a uniform sphere with R >> lambda_h, the surface value is half the interior value, so the standoff is overstated by lambda_h ln 2 = 1.09e-18 m. This is conservative.
Discrepancy (stale rounding): the prose at address.py:163 gives lambda_h = 1.5761e-18 m, which is the withdrawn 125.20 GeV value. The code computes 1.57698e-18 m at the READ 125.13 GeV.
Agrees: neglecting electrons (computed share 8e-4 to 4.5e-3), and the coarse-grained density hypothesis, which address.py:297-303 states.

higgs-yukawa-static-sourcing.lacked_data: The form of the law is a tree-level consequence of the SM Lagrangian and needs no datum. Its numbers need m_h, v, the nucleon coupling f and the density. Shi (2019) and Brax-Burrage (2021) already had m_h and v; the later move is 1.1e-3 on eps. Three things were lacking then or are still soft. (a) The nucleon coupling. Brax-Burrage set it to 1 and describe the gluon part as uncoupled; SVZ is LO; the sigma terms are in ~3 sigma tension. Computed: every f from 0.06 to 0.35 keeps nuclear matter 83x to 518x above eps_det, so the conclusion does not move. (b) The self-coupling shape is still unmeasured, but sympy shows it does not enter the linear law or the O(eps^2) energy. (c) The one genuinely new input is theoretical, not data: Shi 2021 shows the static solution is non-unique, which narrows the result to the perturbative branch. That branch holds at nuclear and atomic scale (margins 4.7e8 and 4.5e9) but not for metre-scale dense sources. On the evidence either way, M's hypothesis is not supported on the data side for THIS result. It is supported only in the weak sense that a later theoretical result narrows the class on which the classical linear picture is the whole story.
higgs-yukawa-static-sourcing.grade_evidence: The re-derivation agrees exactly. The equation, its sign, eps = -rho_H c^2/(v^2 m_h^2), v^2 m_h^2 = 8|V_min|, the Yukawa exterior and the ultralocal leading term all re-derive in sympy with 0 FAIL, and they match Brax-Burrage eq.(10) and Shi p.1 as READ. The owner's EPS_NUCLEAR is reproduced to 1e-12. No moved or contested datum moves a conclusion: m_h shifts eps by 1.1e-3; across f 0.06-0.35 and n0 0.15-0.16 the in-hypothesis ratio stays >= 107; the courier source stays above 3e7x osmium; electrons contribute under 0.5%. It is therefore not WRONG and not DATA-DEPENDENT. It is not STANDS because the statement as used holds on a smaller class than written: (i) 'EXACT' is applied to a linear tree-level law, and the source/field ratio called 'EXACTLY 8/(eps(2+eps)^2)' mixes orders (the exact value is 4(1+eps)/(eps(2+eps))); (ii) psibar psi ~ n is not named at the formula (-2.3% at n0); (iii) uniqueness of the perturbative branch is not named (Shi 2107.04206); (iv) the coupling is LO SVZ with strange dropped at the adopted S, and H2 is unsupported as a Higgs-nucleon coupling; (v) the ultralocal multiplicative form and the eps_0 tail are discrepancies already recorded by siblings. This is consistent with the sibling NARROWED grades. Nothing was repaired.
higgs-yukawa-static-sourcing.what_would_change_the_grade: It would become STANDS if the owner named the class (linear, tree-level, nonrelativistic, perturbative branch, LO SVZ with u, d, s) and dropped the mixed-order 'EXACT'. It would become WRONG given a READ SM calculation showing the in-medium Higgs-nucleus coupling suppressed by more than ~100, or showing the Shi branch realised at nuclear or atomic scale. flrw-comoving-number-conservation.lacked_data: No data the textbook authors lacked moves the published result. FLRW comoving geodesics (C1) and the continuity identity (C3) are exact mathematics for any a(t), and no measurement can move them. The result has always carried two hypotheses: no peculiar motion, and a conserved number current. The source states the first itself ('as long as there aren't any forces acting on them'). The CMB dipole (371 km/s in 1996, 369.82 km/s in 2018) and galaxy formation and mergers show those hypotheses are needed; they do not refute the textbook. So the evidence runs against M's 'lacked data' hypothesis for this result as published. The over-statement is in the tree: permute.py:41 says 'right in the textbook' but drops both hypotheses, which over-represents in M's favour. The scorecard row 'space is a closed index: STANDS' (permute.py:503) rests on that unconditional reading.
flrw-comoving-number-conservation.grade_evidence: The published statement is conditional. Baumann 0907.5424 p.15-16 (READ) says galaxies keep fixed comoving coordinates 'in the absence of peculiar motion', and n a^3 = const holds only for a conserved number current (re-derived exactly, C3). Under those hypotheses both parts are machine-checked correct (C1, C3). The tree drops both hypotheses at permute.py:42-47, 222-224, 418-420, 503, 527-530 and obstruct.py:280. The measured peculiar velocity of 371 +- 1 km/s (Fixsen 1996 p.26, READ) gives about 0.41 comoving Mpc of drift per Gyr (C6). Energy conservation (del.T=0) does not imply number conservation (del.N=0) (C4). The label 'Measured, not asserted' on count_is_conserved describes a tautology (C5); that is recorded here, not repaired. The grade is not WRONG: nothing in the textbook statement is refuted, and the tree's claim holds on the smaller class of the idealised comoving congruence and conserved species.
flrw-comoving-number-conservation.what_would_change_the_grade: It would become STANDS if the tree named both hypotheses at its use sites: 'for the comoving congruence, peculiar velocities neglected' and 'for a species with a conserved current'. It could become WRONG only through a computed failure of Gamma^i_tt = 0 or of the FLRW continuity identity, which C1 and C3 exclude symbolically for general k and a(t). Reading 1807.06205 and 1607.03909 at source would upgrade two NAMED-NOT-READ rows but cannot move the grade.

gr-qc/9607003.name: Ford & Roman, 'Restrictions on Negative Energy Density in Flat Spacetime' (gr-qc/9607003; PRD 55, 2082 (1997)): Lorentzian-sampled QI for the free massless scalar, rho-hat >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), plus the Sec. 4 curved-spacetime scope remark

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/9607003v2 (submitted 1 Jul 1996, revised 2 Oct 1996, v2 24 Jan 1997), L.H. Ford and T.A. Roman, Tufts; journal ref PRD 55, 2082-2089 (Feb 1997), as cited in Kontou-Sanders arXiv:2003.01815 ref. [74] and Fewster-Eveson gr-qc/9805024 ref. [3]
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9607003 returned all 17 pages (abstract, Secs. 1-4, Appendices A-B, references). I read it in full twice, in two sessions, and re-checked every quotation. Eq.(1) on p.2 is quoted from Ref.[21] (Ford-Roman PRD 51, 4277 (1995)), where it was first derived; this paper re-derives it as Eq.(17), the m -> 0 limit of Eq.(16), by a plane-wave method.

gr-qc/9607003.published_statement: p.2 Eq.(1) (and p.5 Eq.(17), the m->0 limit of Eq.(16)): 'for the free quantized massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, rho-hat == (t0/pi) INT_{-oo}^{oo} <T00> dt/(t^2+t0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), for all choices of the sampling time, t0. Here <T00> is the renormalized expectation value of the energy density evaluated in an arbitrary quantum state |psi>, in the frame of an arbitrary inertial observer whose proper time coordinate is t.' (Units hbar = c = 1. The text layer prints 't0' for the proper-time coordinate, which is an extraction artefact.) p.4: 'the energy density is evaluated in the reference frame of an inertial observer, at an arbitrary spatial point which we choose to be x = 0.' The same paper also gives: massive scalar -3 G(y)/(32 pi^2 t0^4), y = 2 m t0 (Eq.16); EM field -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) (Eq.48); 2D massless -1/(8 pi t0^2) (Eq.25). Sec.4 (p.11): 'in Minkowski spacetime, our bounds hold for an arbitrary choice of the sampling time, t0. Recently we argued that such bounds should also hold in a curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries, if the sampling time is restricted to be much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]. An explicit example ... [24] ... static closed and open Robertson-Walker universe models.' p.2: 'In quantum field theory ... the energy density may be unboundedly negative at a spacetime point.'
published_hypotheses: H1 free (non-interacting) quantized field; stress tensor T_mn = phi,m phi,n - (1/2) eta_mn (phi,a phi^,a + m^2 phi^2) (Eq.6). This is MINIMAL coupling (no xi R phi^2 term)
H2 massless scalar for Eq.(1) (massive: Eq.16 with G(y) <= 1; EM: Eq.48, twice as negative)
H3 four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, no boundaries ('derived for Minkowski spacetime, in the absence of boundaries', p.2)

H4 the bounded quantity is the Lorentzian TIME average rho-hat of <T00> along the worldline of an INERTIAL observer at ONE spatial point x = 0, with weight t0/[pi(t^2+t0^2)] of unit integral (Eq.8). It is not <T00> at a point, and not a spatial or spacetime average
H5 one-sided: a LOWER bound on rho-hat; nothing bounds positive energy density
H6 arbitrary state |psi> of the Fock space, with <T00> renormalized (normal ordered w.r.t. the Minkowski vacuum); the mode sums are assumed to converge in the V -> oo / omega_max -> oo limit (p.16)

H7 holds for ALL t0 > 0 in flat space. The extension to curved spacetime or boundaries, for t0 << the smallest local curvature radius and/or the boundary distance, is ARGUED in ref.[23] (PRD 53, 5496) and not proved in this paper. The paper names two supporting cases: Casimir plates, proved in [23] (p.2-3), and static RW (ref.[24], gr-qc/9608005)
H8 the derivation uses no time-energy uncertainty relation (Sec.4). It rests on two norm-positivity lemmas (App. A) and the kernel inequality S_m >= S~_m (App. B)

gr-qc/9607003.lacked_data: No, and the evidence runs one way. Eq.(1) is a theorem about the free massless minimally coupled scalar in 4D Minkowski space, and no measured quantity enters it. I re-derived every step: the Fourier identity, the V->oo limit, and the massive, EM and 2D companions. I also checked the result end to end on 21,900 squeezed states, with a non-vacuity guard. What the 1996 authors lacked was later THEORY, not data. (a) Fewster-Eveson 1998 (READ) makes the Lorentzian bound 64/9 tighter, which moves against M. (b) Curved-spacetime proofs (Fewster-Smith 2008, Kontou-Olum 2015) back the Sec.4 remark that was only argued in 1996. (c) We now know which hypotheses are load-bearing: non-minimal coupling admits no state-independent QEI, the inertial observer matters, interacting 4D fields are open, and 4D has no null-line or spatial-only QEI. (c) is where the result's reach is narrower than a loose reading, and it is where the tree's L4 breaker sits. None of this moves the published conclusion within its stated hypotheses. The only numbers the tree adds are hbar, c and G. hbar and c are exact by definition, and all three cancel from the tree's crossover (script K3).
gr-qc/9607003.grade_evidence: The published theorem stands. I read it at source twice, re-derived it symbolically, and checked it end to end on 21,900 squeezed-state/phase pairs, with a non-vacuity guard and a control. No datum it depends on has moved. The grade is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a wider class than the one published. (1) candidates.py:112-116, candidates.py:346-348 and overturn.py:277 state '|rho| <= 3 hbar c/(32 pi^2 L^4)', which drops the sampling (H4) and the one-sidedness (H5). (2) overturn.py:220-222 says it bounds |rho| 'over a sampling region rather than an average along a line', contradicting the single spatial point x = 0 on p.4. (4) The Sec.4 curved-spacetime scope used in noise.py is an argued claim (ref.[23]) with two worked cases, and noise.py:185-187 drops 'and/or the distance to any boundaries'. The tree's use errs against M in two places. Flat-space Eq.(1) for all t0 excludes a static negative density outright (script I1/I2). Fewster-Eveson's bound is 9/64 of Ford-Roman's (script J1; FE Eq.5.6, READ). That supports, without proving it in 4D, the tree's own record that bounds.py's K = 0 ('saturated') coding is wrong; in 2D, Flanagan's optimal bound makes it firm (script L1). Nothing in the source is refuted, and there is no misprint, so the grade is not WRONG.

gr-qc/9802046.published_statement:
Sec. 7 (Discussion, p.30): 'While the latter [shape functions or embedding diagrams] can certainly be used without risk for detecting flare-out in static wormholes, they are at best misleading if applied to dynamic wormholes. This is simply because the embedding of a wormhole spacetime requires selecting and lifting out a particular time-slice and embedding this instantaneous spatial three-geometry in a flat Euclidean R3. For a static wormhole, any constant time-slice will suffice, and if the embedded surface is flared-out in the spatial direction orthogonal to the throat, then it is flared-out in spacetime as well. But if the wormhole is dynamic, flare-out in the spatial direction does not imply flare-out in the null directions orthogonal to the throat.'

Sec. 4 (p.11): '...suggests why it is that the embedding of the spatial part of a wormhole spacetime in an Euclidean R3 is no longer a reliable operational technique for defining "flare-out" in the time-dependent case.'

Def. 4.1.1: a two-surface satisfies 'simple flare-out' iff theta = 0 and dtheta/du >= 0 (a marginally anti-trapped surface).

Sec. 5.1 eqs. (49)-(50): at a throat, dtheta/du + sigma^2 = -8 pi T_ab l^a l^b, so T_ab l^a l^b <= 0: 'The NEC is therefore either violated, or on the verge of being violated'. Strong flare-out gives a strict violation somewhere (eq. 51). Averaged flare-out gives a sign-averaged violation over the throat (eq. 53). Near the throat the NEC is 'violating, or on the verge of violating' along partial null curves (0, u*_x).

Eqs. (77) and (90): a null throat is simply flared iff the NEC is violated or on the verge there. 'Temporary suspension of the violation of the NEC at a time-dependent throat also leads to a simultaneous obliteration of the flare-out property of the throat itself.'
published_hypotheses: H1 DEFINITIONAL: a throat is a closed, two-sided, spacelike 2-surface on which the expansion of ONE future-directed orthogonal null congruence vanishes, with dtheta/du along that same null direction >= 0 (simple), > 0 somewhere (strong), > 0 everywhere (strongly anti-trapped), sign-averaged > 0 (averaged), or N-fold degenerate (Defs 4.1.1-4.1.6, Table 1). Flare-out is defined on NULL congruences, 'free from notions of embedding and shape-functions'.

H2 Einstein equation G_ab = 8 pi T_ab (eq. 11), optionally plus a totally antisymmetric (Kalb-Ramond) torsion. The NEC statements are about the total T_ab contracted with the SAME null congruence that defines the throat.
H3 No symmetry, no asymptotic flatness, no topology and no staticity is assumed. The congruences are surface-orthogonal and therefore twist-free (eqs. 55-57).
H4 Smoothness: theta is Taylor-expanded in the affine parameter near the throat (eq. 38) for the near-throat statements. Degenerate throats are handled by eqs. (39)-(41).
H5 Under SIMPLE flare-out the NEC conclusion is NON-STRICT: T_ab l^a l^b <= 0, 'violated, or on the verge of being violated'. A strict violation needs strong flare-out.
H6 The conclusion is about the NEC (a null contraction of T_ab). It is not about the WEC, negative energy density, or negative Misner-Sharp mass.

gr-qc/9802046.lacked_data:

birkhoff-einstein-maxwell.published_statement: Frolov & Zelnikov (2011) p.166, restated verbatim in 2605.01811 p.3 as Theorem 1 (Generalized Birkhoff's theorem): 'If the energy-momentum tensor generating a spherically symmetric gravitational field of the form ds^2 = gamma_AB dx^A dx^B + R(x)^2 dOmega^2, where ... R(x) is a non-constant function, obeys the following condition: T_AB = (1/2) T^C_C gamma_AB, then the corresponding solution of the Einstein equations possesses an additional Killing vector field.' With the Maxwell ansatz A = phi(t,r) dt + p cos(theta) dphi, which carries both electric and magnetic charge, the condition holds and the unique solution is f = 1 - 2M/r + (Q_e^2+Q_m^2)/r^2 (eqs 16-18, 62). From p.1: 'A generalization of this theorem to the electro-vacuum case of the Einstein-Maxwell theory gives Reissner-Nordstrom metric as a unique asymptotically flat solution. However, in such a case, there also exists a spherically symmetric but not asymptotically flat solution - the so called Bertotti-Robinson universe', which is AdS2 x S2 with R0 = sqrt(e^2+p^2) (eq 21). Schleich & Witt p.1: generalized Birkhoff theorems 'are local uniqueness theorems ... their corollary is that locally spherically symmetric solutions exhibit an additional local Killing vector field; however this field is not necessarily timelike'.
published_hypotheses: 4D general relativity, G_ab = 8 pi T_ab (Lambda is allowed in the Schleich-Witt and Kubiznak et al. generalizations)
local spherical symmetry: SO(3) with 2-dimensional spacelike orbits; metric gamma_AB dx^A dx^B + R^2 dOmega^2

R(x) NON-CONSTANT (grad R != 0) -- 'The assumption that the radial function R(t,r) is non-constant is crucial' (2605.01811 p.3). R = const gives Bertotti-Robinson when Lambda = 0, and Plebanski-Hacyan or charged Nariai when Lambda != 0
the source obeys T_AB = (1/2) T^C_C gamma_AB. Source-free Maxwell satisfies this, and so does any L(S,P) nonlinear electrodynamics, for the field A = phi dt + p cos(theta) dphi
source-free region (no charged matter); electric and magnetic charge both allowed
the conclusion is local: locally isometric to RN or to BR. The extra Killing vector is timelike only where grad R is spacelike, so staticity is not implied
regularity: C^2 in the classical proof; C^0 piecewise-C^1 per Bergmann-Cahen-Komar 1965 (restated in 2411.09193, not read here)
asymptotic flatness is not a hypothesis of the local theorem; it only excludes BR in the 'unique asymptotically flat' phrasing

birkhoff-einstein-maxwell.lacked_data: The theorem (Hoffmann 1932-33) belongs to classical GR plus linear Maxwell. Its conclusion takes no measured input, so no later datum can move it; E1-E4 hold for arbitrary metric functions and symbolic charges. Four things the 1932 authors lacked were checked: (1) Magnetic monopoles, proposed by Dirac in 1931. Modern restatements include them, and they only replace Q^2 with Q^2+P^2 (E2-E3). (2) A measured Lambda (1998 on; Planck 2018 gives 1.089e-52 m^-2). It changes the frozen formula to m + Lambda R^3/6 and adds Nariai-type exceptions, but m stays frozen, and the term is numerically negligible below about 100 pc (E6, E9). (3) Bertotti-Robinson (1959). It is a real grad R = 0 exception to RN uniqueness, but its m is also frozen (E5). (4) Strong-field QED (Euler-Heisenberg, 1936). The Birkhoff condition holds for any L(S,P) (2605.01811), so the structure survives with a different m(R). Every later datum examined leaves standing that the Misner-Sharp mass of spherical source-free electromagnetism is a fixed function of R. What later knowledge corrects is how complete the statement is (the exception set and the field ansatz), and that is exactly where the tree's wording drifts.

si-speed-of-light.name: Speed of light in vacuum, exact SI value (c = 299 792 458 m/s)

source.located: The defining statement is the SI: the metre redefinition of the 17th CGPM (1983), with c kept as one of the defining constants in the revised SI of 20 May 2019. Neither document is on arXiv. Read here through CODATA 2022 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga, arXiv:2409.03787). Table XXXII p.50 and Table XXXIII p.51 give 'speed of light in vacuum c 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact'. p.60 says c, h, e, k and N_A are exactly known 'as a result of the 1983 redefinition of the meter in terms of an exact value of c and the 2019 revision of the SI'. The p.65 list of symbols calls c 'one of the seven defining constants of the SI'.
source.via: CODATA 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787) restates the SI definition exactly. The 1983 CGPM resolution and the 2019 SI Brochure themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ.

si-speed-of-light.published_statement: CODATA 2022, Table XXXII (p.50): 'speed of light in vacuum  c  299 792 458 m s^-1  exact'. p.60: c, h, e, k and N_A are 'exactly known as a result of the 1983 redefinition of the meter in terms of an exact value of c and the 2019 revision of the SI'. The same table gives G = 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 with u_r 2.2e-5, a value p.60 says is identical to the 2018 one.
published_hypotheses: H1 (definition): the metre is defined by fixing c at 299 792 458 when expressed in m s^-1, with the second defined by the caesium frequency. So c has no uncertainty in SI units. This is a choice of unit system, not a measurement.

H2 (physical content the definition does not supply): c is the invariant speed of relativity and the speed of light in vacuum. For a real electromagnetic signal to travel at c you need a vacuum path, a massless photon and no vacuum dispersion. These are empirical claims, tested separately (for example LHAASO time-of-flight on GRB 221009A, arXiv:2402.06009).
H3: exactness holds only in the SI. In geometric units c = 1 by convention, and the SI value matters only when converting to m, s or J.
hypothesis_drift: No drift in the value. nonstatic.py:253 ('C = 2.99792458e8  # m/s, exact') and transit.py:142 ('C_SI = 2.99792458e8') are exactly the SI value: Fraction(literal) == 299792458. The integer is below 2^53, so it is stored exactly as a 64-bit float and 'exact' still holds in the code (computed).

Label discrepancy in canonical.json, not in the owner files. The merged key 'si-2019-c' dates the fixing of c to 2019. The source says c was fixed in 1983 and the 2019 revision kept it (CODATA 2022 p.60). Neither owner file states a year: grep for 2019, 1983 and CGPM in nonstatic.py and transit.py finds nothing.

Added physical hypothesis at transit.py:145 ('def arrival_time(D): return D/C_SI  # the classical channel, at c'). The SI definition does not say that a real classical channel arrives in time D/c; that needs H2 plus a vacuum path. A real radio signal through interstellar plasma is slower. Computed cold-plasma delay at 1 GHz over Earth-Proxima: 0.054, 0.540 and 5.40 ms for assumed n_e of 0.01, 0.1 and 1 cm^-3 (n_e was not read at source). This delay is never negative, so it can only push advantage_over_light to zero or below. It cannot move the conclusion that there is no advantage over light.

Observation, not a drift. transit.py:146 defines advantage_over_light(D) = arrival_time(D) - D/C_SI, and arrival_time(D) is D/C_SI, so the result is zero for any positive c. Sympy gives D/c - D/c = 0, and the float result is exactly 0.0 at all four DISTANCES. The printed 0.000 comes from how the channel is modelled; it does not test c.

nonstatic.py:256 ('LY = 9.4607304725808e15  # m, exact (Julian year x c)'): 365.25 x 86400 x 299792458 = 9 460 730 472 580 800 exactly (computed). This equals the literal and is stored exactly as a float, since it is even and below 2^54. No drift.

si-speed-of-light.lacked_data: Testing M's hypothesis on this result: for the value itself, no author lacked any data. Since 1983 c has been a definition, so no later measurement can change 299 792 458 m/s; a better measurement would change how the metre is realised, not c. Evidence: CODATA 2022 lists c as 'exact' with no uncertainty (p.50), and leaves it out of the 2018-to-2022 comparison because it is exactly known (p.60). The tree also leans on a physical claim, at transit.py:145 ('the classical channel, at c'), and that claim is empirical. It has since been tested with data nobody had in 1983: from LHAASO's 2024 E_QG,1 bound (read), any vacuum-dispersion deviation for a GHz photon is at most 4e-35 of c (computed). The one effect the tree does not model is plasma along a real path, and that makes signals slower, never faster. So the conclusion that there is no advantage over light holds either way, and more data would not change it.
si-speed-of-light.grade_evidence: The value and its 'exact' status were read in CODATA 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787 Table XXXII p.50, and p.60). The owner literals at nonstatic.py:253 and transit.py:142 equal it exactly and are stored exactly as floats. Every use that rests on it was re-derived symbolically and numerically, and all 22 checks pass: band_time_seconds, crossing_time_seconds, build_energy, band_ratio, and transit's D23 advantage_over_light. No datum can move a defined constant. Three points are recorded, not repaired. (i) The merged key 'si-2019-c' in canonical.json gives the wrong year: c was fixed in 1983 and kept in 2019. This label is outside the owner files. (ii) transit.py:145 adds the physical assumption that a classical channel runs at c, which the definition does not supply. Every correction to it (dispersion in a medium) makes the signal slower, so it cannot move the tree's conclusion. (iii) advantage_over_light is zero by construction, so its printed 0.000 comes from how the channel is modelled; it does not test c.
si-speed-of-light.what_would_change_the_grade: Nothing about the value can change the grade short of a CGPM redefinition of the SI that stops fixing c, and none exists (CODATA 2022). The added assumption at transit.py:145 would make the grade NARROWED only if some conclusion needed arrival at exactly D/c as a time a real channel achieves, rather than as the limit no channel can beat. No conclusion does, because advantage_over_light is zero by construction. A detected faster-than-c vacuum dispersion at radio frequencies larger than about 1e-12 would reopen H2; the bound read here is 4e-35.

snec-freivogel-krommydas.name: Smeared Null Energy Condition (Freivogel & Krommydas 2018), with 1/G_N and B = 1/(32 pi)

source.located: B. Freivogel & D. Krommydas, 'The Smeared Null Energy Condition', arXiv:1807.03808 (v1 10 Jul 2018, which LL ref.[8] cites under the title 'Wormhole Wars IV: A New Bound'; v4 of 19 Apr 2021 read), JHEP 12 (2018) 067. The value B = 1/(32 pi) is NOT in this paper. It comes from S. Leichenauer & A. Levine, arXiv:1808.09970 eq.(1) (JHEP 01 (2019) 133).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries and get_paper_content fullText (v4, 68,992 chars saved at d67/src/1807.03808.txt; grep finds no '32 pi' and no holographic argument for B). 1808.09970 v1, 2012.11569 v2, 2108.06068 v1 and 2111.05772 v1 read at source for B, status and domain. The 2018 v1 text itself was not read, so differences between v1 and v4 are not audited.

snec-freivogel-krommydas.published_statement: FK 1807.03808 v4 p.15: 'Proposed Bound. For all states within the regime of Perturbative Quantum Gravity (PQG), in any dimension d and for locally flat regions, the expectation value of the null-null contracted Stress-Energy tensor, smeared over any achronal null geodesic is bounded by <T^s_kk> >= -B/(G_N tau^2) (36). In (36) B is a constant we have yet to determine and tau is the affine distance over which we are smearing ... The smallest distance we allow ourselves to smear is l_uv, and the largest is such that we remain in a locally flat region.' Precise form, eq.(37): INT f<T_kk> dlambda >= -(B/G_N) INT (f')^2/f dlambda, 'for arbitrary smearing functions f which are smooth and non-negative', with 1/tau^2 = INT (f')^2/f (38). p.4: 'We have not determined the constant B'. Eq.(6): R^s_kk >= -#/tau^2, which 'does not have any factors of hbar'. p.15: 'there are no counter examples to this bound, but whether or not a rigorous proof exists is left for future research.' LL 1808.09970 eq.(1) fixes the coefficient at 1/(32 pi G_N). They prove it for holographic induced gravity on a brane, from the Brane Causality Condition, on a geodesic that is achronal on the support of rho.
published_hypotheses: H1 (FK p.4, p.15): states in the perturbative-quantum-gravity regime; vacuum-subtracted <T> (eq.15)

H2 (FK abstract p.1, p.4, p.15-16): smearing length tau small compared to the radius of curvature ('locally flat regions'); the evaporating-black-hole case at long affine distance is the stated reason (p.16)
H3 (FK eq.36; LL eq.1): the null geodesic is ACHRONAL on the support of the smearing function
H4 (FK eq.17, 36, 38, 44): null GEODESIC with affine parameter, contracted with its tangent
H5 (FK p.15-16): f smooth, non-negative and normalised; 'The bound probably does not hold for discontinuous functions f'
H6 (FK p.15): tau >= l_uv; G_N ~ l_UV^2/N (1-loop 'lore') gives the species scaling
H7 (FK p.19-20): evading Fewster-Roman needs 'an additional rule that the momenta involved in making the state must lie below the UV cutoff'
H8 (FK p.4, p.15): B undetermined ('a single, order one number'); status is a PROPOSAL and unproven
H9 (LL, for B = 1/(32 pi)): holographic CFT, induced gravity on a brane, Brane Causality Condition, semiclassical z0 << eps << l, Einstein equation leading
