snec-freivogel-krommydas.lacked_data: FK 2018 lacked three things: B, a proof, and evidence for smearing beyond the curvature radius. Later work supplied B = 1/(32 pi) (LL, holographic), with FKK arguing B << 1. Proofs arrived only in two restricted frameworks (LL; FF 2021). Evidence past the curvature radius came as two examples (FKK 2020). No datum has moved against the published statement, and no counterexample is known. For the tree's use the later data cut both ways. B arrived at its loosest natural value, and every smaller B strengthens the violation (E6), so nothing the authors lacked opens a door. But the violation sits at tau = 1.4-2.0 L_curv, which is exactly the regime FK 2018 excluded for lack of data and which later work reaches only by argument. M's hypothesis is partly borne out: the 2018 statement was incomplete and was completed later, but not overturned. The remaining open part, validity at tau >~ L in curved spacetime, is OPEN, not WRONG.
snec-freivogel-krommydas.grade_evidence: The form, the G bookkeeping and B = 1/(32 pi) reproduce the source exactly (E1, E3), and the tree's crossover reproduces to 4e-4 (E5). The tree nonetheless uses the bound on a larger class than was published: (i) its violation appears only at tau = 1.40 L_curv off-axis and 2.0 L_curv on the affine axis geodesic, whereas FK 2018 restrict to tau << L; inside that domain the configuration satisfies SNEC (E8). (ii) It integrates along non-geodesic, non-affine lines, though the affine axis geodesic still violates (E7). (iii) Achronality is unchecked (OPEN). (iv) Its truncated Gaussians print bounds that are off by up to -94%, with verdicts unchanged (E4-E5). The attribution of B to FK is a discrepancy, not a refutation. index3.py:750 over-states SNEC as a theorem. No moved datum reverses the verdict (E6).
snec-freivogel-krommydas.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: a proof that SNEC holds for tau >~ L in curved spacetime, plus an achronality check of the ray and the rows recast on the affine geodesic. WRONG, for the extension the use needs: a PQG state that violates SNEC at tau ~ L. DATA-DEPENDENT: a controlled derivation of B >~ 3/(32 pi), since E6 gives w_c > 1.5 there.

casimir-force-measurements.published_statement: Mohideen-Roy (physics/9805038, abstract and p.9) used an AFM to measure the force between a flat plate and a metallized sphere of diameter 196 um (Al plus <20 nm Au/Pd), at separations of 0.1-0.9 um. The result is 'consistent with present theoretical calculations including the finite conductivity, roughness and temperature corrections', with an rms deviation of 1.6 pN, which is 1% at the smallest separation. The ideal formula without corrections gives 6.3 pN, which is 5% at the smallest separation. Theory was compared through the proximity force F0 = -pi^3 hbar c R/(360 d^3). Bressi et al. (quant-ph/0203002, eq. 4) measured parallel Cr-coated silicon surfaces over 0.5-3.0 um through the cantilever frequency shift. They found K_C = (1.22 +- 0.18)e-27 N m^2 against pi h c/480 = 1.3e-27 N m^2, a '15% precision'. Lamoreaux 1997 (via Bordag et al. pp.209-210 and 249) used a torsion pendulum with an Au/Cu lens and plate over 0.6-6 um and reported agreement 'at 5%' with the ideal sphere-plate formula. The 1998 erratum corrects the lens radius from 11.3 cm to 12.5 cm (+10.6% in theory) and adds a 22% Au finite-conductivity correction at 0.6 um. Bordag et al. conclude that '(5-10)% accuracy would probably apply at the smallest separations only' and that the temperature corrections 'remain unconfirmed'. For ideal plates (Bordag et al. eqs 2.36-2.37 and 4.31): E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3) and F/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4), for perfect conductors at T = 0.
published_hypotheses: The measured quantity is a FORCE: sphere-plate force for Mohideen-Roy and Lamoreaux, plate-plate force gradient for Bressi. None of them measures an energy density or a stress tensor.
The plates are real metals: Al+Au/Pd, Cr, and Cu+Au. Agreement at the 1% level needed finite-conductivity and roughness corrections (Mohideen-Roy eqs 2-4).
The sphere-plate results reach E/A through the proximity force approximation F = 2 pi R E/A(d), with R >> d (Mohideen-Roy eq. 1; Bordag et al. eq. 4.106). Only Bressi is plate-plate.
Separation ranges: 0.1-0.9 um (Mohideen-Roy, absolute separation >= 120 nm), 0.5-3.0 um (Bressi), 0.6-6 um (Lamoreaux).

Electrostatic backgrounds were subtracted by calibration fits. In Lamoreaux the electrostatic force was about 5x the Casimir force, and d0 was fitted to the expected Casimir force (Mohideen-Roy p.3; Bordag et al. p.210).
Room temperature. The thermal correction is negligible for a << hbar c/kT, and Lamoreaux did not confirm it at 4-6 um.
Ideal-plate formula: perfect conductors, flat infinite parallel plates, T = 0, renormalised mode sum.
The uniform energy density -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^4) between the plates (Brown-Maclay) holds for perfect conductors only. Dispersive plates add a positive position-dependent term (Sopova-Ford eq. 50).

casimir-force-measurements.lacked_data:
What the authors lacked:
- Lamoreaux 1997 lacked accurate optical data and the correct lens radius (1998 erratum: +10.6% radius, 22% Au correction). His 5% agreement was partly fortuitous: corrections above 20% were 'not observed', and the electrostatic force was 5x the Casimir force (Mohideen-Roy p.3).
- Mohideen-Roy and Bressi lacked later patch-potential characterisation, and Bressi had no model for the 1-2 um residual.

What later data did:
- Harris-Chen-Mohideen 2000 (62-350 nm) and Bimonte et al. 2021 (0.2-8 um) confirmed the force and the Lifshitz theory, narrowed the precision claims, and opened the Drude/plasma question at finite T.
- None of this changes the conclusion the tree takes from these papers: the force is attractive and matches E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) in the limit d >> lambda_p.

What does change the tree's use was never missing from these authors' work:
- No cited experiment measured at 10 nm, and no experiment measures an energy density.
- At 10 nm, real gold gives E/A = 0.110 of ideal (computed here).
- The plasma-model gap-centre energy density there is positive (Sopova-Ford 2002, reproduced here).

Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the derivation re-derives exactly, and all three measurements agree with theory within their corrected errors. Evidence for it, narrowly: Lamoreaux's 5% was overstated for lack of data. That is a discrepancy, not a refutation.
casimir-force-measurements.grade_evidence:
The published results stand:
- The ideal formula re-derives exactly in sympy.
- Bressi agrees with pi h c/480 at -0.45 sigma.
- Mohideen-Roy agree with corrected Lifshitz theory at 1%.
- Bimonte et al. 2021 confirm the force.
- No refuting counterexample exists.

The tree uses the result more broadly than the sources support, in three places:
1. candidates.py:73-74 and tolman.py:483-485 carry 'measured' onto the energy density and the tensor, which no experiment measures (Sopova-Ford pp.15-16).
2. tolman.py:506-507 and 2855 evaluate at d = 10 nm. That is outside every cited range (>= 0.1 um) and below gold's skin depth. There, real-gold E/A is 0.110 of ideal, and the plasma-model gap-centre energy density is positive (+0.0405/a^4, computed here).
3. The Lamoreaux citation omits its 1998 erratum.

The tree does name 'ideal parallel conducting plates' (tolman.py:1317-1322). So the positive control's VERDICT YES stands: it depends only on the sign of p_r for an ideal-plate construction, and the tree already grants it only test_field_background. What moves is the 'measured' / 'not an invention' provenance at 10 nm, and the magnitude m = -2.019814e-21 kg, which is an ideal-plate construction rather than a number from the measured regime.
casimir-force-measurements.what_would_change_the_grade:
Any of these would move the grade:
- **To STANDS:** the tree restricts MEASURED to real-plate forces at d >= ~0.1 um (>= 0.5 um for plate-plate), labels u_0 and the tensor at 10 nm as ideal-plate constructions, and cites the Lamoreaux erratum. Alternatively, it picks d inside the measured range with d >> c/omega_p.
- **To DATA-DEPENDENT:** the verdict or a load-bearing magnitude is made to depend on real-metal E/A at 10 nm. The material model (Drude/plasma/optical data) and the Hamaker constant would then become live inputs.
- **To WRONG:** a measurement contradicts the sign of the force, or the d^-4 law inside the measured range. None was found.
- A direct plate-plate measurement near 10 nm would replace the plasma-model estimate eta = 0.110.

xi-required-reduced-planck-gut-scale.published_statement: BV gr-qc/0003025 sect 2.1 defines 'kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N)'. Sect 2.3 case 3: 'if xi > 0, and we have at least some places where (phi)^2 > kappa/xi ... there is definitely the possibility of ANEC violations'. Cases 1 (xi<0) and 2 (xi>0, phi^2<kappa/xi): 'ANEC is satisfied'. So in hbar=c=1, phi_c^2 = kappa/xi = M_red^2/xi and xi_required(phi) = (M_red/phi)^2. This scale which is presented here as empirical must also be associated with new physics.'

0708.2450.published_statement: Sec.3 p.6-8 (massless, xi > 0, 3+1 Minkowski): 'In this section we consider the massless quantised scalar quantum field with xi > 0 in a (3+1)-dimensional Minkowski space ... It will be shown that local averages of the energy density are unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states.' One-particle states Psi_kappa = a^dag(h_kappa) Omega, with h_kappa(k) = 4 pi sqrt2 (kappa - |k|/3) e^{-|k|/kappa}/kappa^2, <H> = 2 kappa/3 (26) and <rho>(0,0) = -xi (2 kappa)^4/(3 pi^2) (29). The j-particle states give (33) '<rho> < -rho_0 for all x in B(tau')', with total energy (34) '2 j kappa'/3 > 2 pi^2 rho_0/(xi kappa'^3) ... illustrating that the large negative energy density effects also require large positive overall energy, at least in this example.' 'Summarising, we have shown that to any bounded subset O of Minkowski space and arbitrary constant rho_0 > 0 there is a Hadamard state in which the expected energy density is less than -rho_0 throughout O. In particular any smearing rho_quant(f) with a non-negative compactly supported distribution f is unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states.' Theorem 4.2: for xi in [0,1/4], a globally hyperbolic spacetime and a timelike geodesic gamma, (rho_quant o gamma)(f^2) >= -Q_xi(f), where Q_xi(f) = Q~_A 1 + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_B[f]) + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_C[f]) (difference type). Abstract and Sec.5.2: 'Q(f) can be bounded by any power of the Hamiltonian greater than 2, while rho(f) cannot be bounded by powers less than 3'. Footnote 1 adds that q might have to be at least 4, and p.19 says p <= 2 is not excluded. Sec.6: '(at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space) ... the non-minimally coupled scalar field with xi > 0 admits states with arbitrarily large negative energy density over arbitrarily large bounded spacetime regions. Thus [it] cannot obey QEIs ... in which there is a state-independent lower bound'; 'negative energy effects with large magnitude, while possible over large regions, require more energy to achieve than positive energy densities of the same magnitude and ... the energy budget for these two effects will grow with a different power.' On an absolute QEI: 'one would expect that this can also be adapted to the non-minimally coupled field.'

0708.2450.lacked_data:
FO Sec.3 is a mathematical theorem, not a fit to data. Its only inputs are the free-field definitions and one explicit state. Every number re-derives exactly, and the printed looseness is conservative. So M's hypothesis finds no datum that moves the theorem on its own hypotheses. What the authors lacked in 2007 was coverage, not data:
(a) Massive and curved cases of the non-existence claim: still unproved. 1809.05047 repeats the N-copy argument 'even in Minkowski space', which supports the extension but does not prove it.
(b) An absolute version: FO say it is 'expected'. 1809.05047 asserts it was shown, but the math-ph/0611058 pages read here show only the difference form.
(c) The field-value dimension: FFKP (2023) show the negative energy is bought with large <:phi^2:>, and that an EFT field cutoff restores a class-dependent state-independent null bound. That does not change FO's theorem. It does limit the tree's 'the bound does not exist in that theory' to the theory without a cutoff.
For O1, the missing information is internal to the tree. f and c0 were never written down, and the threshold-x-ball accounting was never compared with the state's actual negative energy. Doing that moves the ratio from >= 1039.13 to 22.79 (xi = 1/4) and from >= 1803.55 to 102.02 (xi = 1/6).
0708.2450.grade_evidence:
The theorem stands on FO's own hypotheses. FO (26), (28) and (29) re-derive exactly by sympy, and rho(0,0) < 0 for every xi > 0. FO's printed constants are conservative discrepancies (j 16x larger than needed, (34) loose by 2), not errors.
It is narrowed against the tree's use in three ways:
(i) overturn.py:287-289 and candidates.py:161-166 drop 'massless' and '4D Minkowski', which FO state as hypotheses. qeihps.py:86-89 keeps them.
(ii) candidates.py:170-173 applies the replacement bound to every xi > 0. FO's Theorem 4.2/4.3 cover only xi in [0,1/4], geodesic worldlines, difference type.
(iii) The O1 figures at ledger.py:1976-1980 are not FO's. They are the tree's own computation on FO's one-particle family, reproduced to 3e-6 only under a recovered accounting that the tree never states (f and c0 undefined). The same state's actual negative energy gives <H>/|E_neg| = 22.79 and 102.02. So as a statement about the compensating energy of FO's construction, the '>=' figures are contradicted by computation. 'Cannot be outrun' describes one state family, not a theorem.
The grade is not WRONG, because nothing in FO is refuted. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no measured datum enters.
0708.2450.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: restore 'massless, 4D Minkowski' at overturn.py:287-289 and candidates.py:161-166, and 'xi in (0,1/4]' for the replacement bound. Then either state f, c0 and the threshold-x-ball accounting at ledger.py:1976-1980, with the actual ratios 22.79 and 102.02 beside them, or withdraw the figures.
A proof for massive fields or curved backgrounds would widen what STANDS covers; none was found here.
Toward WRONG, for O1 only: if the author meant E_neg to be the state's actual integrated negative energy, the '>=' figures are contradicted (22.79, 102.02). That cannot be settled without the author's definition of f and c0, which the tree does not hold.
The FO theorem itself would move only on a counterexample to (29) or to Psi_kappa being Hadamard. None exists, since (29) re-derives exactly.

pdg-g_fermi.lacked_data: Test of M's hypothesis for this result. The MuLan authors (2010-2013) lacked three things: (i) the O(alpha^3) QED term and a modern dispersive hadronic term; (ii) the CODATA 2018/2022 muon mass and the exact hbar; (iii) later lifetime input to the average. All three have since arrived. Eberhart et al. 2026 used them and obtained G_F = 1.16637859(59)e-5, 0.18 ppm below the tree's pin, which this pass reproduced to 2.5e-9. The computed moves are 9.0e-8 in v, 1.8e-7 in rho_EW and 3e-5 decades in the instanton exponent. That is evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: having the missing data did not change the conclusion. One datum is still lacking: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision. The EW-fit and CKM routes are about 1000 times less precise and disagree with G_mu by +2 and -3 sigma (2102.02825), so a BSM admixture in G_mu at the 1e-3 level is OPEN. Even a full 1e-3 admixture moves v by at most 3.8e-4 and the exponent by at most 0.12 decades. What does move the tree's printed digits is an unnamed hypothesis, not missing data: the tree-level / G_mu-scheme choice for v, lambda and alpha_W. The loop-level alternatives were available (Buttazzo 2013, PDG 2024). They move the S11 exponent by up to 6 decades and rho_EW's LO digits by about 25 % (illustrative), and no qualitative conclusion moves.
pdg-g_fermi.grade_evidence: MEASUREMENT: STANDS. The pin is READ identically in PDG 2024 Table 1.1. Every later READ value lies within 0.18 ppm of it. The 2026 extraction is reproduced to 2.5e-9, and MuLan's to within 0.27 ppm of its print (a recorded discrepancy inside its own 0.5 ppm error). No datum move exceeds 3.0e-7 in v. USE: NARROWED, because the owners drop two hypotheses. (1) v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) is exact only as the tree-level / on-shell definition (MuLan eq.2; Buttazzo eq.8-9). higgs.py:262-275 builds v, lambda and V_min at LO without saying so, and D20's rho_EW inherits them. (2) alpha_W at massform.py:2105-2110 is the G_mu tree coupling, while the owner's own READ source defines alpha_W = alpha/sin^2 theta_W. The gap is sum r_i = 0.0374, computed from READ PDG 2024 inputs. It moves the printed exponent 10^-160.95 by up to 6.07 decades across standard schemes, 2.1e5 times more than any move in G_F. S11's named mover ('a READ G_F') is met by this audit and moves nothing; the operative uncertainty is the unnamed scheme. Not WRONG: every tree formula is correct at tree level (sympy A1-A4), and no qualitative conclusion moves. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no moved or contested datum moves a conclusion.
pdg-g_fermi.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners name the tree-level / G_mu scheme at higgs.py:262-275 and massform.py:2105-2110, state the exponent as scheme-dependent at the ~6-decade level, and relabel G_F's status as READ (PDG 2024 Table 1.1). To DATA-DEPENDENT: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision confirms a BSM admixture in G_mu, and some tree conclusion turns out to depend on v at the 1e-3 level (none was found). To WRONG: a contradiction of the tree relations at tree level, which sympy A1-A4 exclude, or a qualitative conclusion reversed by the scheme spread, which would take ~160 decades, not 6. Resolving the MuLan 0.27 ppm re-run discrepancy or the Buttazzo last digit would not change the grade.

israel-1966-junction-conditions.name: Israel (1966) / Lanczos (1924) thin-shell junction conditions: S_ab = -(1/8 pi)([K_ab] - h_ab [K]) across a non-null hypersurface; static spherical shell sigma = -(1/4 pi R)[sqrt f], p = (1/8 pi R)[(1-M/R)/sqrt f]; 5D brane form [K_ab] - h_ab[K] = -8 pi G_5 S_ab

source.located: W. Israel, Nuovo Cimento 44B (1966) 1; erratum 48B (1967) 463; K. Lanczos, Ann. Phys. (Leipzig) 74 (1924) 518. None of these is on arXiv. Read through exact restatements: (a) Poisson & Visser gr-qc/9506083, eqs (3)-(8) for the junction condition and the sign convention [K]=K+ - K-, (9)-(13) for the dynamic shell and conservation, (14)-(17) for V(a); it cites Sen 1924, Lanczos 1924 and Israel 1966 with the erratum as ref [7]. (b) Mars & Senovilla gr-qc/0201054, Sec. 5-6: the preliminary junction condition (Clarke-Dray), Theorem 9 (at non-null points the singular part of Riemann vanishes iff the second fundamental form is continuous), and eq (86) as 'the Israel conditions [24]'. (c) Shiromizu-Maeda-Sasaki gr-qc/9910076, eq (15), the 5D brane form, and eq (16) under Z2. (d) Davis hep-th/0208205, eq (10), the Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet generalisation, which reduces to Israel at alpha=0.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9506083 (full), gr-qc/0201054 (pp.1-4, 12, 21-22, 25, 27-29, 31, 33-34, 38, 41), gr-qc/9910076 (full) and hep-th/0208205 (full). Israel 1966 itself and its 1967 erratum are NAMED-NOT-READ; what the erratum says is not known here.

israel-1966-junction-conditions.published_statement: As restated by Poisson-Visser (gr-qc/9506083, eqs 3-8): 'Define [K_ij] = K_ij(+) - K_ij(-). Then R^mu_nu = diag([K^i_j],[K]) delta(eta) ... T^{mu nu} = S^{mu nu} delta(eta), with S^i_j = -(c^4/8 pi G)([K^i_j] - delta^i_j [K]) (6) ... S^i_j = diag(-sigma,p,p) (7) ... in spherical symmetry, G=c=1: sigma = -(1/4 pi)[K^theta_theta], p = +(1/8 pi)([K^tau_tau]+[K^theta_theta]) (8)'. It adds energy conservation, d(sigma A)/dtau + p dA/dtau = 0 (13). Mars-Senovilla (gr-qc/0201054), Thm 9 and eq (86): continuity of the first fundamental form is necessary and sufficient for a continuous metric; at non-null points the singular Riemann part vanishes iff K_ab is continuous; n^sigma[G_sigma lambda]=0 are 'the Israel conditions'. In 5D, Shiromizu-Maeda-Sasaki (gr-qc/9910076, eq 15): '[q_mu nu]=0, [K_mu nu] = -kappa_5^2 (S_mu nu - (1/3) q_mu nu S), [X] := X(+) - X(-)'. Taking the trace shows this is identical to the tree's [K_ab] - h_ab[K] = -8 pi G_5 S_ab.
published_hypotheses: H1: Einstein field equations on both sides (Einstein-Hilbert action; a bulk cosmological constant is allowed). With a Gauss-Bonnet term alpha != 0 the condition changes (Davis hep-th/0208205 eq 10); Israel is the alpha=0 case.
H2: The hypersurface is non-null (Mars-Senovilla Thm 9). Null shells need Barrabes-Israel 1991.
H3: First junction condition: the induced metric is the same from both sides, [h_ab]=0 (M-S eq 49; SMS eq 15).
H4: A thin, distributional (delta-function) surface layer of codimension one (PV eq 5).
H5: Sign convention [X] = X(+) - X(-), with the unit normal pointing from the - side to the + side (PV eq 3; SMS eq 15).
H6: C^2 metrics on each side, with well-defined one-sided limits of their derivatives at the surface.
H7: For the static spherical reduction: spherical symmetry, constant radius, sqrt f positive (areal radius increasing along the normal on both sides) and f > 0 at the shell.
H8: Dimension. Israel 1966 is 4D; the D-dimensional form follows from the D-dim Gauss-Codazzi equations (SMS eq 15 for 5D).
hypothesis_drift: latticectc.py:148-152 (O3_ANSWERED_BY: 'a braneworld whose bulk satisfies its field equations with Israel junction conditions at the brane'). H1 is DROPPED at this site. The bulk field equations are left unspecified, but the Israel form is the correct junction condition only for an Einstein(+Lambda) bulk. For an Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet bulk the correct condition is Davis eq (10). As phrased, O3's answer criterion therefore covers only braneworlds with an Einstein bulk. At latticectc.py:78-80 the condition carries G_5, which implies H1, so there is no drift there. The refusal itself (CODIM1_CTC_IS_BRANEWORLD_RESULT = False) is not affected.
latticectc.py:78-80: H8 ADDED (4D to 5D). This is legitimate: SMS eq 15 restates it exactly, and it is re-derived here from the trace identity [K] = kappa S/(D-2).

latticectc.py:78-80: H5 is not stated (the orientation of the normal and the meaning of [.] are not given). This is harmless: the owner's sign matches PV eq 6 and SMS eq 15, and the condition is used only as a named missing ingredient.

ALL PASS (27 checks).

Starting from the Schwarzschild metric (Christoffels, then K_ab = nabla_a n_b on r=R) and S^i_j = -(1/8pi)([K^i_j] - delta[K]), the script derives sigma = -(1/4piR)[sqrt f] and p = (1/8piR)[(1-M/R)/sqrt f]. Both are symbolically identical to stability.py sigma()/pressure() (:132-142).

Device (M_in=-m, M_out=0): sigma = (sqrt(1+2m/R)-1)/(4piR) exactly, and p = -m^2/(16piR^3)+O(m^3) < 0. DEC holds at all four tabulated points, and the table reproduces to 4 significant figures.

wall.py: sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4piR), p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16piRs), p_0/sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4s), and 8piR(sigma_0-p_0) = -(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s), which is Le Eq 17. Surface DEC holds iff x <= 24/25, and the binding fraction is (1-s)/2. All exact.

Dynamic shell: the two-sided PV eqs (9)-(12) reduce to the static formulas and satisfy d(sigma A)/dtau + p dA/dtau = 0 identically. The tree's V(R) inverts the junction equation on the sqrt(f_out+Rdot^2) > 0 branch. The six V'' values at beta^2=0 reproduce, with V = V' = 0.

5D: [K_ab] - h[K] = -kappa S_ab is equivalent to [K_ab] = -kappa(S_ab - h S/(D-2)). D=5 gives SMS eq 15 and D=4 gives PV eq 6/8.

stefan-boltzmann.name: Stefan-Boltzmann energy density for scalar blackbody radiation: rho = pi^2/(30 beta^4), p = rho/3 (one free massless scalar in flat space, thermal state)

source.located: Stefan (1879), Boltzmann (1884) and Planck (1900) have no arXiv copy and are NAMED-NOT-READ. The per-scalar-dof form was read as restated in arXiv:1804.05382 (Dhumuntarao, Galvez Ghersi, Afshordi 2018), p.2 eq (15) and p.10 eq (86), and in arXiv:2512.15610 (de Farias et al. 2025), pp.5-6 eqs (26)-(33). The imaginary-time image-sum method, which is the route fluctuation.py takes, was read in 2512.15610 eqs (25)-(29). Its spatial analogue was read in gr-qc/9304008 (Kuo-Ford 1993), pp.9-12 eqs (3.28)-(3.45). The measurement of the photon Planck spectrum was read in astro-ph/9605054 (COBE FIRAS, Fixsen et al. 1996).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text for gr-qc/9304008, 1804.05382, 2512.15610 and astro-ph/9605054. Kuo-Ford was read in full and contains no thermal computation. The thermal Delta' = 2/3 is therefore the tree's own extension of their method, and fluctuation.py:83-87 presents it as such.

stefan-boltzmann.published_statement: 1804.05382 p.2 eq (15): 'pi^2/30 [k_B T(tau)]^4 = lim_{x'->x}[d/dtau d/dtau' G~+(x',x)], matching the Stefan-Boltzmann law for scalar radiation'. p.10: 'We precisely recover the Stefan-Boltzmann factor of pi^2/30 for scalar radiation'. 2512.15610 obtains the thermal state from G^(11) = 2 SUM_{l0>=1} G0(x - x' - i beta l0 n0) (eq 27). Eq (33) says that 'in the flat-space limit ... it is reduced to the well-known Stefan-Boltzmann law for a massless scalar field: T00(T) = -pi^2(1+xi)/(30 beta^4)'. The sign follows that paper's own convention. At xi = 0, which is the tree's minimal coupling, both restatements give rho = pi^2/(30 beta^4) with hbar = c = k_B = 1.
published_hypotheses: the field is free (non-interacting): Bose occupation and quasifree/Wick structure (2512.15610 eqs 23-24)
the field is massless, omega = |k| (1804.05382 eq 4; 2512.15610 eq 1)
thermal equilibrium at inverse temperature beta, i.e. a KMS/Gibbs state, realised as imaginary-time periodicity (2512.15610 eq 26, topology S^1 x R^3)
flat Minkowski spacetime (2512.15610 eq 33 is explicitly the flat limit; eq 31 adds redshift and curvature terms)
infinite spatial volume with no boundaries (spatial compactification adds Casimir and thermal-Casimir terms, 2512.15610 eqs 36-50)
renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski vacuum, i.e. the n = 0 image is dropped (2512.15610 eqs 19-20; KF eqs 3.26-3.27)
one real scalar degree of freedom; pi^2/30 is per bosonic dof, and photons with 2 dof give pi^2/15 (computed here, not read)
rho is T00 in the rest frame of the bath; p = rho/3 is the isotropic, traceless case
hypothesis_drift: No source hypothesis is dropped in substance, but several are not restated where the result is used. The hypothesis lists at noise.py:113-114 and fluctuation.py:84-85 name only 'one massless scalar, natural units, thermal equilibrium at beta'. Free/quasifree, flat space, normal ordering against Minkowski and no spatial boundary are stated at file level instead, and the code implements each of them: noise.py:111-112 ('zero-mean Gaussian (quasifree, KMS, Hadamard)'); fluctuation.py:16 ('normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, flat spacetime'); fluctuation.py:265-276 (free massless 1/(4 pi^2 sigma), summed over n >= 1 only, so n = 0 is dropped); fluctuation.py:460 (the shift (i n beta, 0) compactifies imaginary time only, so the volume is infinite).

An unstated step, now verified: noise.py:114 writes 'g(0) = pi^2/(30 beta^4) = rho'. That identifies <:phidot^2:> with rho, which requires <:phidot^2:> = <:|grad phi|^2:>. This equipartition holds for a massless on-shell field and fails for m > 0. Check B3 verifies it here. It is not a drift in use, because masslessness is stated.

Coupling: the tree uses minimal coupling (fluctuation.py:17). In flat space <:phi^2:>_beta = 1/(12 beta^2) is constant, so the improvement term vanishes and the thermal rho does not depend on xi (computed here). No drift.

Added scope in wording. This concerns a consequence drawn from the SB value, not the value itself. fluctuation.py:89 says 'ordinary positive-energy blackbody radiation fails KF's pointwise criterion by the same margin as negative energy', and noise.py:136 says 'with the photons'; both describe the scalar model. The SB coefficient transfers per dof: photon = 2 x scalar. The fluctuation numbers do not transfer. For the free EM field, the same Wick method gives thermal Delta' = 1/3 and Delta = 1/4 (computed here, check G3), not 2/3 and 2/5. Delta = 1/4 is still O(1). The formal claims at fluctuation.py:16-17 and 461-467 are explicitly scalar and are unaffected.

stefan-boltzmann.lacked_data: Stefan had an empirical T^4 fit. Boltzmann derived T^4 from thermodynamics plus radiation pressure p = u/3. Neither could fix the coefficient, which needs quantum (Bose) statistics; all three classics are NAMED-NOT-READ, so their data are not quoted. Three things came later: quantum statistics, which turns pi^2/30 per dof into a theorem; the FIRAS 50-ppm measurement of the Planck spectrum (read); and the 2019 SI, which makes sigma exact (computed). None of them changes the conclusion as the tree uses it. For one free massless scalar in flat, infinite space with natural units, the value is pure mathematics, re-derived here three ways. The law does change when its hypotheses are broken: mass (m/T = 1 lowers rho by 11.0%, computed here), interactions, boundaries, and curvature or redshift (2512.15610). None of these is in the tree's use. For this result the evidence runs against M's hypothesis: no missing datum was found that changes the conclusion. The one caution is scope, not data. The tree calls the scalar model 'blackbody radiation' and 'photons', but the EM field's fluctuation numbers differ (Delta' = 1/3 against the scalar's 2/3, computed here).
stefan-boltzmann.grade_evidence: The statement as used matches the restated source: rho = pi^2/(30 beta^4), p = rho/3 and g(0) = rho for one massless minimally coupled scalar with hbar = c = k_B = 1 (1804.05382 eq 15; 2512.15610 eq 33 at xi = 0). The owners' code implements every source hypothesis, and each is stated at file level (noise.py:111-112; fluctuation.py:16-17, 265-276, 460). The re-derivation agrees by three independent routes (26/26 pass), including the unstated step g(0) = rho and the independence from xi. The only input is the mathematical constant pi^2/30, and no datum has moved. Phys. 298, 2002): p.1-4, 10-13 incl. fn 1, 2, 13; p.16 eq.3.12; p.18. (b) Geroch, 'Faster Than Light?', arXiv:1005.1614 (2010): p.1-13. relativistic-causality-signals-at-most-c.published_statement: LSV 2002 abstract: 'special relativity can easily accommodate -- indeed, does not exclude -- faster-than-c signalling at the kinematical level. As far as causality is concerned, it is impossible to make statements of general validity, without specifying at least some features of the tachyonic propagation.' p.3-4: 'special relativity only requires, for its kinematical consistency, that there be an invariant speed' (invariant, not maximum). p.2: superluminal group velocities 'do not create any problem of principle, because the signal velocity still has c as an upper bound'. fn 2: signal velocity = front velocity. fn 13: with canonical kinetic terms 'the signal speed is c, regardless of whether the proper mass is positive, zero, or imaginary ... quantum mechanically the signal speed is also limited to c'. Geroch 2010 p.6-8: for 'Maxwell's equations, the Klein-Gordon equation, the neutrino or Dirac equations, the spin-s field equation and Einstein's equation -- the causal cone is precisely the future light cone'; 'solutions ... send signals that always lie within the causal cones'. p.10: the cones of other systems 'could very well lie outside the null cones of special relativity ... None of this would contradict our fundamental ideas about how physics is structured.'
published_hypotheses: H_SR (LSV p.4): homogeneity/isotropy, the relativity principle and pre-causality give an INVARIANT speed C, whose value is fixed by experiment. They give no MAXIMUM speed.

H_cone (Geroch p.6-8; LSV fn 13): signals stay inside the causal cone of each field's hyperbolizable equations. 'Signals <= c' holds exactly when every channel's cone lies inside the light cone. This is shown for Maxwell, KG (either sign of m^2), Dirac, spin-s and Einstein. It is a property of each matter equation, not of SR: a superluminal fluid with dp/drho > 1 is still well posed.
H_front (LSV fn 2; Scharnhorst eq.3; de Rham-Tolley eq.2.1): signal speed means the front velocity c/n(infinity), not the phase or group velocity.

H_vac (LSV fn 1; Scharnhorst p.6): c means light speed 'in unbounded empty space'. The Casimir (bounded) vacuum is argued to have front velocity > c under Kramers-Kronig plus passivity; this is contested (Fearn 2007) and unmeasurable.
H_caus (LSV p.12-18): paradoxes need superluminal signals that can go backwards in time in every frame. A speed fixed in a preferred frame can be stably causal.

cauchy-schwarz-inequality.name: Cauchy-Schwarz (Cauchy-Bunyakovsky) inequality in the form INT_0^tau_p f_tau^2 dtau >= (INT f_tau dtau)^2 / tau_p = 1/tau_p (formation.py transverse bound)

source.located: The integral inequality is Bunyakovsky 1859, 'Sur quelques inegalites concernant les integrales ordinaires et les integrales aux differences finies', Mem. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Petersbourg (VIIe ser.) t. I no. 9. The tree's form is exactly his special case (E), with psi = 1. The discrete form is Cauchy 1821 (Cours d'Analyse, Note II, Th. XVI eq. 30) and the quadratic-form proof is Schwarz 1885 (Acta Soc. Sci. Fenn. 15, 315-362). None of the three has an arXiv copy. Exact restatements: S. Kichenassamy, arXiv:2504.19543 (Ganita Bharati 42 (2020) 1-19), pp. 1, 7, 8; and Labropoulou et al., arXiv:2312.03478v2, pp. 1, 4, 6, 9.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2504.19543 (pp. 1-3, 5-9, 11-12 returned verbatim) and 2312.03478 (pp. 1-10, 12-16). Bunyakovsky 1859, Cauchy 1821 and Schwarz 1885 are NAMED-NOT-READ: they were read only as restated.

cauchy-schwarz-inequality.published_statement: Bunyakovsky 1859, as restated in arXiv:2504.19543 pp. 1 and 7: (C) INT_{x0}^{X} phi^2 dx * INT_{x0}^{X} psi^2 dx > (INT_{x0}^{X} phi psi dx)^2, 'for continuous functions of one variable'. '(E): Special case of (C) where psi = 1: (INT_{x0}^{X} phi(x) dx)^2 < (X - x0) INT_{x0}^{X} phi(x)^2 dx.' Equality 'holds for psi(x) = lambda phi(x), where lambda is a constant ... also equality for X = x0'. Bunyakovsky writes < and > where we write <= and >=. Schwarz 1885 (p. 8) derives it from the positive-definite binary form INT (alpha phi + beta chi)^2. He assumes the integrals are absolutely convergent, and the inequality is strict unless phi/chi is constant. Modern form (2312.03478 p. 6): INT_a^b f g <= ||f||_2 ||g||_2, with equality iff f and g are proportional. Identity behind the equality case (2504.19543 p. 7): (f,g)^2 = (f,f)(g,g) - 1/2 INT INT (f(x)g(y) - f(y)g(x))^2 dx dy.
published_hypotheses: Bunyakovsky 1859: phi and psi are continuous functions of one real variable on a finite interval [x0, X] (restated in 2504.19543 p.1)
Equality case: psi = lambda phi (for form (E), phi constant), or X = x0 (2504.19543 p.7)
Schwarz 1885: the integrals of phi^2, phi chi and chi^2 converge absolutely; the inequality is strict when phi/chi is not identically constant (2504.19543 p.8)
Modern Hilbert-space form: f and g are in L^2 of the interval; form (E) needs a finite interval length (2312.03478 p.6)
No physical datum: this is a theorem of real analysis

The inequality needs only three things: H_ENDS (formation.py:375), a finite tau_p, and f_tau in L^2. H_REST serves the integration by parts at formation.py:185-188. The integration by parts at formation.py:185-188 and the pointwise p_T at formation.py:113-114 contain f_tautau, so they need f_tau absolutely continuous; C^1 alone does not guarantee INT f_tautau dtau = [f_tau]. cauchy-schwarz-inequality.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result, and the evidence says the result stands. The inequality takes no data. It is a theorem of real analysis proved from a sum-of-squares identity: Lagrange/Cauchy in 1821, with its integral analogue restated in 2504.19543 p.7. It is re-derived here symbolically (C1) and machine-checked in discrete form (C7). What Bunyakovsky lacked in 1859 was modern integration theory, not data. He assumed continuity and Schwarz assumed absolute convergence; the later L^2 form only enlarges the class. Every function the tree uses is smooth or piecewise C^2 on a finite interval, which is inside every author's class. The one misprint on record is in an application, not in the inequality. What this audit found to record sits at the tree's use sites, not in the external result: (1) the integration by parts needs f_tau absolutely continuous, stronger than the stated C^1; (2) formation.py:196-197's exclusion also needs the static part's sign, which specthm R10(c) already hedges.
cauchy-schwarz-inequality.grade_evidence: The statement was READ via an exact restatement. Bunyakovsky's (E), (INT phi)^2 < (X - x0) INT phi^2 (2504.19543 p.7), is the tree's inequality with phi = f_tau and X - x0 = tau_p. The tree's hypotheses lie inside the source's: continuous or L^2 functions on a finite interval. The tree adds H_REST and H_FAMILY, which the inequality does not need, and drops nothing it does need. The re-derivation agrees on every check, C1 through C8, including the z3 vacuity and encoding guards, and the tree's own selftest rows pass. No datum enters the result, so no moved datum can change it. The drifts recorded all sit at adjacent use-site steps: C^1 against absolutely continuous f_tau in the integration by parts, the need for omega != 0 behind 'strictly', and the static-part sign behind formation.py:196-197. None refutes the inequality, and none changes a computed row.
cauchy-schwarz-inequality.what_would_change_the_grade: Nothing about the inequality itself could change it. A counterexample would need a real L^2 function f_tau on a finite interval with INT f_tau^2 < (INT f_tau)^2/tau_p, and C1's identity excludes that. The grade would become NARROWED only if the tree applied the step outside the source's class: an infinite-duration passage, an f_tau not in L^2, or strictness claimed without a continuous f_tau. A separate computation of the static part of rho + p_T along the sequence would settle formation.py:196-197's prose exclusion. It would not change this grade.

gr-qc/0209075#criterion.name: AMM linearised-stability criterion for validity of semiclassical gravity

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0209075 v1 (21 Sep 2002), Anderson, Molina-Paris & Mottola, 'Linear Response, Validity of Semi-Classical Gravity, and the Stability of Flat Space' (LA-UR-02-5809); PRD 67, 024026 (2003) per the owner (journal ref not re-read here). Abstract p.1; criterion Sec. III p.10; derivation of (3.4) pp.8-9; restatement Sec. V p.13.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(gr-qc/0209075) this stage, pages 1,4,5,8,9,10,13,14 of the v1 text layer; cross-checked against the cached alphaXiv text layer d67/amm_0209075.txt (the file the re-derivation searches). Appendix B and the bibliography not read (not needed for the criterion).

gr-qc/0209075#criterion.published_statement: Sec. III, p.10: 'We now state our stability criterion for the semi-classical approximation. A necessary condition for the validity of the large N semi-classical equations of motion (2.9) is that the linear response equations (3.4) should have no solutions with finite non-singular initial data for which any linearized gauge invariant scalar quantity grows without bound. Such a quantity must be constructed only from the linearized metric perturbation h_ab and its derivatives, and it must be invariant under allowed gauge transformations of the kind described by eq. (3.11).' Abstract: 'solutions to the semi-classical Einstein equations should be stable to linearized perturbations, in the sense that no gauge invariant perturbation should become unbounded in time.' Sec. V, p.13: 'If, for a given state and background geometry that solves the semi-classical equations, one or more solutions to the linear response equations experience unbounded growth in a gauge invariant sense, then the semi-classical approximation is not valid for that particular geometry, at least not for that particular state. Clearly this is a necessary, though perhaps not a sufficient condition for the validity of the approximation.'
published_hypotheses: P-H1 (p.8) the linear response equation comes from expanding the CTP effective action 'around a given semi-classical geometry g_ab that solves eq. (2.9)'; 'the first variation vanishes by (2.9)'; (p.9) the retarded correlator 'is evaluated in the background geometry of the leading order solution of the semi-classical equations (2.9)'

P-H2 large N: N non-interacting (free) quantum scalar fields of arbitrary mass and curvature coupling are the only matter; (2.9) is the large-N, RG-improved one-loop equation from the action (2.7) (pp.5-6)
P-H3 an in-state |in> (CTP in-in formalism); the verdict is specific to the state ('at least not for that particular state', p.13)
P-H4 renormalised Lambda, G_N, alpha, beta in (2.7)/(2.9); (3.4) needs no counterterms beyond those of (2.9)
P-H5 perturbations have finite non-singular initial data
P-H6 the growing quantity is a SCALAR, built ONLY from h_ab and its derivatives, and invariant under allowed gauge transformations (3.11)

P-H7 allowed gauge transformations: (3.11) for any X^a, EXCLUDING singular gauge transformations in the initial data, and excluding any (3.11) under which the action (2.7) is not invariant (boundary/surface terms) (pp.9-10)

2309.10848-eft-breakdown.published_statement: Sec. V: 'suggest that phi^2_max <~ (8 pi G_N |xi|)^-1 ... we will also argue that the quantum theory experiences breakdowns in its perturbative and semi-classical control in both frames when we allow for large field values. In the Einstein frame this breakdown happens in the scalar sector through a tower of irrelevant interactions that become important when phi^2 ~ (8 pi G_N xi)^-1; in the Jordan frame it occurs in the gravitational sector where the gravity path-integral becomes strongly coupled and looses its saddle-point approximation.' On the Jacobian: 'an explicit computation of the Jacobian would be necessary to make the following details exact but this is beyond the scope of this work'. On pNGB / shift-symmetric scalars: 'We do not disallow this possibility. Instead we offer the more conservative conclusion: when viewed as an EFT with field values bounded by |8 pi G_N xi phi^2| << 1, the mapping from Jordan frame to Einstein frame can also be done in the quantum theory.' Sec. V.B: 'our following arguments will apply for the xi > 0'. The constrained saddles are 'not true saddles'. 'as phibar^2 approaches (8 pi G_N xi)^-1 the action approaches zero'. Once the path integral is dominated by the one-loop term, 'We regard this as a manifestation of the breakdown of the semi-classical path-integral'. On xi < 0: 'the gravitational action moves to weaker coupling', the zero-mode integral 'diverges', and 'there is no natural reason to associate this field cutoff with the Planck scale'. Sec. I: 'This result provides a justification for our EFT requirement for xi >= 0. We do not have a similar argument for xi <= 0'.
published_hypotheses: P1 One free scalar, action (109) with V = 0 in the constrained analysis (112)-(113). The Einstein-frame expansion (106)-(107) is for n = 4.

P2 It is an ARGUMENT, not a theorem: the paper says 'suggest', 'argue' and 'points of evidence'. The Jacobian is not computed, and the Einstein-frame tower is dimensional analysis with M_cutoff ~ M_Planck.

P3 The Jordan-frame breakdown is argued for xi > 0 only. For xi < 0 the coupling weakens at large field, and the only signal left is that the zero-mode integral cannot be normalised; the paper gives no Planck-scale association for that case.

P4 Euclidean constrained instantons at a fixed constant zero mode, which are not true saddles. Compact boundary conditions, a bare Lambda > 0 (footnote 11), and the case analysed is Lambda_eff > 0. z_1-loop is only schematic.
P5 A shift-symmetric pNGB scalar with super-Planckian field values is explicitly left open ('We do not disallow this possibility').
P6 The conservative conclusion is |8 pi G xi phi^2| << 1. The '<~' form is an order-of-magnitude suggestion.
P7 Units hbar = c = 1 and G_N (not reduced). In the sign convention of (109) the effective Planck mass^2 goes as 1 - 8 pi G xi phi^2, so FFKP's xi < 0 is the Higgs-inflation sign.

schwarzschild-radius.published_statement: This is the sibling stage's record of physics/9905030, not re-read here. Eq.(14): ds^2 = (1 - alpha/R) dt^2 - dR^2/(1 - alpha/R) - R^2 dOmega^2, followed by 'the latter contains only the constant alpha that depends on the value of the mass at the origin'. Sec.6: 'alpha/r is nearly equal to twice the square of the velocity of the planet' (units c = 1). With v^2 = GM/r this gives alpha = 2GM/c^2. The tree uses the textbook form: r_s = 2GM/c^2, the areal radius of the horizon of the Schwarzschild solution of mass M.
published_hypotheses: Classical general relativity: the Einstein field equations hold.
Vacuum, R_mn = 0, everywhere except the origin. The horizon reading also needs the mass to lie inside r_s.
Static (1916 condition 1), with no time-space cross terms (condition 2).
Spherical symmetry (condition 3), hence non-rotating. Uncharged: no electromagnetic stress-energy.
Asymptotic flatness (condition 4).
M is the mass seen in the far-field Newtonian limit. alpha > 0 is taken on physical grounds, not derived.
Reading r = alpha as a horizon comes after 1916 (Lemaitre 1933 onward). Schwarzschild's own chart covers only R > alpha.

schwarzschild-radius.lacked_data: What the authors had: in 1916 alpha is a free integration constant fixed by the Newtonian limit, so no measured datum enters the form 2GM/c^2. Its numerical value needs only G and c. What came later: the current G (CODATA 2018 = 2022) and an exact c (SI 2019). Computed effect: moving G by 1 sigma, or to the 2014 value, shifts r_s by at most 3.3e-5 relative, two decades inside the tree's 5e-3 tolerance, so the conclusion does not move (R6). Data still lacking, then and now: no black hole near 100 kg has ever been observed, and GR is untested at curvature radii around 1e-25 m (energy scale 1.33e9 GeV). Evidence on whether that gap matters: within GR the Schwarzschild family is exactly scale-free in M, and leading EFT corrections are (l_P/r_s)^2 = 1.2e-20. Beyond-GR effects at that scale are not excluded by anything read here and are OPEN. They could change the physics of a real 100 kg hole, but not the arithmetic the tree uses r_s for. So for the result as the tree uses it, the missing data would not change the conclusion. For r_s as a physical horizon radius at 100 kg, the extrapolation is a named hypothesis, not a measurement.
schwarzschild-radius.grade_evidence: The tree evaluates r_s = 2GM/c^2 at 100, 5000 and 1e5 kg to confirm that the document's proportionality arithmetic is correct (warpfolder.py:42-44, 297-298, 491-502). As used there, the result is re-derived from the vacuum Einstein equations, and C is matched to the Newtonian mass three independent ways (R1-R2). The tree's 1.485e-25 m is exact to 4 s.f., no moved datum moves it (R6), and the tree's own selftest agrees. Five discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and none moves the grade. (1) The hole is quasi-static, not static: 8.41e-11 s, or 1.7e23 light-crossing times (R7). (2) Classical GR at r_s ~ 1e-25 m is an extrapolation; it is named here and not load-bearing. (3) The canonical data_used labels two document-printed values as computed r_s values. (4) The document's figures are 3-s.f. truncations, not roundings, and use 70% of the tolerance. (5) The stated hypothesis (uncharged, non-rotating) is narrower than the use needs; across Kerr-Newman the linear scaling survives and 2GM/c^2 becomes an upper bound (R4). gr-qc/9406053#causal-compactness.name: Borde, 'Topology change in classical general relativity' (arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, 30 Jun 1994), Sec. IX bullet 5 with Theorem 1 (Sec. IV): under causal compactness, topology change forces a closed timelike curve even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. So the 'singularity escape' fails, under the standard incomplete-geodesic definition.

source.located: arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1. The quotation is in Sec. IX 'Concluding Comments', 5th misconception bullet, which reads 'Closed-universe topology change leads either to closed timelike curves or to a singularity'. The theorem behind it is Sec. IV Theorem 1, with the non-time-orientable variant in Sec. VII. Definitions are in Sec. II.A (interpolating spacetime: smooth Lorentz metric, S1 and S2 spacelike, compact timelike tube T), Sec. III.B (causal compactness: the closure of I(p) is compact for every p) and Sec. III.E (open universes, 'externally simple'). 'The very end of this paper', which the bullet points to, is IX.C (degenerate metrics). Tipler 1977 and Geroch 1967 are NAMED-NOT-READ: they are known here only as Borde restates them.

gr-qc/9406053#causal-compactness.published_statement:
Sec. IX, bullet 5: 'Closed-universe topology change leads either to closed timelike curves or to a singularity. The truth of this depends on the definition of a singularity. If the standard incomplete-geodesic definition is used, then this statement is not true: as long as the causal compactness condition is met, causality violations have to occur when the topology changes, even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. But, other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true: this is briefly discussed at the very end of this paper.'

Sec. IV: 'By "causality violation" it is meant that there is at least one closed timelike curve.'

Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).'

Sec. VII: 'a causally compact spacetime that interpolates between non-empty boundaries S1 and S2 and which does not have closed timelike curves must (a) be diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and (b) hence be time-orientable.'

Abstract, on Theorem 3 (a different, dynamical theorem): 'it does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities (of the standard incomplete-geodesic variety)'.
published_hypotheses: M is a connected n-manifold with boundary S1 u S2 u T, where T is compact and possibly empty. M is smooth, Hausdorff and paracompact, and no dimension is assumed. If T is non-empty, it meets each S_i in that surface's boundary, the boundaries of S1 and S2 are diffeomorphic, and T is diffeomorphic to (boundary of S1) x [0,1] (Sec. II.A).

There is a SMOOTH, non-degenerate Lorentz metric in which S1 and S2 are spacelike and T is timelike (Sec. II.A). Borde names relaxing this as a way out: Sec. VIII (C^0 metrics) and IX.C (degenerate metrics).
Causal compactness: the closure of I(p) is compact for every p in M (Sec. III.B).
Theorem 1: M is time-oriented. Sec. VII extends the result to non-time-orientable metrics when S1 and S2 are both non-empty. When one boundary is empty, a non-time-orientable metric can avoid CTCs.

For open or asymptotically flat universes: M is the causally compact region of a larger 'externally simple' spacetime, i.e. outside that region the initial and final surfaces are diffeomorphic (Sec. III.E).
Topology change means S1 is not diffeomorphic to S2.
There is NO geodesic-completeness assumption.

'The escape fails' holds under the STANDARD incomplete-geodesic definition of singularity. Borde says 'other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true' and points to IX.C, metrics that degenerate at isolated points.

whitehead-convex-normal-neighbourhoods.published_statement: NOT READ at source (see source.via). The standard statement, NAMED-NOT-READ: on a manifold with an affine connection, every point has a neighbourhood U that is a normal neighbourhood of each of its points, and any two points of U are joined by a unique geodesic lying in U. The Levi-Civita connection of a sufficiently regular non-degenerate metric of any signature qualifies. The form READ in the tree's own sources is Fewster-Smith 0702056 p.7, stated for a globally hyperbolic M: 'every point x in M has such a neighbourhood U_x', where 'such' means a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood.

Yau proved the Riemannian positive mass theorem E >= 0 in dimension less than eight ... a separate argument is used to give a characterization of the equality case that if E = 0, then (M, g) is isometric to Euclidean space. Let (M, g, k) be an n-dimensional asymptotically flat initial data set that satisfies the dominant energy condition and has E = |P| ... Then E = |P| = 0.' It is an implication from geometric hypotheses (a complete, boundaryless, C^2, AF Riemannian slice with R_g >= 0 for k = 0) to E = 0 => flat. gr-qc/9304008-eq3.45.published_statement: KF v1 p.11-12, after (3.43)-(3.44): 'We may obtain lower bounds on Delta' and Delta. The minimum value of the right hand side of Eq. (3.43) is 1/2 and occurs when xi1 = xi2 = xi3 = 0. Thus we have that Delta' >= 1/2, Delta >= 1/3. (3.45) This means that the dimensionless Casimir energy density fluctuations are always at least of order unity. Note that this bound is independent of the details of the geometry of the boundaries. For the particular case of periodicity in one spatial direction, we have from Eq. (3.32) that xi1 = xi2 = -1 and xi3 = 3, so that Delta' = 6 and Delta = 6/7. ... hence we conclude that the gravitational field due to Casimir energy is not described by a fixed classical metric.' Inputs: (3.40) <:T00^2:>_C = <:T00:>_C^2 + (1/2)[<:phidot^2:>^2 + <:phi_x^2:>^2 + <:phi_y^2:>^2 + <:phi_z^2:>^2]; (3.41) <:phidot^2:>^2 = (1/2)(rho+p1+p2+p3)^2; (3.42) <:phi_x^2:>^2 = (1/2)(rho+p1-p2-p3)^2; (3.43) Delta' = (1/8)[(rho+xi1+xi2+xi3)^2 + (rho+xi1-xi2-xi3)^2 + (rho-xi1+xi2-xi3)^2 + (rho-xi1-xi2+xi3)^2], xi_i = p_i/rho (as printed in the v1 text layer); (3.44) Delta' = Delta/(1-Delta), Delta = Delta'/(1+Delta').
published_hypotheses: K1: flat (Minkowski) background (Sec. V: 'restricted to a flat spacetime background').
K2: massless scalar with the minimally coupled stress tensor ('for the massless scalar field we have' (3.41)).
K3: operators normal ordered with respect to the MINKOWSKI vacuum, with the expectation taken in the Casimir vacuum ((3.34)).
K4: pointwise (coincidence-limit) quantities; Delta as in (3.2) with its absolute value; Delta' as in (3.43).

K5: Wick condition. 'Wick's theorem applies to any quantum state |psi> for which there is a decomposition ... phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0. Both the Minkowski and Casimir vacua satisfy this condition.' This gives (3.39).

K6 (implicit, never stated): only the DIAGONAL squares appear in (3.40), i.e. G_AB = <:d_A phi d_B phi:> is taken diagonal. This is exact for periodic z, yet KF still assert the bound is 'independent of the details of the geometry of the boundaries'.

hypothesis_drift: RECHARACTERISED. fluctuation.py:79-80 says 'KF reach 1/3 assuming G diagonal; the proof here does not need it', and the canonical hypothesis reads 'KF: G_AB diagonal' (BOUND_NEEDS_DIAGONAL_G = False at fluctuation.py:151). KF state no such assumption: their (3.40) simply keeps only the diagonal squares (K6). The general Wick result is <:T00^2:> = rho^2 + (1/2) sum_AB G_AB^2 (A1). So KF's (3.40) is an identity only for diagonal G (E4). The part it drops, (1/2) sum_{A!=B} G_AB^2, is non-negative (A2), so (3.45) itself holds a fortiori for non-diagonal G (E5, E1). The tree's sentence is accurate about KF's written derivation. Read as 'KF's bound needs diagonal G', it would under-represent KF. The heading 'A THEOREM STRONGER THAN THEIRS' (fluctuation.py:64) leans mildly in the tree's favour: what is stronger is how general the proof is written, not whether (3.45) is true within K5.

KF's K5 names only pure vacuum-like states. The broadening is valid, because Wick factorisation holds for mixed quasifree states too. harmonic-function-maximum-principle.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE. The usual textbook form, given as the standard statement and not quoted from a source: (weak) if U is bounded and open in R^n, u is C^2 on U and continuous on its closure, and Laplacian(u) = 0 on U, then max and min of u over the closure are attained on the boundary. (strong) If U is also connected and u attains an interior max or min, then u is constant on U. Mean-value property: if u is harmonic near a closed ball B(x0, rho), then u(x0) equals the average of u over |x - x0| = rho. In R^3, Laplacian(1/|x|) = 0 for x != 0. The tree uses the local corollary (no strict interior minimum) and the 3-D kernel fact. Both are re-derived here rather than quoted.
published_hypotheses: u is C^2 with Laplacian(u) = 0 on an open set U (the source-free region)
Strict-extremum corollary: a closed ball around the point lies in U. This is local; connectedness is not needed.
Strong principle (no non-strict interior extremum unless u is constant): U connected, and the conclusion is 'constant on the component'
1/r is harmonic only in three spatial dimensions (in R^n the radial kernel is r^(2-n)), and only away from the sources
[All four are the standard form and were NOT READ at source]
hypothesis_drift: IMPLICIT, NOT DROPPED: three spatial dimensions. stability.py:115-118 and chain.py:140-142 compute the trace as (3r^2 - 3r^2)/r^5, which assumes n = 3. The canonical hypothesis list does not name this. Rederive S1c: in R^n the Laplacian of 1/r is (3-n)/r^3, zero only at n = 3. The tree is 3-D throughout, so there is no consequence; recorded so the limitation is named.

WEAKER THAN AVAILABLE: stability.py:117-118 says 'no strict minimum'. The strong principle gives more: no local minimum at all unless u is constant on the component. The step from there to 'NO static configuration is stably in equilibrium' (stability.py:118-119) also needs the converse of Lagrange-Dirichlet. That step is not part of this result; it belongs to the sibling entry earnshaw-1842-theorem.

SCOPE EXTENDED, VALID: the tree states the result for 'any point sources' (stability.py:115-116) and applies it to the device's continuous uniform shell (stability.py:119-120). Superposition covers this. S8 computes the interior shell potential exactly as 1/R_s, with zero derivative.

WORDING DISCREPANCY, NOT A REFUTATION: stability.py:118-119 reads 'The one escape Earnshaw permits is the DEGENERATE case, constant potential'. A degenerate Hessian at a point is not the same as a constant potential. S5: u = x^3 - 3xy^2 is harmonic, has grad = 0 and Hessian = 0 at the origin, is not constant, and is not a minimum. chain.py:336 has the correct form, 'Hessian identically zero'. The conclusion is unaffected.

SIGN-INDEPENDENCE, HOLDS: stability.py:116 says 'whatever their signs' and chain.py:149 says 'negating m flips U = m phi, and -phi is harmonic too'. The mean-value identity is linear in the m_i, and a harmonic function has neither a strict minimum nor a strict maximum. So the claim holds under either negative-mass dynamics convention. Numerically: S3a on 40 random mixed-sign configurations (worst relative deviation 3.1e-15), and S6 on 41 mixed-sign equilibria, all with indefinite Hessians.

INSTRUMENT PROXY (chain.py, not the owner): chain.py:323-326 has_strict_minimum returns True when the relative Laplacian exceeds 1e-9. A nonzero Laplacian does not imply a strict minimum, so this is a proxy. It is only ever asserted False (chain.py:416), and that is the valid direction.

source.located: Gao & Wald, 'Theorems on gravitational time delay and related issues', CQG 17, 4999 (2000), arXiv gr-qc/0007021v2, p.7, eqs.(11)-(13). gr-qc/0007021-eq11.published_statement: Gao & Wald (2000) eq.(11): take a null geodesic from p with affine parameter lambda and tangent k. The Jacobi matrix obeys d^2A^mu_nu/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta. This is the geodesic-deviation equation eta'' = -R(k, eta)k. On a transverse screen it reads eta_i'' = -K_ij eta_j with K_ij = R_{k e_i k e_j} (MTW sign). A point q is conjugate to p where det A = 0; 2004.12523 eq.(2.1) restates this in those words. Eq.(13), G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma^2 + R_kk] with G = sqrt(det A), follows from the Raychaudhuri equation, which the paper quotes from ref.[10]. Eq.(11) is a kinematic identity of Lorentzian geometry and assumes no energy condition. Gao-Wald's Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 add NEC and the null generic condition only to guarantee that det A does reach zero.
published_hypotheses: H1: a null geodesic, affinely parametrised, with tangent k. 2004.12523 adds the normalisation k.t = -1.
H2: a congruence from a point, A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta. It is twist-free by construction, so eq.(13) has no vorticity term.
H3: a smooth Lorentzian metric. Eq.(11) itself needs no energy condition, symmetry or field equation.
H4: four dimensions, for the coefficient 1/2 in eq.(13) and for G = sqrt(det A). For the literal 4x4 matrix, det A = lambda^2 det A_perp (sibling audit B2).
H5: the sign of the curvature term is tied to a convention (Wald's R_{abc}^d with the deviation equation's minus sign). An implementation must pair its Riemann convention with the matching sign.
H6: this is for the achronality consequence and is not part of eq.(11). A null geodesic is not achronal past a point conjugate to p (Hawking-Ellis Prop. 4.5.12, NAMED-NOT-READ).
hypothesis_drift: SIGN. A discrepancy in the tree's implementation, shown by computation. Eq.(11) is eta'' = -K eta with K_ij = R_{k e_i k e_j}. composite.py:233 defines T_ij = -R_{m a n b} k^m e_i^a k^n e_j^b using a standard MTW Riemann (composite.py:172-187), so T = -K (E2). composite.py:256 then evolves A'' = -T A = +K A, which is the opposite sign to eq.(11). A convention-free check confirms it (E3/E3b): with parallel starting data, the sign in eq.(11) reproduces the owner's own geodesic separations, while composite's sign returns the two transverse axes swapped. For a diagonal traceless T the sign flip changes neither det A nor any conjugate point (E4). gr-qc/0007021-eq11.lacked_data: Eq.(11) has no empirical input. It is the Jacobi (geodesic-deviation) equation, an identity that holds for any smooth metric. It was classical before 2000, it is restated unchanged in 2022 (2004.12523), and it is re-derived here (E1). There is no datum the authors could have lacked. I looked for evidence of something wrong and found it only in the tree's implementation: composite.py reverses the sign of the curvature term (E2, E3b). That is not missing data and not an error by Gao & Wald. It changes no number on the vacuum rays composite uses (E4). It changes the answer only on rays that pass through matter (E9).
gr-qc/0007021-eq11.grade_evidence:
**The source.** Eq.(11) and the det A = 0 criterion stand as published. They are re-derived (E1) and restated identically in 2004.12523.

**The tree's use is narrowed, and this is shown by computation.** composite.py:233 and :256 carry the curvature term with the opposite sign to eq.(11) (E2). A convention-free check against the owner's own geodesics confirms it (E3b). The code therefore agrees with eq.(11) only when the tidal matrix is traceless and diagonal (R_kk = 0). That condition is an unstated hypothesis.

**What still holds.** Every verdict resting on this key lies inside that class and survives:
- the window table and 'SEATS AND EARLY' at M = -2e-3 are reproduced exactly with the sign corrected (E4b);
- an independent eq.(11) integration gives 56.56 against 56.50 and 55.21 against 55.17 (E5);
- SR3's result for composite.survey(+2e-3), seats = True with delay > 0, is unchanged.

**Where it fails.** concentric.py:207 copies the same loop, and on its withdrawn non-vacuum ray the loop gives wrong conjugate points (E9).

**Other limits, each named.** The detector is sufficient but not necessary (E7). 'Pure Weyl' holds only to about 5% (E5).

**Why not another grade.** It is not WRONG, because nothing in the source is contradicted. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because there is no datum.
gr-qc/0007021-eq11.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade would become STANDS if composite's tidal or acc sign were brought into line with eq.(11), or if composite.survey stated R_kk = 0 as a named hypothesis and every caller stayed inside it. Every current standing caller does: concentric's design point is vacuum to 7e-4. It would become a finding against a tree verdict if a standing result used this loop on a ray through matter. A different sign in the paper's own printing would change nothing, because E3b compares the code with geodesics, not with the paper.

causality-sound-speed-beta2-le-1.name: Causality proxy: surface EOS slope beta^2 <= 1 as subluminal sound speed

source.located: The reading is not one paper's theorem. It is a convention of the thin-shell literature, and these sources state it together with their own caveats: E. Poisson & M. Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/9506083v1, PRD 52, 7318 (1995), sec. IV (pp. 3-4); M. Ishak & K. Lake, arXiv:gr-qc/0108058v2, PRD 65, 044011 (2002), sec. II.D; E. F. Eiroa et al., arXiv:2408.14328v3 (2024), after Eq (42). The causal content it borrows is textbook: a barotropic relativistic perfect fluid has characteristic speed sqrt(dp/deps), and is causal iff that is <= 1. That content is MACHINE-CHECKED here for the shell's 2+1 worldvolume, not read. The radial criterion that beta^2 is compared with is cross-checked against Pitre, Schneider & Poisson, arXiv:2604.05980v1 (2026) Eqs (3.11)-(3.16c). Their surface fluid is a thermodynamic polytrope, so its sound speed is defined. Later context: Simmonds & Visser, arXiv:2606.01061v1 (2026) sec. 2.6; Curiel, arXiv:1405.0403v1 (2014). Ellis, Maartens & MacCallum, GRG 39, 1651 (2007), arXiv:gr-qc/0703121 is NAMED-NOT-READ.

causality-sound-speed-beta2-le-1.published_statement: PV 1995 sec. IV: 'Under normal circumstances one might (naively) try to interpret beta0 as the speed of sound in the exotic matter located at the wormhole throat. Furthermore, under normal circumstances one would require beta0 to lie in the interval beta0 in (0, 1]. (One would normally deduce beta0 > 0 from the assumed stability of matter, and argue that beta0 <= 1 based on the requirement that the speed of sound should not exceed the speed of light.) ... there is no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound. A detailed microphysical model for the exotic matter would be necessary in order to settle such issues with any certainty. We therefore conclude that wormhole configurations with |beta0^2| > 1 should not be ruled out a priori.' Ishak-Lake 2002 sec. II.D: 'Phenomenologically, for timelike Sigma, P'/sigma'(R) represents the square of the speed of sound on Sigma and so one would normally expect 0 <= P'/sigma'(R) < 1. However, one could also construct Sigma out of (say) fields for which P'/sigma'(R) need not even be positive.' Eiroa et al. 2024: 'although kappa is the squared speed of sound in the case of ordinary matter, for which 0 < kappa <= 1, this may not be the case for exotic matter [PV 1995].'
published_hypotheses: S1: beta^2 = dp/dsigma is a PARAMETER of the linearised equation of state. Reading it as c_s^2 is an interpretation: PV call it 'naive', Ishak-Lake 'phenomenological'.
S2: the reading is offered for ORDINARY matter (sigma > 0). For exotic matter all three sources say it may fail, and none of them imposes beta^2 <= 1 there.
S3: settling whether beta is the sound speed needs a microphysical model of the shell matter (PV sec. IV). No source supplies one.
S4 (implicit; made explicit by PSP 2026): the shell matter is a barotropic, isentropically perturbed 2D perfect fluid, so the slope along the perturbation is (dp/deps)_s.
S5: the bound is the perfect-fluid one, characteristic speed <= light speed. Ishak-Lake write a strict '< 1'; PV and Eiroa write '<= 1'.
hypothesis_drift: KEPT (S1/S3): wall.py:201-203 calls beta^2 the thin-shell EOS slope, 'not identical to the microphysical sound speed ... The causality reading beta^2 <= 1 is the standard one and is a proxy.' That is the sources' own caveat, carried.

KEPT (S2): the wall is ordinary matter. sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4 pi R) > 0 and p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0, which matches PSP Eq 3.12 (check C3). The exotic-matter exemption in PV and Eiroa does not arise.

WEAKENED where the conclusion is stated: the proxy qualifier from wall.py:201-203 is dropped at wall.py:39-40 ('WITH A SUBLUMINAL SOUND SPEED'), wall.py:33 ('the causal ceiling'), wall.py:292 ('superluminal sound'), wall.py:558, wall.py:676-683 (table columns 'c_s / c' and 'causal?', then 'every window ... is causal'), warpshell.py:72-73 and restatus.py:155. The wording drifts; the arithmetic does not.

DROPPED (S4, shear-free fluid; not named in the tree): beta^2 = c_s^2 and the bound c_s <= 1 are exact only for a perfect-fluid surface (C4). The radial mode is a uniform change of area, so it sees only the bulk response. For an elastic wall beta^2 = K/(eps+p), while longitudinal waves have c_L^2 = beta^2 + mu_s/(eps+p) (RECONSTRUCTED from linear elasticity, C5b). The causal ceiling therefore falls to 1 - mu_s/(eps+p). The window stays open iff mu_s/(eps+p) < 0.92067 at x=0.3, 0.63397 at x=2/3, 0.26393 at x=4/5. wall.py:195-196 does list 'anisotropic elastic matter' as not treated, but as a question of clearing the stability threshold, not of the causal ceiling. Le's Bowers-Liang wall (wall.py:195) is an anisotropic fluid and the Einstein-Vlasov model is collisionless, so the models the tree actually works are untouched.

DROPPED (S4, isentropic perturbation): off an adiabatic perturbation, as in the RADIATING shell, the EOS slope is not the sound speed (Simmonds-Visser 2026 sec. 2.6 makes this point in general). Partly carried: wall.py:199-200 leaves the flux-coupled stability open, but not as a condition on the causality reading.

DIRECTION, carried: in a finite-thickness wall beta^2 is a positive-weight average of the local c_t^2 (C5a). So beta^2 <= 1 is necessary for local causality but not sufficient: beta^2 = 0.46 can coexist with a layer at c_t^2 = 1.5. restatus.py:156-157 keeps this open ('Open: admissible matter at that stiffness').
DISCREPANCY, immaterial: the sources differ on '< 1' versus '<= 1'. The boundary sits at x* = 0.84374, outside the operative window x < 4/5, so the difference changes nothing.

causality-sound-speed-beta2-le-1.lacked_data: PV 1995 named what they lacked: a microphysical model of the shell matter. For the tree's ordinary-matter wall, PSP 2026 has since supplied one for exactly this configuration. In that thermodynamic polytrope, beta^2 = dp/dmu IS the adiabatic sound speed squared, and its radial criterion reproduces beta2_crit exactly (C3). So having the data confirms the reading for the fluid class rather than overturning it (C4). Three things are still unknown and could narrow it: (i) shear, which lowers the causal ceiling to 1 - mu_s/(eps+p) and closes the window at x=4/5 once that fraction reaches 0.264, but at x=0.3 only once it reaches 0.921; (ii) non-adiabaticity of the radiating shell; (iii) the wall's thickness structure, which makes beta^2 <= 1 necessary but not sufficient. None of these is a datum that has moved. Each is an unmeasured property of an unbuilt wall. For orientation only, NOT read at source here and not used in the grade: textbook solids have mu_s/(rho c^2) of order 1e-10.
causality-sound-speed-beta2-le-1.grade_evidence: The arithmetic stands. x* = 0.843741892629416; beta2_crit increases with x (proved by z3) and is < 1 on all of x < 4/5; it equals PSP 2026's independent Gamma_1 exactly (C1-C3). The borrowed causal content also stands, but exactly only for a shear-free, isentropically perturbed surface fluid (C4). The tree applies it to ordinary matter, which is where the sources call it normal. The grade is NARROWED for two reasons. (a) The tree does not name the shear-free/isentropic hypothesis. For an elastic wall the ceiling is lower, beta^2 <= 1 - mu_s/(eps+p) (C5b). So the causality claims at wall.py:39-40, wall.py:683, warpshell.py:72-73 and restatus.py:155 are true for fluid walls and only conditional for solid ones. (b) The proxy qualifier at wall.py:201-203 is dropped at every site that states the conclusion. It is not WRONG: nothing refutes it within the models the tree actually works (a Bowers-Liang fluid, and Einstein-Vlasov with slope ceiling 1/2), and the owner does name the proxy.
causality-sound-speed-beta2-le-1.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names 'shear-free surface fluid, isentropic radial perturbation' as a hypothesis, and carries the proxy qualifier at wall.py:39-40 and 683, warpshell.py:72-73 and restatus.py:155, or else restricts the claim to fluid walls. Toward further narrowing: a read of Ellis-Maartens-MacCallum 2007, or of a relativistic-elasticity source, giving a stricter signal-speed bound, or a different longitudinal-speed coefficient than the linear one used in C5b. Toward WRONG: only a shear-free adiabatic surface fluid with dp/deps < 1 and superluminal characteristics, which C4 excludes.

no-existence-theorem-ssaf.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply here in its empirical form. Whether such a theorem exists is a mathematical and bibliographic question; no measured quantity enters it, and no measurement can create or remove a theorem. What the 1997-2021 literature lacked was technique, not data. HPS had only the AHS approximation and numerics, and HPS's own solution is not asymptotically flat. Sanders had rigorous tools only for compact ultrastatic slices, and calls the non-compact case 'more challenging, because the symmetry group becomes non-compact'. Two later Juarez-Aubry papers (2022, and 2024/2026) suggest the gap may be closing; both are NAMED-NOT-READ. Supporting the tree: no READ source up to April 2026 names such a theorem. Those later papers could change the conclusion, and that cannot be decided here.
no-existence-theorem-ssaf.grade_evidence: The claim is a universal negative over the literature and cannot be established or refuted here. For it: Sanders 2021 (READ) says static solutions had not been studied except Minkowski; HPS 1997 (READ) is numerical and not asymptotically flat (C2); the 2026 survey 2604.01047 (READ) names no such theorem. Undetermined: the discover_papers sweep did not run (alphaXiv quota), and Juarez-Aubry 2011.05947 and 2412.08402 are NAMED-NOT-READ. Two discrepancies in the tree's wording are computed. First, the class is not empty, since flat space solves HPS eqs (5)-(7) identically (C1), so the missing theorem is for NON-TRIVIAL existence. Second, 'closed ONLY by' fails as logic (z3, C3); hpscentre.py:303-308 has already superseded it. These are discrepancies in the wording, not refutations, so they do not make the grade WRONG. They do mean the best grade reachable is NARROWED, not STANDS.
no-existence-theorem-ssaf.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED, the expected ceiling, needs two things. First, 2412.08402 and 2011.05947 are read at source and hold no non-flat static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat solution or theorem. Second, a completed discover_papers sweep finds nothing contrary. The claim would then hold as NOT-FOUND, narrowed by the 'non-trivial' qualifier and the 'only'. qed-one-loop-beta-coefficients.lacked_data: The coefficients 4/3 and -7 are one-loop group-theory results. They use no measured input, so no later datum can move them, and none has: checks C3-C6 reproduce them exactly from the 2013 and 2024 sources read. The only numerical input to the tree's product is alpha. It moved from the CODATA 2018 value to the PDG 2024 average by -6.9e-10 relative, and no printed figure changes (checks C8, C10). M's hypothesis gains traction not on the coefficients but on the light-quark rows. There the tree applies the perturbative 4/3 N_c Q^2 at a hadronic threshold. What that step actually needs is the sensitivity of the hadronic vacuum polarization to Lambda_QCD and to the current masses m_u, m_d, m_s, which are proportional to v. That sensitivity is data-driven (PDG uses the dispersive Delta alpha_had), and the tree did not use it. Having it would move the 43/54 by an amount this audit brackets but does not measure: -37% to +65% for the extreme weights of check C9. The evidence against M's hypothesis for this result is that every source read agrees exactly with the tree's values. The evidence for a narrower scope is that the tree carries the coefficient into the non-perturbative region under a chiral-limit hypothesis it does not name.
qed-one-loop-beta-coefficients.grade_evidence: The coefficients themselves stand. b = 4/3 per unit N_c Q^2 and b_W = -7 are reproduced exactly from PDG 2024 eq.(10.13) and Buttazzo et al. eqs.(96)-(97), both read (checks C3-C6). The sign and the 43/54 re-derive (checks C1, C7). The one moved datum, alpha, moves nothing (check C8). The grade is NARROWED because the tree's use (address.py:526-542, 369-375) applies the coefficients to a larger class than the sources support, under three hypotheses it does not name. (i) The u,d,s rows, 16/43 of K, use the perturbative coefficient at a hadronic threshold in an implicit chiral limit, where PDG says the region is non-perturbative and data-driven. (ii) H1 assumes only SM charged content between the thresholds and Lambda. (iii) The O(alpha_s) quark corrections are not covered by 'one loop' in QED. No contradiction is shown, so this is not WRONG, and the C9 figures are brackets, not a corrected value. The split -22/3 + 1/3 remains NAMED-NOT-READ; only its sum enters the tree.
qed-one-loop-beta-coefficients.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade would become STANDS if the tree named the chiral-limit/hadronic hypothesis on the u,d,s rows and the SM-content hypothesis on H1. It would also become STANDS if a lattice or dispersive computation of d Delta alpha_had/d ln m_q, read at source, showed the current-mass sensitivity to be negligible against the 2/9 weight. It would become DATA-DEPENDENT if such a computation showed the light-quark weight differs materially from 2/9, which would move the 43/54 and with it the Th-229 and optical rows. Nothing found here could make it WRONG: the coefficients are exact group theory, reproduced from two sources read. Reading Erler hep-ph/9803453 and a background-field or pinch-technique paper would upgrade the -22/3 + 1/3 split from NAMED-NOT-READ.

flrw-perfect-fluid-first-law.name: Perfect-fluid continuity / first law in FLRW: d(rho a^3) = -p d(a^3), dS = 0; rho a^{3(1+w)} = const

source.located: This is a textbook result with no single primary arXiv source. The continuity half was READ in Baumann, 'TASI Lectures on Inflation', arXiv:0907.5424v2, p.20, eqs (21)-(26), and in the Problem eqs (112)-(113). The dS = 0 half was READ as an ASSUMPTION stated outright in Bousso, 'The holographic principle', arXiv:hep-th/0203101v2, Sect. 7.1, eqs (7.4)-(7.5): 'We will assume, for now, that the universe evolves adiabatically ... The comoving entropy density s is constant in space and time'. It was also READ in Masoumi & Mathur, arXiv:1412.2618v2: the Fig. 4 caption says 'assume that entropy is conserved in each comoving volume', and first-law eq (24) is 'T dS = dE + p dV' with no mu dN term. Classics NAMED-NOT-READ: Weinberg 1971, ApJ 168, 175 (bulk-viscous entropy production); Kolb & Turner 1990, ch.3; Weinberg 1972, Gravitation and Cosmology; Maartens, astro-ph/9609119.
