flrw-perfect-fluid-first-law.published_statement: Baumann 0907.5424, p.20: 'Eqns. (21) and (22) may be combined into the continuity equation d rho/dt + 3H(rho + p) = 0 (23). This may also be written as d ln rho / d ln a = -3(1+w) (24), if we define the equation of state parameter w = p/rho (25). Eqn. (24) may be integrated to give rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)} (26).' Problem (113): 'Derive the continuity equation from nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0.' Bousso hep-th/0203101, Sect. 7.1: 'We will assume, for now, that the universe evolves adiabatically. Thus, the physical entropy density is diluted by cosmological expansion: sigma(eta) = s/a(eta)^3 (7.5). The comoving entropy density s is constant in space and time.'
published_hypotheses: A homogeneous, isotropic FLRW metric with any k. The stress tensor is the perfect-fluid form T_mu_nu = diag(rho, -p, -p, -p) in the comoving frame (Baumann eq 20).
A perfect fluid: no shear viscosity, no bulk viscosity, no heat flux.
EITHER the Friedmann equations (21)-(22) OR local conservation nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0 (Problem 113). Either one is enough for continuity.
For the closed form rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)}: w = p/rho is constant (Baumann integrates (24) with w fixed).

For dS = 0: adiabatic evolution is ASSUMED (Bousso 7.1, 'We will assume, for now'). The thermodynamic route needs a Gibbs relation T dS = dE + p dV - mu dN in local equilibrium, with mu dN = 0 (Masoumi-Mathur eq 24 writes T dS = dE + p dV, i.e. fixed N).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, the thermodynamic step. The docstring at permute.py:256 reads 'd(rho a^3) + p d(a^3), which is T dS'. It equates the continuity residual with T dS without naming the Gibbs relation, local equilibrium or mu dN = 0. Check (4c) shows that continuity alone leaves T dS = -mu dN.

DROPPED, the perfect-fluid qualifier in the conclusions. permute.py:80-81 says 'for a comoving volume of perfect fluid'. The conclusions drop it and speak of the whole expansion without condition: permute.py:85 'THE EXPANSION IS ISENTROPIC', permute.py:274 'EXPANSION_DISSIPATES = False', the scorecard at permute.py:508 and the verdict at permute.py:541-543. With bulk viscosity the expansion itself produces entropy: T dS/dt = 9 zeta H^2 a^3 > 0 (check 5). With out-of-equilibrium energy exchange between perfect fluids (a decay), T dS_r/dt = Gamma rho_m a^3 > 0 (check 6b).

WEAKENED, an assumption presented as a measurement. The literature read here states comoving-entropy conservation as an assumption (Bousso Sect. 7.1; Masoumi-Mathur Fig. 4). permute.py:84 says it is 'measured below to machine precision'. The check at permute.py:250-270 tests rho_of_a, which is itself the continuity solution (permute.py:251), against continuity by a central difference. Any w used consistently passes (w = 5.7, check 8c). A mismatched rho and p gives an O(1) residual of 0.769 (check 8b). So the check verifies an identity and measures no physical system.

DISCREPANCY, not a refutation: the words 'machine precision' (permute.py:84). The measured relative residuals are 7.3e-12, 4.8e-11, 0 and 1.5e-11. That is central-difference error at h = 1e-6, about five orders above double epsilon (2.2e-16). What the check actually asserts is tol 1e-9 (permute.py:268).

DISCREPANCY, a label in the tree, not in the source. permute.py:436 and 449, and the prose at :117, call w = -2/3 'curvature-like'. But w = -2/3 gives rho ∝ a^-1, which is domain-wall-like. Curvature k/a^2 read as a fluid has w = -1/3 (checks 7 and 7b). The first-law check passes at w = -2/3 either way, so this does not move the result.
KEPT: constant w (the tree's hypothesis 1) matches the integration in Baumann (26). The tree never applies rho a^{3(1+w)} = const to a component whose w varies.

flrw-perfect-fluid-first-law.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis gets no support from this result: there is no datum for the authors to have lacked. The result is a theorem of local conservation, or equivalently of the Friedmann equations through the contracted Bianchi identity. It takes no numerical input, so no later measurement can falsify it; it was re-derived here symbolically for every k.

Only two kinds of data bear on how the tree uses it:
(a) The equation of state of real components. DESI DR2 now prefers an evolving w at 2.8-4.2 sigma. That kills the closed form rho a^{3(1+w)} = const for dark energy only. Continuity and perfect-fluid isentropy survive (check 3c), so the conclusion does not change.
(b) Whether real components are perfect fluids in equilibrium. The entropy the real universe produces comes from departures from that: bulk viscosity in mixtures, decays out of equilibrium, first-order transitions, reheating. Weinberg already had this in 1971, so it is not a gap in the data. It narrows the scope of the tree's use; it does not overturn the result.
flrw-perfect-fluid-first-law.grade_evidence:
The external result itself STANDS. Continuity rho' + 3H(rho+p) = 0, equivalently d(rho a^3) = -p d(a^3), was re-derived from nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 on FLRW for every k and from the Friedmann equations. rho a^{3(1+w)} = const is exact for constant w (sympy, 19/19 checks pass).

As the tree uses it, the result is NARROWED, because the tree drops two hypotheses:
(i) dS = 0 needs a Gibbs relation in local equilibrium with mu dN = 0. permute.py:256 calls the residual T dS without naming either, and the literature read (Bousso, Sect. 7.1) states adiabaticity as an assumption.
(ii) The perfect-fluid qualifier at permute.py:80-81 is dropped at :85, :274 (EXPANSION_DISSIPATES = False), :508 and :541-543. A bulk-viscous fluid gives T dS/dt = 9 zeta H^2 a^3 > 0 (check 5), so outside the hypothesis the expansion does dissipate.

It is not WRONG: within the perfect-fluid and equilibrium hypotheses the claim is exact.

Two discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and neither moves the result:
- The words 'measured to machine precision'. The relative residuals reach 4.8e-11, and the check tests the solution against its own equation.
- The label 'curvature-like' for w = -2/3, where curvature is w = -1/3.

No datum moves the conclusion.
flrw-perfect-fluid-first-law.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: the tree states the hypotheses at each place it uses the result. That means limiting 'THE EXPANSION IS ISENTROPIC' and EXPANSION_DISSIPATES = False to a perfect fluid in local equilibrium with mu dN = 0, as permute.py:80-81 already does for the first-law line.

relativistic-rocket-photon-exhaust.published_statement: Classic form (NAMED-NOT-READ at source): for a rocket whose exhaust is light, the rest-mass ratio needed to go from 0 to beta (or from beta to 0) is M0/M1 = sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta)). The READ generalisation, Le 2606.22531v4 Lemma 2.1, verbatim: 'Let P(s) be a C1 future timelike momentum on a finite interval in one Minkowski vector space, with F = -dP/ds future causal or zero. Set M = sqrt(-P^2), V = P/M, w = log(M_i/M), and E = -V.F. For E > 0 define eta = sqrt((F - E V)^2)/E, and set eta = 0 when E = 0. Then 0 <= eta <= 1 and L := Int sqrt((dV/ds)^2) ds = Int eta dw, d := arcosh(-V_i.V_f), log(M_i/M_f) - d = (L - d) + Int (1 - eta) dw >= 0. In particular, M_f/M_i <= e^{-L} <= e^{-d}. Equality in the first bound requires null nonzero flux almost everywhere with respect to dw; equality in the second requires a geodesic velocity path traversed without reversal, allowing coasts.' The paper then explains: 'Here eta is the magnitude of exhaust momentum per unit emitted energy in the instantaneous rest frame.' For a straight burn from beta to rest, d = artanh(beta) and e^d = sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta)). The tree's formula is therefore the equality case, and the lemma makes it a floor on M_i/M_f.
published_hypotheses: (Le L2.1) one Minkowski vector space: special relativity, flat spacetime. The GR extension Le cites is Henriques-Natario 1105.5235 (NAMED-NOT-READ).
(Le L2.1) P(s) is C1 and future timelike: the vehicle is a massive body with a well-defined total 4-momentum.
(Le L2.1) F = -dP/ds is future causal or zero: the only change in the vehicle's 4-momentum is emission of future-causal momentum (exhaust). Nothing is absorbed and no external momentum acts.

(Le L2.1, equality in the first bound) the exhaust is null almost everywhere (eta = 1): massless and collimated in the instantaneous rest frame. Any angular spread pushes eta below 1; Le eq 2.6 says 'equality requires a single emission direction'.
(Le L2.1, equality in the second bound) a geodesic velocity path with no reversal: the burn runs along one straight line in velocity space.
(classic, restated) M is REST mass, so the mass ratio counts all rest mass converted to exhaust.

relativistic-rocket-photon-exhaust.lacked_data: The result is a closed-form consequence of special-relativistic 4-momentum conservation and uses no measured datum. It depends only on beta, and c is now exact by definition. Ackeret lacked three things. (i) Modern precision tests of Lorentz invariance (Will 1403.7377, READ as cached text): these confirm his input rather than move it. (ii) A realistic account of what annihilation produces: proton-antiproton annihilation goes largely to pions, and part of that energy ends up in neutrinos and uncollimated gammas. No source for this was READ here, so it is only NAMED. By Le L2.1, any such loss pushes eta below 1, which can only raise the mass ratio, so it strengthens the 'floor' reading. (iii) The GR and arbitrary-path generalisations (Henriques-Natario, NAMED-NOT-READ; Le Lemma 2.1, READ): these extend the result and reduce to it in the tree's regime. Nothing found moves the conclusion. What changes is the class of propulsion it applies to, and that comes from a hypothesis the tree drops at arrival.py:13, not from a datum the authors lacked.
relativistic-rocket-photon-exhaust.grade_evidence: The formula itself stands. It is re-derived symbolically from 4-momentum conservation, cross-checked numerically to within 1.5e-10, and identified as the equality case of the READ Lemma 2.1 in Le 2606.22531v4; no datum can move it. Every number built on it (arrival.py:74-75 and 121-128, shipspec.py:142, index3.py:85-86) lies inside the result's class and reproduces; 3.7314 against 3.7317 is a 7e-5 discrepancy, recorded. The grade is NARROWED for one reason only. arrival.py:13 says 'no propulsion does better per unit energy', which drops the condition in Le L2.1 that momentum leaves only through the vehicle's own exhaust. The result holds for self-contained rocket propulsion, a smaller class, and the owner's own file prices two counterexamples to the unconditioned sentence (the slingshot and the magsail). Separately, two errors in the tree's own arithmetic, not in the external result, are recorded: '76x' (arrival.py:137) comes out as 55.99, and the '2.73 t of antimatter' (arrival.py:127) is the total converted mass, with an antimatter share of 1.37 t if the fuel is annihilated in pairs. Outside this entry's scope, and seen only while running arrival.py read-only: the magsail prose says '810 AU' and '2.6 ly' (arrival.py:150-152, 159), but the table the same report prints gives 2002 AU and 0.08 ly for that sail. That belongs to the magsail entry and is not graded here.
relativistic-rocket-photon-exhaust.what_would_change_the_grade: It becomes STANDS if arrival.py:13 is read as 'no self-contained rocket does better', meaning momentum leaves only as exhaust, because every other use is inside that class. It becomes WRONG only if an isolated system could change its rapidity by d with only future-causal emission while losing less than a fraction 1 - e^{-d} of its rest mass; Le's proof (READ) and the checks here rule that out. maxwell-stress-energy-curved.name: Maxwell stress-energy tensor and curved-space Maxwell equations (Gauss law sqrt(-g) F^{tr} = Q) in dynamical spherical symmetry

source.located: A textbook definition with no single originating paper. The originals (MTW Sec.22, Landau-Lifshitz) are NAMED-NOT-READ. The result was read directly on arXiv in Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, gr-qc/9712019v1 (Dec 1997): eq (7.106) is the dynamical spherical metric; eq (7.107) is T_mn = (1/4pi)(F_mr F_n^r - (1/4) g_mn F^2); eq (7.108) reads 'the most general field strength tensor will have components F_tr = f(r,t), F_thph = g(r,t) sin th'; eq (7.109) gives the curved Maxwell equations; eq (7.112) is the dyonic RN field; eqs (4.24)-(4.27) give curved Maxwell in form language; eq (8.26) is tracelessness. Corroborated by Bronnikov et al arXiv:2604.23741 p.2 eqs (2),(5),(6) and by Kubiznak-Svitek-Tahamtan arXiv:2605.01811 Sec.III Theorem 1, which restates Frolov-Zelnikov 2011.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9712019 (pp.1,24,27,35-37,114-118,123-124,146,208-209,229), 2604.23741 (pp.1-7), 2605.01811 (pp.1-6,10,17-18) and 0809.1003 (pp.1,13-15,34). maxwell-stress-energy-curved.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 p.201: 'The energy-momentum tensor for electromagnetism is given by T_mn = (1/4pi)(F_mr F_n^r - (1/4) g_mn F_rs F^rs) (7.107) ... Since we have spherical symmetry, the most general field strength tensor will have components F_tr = f(r,t) = -F_rt, F_thph = g(r,t) sin th = -F_phth (7.108) ... F_tr corresponds to a radial electric field, while F_thph corresponds to a radial magnetic field ... g^{mn} nabla_m F_ns = 0, nabla_[m F_nr] = 0 (7.109).' p.202: 'F_tr = -q/r^2, F_thph = p sin th (7.112). Conservatives are welcome to set p = 0 if they like.' p.107: nabla_m F^{nm} = 4pi J^n and nabla_[m F_nl] = 0, which are equivalent to d(*F) = 4pi(*J) and dF = 0. Bronnikov et al 2604.23741 p.2: 'the only admissible components of the Maxwell tensor F_mn are F_tr (a radial electric field) and F_thph (a radial magnetic field)', with T^t_t = T^u_u for any L(f).
published_hypotheses: The Maxwell Lagrangian is linear and minimally coupled. Carroll eq 4.32: a nonminimal (1+alpha R)F coupling is excluded by the equivalence principle, alpha = 0.
The photon is massless: there is no Proca term. This is implicit in 'Maxwell'.
The region is source-free (J = 0) for eq (7.109).
Spherical symmetry: the most general field has both F_tr = f(t,r) and F_thph = g(t,r) sin th. Setting p = 0 is a choice.
Gaussian units with G = c = 1 (normalisation 1/(4pi)); signature (-,+,+,+).
The metric is time-dependent (dynamical). The tree's R(t,r) form is a coordinate change that the covariant equations cover.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, magnetic component. drivensource.py:285-286 says 'the ONLY spherically symmetric field' and :302 says 'Spherical symmetry admits only F_{tr}'. The source (Carroll 7.108; Bronnikov 2604.23741 p.2) also admits F_thph = g sin th. Computed here: dF = 0 forces g = P constant. The dyonic field satisfies both Maxwell sets in the full dynamical metric and gives rho = (Q^2+P^2)/(8 pi R^4), j = 0, p_r = -rho, p_T = rho. m = M - (Q^2+P^2)/2R satisfies both Misner-Sharp equations for arbitrary Phi, Lambda, R. 'ONLY' overstates what the tree's statement covers. That is a DISCREPANCY in the statement; the conclusion is unchanged under Q^2 -> Q^2+P^2.

NORMALISATION, comment only. drivensource.py:302-303 says 'sqrt(-g) F^{tr} = Q'. For the code's F_tr = Q e^{Phi+Lambda}/R^2, sqrt(-g)F^{tr} = -Q sin(theta), computed. The comment holds in the form sqrt(-g)F^{rt}/sin(theta) = Q. The residual the code actually checks, d_a(sqrt(-g)F^{ab}) = 0 at lines 309-310 and selftest line 511, is correct and passes. This is a difference in wording, not in the computation.
SIGN CONVENTION, no effect. In Carroll's convention (7.112), F_tr = -q/r^2, the tree's F_tr = +Q e^{Phi+Lambda}/R^2 is charge q = -Q. T is quadratic in F.

IMPLICIT, NOT NAMED in the canonical hypotheses: m_gamma = 0 and minimal linear coupling. The owner's SCOPE (drivensource.py:459-460) and emwarp.py:183-185 name nonlinear electrodynamics as not covered. Neither names m_gamma = 0 or nonminimal coupling. A Proca term adds mu^2 A_t^2 e^{-2Phi}/(4pi) >= 0 to rho + p_r, computed. gr-qc/9802048.published_statement: '(1) A time-dependent traversable wormhole will have two throats, one throat being associated with each direction of travel ... (2) For each one of these throats the NEC is either violated or on the verge of being violated on the throat itself. (3) For each one of these throats there will be an open region (topologically open in one of the null hypersurfaces passing through the throat) whose closure intersects the throat such that the NEC is violated throughout the open region. (4) For each one of these throats there will be an open interval such that the transverse averaged NEC (transverse averaged over the throat after it is pushed out in the appropriate null direction) is violated throughout the open interval.' Eq.(8): T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 on the throat. Eq.(13): T_ab l^a l^b < 0 on an open neighbourhood near it. On (4): 'follows from appropriate modifications of the integrated constraint Eq.(11). See [11,14] for details.' Discussion: 'the suspension of the NEC is essentially an illusion in that if one ever succeeds in passing through the wormhole and reaching the other universe then one must have passed a throat as defined above and there must be NEC violations at or near this throat.'
published_hypotheses: H1: classical 3+1 spacetime with the Einstein equations, used to go from R_ab l l <= 0 (eq.7) to T_ab l l <= 0 (eq.8). The statement is about the TOTAL stress-energy; the Letter calls splitting it into exotic + normal parts 'semantic games' (Brans-Dicke, higher-derivative, dilaton, scalar-tensor).
H2: the throat Sigma is a compact, orientable, two-sided, spacelike 2-surface, with both orthogonal null geodesic congruences defined on a neighbourhood of it.

H3: A[Sigma] > 0 and A[Sigma(u)] >= A[Sigma] for every u(x) in an open neighbourhood of zero (eq.3). This gives theta_pm = 0 (eq.4) and pointwise NULL flare-out dtheta/du >= 0 everywhere on Sigma (eq.5).
H4: for the strict results (3) and (4), the strict-increase condition eq.(9): A[Sigma(eps f)] > A[Sigma] for some f. This excludes apparent horizons and bifurcation 2-spheres.

H5: for result (4), the averaged flare-out of footnote [14], 'outward-flaring over at least half its area'. The companion [11] def.4.1.3 defines it as int sqrt(gamma) sgn(dtheta/du) > 0. The transverse-averaged NEC is then [11] eq.(53): int sqrt(gamma) sgn(T_ll) < 0.
H6: twist omega = 0 (hypersurface-orthogonal congruence) and sigma^2 >= 0; enough smoothness for Raychaudhuri eq.(1) and for the fundamental theorem of calculus.
H7: the NEC conclusion holds for the SAME null congruence that defines the throat.
H8: the traversal step (every traversal passes 'a throat as defined above') is ASSERTED in the Discussion, not proved. No asymptotic-flatness, symmetry or causality assumption is made.

qcd-trace-anomaly-nucleon-mass.name: QCD trace anomaly is essentially the whole of the nucleon mass

source.located: X. Ji, 'A QCD analysis of the mass structure of the nucleon', hep-ph/9410274 (PRL 74, 1071 (1995)). The trace-anomaly operator comes from Crewther 1972, Chanowitz-Ellis 1972, Collins-Duncan-Joglekar 1977 and Nielsen 1977 (Ji ref [5]), and the heavy-quark theorem from Shifman-Vainshtein-Zakharov (Ji ref [11]). The current status was read in Yang et al. (chiQCD) 1808.08677 and in Hoferichter & Ruiz de Elvira 2506.23902.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-ph/9410274 (full pages 1-9 returned, eqs (1)-(38) and Table I). The 1970s anomaly papers (Crewther, Chanowitz-Ellis, CDJ, Nielsen, SVZ) are NAMED-NOT-READ. They were read only through restatement, in Ji eq (5) and in Hoferichter-Ruiz de Elvira 2506.23902 eqs (16)-(18) and (33).

qcd-trace-anomaly-nucleon-mass.published_statement: Ji 1995 eq (5): T^mu_mu = (1+gamma_m) psibar m psi + beta(g)/(2g) F^2. The second term 'is called the trace anomaly and is generated in the process of renormalization'. Eq (36): <P| (1+gamma_m) psibar m psi + beta(g)/(2g) F^2 |P> = M, 'an explicit form of Eq. (11)'. Eqs (10)-(11): <Tbar^00> = 3/4 M and <That^00> = 1/4 M, 'valid for any bound states in field theory'. In the rest-energy (Hamiltonian) breakdown, the trace-anomaly part H_a contributes (1-b)/4. Table I gives 190 MeV (m_s->0) and 210 MeV (m_s->inf) out of 939, and the text says 'the trace anomaly part contributes about 1/4'. 'In the chiral limit, the gluon energy from the trace anomaly (M/4) corresponds exactly to the vacuum energy in the MIT bag model.' Hoferichter & Ruiz de Elvira 2506.23902: the trace anomaly 'generates most of the nucleon mass via the gluon fields and thus contributes even in the case of vanishing quark masses'. Their eq (35) is m_N ~ (69+43+68+65+63+630) MeV: 'two thirds of the nucleon mass are of gluonic origin'.
published_hypotheses: The QCD energy-momentum tensor is symmetric and conserved, with forward nucleon matrix element <P|T^{mu nu}|P> = P^mu P^nu/M (Ji eq 4).
The operator trace comes from renormalization: T^mu_mu = (1+gamma_m) m psibar psi + beta/(2g) F^2 (Ji eq 5). The vacuum matrix element is subtracted.

n_f = 3 light flavours, with heavy quarks integrated out: 'their contributions cancel each other in the limit m_f -> infinity ... I neglect them' (Ji p.5). The heavy-quark sigma terms are then absorbed into F^2 via SVZ, <m_Q QbarQ> = -(alpha_s/12pi)<F^2>.
gamma_m and higher orders in beta(g) are neglected in the Hamiltonian split (Ji p.5).
Inputs: sigma_piN = 45 +/- 5 MeV (GLS 1991); a model estimate of the strange scalar charge (bM = 160 or 107 MeV); a(1 GeV^2) = 0.55 (CTEQ2).
'The anomaly is the whole mass' is exact only in the chiral limit (b = 0). At physical quark masses the anomaly is the fraction 1-b of the Lorentz-invariant trace.
The result concerns an integrated forward one-hadron matrix element. It says nothing directly about the local stress tensor at a point.
hypothesis_drift: DECOMPOSITION DROPPED (tolman.py:803-806). The tree says 'the trace anomaly is essentially the whole of the nucleon mass' without naming a decomposition. That is true for the Lorentz-invariant TRACE sum rule (Ji eq 36): 1-b ~ 0.83-0.89 with 1995 inputs and 0.88-0.91 with current ones. In the same source's rest-energy (Hamiltonian) decomposition the anomaly is only (1-b)/4 ~ 0.21-0.23 (Ji Table I: 190/210 MeV; chiQCD 23(1)(1)%). Which decomposition counts as 'the origin of mass' is contested in 2020-2026 literature. This is a gap in wording, not a refutation.

CHIRAL LIMIT WEAKENED to 'essentially' (tolman.py:803-806). The fraction is exactly 1 only for massless u, d and s quarks. At physical quark masses it is 1 - (sigma_piN + sigma_s)/m_N = 0.88-0.91 (computed). The canonical entry records the massless-quark hypothesis; the owner's sentence does not.

FLAVOUR COUNTING DROPPED (tolman.py:803-806). The ~0.9 holds with n_f = 3 counting, heavy quarks absorbed into F^2. If the c, b and t sigma terms are counted as quark-mass terms (n_f = 6, 2506.23902 eq 35), the F^2-only share falls to 0.672 (630 MeV).

LOCAL USE ADDED (tolman.py:800-806, against the pointwise hypothesis -u + p_r + 2 p_t = 0 at tolman.py:440). The tree applies an integrated forward matrix element to the local stress of the flux tube and the confining region. The source does not close that gap. Later literature closes it for the flux tube only, in pure Yang-Mills: Yanagihara et al. 1803.05656 measure a nonzero local trace, <T^R_mu_mu(r)> < 0, inside the SU(3) flux tube, 'in sharp contrast to' Maxwell, where it is zero everywhere.

NOTHING THE CONCLUSION NEEDS IS DROPPED. The inference 'QCD matter is NOT traceless' needs only <N|T^mu_mu|N> = M != 0, which is exact for any massive bound state (re-derived A1/A5), plus the fact that the nonzero trace is ~0.9 anomaly rather than quark mass.

qcd-trace-anomaly-nucleon-mass.lacked_data:
Ji lacked three things: a controlled strange scalar content (he called it 'the only large uncertainty' and bracketed it at 62 or ~115 MeV), any lattice decomposition, and a precise sigma_piN (he used 45 +/- 5). All three have since arrived. Lattice now gives sigma_s ~43 MeV, chiQCD 2018 measured the split, Roy-Steiner gives sigma_piN = 59.0(3.5) (in tension with lattice's 42.2), and there is a local lattice stress tensor for the flux tube.

Evidence against a change: every current input set gives an anomaly share of 0.88-0.91, higher than Ji's 0.83-0.89. The missing data made 'essentially the whole' stronger, not weaker. The sigma_piN tension moves the share by < 0.02. The forward trace = M is exact and needs no data. The flux tube is measured non-traceless locally.

Evidence for a limitation: it is a matter of definitions, not data. The phrase depends on the decomposition: the anomaly is ~1/4 in Ji's Hamiltonian split and the F^2 part is ~2/3 with n_f = 6 counting, and the 2020-2026 literature contests which decomposition counts as 'the origin of mass'.

For this result, M's hypothesis is confirmed that the authors lacked data. Having the data does not overturn the conclusion. What remains incomplete is scope and wording.
qcd-trace-anomaly-nucleon-mass.grade_evidence:
The load-bearing inference at tolman.py:803-806, that QCD matter is not traceless and so falls outside the identity's hypothesis, stands on its own. Three things support it: <N|T^mu_mu|N> = M != 0 for any massive hadron (sympy A1/A5); the anomaly is ~0.9 of the n_f = 3 trace sum rule on every current input set (0.88-0.91; chiQCD 91%); and the flux tube's local trace is measured nonzero in SU(3) Yang-Mills (1803.05656).

The supporting clause 'essentially the whole of the nucleon mass' is NARROWED, not wrong. It holds only (i) for the trace sum rule, (ii) with n_f = 3 counting, and (iii) exactly only in the chiral limit. In the same source's rest-energy decomposition the anomaly is ~0.22 (Ji Table I; chiQCD 23%), and with n_f = 6 counting the F^2 share is 0.67. The tree names none of these three conditions. It also applies an integrated matrix element to a local stress, a gap that later pure-Yang-Mills lattice work closes and the source does not.

No datum that has moved changes the conclusion, which rules out DATA-DEPENDENT. The Table I discrepancy (300 published vs 307 computed) is within the source's stated error and is recorded, not repaired.
qcd-trace-anomaly-nucleon-mass.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: tolman.py names the decomposition, for example '~90% of the trace sum rule, n_f = 3; all of it in the chiral limit'. Alternatively it drops the quantitative clause and rests on <N|T^mu_mu|N> = M != 0 plus the lattice flux-tube trace.

To WRONG: a first-principles result showing that the renormalized QCD flux-tube or nucleon stress is locally traceless. None was found, and 1803.05656 finds the opposite. For the quantitative clause alone: a sigma-term total above ~0.5 m_N in the n_f = 3 trace sum rule (current values are ~0.09-0.12 m_N).

To DATA-DEPENDENT: a sigma-term resolution that pushes the anomaly share below ~0.5. No current determination comes near that.

fewster-osterbrink-qei.published_statement:
Abstract (verbatim): 'By an explicit example, we show that such averages are unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states. This contrasts with the minimally coupled field, which obeys a state-independent lower bound known as a Quantum Energy Inequality (QEI). Nonetheless, we derive a generalised QEI for the non-minimally coupled scalar field, in which the lower bound is permitted to be state-dependent. This result applies to general globally hyperbolic curved spacetimes for coupling constants in the range 0 < xi <= 1/4.'

Theorem 4.2: (rho_quant o gamma)(f^2) >= -Q_xi(f) on Hadamard states, where Q_xi(f) = Q~_A^xi(f) 1 + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_B[f]) + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_C^xi[f]). The paper adds: 'for xi = 0, we recover results known for minimal coupling [5]'.

Sec.5 p.13: 'The lower bounds that we derived have the characteristic that they are state dependent except for minimal coupling.'

Conclusion p.20: the field 'cannot obey QEIs of the type previously studied in the literature, in which there is a state-independent lower bound.'
published_hypotheses: Real scalar field with L = (1/2)(grad phi)^2 - (1/2)(m^2 + xi R)phi^2, m real, using the Birrell-Davies sign conventions
xi in [0,1/4] for Theorems 4.2 and 4.3. The bound has a state-dependent term for xi in (0,1/4] and is state-independent only at xi = 0, where it reduces to [5] and [16]
Globally hyperbolic spacetime with smooth metric (Thm 4.2); n-dimensional Minkowski space with the vacuum as reference state (Thm 4.3)
Averaging only along a timelike geodesic parametrised by proper time (connected, need not be inextendible). No null or spatial averaging
Smearing weight f^2, with f in D(R,R): real, smooth, compact support
States are Hadamard states. The density is normal-ordered relative to a reference Hadamard state omega_0, so this is a difference inequality, and Q~_A depends on omega_0
The right-hand side -<Q_xi(f)>_Psi contains the Wick square :Phi^2:, so it depends on the state. Q_C carries the background Ricci curvature
The counterexample (Sec.3) uses a massless field with xi > 0 in 3+1 Minkowski space, with one-particle states Psi_kappa and their j-fold products
Sec.5.2 (n = 4, m > 0 for Thm 5.3): Q_xi(f) <= c(H+m)^p for any p > 2, while the smeared density cannot be bounded by H^q for q < 3

No missing datum. The result is a mathematical theorem about a free field on a fixed background, and no measured value enters it.

What came later is mathematics, not data. Fewster-Kontou (2018) extended the same method and confirmed the no-state-independent-bound argument, correcting one misprint while saying 'the final results are correct'. Fliss (2026) restates the result unchanged. The counterexample and the closed forms are re-derived here.

sm-tree-vev-from-gf.name: Tree-level SM relation v = (sqrt(2) G_F)^(-1/2) = 246.22 GeV (higgs.vev(); consumed by massform.py as y_f = sqrt2 m_f/v and g = 2 m_W/v)

source.located: The relation is the tree-level matching of the SM charged current onto Fermi theory (Weinberg 1967 / Glashow / Salam; no arXiv copy). Read in its exact modern statement in four places. (1) PDG 2024 Review sec.10 'Electroweak Model and Constraints on New Physics' (Erler & Freitas, rev. April 2024; PRD 110, 030001), pp.1-4, 7-9 and 21: eq.(10.5b) 'M_W = g v/2' '(at tree level, i.e., to lowest order in perturbation theory)'; p.2 'G_F/sqrt2 = 1/2v^2 = g^2/8M_W^2' and 'v = 246.22 GeV'; eq.(10.8) G_F = 1.1663788(6)e-5; eq.(10.22b) on-shell Delta r = 0.03685. (2) Buttazzo et al., arXiv:1307.3536, eqs.(8)-(11), (17)-(18), (27) and Tables 1-3. (3) Martin & Robertson, arXiv:1907.02500v5, eqs.(1.2)-(1.3), (1.11) and (4.1). (4) Morrissey & Ramsey-Musolf, arXiv:1206.2942, p.4 eq.(1) and p.21: this is the paper massform.py cites for 'masses proportional to phi'.

sm-tree-vev-from-gf.published_statement:
PDG 2024 sec.10, p.2: 'For mu^2 negative, phi develops a vacuum expectation value, v/sqrt2 = |mu|/lambda, where v = 246.22 GeV'. It continues: 'one obtains the EW boson masses (at tree level, i.e., to lowest order in perturbation theory) ... M_W = g v/2 = e v/(2 sin theta_W) (10.5b)', and 'For momenta small compared to M_W, this term gives rise to the effective four-fermion interaction with the Fermi constant given by G_F/sqrt2 = 1/2v^2 = g^2/8M_W^2'. The Yukawa coupling of H to psi_i is g m_i/2M_W (= m_i/v). Beyond tree level (p.8, eq.10.22b): M_W = A_0/(s_W (1-Delta r)^(1/2)), with A_0 = (pi alpha/sqrt2 G_F)^(1/2) = 37.28038(1) GeV and Delta r = 0.03685.

Buttazzo 1307.3536, eqs.(8)-(9): 'G_mu/sqrt2 = (1+Delta r_0)/(2 v_0^2)' and 'v_OS^2 = 1/(sqrt2 G_mu), delta v_OS^2 = -Delta r_0/(sqrt2 G_mu)'. Table 1 lists the tree-level (0-loop) thresholds 'g_2 = 2M_W/V', 'y_t = sqrt2 M_t/V' and 'lambda = M_h^2/2V^2', with 'V == (sqrt2 G_mu)^(-1/2)'. Table 2 gives 'V = 246.21971 +- 0.00006 GeV'.

Martin-Robertson 1907.02500, sec.IV: 'G_F = 1/(sqrt2 v^2) at tree-level. Including radiative corrections ... G_F = (1+Delta r)/(sqrt2 v_tree^2) = (1+Delta r~)/(sqrt2 v^2) (4.1)'. Their tadpole-free MS-bar v(173.1 GeV) = 246.60109 GeV (eq.1.11).
published_hypotheses: Tree level, i.e. lowest order in perturbation theory. PDG 2024 states eq.(10.5) 'at tree level, i.e., to lowest order in perturbation theory'; Martin-Robertson (4.1) writes 'G_F = 1/(sqrt2 v^2) at tree-level'.

Momentum transfer small compared with M_W (the four-fermion limit): PDG p.2 'For momenta small compared to M_W'. The correction 3m_mu^2/(5M_W^2) is a matter of convention: PDG footnote 3 and MuLan put it into Delta r, while Buttazzo eq.(27) does not (G_mu = 1.1663781 against 1.1663787).

Minimal SM with one Higgs doublet and a V-A charged current (PDG eqs.10.1-10.2). Buttazzo p.8: G_F is 'defined in terms of the muon lifetime as computed in the 4-fermion V-A Fermi theory supplemented by QED'.

Scheme. Beyond tree level, v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) is exact only as the on-shell (G_mu-scheme) definition of v, with the radiative corrections Delta r moved into counterterms (Buttazzo eq.8-9). In the tadpole-free MS-bar scheme v is a running, Landau-gauge quantity: v(173.1 GeV) = 246.60109 GeV (Martin-Robertson eq.1.11).

The couplings derived at tree level (g = 2M_W/V, y_t = sqrt2 M_t/V) are LO thresholds and differ from the MS-bar values at mu = M_t: g_2 is 0.65294 at LO against 0.64779 at NNLO, and y_t is 0.99561 at LO against 0.93690 (Buttazzo Table 3, eq.57).
Input: G_F from the muon lifetime, 1.1663788(6)e-5 GeV^-2 (PDG 2024 eq.10.8).

sm-tree-vev-from-gf.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis tested for this result. The relation is a tree-level identity of the SM Lagrangian (sympy A1-A3), and its only input is G_F.

What earlier users lacked, and what having it does:
(i) Post-2013 G_F refinements: new muon mass, exact hbar, O(alpha^3) QED and hadronic terms. Having them moves v by at most 9e-8 (COMPUTED).
(ii) Complete loop relations between G_F and a Lagrangian vev. These are now available (full 2-loop Delta r~ from Martin-Robertson 2019; leading 3-loop from Martin 2025). They make the MS-bar vev 0.155% larger, which says which vev is meant; it does not correct the tree identity.
(iii) A resolved M_W. Still lacking: CDF II against the other measurements is about 4 sigma. It moves the one consumer that amplifies it by only 0.28 decade.

The evidence runs against M's hypothesis here: no later data changes any conclusion the tree draws from v. What does change the tree's digits is an unnamed hypothesis, not missing data. The choice of the tree-level G_mu-scheme coupling g = 2M_W/v sets the instanton exponent at -160.95, while the other READ schemes give values down to -167.14. That scheme information was available (PDG, Buttazzo 2013) when the tree was written.
sm-tree-vev-from-gf.grade_evidence:
Taken as a tree-level identity the statement STANDS. sympy re-derives v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) from PDG 2024's tree relations, with g cancelling. The tree's 246.219640 GeV reproduces PDG's 246.22 and Buttazzo's 246.21971 (from his own G_mu). No READ muon-decay G_F moves v by more than 3e-7.

It is narrowed by hypotheses the owners drop, each sized from READ numbers:
(1) higgs.py:262-264 states the relation without 'tree level' or 'on-shell definition', which PDG eq.(10.5) and Martin-Robertson eq.(4.1) attach. The MS-bar vev differs by 0.155%.
(2) massform.py:528 and :2105-2106 build alpha_W from g = 2m_W/v, the 0-loop G_mu-scheme threshold (Buttazzo Table 1), without naming the scheme. Across five READ schemes the printed exponent -160.95 spans 6.19 decades, and '10^189.10' rises to as much as 10^195.28.

massform names H-TREE correctly for the Yukawas, and its qualitative Yukawa conclusions do not depend on the scheme.

Not WRONG: nothing is refuted, the formulae are exact at tree level, and no order-of-magnitude conclusion moves. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the one contested datum, M_W, moves the most sensitive consumer by 0.28 decade.
sm-tree-vev-from-gf.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: three things together. higgs.py names v at vev() as the tree-level (on-shell, G_mu-scheme) vev. massform names alpha_W = (2m_W/v)^2/4pi as the tree-level G_mu-scheme coupling, or carries the 6.19-decade scheme spread on the exponent. The G_F status reads READ (PDG 2024 eq.10.8).

To DATA-DEPENDENT: either of two things. An independent G_F at muon-decay precision contradicts G_mu at the 1e-3 level, and some tree conclusion turns on v at that level (none found). Or a resolution of M_W moves a conclusion (the full CDF shift moves the exponent by only 0.28 decade).

To WRONG: only a computed contradiction of the identity at tree level, which sympy A1-A5 exclude.

braneworld-definition-z2-field-equations.name: What a braneworld is: bulk field equations + brane action + junction conditions + Z2 identification (Randall-Sundrum-type construction)

source.located: Randall & Sundrum, 'An Alternative to Compactification', hep-th/9906064 (1999), eqs 3-5 and p.5; Shiromizu, Maeda & Sasaki, 'The Einstein Equations on the 3-Brane World', gr-qc/9910076 (2000), eqs 6, 12-16; Israel, Nuovo Cim. 44B, 1 (1966) = SMS ref [19]. Israel is NAMED-NOT-READ and was read through SMS eq 15 and Konya gr-qc/0605119 eq 19 (alpha=0).
source.via: Page text from alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries for hep-th/9906064v1, gr-qc/9910076v3, gr-qc/0605119v4 and 1211.5448v1. Israel 1966 is READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (SMS eq 15; Konya eq 19).

braneworld-definition-z2-field-equations.published_statement: RS2 (hep-th/9906064 eq 3): S = S_gravity + S_brane + S_brane', where S_gravity = int d4x dy sqrt(-G){-Lambda + 2M^3 R} and S_brane = int sqrt(-g_brane){V_brane + L_brane}. The paper says 'the related orbifold boundary conditions are described in Refs [8]'. Eq 4 is ds^2 = e^{-2k|y|} eta dx dx + dy^2, and eq 5 states 'The solution holds only when V_brane = -V_brane' = 24M^3 k, Lambda = -24M^3 k^2'. On p.5: 'we were initially interested in studying a theory without the orbifold boundary condition ... trivial to extend ... to a fully infinite extra dimension ... From now on we will consider this to be the case.' SMS (gr-qc/9910076) says 'Later, we assume the Z2-symmetry ... in accordance with the brane world scenario based on the Horava & Witten theory'. Eq 13 is T = -Lambda g + S delta(chi), with S = -lambda q + tau taken 'by the variational principle of the 4-dimensional Lagrangian for matter fields'. Eq 15 reads 'The singular behaviour in the energy-momentum tensor leads us to the so-called Israel's junction condition [q]=0, [K_mu nu] = -kappa5^2(S_mu nu - q S/3)'. Eq 16 reads 'Now we impose the Z2-symmetry ... K+ = -K- = -(1/2)kappa5^2(S - qS/3)'.
published_hypotheses: A 5D bulk that obeys Einstein's equations with a negative bulk cosmological constant (RS2 eq 3; SMS eqs 6, 13)
The brane is a thin, distributional (delta-function) hypersurface whose stress tensor S_mu nu comes from a brane Lagrangian: tension plus matter (RS2 eq 3; SMS eqs 13-14)
A Gaussian normal coordinate chi with a_mu = 0 near the brane (SMS eqs 11-12)
The Israel junction condition is DERIVED from the singular part of the Einstein equations with the delta source (SMS eq 15, citing Israel 1966)

Z2 symmetry is an ADDITIONAL, imposed assumption motivated by Horava-Witten (SMS p.2-3). RS2 uses orbifold boundary conditions to regulate the KK sum, then drops them for the infinite extra dimension (RS2 p.5)
A fine tuning V_brane = 24M^3 k, Lambda = -24M^3 k^2, giving zero 4D cosmological constant, which RS2 says it accepts 'without further explanation' (eq 5)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (latticectc.py:79-80, :140-143 CODIM1_CTC_REFUSAL): the tree lists Z2 identification as a required ingredient of 'a braneworld'. At source it is an extra assumption that is imposed ('Now we impose the Z2-symmetry', SMS). RS2 itself drops the orbifold condition (p.5), and non-Z2 braneworlds are an established literature (Konya gr-qc/0605119 and its refs [10]). Machine-checked here (C4, C4b): an asymmetric warp with k1 != k2 satisfies the bulk equations on both sides and the full junction conditions without Z2.

ADDED-AS-INDEPENDENT (latticectc.py:78-80): the tree counts four missing ingredients, but they are not independent. At source the Israel condition is the distributional content of the bulk field equation with a brane source (SMS eq 15). Machine-checked (C3): the delta-coefficient of G_mu nu equals the Israel condition exactly.

ADDED (latticectc.py:78-81): the tree requires the thin-brane (junction-condition) form. Smooth thick-brane braneworlds need neither a junction condition nor a brane action; checked here (C5: A = b ln cosh(cy), kappa^2 phi'^2 = 3A'' >= 0). DeWolfe-Freedman-Gubser-Karch (hep-th/9909134) is NAMED-NOT-READ.

H3 is a named hypothesis and the theorem is correctly styled a flat-quotient result, so this is a recorded scope difference, not an error.

later_literature.what: A braneworld without Z2 symmetry. Its generalized Israel condition (eq 19) reduces to the tree's form at alpha=0, and it states that Z2 is an assumption motivated by Horava-Witten, not a defining ingredient. It also finds that Z2-breaking terms decay at late times.

bose-integral-coth-identity.name: INT_0^oo sin(ku)/(e^k - 1) dk = (pi/2) coth(pi u) - 1/(2u)

source.located: A classical definite integral. In Legendre's form it reads INT_0^oo sin(ax)/(e^{2 pi x}-1) dx = (1/4)coth(a/2) - 1/(2a), and it is tabulated as Gradshteyn-Ryzhik 3.911.2. Neither Legendre nor G&R is on arXiv, so both are NAMED-NOT-READ. The tree gives no source for it: noise.py:112-114 and 573-574 state it without attribution. The theorem it follows from was READ at source. That theorem is the Abel-Plana summation formula in Henrici's form, restated with its full hypotheses in Berndt-Dixit-Gupta-Zaharescu, arXiv:2112.09819v1, Thm 2.1 p.3. The same formula appears as eq (2.16)-(2.17) of Saharian, arXiv:0708.1187v1 p.9. The tree's third-derivative kernel was READ independently as Ramanujan's Entry 8.2 at w = 4 (arXiv:2112.09819v1 p.16). Two further papers were read and do not state this entry: Coffey arXiv:1803.00632 and Gaunt arXiv:2601.13158.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2112.09819 (Thm 2.1 p.3, Entry 8.2 p.16), 0708.1187 (eqs 2.13-2.17), 1803.00632 and 2601.13158 (checked; the entry is absent). No paper read prints the identity verbatim. It is DERIVED here from the READ Abel-Plana theorem with phi(x) = e^{-xz}. Legendre and G&R 3.911.2 remain NAMED-NOT-READ.

bose-integral-coth-identity.published_statement:
Abel-Plana, as stated in 2112.09819 Thm 2.1 (Henrici's form). Suppose phi is analytic for Re z >= 0, and either SUM phi(n) or INT phi converges. Suppose also that |phi(x+-iy)| e^{-2 pi y} -> 0 uniformly on finite x-intervals, and that INT_0^oo |phi(x+-iy)| e^{-2 pi y} dy exists for every x >= 0 and tends to 0 as x -> oo. Then SUM_{n>=0} phi(n) = phi(0)/2 + INT_0^oo phi + i INT_0^oo [phi(iy) - phi(-iy)]/(e^{2 pi y}-1) dy.

Taking phi = e^{-xz} with z > 0 gives 1/(1-e^{-z}) = 1/2 + 1/z + 2 INT sin(zy)/(e^{2 pi y}-1) dy. That is Legendre's form, coth(z/2)/4 - 1/(2z). The substitutions y = k/2pi and z = 2 pi u turn it exactly into the tree's form.

Entry 8.2 (p.16): for Re w > 1 and Re z > 0, SUM n^{w-1} e^{-nz} = Gamma(w) z^{-w} + 2 INT y^{w-1} cos(pi w/2 - zy)/(e^{2 pi y}-1) dy.
published_hypotheses: Abel-Plana (Henrici's form): phi is analytic on Re z >= 0; SUM phi(n) or INT phi converges; |phi(x+-iy)| e^{-2 pi y} -> 0 uniformly on finite x-intervals; INT_0^oo |phi(x+-iy)| e^{-2 pi y} dy exists and tends to 0 as x -> oo. All of these hold for phi = e^{-xz} with z > 0.

The resulting identity holds for every real u != 0. It is odd in u, and the singularity at u = 0 is removable with value 0. By analytic continuation it holds on the strip |Im u| < 1 and fails at |Im u| = 1.
Entry 8.2 requires Re w > 1 and Re z > 0; the tree's kernel uses w = 4.
hypothesis_drift: noise.py:573-574: the tree assumes 'u > 0'. The source needs less: the identity holds for all real u and for |Im u| < 1. This narrowing is on the safe side, and no use in the tree falls outside it. No effect.

noise.py:112-114: the beta-scaled form (pi/2beta)coth(pi u/beta) - 1/(2u) relies on beta > 0, which the tree does not state. Beta is an inverse temperature, so the condition holds. The scaling is derived symbolically in rederive D1 and checked numerically in E5. No effect.

noise.py:112-114 and 575-577: the tree differentiates three times under the integral sign without stating that this is allowed. It is: dominated convergence applies with k^3/(e^k-1), whose integral is pi^4/15 (F4). The closed form equals the mode integral to 3.6e-27 (F3), and it matches Entry 8.2 at w = 4, READ at source (F5). The hypothesis is missing from the statement but satisfied in the use; this is not a narrowing.

noise.py:112-114 and 573-574 cite no source (neither Legendre, G&R 3.911.2 nor Abel-Plana). The tree's own CONTROL (noise.py:1030-1032) checks only the differentiated kernel, and only at u = 0.7. This is a documentation and coverage gap, not an error. Rederive E1 checks the identity itself at 8 points to 4.8e-28.

Out of scope and NOT audited here: the physical normalisation <:phidot phidot:>_beta = (1/2pi^2) INT k^3 cos(ku) n(k) dk. Only the arithmetic g(0) = pi^2/30 and g ~ -3/(2 pi^2 u^4) is confirmed here; the normalisation belongs to thermal-state-kms-hadamard.

rederivation.outcome:
All 23 checks pass; the script exits 0.

Three independent routes agree:
(A) Geometric series plus Mittag-Leffler. The Laplace term u/(n^2+u^2) is symbolic, and a symbolic Tonelli bound of pi^2 u/6 licenses swapping sum and integral. The Mittag-Leffler sum could not be closed symbolically (sympy 1.14 cannot sum it); instead it matches the RHS by mpmath.nsum at 40 dps, worst difference 1.0e-40.
(B) Abel-Plana with phi = e^{-xz}, fully symbolic, with its hypotheses checked.
(C) Taylor coefficients of the RHS equal (-1)^j zeta(2j+2), matching the termwise moments.

Numerical checks: 30-digit quadrature matches at 8 values of u in [0.01, 10], worst 4.8e-28. The identity is odd in u, holds at u = 0.3+0.5i, and fails at u = i, as the source's strip predicts. The beta-scaled form checks both symbolically and numerically.

The tree's use checks out: g(0) = pi^2/30; g ~ -3/(2 pi^2 u^4); the closed form equals the mode integral (3.6e-27); Entry 8.2 at w = 4 agrees symbolically; and the tree's own CONTROL at u = 0.7 is reproduced to 1.7e-20.

Side finding, recorded and not repaired: sympy 1.14 returns -oo for sp.limit((pi/2)coth(pi u) - 1/(2u), u, 0). That is a sympy defect; the true value is 0, since the series begins pi^2 u/6. The tree never takes this limit; it takes the correct sp.limit(g, u, 0).

later_literature.what: Restates Abel-Plana with rigorous hypotheses, together with Ramanujan's Entry 8.2. Between them they give the identity and its third-derivative kernel exactly. Nothing in it narrows the classical case.
States Abel-Plana as eq (2.16) with growth condition (2.17), the form used in QFT mode sums. Same conclusion.
Proves G&R hyperbolic-trigonometric entries by the same geometric-series method. It flags G&R 4.124.2 as needing correction; that is a different entry, and 3.911.2 is not discussed.
Gives new closed forms for INT sin(ax)/(b^2+x^2)^n. It does not treat this integral and gives no erratum to 3.911.2.

entanglement-distribution-requires-prior.name: A Bell pair spanning D must first be distributed by something crossing D at <= c (entanglement cannot be created by LOCC)

source.located: Primary theorem: Horodecki^4, 'Quantum entanglement', RMP 81, 865 (2009), arXiv:quant-ph/0702225v2: pp.4, 9, 12 (III.D swapping), 39-40 (XI LOCC), 45 eqs.(110)-(111), 51. Bennett-DiVincenzo-Smolin-Wootters 1996 (quant-ph/9604024) and Werner 1989 NAMED-NOT-READ (cited through the review). Counter-class sources READ: Reznik quant-ph/0212044 (2003); Pozas-Kerstjens & Martin-Martinez 1506.03081; Gao & Klco 2410.04162v2. Zukowski et al. 1993, Summers-Werner 1985 and Valentini 1991 NAMED-NOT-READ (restated in Horodecki p.12, Reznik pp.2-3, Pozas-Kerstjens p.1).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text on quant-ph/0702225, quant-ph/0212044, 1506.03081, 2410.04162. transit.py:46-49 cites no source; the theorem it needs was read at source in the Horodecki review.

entanglement-distribution-requires-prior.published_statement: Horodecki p.51: 'In bipartite states we cannot transform separable state into entangled one by LOCC at all.' p.45: 'LOCC operations can only transform separable state into another separable state (i.e. the set of separable states is closed under LOCC operations)', proved by eqs.(110)-(111). p.40: 'No transfer of quantum systems between the labs is allowed ... classical bits cannot convey quantum information and cannot create entanglement so that entanglement remains a resource that can be only manipulated.' p.12: particles 'which have never interacted in the past' can be entangled by swapping; 'If Alice and Bob will get to know the outcome, they can perform local rotation'. Counter-class, READ: Reznik abstract: 'causally disconnected probes ... even when the probes are initially non-entangled, they can wind up to a final entangled state ... entanglement persists between disconnected regions in the vacuum', and it vanishes at large enough separation. Pozas-Kerstjens p.10: 'spacelike entanglement is the result of the harvesting of only preexisting correlations in the quantum vacuum'; with Gaussian switching this is always possible if the gap is raised, and the amount harvested gets smaller. Gao-Klco: vacuum entanglement is 'available at all distances', with N ~ exp(-(m r)^2).
published_hypotheses: H1 bipartite A|B; the operation is LOCC (C3), or more generally a separable operation (C4, product Kraus operators) -- Horodecki p.40
H2 the INITIAL state is separable: the theorem says the separable set is closed under LOCC, and it does not forbid entanglement that already exists
H3 no quantum system passes between the labs (p.40); 'a quantum carrier must pass' is the contrapositive of H1-H2
H4 (swapping) the parties share entanglement with intermediaries; the Bell-measurement outcome has to reach the parties

H5 (harvesting) probes couple locally to a relativistic field whose vacuum is entangled across spacelike regions, so the initial state is not separable across the sites; perturbative Unruh-DeWitt detectors; Gaussian switching is spacelike only approximately (d > 7T/sqrt2)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 (separable initial state) -- transit.py:46-49, :251-258, ledger.py D23 :600-601: the theorem forbids CREATING entanglement from a separable start. The vacuum of a relativistic field is already entangled across spacelike regions, and initially unentangled local probes can take that entanglement with no carrier crossing (Reznik; Pozas-Kerstjens; Gao-Klco; computed here in C4). The canonical entry's hypothesis, 'entanglement arises only from a carrier that interacted locally and then travelled', is not the theorem and is false for the vacuum class.

2309.10848-verdict-anec.published_statement:
The verdict, Sec. II.C p.9, quoted in full: 'Short wormholes, those allowing for causality violations, can only be constructed and sustained when the achronal ANEC is violated [10]. As we showed, the self-consistent, effective, ANEC is only violated when we have large field values, an unphysical effect if we view non-minimal coupling as an EFT. Long wormholes such as the one in Ref. [13] do not require the violation of the achronal ANEC as there are no achronal null geodesics passing through their throat. While there is no relevant theorem, it is obvious that the violation of effective ANEC is needed to sustain long wormholes. Considering only cases where the connected areas are asymptotically flat, the divergence of null geodesics passing through the throat requires the violation of average null convergence condition and thus the effective ANEC. This point requires further consideration, but so far it seems that it is impossible to construct traversable wormholes in the Jordan frame without unphysical field values. In that sense the two frames can be considered equivalent.'

Classical result, eqs. (19)-(20): the effective ANEC integral equals INT dlambda [1 - 8 pi xi G(1-4xi) phi^2]/(1 - 8 pi G xi phi^2)^2 (dphi/dlambda)^2, 'where we discarded the boundary terms, assuming a smooth geodesic ... non-negative for xi < 0 and xi > 1/4. For 0 < xi < 1/4 it is positive for small field values, 8 pi xi(1-4xi)G phi^2 < 1, and negative for large values.'

Semiclassical result, eq. (89): INT dx^- <T_--> >= 0. 'we recover ANEC for any coupling in Minkowski spacetime. In the classical case we can do that, for bounded field values, for any spacetime curvature using the effective null energy.'

Discussion, p.28: 'Bounded field values additionally lead to a semiclassical proof of ANEC.'
published_hypotheses: H1: the EFT assumption is ADOPTED, not derived (abstract: 'we adopt the view'; eq. 2, a single cutoff with k^2_max ~ phi_max^{4/(n-2)} ~ M^2_cutoff). 'Unphysical' means outside this EFT. Sec. V motivates the assumption but does not prove it.
H2: the classical effective ANEC uses T_eff from eq. (15), integrated over an ENTIRE smooth null geodesic with the boundary terms discarded. It holds for any curvature.

H3: in the classical result the field bound is needed only for 0 < xi < 1/4, and there it is 8 pi xi(1-4xi)G phi^2 < 1. For xi < 0 and xi > 1/4 no bound is needed (away from the pole at 8 pi G xi phi^2 = 1).

H4: the semiclassical ANEC (eq. 89) holds for a free scalar in n-dimensional MINKOWSKI spacetime, for Hadamard states with <:phi^2:> <= phi^2_max finite (eq. 79), in the smearing limit of eq. (88). The quantity bounded is the ordinary <T_-->, not an effective stress tensor.
H5: in curved spacetime the semiclassical result is only the state-dependent smeared bound of eq. (72), not an ANEC.

H6: that ANEC must be violated is a theorem only for SHORT (causality-violating) wormholes, via achronal ANEC (Graham-Olum [10]). For LONG wormholes the source says 'there is no relevant theorem'; its argument covers only asymptotically flat connected regions and 'requires further consideration'.
H7: Jordan frame, a single real scalar, classical Einstein equation G = 8 pi G T_eff (eq. 14).

The canonical entry's kind, 'theorem', is stronger than the source, which says there is no theorem for long wormholes.

In the source that is a theorem only for short (causality-violating) wormholes, via achronal ANEC [10]. For long wormholes it is an unproved argument restricted to asymptotically flat regions. The unhedged 'must' does follow the source's own abstract and Discussion wording, so this is partly an inconsistency inside the source, recorded as such.

The source's semiclassical result (eq. 89) is the ORDINARY ANEC for <T_--> in MINKOWSKI spacetime, for a free scalar with bounded <:phi^2:>. feynman-hellmann.published_statement: Feynman-Hellmann in textbook form, re-derived here (T1-T2): for a Hermitian H(lambda) with a normalized eigenstate |psi(lambda)> of a non-degenerate (isolated) eigenvalue E(lambda), dE/dlambda = <psi| dH/dlambda |psi>. QCD form (FLAG 2024 Eqs.(431)-(433),(446), as transcribed by sibling audit sigma-term-scan and in massform.py): sigma_q = m_q <N|qbar q|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q, with sigma_piN = m_ud <N|uu+dd|N>. FLAG p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses'. The isospin limit is defined with the neutral pion.
published_hypotheses: FH-1: H(lambda) is Hermitian (self-adjoint) and differentiable in the parameter. In QCD, lambda = m_q enters linearly through m_q qbar q, so dH/dm_q = integral qbar q.

FH-2: the state is a normalized eigenstate of an ISOLATED, non-degenerate eigenvalue. The nucleon pole lies below the N-pi threshold. At a level crossing the ordered eigenvalue is not differentiable (T3).
FH-3: the result is a DERIVATIVE at a point, i.e. a first-order (linear) response. It is not the finite change M_N(m_q) - M_N(m_q = 0).

FH-4 (QFT): everything else is held fixed in the derivative, namely the other quark masses and the QCD scale / bare coupling (on the lattice, a fixed lattice spacing of the N_f theory simulated). The vacuum matrix element is subtracted. m_q qbar q is renormalization-group invariant, so sigma_q does not depend on the scheme.
FH-5 (FLAG): QCD only, isospin limit (neutral pion), N_f = 2+1 or 2+1+1 sea. The numerical sigma values carry FLAG's quality criteria and its named excited-state caveat.

1404.3565.published_statement: Abstract p.1: 'the cross-over is sharply defined at T_c = (159 +/- 1) GeV. The sphaleron rate in the symmetric phase (T > T_c) is Gamma/T^4 = (18 +/- 3) alpha_W^5, and in the broken phase in the physically interesting temperature range 130 GeV < T < T_c it can be parametrized as log(Gamma/T^4) = (0.83 +/- 0.01)T/GeV - (147.7 +/- 1.9). The freeze-out temperature in the early Universe, where the Hubble rate wins over the baryon number violation rate, is T* = (131.7 +/- 2.3) GeV.' p.3: 'In the interval 140 <~ T <~ 155 GeV the broken phase rate is very close to a pure exponential, and can be parametrized as log Gamma_Broken/T^4 = (0.83 +/- 0.01) T/GeV - (147.7 +/- 1.9). (7) The error in the second constant is completely dominated by systematics.' p.4: 'Gamma_Symm./T^4 = (8.0 +/- 1.3) x 10^-7 ~ (18 +/- 3) alpha_W^5, (8) where, in the last form, factors of ln alpha_W have been absorbed in the numerical constant.' p.4: 'the match gives us confidence to extend the range of validity of our fit (7) down to T ~ 130 GeV'. p.4: 'The freeze-out temperature T* can now be solved from [11] Gamma(T*)/T*^3 = alpha H(T*), (9) where alpha ... can be approximated by a constant alpha = 0.1015 ... Taking H^2(T) = pi^2 g* T^4/(90 M_Planck^2), with g* = 106.75, we find T* = (131.7 +/- 2.3) GeV'. p.1: 'the symmetric phase at T > T_c, where the (expectation value of the) Higgs field was approximately zero, to the broken phase at T < T_c GeV where it is finite'. p.3: 'If the temperature is below T_c, v^2(T) is approximately linear in T, and at T > T_c, it is close to zero. The observable <phi^dagger phi> is ultraviolet divergent and is additively renormalized; because of additive renormalization, v^2(T) can become negative.'
published_hypotheses: H-MSM: the minimal Standard Model is the complete electroweak-scale theory ('If the Standard Model is indeed the complete description', p.1); Higgs mass 125-126 GeV (p.1, p.4).

H-DR: dimensional reduction. The non-perturbative infrared (k <~ g_W^2 T) physics is 'fully contained' in the 3d SU(2)+Higgs effective theory eq.(4), with m_3^2, g_3^2, lambda_3 from 1- and 2-loop matching to (alpha_S(M_W), G_F, M_Higgs, M_W, M_Z, M_top, T) (p.2); all fermionic modes are treated perturbatively.
H-U1: the hypercharge U(1) field is left out of the effective dynamics ('little effect on the infrared physics') and counted only in the error budget: ~1% on E_sph and ~1 GeV on T_c (pp.2,4).
H-LL: Bodeker's leading-logarithmic Langevin dynamics, accurate to ln^-1(1/g_W), sigma_el ~ 0.9239 T (p.2); the Higgs is evolved by faster diffusive (heat-bath) dynamics.

H-LAT: a single lattice spacing beta_G = 9 and V = 32^3 a^3. The symmetric-phase rate is 'in practice indistinguishable from the continuum'; the broken-phase rate is 'within a factor of two' of the continuum estimate; finite-volume effects are negligible (p.3).
H-SYST: the uncertainties of the leading-log approximation and of the lattice spacing 'may affect the rate by a factor of two'; these and the U(1) errors are 'added linearly' into the +/-1.9 (p.4).

H-FIT-RANGE: eq.(7) was MEASURED over 140 <~ T <~ 155 GeV and extended to T ~ 130 GeV on the match to perturbation theory, using an ad hoc +1.6 shift of Burnier et al.'s rate (p.4); the abstract states 130 GeV < T < T_c.
H-EQ: close to thermal equilibrium, with Chern-Simons diffusion and Gamma defined by eq.(3) in the V,t -> infinity limit (p.1).

H-HUBBLE: T* is a COSMOLOGICAL freeze-out. It assumes a radiation-dominated expanding Universe cooling as dT/dt = -HT, with H^2 = pi^2 g* T^4/(90 M_Planck^2), g* = 106.75 (the top-quark mass effect on g* neglected, footnote 1) and alpha = 0.1015 constant to 0.5% (p.4, following Burnier-Laine-Shaposhnikov hep-ph/0511246).

H-COND: the 'approximately zero' Higgs above T_c is the additively renormalized, gauge-invariant condensate v^2/T^2 = 2<phi^dagger phi>/T, which 'can become negative'; there is 'no true phase transition' (abstract; p.3).

It does not say that T* is set by the Hubble rate of a radiation-dominated Universe with g* = 106.75. The tree's own SOURCES quote does hold the qualifier word for word (DRT-rate, massform.py:1141-1149, 'in the early Universe, where the Hubble rate wins'). But the prose, the S11 row and anomaly_route_priced() (massform.py:2195-2199, which evaluates broken_phase_ln_rate(T_FREEZE_GEV)) treat T* as a property of the window. Re-derived here: replacing H by 1/tau in the source's own eq.(9) moves the freeze-out temperature from 131.5 GeV (tau = 1/H = 2.7e-11 s) to 143.7 GeV (tau = 1e-15 s), 157.5 GeV (1e-20 s), and 165.8 GeV (1e-23 s), which is above the fit's range. 1710.05834.published_statement: Abstract: 'We use the observed time delay of (+1.74 +/- 0.05) s between GRB 170817A and GW170817 to: (i) constrain the difference between the speed of gravity and the speed of light to be between -3e-15 and +7e-16 times the speed of light'. Sec 4.1: 'the fractional speed difference during the trip can be written Delta v/v_EM ~ v_EM Delta t / D, where Delta v = v_GW - v_EM ... we conservatively use here D = 26 Mpc, the lower bound of the 90% credible interval on luminosity distance derived from the GW signal ... If we conservatively assume that the peak of the GW signal and the first photons were emitted simultaneously, attributing the entire (+1.74 +/- 0.05) s lag to faster travel by the GW signal, this time difference provides an upper bound on Delta v. To obtain a lower bound ... we assume the SGRB signal was emitted 10 s after the GW signal. The resulting constraint ... -3e-15 <= Delta v/v_EM <= +7e-16 (1)'. The same section continues: '... emission of photons before the merger is also possible (Tsang et al. 2012). Hence, certain exotic scenarios can extend this time difference window to (-100 s, 1000 s), yielding a 2 orders of magnitude broadening of the allowed velocity range on either side. While the emission times of the two messengers are inherently model dependent...'
published_hypotheses: H1 distance: D = 26 Mpc, the lower end of the 90% credible interval on the GW luminosity distance. A smaller D gives a weaker bound, so this choice is conservative.

H2 emission ordering (upper bound): the GW peak and the first photons were emitted simultaneously, so no photons left before the GW peak. The source itself says pre-merger photon emission is possible, and names an exotic window (-100 s, 1000 s).
H3 emission lag (lower bound): the SGRB was emitted no more than 10 s after the GW.
H4 the bound is on v_GW relative to v_EM (the photon speed), and dispersion of the gamma rays by the intergalactic medium is taken as negligible.
H5 background gravitational potentials affect both messengers in the same way (the Shapiro difference is treated separately in sec 4.3).
H6 the travel-time difference is small, the fractional speed difference is constant over the trip, and luminosity distance serves as the travel distance.
H7 one event and one line of sight (NGC 4993). The source says future joint detections are needed to separate emission delay from propagation delay.

1710.05834.lacked_data: In October 2017 the authors lacked three things. (a) A precise electromagnetic distance to NGC 4993. They used the GW-only 90% lower limit of 26 Mpc. The later SBF distance (about 40.7 Mpc, NAMED-NOT-READ) tightens the fast edge from 6.69e-16 to 4.27e-16 (computed). Here M's hypothesis runs against M: the missing datum would have made the bound stricter, not wrong. (b) Any model-independent value for the intrinsic emission delay between the GW and the gamma rays. The authors said so, assumed simultaneous emission, and named the exotic window that loosens the fast edge 57x. That datum is still missing: there is still one joint event (N = 1, as branelink.py:95 records). So this is not data that has since arrived; it is a stated hypothesis that the tree drops. (c) Anything about braneworlds. The bulk/brane mapping and its dependence on direction come later (GKLM, Polychronakos) and are hypotheses the tree adds. On the evidence either way, no moved datum weakens eq. (1). The only ways the tree's 7e-16 could be too tight are a failure of the emission-ordering assumption or an unlucky line of sight for an anisotropic bulk speed, and neither is a datum that has moved.
1710.05834.grade_evidence: The measurement stands as published. Eq. (1) re-derived from the source's own inputs gives a fast edge of 6.689e-16, printed as 7e-16; the comoving correction gives 6.728e-16; every later distance only tightens it. The tree's arithmetic on it reproduces to every digit (beta = 3.74165738677e-8, Delta_tau = 93.80654 ns). The grade is NARROWED because the tree uses +7e-16 without condition (branelink.py:61, :132; ledger.py:1787-1790; manyc.py:32, :68-69), while the source derives it only under simultaneous emission and itself names pre-merger photon emission. The source's exotic window would loosen the fast edge to +3.80e-14, giving beta <= 2.76e-7 and a B = 0 saving of 5.10 us. The tree names the bulk-graviton condition, but not the emission-ordering condition, and it does not attach a one-line-of-sight qualifier to the beta bound. The tree's qualitative conclusion survives even the exotic window: 5.1 us over a 4.2465-year light time is negligible, and O7 stays open on B. Two discrepancies in the tree's prose are recorded, not repaired. First, manyc.py:28-30's '4.226e-16 ... one part in 2.4e15' is the tree's own lag ratio, not a published figure. Second, manyc.py:33-34/167-172 and index3.py:1398 use the slow-side magnitude 3e-15 as a fast speed, 4.29x too large; this overstates the saving and so only strengthens the tree's conclusion. The source prints its slow side -3.105e-15 as -3e-15: a rounding discrepancy, not a refutation.

(1) from the source's own inputs; the re-derivation here found none. gr-qc/9406053#dynamics.published_statement:
Abstract: 'in dimensions >= 3 causally compact topology-changing spacetimes cannot satisfy Einstein's equation (with a reasonable source); i.e., there are severe dynamical obstructions to topology change. This result extends a previous one due to Tipler. Like Tipler's result, it makes no assumptions about geodesic completeness'.

Theorem 3: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact interpolating spacetime of dimension >= 3 with initial surface S1 and final surface S2. Suppose that i) every full ... null geodesic has a point on it at which F_abcd = U_[a R_b]ef[c U_d] U^e U^f != 0 ...; and ii) for any point u0 on a past-complete, affinely parametrized null geodesic lambda(u), the half-integral null convergence condition ... holds along lambda to the past of u0. Then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected.'

Sec. V: the curvature restrictions 'mainly follow from reasonable restrictions on the source'.

Sec. VI: for quantum fields, integral conditions 'might perhaps hold. This is so far only a piece of wishful thinking.'

Sec. IX.B: 'there might be violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are ... based precisely on large violations of the energy condition'. Also in IX.B, weakening the curvature constraints 'would not affect the presence of causality violations'.
published_hypotheses: H1: a smooth, non-degenerate Lorentz metric on a smooth, Hausdorff, paracompact manifold. Sec. VIII (C^0 metrics) and Sec. IX.C (degenerate metrics) name these cases as outside.
H2: time-oriented.
H3: M is a connected interpolating spacetime between disjoint spacelike S1 (initial) and S2 (final), with an optional compact timelike tube T diffeomorphic to dS1 x [0,1].
H4: causally compact, i.e. the closure of I(p) is compact for every p.
H5: dimension n >= 3 (the focusing lemma is stated for n > 2).
H6 (i): the null generic condition on every FULL null geodesic. This is weaker than Tipler's version.
H7 (ii): the half-integral null convergence condition along every past-complete affinely parametrised null geodesic.

H8 (only for reading the theorem): Einstein's equation, with Lambda allowed, serves only to turn a source restriction into (i)/(ii). 'Reasonable source' means a T_ab that yields (i) and (ii). The theorem itself is about curvature.
No geodesic-completeness assumption.

gr-qc/9406053#dynamics.lacked_data:
Theorem 3 uses no measured datum. The one constant it touches, Lambda, was unmeasured in 1994 and is measured now, and it drops out identically (D2). What Borde lacked, by his own account, was knowledge of how quantum sources behave on average: he calls (ii) for quantum fields 'wishful thinking'.

Later work points both ways.
(a) Several results show that making or holding a throat needs a source that violates integrated null convergence: D6 for every static zero-redshift throat, 2505.02210 for an explicit nucleation, and FSW. That confirms the theorem's logic: no counterexample satisfying (i)-(ii) exists, and the escapes sit where Borde placed them.
(b) Quantum-inequality work, read here only via restatement, suggests half-line integrated conditions can fail for quantum fields. That narrows how often the theorem applies to a semiclassical source. It does not falsify the theorem, and it was not shown here that (ii) itself fails.

No missing datum makes the theorem wrong. The open question is whether real sources meet its hypothesis. This does not favour M either: where (ii) fails, IX.B and Theorem 1 keep the CTC price under causal compactness.

semiclassical-einstein-equation.published_statement: HV 0802.0658 pp.7-8: the theory is 'the leading 1/N approximation of quantum gravity interacting with N independent and identical free quantum fields ... keeping the value of N G finite'. It is set on 'a globally hyperbolic four-dimensional spacetime', with T^R_ab = T_ab + F^C_ab I, finite in Hadamard states and satisfying Wald's axioms. 'The choice of these counterterms is not unique but this ambiguity can be absorbed into the renormalized coupling constants ... G_ab[g] + Lambda g_ab - 2(alpha A_ab + beta B_ab)[g] = 8 pi G <T^R_ab[g]>, (3.7) ... G, Lambda, alpha and beta are the renormalized coupling constants ... two dimensionless coupling constants which are zero in the classical Einstein equation.' HV p.13: 'the scope and limits of semiclassical gravity are not well understood'. HPS eq. (1): 'G_mu nu = 8 pi <T_mu nu>'; eq. (3): 'G^nu_mu(f(l), r(l)) = 8 pi <T^nu_mu(f(l), r(l); xi)>'; fn [20]: 'm = kappa = 0 ... the arbitrary renormalization scale parameter mu ... can be absorbed into the definition of f.' FW eq. (1.1): 'G_ab[g_cd] = 8 pi <T_ab[g_cd]>'. FW apply 'reduction of order ... to eliminate spurious solutions' and restrict to 'lengthscales ... much larger than the Planck length'.

newton-shell-theorem.name: Newton's shell theorem (potential constant, field zero, at every point inside a uniform spherical shell)

source.located: I. Newton, Principia (1687), Book I, Props. 70 (inside) and 71 (outside). There is no arXiv copy, and the Principia itself is NAMED-NOT-READ. I read the theorem through two restatements: (a) A.R. Klotz, arXiv:1308.1342v1 (2013), p.2 eq.(1), 'the force of gravity F_G acting on a test mass m at radial position r comes from the mass of the sphere below the object, due to the shell theorem: F_G(r) = -Gm(4/3 pi rho r^3)/r^2'; (b) J. de Haro, arXiv:2601.18660v1 (2026), p.10, 'by virtue of the shell theorem [29], the motion of a dust particle located inside the star satisfies r'' = -GM(r)/r^2', where [29] is the Principia. Both give the enclosed-mass form. Neither prints Prop. 70 word for word, so the exact interior form (-M/R inside, -M/d outside) was derived here by an exact sympy integral (S1). The GR cross-check is Birkhoff, read through the restatement in Johansen-Ravndal, arXiv:physics/0508163v2 p.1.

newton-shell-theorem.published_statement: Principia I, Prop. 70, as restated and as re-derived here. A particle inside a spherical shell of uniform surface density, attracted by an inverse-square force to every point of the shell, feels no net force at any interior point. Prop. 71: outside the shell, the attraction is as if the whole mass sat at the centre. The restatements read give the enclosed-mass form: Klotz eq.(1) and de Haro p.10, r'' = -GM(r)/r^2. Potential form, derived in S1: Phi = -GM/R for d<R (constant) and -GM/d for d>R.
published_hypotheses: H1: the force is exactly inverse-square (Newtonian gravity)
H2: the shell is exactly spherical with uniform surface density (spherical symmetry of the source)
H3: the attracted body lies wholly inside the cavity
H4: Newtonian statics, with forces adding by superposition (linear source) and no relativistic corrections
H5 (implicit): positive masses only; negative mass is not contemplated

newton-shell-theorem.lacked_data:
Newton lacked three things the tree relies on. None of them changes the conclusion as the tree uses it.

(1) General relativity. A constant-Phi metric is exactly flat (S4). By Birkhoff, the region inside a spherical shell is independent of the shell apart from a clock rescaling. A displaced core in GR is neither read nor computed here, and the owner marks it NOT-RUN.

(2) Negative mass. The theorem is about the shell's field, and m_core x 0 = 0 for either sign (S5).

(3) Precision tests of the inverse-square law. The theorem is exactly as strong as that law: S9 shows a Yukawa admixture breaks the interior null. The tests are named but not read, so no bound is quoted. Inside the tree's Newtonian-limit-of-GR framework the exponent is exactly 2.

Where the theorem reaches less far than an unqualified sentence in the tree, the cause is geometric scope, not missing data: crossing rays at 2.5e-5, and the non-compact core below 1e-8.

source.located: Classic content: Sachs, Proc. R. Soc. A 264, 309 (1961), the null optical scalars (Ricci term = trace, Weyl term = trace-free part of the optical tidal matrix), plus the vacuum Einstein equations R_ab = 0. No arXiv copy: NAMED-NOT-READ. Restatement used: Gao & Wald, gr-qc/0007021v2 (CQG 17, 4999, 2000). Its eq.(11) is the Jacobi-matrix equation d^2A/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta. Its eq.(12) is G = sqrt(det A). Its eq.(13) reads 'G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b] where sigma_ab denotes the shear of the congruence of null geodesics emanating from p'. This is the paper the tree itself cites (composite.py:112-114).

vacuum-ricci-flat-traceless-tidal.published_statement: Gao & Wald 2000 eq.(13), READ: G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b], where G = sqrt(det A) and A is the Jacobi matrix of eq.(11). The standard content (Sachs 1961, NAMED-NOT-READ; proved here as V1): take a screen {e1,e2} that is orthonormal and orthogonal to a null k and to an auxiliary null l with k.l = -1. The optical tidal matrix T_ij = R_{a m b n} e_i^a k^m e_j^b k^n then satisfies tr T = R_ab k^a k^b, and T = T_Weyl + (1/2) R_kk I with T_Weyl trace-free. The vacuum Einstein equations R_ab = 0 give tr T = 0, so all focusing comes from the Weyl part, which sources shear.
published_hypotheses: A 4D Lorentzian metric with the Levi-Civita connection. The identity tr T = R_kk follows from the Riemann symmetries alone (V1).
k is NULL (g(k,k) = 0), and the screen is orthonormal and orthogonal to k and l. With a non-null k the 2-D screen trace is not R_kk.
The vacuum Einstein equations R_ab = 0 with Lambda = 0, or Lambda-vacuum R_ab = Lambda g_ab. The second still gives R_kk = Lambda g(k,k) = 0 (V1h).
An EXACT solution of those equations. The conclusion is tr T = 0 exactly, not to some order.
Gao-Wald's Lemma 1 / Theorem 1 hypotheses (NEC, the null generic condition, completeness) govern their theorems, not eq.(13) and not this identity.

vacuum-ricci-flat-traceless-tidal.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested. The result is an algebraic identity plus the field equations and uses no measured datum. The identity is that the screen-projected Riemann tensor has trace R_kk and the Weyl part is trace-free (V1, proved over a basis). The one physical quantity that could have been missing in 1961 is the cosmological constant, measured since 1998 (Omega_Lambda = 0.6847 +- 0.0073, Planck 2018, READ from cache). It does not change the conclusion: R_ab = Lambda g_ab gives R_kk = Lambda g(k,k) = 0 for null k (V1h, symbolic). The sign of M does not change it either: exact Schwarzschild is Ricci-flat for either sign (V2a), so a negative-mass lens is exactly as much a vacuum as a positive one. The evidence therefore runs one way: no later datum moves the result. What moves is the tree's application, and that is a matter of approximation, not data. The linearised metric is not a vacuum at O(M^2). The tree names this but gets its size wrong: it claims four digits where a correct null screen gives about 0.9 %, and it calls the metric's own Ricci term an 'Euler leak'.
vacuum-ricci-flat-traceless-tidal.grade_evidence:
The external result STANDS. 'Vacuum (R_ab = 0, or R_ab = Lambda g_ab) implies R_kk = 0, so the optical tidal matrix is trace-free and pure Weyl' is proved here for every 4D curvature tensor and every null k with an orthonormal screen (V1: exact rational arithmetic over a 20-element basis, vacuity guard passing; V1h covers Lambda). It is confirmed on exact Schwarzschild with symbolic M of either sign (V2: T = diag(+-3ML^2/r^5), trace identically 0), and it agrees with Gao-Wald eq.(13), read from cache. No datum enters: V1h shows the measured value of Lambda cannot move it.

Five discrepancies are recorded on the tree's side. None refutes the result, and none is attributed to the source.
(1) The tree applies the result to a linearised metric that is Ricci-flat only at O(M). The tree names this (composite.py:102-104, 326-327). On a correct null screen that metric's trace is 8.69e-3 of the maximum component at the static point, not 'four digits' (composite.py:43-44).
(2) The quoted 1.6e-4 comes from a non-null k = (1,1,0,0), with g(k,k) = -4 Phi, plus finite-difference error. It varies with h by a factor of 29, which contradicts 'h-independent' (composite.py:326).
(3) The along-ray 'Euler leak' (composite.py:328-333) does not depend on step count and is linear in |M|. It is the O(M^2) Ricci term, and it reaches about 4.4-17.8 % at the window's upper rows, |M| = 1e-2 to 4e-2.
(4) 'T_kk = 0 along the whole path' (composite.py:90-92) is true of the exact vacuum completion but not of the metric actually integrated. That metric's O(M^2) R_kk has an ANEC-type integral of -pi M^2/(4b^3) < 0, which is small: 6.5e-4 of the Weyl power at |M| = 2e-3.
(5) composite.tidal has the opposite sign to the MTW tidal matrix, which swaps which screen direction focuses. It leaves every conjugate parameter unchanged (55.17 and 56.50 under both signs, against geodesic-bundle values of 55.23 and 56.63), precisely because T is traceless.

The claims resting on it hold. 'Ricci focusing is OFF here' (composite.py:334) holds at O(M), and to 6.5e-4 in integrated effect at |M| = 2e-3. 'Weyl focusing is sign-blind' (specthm.py:1326) holds for both the existence and the location of the conjugate point (V5c).
