gr-qc/9304008-qualitative-conclusion.published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We find in all cases studied that the energy density fluctuations are large whenever the local energy density is negative. This is taken to mean that the gravitational field of a system with negative energy density, such as the Casimir vacuum, is not described by a fixed classical metric but is undergoing large metric fluctuations.' Sec. III.B (p.9): 'Our primary concern is whether or not Delta << 1, which is best determined by numerical evaluation of Delta using Eqs. (3.2), (3.18), and (3.19). The figures illustrate the results. For states which are sufficiently close to coherent states, i.e. r << |alpha|, we do indeed find that Delta << 1. However, as the magnitude of the squeeze parameter r increases relative to that of |alpha|, we find that Delta increases. By the point that the state is sufficiently squeezed to have rho = <:T00:> < 0, we always have that Delta is at least of order unity. Thus squeezed states for which the energy density is negative exhibit large energy density fluctuations.' Fig. 2 caption: '...gamma = delta = 0 and theta = pi/2... Delta << 1 only when s >> r, the region of classical behavior. Otherwise, Delta ~ 1.' Sec. III.A (p.6): 'cos(2theta) > sqrt2 eps. In this case we have Delta(x) > 1.' Sec. III.C (p.12): 'Delta' >= 1/2, Delta >= 1/3 ... the dimensionless Casimir energy density fluctuations are always at least of order unity.' Sec. V (p.16): 'states of a quantized field in which the mean energy density is negative seem to exhibit large energy density fluctuations. This was illustrated in our model calculations for squeezed states and for the Casimir vacuum state.'
published_hypotheses: H1: a massless, minimally coupled scalar field in FLAT spacetime, in a box of side L with periodic boundary conditions (2.1)-(2.6).

H2: the measure is KF (3.2), Delta(x) = |(<:T00^2:> - <:T00:>^2)/<:T00^2:>|. It is taken in the coincidence limit, for the 00 component, with every operator normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, the quartic one included. It is a POINTWISE measure.

H3: the 'cases studied' are four. (i) The vacuum+2 superposition (2.15). (ii) The squeezed COHERENT family D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> of (3.9)-(3.19). (iii) The squeezed vacuum, which is the alpha=0 limit (3.22)-(3.23). (iv) The Casimir vacuum with periodic z (3.24)-(3.45).

H4: for case (ii) the conclusion comes from NUMERICAL evaluation of (3.2) using KF's printed (3.18) and (3.19), on plotted slices. Figs. 1-2 use gamma=delta=0, theta=pi/2 over (r,s). Figs. 3-4 use delta=0, s=1/2, theta=pi/2 over (r,gamma). It is not a proof over the whole family.
H5: 'large' and 'at least of order unity' are not given a threshold. The abstract's 'in all cases studied ... whenever' is universal, while Sec. V's 'seem to exhibit' is hedged.
H6: for case (i) the inequality is drawn from (3.8). For case (iv) it is drawn from (3.43)-(3.45), under the Wick condition and a diagonal <:d_A phi d_B phi:>.

gr-qc/9304008-qualitative-conclusion.lacked_data: KF lacked no physical data: no measured constant enters the result, since K_00 cancels. For case (ii) what they lacked was the correct quartic moment. They evaluated Delta numerically from their printed (3.19), which is not exact (C2). With the exact moment the universal conclusion MOVES: on the surface t=2 (the curve s^2=(1-e^{-2r})/8 on KF's own Fig.1/2 slice), Delta = 0 exactly while rho<0 (C3-C4). There is also a thin band around it, t in (1.978, 2.029), where Delta<0.1. The evidence the other way was computed just as carefully. The conclusion is untouched for vac+2 (1/3<Delta<1), the squeezed vacuum (2/3), Casimir (6/7) and every zero-mean Gaussian state (the tree's T1). In case (ii) the band is thin and sits next to a region where <:T00^2:> < 0 and Delta > 1. That the figures were drawn from the printed (3.19) is consistent with C5 and the Fig. 2 caption, but it is inference, since the figures were not viewed. M's hypothesis is confirmed for this result in a non-empirical form: the missing piece was a computation, not a datum. It overturns the universal conclusion but not the generic one.

2604.05980-nonradial-instability.published_statement: Abstract: 'We establish the dynamical instability of a static, spherically symmetric, and infinitesimally thin shell in general relativity. The shell is made up of a perfect fluid with a barotropic equation of state, and it produces a Schwarzschild spacetime in its exterior and a Minkowski spacetime in its interior. ... We reveal the existence of two modes with a purely imaginary frequency, one negative ..., the other positive (which describes an exponential growth); these modes occur for all sampled values of the shell's compactness and adiabatic index, and all sampled values of the multipolar order l >= 2, in the even-parity sector of the perturbation. ... we show that a Newtonian shell also is necessarily unstable to a time-dependent perturbation. Our conclusion suggests that a compact object that features a thin shell at its surface will be dynamically unstable.' Sec I D (p.4): 'An unstable mode exists also for l = 3 ... and for all other values of l that we could sample in our numerical exploration.' Sec VII A (p.23): l = 4 also computed. Fig. 1 (p.3), l = 2 only: Im{omega (R^3/M)^{1/2}} against M/R in [0, 0.30] at Gamma = 2 (axis 0.52-0.66), and against Gamma in [1.8, 2.4] at M/R = 0.2 (axis 0.56-0.64). Sec X H (p.41): 'The dynamical instability for any multipole order l takes its origin in the existence of a normal mode of vibration with a negative eigenvalue'; for l = 0, lambda = Gamma - 3/2; for l = 1, lambda_+ = (3 Gamma - 4)/2 and lambda_- = 0, the translation.
published_hypotheses: H1 infinitesimally thin shell: a timelike hypersurface with Israel junction conditions (Sec I B, Sec II Eqs 2.10)
H2 perfect fluid, S_ab = mu u_a u_b + p(h_ab + u_a u_b): isotropic surface stress, with no shear modulus and no bending rigidity (Eq 2.2)

H3 barotropic and isentropic EOS, mu = sigma + eps(sigma), p = p(sigma); the relativistic computation uses a polytrope p = K sigma^Gamma with constant Gamma (Eqs 1.1, 2.4-2.7). Gamma is d ln p/d ln sigma in the rest-mass density
H4 vacuum on both sides: 'We assume that there is no matter inside and outside the shell' (Sec II)
H5 Minkowski interior (M_in = 0) and Schwarzschild exterior. Interior-independence is stated as 'our belief' (p.2), and Pani et al. [21] found no unstable mode with a de Sitter interior

H6 static spherically symmetric background on the equilibrium sequence (3.13); linear perturbations; Regge-Wheeler gauge; outgoing-wave boundary conditions in outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates
H7 numerical sampling in full GR: l = 2, 3, 4; M/R in [0, 0.3] at Gamma = 2 and Gamma in [1.8, 2.4] at M/R = 0.2 (l = 2, Fig 1). The result is 'for all SAMPLED values', not a proof over all values
H8 Newtonian analogue (Sec X): the same thin barotropic fluid shell. This is the analytic 'necessarily unstable' statement

2604.05980-nonradial-instability.lacked_data: PSP's conclusion rests on no measured datum. It is a linear-stability computation within a stated model, so no later measurement can move it. What they lacked was coverage: in GR they sampled l = 2-4, M/R <= 0.3 and Gamma in [1.8, 2.4]. Evidence FOR: the Newtonian derivation here, which reproduces four printed formulas exactly, closes that gap in the Newtonian limit. A growing mode exists for every Gamma > 0 and every l >= 2 (z3 unsat), and it grows faster with l, so more coverage strengthens the instability. Evidence AGAINST the tree's extension: the model has no shear or bending rigidity, no finite thickness, no collisionless (Vlasov) or anisotropic matter, and no non-vacuum surroundings. PSP do not claim these, the tree's own matter models fall there, and Le 2606.22531v4 says so. Pani et al.'s de Sitter-interior null result is an unresolved counter-indication for interior-independence. Net: no datum moves PSP's statement; the tree's use needs hypotheses PSP do not supply.

An independent Newtonian derivation reproduces Eqs (10.52b), (10.54) and (10.57) and the l = 0 eigenvalue exactly, and proves (z3 unsat) the Newtonian instability for all Gamma > 0 and l >= 2. (2) The tree's use is broader than the source in four named ways: (a) 'all compactness, all Gamma' where the source has 'all sampled' (GR: M/R <= 0.3, Gamma in [1.8, 2.4]), stability.py:81-83 and obstruct.py:120-121; (b) M_in >= 0 where the source computes M_in = 0 and calls interior-independence a contested belief, stability.py:83-84; (c) the barotropic perfect-fluid hypothesis is dropped in 'not escapable while self-gravitating', wall.py:186-187 and obstruct.py:119-127, although the tree's own matter models are outside it (Le 2606.22531v4 restates PSP with exactly this restriction); (d) 'beta^2 does not appear in the unstable branch at all' (wall.py:128, 455-456) holds for the mode's existence but not its rate, since kappa_2 falls from 0.627 to 0.346 as Gamma goes from 1.5 to infinity. finite-nuclear-size-shift.published_statement: CODATA 2022 eq (50), verbatim: 'The first and lowest-order contribution is E(4)_nucl = (2/3) m_e c^2 (Z alpha)^4/n^3 (m_r/m_e)^3 (r_N/lambda_C)^2 delta_l0 (50) and is solely due to the finite rms charge radius r_N of nucleus N. Here, lambda_C = hbar/m_e c is the reduced Compton wavelength of the electron.' Using E_h = alpha^2 m_e c^2 = 2 R_inf hc (eq 26) and lambda_C = alpha a_0, this equals (4/3) Z^4 (m_r/m_e)^3 (r_N/a_0)^2/n^3 R_inf hc exactly. The higher orders are separate terms of the series in eq (49): the alpha^5 Friar term in eq (51), with r_pF = 1.947(75) fm, and the alpha^6 term in eq (56), which includes a delta_kappa1 piece that shifts P1/2 states.
published_hypotheses: r_N is the rms charge radius. No shape model is used: at this order the shift depends only on <r^2>.
Leading order in alpha: this is the E(4) term of the series in eq (49). The alpha^5 term (eq 51) and alpha^6 term (eq 56) are separate.
delta_l0: at this order only S states are shifted. P1/2 is shifted at order (Z alpha)^6 (eq 56).
Finite nuclear mass enters through the factor (m_r/m_e)^3.
Hydrogenlike atom with nuclear charge Z.

schwarzschild-isotropic-vacuum.published_statement: Schwarzschild 1916 eq.(14): ds^2 = (1-alpha/R)dt^2 - dR^2/(1-alpha/R) - R^2(dtheta^2+sin^2 theta dphi^2), with R = (r^3+alpha^3)^(1/3). He calls it 'the exact solution of Einstein's problem', where alpha depends on the mass, and states it is unique under his conditions (sec.5). Isotropic restatement (Poplawski 0902.1994 eq.1, credited to Weyl 1917): 'The interval of the static, spherically symmetric, gravitational field in vacuum, expressed in isotropic coordinates': ds^2 = (1-rg/4r)^2/(1+rg/4r)^2 c^2dt^2 - (1+rg/4r)^4(dr^2+r^2 dOmega^2), with rg = 2GM/c^2. The substitution r_S = r(1+rg/4r)^2 brings it to the standard form. This is identical to certify.py's A = ((1-u)/(1+u))^2, B = (1+u)^4, u = M/2r, since rg/4 = M/2.
published_hypotheses: Schwarzschild 1916: field equations (eq.4), i.e. vacuum R_mn = 0 everywhere except the origin
Schwarzschild 1916: determinant condition |g| = -1 (eq.5). This is Einstein's 1915 unimodular coordinate condition, a gauge choice
Schwarzschild 1916 condition 1: all components independent of time (static)
Schwarzschild 1916 condition 2: g_rho4 = 0 exactly (no time-space cross terms)
Schwarzschild 1916 condition 3: spherical symmetry (invariance under rotations)
Schwarzschild 1916 condition 4: asymptotic flatness, g -> diag(-1,-1,-1,+1) at infinity
Schwarzschild 1916 sec.3 item 4: continuity except at the origin (this fixes rho = alpha^3)

Isotropic chart (Poplawski 0902.1994): valid for r != rg/4 = M/2, where det g = 0 (the common horizon). The region r < M/2 is the image r -> rg^2/16r of a second exterior sheet (Einstein-Rosen bridge). If the full r in (0,inf) sheet is treated as one solution, Guendelman et al. (restated in 0902.1994 sec.IV, eq.25) find a delta-function source at r = M/2

qnec-bousso-fisher-leichenauer-wall-bala.published_statement: BFKLW 1509.02542 abstract: 'Our proof applies to free and superrenormalizable bosonic field theories, and to any points that lie on stationary null surfaces. An example is Minkowski space, where any point p and null vector k^a define a null plane N (a Rindler horizon) ... The QNEC states that <T_kk(p)> >= (hbar/2pi) lim_{A->0} S''_out/A.' Formal version, eq (2.2): <T_kk(p)> >= hbar/(2pi sqrt h(p)) delta^2 S_out/delta lambda(p)^2. This is the diagonal coefficient after the delta-function is factored out (eq 2.1), 'if the expansion and the shear of k^a(y) vanish at p'. p.2: 'the right hand side can have any sign ... By integrating the QNEC along a null generator, we can obtain the ANEC, in situations where the boundary term S'_out vanishes at early and late times.' p.4: 'fixed background spacetimes with no dynamical gravity'. BFKW 1706.09432 eq (1.3): Q_- = INT dx^- <T_--> - (1/2pi) dS(B)/dx^- + (1/2pi) dS(A)/dx^- >= 0, in flat metric (2.1), for locally stationary cuts; 'we worked exclusively in flat space' (p.65). CF 1812.04683: 'relativistic QFT in d-dimensional Minkowski space with d >= 2 and with cuts along a Rindler horizon'. It is a theorem for half-sided modular inclusions, 'with the additional assumption that the input state has finite averaged null energy'. The QNEC takes the form of convexity of relative entropy in the cut position (eq 3.19).
published_hypotheses: BFKLW: free or superrenormalizable bosonic fields, massive or massless. Fermions are 'expected', not proved. D > 2 directly; D = 2 by dimensional reduction. Interacting marginal and nonrenormalizable theories are left open (p.26).

BFKLW: the point p lies on a stationary null hypersurface: Minkowski Rindler horizons, de Sitter or Poincare horizons, or the horizon of an eternal Schwarzschild/Kerr black hole only. The background is fixed, with no dynamical gravity.

All three proofs: the surface is deformed along null generators by affine parameter, and the expansion and shear vanish at p. BFKW adds that the extrinsic curvature K^+ and enough of its y-derivatives vanish at the point.
S''_out is the diagonal (delta-function) coefficient of the second functional derivative per unit transverse area (BFKLW eqs 2.1-2.3).
<T_kk> is a quantum expectation value in a state of the QFT. Hollands-Longo prove it on a dense set of vector states; 'all vector states remains an open problem'.

BFKW: flat space, a QFT with an interacting UV fixed point, and a lightcone-limit / defect-OPE / modular-analyticity argument that the authors call a 'proof strategy'. QNEC implies ANEC only when the boundary term [S'_out] vanishes at early and late times (BFKLW p.2), along a complete generator of the stationary null surface.

qnec-bousso-fisher-leichenauer-wall-bala.lacked_data: No empirical datum enters the QNEC. It is a QFT theorem whose only constant, hbar/2pi, is exact, so no later measurement can move it, and none has. What the 2015-2019 authors lacked was proof coverage, not data. BFKLW covered free/superrenormalizable bosons on stationary null surfaces. BFKW gave a flat-space strategy for interacting QFTs. CF made the argument rigorous for Minkowski Rindler cuts with finite ANE. Hollands-Longo (2025) still record 'all vector states' as open. No proof read covers curved, non-stationary null surfaces. That is a limit on the theorem's scope, not an error in it: four independent proofs and no counterexample to the stress-tensor QNEC in its class support it where it is stated, and more data would not change that. What changes is the tree's use. On a curved warp background with a classical T and an asserted boundary term, the QNEC reduces to the NEC, which already fails pointwise. The step 'integrates to ANEC, ANEC fails, so the configuration is forbidden' rests on conditions the source states as conditions. The evidence cuts the other way too: the tree's conclusion is not shown false. Its on-axis affine ANEC is negative (-0.0524), and the achronal-ANEC route would forbid the configuration if its hypotheses held. That route is conjectural (Graham-Olum) or conditional (Wall: GSL plus an NEC background), and achronality is unchecked.
qnec-bousso-fisher-leichenauer-wall-bala.grade_evidence: The published QNEC stands as stated. Four proofs were read (1509.02542, 1706.09432, 1812.04683, with 2503.04651 confirming), no counterexample to the stress-tensor QNEC in its class was found, and the exact coefficient hbar/2pi agrees. The tree uses the QNEC on a strictly larger class than any proof covers, and drops four hypotheses that the sources state. (i) Background: the proofs need a fixed background with a stationary null surface, or flat space; the tree uses the curved warp metric. (ii) State: the proofs need a quantum state; the tree supplies a classical T, where hbar -> 0 turns the QNEC into the NEC (Q3). (iii) Boundary term: [S'] = 0 is the source's own condition, and the tree asserts it without computing it. z3 gives UNSAT with the condition and SAT without it, and sympy gives a counterexample profile with INT T_kk = -a hbar/pi. (iv) Parametrisation: the proofs use affine generators; the tree uses a non-affine k and non-geodesic off-axis curves (Gamma^y_kk = F_y != 0), although the on-axis sign survives at -0.0524 affine. The ANEC that the QNEC integrates to is the flat-space one, and in curved space ANEC fails on chronal geodesics (Wall 0910.5751). No computed contradiction refutes the tree's conclusion, so the grade is not WRONG. No datum moved, so it is not DATA-DEPENDENT. Result: NARROWED. A separate citation discrepancy (not a refutation): anec.py:53 credits the conjecture paper's author list; the proof paper adds Koeller.
qnec-bousso-fisher-leichenauer-wall-bala.what_would_change_the_grade: Toward STANDS for the tree's use, any one of: (a) a proof of the QNEC, or of the achronal ANEC, on null surfaces of a curved, non-stationary warp-type background for semiclassically self-consistent states; (b) a proof that the on-axis ray is a null line of the moving-bubble spacetime, plus a curved-space ANEC theorem whose hypotheses that spacetime meets; (c) an explicit quantum state with S_out computed and [S'] shown to vanish. Toward WRONG for the tree's conclusion: an explicit semiclassical state on a warp background with negative achronal ANEC. For the theorem itself: a counterexample to the stress-tensor QNEC within its stated class. None is known; BFKW fn 23 concerns only the higher-spin version.

source.located: arXiv:1801.08358v2 [gr-qc], 7 Feb 2018, L. Herrera (Salamanca), 'New definition of complexity for self-gravitating fluid distributions: The spherically symmetric, static case'. Journal ref Phys. Rev. D 97, 044010 (2018), as cited in ref [1] of Abbas & Nazar arXiv:1806.05042. Eq. (10) is on p.3, Sec. II.A.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(paper='1801.08358') returned pp.1-10, the whole paper including references, as the PDF text layer. Eqs (1)-(13), (19)-(22) and (31)-(33) were read there. 1801.08358-eq10.published_statement: p.3: 'Alternatively, using nu' = 2 (m + 4 pi P_r r^3)/(r (r - 2m)), (10) which follows from the field equations, we may write P_r' = -(m + 4 pi P_r r^3)/(r(r - 2m)) (mu + P_r) + 2(P_perp - P_r)/r, (11) where m is the mass function defined by: R^3_232 = 1 - e^{-lambda} = 2m/r, (12) or, equivalently as m = 4 pi INT_0^r r~^2 mu dr~. (13)'. Context: 'The metric (1) has to satisfy Einstein field equations G^nu_mu = 8 pi T^nu_mu, (2)'. Eq. (10) is solved from eq. (7), P_r = -(1/8 pi)[1/r^2 - e^{-lambda}(1/r^2 + nu'/r)].
published_hypotheses: Static: nu(r) and lambda(r) depend on r only, and the fluid is at rest, u^mu = (e^{-nu/2},0,0,0) (eqs 1, 14)
Spherically symmetric, in Schwarzschild-like (areal) coordinates: ds^2 = e^nu dt^2 - e^lambda dr^2 - r^2 dOmega^2, signature (+,-,-,-) (eq 1)
Locally anisotropic fluid: T^0_0 = mu, T^1_1 = -P_r, T^2_2 = T^3_3 = -P_perp (eqs 3-5), given physical meaning through Bondi's local Minkowski frame
General relativity with NO cosmological constant: G^nu_mu = 8 pi T^nu_mu (eq 2). G = c = 1 is implicit in the 8 pi
m is defined geometrically by e^{-lambda} = 1 - 2m/r (eq 12). Eq (13), m = 4 pi INT mu, is called 'equivalent', which presumes m(0) = 0 (a regular centre); eq (10) does not use it
Implicit and never stated: r != 0 and r != 2m (both are divided by), and 1 - 2m/r > 0 so that lambda is real and metric (1) is Lorentzian
The distribution is bounded by Sigma and matched to Schwarzschild (eqs 19-22). This is a global hypothesis of the paper and the local eq (10) does not use it

1801.08358-eq10.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result: eq (10) has NO measured input. It follows algebraically from one component of G^mu_nu = 8 pi T^mu_nu for the static spherical metric, together with the definition e^{-lambda} = 1 - 2m/r. It was re-derived here from scratch in both sign conventions (residual 0) and checked numerically on an exact interior solution. No datum the author might have lacked could change it, and newer data cannot move a closed-form identity. What CAN move the conclusion is the theory, not data. (i) A nonzero cosmological constant (measured since 1998, so known in 2018 and excluded by the choice of eq (2)) adds -Lambda r^3/2 and makes THEOREM X's Phi' = 0 branch non-empty (m = Lambda r^3/4, computed). (ii) Modified gravity adds curvature source terms (f(R): 1806.05042 eq 15, READ). Neither is a flaw in Herrera's GR statement. Both mean the tree's I7/I8/THEOREM X conclusions are statements about GR with Lambda = 0, which is what the tree says it uses. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the from-scratch computation (re-derivations A, B, D). Evidence for it: none found; the later literature checked surfaced no erratum or contradiction.
1801.08358-eq10.grade_evidence: The statement was READ verbatim at arXiv:1801.08358v2 p.3 and matches the tree's quote (tolman.py:94-95, 2511-2513). It was re-derived from scratch with sympy in Herrera's (+,-,-,-) conventions and in the tree's (-,+,+,+) conventions, residual 0 in both, together with eqs (6)-(9), (11)-(13) and (32)-(33). A numeric check on the constant-density Schwarzschild interior agrees to 3e-10. The tree's hypotheses match the source's. The added r - 2m > 0 is implicit in the source and is shown not to carry the result, and the fluid hypothesis is shown unnecessary: eq (10) needs only T^r_r. The tree's use (Phi' = 0 plus the identity forces m = p_r = 0, i.e. I7/I8) was re-checked independently by sympy and by z3 with vacuity guards. No datum enters. Two notes do not change the grade. (1) Lambda = 0 is carried by both source and tree but not named in tolman.py's hypothesis ledger, and it is load-bearing for I7/I8 (computed). (2) V18/V18a use the undivided relation at r = 2m, outside the source's chart; this is a valid limit and not a rests_on_it site.
1801.08358-eq10.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED, if a rests_on_it site (THEOREM X, I7/I8, X1-X3, W4, D9, specthm:R2) were shown to apply eq (10) with Lambda != 0, in a modified-gravity setting, or at r <= 2m in the divided form. WRONG, only on a computed counterexample to eq (10) under its own hypotheses; none exists, since re-derivation A is an identity. OPEN, only if the source became unreadable. A misprint in a later version of the paper would be a discrepancy, not a refutation.

magnetar-surface-field.name: Magnetar surface field ~1e11 T (inferred), used by tolman.py as the best in-hypothesis (traceless, electromagnetic) tension known, B^2/(2 mu0) = 3.9789e27 Pa, and as the denominator of the shortfall 2.4573e13

source.located: No source is cited at the owner site (tolman.py:1592-1593 says only 'magnetar surface field 1e11 T ... DERIVED from an inferred B'). The standard sources for the value were READ at source. (a) Olausen & Kaspi, 'The McGill Magnetar Catalog', ApJS 212, 6 (2014), arXiv:1309.4167. p.2 gives B = 3.2e19 (P Pdot)^(1/2) G for the 'surface dipolar magnetic field strength', with I = 1e45 g cm^2, and the caveat that it 'assumes simple vacuum dipole radiation and ignores the potentially important torques due to magnetospheric variability and the internal superfluid'. Table 2 (p.18): SGR 1806-20 has P = 7.547728 s, Pdot ~ 49.5e-11 and B = 20e14 G, the catalogue maximum. (b) Kouveliotou et al. 1998, astro-ph/9809140. p.9 restates Kouveliotou et al. 1998a (Nature 393, 235; SGR 1806-20, Pdot = 8.3e-11, B = 8e14 G). p.10 says the P-Pdot estimate is an overestimate once a particle wind acts, so for SGR 1806-20 B drops to 2e14 G. The Nature paper 1998a itself was NAMED-NOT-READ and is read here only through the authors' own restatement in (b). (c) Tiengo et al. 2013, arXiv:1308.4987. It measures the field without using spin-down: a proton-cyclotron line gives a local field of 2e14 to >1e15 G, with R_NS = 12 km and a model loop B_max = 7.41e15 G.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1309.4167, astro-ph/9809140 and 1308.4987; page text was returned and quoted. Comparison papers 0907.1396, 2304.03430 and 2405.15484 were also read at source. Kouveliotou 1998a (Nature) and Duncan & Thompson 1992 were not read directly, only through the restatements above.

magnetar-surface-field.published_statement: Olausen & Kaspi 2014 (arXiv:1309.4167 p.2): 'the surface dipolar magnetic field strength B, defined as B = 3.2 x 10^19 (P Pdot)^(1/2) G ... Note that the expression for B assumes simple vacuum dipole radiation and ignores the potentially important torques due to magnetospheric variability and the internal superfluid.' Table 2: the largest B is 20 x 10^14 G (SGR 1806-20). Kouveliotou et al. 1998 (astro-ph/9809140 p.9-10): SGR 1806-20 '(dipolar) magnetic field strength ... 8 x 10^14 G'; 'the simple estimate of the magnetic field derived above from P and Pdot is an overestimate ... for that source the required value of B* is reduced to 2 x 10^14 G.'
published_hypotheses: H1: spin-down comes from magnetic dipole radiation in a VACUUM.
H2: orthogonal rotator (alpha = 90 deg). This is implicit in the 3.2e19 coefficient.
H3: moment of inertia I = 1e45 g cm^2.
H4: neutron-star radius R = 10 km. This is implicit in the coefficient.
H5: B is the EQUATORIAL surface dipole field; the polar field is twice as large.
H6: no other torque acts (magnetospheric twist, superfluid, particle wind). Kouveliotou says a wind makes the estimate an OVERESTIMATE.
H7: Pdot is taken over a stated range. For SGR 1806-20 it is a long-term average, because Pdot varies strongly.
H8: only the large-scale DIPOLE is measured. Multipolar and internal fields are not seen by P and Pdot.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, and load-bearing. tolman.py:59-61, 805-808 and 3080 call the magnetar rung 'the best in-hypothesis tension known'. No source read here says a magnetar field is the strongest EM field or tension known. The superlative holds only for an unnamed class: macroscopic, quasi-static fields. Skokov et al. 2009 (0907.1396 p.4) put heavy-ion collision fields 'about 4 orders of magnitude' above a magnetar surface field; those fields are calculated with UrQMD and last about 0.1 fm/c. STAR 2024 (2304.03430) quotes '~1e18 Gauss' and 'the highest strength ever achieved on earth'. It observes the field's effect at 5.2-14.3 sigma, but the magnitude itself is still model-calculated. The tree's own ladder also admits femtoscale rungs: the 'largest tensions nature is known to sustain' at tolman.py:801-803, and the nucleon core pressure ~1e35 Pa at tolman.py:1590. By that same standard, the static Coulomb field at the surface of a Pb-208 nucleus counts. It is traceless because it is electromagnetic, and it gives eps0 E^2/2 = 2.43e31 Pa, 6.1e3 times the magnetar rung.

WEAKENED (hypotheses compressed). The owner site says only 'spin-down dipole inference' / 'DERIVED from an inferred B'. That status word is honest, but H1-H6 are not named. Each one moves B: a force-free magnetosphere gives x0.577 to x0.816; the polar field gives x2; R = 12 km gives x0.579; a particle wind brings SGR 1806-20 down to 2e14 G.

VALUE CHOICE, not stated. tolman.py:1592 uses a round 1e11 T. The catalogue maximum is 1.956e11 T, recomputed here. Using the round value makes the quoted shortfall 3.8x LARGER than the catalogue maximum would (2.457e13 against 6.42e12). That overstates the case for the refusal, i.e. against M. It is recorded as a discrepancy, not as an error.

No drop in the physics of the rung. sympy confirms that B^2/(2 mu0) is exactly the Maxwell tension along the field lines, and that the EM trace is exactly 0. So the rung does sit inside tolman's traceless hypothesis, as the tree says.

magnetar-surface-field.what_would_change_the_grade: To reach STANDS, the tree would need to say 'best MACROSCOPIC, quasi-static' tension and name the vacuum / orthogonal / I / R / equatorial hypotheses at tolman.py:59-61, 805-808, 1592-1593 and 3080. The grade becomes DATA-DEPENDENT if the ladder is read to count transient femtoscale EM fields; the denominator would then move by 1e6-1e9 with a model-calculated heavy-ion datum. It becomes WRONG only if magnetar surface fields are shown not to be ~1e10-1e11 T for the population (for example, fallback-disk spin-down established; Olausen-Kaspi call the evidence for that 'weak'). No such demonstration was found.

Each m_H input is a fit to the peak position with the signal normalisations left free. ATLAS treats gamma-gamma interference as a systematic and applies no shift; modelling the SM interference would add 15 MeV. CMS assumes the natural width is much smaller than the m4l resolution.

Gamma_H, PDG p.8 verbatim: 'the total Higgs width cannot be measured indirectly without additional assumptions ... Constraints ... from the combination of on-peak and off-peak contributions in Higgs decays to ZZ* rely on the assumption of equal on- and off-shell effective couplings.'

Having the datum changes no conclusion. Every m_h figure scales by at most 1.1e-3, and theorems D15, D16, D18 and D19 do not contain the numerical value. The S = 1.5 tension is also carried by the average; resolving it would move m_h about another 0.5 sigma, again with no verdict moving. (2) Gamma_h: here the missing datum is built into the method rather than waiting on a later measurement. The LHC cannot measure the total width without assuming equal on- and off-shell couplings (PDG p.8), and a width that does not depend on the model needs an e+e- Higgs factory. If the assumption is relaxed, the bound weakens by up to about x2 (2603.05020). The value also moved between editions, from 3.7 to 3.0 MeV. The tree's order-of-magnitude statements survive every band tested. Its single printed digits ('5e-16' and '2e-22') sit inside the datum's own 68% band, and the ceiling would have printed '4e-16' at the edition the tree used to pin. This is precision beyond what the datum supports, not an error in the source and not a refutation of the tree.

yukawa-green-function.published_statement: Ishii-Tanaka 2412.19539 define the Green function k(x;d) as the solution of d Delta k - k + delta = 0 on R^n, for d > 0. Eq (3.1) gives k = d^{-n/2} G(|x|/sqrt d) with G = (2pi)^{-n/2} |x|^{1-n/2} K_{n/2-1}(|x|). Lemma 3.1 states: k_m is continuous on R^n minus the origin and in L^1, with F[k_m] = 1/(1+d_m|xi|^2); k_m(x) > 0 for x != 0; and ||k_m||_1 = 1. Setting d = 1/m^2 gives k = m^2 G_m with (-Delta + m^2) G_m = delta, so INT G_m = 1/m^2, and at n = 3, G = e^{-mr}/(4 pi r). Brax-Burrage 2101.10693 p.14-15: outside a static source the perturbation is a decaying exponential over r; inside it is A sinh(sqrt(y+) r)/(sqrt(y+) r) - C/y+ with C = rho/v, which is the algebraic -J/m^2 term. They impose that 'the perturbations to the fields should decay to zero as r -> infinity and that the fields should be regular at r = 0'.
published_hypotheses: The whole space R^n with the flat (Euclidean) Laplacian (Ishii-Tanaka p.2; Brax-Burrage eq 54). In Zamperlini-Barros eq 3, curvature adds corrections.
d > 0, i.e. m^2 > 0. In Brax-Burrage every vacuum mass eigenvalue is positive and far from a vanishing eigenmass (p.3, p.14).

The Green function is the one selected by integrability or decay at infinity: k in L^1 (Ishii-Tanaka Lemma 3.1(i)); perturbations decay to zero as r -> infinity and are regular at r = 0 (Brax-Burrage p.15).
The source is a distributional delta; convolution is taken with f in L^q, using Young's inequality (Ishii-Tanaka Cor. 2.2).
Linear regime: fields are small perturbations and the density is not too high (Brax-Burrage p.14, eq 40).
Static source (Brax-Burrage Sec III A).
The kernel is positive, k > 0 for x != 0 (Ishii-Tanaka Lemma 3.1(ii)). The source proves this; any sup-norm bound uses it as a premise.

1208.5399-w22-remark.published_statement: 1208.5399 p.10: 'In the m = 0 case, the bound simplifies, and actually gives a bound valid for all m >= 0: INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT_{-oo}^{oo} |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' ... 'The bound requires a certain degree of smoothness in g. In four-dimensions, it remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R), i.e., g, g' and g'' are required to exist (in the distributional sense) and be square-integrable.' p.11: 'But the bound does not apply to g with lower regularity, in particular, to discontinuous g. By sharp switching, one can trap arbitrarily large negative energy densities.' Bound (1), of which (3) is the weakening that holds for every m, is stated 'for any smooth compactly supported g, and all Hadamard states w' (p.10). The lecture notes assert the remark and do not prove it. Its rigorous backing is Fewster-Teo gr-qc/9908073 Thm 3.2: the form domain is W^{2,2}_0(I) and C0^oo(I) is a form core. Their footnote 7 says that extending by zero maps W^{m,2}_0(I) into W^{m,2}(R) as a continuous isometry.
published_hypotheses: Free real scalar (Klein-Gordon) field, mass m >= 0, minimal coupling (pp. 10, 27).
4-dimensional Minkowski spacetime ('In four-dimensions', p.10), inertial worldline (t,x) (p.27).

g is real-valued, as written g(t)^2 in (3). The derivation on pp. 24-25 is for real g; complex g is handled by taking real and imaginary parts separately.
The base statement takes g smooth and compactly supported (p.10 for (1); Theorem 2.4 on p.25 has g in C0^oo(R)). The remark extends this to g in W^{2,2}(R) and prints NO condition on the support.
The bound is not optimal (p.10).

later_literature.what: Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 3.1 cover every energy density rho in their class W_m, which includes every smooth bounded Hadamard energy density. For such rho the QI form sum on an interval I has form domain W^{m,2}_0(I), with C0^oo(I) a form core. So a QI checked on C0^oo(I) is equivalent to positivity on all of W^{2,2}_0(I) (m = 2, the 4D case). Footnote 7: extending by zero maps W^{m,2}_0(I) into W^{m,2}(R) as a continuous isometry. This is the rigorous version of the remark for compactly supported g. Footnote 11 notes that the square root of Ford-Roman's delta-pulse sampling function is not in W^{2,2}(R), so it is not a legitimate sampler: the regularity threshold matters in the literature as well.

hoelder-inequality.name: Hoelder inequality (L^inf x L^1); autocorrelation maximum h(0) = ||f||_2^2

source.located: Classical: L.J. Rogers 1888 and O. Hoelder, 'Ueber einen Mittelwertsatz', Nachr. Akad. Wiss. Goettingen (1889) 38-47; neither is on arXiv. Exact modern restatement: N. Albuquerque, G. Araujo, D. Pellegrino, J.B. Seoane-Sepulveda, 'Hoelder's inequality: some recent and unexpected applications', arXiv:1412.2017v3 [math.FA] (2015), Theorem 1.1, p.2 (history p.1-2, citing Maligranda, 'Why Hoelder's inequality should be called Rogers' inequality', Math. Inequal. Appl. 1 (1998) 69-83). The autocorrelation half has no separate classical source: it is Hoelder at p = q = 2 (Cauchy-Schwarz, same Theorem 1.1) plus translation invariance of Lebesgue measure. Autocorrelation notation and positive-definiteness read in J. Madrid & J.P.G. Ramos, 'On optimal autocorrelation inequalities on the real line', arXiv:2003.06962v2, pp.1-4 and p.7 (0 <= |f^(xi)|^2 = INT e^{-2 pi i xi t} g(t) dt with g(t) = INT f(x) f(x+t) dx).

hoelder-inequality.published_statement: arXiv:1412.2017 p.2, 'Theorem 1.1 (Hoelder's inequality, 1889). Let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a measure space and let p, q in [1, infinity] with 1/p + 1/q = 1 (Hoelder's conjugates). Then, for all measurable real or complex valued functions f and g on Omega, INT |f g| dmu <= (INT |f|^p dmu)^{1/p} (INT |g|^q dmu)^{1/q}. If one has p, q in (1, infinity), f in L^p(mu), and g in L^q(mu), then this inequality becomes an equality if and only if |f|^p and |g|^q are linearly dependent in L^1(mu). When one has p = q = 2 we recover a form of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.' Endpoint used by the tree: p = infinity, q = 1, i.e. INT |h| w <= ||h||_inf ||w||_1. Autocorrelation (2003.06962 p.7 notation): g(t) = INT_R f(x) f(x+t) dx, with Fourier transform |f^|^2 >= 0.
published_hypotheses: P1 (1412.2017 Thm 1.1) a measure space (Omega, Sigma, mu); here (R, Lebesgue)
P2 exponents p, q in [1, infinity] with 1/p + 1/q = 1; the tree uses the endpoint (infinity, 1), which Thm 1.1 includes
P3 f, g measurable, real or complex valued; the inequality is for INT |fg|, so INT h w <= INT |h| |w| is the (trivial) step that passes to a signed integrand
P4 (for the h-bound, via p = q = 2) f in L^2(R) real; h(u) = INT f(t) f(t+u) dt is the AUTOCORRELATION (not the convolution); translation invariance of Lebesgue measure gives ||f(.+u)||_2 = ||f||_2
P5 (equality clause) equality only for p, q in (1, infinity); not used by the tree

hoelder-inequality.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence is direct. Hoelder's inequality (Rogers 1888, Hoelder 1889; restated as Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:1412.2017) is a theorem about integrals on a measure space. Its conclusion takes no measured input, so no later datum can move it. What the authors 'had' was the proof, and the proof is re-run here: the autocorrelation half as an exact identity h(0) - h(u) = (1/2)||f - f(.+u)||^2 (H1, H2), and the (infinity, 1) step machine-checked in z3 in its finite form, with a vacuity guard and a mutation (H3). The only inputs to the tree's use are mathematical constants: pi, zeta(6), zeta(7), the Stefan-Boltzmann value rho = pi^2/30 in units beta = 1, and ||g^2||_1. Each is re-derived; ||g^2||_1 is checked by two independent routes that agree to 20 digits (H5-H7). One thing is genuinely data-like here: the bound's usefulness depends on tau/beta. The bound decides T1 at tau = beta (0.128 < 1/2) and cannot decide it at tau = beta/10 (1.283 > 1/2). The tree records this itself with its vacuity guard, so that is scope, not a moved datum. The physics the inequality is applied to is not part of this entry and is not audited here: the thermal normal-ordered kernel, isotropy's factor 2/3, and Kuo-Ford's measure.

teleportation-transfers-state-not-matter.name: Teleportation transfers a quantum state onto matter already at the destination; no mass or energy moves

source.located: Bennett, Brassard, Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres, Wootters, PRL 70, 1895 (1993): no arXiv copy exists, and alphaXiv resolved the title to Boschi et al. instead. The result is restated in Pirandola et al., arXiv:1505.07831 (2015), p.1-3 and p.7, and in Boschi et al., arXiv:quant-ph/9710013 (PRL 80, 1121, 1998), p.1-2, which quotes Bennett's abstract. The energy clause was read at source in Hotta, arXiv:1101.3954 (2011): p.4 covers standard teleportation and sec.3, p.18-24, the minimal QET model. It was also read in Ikeda, arXiv:2301.02666v5 (2023), p.1-4, Tables II and IV.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1505.07831, quant-ph/9710013, 1101.3954 (two calls), 2301.02666 and 2601.18718. Bennett 1993 itself is NAMED-NOT-READ; everything attributed to it here comes from the quoted restatements.

teleportation-transfers-state-not-matter.published_statement: Bennett 1993, as quoted by Boschi et al. (p.1-2): an unknown quantum state can be "disassembled into, then later reconstructed from, purely classical information and purely nonclassical Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) correlations." Pirandola et al. 2015 (p.1): "an unknown quantum state of a physical system is measured and subsequently reconstructed or 'reassembled' at a remote location (the physical constituents of the original system remain at the sending location). This process requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication. Most importantly, it requires the resource of quantum entanglement." Pirandola p.2: "Alice's input state is assumed to be unknown, otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation." ENERGY (Hotta 2011 p.4; this is not a claim Bennett makes): standard teleportation "is not sufficient to teleport energy by itself. Transfer of an excited state to a distant point requires preparation in advance of the same amount of energy of the state at the point ... No energy is teleported in this case." Hotta then states the exception, Quantum Energy Teleportation (QET): "effective energy transportation simply via local operations and classical communication" by "extracting zero-point energy of entangled many-body systems", with E_A >= E_B (p.16).
published_hypotheses: H1: Alice and Bob already share an entangled pair; Bob's half B is at the destination before the protocol runs (Pirandola p.1-2).
H2: two classical bits per qubit (d^2 outcomes in dimension d) travel over an ordinary classical channel; nothing is superluminal (Pirandola p.1).
H3: the input state is unknown to Alice; with a known state the protocol reduces to remote state preparation (Pirandola p.2).
H4: Bob's system has a Hilbert space able to carry the state. It need not be the same species: light-to-matter and matter-to-matter teleportation are reported (Pirandola p.7).
H5: the physical constituents of the input stay at the sender (Pirandola p.1).
H6 (energy, Hotta p.4): in standard teleportation between non-interacting systems, Bob's local device supplies or absorbs the energy of the teleported state.

H7 (the QET exception, Hotta sec.3-5; Ikeda 2023): in an interacting medium in an entangled ground state spanning A and B, local operations and classical communication (LOCC) let Bob extract E_B > 0 from local zero-point fluctuations, with E_B <= E_A. What is sent is classical information, not energy.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED hypothesis, at transit.py:57-59 and 260-263: 'an identical stock of matter must already be there -- and that had to travel.' teleportation-transfers-state-not-matter.lacked_data: Bennett 1993 is a theorem with no numerical inputs. What the authors lacked in 1993 was experimental confirmation (first obtained 1997-98) and QET (proposed 2008, demonstrated on hardware and by NMR in 2023). The experiments confirm the result: every platform reviewed by Pirandola pre-positioned the receiver and left the input's constituents at the sender. QET moves only the tree's energy clause, which Bennett does not claim; the source support for that clause is Hotta p.4, and only for non-interacting systems. QET delivers E_B > 0 at the destination (computed here, and Ikeda's table reproduced), but the energy comes from B's own zero-point fluctuations in a medium that must already span A-B. It also satisfies E_B <= E_A, needs bits sent at <= c, and in gapped systems decays exponentially with distance. No matter moves, so CARRIES_SUBSTANCE = False and BEATS_LIGHT = False stand. M's hypothesis therefore holds for the energy clause as the tree states it, but not for the state-not-matter core.
teleportation-transfers-state-not-matter.grade_evidence: The core stands: teleportation transfers a state onto a pre-positioned receiver while the constituents stay at the sender (Pirandola p.1, READ), and this was re-derived symbolically (8/8). The claim as the tree states it is narrowed on three counts. (1) 'No energy moves' holds for standard teleportation between non-interacting systems (PART 2 computes it), but it is stated without qualifier, and QET gives E_B > 0 at the destination by LOCC (PART 3, 22/22). (2) 'An identical stock of matter ... that had to travel' is a hypothesis the source does not carry: the receiver need not be the same species, and only the entanglement carrier had to cross at <= c. The tree's own transit.py:46-47 and stockgate.py:801 use the weaker, correct form. (3) The destination must also supply the state's energy (Hotta p.4), and the tree does not price that. None of the three reaches CARRIES_SUBSTANCE = False, BEATS_LIGHT = False, or the zero advantage over light that R11, Rec and M-S1A-P5 rely on. The grade is not WRONG, because no counterexample exists.
teleportation-transfers-state-not-matter.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade becomes STANDS if the owner sentence is read, or annotated, as scoped to Bennett teleportation between non-interacting systems, with 'a suitable pre-positioned receiver whose entanglement was carried at <= c' in place of 'an identical stock that had to travel'. The energy clause becomes OPEN if DOCKET 66 finds a QET variant not bounded by E_A or by a local zero-point budget. The grade becomes WRONG only if some LOCC-plus-entanglement protocol transferred rest mass or particle number; none is known. Reading Bennett 1993 at source would change only read_status.

gr-qc/9406053.published_statement: Abstract: 'extends to a wider class of spacetimes previous results of Geroch and Tipler that show that topology change is only to be had at a price ... causal compactness, a condition satisfied in a very wide range of situations ... topology change is kinematically possible ... Geroch's closed-universe argument is applied to causally compact spacetimes to show that even in this wider class of spacetimes there are causality violations associated with topology change ... in dimensions >= 3 causally compact topology-changing spacetimes cannot satisfy Einstein's equation (with a reasonable source) ... it does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities (of the standard incomplete-geodesic variety).' THEOREM 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' THEOREM 3: (time-oriented) causally compact interpolating spacetime of dimension >= 3 with (i) the null generic condition on every full null geodesic and (ii) the half-integral null convergence condition; then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected. SEC. IX: 'Neither Geroch's original theorem, nor its mild generalization in section IV, assume anything about the energy-momentum tensor, or indeed about a field equation'; 'If the standard incomplete-geodesic definition is used ... as long as the causal compactness condition is met, causality violations have to occur when the topology changes, even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. But, other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true'. Escapes: the Euclidean path integral abandons the Lorentzian framework; 'even within the general Lorentzian framework there are still several interesting possibilities': A] drop causal compactness (Tipler Thm 5, closed universe, 'mild additional assumptions': a singularity or a point at infinity, 'a highly undesirable feature'); B] weaken the curvature constraints ('would not affect the presence of causality violations'; either alter Einstein's equation, which 'would have to be fairly severe', OR energy-condition violations large enough to break assumption (ii)); C] degenerate metrics (Sorkin, Ashtekar, Horowitz: 'even in standard general relativity (couched in first-order language) ... this might well prove to be the correct approach').
published_hypotheses: M is an interpolating spacetime: connected smooth (C^3 manifold with C^2 fields suffices, Sec. VIII) Hausdorff paracompact n-manifold with boundary S1 u S2 u T, T empty or a compact timelike tube (Sec. II.A)
a smooth NON-DEGENERATE Lorentz metric everywhere on M; S1 and S2 spacelike, S1 initial, S2 final (Sec. II.A)
time-oriented (Thm 1, Thm 3); removable for non-empty boundaries (Sec. VII)
causal compactness: I(p) compact for every p (Sec. III.B); for open universes, M is the causally compact region of an externally simple spacetime (Sec. III.E)

differentiable (C^1) timelike vector field: 'If we were satisfied with metrics that are only continuous ... S1 and S2 need not be diffeomorphic, even if causality violations are forbidden' (Sec. VIII)
Theorem 1 assumes nothing about T_ab or a field equation (Sec. IX)

Theorem 3 only: dim >= 3; (i) null generic condition on every full null geodesic; (ii) half-integral null convergence, implied via Einstein's equation (any Lambda) by T(V,V) >= K for all unit timelike V (Sec. VI); no completeness assumption

gr-qc/0209075#flat-scalar-and-conclusion.published_statement: (4.5b) k^2[12 beta k^2 - 1/(4 pi G_N) + (k^2)^2 int_0^inf ds rho^(S)(s)/(s^3 (s + k^2 - i eps sgn k^0))] = 0. Greek letters are restored here; the sign in front of 12 beta k^2 is not legible in the text layer. p.12: 'The net effect of either the covariant or canonical analysis is to remove the overall k^2 = 0 propagating solution from the scalar sector, as it is not dynamically allowed by the constraints. The possibility of a finite number of non-propagating (global) modes in the scalar sector at k = 0 cannot be excluded by this argument, and must be investigated by imposing appropriate boundary conditions at spatial infinity. We do not treat this possibility in this paper.' pp.12-13: 'there are no scalar mode solutions (stable or otherwise) with 4 pi G_N |k^2| << 1, for exactly the same reason as in the tensor case ... (4.11) Re F^(S)(k^2/m^2) -> (1/(96 pi^2)) (1-6 xi)^2 log(|k^2|/m^2) as |k^2| -> inf, which shows that the linear response eq. cannot be satisfied for either sign of k^2 unless G_N|k^2| becomes of order unity.' p.13: 'there are no new solutions of the linear response equations, stable or unstable, far from the Planck regime.' Abstract: flat space 'is stable to all perturbations on distance scales much larger than the Planck length.' V p.14: 'provided we restrict ourselves to solutions with 4 pi G_N|k^2| <~ O(1). The exact finite number of order unity ... determines the values of k^2 for which new Planckian solutions and instabilities will appear. Its value depends on both the matter theory and the values of the renormalized coefficients alpha and beta of the fourth order terms.' Also p.14: '... stability of flat space for all local perturbations obeying the inequality (4.6).'

gr-qc/0209075#flat-scalar-and-conclusion.lacked_data: In 2002 AMM had no measured alpha or beta, and nobody has one now. They also had sub-mm tests down to about 0.2 mm and no CMB constraint on R^2 inflation. Later work tightened the sub-mm tests (NAMED-NOT-READ; per the READ 0803.1836 these still allow |beta| up to about 1e60). Planck-era fits favour Starobinsky R^2 inflation (NAMED-NOT-READ); that gives |beta| of about 1e9 only if its R^2 term is this same constant. The species-cutoff literature also came later (2303.11091, READ). None of this changes the computed parts: the subtractions, both log coefficients, (B44) and (B45) re-derive exactly, and there is no root below about 12 l_P for O(1) coefficients. The unconditional abstract form does move with beta (computed: a growing mode at 3.9e5 l_P for |beta| = 1e9). That is not a datum AMM lacked and got wrong. It is a constant nobody has measured, whose role AMM themselves state on p.14, and the tree already carries it as H6. So M's hypothesis gets no support against this computation. Its real content here is that the Planck-scale claim depends on an unmeasured constant (H6) and, for large N, on the species count. Both are recorded as named hypotheses, not as errors.

israel-lanczos-poisson-visser-thin-shell.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: Poisson-Visser (1995) and Ishak-Lake (2002) used NO measured data. The re-derivation here reproduces every printed formula exactly (PV eqs 27 and 33 and the discriminant; IL eq 5 and the sec. III.B numbers). What the authors lacked was not data but two other things. (i) A microphysical model fixing beta^2: PV sec. IV say so explicitly, and it is still absent. The tree correctly treats beta^2 as a free EOS parameter and states its result for all beta^2 > beta^2_crit. (ii) The NON-RADIAL analysis, which arrived in 2026 (Pitre-Schneider-Poisson) and shows that radial stability does not imply stability for positive-mass interiors. (ii) narrows the reach of 'stable', not the l = 0 statement the tree makes. Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: all 24 checks agree exactly, including two separately published numbers (2.37, 3) and a second radial criterion (Gamma_1, taken from the tree's quotation), and no measured quantity enters.

2309.10848-frame-map.published_statement: (a) Sec. I: 'classically, non-minimal coupling can be eliminated by a combined conformal transformation and field redefinition ... it takes us to the Einstein frame, where the NEC is obeyed. However, if the scalar field was initially free ... the field redefinition introduces a self-interaction.' 'both descriptions are equally valid, and the question of which metric is the physical one depends on the probe ... our EFT assumption enforces that the two metrics differ by a small amount. In particular, they are related by g~_mn ≈ e^{-(2/(n-2))(8 pi G_N xi) phi^2} g_mn. (3) Within the EFT framework, when M^2_cutoff is Planckian or sub-Planckian, the quantity in the exponent is small and the two metrics are close.' (b) Sec. II.C: g~ = Omega^2 g, phi~ = F(phi) (21); V~ = Omega^-n (Lambda/(8 pi G_N) + V) (22); T~ (23); 'the null energy is rho~_n = (l.d~phi~)^2 (24) thus always obeying the NEC classically. The two frames are evidently not equivalent in terms of classical energy conditions as the NEC in the Einstein frame is obeyed while in the Jordan frame there are violations. Extending this argument from classical to quantum field theory is not straightforward.' ... 'While there is no relevant theorem ... This point requires further consideration, but so far it seems that it is impossible to construct traversable wormholes in the Jordan frame without unphysical field values. In that sense the two frames can be considered equivalent.' (c) Sec. V.A: Omega = (1 - 8 pi G_N xi phi^2)^{1/(n-2)} (99); F' = (1 - 8 pi G_N xi phi^2)^-1 sqrt(1 - 8 pi G_N xi (1 - xi/xi_c) phi^2) (100); arctanh form at xi_c (103); Jacobian 'beyond the scope of this work'; 'when viewed as an EFT with field values bounded by |8 pi G_N xi phi^2| << 1, the mapping from Jordan frame to Einstein frame can also be done in the quantum theory.' (d) Sec. VI: 'the Einstein frame theory [is] an interacting QFT, for which there are no known state-independent bounds in n > 2.' (e) Sec. II.B eq.(18): 'For xi < 0 any local maximum of phi^2 violates the NEC. For xi > 0 and small field values 8 pi xi G_N phi^2 < 1 any local minimum of phi^2 is a violation' (effective NEC, Jordan frame).

2309.10848-frame-map.lacked_data: The frame map is a classical change of variables, not an extrapolation from data. Knowing xi and phi_max would decide where x << 1 holds, not whether the map is right. The quantum gaps are gaps in the derivation, and they bear on the tree's 'frame artefact' sentence, which the source does not make. 2309.10848-frame-map.grade_evidence: The mathematics the tree quotes stands as re-derived. The map (FFKP 21, 98-103) follows exactly from the n-dimensional curvature transformation (K1, K2). The Einstein-frame null energy is (l.d phi~)^2 >= 0 for any potential (K3). The exponential is the O(x) form of the exact (1-x)^{2/(n-2)} (K4). The tree's use is broader than the source in two ways. (i) candidates.py:236-237, 'the exotic behaviour is a frame artefact everywhere the EFT is valid', is not FFKP's claim. FFKP say the frames are 'evidently not equivalent in terms of classical energy conditions' and show Jordan-frame effective-NEC violations at small field values (eq. 18; K6 at kappa xi phi^2 <= 0.003). They claim equivalence only 'in that sense' (no traversable wormholes at bounded field), argued from the effective ANEC with 'no relevant theorem'. K8 shows the local violation does not vanish as the metric factor goes to 1. (ii) The sentence has no classical qualifier, but the source only argues the quantum map, and says the Einstein frame has 'no known state-independent bounds in n > 2'. The exact-versus-'≈' factor at candidates.py:235-236 is a discrepancy, not WRONG. The tree's downstream verdict that non-minimal coupling fails does not rest on this sentence alone: the magnitude gate is separate (audits/2309.10848.json). The result holds for the classical averaged (effective-ANEC) obstruction on 8 pi G xi phi^2 < 1, which is a smaller class than the tree's use.

1307.3536.published_statement: p.3: 'in the context of the SM the measured value of M_h is special because it corresponds to a near-critical situation in which the Higgs vacuum does not reside in the configuration of minimal energy, but in a metastable state close to a phase transition'. p.19: 'M_h > 129.6 GeV + 2.0(M_t - 173.34 GeV) - 0.5 GeV (alpha_3(M_Z) - 0.1184)/0.0007 +- 0.3 GeV. (64) The quoted uncertainty comes only from higher order perturbative corrections.' p.20: 'take M_t = (173.34 +- 0.76_exp +- 0.3_th) GeV. Combining in quadrature theoretical uncertainties with experimental errors, we find M_h > (129.6 +- 1.5) GeV (stability condition). (65) From this result we conclude that vacuum stability of the SM up to the Planck scale is excluded at 2.8 sigma (99.8% C.L. one-sided). Since the main source of uncertainty in eq. (64) comes from M_t ... M_t < (171.53 +- 0.15 +- 0.23_alpha3 +- 0.15_Mh) GeV = (171.53 +- 0.42) GeV. (66)'. Eq.(67): log10(Lambda_V/GeV) = 9.5 + 0.7(M_h - 125.15) - 1.0(M_t - 173.34) + 0.3 dalpha3. 'Lambda_I at which lambda_eff vanishes, is gauge dependent. In the Landau gauge we find Lambda_I ~ 13 Lambda_V'. p.31: 'the SM vacuum is likely to survive for times that are enormously longer than any significant astrophysical age'. Also p.31: 'assuming the validity of the SM up to very high energy scales ... we cannot conclusively establish the fate of the EW vacuum, although metastability is now preferred at 99.3% CL.' p.32: 'We find Lambda_I = 10^10-10^12 GeV, see eq. (67)'.
published_hypotheses: H-SM-UV: the SM alone is extrapolated to M_Pl with no new physics ('assuming the validity of the SM up to very high energy scales', p.31). The paper itself reads Lambda_I as a possible new-physics threshold (p.32).

H-NNLO: two-loop threshold matching to the pole masses and G_mu, three-loop RGEs and a two-loop effective potential (p.1, Table 1 p.4, p.19). The +-0.3 GeV theory error in eq.(64) covers higher-order perturbative corrections only.
H-TOP-POLE: the collider top mass is taken as the pole mass up to an O(Lambda_QCD) ambiguity, carried as +-0.3_th GeV (p.20; p.14).
H-LIN: eqs.(64) and (67) are linearisations valid only near the measured values (pp.19-20).

H-GAUGE: the stability bound and Lambda_V are gauge- and scheme-independent. Lambda_I is gauge dependent, with Lambda_I ~ 13 Lambda_V in Landau gauge; Lambda_lambda ~ 2 Lambda_V is scheme dependent (p.20).

H-TUNNEL: one-loop bounce action S = 8 pi^2/(3|lambda|). Gravity is irrelevant for Lambda_B << M_Pl and slows tunnelling; 'unknown Planckian dynamics can affect the tunnelling rate [52]' (p.30). The lifetime depends on the future cosmology assumed (eqs.84-87, Fig.7b).

1307.3536.lacked_data:
What the authors had in 2013/14: M_t = 173.34 +- 0.76 GeV (the first world combination), M_h = 125.15 +- 0.24 GeV, alpha_s = 0.1184 +- 0.0007, a one-loop tunnelling action, and a +-0.3 GeV allowance for the pole-mass identification. What came later: the top-mass error shrank (0.29 GeV for the MC mass) while its interpretation split (M_t^MC 172.57 +- 0.29 against the cross-section pole mass 172.4 +- 0.7); a complete NLO lifetime (AFS 2018); and higher-order running (Hiller 2024).

Evidence that the new data do not change what the tree uses: every later analysis read here keeps the central values on the metastable side (AFS 2.48 sigma; Hiller 1.9-5.1 sigma; eq.(64) at PDG 2024 gives 1.67-2.86 sigma). Lambda_I stays inside 10^10-10^12, the lifetime stays near 10^161 yr, and the critical top mass (171.1-171.2 GeV) stays below both measured values.

Evidence for M's hypothesis, in a narrower form:
(a) The headline 2.8 sigma was not stable. It became 2.48 sigma in 2018, and today it spans 1.9-5.1 sigma depending on the meaning of M_t, which the authors could only bound.
(b) The source's own arithmetic has four rounding- or linearisation-level discrepancies. The later full analyses land near the eq.(64)-inverted value of 171.12, not near 171.53.
(c) Everything is conditional on the SM holding to M_Pl, which the data cannot test.

None of this changes 'metastability preferred, not established, top-mass dependent', which is the only form in which the tree uses the result, and C4 does not turn on it.

To DATA-DEPENDENT: a verdict of the tree is shown to turn on the metastability status or its significance. It does not today (rederive C7).

sakharov-1967.published_statement: Rubakov & Shaposhnikov, hep-ph/9603208 Sec. 1 p.2, restating Sakharov 1967: 'Today, this short extract is usually dubbed as three necessary Sakharov's conditions for baryon asymmetry generation from the initial charge symmetric state in the hot Universe, namely: (i) Baryon number non-conservation. (ii) C and CP violation. (iii) Deviations from thermal equilibrium.'
published_hypotheses: The conditions are NECESSARY: R&S write 'three necessary ... conditions'. Nothing in the restatement makes them sufficient or fixes a yield.
The initial state is charge symmetric, i.e. B = 0 at the start.
The setting is 'the hot Universe' (cosmological). The necessity argument itself does not depend on cosmology.

Not stated in the restated sentence, but the standard derivation of (iii), <B>_eq = Tr(e^{-beta H} B)/Z = 0, needs it: H is CPT-invariant, B is CPT-odd, and there is no B chemical potential or CPT-odd background. The literature that evades (iii) this way (Cohen-Kaplan 1987; Davoudiasl et al. hep-ph/0403019) is NAMED-NOT-READ. Rederive check C shows by computation that this hypothesis is load-bearing.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (warpfolder.py:83-84): the tree says getting net B 'requires the Sakharov conditions and delivers eta ~ 6.1e-10 per photon'. The source gives necessary conditions only, and those conditions produce no value. 6.1e-10 is the OBSERVED asymmetry; the tree's own constant at warpfolder.py:229 labels it 'Planck 2018 NAMED-NOT-READ'. This is a discrepancy in the tree's wording. The number enters no computation and no flag.

ADDED, AND CONTRADICTED BY A READ SOURCE (warpfolder.py:402-403, printed by report()): 'SM baryogenesis gives eta = 6.1e-10'. The DOCKET 65 READ of 1206.2942 Sec. 1 says 'EWBG is unable to explain the observed baryon asymmetry within the SM alone'. 1404.3565 p.1 says 'the origin of the baryon asymmetry must rely on physics beyond the Standard Model'. The discrepancy is recorded, not repaired. It points the same way as the tree's conclusion: the SM yields less, not more.

DROPPED (warpfolder.py:81-85): neither CPT invariance nor a zero B chemical potential is named as a hypothesis. In rederive check C, a finite Theta-invariant toy with B and C violated gives <B>_eq = -8.0e-17, which is zero. Adding a CPT-odd term -mu*B gives <B>_eq = 0.086 at mu = 0.05 and 0.508 at mu = 0.3. So the necessity of (iii) holds on the CPT-invariant class. A lab flash in the SM meets that hypothesis, so dropping it does not move the conclusion.

INTERNAL TENSION (warpfolder.py:75-79 against 81-83, and the hypothesis that the flash is '(near) thermal equilibrium'): item (b) calls the flash a rapid quench (Kibble-Zurek), which is out of equilibrium. Item (c) calls it a thermal flash. If the quench is out of equilibrium, condition (iii) is met and cannot be what closes (c). The closure then rests on two things. First, condition (i): B is conserved below T_EW, and above it sphalerons conserve B-L; check D gives B_eq = 28/79 (B-L) = 0 from a start with B-L = 0. Second, condition (ii) and the size of the yield: SM CP violation is insufficient per the DOCKET 65 READ of 1206.2942. In check C, unitary evolution from a C-symmetric state with B = 0 reaches |<B(t)>| = 1.24, so (iii) is necessary but does not block B on its own. The tree names these grounds only in part; its hypothesis 2 records sphalerons as 'not addressed'.

WEAKENED (the '(near) thermal equilibrium' hypothesis for warpfolder.py:81-85): the theorem gives <B> = 0 exactly only at equilibrium. Near equilibrium, a small nonzero asymmetry is allowed when (i) and (ii) hold. This does not move the conclusion; see the yield scale in data row 4.

cmb-dipole-370kms.published_statement: As restated (see source.via), Planck 2018 I gives a solar dipole amplitude of 3362.08 +/- 0.99 uK. That corresponds to beta = (1.23357 +/- 0.00036)e-3 and v = 369.82 +/- 0.11 km/s, towards (l, b) = (264.021, 48.253) deg. Planck attributes the solar dipole to the motion of the Solar System barycentre relative to the CMB, and treats the orbital dipole as a separate modulating term. The HFI paper (1807.06207), as restated, gives 369.8160 km/s.
published_hypotheses: H1, kinematic interpretation: the whole temperature dipole is a Doppler effect, so v/c = A/T0 and any intrinsic dipole is negligible. Reading a velocity off the amplitude is this hypothesis: the dipole coefficient of a boosted blackbody is beta + beta^3/10 (sympy).
H2, reference point: the velocity is the Solar System barycentre's relative to the CMB frame. The observer's orbital motion is removed separately as the orbital dipole.
H3, monopole: T0 = 2.7255 K (Fixsen 2009) converts uK to beta. Using 2.72548 K or 2.7255 K gives 369.816 or 369.813 km/s, both inside +/- 0.11 km/s (computed).
H4, frame: 'the CMB rest frame' is the cosmological frame in which the dipole vanishes. Planck does not claim it is a preferred frame of any Lorentz-violating or brane dynamics.
hypothesis_drift: H1 (kinematic interpretation) DROPPED at branelink.py:150 and branelink.py:270-272. This does not move O7.

cmb-dipole-370kms.lacked_data: The measurement does not lack precision: the temperature dipole is known to about 3e-4. What it lacks is a way to split the dipole into kinematic and intrinsic parts, because converting uK to km/s assumes the whole dipole is a Doppler effect (H1). The data that could test this came later and are contested. One is the aberration test (Planck 2013 XXVII, not read here). The other is the matter dipole, reported at about 2x the kinematic expectation and 4.9 sigma according to a search summary, with reassessments whose verdicts were not read. For the result as the tree uses it, the evidence runs one way: none of this moves O7. If half the dipole were intrinsic, B would halve. If the matter dipole's amplitude were read as a velocity, B would reach about 2.5e-3. Either way B stays at least about 400x below the priced escape of 0.999387630, and the tree already says B is unmeasured and the CMB frame is only a candidate. What matters at the tree's printed precision is not new data but a dropped reference point: Earth's Gamma - 1 swings by about 16 % over a year. So M's hypothesis is partly borne out for the interpretation of the measurement, which is contested, and not borne out for the measurement itself or for the tree's conclusion.

Gamma - 1 = 7.6161e-07 is exact arithmetic on 3.7e5. The tree does, however, drop two published hypotheses. It drops H1, the kinematic interpretation, which the quasar-dipole literature contests (NAMED-NOT-READ). It moves H2 from the barycentre to 'the RECEIVER'/Earth at branelink.py:73-75 and ledger.py:1878-1881, where Gamma - 1 actually ranges from 6.46e-07 to 8.86e-07 over a year (computed). Under the rubric, a dropped hypothesis grades NARROWED. Neither drift moves O7: Earth's maximum B is 1.33e-3 against the priced 0.9994, and the tree-model saving rises by at most 0.5 %. The +9.7e-4 gap between the five-figure value and the Planck value is a rounding discrepancy, not an error. The grade stands on restatement only, because the Planck pages could not be read here.

ew-symmetry-restoration-crossover.lacked_data:
The decisive datum here is the Higgs mass. Before the discovery, the SM transition was conditional: first order for m_H <~ 72 GeV, a crossover above. The 1996 endpoint work did not have m_H. When the datum came (125.13 GeV in the PDG-2026 capture), it settled the question as a crossover, in the direction the tree uses, with a 53 GeV margin.

The 2014-16 lattice authors worked after the discovery. Their inputs were not re-read here. The current m_H and m_t shift the model's T0 by 0.12 and 0.20 GeV, an order of magnitude below the authors' own 1.5 GeV systematic.

If that datum existed, the census status word would be restored. Its absence narrows the entry but cannot loosen the refusal, because taking a candidate source out of the census only shrinks what the core could draw on.

gr-qc/0702056.published_statement:
Abstract (p.1): 'we obtain the first 'absolute' QEI for the minimally-coupled massive quantum Klein–Gordon field on four dimensional globally hyperbolic spacetimes; that is, a bound which depends only on the local geometry ... the bound is explicit and can be formulated covariantly under additional (general) conditions. We also generalise our results to incorporate adiabatic states.'

Intro (p.3), eq. (5): 'For averaging along timelike worldline γ, our result takes the form ∫dt f²(t)⟨v^a v^b T^ren_ab⟩_ω(t) ≥ −B_A (5)', with B_A = ∫_{R+} dξ/π [f⊗f ϑ* T^split H̃]^(−ξ,ξ) + "local curvature terms" (6).

Theorem 3.1 (p.18): 'Let Σ be a small sampling domain of dimension n in (M,g) with hyperbolic coordinate map κ ... Set k = max{n+3,5}. For any real-valued f ∈ C∞_0(Σ) and any Hadamard state ω we have the inequality ∫_Σ dvol f² (Q⊗Q(Λ_ω − H_2))(x,x) ≥ −B > −∞ (64)'. Remarks (p.18): 'This bound depends nontrivially on the coordinates (and on any partition of unity ...)'.

Worldline form, eq. (82) (p.23): ∫dτ f²⟨u u T^ren⟩ ≥ −∫_{R+} dξ/π [ ... ϑ* T^split H̃_5]^(−ξ,ξ) + ∫dτ f²(Q + u^a u^b C_ab). Here T^split uses 'any smooth tetrad ... e_0 = u on γ'.

Renormalisation (p.8): 'any remaining finite renormalisation must take the form of a state-independent conserved local curvature term C_ab that vanishes in Minkowski space'. Also: 'C_ab should, in principle, be measurable.'

Flat check (p.24): '≥ −(1/16π³)∫_{R+} dη |f̂(η)|² η⁴ (88) which is the same as the QEI for the massless field in Minkowski spacetime obtained in [9]'. On the small-scale approach to the flat bound: 'This will be investigated in a future work.'

Non-minimal coupling (p.8): 'one must smear the stress-energy tensor even to obtain an inequality on the classical field [21], which necessitates a more complicated analysis at the quantum level [22].'
published_hypotheses: H1 field: minimally coupled Klein-Gordon field, (∇²+μ²)φ = 0, mass μ ≥ 0. Free field with CCR (p.4).
H2 spacetime: four-dimensional, smooth, Hausdorff, paracompact, no boundary, Lorentzian with signature (+,−,−,−), globally hyperbolic (p.4).
H3 states: Hadamard (Thm 3.1, p.18). Thm 3.3 (p.25) widens this to adiabatic states of order N > 9/2.

H4 small sampling domain (p.17-18): Σ lies inside a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood and is covered by one hyperbolic chart with a bounded coordinate speed of light (62). For a worldline: 'provided that the track of γ can be contained in a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood' (p.23). Otherwise a partition of unity is used, and the bound depends on it (p.18).
H5 smearing: real f ∈ C∞_0 with weight f². Smooth timelike worldline in proper-time parametrisation; a geodesic is NOT required. Tetrad with e_0 = u on γ.

H6 renormalisation: Hadamard point-splitting with w_0 = 0 and length scale ℓ. It carries the conservation term −Q g_ab and a residual C_ab that is state-independent, conserved, a local curvature term, and zero in Minkowski. C_ab is part of the specification of the field species (p.5 fn 2, p.8).

H7 bound: built from partial Hadamard sums H̃_k (H̃_5 on a worldline) plus ∫f²(Q + u u C_ab). It is finite and does not depend on a reference state (p.21). It does depend on coordinates and in some cases on the tetrad; covariance is shown only for worldvolume averages in Fermi normal coordinates (p.18, 25-27).
H8 eq. (88): massless field, Minkowski spacetime, inertial worldline, where the full Hadamard series is its leading term (p.23).

gr-qc/0702056.lacked_data:
FS is a theorem of mathematical physics. Its conclusion uses no measured datum, so M's hypothesis has no empirical input to act on for the theorem itself.

By their own statement, the authors lacked two things in 2007.

(i) Control of the scale on which the curved-spacetime bound approaches the Minkowski massless bound (88): 'This will be investigated in a future work' (p.24), 'ongoing work' (p.27). This is missing analysis, not missing data. It affects the wording at throatmass.py:85-87 ('gap ... narrow'), not any tree verdict.

(ii) A value for C_ab, which FS say 'should, in principle, be measurable' (p.8). The bound's existence and form do not move with it. Any number from evaluating (82) on the corridor moves additively by INT f^2 u u C_ab, so a future O2 evaluation would depend on this datum. The tree already carries C_ab unevaluated.

Evidence either way: the finite, closed-form parts (84)-(88) re-derive exactly (11 of 11 checks). The flat constant agrees with Fewster-Eveson (through the 9/64 Lorentzian ratio, which matches the tree's independent fixture) and with F&T (5.6) at C=0. The one discrepancy found, (87)'s missing 1/pi in the text layer, does not propagate to (88). The later papers read (FO 2007, FFKP 2023, Kontou-Sanders 2020) restate FS's scope and do not correct it. Whether a C_ab measurement or a small-scale approximation theorem appeared later was NOT-SEARCHED, because the alphaXiv quota was exhausted.
gr-qc/0702056.grade_evidence:
The theorem stands as published:
- The flat check re-derives exactly (K1-K6, 11 of 11 pass).
- The tree's quotes at qeihps.py:63-72 are word for word from pp.1 and 8.
- The core use is accurate. An absolute, reference-state-free lower bound on the Hadamard-renormalised energy density along a worldline exists for the minimally coupled KG field of mass >= 0 on 4D globally hyperbolic spacetimes. throatmass.py's demotion of 'no QEI can bound rho_ren' is therefore correct.

It is NARROWED because the tree states it on a larger class than FS prove:
(a) The Hadamard-state hypothesis of Thm 3.1 (p.18) is dropped at fewsterteo.py:113-121/177-179, specthm.py:2146-2153 and ledger.py:1819-1820. It is carried at qeihps.py and in O5.
(b) The small-sampling-domain hypothesis (p.17-18, 23) is dropped at every owner, and qeihps.py weakens it to 'a causal diamond suffices'.
(c) 'Depends ONLY on local geometry' leaves out the coordinate, tetrad and partition-of-unity dependence stated on p.18 and p.25.
(d) The residual term is C_ab plus Q, not C_ab alone. Eq. (88) is a Minkowski special case, and FS leave its approximation to the curved bound as future work (p.24, 27). That cuts against throatmass.py:85-87's 'gap is real but narrow'.

None of these moves a tree verdict: O2 stays OPEN and unevaluated, and O5's demotion stands. No moved datum moves the conclusion. The factor-pi discrepancy in (87) is recorded, not graded; the step from (86) to (88) holds.
gr-qc/0702056.what_would_change_the_grade:
- To STANDS: the owners carry Thm 3.1's hypotheses as FS state them (a Hadamard state or adiabatic N > 9/2; a small sampling domain or an explicit partition of unity; the chart and tetrad dependence; the Q + C_ab term), and throatmass.py:85-87 drops 'narrow' or cites a result that controls the gap between the curved and flat bounds.
- To WRONG: a computed counterexample to Thm 3.1 or to (88). None was found; K1-K6 agree.
- To DATA-DEPENDENT: an evaluation of (82) on the corridor, whose number would move with the unmeasured C_ab.
- On (87): reading the journal version (Ann. Henri Poincare 9, 425) would settle whether the missing 1/pi is a v3 misprint or a text-layer artefact. This does not change the grade.
- On later literature: a discover_papers run, blocked here by the quota, could add later work that narrows or extends FS.

tipler-1977-singularities-topology-chang.published_statement: Borde IX.A, verbatim: 'there is the theorem of Tipler (ref. [8], Theorem 5) ... this result shows (in the closed universe case) that if topology change occurs via a non-compact interpolating spacetime, then it contains (under some mild additional assumptions) a singularity (in the sense of an incomplete timelike geodesic) or a point at infinity. That it is a singularity that must occur may be inferred only under the significant additional assumption that there is an upper bound on the lengths of certain timelike curves in the region of interest. It has been shown by Yodzis [27] that ... (i.e., the singularity may be pushed to infinity). But the presence of points at infinity is still a highly undesirable feature.' Borde, earlier in IX: 'originally presented -- and has been quoted -- as a singularity theorem. Compactness assumptions are not made in this theorem, and topology change is then shown to lead to singularities, but only under a significant additional assumption.' Tipler's own wording of Theorem 5 was NOT READ.
published_hypotheses: The closed-universe case: S1 and S2 are closed (compact without boundary).
Topology change occurs via an interpolating spacetime M.
M is NON-COMPACT ('Compactness assumptions are not made in this theorem').

'Some mild additional assumptions', which are UNNAMED in Borde. Tipler's list was not read. Whether they include the Einstein equation with the weak energy condition is OPEN. The abstract, seen only as a search snippet, ties the paper's topology-change results to the Einstein equations and the WEC.
The conclusion is a disjunction: an incomplete timelike geodesic OR a point at infinity.
A singularity alone follows only under a 'significant additional assumption': an upper bound on the lengths of certain timelike curves.
Singularity is meant in the incomplete-timelike-geodesic sense.

published_hypotheses: Classical Maxwell theory with no vacuum polarisation. Valid for B << B_c = m_e^2 c^2/(e hbar) = 4.414e9 T (computed here from CODATA 2022).

SI units with x^0 = ct. u is T_00, the energy density a static observer measures. It is NOT a null contraction T_kk.
Flat background or a local inertial frame, with minimal coupling.

plummer-potential.name: Plummer-smoothed point-mass potential (Plummer 1911), used as the core model

source.located: Plummer, H. C. 1911, MNRAS 71, 460. It predates arXiv, and the 1911 paper itself is NAMED-NOT-READ. The pair was read in an exact restatement in galpy 1.12.0 (Bovy; pypi wheel md5 87178c69b735417a3c6c8ca1c28a95d9). The C extension agrees, and isotropicPlummerdf.py gives the DF f(E) proportional to (-E)^(7/2).
