plummer-potential.published_statement: As galpy's PlummerPotential restates it: Phi(r) = -GM/sqrt(r^2+b^2), with total mass M and scale b. The density is rho(r) = (3M/4 pi b^3)(1+r^2/b^2)^(-5/2), and the enclosed mass is M(<r) = M r^3/(r^2+b^2)^(3/2). Plummer 1911's own wording was not read.
published_hypotheses: Newtonian gravity, grad^2 Phi = 4 pi G rho, which implies a weak field (|Phi| << c^2)
spherical symmetry
positive mass M > 0 (a stellar system); the density has infinite extent (no compact support), so M(<r) reaches M only as r -> infinity
as a stellar-dynamical model: a self-gravitating isotropic equilibrium with f(E) proportional to (-E)^(7/2) (the equilibrium and DF part, as restated by galpy's isotropicPlummerdf)
hypothesis_drift: SIGN (added, named by the owner). The tree's core has mass -m and negative density (concentric.py:44, 122-133). Poisson's equation is linear, so the pair is sign-symmetric. Re-derived: grad^2[m/sqrt(r^2+a^2)] = -3ma^2/(r^2+a^2)^(5/2), which is the Plummer profile with total mass exactly -m. This is a stated change of hypothesis, not an error.

EQUILIBRIUM / MATTER MODEL (dropped, named by the owner). Plummer's model is a self-gravitating equilibrium. The tree uses only the potential-density pair and says it is 'not claimed as a solution of any matter model; no stability analysis' (concentric.py:145-147).

WEAK FIELD (weakened, partly named by the owner). The pair is Newtonian, and the tree puts it into ds^2 = -(1+2Phi)dt^2 + (1-2Phi)dx^2 (composite.py:133-137). At the design point Phi_max ~ m/a = 0.25, which the owner calls 'NOT small' (concentric.py:139-143). What the owner does not name: for m >~ a/2 the model metric stops being Lorentzian at the core centre. At m = 2e-2, 4e-2 and 8e-2, Phi(0) = 0.9999, 1.9998 and 3.9996, so g_xx < 0 for r < 0.0346, 0.0774 and 0.1586. These m values are header-table rows (concentric.py:73-75). The ray at b = 1 never enters that region, and specthm's mu = 5e-3 and 0.6 mu are Lorentzian everywhere.

At a = 0.02, R_s = 200, a fraction 1.500e-8 of the core mass lies outside the shell. This does not affect M_ADM = 0: for r > R_s there is no 1/r term, and the leading tail is -ma^2/(2r^3).

lens-focal-length-b2-over-4m.published_statement: Not read at source. The textbook form the tree uses was re-derived here, not quoted. A ray passing a mass M at impact parameter b (weak field M << b, thin lens b << distances, G = c = 1) is deflected toward it by alpha = 4M/b. Rays at that b from a source at infinity cross the axis at f = b/alpha = b^2/(4M). For a point source at distance D_s, the rays at that b reconverge at D_i with 1/D_s + 1/D_i = 4M/b^2. D_i is positive (a real caustic or image) only when D_s > b^2/(4M).
published_hypotheses: weak field: |M|/b << 1, with corrections of order M/b
thin lens: b << D_s, D_i
fixed impact parameter b: f depends on b, so the lens has a focal line and 'no real image' refers to the rays at that b
vacuum exterior along the ray: b larger than the lens radius
geometric optics (null geodesics)
PPN gamma = 1 (GR) in alpha = 2(1+gamma)M/b
positive M for the axis-crossing reading; for M < 0 the axisymmetric lens diverges
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED ROUTE for M < 0 (composite.py:290-293; canonical hypothesis 'follows from the 4M/b deflection'). The integrated tidal matrix is astigmatic: azimuthal power +4M/b^2 (= alpha/b), radial power -4M/b^2 (= -d alpha/db), trace 0. So the focusing power is 4|M|/b^2 for either sign: azimuthal for M > 0, radial for M < 0. The stated derivation route holds only for M > 0.

gr-qc/9304008-averaging-scale.published_statement: v1 pp.16-17, verbatim: 'The analysis in this paper was restricted to a flat spacetime background. In this case, the expectation values of quartic operators which appear in the dimensionless measure of the fluctuations, Delta, or in the Langevin equation, Eq.(4.27), may be defined in terms of normal ordered products. The generalization of this analysis to curved spacetime backgrounds will require a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such spacetimes, which has not yet been developed. Note that an alternative approach to fluctuations is to discuss only averaged quantities. If we were to average fields over finite space or time intervals, then we could define a quantity similar to Delta without invoking normal ordering. This approach is used by Barton [10] in his treatment of the fluctuations of the Casimir force. In the present context, this procedure suffers from the defect that it introduces an arbitrary length or time scale into the problem. If, for example, one wished to obtain an equation of the form of Eq.(4.3) using averaged rather than normal-ordered quantities, there would be an inherent ambiguity in the resulting equation.' Reference [10] is G. Barton, J. Phys. A 24, 991 & 5533 (1991). Eq.(4.3) is the Langevin mean-squared velocity <v^2> = m^-2 double-integral [F_c F_c + <F(t1)F(t2)>].
published_hypotheses: H1 'In the present context': a flat (Minkowski) background, a free scalar field, the paper's Delta of Eq.(3.2), and the Langevin description of Sec. IV (Eqs. 4.1-4.3, 4.27).
H2 The averaged alternative is defined 'without invoking normal ordering'. Its purpose is to avoid the Minkowski normal ordering KF use, which does not carry over to curved space.
H3 Fields are averaged 'over finite space or time intervals' with an unspecified window. The scale is 'arbitrary' in the sense that nothing in the field theory fixes it.

H4 The stated consequence is an 'inherent ambiguity' in an equation of the form (4.3). The paper states no theorem and gives no computation of how any averaged quantity depends on the scale. It is a qualitative remark.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (context qualifier): the tree quotes the clause 'introduces an arbitrary length or time scale' (fluctuation.py:110-111) without KF's 'In the present context' (H1) and without the consequence KF draw from it, an 'inherent ambiguity' in an equation of the form (4.3) (H4). The quoted words are a verbatim substring of v1 p.17, checked against line 3029 of the saved text layer. The drop does not change what the tree uses the clause for, which is only that averaging brings in a scale, so it moves nothing. It is named here, not graded down.

REPRESENTATION RISK (not a misquote): KF present averaging as an ALTERNATIVE THEY DECLINE, and call the scale its 'defect'. The tree puts 'KF say so themselves' (fluctuation.py:110) in its list of reasons why the POINTWISE Delta cannot be the demand row (fluctuation.py:105-116), right after '(a) ... the physical quantity is smeared, not pointwise' (fluctuation.py:107-109). A reader could take 'say so themselves' to mean KF endorse smearing. They do not; all KF say is that averaging introduces a scale. The tree's next words, 'AND FOR THE CORRIDOR THE SCALE IS NOT ARBITRARY', do treat the remark as an objection to be answered, which is the faithful reading.

ADDED BY THE TREE (not KF's claim; named so it is not attributed to them): 'FOR THE CORRIDOR THE SCALE IS NOT ARBITRARY. It has its own: the width b, and Fewster's sampling time' (fluctuation.py:111-112). These are two scales, not one. The tree's own successor, noise.py:180-193, shows the sampling time is a RANGE rather than a single value. At b = 1 m, tau = b/c is 61 times the curvature length l_G that the demand sets. That breaks Ford-Roman's condition, 'sampling time ... much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature' (gr-qc/9607003 Sec. 4). noise.py therefore shortens it to eps*l_G with eps left free; at eps = 1 and 0.1 the shortfall is 64.108 and 60.108 orders. Pfenning's thesis says the same: 'tau_0 is an arbitrary sampling time' (gr-qc/9805037, cached text line 665), restricted only to be smaller than the local radius of curvature. So the tree's rebuttal cuts KF's 'arbitrary' down to 'bounded above by the geometry'. The refusal it supports (PRICES_THE_CORRIDOR = False, fluctuation.py:157) holds across that whole range. This is a finding about the tree's addition, not about KF.

WEAKENED IN THE SUCCESSOR (named): KF define the averaged alternative WITHOUT normal ordering (H2). noise.py:100 smears 'Kuo-Ford's own measure (normal-ordered square, their normalisation)', so it keeps the Minkowski normal ordering the averaged route was meant to avoid. The tree does not hide this. noise.py:145 and 621 also compute the FULL (un-normal-ordered) noise-kernel relative variance, and noise.py:1153 records 'Kuo-Ford <:A^2:> needs a reference state in curved space; Var does not'. Both halves are therefore in the tree. The owner of THIS key, fluctuation.py, carries only the hypothesis 'smeared rather than pointwise fluctuation', which leaves out H2.

KEPT (correct): the tree limits its reading to arXiv v1 and marks the journal version NAMED-NOT-READ (fluctuation.py:122-126, and JOURNAL_VERSION_READ = False at fluctuation.py:135). This audit keeps the same scope.

data_at_publication.value_now: Computed here in KF's own single-mode model with a Gaussian time window, whose factor is s = exp(-omega^2 tau^2). Squeezed vacuum at r = 0.5, phi = 0.3, theta = 0.1: Delta_s = 0.666667, 0.694577, 0.731668, 0.782013, 0.850360 at s = 1, .75, .5, .25, 0. data_at_publication.source_now: d67/rederive/gr-qc_9304008-averaging-scale.py (sympy + mpmath). Two independent routes, the Wick closed form and truncated-Fock numerics, agree to better than 1e-12.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. For non-classical states it CONFIRMS KF's remark: the averaged measure is a function of omega*tau, so its value depends on the chosen scale, and so does the sign of the averaged energy density (rho_s < 0 is reachable only if s > tanh r). It does not hold for coherent states, where Delta_s = 0 at every tau. Nor does it hold for dimensionless shape numbers of a massless vacuum: in FFR 1004.0179 eq.22, omega_0*beta = c/24, which does not depend on tau. In those cases the introduced scale causes no ambiguity. That exception narrows KF's 'inherent ambiguity' (H4), which the tree does not use; the clause the tree does use is untouched.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS; output in rederive/gr-qc_9304008-averaging-scale.out. The script is independent of fluctuation.py and noise.py and imports neither. C1: the Gaussian window f = exp(-t^2/tau^2)/(sqrt(pi) tau) gives the factor s = exp(-omega^2 tau^2) on the oscillating terms (sympy integral), so A_s = K(2N - s z a^2 - s zbar a+^2). C2: the normal-ordered square :A_s^2:/K^2 = (4+2s^2)a+^2a^2 - 4sz a+a^3 - 4s zbar a+^3a + s^2z^2a^4 + s^2zbar^2a+^4 agrees with the operator square minus its contractions, using exact Fock matrices. C3: for a coherent state, <:A_s^2:> - <:A_s:>^2 = 0 identically in s, theta and alpha, so KF (3.21) survives averaging with no scale dependence. C4: for the squeezed vacuum, the Wick closed form of Delta_s matches truncated-Fock numerics at 4 points. s = 1 gives exactly 2/3, agreeing with fluctuation.py's pointwise record, and s = 0 gives (1+2 sinh^2 r)/(1+3 sinh^2 r). dDelta/ds = -0.1717 at r = 0.5, s = 0.5. The same state gives Delta from 0.6667 to 0.8504 as tau runs from 0 to infinity. C5: rho_s = 2 sinh^2 r + 2 s sinh r cosh r cos(phi+2theta). At r = 0.5 (tanh r = 0.4621) the averaged density can go negative at s = 0.9 (minimum -0.5146) but not at s = 0.3 (minimum +0.1905). C6: for vacuum+2 (KF 2.15), Delta_s = 0.5134, 0.8868, 0.9802 at s = 1, 1/2, 0. C7: FFR eq.(22) gives omega_0*beta = c/24 = alpha, independent of tau. A first draft of C4c used Var(N)/<N^2> (not normal-ordered) as the s = 0 expectation. It FAILED and was corrected to the normal-ordered ratio of KF (3.2); the correction is recorded in the script. later_literature.ref: Fewster, Ford & Roman, arXiv:1004.0179 (PRD 81, 121901(R), 2010), 'Probability distributions of smeared quantum stress tensors'
later_literature.what: Ford himself, with Fewster and Roman, takes the averaged route KF declined. The objects are 'smeared stress tensors' with a sampling time tau, and the distribution is given in units of tau (omega_0 = c/(24 pi tau^2), beta = pi tau^2, eq.22). For a massless vacuum its dimensionless content does not depend on tau: P(negative) = 0.89 for the flux and 0.84 for the energy density, at c = 1. The scale is still introduced, but it is treated as the physical sampling time of a measurement rather than as a defect.

gr-qc/9304008-averaging-scale.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. In 1993 KF had none of the following: a worked averaged-fluctuation calculation for these states; a quantum-inequality theory with a sampling time (Ford-Roman QIs 1995-97, Fewster's general QIs later); probability-distribution results for smeared stress tensors (FFR 2010); or the stochastic-gravity noise kernel (Hu-Verdaguer, 1999-2008) showing that the smeared two-point function is finite in curved space. What that later data does: (i) It does NOT falsify the remark. The re-derivation here shows that in KF's own model the averaged Delta is a function of omega*tau: from 0.667 to 0.850 for a squeezed vacuum, and from 0.513 to 0.980 for vac+2. The later warp literature itself still calls the sampling time 'arbitrary' (Pfenning 1998), bounded only above by curvature (Ford-Roman 1997). (ii) It DOES change the value judgment KF attached to the remark. Later work, including Ford's own, treats the scale as the physical duration of a measurement. It also shows that for coherent states and for dimensionless shape numbers of a massless vacuum, the introduced scale causes no ambiguity (C3, C7). (iii) It removes the 1993 obstacle KF named for the curved-space route: smeared (distributional) fluctuations need no new renormalisation (Hu-Verdaguer). The tree already records this against the neighbouring clause, in ledger.py's D22 DOCKET 64 wording. Net: the data KF lacked narrows their 'defect' and 'inherent ambiguity' judgment, not the statement the tree quotes.
gr-qc/9304008-averaging-scale.grade_evidence: The tree's quotation 'introduces an arbitrary length or time scale' (fluctuation.py:110-111) is verbatim v1 p.17 (saved alphaXiv text layer, md5 f1a66286..., line 3029). Its hypothesis, 'smeared rather than pointwise', matches KF's 'average fields over finite space or time intervals'. The one checkable claim is that an averaged analogue of Delta depends on the averaging scale. Computation in KF's own model confirms it. In C4 and C6, Delta_s moves with s = exp(-omega^2 tau^2); in C5, the sign of the averaged density moves with tau. Two independent routes agree to 1e-12. No empirical datum exists for this remark. Named limits: (1) The tree drops KF's 'In the present context' and the 'inherent ambiguity' consequence, which does no harm to how it uses the clause. (2) The 'NOT ARBITRARY' rebuttal is the tree's own addition, and it holds only as 'bounded above by curvature', as the tree's noise.py:180-193 itself shows. (3) Coherent states and massless-vacuum shape numbers are exempt from the ambiguity (C3, C7). This narrows a part of KF's remark the tree does not rely on. The source fetch in this stage failed (quota), so the READ rests on the v1 text layer saved earlier. The PRD version is NAMED-NOT-READ.
gr-qc/9304008-averaging-scale.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree or a successor relied on KF's 'inherent ambiguity' for coherent states or for scale-free vacuum ratios, which C3 and C7 exempt; or if the PRD 47, 4510 journal text qualifies the sentence differently from v1. static-metric-g0i-vanishes.published_statement: As read: projecting the Einstein equation once along the normal and once along the slice gives the momentum constraint 8 pi J_i = [div_g(k - (tr k) g)]_i, where J_i = h^b_i n^a T_ab is the momentum density seen by observers at rest in the slices (2409.07639 eq.2.4b, Maxwell term dropped). A t = const slice of a static metric is time-symmetric data, k = 0 (2409.07639 p.15, for its metric), and time-symmetric data have P = 0 (1110.2087 p.2). So for ds^2 = -N^2 dt^2 + h_ij dx^i dx^j with N and h independent of t, J = 0 and T^{0i} = -E beta^i/N^2 + J^i/N = 0 (beta = 0, J = 0) in these coordinates. Equivalently G_{0i} = R_{0i} = 0 identically (re-derived, check B). No source read here states a converse of the form 'a shift vector forces T^{0i} != 0'. Le 2602.18023 Lemma 2 says the opposite for gradient and rigid-rotation shifts.
published_hypotheses: Static: a timelike Killing field that is orthogonal to the t-slices, so coordinates exist with g_{0i} = 0 and every g_ab independent of t (restated as time-symmetric slices, k = 0).
T^{0i} = 0 is a statement about components in those static-adapted coordinates: J_i is defined relative to the normal n of the t-slices.
Einstein's equation G_ab (+ Lambda g_ab) = 8 pi T_ab carries k = 0 over to J = 0. Lambda g_{0i} = 0, so a cosmological constant changes nothing.
The metric is regular enough to define curvature (C^2 in the classical statement).

No source asserts a converse. For a metric with a shift, J vanishes exactly for gradient-plus-rigid-rotation shifts, on smooth R^3 with bounded vorticity and on flat, unit-lapse, time-independent slices (Le 2602.18023 Lemma 2).

The theorem holds only in static-adapted coordinates. le-2026-stiffer-wall-clause.published_statement:
Le, arXiv:2606.22531v2, p.28, verbatim: 'Linear stability: marginal, conditionally burn-limited. The realized tangential-pressure wall sits exactly on the Poisson-Visser marginal curve V''(R) = 0 (App. J): a radial displacement is a neutral zero mode. Under the frozen-background rear-pole redshift the marginal wall e-folds in tau_efold = sqrt(2/|V''|), of order a light-crossing time (App. J), so the Tsiolkovsky burn outruns the instability only in a restricted high-compactness, brief-rapidity corner. A slightly stiffer, still-admissible wall is strictly stable at no cost in the surface dec margin, which is junction-fixed and independent of the equation-of-state slope, so strict stability and strict dominant energy decouple; this stiffened wall is a nearby model, not the realized one (App. J). ... the fully-dynamic, flux-coupled stability of the radiating shell remains open.'

The cached pages of v4 (13 Sep 2026) contain no stiffer-wall clause, no 'marginal' and no V''. Instead v4 says that self-similar shells 'have growing normal modes with the ambient geometry and coefficients held fixed' and that 'DEC does not establish stability', and it cites PSP [19] for growth at l >= 2. v4 pages 11-12 are not cached, so it is unread whether v4 restates, withdraws or supersedes the clause.

codata-g-and-constants.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis, tested for this result.

What the earlier physicists lacked: G is the least well known constant CODATA recommends (u_r 2.2e-5), and its input measurements disagree by more than their stated uncertainties. The recommended values read here are 6.67428 (2006), 6.67384 (2010), 6.67408 (2014) and 6.67430 (2018, 2022). That is a spread of 6.9e-5, and the 2010 value sits 3.1 sigma(2018) below the 2018 value. So "previous physicists lacked data" is literally true of G. It is why the recommended value moved at each of the three adjustments 2006-2010, 2010-2014 and 2014-2018; it did not change 2018-2022.

Would more data change wall.py's conclusion? Computed evidence says no. wall.py's figures depend on G at most as G^1. Several do not depend on G at all: the 14-orders inversion, the AU radii, the areal density, and the Msun figures when M_sun is taken consistently as GM_sun/G. A +-1000 ppm move in G is about 14 times the whole 2006-2022 spread and about 45 times u_r, and it leaves every conclusion and every order of magnitude in place.

The other four inputs lack nothing. c, g_n and the au are definitions, and GM_sun is known to about 1e-10.

The one datum wall.py is behind on is its own M_sun. 1.98847e30 is the pre-2019 value, derived from G(2014). Pairing it with the 2018 G shifts the Msun figures by 3.0e-5. This is recorded as a discrepancy; it changes no printed digit.

hyperfine-optical-scaling.name: Atomic scaling laws: nu_opt/(c R_inf) = F(alpha); nu_hf/(c R_inf) ~ alpha^2 g_I (m_e/m_p) F_rel(Z alpha); R_inf proportional to m_e

source.located: These are textbook atomic-structure scaling laws, not the result of one paper: Bohr and Dirac levels, plus the Fermi-contact hyperfine term with a Casimir-type relativistic factor. The variation-of-constants literature uses them: Prestage-Tjoelker-Maleki 1995; Karshenboim 2000 (physics/0008051); Dzuba-Flambaum-Webb 1999; Flambaum-Tedesco 2006 (nucl-th/0601050). The one source READ is the restatement the tree itself cites: Godun et al., PRL 113, 210801 (2014) = arXiv:1407.0164v2, p.4. It prints the coefficients the laws imply (B_E3 = B_E2 = 0, B_Cs = -1, A_Cs = 2.83) and the condition under which B_Cs = -1 holds. It does not print the formulae themselves.
source.via: The arXiv:1407.0164v2 page text is cached verbatim at scratchpad/d67/src/1407.0164.cached.txt (lines 535-570; references at 865-878). In this run every alphaXiv tool (answer_pdf_queries on nucl-th/0601050 and physics/0008051, get_paper_content, discover_papers) returned 'quota exceeded'. The egress proxy refuses arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org and alphaxiv.org (CONNECT 403). The following are therefore NAMED-NOT-READ: Prestage 1995, Karshenboim 2000, DFW 1999, Flambaum-Tedesco 2006, Berengut-Flambaum-Kava 2011, the Casimir relativistic factor and the Barker-Glover recoil formula. Because the laws are derivable, they were re-derived here from first principles in sympy.

hyperfine-optical-scaling.published_statement:
arXiv:1407.0164v2 p.4 (READ): 'Time variation of alpha and mu is measured via the frequency ratio of two clock transitions r = nu_1/nu_2 using the relation r-dot/r = (A_1 - A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1 - B_2) mu-dot/mu. The sensitivity coefficients A_i of the relevant atomic transitions are: A_E3 = -5.95 [34], A_E2 = 0.88 [35], and A_Cs = 2.83 [36]. Dependence on mu-dot arises through the nuclear magnetic moment and is negligible for optical transitions (the sensitivity coefficient B_E3 = B_E2 = 0). As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38], an AFM history can also be interpreted to set constraints on mu-dot/mu (B_Cs = -1).'

The formula form is the tree's own (address.py:62). Re-derived here: nu_hf/(c R_inf) = (2/3) alpha^2 g_I g_e (m_e/m_p)(2I+1) at Fermi-contact order.
published_hypotheses: P1 (Godun p.4): linear response in the constants, i.e. nu ~ alpha^A mu^B with everything else fixed, where mu = m_p/m_e.

P2 (Godun p.4): B_opt = 0 is called 'negligible', not zero. Godun names mu entering only through the nuclear magnetic moment. Nuclear mass (recoil) and nuclear size also bring it in; see rederive B and D.
P3 (Godun p.4): B_Cs = -1 holds 'As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction'. Fixed g_I is a stated CONDITION.
P4 (Godun p.4): the A_i, including A_Cs = 2.83 = 2 + 0.83, are many-body atomic calculations from refs [34]-[36], not measurements.

P5 (re-derived, rederive A): nu/(c R_inf) depends on m_e only through three dimensionless groups: alpha, m_e/M and r_N m_e c/hbar. It is a function of alpha alone only when M -> infinity and r_N -> 0, i.e. a point nucleus of infinite mass.

P6 (re-derived, rederive E): the form alpha^2 (m_e/m_p)^1 g_I^1 is the non-relativistic Fermi-contact term, taken at first order in the nuclear dipole, with infinite nuclear mass. Reduced mass adds a factor (1+m_e/M)^-3. F_rel carries the Z alpha dependence, plus finite-size terms (Breit-Rosenthal, Bohr-Weisskopf).
hypothesis_drift: NAMED CORRECTLY, no drift. address.py:38-40 states 'AT TREE LEVEL, FOR A POINT NUCLEUS OF INFINITE MASS'. address.py:41-44 records that Godun calls the optical B 'negligible', not zero. address.py:47-53 (W10) withdraws 'EXACTLY BLIND' because of finite nuclear size. address.py:53-58 names the same-place hypothesis.

DROPPED: fixed g_I (P3). 'g_I' appears in address.py only inside the formula (lines 62, 615, 1243) and is never stated as a hypothesis. The Godun quote at address.py:434-438 cuts, with '...', exactly the sentence that sets the g-factor condition. In the tree's own scenario a displaced vev moves X_q = m_q/Lambda_QCD by 7/9 (H1) or 1 (H2), which is the change P3 assumes negligible. friedmann-equations.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 p.223: 'addot/a = -(4 pi G/3)(rho + 3p), (8.35) and (adot/a)^2 = (8 pi G/3) rho - k/a^2. (8.36) Together these are known as the Friedmann equations.' These are obtained from the 00 equation (8.33) and the ij equations (8.34) of R_mu_nu = 8 pi G (T_mu_nu - g T/2). Ellis & van Elst gr-qc/9812046v5 p.22: 'The remaining non-trivial equations are the energy equation (37), the Raychaudhuri equation (29), which now takes the form 3 Sddot/S + (1/2)(mu + 3p) = 0, (106) and the Friedmann equation ... 3R = 2mu - (2/3)Theta^2 = 6k/S^2, (107) where k is a constant. Any two of these equations imply the third if Sdot != 0 (the latter equation being a first integral of the other two).' And p.13: 'when omega_a = 0, the generalised Friedmann equation (55) is an integral of the Raychaudhuri equation (29) and energy equation (37).'
published_hypotheses: General relativity: Einstein field equations with the Levi-Civita connection (Carroll 8.29, 8.32; Ellis-van Elst p.10: 'the twice-contracted Bianchi identities which, by Einstein's field equations (1), imply the conservation equations (2)').
FLRW metric: homogeneous and isotropic, with k a constant (Carroll 8.7, 8.12-8.14; Ellis-van Elst (107)).
Perfect fluid comoving with the cosmic frame: U^mu = (1,0,0,0) and T^mu_nu = diag(-rho,p,p,p) (Carroll 8.15-8.18). Ellis-van Elst allow p = p(mu), a sum of such fluids, or a scalar field.
p = w rho with w constant (Carroll 8.21). This is used only to integrate continuity; the Friedmann pair itself does not need it.
Lambda is equivalent to a w = -1 vacuum fluid with rho = -p = Lambda/(8 pi G) (Carroll 8.29-8.31).

The energy, Raychaudhuri and Friedmann equations are not independent: 'any two imply the third if Sdot != 0', and the Friedmann equation is a first integral of the other two. In the general 1+3 setting this needs omega_a = 0 (Ellis-van Elst p.13), which holds automatically in FLRW.
hypothesis_drift: No hypothesis is dropped on the direction the tree uses. The source's one conditional, 'if Sdot != 0' (Ellis-van Elst p.22), applies only to constraint + continuity => acceleration. The tree uses constraint + acceleration => continuity (permute.py:115-116, 290-297). That direction is a polynomial identity with no division by adot (C3b, C3d); z3 finds no counterexample (C5a unsat, with the vacuity guard C5b sat). A static counterexample shows the condition is needed in the other direction (C4b).
UNITS (permute.py:280, 285-287): 8piG/3 = 1 gives addot = -(1/2)(rho+3p)a, which is exactly _accel (C1g). No drift.
LAMBDA as the w = -1 fluid matches Carroll 8.29-8.31 (C1h). No drift.

EQUATION OF STATE (permute.py:115-117, 445-451): the tree uses constant w, while the source allows p = p(mu). The identity holds for any pressure P (C3c), so the tree's class is narrower than the source's. No drift.

CURVATURE (permute.py:117, 300-303): k = 0 or +/-1/4 with a0 = 1 is a rescaling of Carroll's k in {-1, 0, +1}. The requirement adot0 = sqrt(1-k) > 0 is guarded by the ValueError at permute.py:302-303. No drift.

GR is not listed among the canonical hypotheses, but the owner states it at permute.py:107 ('Couple it to Einstein's equation'). It is named here so it is not lost: minimally coupled matter, Levi-Civita connection, no modified gravity.

At 20,000 random (a, adot, k, w) points it stays at rounding level with no integration at all (C6c, at most 1.1e-13). On the fixture the worst value is 7.2e-16, and it is 6.0e-16 at 500 steps against 5.9e-16 at 8000. So the RK4 integration does no work, and any integrator would show the same flatness. sr-velocity-addition-slingshot-strong-fi.published_statement: Tree (arrival.py:7-9): 'REVERSE SLINGSHOT. The coupling is time-symmetric: a pass with the deflector receding takes back exactly what a head-on pass gave, dv = 2U/(1+U^2) either way.' arrival.py:37: 'dv = 2U/(1+U^2), the strong-field limit. Sign is the encounter geometry.' arrival.py:109-111: 'the same magnitude negative with it receding. Braking is departure run backwards and costs nothing.' External content that could be read: Zhang (2020) p.13 says head-tail encounters decelerate, and that aberration makes head-on encounters statistically commoner. The optimised upper limit is 'a 50% gain [in gamma] when |v_A| = 0.2c'. The Newtonian analogue in Acevedo & Ritz (2026) Eq. (2.10) is Delta eps = u_M2 v_i (cos beta - cos(beta+chi)), 'maximal energy gain is 2 u_M2 v_i, which occurs when beta = 0 and chi = 180 deg'. That formula is 'technically only valid for the restricted 3-body problem, in which the heavy component is effectively at rest and a sufficiently close encounter ... can be described as a two-body hyperbolic scattering event in the rest frame of the secondary'. The exact law re-derived here: a full reversal in the rest frame of a deflector moving at U adds exactly 2 artanh U to the ship's rapidity. From rest this gives v_f = 2U/(1+U^2).
published_hypotheses: Elastic scattering in the deflector's rest frame: the speed at infinity is conserved there. This needs a stationary field in that frame, i.e. an isolated deflector moving uniformly during the encounter (restricted-3-body idealisation; Acevedo & Ritz Sec. 2).
Test particle: the ship's mass is negligible against the deflector's, so recoil is neglected (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Maximum gain needs the head-on geometry (beta = 0) and full reversal (chi = 180 deg) (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Deflection near pi without striking the body needs a compact deflector, which is the strong-field clause (Zhang abstract, p.1).
The single-encounter formula holds when one hyperbolic encounter describes the event. In compact equal-mass BH binaries ejections exceed it by an order-unity factor (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Zhang's 50%-per-pass figure is optimised over the entry phase phi0 and the angular momentum L (Fig. 8, pp.13-14).
Special-relativistic velocity addition between the deflector frame and the lab frame (Einstein 1905; NAMED-NOT-READ; re-derived here).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, arrival.py:7-9, 36-39, 109-111: 'either way' / 'the same magnitude negative with it receding' holds as a VELOCITY change only when the incoming speed is exactly w = 2U/(1+U^2), the exact time reverse of a from-rest departure. The general law is in rapidity. Head-on: theta_f = theta_w + 2 artanh U. Tail-on: theta_f = 2 artanh U - theta_w. Counterexample to the unconditioned reading: at w = 0.866, U = 0.35 the speed falls by 0.3390, not 0.6236, and the ship ends at -0.5270 c (rederive D). slingshot_dv(U, head_on=False) takes no incoming-speed argument, so it silently encodes this condition.

DROPPED, arrival.py:36-39: 'ship initially at rest in the frame where the deflector moves at U'. The formula is Einstein addition of U twice FROM REST. Speeds from successive passes do not add; only rapidities do.

DROPPED, arrival.py:160 ('0.87 c -- reverse slingshot IF the destination has a deflector'): one reverse pass stops 0.866 c only if the deflector recedes at U = 0.577316 c. At U = 0.35 c braking needs 1.802 passes, at 0.20 c 3.248, at 0.10 c 6.562 and at 0.04 c 16.45 (rederive F). Each full-reversal pass flips the ship's direction, so multi-pass braking also needs the destination binary to return the ship between passes and every pass to be steered. None of this is stated at the owner.

DROPPED (never named), arrival.py:7-10, 108-117: an isolated, unaccelerated deflector during the encounter (restricted-3-body idealisation). Acevedo & Ritz (2603.08781 p.5) find that in compact equal-mass BH binaries the single-encounter formula fails by an order-unity factor. Time reversal of a trajectory through a binary maps it to one through the counter-orbiting binary, so 'takes back exactly' in a real binary needs the destination configuration to be the time-reversed image of the departure.

At v_inf = 0.35 c around Schwarzschild, chi = pi needs b = 13.1783 M, only 9.4% above the capture threshold b_crit = 12.0476 M, with periapsis 5.604 M. d(chi)/db = -0.984 rad/M, so holding chi within 0.01 rad needs |db| ~ 0.0102 M (rederive H). 'Costs nothing' holds for propellant only; steering precision is unpriced, which the tree records as OPEN at shipspec.py 'timing precision required'.

sr-velocity-addition-slingshot-strong-fi.lacked_data: Evidence AGAINST 'the authors lacked data' changing it: the result is pure special-relativistic kinematics (Lorentz velocity addition applied to a speed-conserving scatter). It has no empirical input except c, which is exact by definition, and it is re-derived symbolically here (checks A-C). No datum has moved and none can move it. Evidence FOR a gap, of a different kind: what the tree's use lacks is three hypotheses, not data. (1) The incoming speed must equal the departure gain for 'takes back exactly' to hold as a velocity statement; in general only rapidity is additive. (2) The deflector must be isolated and unaccelerated; the one later paper that tested the single-encounter formula inside compact BH binaries (Acevedo & Ritz 2026, numerical three-body runs, data Zhang 2020 did not have) finds order-unity departures. (3) Steering precision: b must be held to about 0.01 M near 1.09 b_crit. Having (2) narrows where the formula may be applied. It does not overturn the kinematics.
sr-velocity-addition-slingshot-strong-fi.grade_evidence: The kinematics STANDS: 2U/(1+U^2) is exactly the full-reversal gain from rest (sympy, check A), it is the ceiling over all geometries (check E), and the exact time reverse ends at rest identically (check C). Deflection pi is attainable outside the horizon at finite b (check H). The TREE'S USE is broader than the result. (a) 'The same magnitude negative' holds as a velocity change only for incoming speed 2U/(1+U^2); at w = 0.866, U = 0.35 the loss is 0.339, not 0.624 (check D). (b) Braking 0.866 c needs 1.80 to 3.25 passes at U = 0.35-0.2 c, or a single deflector at 0.577 c (check F), and arrival.py:160 does not state this. (c) The isolated/unaccelerated deflector and test-particle hypotheses are never named; in a compact binary the single-encounter law departs by an order-unity factor (Acevedo & Ritz 2026, READ). (d) 'Costs nothing' prices propellant only; steering needs |db| ~ 0.01 M (check H). (e) The selftest time-symmetry row at arrival.py:80-81 is hollow. None of these contradicts a statement the tree actually evaluates, because its only numeric use is the exact reverse configuration, so the grade is not WRONG. Cross-key DISCREPANCY recorded, not graded here: the 50%/pass-from-gamma0=1 ladder behind 0.866 c (THE-ENGINE.md:116, slingshot.py:55) exceeds the full-reversal kinematic ceiling (check G).
sr-velocity-addition-slingshot-strong-fi.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restricts the claim to the exact reverse configuration (or the rapidity form theta -> theta - 2 artanh U per pass), names the isolated-deflector and test-particle hypotheses, and states the pass count for 0.866 c. energy-conditions-definitions.published_statement: WEC: T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi (Curiel p.6; MM&V eq 2.5; K&S eq 18). NEC: T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for every null k (MM&V eq 2.6). SEC: (T_ab - T g_ab/2) xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi (4D; K&S eq 20 gives T/(n-2) in n dimensions). DEC: T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 AND -T^a_b xi^b causal and future-directed for every timelike xi; equivalently T_ab t^a xi^b >= 0 for co-oriented timelike t, xi. Implications: 'Clearly, the SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC' (Curiel p.8); 'if the WEC is not satisfied, then the DEC has to be violated. However, the WEC and the SEC are, in principle, completely independent' (MM&V p.3); 'the DEC is just the combination of the WEC and the FEC' (MM&V p.13); 'even though the name suggests it, the SEC does not imply the WEC' (K&S p.9). Type-I effective forms: NEC rho+p_i>=0; WEC adds rho>=0; SEC adds rho+Sum p_i>=0; DEC |p_i|<=rho, rho>=0 (MM&V p.6).
published_hypotheses: These are definitions, not theorems. They quantify over ALL timelike (resp. null) vectors at a point: 'holds' needs every observer, 'fails' needs only one.
4-dimensional Lorentzian (M,g) with signature (-,+,+,+). The SEC's 1/2 is the n=4 value of 1/(n-2).
The Hawking-Ellis DEC includes the WEC clause. The flux-only condition (FEC, MM&V eq 4.3) is a different condition and does NOT imply the WEC.
The effective (rho, p_i) forms require Hawking-Ellis type I. The covariant forms need no type assumption.
The physical form equals the geometric form only when the Einstein equation holds (Curiel p.5). T_ab = G_ab in certify.py's units is exactly that identification.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED NAME, certify.py:353-355. dec_holds(wec_min) = wec_min >= 0 is only the NECESSARY half of the DEC. The published DEC also needs the flux -T^a_b V^b to be causal (z3 counterexample: rho=0, p_i=1/2 satisfies the WEC and fails the DEC). The tree uses it only in the published direction (WEC fails => DEC fails; certify.py:85, :453), and every sampled WEC minimum is negative, so no printed verdict is affected. The DEC column at certify.py:450 would still print 'ok' for a tensor that satisfies the WEC and violates the DEC. This is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

ADDED SAMPLING, certify.py:336-351. The published WEC/SEC quantify over all timelike vectors; the tree samples 200 Fibonacci directions x speeds j/11, j=1..10. The static observer s=0 is not in the sample, and the cap s=10/11 excludes s->1. One negative sample is a valid witness of violation, so 'VIOLATED' stands. The sampled minima are NOT infima: where rho+p<0 the WEC infimum over observers is -infinity (K&S Prop 2.1; Le 2602.18023 sec 2.2). Measured at r=1: gamma^2(rho+s^2 p) = -4.66e-3 at s=10/11, -4.39e-2 at s=0.99, -4.41e2 at s=0.999999. The tree's own hypothesis list already names this.

SEC at certify.py:336-351 uses w + T/2 with T = eta^mn T_mn. Machine-checked equal to (T_ab - T g_ab/2)V^aV^b for unit timelike V (sympy). Valid only at n=4, which is the tree's dimension. No drift.

source.located: C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964) and W. C. Hernandez & C. W. Misner, Astrophys. J. 143, 452 (1966). Neither has an arXiv copy. Both were read through exact restatements. (ii) Herrera, Santos & Wang, arXiv 0810.1083 (PRD 78, 084026, 2008), eqs (1),(2),(6),(12)-(18),(25)-(31),(37): the Misner-Sharp mass function and D_T operator (their ref [9]), extended to a dissipative anisotropic comoving fluid with heat flux q. misner-sharp-hernandez-evolution-equatio.published_statement:
From MMR gr-qc/0412063 p.7-8, restating MS 1964. Metric: ds^2 = -a^2 dt^2 + b^2 dr^2 + R^2 dOmega^2, comoving. Operators: D_t = (1/a) d/dt, D_r = (1/b) d/dr, with U = D_t R and Gamma = D_r R. For p = p(e): (9) D_t U = -[Gamma/(e+p) D_r p + M/R^2 + 4 pi R p]; (12) D_r a = -a/(e+p) D_r p; (13) D_r M = 4 pi Gamma e R^2; (14) Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R.

Hernandez-Misner, from MMR p.9-10: f du = a dt - b dr; (20) D_r = D_k - D_t; (25) D_k M = 4 pi R^2 [e Gamma - p U]; (26) Gamma = D_k R - U.

From HSW 0810.1083, comoving, ds^2 = -A^2dt^2 + B^2dr^2 + R^2dOmega^2:
- (14) 8 pi T_01 = -8 pi (q+eps) A B = -2(Rdot'/R - Bdot R'/(B R) - Rdot A'/(R A))
- (18) m = (R/2)[(Rdot/A)^2 - (R'/B)^2 + 1]
- (28) E = R'/B = (1 + U^2 - 2m/R)^{1/2}
- (30) D_T m = -4 pi [(P_r + eps - 4 eta sigma/3) U + (q+eps) E] R^2
- (31) D_R m = 4 pi [mu + eps + (q+eps) U/E] R^2
- (37) D_T U = -m/R^2 - 4 pi (P_r + eps - 4 eta sigma/3) R + E a

None of the sources read writes a separate D_T Gamma equation. In them that content is the tr momentum constraint, HSW eq.(14).
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry; four-dimensional general relativity, G_ab = 8 pi T_ab, no cosmological constant. MMR p.18 includes Lambda only by adding e_v = Lambda/8pi and p_v = -Lambda/8pi to e and p.
Diagonal metric with R the areal radius. MS uses coordinates comoving with the fluid (Lagrangian rest-mass labels, MMR eq.2-3).
MS 1964 as MMR restates it: perfect fluid with a one-parameter equation of state p = p(e).
HSW generalisation: anisotropic pressure, heat flux q, null radiation eps, shear viscosity eta, still comoving.
Hernandez-Misner: outgoing null ('observer time') slicing, perfect fluid.
For m as an integral of density: a regular centre, m(0) = 0 (HSW eq.32).
HSW: A, B, R positive; D_R = (1/R') d/dr needs R' != 0.

The one physical fact the 1964 authors lacked is a nonzero cosmological constant, measured in 1998. With it, EV-W, the tree's load-bearing line, is exactly unchanged (C10a). MS-r, MS-t and EV-U gain Lambda terms (C10b-d). The tree already absorbs these through T := G/8pi (nonstatic.py:297), and they come to 8.05e-7 M_sun at the Proxima span (N3).

Evidence the other way: later work extended the system to heat flux, anisotropy, viscosity and radiation (0810.1083, gr-qc/0403006) and to arbitrary frames (2601.03077), and corrected no MS line. The one narrowing found (0910.2387) concerns theories beyond GR, not missing data.

For this result, M's hypothesis is not borne out: no datum the authors lacked changes the conclusion.
misner-sharp-hernandez-evolution-equatio.grade_evidence:
The mathematics STANDS. All five tree lines re-derive with residual 0 from an independently coded Einstein tensor (C1). They agree exactly with the published restatements of Misner-Sharp (MMR 9, 12-14; C5), Hernandez-Misner (MMR 25-26; C6) and the dissipative generalisation (HSW 14, 28, 30, 31, 37; C3-C4). No datum enters, and Lambda leaves EV-W unchanged (C10a).

The grade is NARROWED only because the tree's use drops hypotheses. 'Geodesic slicing (Phi = 0, always available)' (nonstatic.py:87, relied on at driven.py:239-241 and foliation.py:338-341) holds only up to the first focal point of the normal congruence; contracting Milne focuses at finite proper time (C9). GR and the absorption of Lambda into T are also unstated (nonstatic.py:297).

No verdict in rests_on_it is shown to move. SUSTAINING_FORCES_NEGATIVE_RHO = False rests on global exact witnesses (C8), and E = R dGamma needs only U = 0, not geodesic slicing (C11).

Recorded discrepancies, not refutations:
- EV-W and EV-U' are one equation counted as two (C2a).
- nonstatic.py:82-83 over-reads EV-W (C7, C4a).
- The owners state different hypotheses for E = R dGamma (foliation.py:338-341 against nonstatic.py:178-184). Under nonstatic's, Gamma = sqrt(1-2m/R) is a scalar (C12). This bears on foliation.py:868 BUILD_BILL_IS_GAUGE_CONDITIONAL and is not adjudicated here.
misner-sharp-hernandez-evolution-equatio.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: restate nonstatic.py:87 as geodesic slicing available locally (until the normal congruence focuses), and name GR with Lambda absorbed into T. The equations themselves need no change.

To WRONG: a nonzero residual in C1a-e under a different, verified Einstein-tensor code, or a published MS or HM line that contradicts the tree's form once conventions are matched. Neither was found.

Reading the MS 1964 or HM 1966 originals (NAMED-NOT-READ here) and finding they differ from both restatements would reopen the source status, but not the identities, which are checked independently.

coulomb-exterior-field-energy.name: Electrostatic energy of the Coulomb field outside radius a, Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a), and ADM mass >= X/a

source.located: Three layers. (i) Flat-space field energy U = int_a^inf (eps0/2)E^2 dV = Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a): textbook electrostatics (Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics). Pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Its exact GR counterpart was READ in arXiv:2608.16534v1 (Jaraba, Campos, Baldiotti, 17 Aug 2026) p.6 eqs (38)-(39) and p.7. (ii) ADM mass of a charged thin shell: Arnowitt, Deser, Misner, PRL 4, 375 (1960) and PR 120, 313 (1960). Pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Restated exactly in arXiv:1303.1274v1 (R. Casadio 2013) eqs (2.22)-(2.24) and (3.1)-(3.3), using Israel's junction conditions (Israel, Nuovo Cimento B44, 1 (1966), NAMED-NOT-READ), with the areal form at eq (3.14). Also restated in arXiv:1303.2706v3 (G. Dillon 2013) Sec. 2 eq (4) and eq (9). (iii) Constants: CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787v1, Tables XXXII/XXXIII p.50-51 and Table XXXVIII p.60.

coulomb-exterior-field-energy.published_statement: 2608.16534 p.6-7: 'For an RN spacetime, the KS scalar is given by f_RN(r) = 2M/r - Q^2/r^2 ... the quasi-local energy evaluates to Delta E_RN(r) = M - Q^2/(2r)' [= the Misner-Sharp mass, eqs (31)-(33)]; 'At any finite radius r, the evaluated energy is less than the total ADM mass M. The subtracted term, -Q^2/(2r), corresponds precisely to the classical electrostatic energy of the electric field stored in the exterior region (from the boundary r to spatial infinity).' Casadio 1303.1274, restating ADM 1960 through Israel's junction equations, p.5-6: 'K_thth(r = eps) - K^0_thth(r = eps) = -m0, (2.22) leads to M^2 + 2 eps M - 2 eps m0 - Q^2 = 0, (2.23) ... M = -eps + sqrt(eps^2 + 2 eps m0 + Q^2), (2.24)'. Here eps is the isotropic radius, m0 the bare mass, M the ADM mass, and G = c = 1. Eq (3.1): as eps -> 0, M = |Q|. Eq (3.2): the areal radius is (m0 + eps + sqrt(...))/2. Eq (3.14), at areal radius lambda: 'M_lambda = m0(1 - m0/(2 lambda)) + Q^2/(2 lambda)'. Dillon 1303.2706 p.2-3, restating ADM: 'M(R) = M0 - (G/2) M(R)^2/(R c^2)' plus e^2/2R, which gives M(R -> 0) = |e|/sqrt(G).
published_hypotheses: Einstein-Maxwell theory; static and spherically symmetric; the exterior is Reissner-Nordstrom and asymptotically flat (Casadio Sec 2.2, eq 2.3)
an infinitely thin shell of bare (rest) mass m0 >= 0 and charge Q at isotropic radius eps >= 0 (eps >= r_min when |Q| > M), with a flat Minkowski interior (Casadio Sec 2.1, 2.3)

Israel junction conditions: the induced metric is continuous, and the jump in extrinsic curvature equals the shell's surface stress (Casadio eqs 2.21-2.22). The shell carries a surface tension p (eq 2.20), and the source puts no energy condition on it
geometric units G = c = 1 with Gaussian charge; the areal radius and the isotropic radius are kept distinct (Casadio eq 2.6)
the 'electrostatic energy outside r' (2608.16534 p.7) is the Misner-Sharp (quasi-local) measure M - m(r), i.e. the integral of rho over areal volume 4 pi r^2 dr, not over proper volume
flat-space version (Jackson): Coulomb field of total charge Q inside radius a, energy density eps0 E^2/2, integrated over Euclidean volume
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED/APPROXIMATED: additivity with the bare mass. drivensource.py:360-363 (shell_ratio: 'BARE mass mu. Equals 1/(1 + mu a / X)') and :427 (z3 model 'Mt == mu + X / a') add the flat-space field energy to the bare mass. In exact GR the bare rest mass enters as M = m0 + Q^2/2a - m0^2/2a (Casadio eq 3.14; re-derived here in section D), so the tree drops the gravitational binding term -G m0^2/(2 a c^2). The additive form becomes exact if mu is read as the Misner-Sharp mass at the surface, m(a+) = M - X/a, which is how :149 words it ('the body's own contribution to M'). The conclusion is unaffected: z3 proves r_c <= a for every GR shell with m0 >= 0. At the pinned configuration (:550) the correction is 3.7e-28 kg. This is a discrepancy in the model, not a refutation.

IMPLICIT: which volume measure. drivensource.py:144-145 ('carries energy Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a)') uses the flat-space formula. In GR this value is exact only as the areal integral, which equals M - m(a) = X/a. The proper-volume integral is strictly larger (0.1654 vs 0.1350 at M = 1, Q = 0.9, a = 3). The bound uses only M - m(a), so the drift is harmless.

The supremum is reached only by NEC-violating shell matter, and under the NEC the bound is strict. The tree does not claim the supremum is physical, so this is recorded, not charged against it.

1801.08358-eq22.name: Herrera 2018, eq. (22): Darmois matching condition [P_r]_Sigma = 0

source.located: arXiv:1801.08358v2 [gr-qc], L. Herrera, 'New definition of complexity for self-gravitating fluid distributions: The spherically symmetric, static case' (dated 8 Feb 2018), section II.A, p.3, eqs (19)-(22)
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1801.08358 (pages 1-10 of the v2 PDF text returned). Eqs (1)-(13), (19)-(22) and (32) and the 'necessary and sufficient' sentence were read word for word at source in this audit.

1801.08358-eq22.published_statement: p.3: 'For the exterior of the fluid distribution, the spacetime is that of Schwarzschild: [eq (19)]. In order to match smoothly the two metrics above on the boundary surface r = r_Sigma = constant, we require the continuity of the first and the second fundamental forms across that surface, producing e^{nu_Sigma} = 1 - 2M/r_Sigma (20), e^{-lambda_Sigma} = 1 - 2M/r_Sigma (21), [P_r]_Sigma = 0 (22) ... Eqs. (20), (21), and (22) are the necessary and sufficient conditions for a smooth matching of the two metrics (1) and (19) on Sigma.' The exterior (19) is vacuum, so [P_r]_Sigma = 0 means P_r(r_Sigma^-) = 0.
published_hypotheses: H1 static, spherically symmetric metric (1) in Schwarzschild-like coordinates
H2 the metric is SOURCED: the Einstein equations G^nu_mu = 8 pi T^nu_mu (2) hold inside, with T the fluid's own stress tensor (a self-gravitating distribution)
H3 locally anisotropic fluid, T = diag(mu, -P_r, -P_perp, -P_perp) in Bondi's local Minkowski frame, comoving observer (eqs 3-5)
H4 the fluid is bounded by a spherical surface Sigma at r = r_Sigma = constant
H5 the EXTERIOR is VACUUM Schwarzschild (19) with mass M
H6 SMOOTH matching: the first AND second fundamental forms are continuous across Sigma (Darmois), so there is no thin shell or surface layer
H7 (implicit in eq 20) the exterior time is normalised so that [h] = 0 carries no constant rescaling factor; this is a coordinate choice
H8 general relativity only
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED at the use site: VACUUM EXTERIOR (H5). tolman.py:2396-2398 turns '[P_r]_Sigma = 0' into 'a BOUNDED source has p_r = 0 at the cut'. [P_r]_Sigma = 0 says p_r is continuous across Sigma. It gives p_r = 0 only because Herrera's exterior is vacuum. If the exterior carries stress (the RN field of a charged body has T^r_r = -Q^2/(8 pi r^4); cavity walls may sit beyond the cut), continuity gives p_r(Sigma^-) = the exterior's radial stress, not 0. 'Bounded' carries H5 only if it is read as 'T = 0 everywhere outside', and the file does not say so. The canonical hypothesis 'matched smoothly to an exterior' does not say which exterior.

DROPPED at the use site: NO SURFACE LAYER (H6). The L1 label at tolman.py:2399-2402 states only boundedness. Re-derived here: if P_r(r_S) = p0 != 0 while (20) and (21) hold, the Israel shell has zero surface energy and a tangential stress proportional to p0 (C1-C2). On a fixed background the delta-coefficient of div T is -P(R) + nu'(R) sigma/2 - 2s/R (E1). A bounded traceless source with a traceless shell has p_r(R^-) = p0 != 0 (F1). The canonical hypothesis 'matched smoothly' carries H6, and the file REFUSES 'a ball enclosing a mirror' at tolman.py:549 and 2494, a mirror being a surface layer. So this is a drop at the L1 site that the file partly covers elsewhere.

UNSTATED CLASS TRANSFER, SOURCED to TEST-FIELD (H2). Herrera derives (20)-(22) for a self-gravitating fluid: the second fundamental form jumps because the fluid sources the metric. tolman.py works in the opposite class: 'TEST-FIELD-background ... NOTHING SOURCED -- THEOREM X shows the exactly-sourced class is empty' (tolman.py:2486-2491; also 2439, 2419 and section 2 at 214). On a fixed smooth background the extrinsic curvature of r = const is trivially continuous, so Herrera's derivation does not apply to L1's class as cited. The conclusion still transfers, by another route: distributional conservation on any fixed background. D1 checks that this conservation law is Herrera's eq (9), and E2 shows it forces p_r(R^-) = 0 under H5 and H6. The file does not cite that route.

A WEAKER DEPENDENCY, IN THE TREE'S FAVOUR: L1's TOTAL-mass conclusion does not need eq (22). Place the cut anywhere outside all matter: p_r = 0 there because T = 0, with no matching condition, and m(R) = 4 pi R^3 p_r(R) gives m = 0. In worked example F3 the traceless shell's 4 pi R^2 sigma = -4 pi R^3 p0 cancels the interior m exactly. Eq (22) matters only if 'the cut' is the source's own boundary approached from inside. tolman.py:2399-2402 does not say which cut it means. PEER_STATUS at tolman.py:2621-2625 uses von Laue with the cut outside ('ANY ball enclosing the whole device').

NO DRIFT on 'necessary AND sufficient', which tolman.py:2514-2517 quotes. Re-derived in B1-B5: [K^th_th] = 0 <=> (21); given (21), [K^t_t] = 0 <=> P_r(r_S) = 0; and (21)+(22) imply every mixed K component matches. Necessity needs H6. Eq (20) is [h] = 0 up to a constant rescaling of t (H7). The tree quotes the source accurately.
NO DRIFT on the theory (H8). The tree is GR. Rosa 2103.11698 shows f(R,T) adds smooth-matching conditions but keeps [h] = [K] = 0.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS: 22 checks, exit 0, output in rederive/1801.08358-eq22.out. A1-A3: eqs (6) and (7) come out of the computed Einstein tensor of metric (1), and eq (10) follows from (7) and (12). B0-B5: for r = const, K^t_t = e^{-lam/2} nu'/2 and K^th_th = e^{-lam/2}/r, up to one common sign. Against Schwarzschild, [K^th_th] = 0 <=> (21) <=> m(r_S) = M. Given (21), [K^t_t] = 0 <=> P_r(r_S) = 0. (21)+(22) are sufficient. Herrera's 'necessary and sufficient' is CONFIRMED. C1-C2: if p0 != 0, the Israel shell has S^t_t = 0 and S^th_th = -p0 r_S^{3/2}/(2 sqrt(r_S-2M)). D1: div T = 0 on a fixed background is Herrera eq (9). E1-E2: the delta-coefficient is -P(R) + nu'(R) sigma/2 - 2s/R, so with no surface layer p_r(R^-) = 0 on any fixed background. F0-F4: a counterexample when a surface layer is present. Take p_r = p_t = p0 and u = 3 p0 inside R, with a shell s = -p0 R/2 and sigma = -p0 R. Then p_r(R^-) = p0 != 0, m(R^-) = 4 pi R^3 p0 and m(R^+) = 0. G1-G3: an in-class positive control gives m(r) = 4 pi r^3 p_r(r) at every r and m(R) = 0.

1801.08358-eq22.lacked_data: Evidence runs against M's hypothesis for this result. Eq (22) is a theorem of differential geometry plus the Einstein equations. No numerical input enters it: no G, no c, no measured constant, and M and r_Sigma are free symbols. So there is no datum Herrera could have lacked in 2018, and none has moved since. This audit re-derives the result exactly in both directions (B1-B5). The later papers change the matching conditions only by changing the theory of gravity, and that is a hypothesis (H8), not missing data. The gaps belong to the tree's use of the result. The tree leaves two hypotheses unnamed at the site: vacuum exterior and no surface layer. It also does not say that its test-field class reaches the conclusion through conservation of T rather than through Herrera's sourced derivation. These are drifts in the tree, not a data gap or a defect in Herrera.

No numerical input exists to move, and no later paper contradicts it in GR. The grade NARROWED is for the result AS THE TREE USES IT, at tolman.py:2396-2402 (L1). This is just the statement of the positivity of the relative entropy ... It is always positive (20), and is zero only when rho1 = rho2. This gives a proof of the present formulation of the bound.' 1309.1121 p.2: 'Delta S_A <= Delta<H_A> (3) ... In the form (3), the bound is valid for any region A (not necessarily the half space) and for any "object" state rho^1, due to the positivity of relative entropy S(rho^1_A|rho^0_A) = Delta<H_A> - Delta S_A >= 0 (4)'. ftc-absolute-continuity.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus for the integration step (r^3 p_r absolutely continuous on (0, R] with a limit at 0)

source.located: H. Lebesgue, Lecons sur l'integration (1904) and G. Vitali (1905), neither on arXiv. Read through G. Banerjee, arXiv:2510.20843v2 (2025), pp.1-2 and 5-6: the exact statement of Lebesgue's FTC for absolutely continuous (AC) functions on [a,b], the definition of AC on an interval, and AC vs AC_loc on non-compact intervals (cites Folland 3rd ed.). Also R. Affeldt and Z. Stone, arXiv:2403.18229v2 (ITP 2024), pp.1 and 12-15: the first FTC for the Lebesgue integral machine-checked in Coq/MathComp-Analysis, with the AC (second) FTC named as future work on p.15.
source.via: The Lebesgue 1904 and Vitali 1905 originals are NAMED-NOT-READ. The theorem is READ as restated verbatim in arXiv:2510.20843 p.5 and p.1. Its first-FTC half is READ as formalised in arXiv:2403.18229 sec.10.1 (Lemma FTC1_lebesgue_pt, Corollary FTC1Ny). Rudin RCA Thm 7.21 is NAMED-NOT-READ and is used only as a pointer.

ftc-absolute-continuity.published_statement:
arXiv:2510.20843 p.5: 'Let f : [a,b] -> R be an absolutely continuous function. Then: 1. f is differentiable almost everywhere on [a,b], 2. its derivative f' is Lebesgue integrable on [a,b], and 3. for all x in [a,b], f(x) = f(a) + INT_a^x f'(t) dt. Conversely, if g in L^1([a,b]) and we define F(x) = INT_a^x g(t) dt, then F is absolutely continuous on [a,b], F' = g almost everywhere.'

p.1: 'a function F defined on [a,b] is absolutely continuous if and only if F' exists almost everywhere, belongs to L^1([a,b]), and F(x) = F(a) + INT_a^x F'(t) dt.'

p.2, Def 2.0.1: AC on an interval I is the eps-delta condition over finite disjoint subintervals of I. p.2: 'A function may be absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval yet fail to be absolutely continuous globally.'

arXiv:2403.18229 p.13: 'for f in L^1, F(x) := INT_{]-oo,x]} f(t) dmu is differentiable and F'(x) = f(x) a.e.'
published_hypotheses: Compact interval [a,b] (2510.20843 p.5). On a non-compact interval only AC on each compact subinterval (AC_loc) comes for free, and AC_loc does not imply AC (p.2, Example 3.0.1).
F is absolutely continuous on [a,b] in the eps-delta sense of Def 2.0.1 (p.2).
The conclusion is an identity between LEBESGUE integrals: F' exists a.e. and lies in L^1([a,b]) (p.5).
The theorem makes no assumption about the value of F at the endpoint. F(a) appears in the conclusion, so the FTC never sets a boundary term to zero.

Continuity plus a.e. differentiability is not enough: the theorem is an iff, and the Cantor function is the standard counterexample. That counterexample is re-derived here (T4); 2510.20843 does not show it.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: 'the limit is ZERO'. tolman.py:935 words the hypothesis as 'r^3 p_r must be absolutely continuous on (0, R] with a limit at 0', and :935-936 says 'Regular centre means exactly that'. With a limit L at 0, the FTC gives m(R) = 4 pi (R^3 p_r(R) - L) (T1). The conclusion at :933-934, m = 4 pi R^3 p_r, needs L = 0. The tree's own independence_witness (tolman.py:1380-1386, V32 at :1937) meets the hypothesis exactly as worded: r^3 p_r = A is constant, so it is AC on (0,R] with limit A. Yet the identity fails by -4 pi A (T2). The zero limit IS carried elsewhere in the same file: :51 says 'r^3 p_r -> 0', the master formula at :281-286 carries C = 4 pi lim r^3 p_r, and z3's FULL at :2055 imposes Cc == 0 before B1 (:2070) is discharged. The drift is confined to the citing sentence.

OVERSTATED COMPARISON: tolman.py:936 says the regular centre 'is STRONGER than p_r is finite at the centre'. Read as an implication, this fails. The tree's own W3 (tolman.py:584, p_r = -2 + 10 r^(-5/2), labelled 'regular centre') has r^3 p_r -> 0 while p_r -> +oo (T3). The true half is the other direction: finiteness alone does not suffice (Cantor witness, T4). The two conditions are incomparable, not ordered. This is a wording discrepancy, not a refutation of anything the file computes.

WEAKENED/AMBIGUOUS: 'absolutely continuous on (0, R]' (tolman.py:935) is stated on a half-open interval, and it can be read two ways. (a) AC on (0,R] itself, in Def 2.0.1's sense: this implies uniform continuity, so the limit at 0 exists automatically ('with a limit at 0' is then redundant) and r^2 u is in L^1(0,R). (b) AC_loc, i.e. AC on every compact subinterval: then the FTC plus the limit gives the identity with m(R) as an IMPROPER integral, which need not be a Lebesgue integral. Example: r^3 p_r = r^2 sin(r^-2) is differentiable on (0,R] with limit 0, while INT |r^2 u| diverges logarithmically (T6). The tree does not say which reading it means; m is written INT_0^R r^2 u dr. Where u has one sign (the G2 route, :940-942), monotone convergence makes the two readings agree.

ADDED (a hypothesis the tree may not need): if the ODE d/dr(r^3 p_r) = r^2 u holds at EVERY r in (0,R], which is the pointwise setting of V2/V3, then F = m - 4 pi r^3 p_r has F' = 0 identically (T5). F is then constant by the mean-value theorem, with no absolute-continuity hypothesis at all. The same file's own device, 'C IS A FIRST INTEGRAL, NOT A LIMIT' (:291-296), takes exactly this route. AC is load-bearing only when the ODE holds merely almost everywhere (T4). So the hypothesis is sufficient but not necessary. Recorded, not a fault.

modified-spherical-bessel-k_l.name: Closed form of modified spherical Bessel functions of the second kind k_l(x) = e^{-x} sum_j (l+j)!/(j!(l-j)!) (2x)^{-j} / x

source.located: Classical special-function identity. The standard references are DLMF 10.47.9 (k_n = sqrt(pi/(2z)) K_{n+1/2}), DLMF 10.49.12 (k_n(z) = (pi/2) e^{-z} sum_{k=0}^n (n+k)!/(2^k k!(n-k)!) z^{-k-1}) and Abramowitz & Stegun 10.2.15. None of these is on arXiv, so they are NAMED-NOT-READ. The closed form is READ through an exact restatement in arXiv:2207.00707v4 (Stoutemyer 2022), Sec. 5, pp.22-23: Table 6 rows n=0..4, recurrence (17), the Rayleigh-type formula, k_n ~ e^{-x}/x, and the note that DLMF defines k_n as pi/2 times the table's normalisation. The radial ODE and the 3D exterior multipole expansion are READ in arXiv:2003.03370v1 (Hinzen et al. 2020): eqs (14), (39) and (41).

published_hypotheses: l is a non-negative integer. The sum terminates only for half-integer order l+1/2.
z != 0. There is a pole of order l+1 at the origin.
Normalisation: MathWorld/Stoutemyer write k_n = e^{-x} q_n(x). DLMF's k_n is pi/2 times that, which equals sqrt(pi/(2z)) K_{n+1/2}(z).
The ODE is the 3-dimensional radial modified Helmholtz equation, with angular eigenvalue l(l+1). k_l is the solution that decays at infinity.
Multipole use (2003.03370): a LINEAR equation, with the source compactly supported inside a sphere, and the expansion valid outside it. It runs over all l; l_max is only a numerical cutoff.
hypothesis_drift: No drift on the identity itself. The tree's p_l(y) (excite.py:710-712, 715-719) is exactly the MathWorld/Stoutemyer normalisation: Table 6 is reproduced coefficient by coefficient (C4). It is also (2/pi) times DLMF 10.49.12, agreeing with K_{l+1/2} to 2.3e-41 (C3). The tree's 'up to normalisation' is accurate.

RESTRICTED, not dropped (excite.py:79, 1490-1492, 1767-1776). The tree checks only l = 0..5, while the source covers every integer l >= 0. This audit proves the identity for general l symbolically (C1) and checks it exactly for l <= 12 (C2). A general non-spherical tail needs every l, so the l > 5 content that 'covered ... by the multipole witnesses k_l (l = 0..5)' relies on is supplied by the source and by C1, not by the tree's own check.

UNNAMED in the tree (excite.py:77-79, 1082). H-e says the nonlinear proof is radial 'in any dimension d', but the multipole witnesses k_l with eigenvalue l(l+1) solve the radial equation only in d = 3. C8a shows the tree's k_l fails f'' + (d-1)f'/x - l(l+d-2)f/x^2 - f = 0 for d = 2, 4, 5. The d-dimensional analogue x^{1-d/2} K_{l+d/2-1} does solve it, and its rate still tends to 1 (C8b), but the tree does not seat it. So non-spherical coverage carries an unnamed hypothesis: d = 3.

ADDED by the tree and named ('linear tail (f small)', excite.py:78-79). The linear coefficient of (1/2)f(f+1)(f+2) is exactly 1 (C7), so the operator matches the source's (Delta - 1). But neither the source (which is linear) nor any tree row for l >= 1 proves that the nonlinear O(f^2) remainder leaves the non-spherical tail rate unchanged. The tree's nonlinear proof, steps (i)-(iii), is radial only.

IMPLICIT (excite.py:78-79). Carrying 'rate -> 1' through an infinite sum over l means swapping a limit and a series, and neither the tree nor the source restatement says so. The step is supplied here (C9): k_l(x) e^x x = 1 + positive powers of 1/x, decreasing in x, so for x >= X > r_s each term is bounded by its value at X and the per-l limit passes to the sum.

rederivation.outcome:
All 14 rows pass.
- C1 (general l, symbolic): the residual vanishes if and only if 2k a_k = (l(l+1) - k(k-1)) a_{k-1}. The tree's coefficients satisfy this identically, and the series closes at k = l+1. The identity is therefore proved for every integer l.
- C2: exact residual 0 for l = 0..12.
- C3: the tree's k_l equals (2/pi) sqrt(pi/2x) K_{l+1/2} to 2.3e-41 (mpmath, l <= 12), and symbolically via sympy for l <= 5.
- C4: Stoutemyer's Table 6 is reproduced.
- C5: -R'/R = 1 + 1/x + l(l+1)/(2x^2) + O(x^-3), with limit 1. The tree's x = 1e6 value (1.0000150e-6) is reproduced.
- C6: the control using l^2 in place of l(l+1) fails, as it should.
- C7: the linear coefficient of the nonlinearity is exactly 1.
- C8: the tree's k_l fails the radial equation in d = 2, 4, 5. x^{1-d/2} K_{l+d/2-1} solves it there, with rate tending to 1.
- C9: each term is monotone and dominated, so the sum over l converges uniformly.
The owner's own excite.py --verify V6 rows were also run; they print 0 for l = 0..5.

fermi-constant-g_f-and-tree-level-vev.name: Fermi constant G_F = 1.1663788e-5 GeV^-2 and tree-level v = (sqrt(2) G_F)^(-1/2)

source.located: MEASUREMENT: MuLan, Tishchenko et al., Phys. Rev. D 87, 052003 (2013), arXiv:1211.0960 (final G_F); MuLan, Webber et al., PRL 106, 041803 (2011), arXiv:1010.0991 (the 1.1663788(7) value); PDG 2024 Table 1.1 'Physical Constants' (pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-phys-constants.pdf) lists G_F/(hbar c)^3 = 1.166 378 8(6)e-5 GeV^-2, which is the tree's pin exactly. TREE RELATION: Buttazzo et al., JHEP 12 (2013) 089, arXiv:1307.3536, eqs. (8)-(11) and Tables 1-3 (V = (sqrt2 G_mu)^(-1/2) as the on-shell definition, with (1+Delta r)); MuLan 1211.0960 eqs. (2)-(3).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1211.0960 (pp.1-2, 28-30), 1010.0991 (pp.1, 4), 1307.3536 (pp.4, 6-8, 13), the PDG 2024 physical-constants PDF by URL (p.1), and CODATA 2022 arXiv:2409.03787 (pp.5, 41, 51). vRS 1999 (hep-ph/9808283) and Pak-Czarnecki 2008 are used only as MuLan and Eberhart et al. restate them, so they are NAMED-NOT-READ themselves.

fermi-constant-g_f-and-tree-level-vev.published_statement: MuLan 1211.0960 eq.(24): 'G_F(MuLan) = 1.166 378 7(6) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.5 ppm)'. It comes from eq.(23), G_F = sqrt(192 pi^3/(tau_mu m_mu^5)) (1+Dq0+Dq1+Dq2)^(-1/2), with tau_mu = 2 196 980.3(2.2) ps. The 2011 PRL (1010.0991 eq.5) printed 1.1663788(7). PDG 2024 Table 1.1 gives G_F/(hbar c)^3 = 1.166 378 8(6)e-5 GeV^-2. The relation to v: MuLan eq.(2) is G_F/sqrt2 = g^2/(8 M_W^2)(1 + sum r_i). Buttazzo eq.(8)-(9) is G_mu/sqrt2 = (1+Delta r_0)/(2 v_0^2), with v_OS^2 = 1/(sqrt2 G_mu) and delta v_OS^2 = -Delta r_0/(sqrt2 G_mu). So v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) = 246.21971 GeV is the on-shell (G_mu-scheme) vev BY DEFINITION, because the radiative corrections are moved into counterterms. The tree-level couplings built from it (lambda_OS = G_mu M_h^2/sqrt2 = 0.12917) differ from the MS-bar ones at mu = M_t (lambda = 0.12604 at NNLO, m = 131.55 GeV).
published_hypotheses: V-A current-current Fermi interaction as the effective theory that defines G_F: 'The above extraction of G_F from tau_mu is based on the assumption of the V - A chiral structure of the charged-current interaction. If the assumption of the V - A character is relinquished, the relation between tau_mu and G_F is modified' (1211.0960 p.29)
G_F universality: 'we assume that G_F is universal for weak interactions. Strictly speaking, tau_mu+ determines a muon-decay-specific coupling, denoted G_mu' (1010.0991 p.1)

QED corrections in Fermi theory to two loops (vRS) plus two-loop electron-mass terms (Pak-Czarnecki): Dq0 = -187.1, Dq1 = -4233.7, Dq2 = +36.3, and -0.4 ppm, with 0.14 ppm theory uncertainty from unknown 3-loop QED (1211.0960 p.29)
the free-muon lifetime equals the lifetime in the stopping targets (muonium vs mu+ difference ~0.6 ppb, Czarnecki-LePage-Marciano) (1211.0960 p.30)
convention: the tree-level W-propagator term 3 m_mu^2/(5 M_W^2) is absorbed into G_F (Buttazzo eq.27 removes it and gets G_mu = 1.1663781(6)e-5, '1 sigma lower')

tree relation: v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) holds exactly only as the on-shell definition of v; physically G_F/sqrt2 = (1+Delta r)/(2 v^2) (Buttazzo eq.8-9, MuLan eq.2-3). lambda = m_h^2/(2v^2) and V_min = -m_h^2 v^2/8 are tree-level (Buttazzo Table 1 'LO')

fermi-constant-g_f-and-tree-level-vev.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested on this result. The 2010-2013 MuLan authors lacked three things: (i) the O(alpha^3) QED correction and a modern dispersive hadronic term (they carried a 0.14 ppm theory uncertainty from 'unknown 3-loop'); (ii) the CODATA 2018/2022 muon mass (105.6583755 vs 105.6583715 MeV) and the exact hbar; (iii) later lifetime data in the average (2196981.1 vs 2196980.3 ps). All three have since arrived. Eberhart et al. 2026 computed (i) and used (ii)-(iii), obtaining 1.16637859(59)e-5. That is 0.18 ppm (0.36 sigma) below the tree's pin, a move of 9.0e-8 in v and 1.8e-7 in rho_EW (COMPUTED). For this result the evidence runs AGAINST the hypothesis: having the data did not change the conclusion. Data is still lacking in one place: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision. The EW-fit and CKM routes are about 1000x less precise and disagree with G_mu by +2 and -3 sigma (2102.02825), so whether G_mu carries a BSM admixture of order 1e-3 is OPEN. Even a full 1e-3 admixture would move v by at most 3.8e-4, which cannot move any order-of-magnitude figure. For the TREE RELATION, what is missing is a hypothesis rather than data. The tree uses LO lambda and V_min, although the loop-level parameters were available (Buttazzo 2013, before the tree was written); they move lambda by -2.4 % and m^2 by +10.5 %.
fermi-constant-g_f-and-tree-level-vev.grade_evidence: The MEASUREMENT half STANDS without qualification. The tree's pin 1.1663788e-5 is READ identically in PDG 2024 Table 1.1. Every later READ value (MuLan 2013 1.1663787(6), CODATA 2022 1.1663787(6), Eberhart 2026 1.16637859(59)) lies within 0.18 ppm of it. The MuLan and 2026 extractions were re-run here: the 2026 value reproduces to 2.5e-9, and MuLan comes out 0.27 ppm from its print, a recorded discrepancy inside its 0.5 ppm error. No datum move exceeds 3e-7 in v. The TREE-RELATION half is narrowed by a hypothesis the owner drops. v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) is exact only as the on-shell tree-level definition (Buttazzo eq.8-9; MuLan eq.2-3), and higgs.py:262-275 builds lambda and V_min at LO without naming 'tree level' anywhere in the owner (per grep). The canonical entry names the hypothesis; the owner does not. Its size is COMPUTED from READ numbers: MS-bar NNLO lambda(M_t)/LO = 0.9757 and m^2/M_h^2 = 1.105. The grade is not WRONG: nothing is refuted, no counterexample exists, the tree-level formulae are correct at tree level (sympy A1-A3), and no order-of-magnitude figure (rho_EW ~ 2.5e45 J/m^3, xi_required ~ 1e32) moves. It is not STANDS either, because the 1e-6 fixture digits on rho_EW and lambda are LO digits presented without the LO qualifier.
fermi-constant-g_f-and-tree-level-vev.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner names the tree-level (on-shell, LO) hypothesis at higgs.py:262-275 / excite.py:390 and updates the G_F status to READ (PDG 2024 Table 1.1); statement and hypotheses would then match the source. To DATA-DEPENDENT: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision that disagrees with G_mu (confirming a BSM admixture), together with a tree conclusion that depends on v at the 1e-3 level (none was found). To WRONG: only a computed contradiction of the tree relation at tree level, and sympy A1 excludes one. Resolving the 0.27 ppm MuLan re-run discrepancy, or the last digit that differs between PDG 2024 (...788) and CODATA 2022 (...787), would not change the grade.

hierarchy-problem-v-over-mpl.name: The hierarchy problem: v sits sixteen orders below the (reduced) Planck scale

source.located: There is no single originating paper. The 'hierarchy problem' is a statement the field built up over time: Gildener-Weinberg 1976, Wilson 1970, Susskind 1978, 't Hooft 1979 and Veltman 1981, all NAMED-NOT-READ. It was READ at source in three standard restatements: G.F. Giudice, 'Naturally Speaking', arXiv:0801.2562v2 (2008), secs 2-5 and 9, eqs (1), (5), (9); N. Craig, 'Naturalness: A Snowmass White Paper', arXiv:2205.05708v1 (2022), sec 5; S. Koren, 'The Hierarchy Problem: From the Fundamentals to the Frontiers', arXiv:2009.11870v1 (2020), ch.2. The threshold the tree equates it with is Barcelo & Visser, gr-qc/0003025v2: eq (2.1) p.3, ANEC cases 1-3 p.6, and the m_p/sqrt(xi) sentence on p.16. Data sources: CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787 (Tables XXX, XXXII, XXXIII), and MuLan, arXiv:1211.0960 eq (24).

Sec 3: 'The really problematic aspect about the G_F/G_N ratio in eq. (1) comes about when we consider the effects of quantum mechanics', with delta m_H^2 = kappa Lambda^2 (5), and 'if we take Lambda = M_Pl [= G_N^{-1/2}], the cancellation in kappa must be one part in 10^32.' Craig 2205.05708 sec 5: 'The Standard Model in isolation does not suffer from a hierarchy problem ... It is only in the presence of additional UV scales that the problem emerges ... it is typical to invoke Lambda ~ M_Pl ... quantum corrections that are 32 orders of magnitude in excess of the doublet mass parameter.' Koren 2009.11870 sec 2.3: 'In a theory of physics beyond the Standard Model where the Higgs mass is an output, physical parameters must be finely-tuned in order to produce a mass which is far below the scale of new physics.' published_hypotheses: H1 (the datum): the measured ratio of the weak scale to the gravitational scale is G_F/G_N ~ 1.7e33, i.e. v << M_Pl. This is a measurement, not the problem.

H2 (the problem proper): the Higgs mass is an OUTPUT of a more fundamental theory whose physical scales above the weak scale (GUT, Planck, Landau pole) couple to the Higgs. Then delta m_H^2 ~ Lambda^2, and m_H << Lambda needs a fine-tuned cancellation (Giudice secs 3-4; Craig sec 5; Koren sec 2.3).
H3: no symmetry of the SM protects a scalar mass (technical naturalness; Giudice sec 4; Koren sec 1.3).
H4: it is a naturalness criterion, not an inconsistency. Giudice p.20: 'not a problem of internal consistency ... but an acute problem of naturalness'.
H5 (scale convention): the literature treats 'the Planck scale' loosely. Giudice uses M_Pl = G_N^{-1/2} = 1.22e19 GeV.

H6 (the BV side of the equation): kappa G = T with kappa = 1/(8 pi G_N) (BV p.3). ANEC can be violated only where phi^2 > kappa/xi (case 3, p.6). BV's prose 'above ~ m_p/sqrt(xi), where m_p is the Planck mass' (p.16) is an order-of-magnitude version of that exact condition.

source.located: arXiv:1004.0179v2 [quant-ph], C.J. Fewster (York), L.H. Ford (Tufts), T.A. Roman (CCSU), ESI 2250. Footnote [18] is on pp. 8-9 and is cited from the body at p. 2.
