1004.0179-note18.published_statement: Note [18] (pp. 8-9): 'The connection begins with the observation that the following three statements are equivalent, where A is a self-adjoint operator (with domain D(A) and spectrum sigma(A)) representing a quantum observable: (a) <psi | A psi> >= -Q for all normalised psi in D(A); (b) sigma(A) subset [-Q, oo); (c) the probability measure mu_psi that describes the distribution of individual measurement results of A in state psi has support supp mu_psi subset [-Q, oo). [The implication (a) => (b) is the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle; (b) => (c) because measurements always give values in the spectrum; (c) => (a) because any random variable taking values in [-Q, oo) has its expected value in that range.] In general, supp mu_psi (for a fixed choice of psi) can be a proper subset of sigma(A), and in particular the infimum of the support of mu_psi can exceed inf sigma(A). ... However, the spectrum and the support of the probability measure coincide if A is a local observable, such as a smeared field, and psi is the vacuum state Omega of a Minkowski space QFT obeying the standard assumptions of algebraic quantum field theory [11]. ... In particular, sigma(A) and supp mu_Omega have a common infimum, which provides a sharp quantum inequality bound <psi | A psi> >= inf supp mu_Omega for all normalized psi in D(A).' Body, p. 2: 'These lower bounds represent the lowest eigenvalues of the smeared operators. As a consequence of the Reeh-Schlieder theorem ..., they are also the lower bounds of the support of the corresponding probability distributions in the vacuum state [18].'
published_hypotheses: N1: A is SELF-ADJOINT. A symmetric operator on a dense domain is not enough. D(A) is the domain of that self-adjoint operator.
N2: (a) holds for ALL normalised psi in D(A), i.e. one state-independent bound Q over the whole domain of that self-adjoint operator.
N3: mu_psi is the spectral measure <psi, P_A(.) psi>, the Born-rule distribution of individual outcomes. 'Distribution' means the quantum spectral measure.
N4: the three-way equivalence is abstract Hilbert-space operator theory. It assumes no spacetime, dimension, field or state.
N5: (c) for ONE fixed psi does not give (b). The equivalence is with (c) for every psi; the note's own caveat is that inf supp mu_psi can exceed inf sigma(A).
N6: spectrum = support, and hence a sharp bound, holds ONLY for local A and psi the vacuum of a MINKOWSKI QFT obeying the AQFT axioms (Reeh-Schlieder).

N7: Q can be any valid bound. Only the OPTIMAL Q equals inf sigma(A). The body sentence 'these lower bounds represent the lowest eigenvalues' is exact only for optimal bounds: FFR 1204.3570 p. 12 shows the Fewster-Eveson 4D bound is about 9x weaker than the estimated optimal one.
hypothesis_drift: NONE in the flat theorem C1 (noise.py:165-177). N1 is supplied by H3 (noise.py:156-162): A_tau is the Friedrichs extension on Hadamard vectors, which is the self-adjoint operator FFR 1204.3570 p. 2 say they mean. N2 is met because the tree bounds the FORM on the form domain (noise.py:172-173). That domain contains D(A), so the premise is stronger, not weaker. N3 is H6 word for word (noise.py:164-168). Only (a)=>(b)=>(c) is used, never N6. The chain is used exactly as published.

WEAKENED (the domain and self-adjoint-realisation hypothesis, N1+N2) in the CURVED application. noise.py:42-44 and ledger.py:1822-1826 (the O2 row; LEDGER.md:111) apply note [18] to 'an absolute QEI evaluated on the corridor'. Neither site says that the corridor's sampled operator must be realised self-adjointly, with the absolute QEI holding on ALL of its domain. H3 as defined (noise.py:156-162) is a Minkowski statement about the smeared Wick-ordered operator on Hadamard vectors. Fewster-Smith gr-qc/0702056, the tree's RIGHT_INSTRUMENT (fewsterteo.py:181-183), bounds Hadamard states only. The corridor therefore needs a curved analogue of H3 (the Friedrichs extension from the corridor's Hadamard vectors, or those vectors forming a form core), and these two sites do not state one. ledger.py:584-597 (the D22 row) does append 'Or a failure of H3 ... a self-adjoint extension other than Friedrichs need not keep the bound', which carries the hypothesis there, but under a flat-space H3 label. Rederive E1-E5 shows the failure mode is real: -d^2/dx^2 on (0,oo) has form >= 0 on C_c^oo, yet its Robin extension psi'(0)=a psi(0), a<0, has eigenvalue -a^2 < 0.

ADDED/OVERSTATED: the word 'decides' claims a sharpness the note does not supply. Sites: noise.py:42-44 ('an absolute QEI evaluated on the corridor decides the distribution question there with no variance at all') and ledger.py:584-585 ('by FFR 1004.0179 note [18] it decides the distribution question there'). With a non-optimal bound Q, note [18] gives only supp mu_psi in [-Q,oo). That decides Prob(outcome <= -D) = 0 when D > Q, and decides NOTHING when D <= Q. Rederive D1-D3 shows this: with inf sigma = -1 and a valid bound Q = 2, the true probability is 1/3 at D = 0.5 and 0 at D = 1.5, and the bound is silent on both. N6 sharpness holds only in the Minkowski vacuum, and even there it is sharpness of inf sigma, not of a given QEI's value. The corridor's absolute QEI has NOT been evaluated (fewsterteo.py:149 O2_CLOSED = False; fewsterteo.py:184-187 records it as blocked on the mode functions), so which case obtains is unknown. ledger.py:1822-1826's own wording ('supported in the spectrum of the sampled operator, which an absolute QEI bounds below') is exact and does not overstate.

NOT drift, recorded for completeness: 'every measurement distribution mu_psi is supported in sigma(A_tau)' (noise.py:175-176) holds for every normalised psi in the Hilbert space and for every density matrix, not only for psi in D(A). If anything, the tree reads the result more narrowly than the spectral theorem allows.

later_literature.what: Sec. I p. 2: the smeared normal-ordered operators are 'defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain' and may have more than one self-adjoint extension. The Friedrichs extension is singled out, 'whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind.' Whether the operators are essentially self-adjoint 'is nontrivial and not fully resolved', and distinct extensions share vacuum moments. This paper is the source of the tree's H3, and it makes explicit the N1 hypothesis that note [18] states only as 'A is a self-adjoint operator'. Further: p. 3 restates the (b)=>(c) and Reeh-Schlieder parts. p. 12 sets the non-optimal Fewster-Eveson bound 27/128 against an estimated optimal 0.0236, which is the N7 gap between a QEI and inf sigma. p. 20: 'the conclusion that the probability distribution has a lower bound is independent of any concerns about uniqueness, because this follows from existing quantum inequality bounds'.

1004.0179-note18.lacked_data: Note [18] is a theorem of operator theory. Its conclusion depends on no measured quantity, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked that would move it, and M's hypothesis gets no grip on the equivalence itself. That is shown, not presumed: the published text has no numerical input (READ), and z3 proves the three implications with Q, the spectrum and the state weights all left free (A1-A4). What came later was mathematical, not empirical. FFR 1204.3570 (2012) made explicit that the self-adjoint realisation of the smeared operator is not unique in general ('not fully resolved'), and that the Friedrichs extension is the one whose lower bound is the sharp QEI. The tree already carries this as H3, marked LOAD-BEARING. Fewster-Hollands 1805.04281 (2018) settled self-adjointness for 2D CFT and confirmed again, on two new families, that the support infimum equals the optimal QEI. The one number the tree passes through the note (Q at b = 1 m) moves by 6.13e-10 relative between the tree's rounded HBAR and the exact SI-2019 value, which leaves 71.256 unchanged. So no missing datum changes the conclusion. The only gap is a hypothesis the tree's curved rows leave unstated (see drift), and that is not a datum.
1004.0179-note18.grade_evidence: The theorem itself STANDS exactly as published. It was READ in full at source (1004.0179v2 pp. 8-9). The three implications were machine-checked by z3 with vacuity guards (A1-A7) and illustrated at 30 digits on random Hermitian operators (B). The note's caveat was reproduced (C), and the paper's own closed forms were re-derived exactly (F1-F9). The later literature read here (1204.3570, 1805.04281) confirms it and corrects nothing. Its use in the FLAT theorem C1 (noise.py:165-177) is exact: self-adjointness comes via H3, the form bound is on the form domain, H6 = mu_psi, and only (a)=>(b)=>(c) is used. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS only because of the CURVED application at noise.py:42-44, ledger.py:584-585 and ledger.py:1822-1826 / LEDGER.md:111. (i) 'An absolute QEI ... decides the distribution question' holds only on the smaller class D > Q_corr, where Q_corr is the evaluated bound. A non-optimal bound gives support in [-Q_corr,oo) and nothing sharper (rederive D3: the bound is valid, the true probability is 1/3, and the bound is silent). 1608.05687.published_statement:
Abstract: 'After turning on an interaction that couples the two boundaries of an eternal BTZ black hole, we find a quantum matter stress tensor with negative average null energy, whose gravitational backreaction renders the Einstein-Rosen bridge traversable ... which we suggest might be related to quantum teleportation. However, it cannot be used to violate causality.'

Eq. (3.18): int_{U0}^inf dU T_UU = -h Gamma(2D+1)^2/(2^{4D}(2D+1)Gamma(D)^2 Gamma(D+1)^2 l) * 2F1(1/2+D,1/2-D;3/2+D;1/(1+U0^2))/(1+U0^2)^{D+1/2}. The paper says it is 'always negative' for 0<D<1 and zero at D=0.

Sec. 1: 'signals from early times on the horizon can intersect it again at late times, by passing through the directly coupled boundaries ... making them no longer achronal ... Hence the above impossibility results do not apply.'

Footnote 2: 'We do not consider the case of a time-independent interaction, in order to prevent the quantum state from becoming non-regular on the past horizon.'

Sec. 5, in prose with no calculation: 'The direct boundary interaction could then be produced by propagation through the ambient spacetime -- this would be the same as the interaction we studied, except with a time delay. A similar calculation would then lead to a traversable wormhole ... Since any infinite null geodesic which makes it through a wormhole must be chronal ..., such wormholes do not enable one to travel faster than light over long distances through space ... bank loan.'

Sec. 5, on teleportation: 'somewhat analogous ... Unlike the usual description of quantum teleportation, in our example it is essential that the channel ... is a quantum one ... we propose that the gravitational dual description of quantum teleportation ... is that the qubit passes through the ER=EPR wormhole'.
published_hypotheses: H1: the background is an eternal two-sided BTZ black hole (AdS3, l=1, beta=2 pi/r_h) with the bulk scalar in the Hartle-Hawking/TFD state. The paper 'expects' the D>3 case but does not compute it.
H2: the coupling is a relevant double-trace term h O_R(t) O_L(-t) with Delta<d/2, using the alternative quantisation and a bulk mass satisfying M^2 > -(d/2)^2 (eq. 1.2, footnote 4 on p.4).

H3: h(t) = h(2pi/beta)^{2-2D} for t>=t0 and zero before, uniform in phi (eq. 3.3). The case where the coupling is 'turned on at U0 and never shut off' is computed (Fig. 3.1a, eq. 3.18). The on-off case is the difference of two such results (Figs. 3.1b, 3.2). Footnote 2 excludes only a time-independent interaction.
H4: the calculation is first order in h, one loop, with large-N factorisation (eq. 2.9), and uses the linearised Einstein equation (1.3)-(1.5) with T_UU decaying faster than U^-2.
H5: the two-point function is chosen to be regular on the horizon. The authors say the global-mode construction 'is very tricky' and do not include it (footnote 4 on p.6).
H6: the Hadamard subtraction does not change when the boundary condition changes.
H7: the flat-space case, the Casimir reading, the no-faster-than-light 'bank loan' and the teleportation interpretation are discussion-section prose. They are not derived.

1608.05687.what_would_change_the_grade:

parseval-plancherel.name: Parseval/Plancherel: ||g^2||_1 = 180(zeta6-zeta7)/(pi^3 beta^7) (noise.py) and INT_0^oo u^4|ghat|^2 du = pi INT (g'')^2 = pi mu_1^4 for the clamped sampler (fewsterteo.py)

source.located: The theorem is a classic: Parseval 1799 for series, Plancherel 1910 for L^2(R). No arXiv copy exists, so the originals are NAMED-NOT-READ. The step the tree uses was READ at source in C.J. Fewster, 'Lectures on quantum energy inequalities', arXiv:1208.5399v1, at these places: p.3 and p.30 (Fourier convention fhat(k) = INT e^{ikx} f dx); p.10, eq (1) -> eq (3), where the m=0 Fourier bound -(1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat|^2 u^4 du becomes -(1/16 pi^2) INT_R |g''|^2 dt, which is exactly the one-sided Parseval step with factor pi; pp.10-11, the W^{2,2}(R) regularity remark; p.29, eq (15), the two-sided form plus the remark '|ghat(u)|^2 is even'. The clamped boundary condition was READ in Fewster & Teo, arXiv:gr-qc/9908073v2, Prop. 2.1 (elements of W^{m,2}_0(I) vanish on the boundary together with their first m-1 derivatives), and in eqs (1.3)/(1.5), which give c_2 = 16 pi^2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1208.5399 (pp.3,10,11,25,27-30) and on gr-qc/9908073 (pp.1-2,4). Plancherel 1910 and Parseval 1799 are NAMED-NOT-READ.

parseval-plancherel.published_statement: As restated at source in 1208.5399: p.10, eqs (1),(3), for m=0: (1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat(u)|^2 u^4 du = (1/16 pi^2) INT_R |g''(t)|^2 dt, with fhat(k) = INT e^{ikx} f dx. p.29, eq (15): (1/32 pi^3) INT_R |ghat|^2 u^4 du = (1/16 pi^2) INT |g''|^2, which is INT_R |ghat|^2 = 2 pi INT_R |g|^2 applied to g''. The theorem behind it is standard and was not read in an original: the Fourier transform is a bijection of L^2(R) with INT |fhat|^2 = 2 pi INT |f|^2 in either e^{+-iut} convention.
published_hypotheses: f in L^2(R). The restatement's eq (1) is for g in C_0^oo(R); its own remark extends this to g in W^{2,2}(R), meaning g, g' and g'' exist distributionally and are square-integrable (1208.5399 p.10).
g is real-valued, so |ghat|^2 is even and INT_0^oo = (1/2) INT_R (1208.5399 p.25 and p.28).
FT(g'') = (-iu)^2 ghat with no boundary delta terms. This holds exactly when the zero extension lies in W^{2,2}(R), i.e. g = g' = 0 at both ends of the support (gr-qc/9908073 Prop 2.1).
The Fourier sign convention does not change |ghat|^2 for real g.
hypothesis_drift: noise.py:117-118 and 581-586 name only the series hypothesis. Three Plancherel hypotheses go unstated: (i) g is the one-sided cosine transform of S = k^3 n(k)/(2 pi^2); (ii) S is in L^2; (iii) ||g^2||_1 is a whole-line integral. All three hold, and this was COMPUTED (rederive A2, A4, A6b; noise.py:650 uses Y = 2 INT_0^oo, i.e. the whole line). Dropped from the statement but satisfied where it is used, so this is not a narrowing.
noise.py:583: the series identity holds only for x > 0. The integration range is x > 0, so this is satisfied (A1a).

noise.py:1043 checks only the series step (series = closed form), not the Parseval step INT_R g^2 = pi INT_0^oo S^2. That step is exercised only indirectly, by the spectral-convolution control at noise.py:1048 (tau = beta, 1e-8). This is a DISCREPANCY OF COVERAGE, not an error. Rederive A3 checks the step directly: rel 2.6e-30.

fewsterteo.py:46-54 and 301-303: the source's eq (1) is stated for smooth g, but the clamped-beam mode is not C^oo on R (g''(0) = g''(1) = 44.7466). The regularity is weakened, which the source's own W^{2,2} remark permits; the zero-extended mode is in W^{2,2} because g = g' = 0 at both ends (B1b, 3e-29). Not a narrowing.

fewsterteo.py:47-48: the 'clamped' hypothesis carries weight, and the tree states and checks it (fewsterteo.py:571-572). Guard B5i confirms it: without it, INT u^4|ghat|^2 diverges (per-period integral -> 4 pi^3 = 124.025) while pi INT (g'')^2 = pi^5/2 stays finite. No drift.

The 'real g, u >= 0' hypothesis also carries weight and is stated. Guard B5ii uses g e^{3it}: the one-sided halves are 7492.39 and 335.81 against pi INT|g''|^2 = 3914.13, while the two-sided sum still equals 2 pi INT|g''|^2 to 6.6e-6. No drift.
The normalisation INT g^2 = 1 is ADDED, but it is not a Parseval hypothesis, since the identity is homogeneous. It is needed only for the final equality with pi mu^4. Harmless.

fewsterteo.py:306-316: _tail keeps only the period average (g''(0)^2 + g''(1)^2)/U and drops the oscillating cross term -2 g''(0) g''(1) INT_U^oo cos(u)/u^2 du. At U = 2e4 that term is 3.70e-9 relative. The tree's own residual, re-run read-only here, is -3.709e-9, so nearly all of it is the dropped term, and it uses 37% of the 1e-8 tolerance at fewsterteo.py:577. This is a RECORDED DISCREPANCY in an approximation, not an error.

parseval-plancherel.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply here, and that conclusion is computed. Plancherel is a theorem of pure analysis, so no measured datum could have been missing. The only numbers are pi, zeta(6), zeta(7) and mu_1, all recomputed here to 30-40 digits. What a user of the theorem can lack is a hypothesis, not data: L^2, real g, and clamping. The guards show that real g and clamping carry weight: removing clamping makes the integral diverge, and removing real g moves the one-sided integral from 3914 to 7492. The tree states and checks both. The re-derivation agrees to 2.6e-30 (noise.py) and 1.65e-11 (fewsterteo.py).
parseval-plancherel.grade_evidence: The statement and hypotheses as used match the restatement READ in 1208.5399 (eqs (1)->(3) and (15), plus the W^{2,2} remark) and in gr-qc/9908073 Prop 2.1. The re-derivation agrees. The Parseval step for the thermal kernel was checked directly by quadrature, rel 2.6e-30; the tree checks only the series step at noise.py:1043, which is recorded as a coverage discrepancy, not an error. The clamped-sampler identity agrees to 1.65e-11. Every hypothesis the tree leaves out of its statement is satisfied where it is used, and this was computed. The hypotheses that carry weight are stated, and the guards show that removing them breaks the identity. No measured datum enters. One approximation discrepancy is recorded: _tail drops a cross term worth 3.70e-9 relative, which explains the tree's -3.709e-9 residual and sits inside its 1e-8 tolerance.
parseval-plancherel.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade would become NARROWED if any tree site applied the one-sided form to a complex or unclamped sampler, or used ||g^2||_1 as a half-line integral. None was found at the owner sites: noise.py:117-118, 581-586, 650, 1043 and fewsterteo.py:46-54, 301-316, 575-580. Tightening fewsterteo.py:577 below about 4e-9 without adding the cross term would make that check fail; that would be a fault in the check, not in Parseval. The grade would become WRONG only with a computed counterexample to the equalities, which the quadratures here rule out to 1e-11 and 1e-30.

published_hypotheses: H1: the table gives the present-day solar photosphere, and by extension the convection zone (p.23). It is not the bulk or protosolar composition, which is +0.05 dex for He and +0.04 dex for heavier elements (sec 3.11).

H2: photospheric values come from a 3D hydrodynamical model atmosphere with non-LTE 'whenever possible' (p.8). P explicitly has no non-LTE study: 'No non-LTE investigation has been performed to date for these high-excitation P i lines' (p.15).
H3: the quoted 1-sigma uncertainties are part of the result: Li +-0.10, P +-0.03, K +-0.09. For K the paper says the 'line-to-line scatter is disappointingly large' (p.15).
H4: the noble gases (bracketed) are INDIRECT estimates: He from helioseismology, Ne from a coronal Ne/O ratio of 0.175 (Young 2005b), Ar similarly (sec 3.9).

H5: the meteoritic column is CI chondrite, depleted in volatiles. The paper says it is 'not possible to rely on meteorites to determine the primordial solar system abundances' for H, He, C, N, O and Ne (p.3). The column is pegged to photospheric Si = 7.51 (p.24).

H6: Li is depleted in the photosphere by burning, through mixing below the convection zone that standard models do not produce (p.10). Li is the one non-volatile element depleted in the photosphere (p.25).
H7: the table describes the Sun. Comparing it with other stars or the ISM needs corrections for diffusion (0.04 dex) and Galactic chemical enrichment (0.05-0.15 dex) (sec 4.2, p.30).

0909.0948.lacked_data:
In A09's own words, the authors lacked:
(a) any non-LTE study for P (p.15). One now exists (Andrievsky & Korotin 2026), and AG26 applies it as -0.07 dex, giving P 5.35.
(b) 3D non-LTE Li with complete UV background opacity. Wang+2021 supplies it, giving Li 0.96.
(c) Genesis solar-wind Ne and Ar.
(d) 3D non-LTE K.

Evidence FOR M's hypothesis: with the later data, the tree's 'P binds against a stellar photosphere' flips to Li on AAG21 (by 0.053 dex), on C11, and on L25 (by 0.6 %). On AG26 it survives by only 1.7 %; the margin shrinks from 0.037 to 0.007 dex.

Evidence AGAINST over-reading this:
(i) A09 is not shown wrong. Its quoted Li +-0.10 covers every later value and already gives Li a 36 % chance of binding, so the later data moved within A09's stated error.
(ii) The magnitude does not move on any compilation read here: 1.9e3 to 2.2e3 kg of stock per kg, or 134 to 154 t per 70 kg. Neither do 'a chondrite beats a star', 'site-selection criterion' or 'not a barrier'.
(iii) The CNO/metallicity dispute cannot affect the Li-P criterion, which does not depend on normalisation.

So the missing data matter for exactly one tree conclusion, which element binds, and A09's data never determined that in the first place.

gr-qc/0209075#renorm-4.4.name: AMM renormalisation: three subtractions at k^2 = 0; scalar sector (4.5b) carries overall k^2, no k-independent term

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0209075 v1 (21 Sep 2002), Anderson, Molina-Paris, Mottola, PRD 67, 024026 (2003); Sec. IV pp. 10-13 (eqs. 4.1-4.12), App. B pp. 17-21 (B37-B47)
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries (pp. 1, 8, 10-13, 17, 19, 21) plus the banked full text layer d67/amm_0209075.txt (lines 1760-2330, 4540-4760). The text layer drops minus signs (c_AB printed 'diag(1; 1)'), and no conclusion here depends on a sign that was not restored.

gr-qc/0209075#renorm-4.4.published_statement: p. 11: 'subtracting the first three terms in its Taylor series expansion around k^2 = 0 ... Re[Pi^(i)(ret)(k^2)]_R = Re{Pi(k^2) - Pi(0) - k^2 dPi/dk^2|_0 - (k^2)^2/2 d^2Pi/d(k^2)^2|_0} = -(k^2)^3 P int ds rho^(i)(s)/(s^3(s+k^2)) (4.4) ... The three subtractions in (4.4) correspond physically to renormalizing the coefficients of the cosmological constant (Lambda), Newton's constant (1/G_N), and the coefficients of the fourth order terms (alpha and beta). These are of order (k^2)^0, k^2 and (k^2)^2 respectively. The renormalized values of these parameters at k^2 = 0 are what appear then on the left hand side of (2.9).' Then (4.5a) k^2[2 alpha k^2 + 1/(8 pi G_N) + (k^2)^2 int rho^(T)/(s^3(s+k^2-i eps))] = 0 and (4.5b) k^2[12 beta k^2 - 1/(4 pi G_N) + (k^2)^2 int rho^(S)/(s^3(s+k^2-i eps))] = 0.
published_hypotheses: A1 flat background: 'Flat spacetime is a solution of the semi-classical Einstein equations for vanishing expectation value of T_ab and cosmological term, with the quantum matter field in its Lorentz invariant vacuum ground state' (p. 10)
A2 large-N free scalar fields, arbitrary mass m > 0 and coupling xi; CTP in-in effective action
A3 Kallen-Lehmann representation (4.2) with positive spectral functions rho^(i)(s); support s > 4m^2 for the scalar (B37a,b)

A4 renormalisation by subtracting the covariant counterterms up to dimension four, done as three Taylor subtractions at k^2 = 0; needs m > 0 ('no longer tenable in the zero mass limit'; otherwise renormalise at mu^2, (4.10), p. 12)
A5 at xi = 1/6 two subtractions are enough in the scalar sector, (4.12)
A6 the scalar k^2 = 0 solution is removed as non-dynamical by the constraints; global k = 0 modes 'We do not treat' (p. 12)
hypothesis_drift: NONE on the quoted text: linstab.py:106-110 reproduces AMM p. 11 word for word. The tree names only (4.5b), but (4.5a) has the same overall k^2. That makes the tree's statement narrower than the source; it is not a drift.

WEAKENED (framing), linstab.py:166-168 and H4: the tree says 'AMM's k^2 = 0 subtraction is the choice that leaves no k-independent term'. In AMM the missing k^0 term needs three things together: the (k^2)^0 subtraction, A1 (Lambda_R = 0 and <T> = 0 on the flat background), and AMM's identification of the k^0 coefficient of the linear response with the Lambda of (2.9). GMMPS (2604.01047 Thm 3.6, pp. 22, 32-33) do not make that identification. The subtraction point does not decide the k^0 term. The tree already says 'not adjudicated here' (linstab.py:181-183).
DROPPED from H4: m > 0 is a hypothesis of the k^2 = 0 scheme (AMM p. 12, (4.10)). The tree holds it one level up, in the SETTING at linstab.py:99.

SCOPE, linstab.py:167-168 'i.e. the alpha~^S_1 = 0 case': computed in C7, this holds at order k^0 only. AMM's thrice-subtracted polarization and GMMPS's gamma(a-gamma)^2 J(gamma) differ by c1 gamma + c2 gamma^2 with no constant term. The dependents (LITERATURE_SPLIT_IS_ONE_CONSTANT, linstab.py:344-349) use only F_S(0) = -b_0, so this changes none of them.

CONTEXT, linstab.py:168 'gamma = 0 is an exact root': that root belongs to GMMPS's F_S. AMM remove the scalar k^2 = 0 solution as non-dynamical and do not treat global modes. The tree records NOT TREATED (linstab.py:122-124) and ALPHA_ZERO_ROOT_GROWTH = 'OPEN' (linstab.py:352-353), so nothing is over-claimed.

rederivation.outcome: All 20 checks pass (output in rederive/gr-qc_0209075_renorm-4.4.out). C1: the (4.4) kernel identity 1/(s+x) - [1/s - x/s^2 + x^2/s^3] = -x^3/(s^3(s+x)) is exact. C2: F^(T) and F^(S) (xi = 0 and 0.3) go to 0 linearly as k^2 -> 0. C3: E_T(0) = E_S(0) = 0 exactly, with dE/dk^2(0) = +1/(8piG) (tensor) and -1/(4piG) (scalar), so nothing k-independent survives. C4: the B44 closed form matches the numerical integral to 1.8e-14. C5: the log slopes 1/(960pi^2) (4.9) and (1-6xi)^2/(96pi^2) (4.11) are reproduced to 1e-6, and the (4.10) coefficient 1/(1920pi^2) is consistent. C6: rho^S ~ (s-a)^2 with a = 2m^2/(6xi-1), and rho^T ~ (s-4m^2)^2, the same a as GMMPS (5.1)-(5.2). C7: the AMM and GMMPS-type polarizations differ by a polynomial with no gamma^0 term, so in GMMPS's F_S the only k^0 term is b_0 (alpha~^S_1).

later_literature.what: The S equation (3.16) carries a local k^0 term alpha~^S_1 m^4 h^S. Thm 3.6 fixes alpha~^S_1 = 1/(64pi^2) by general local covariance plus perturbative agreement, after the background fixes alpha_1 (the cosmological-constant role, p. 22). Sec. 5.2.1 attributes the difference from AMM to 'the choice of the renormalisation parameters done in Theorem 3.6'. This contests AMM's renormalisation condition, not AMM's algebra. Not adjudicated here.

Holographic (strongly coupled CFT) semiclassical gravity; cites AMM as [9]. Non-negative powers of m^2 are absorbed into alpha_i. The perturbed Minkowski equations are proportional to m^2 on both sides ((4.25); p. 12), so there is no k-independent term, the same structure as AMM (4.5). In d = 4 Minkowski is unstable for gamma_4 >= gamma_4*. The matter content is different, so this does not test AMM's scalar result.

gr-qc/0209075#renorm-4.4.lacked_data: In 2002 AMM had the Kallen-Lehmann representation, explicit rho^(T) and rho^(S) (B37, agreeing with their refs [28] and [29]), and already knew of Lambda > 0 (p. 2: it 'may be taken to be zero in some applications'). The result uses no measured datum: it is a scheme plus an identity, re-derived exactly here (C1-C3), so no new datum can move it. That is the evidence against M's hypothesis for this key. What came later is a theoretical principle, not data. GMMPS 2026 apply general local covariance plus perturbative agreement and fix the k^0 coefficient to be nonzero (alpha~^S_1 = 1/(64pi^2)); AMM's identification at k^2 = 0 sets it to zero. That is the evidence that later knowledge bears on it: the split falls exactly on the k^0 term this key describes (C7). It is a dispute over renormalisation conditions, not missing data, and it is not adjudicated here.
gr-qc/0209075#renorm-4.4.grade_evidence: The source was READ at alphaXiv p. 11. The tree's quotation at linstab.py:106-110 is word for word, and both (4.5a) and (4.5b) carry an overall k^2. The re-derivation passes 20 of 20 checks: the (4.4) identity is exact, and F^(T) and F^(S) are O(k^2), so E(0) = 0 identically for every m > 0 and xi tested. B44, (4.9), (4.10) and (4.11) are reproduced. No datum enters. The tree's step 'AMM's scheme = alpha~^S_1 = 0' is corroborated at order k^0 (C7), which is the only order its dependents use. The drifts are framing and scope: 'choice' leaves out A1 and AMM's identification of the k^0 coefficient with Lambda; m > 0 is held in the SETTING rather than in H4; the equivalence holds only at k^0. None of them changes a conclusion the tree draws. GMMPS 2026 contest the renormalisation condition, and the tree already marks that not adjudicated (linstab.py:181-183, SPLIT_ADJUDICATED_HERE = False at linstab.py:353). This grade covers AMM's description of its own scheme. Which scheme is physically right is OPEN and is not graded here.
gr-qc/0209075#renorm-4.4.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if some dependent is found to use 'AMM's scheme = alpha~^S_1 = 0' beyond order k^0 (C7 shows AMM also differs at order gamma and gamma^2), or to treat the missing k^0 term as independent of A1 and AMM's flat-background identification. A shown result that covariance forces a nonzero k^0 coefficient in the gauge-invariant scalar response would make AMM's condition inconsistent rather than just different: that would reopen the split (OPEN or DATA-DEPENDENT there). No source read here shows it. WRONG only if the (4.4) identity or the O(k^2) vanishing of F^(i) failed, and C1-C3 rule that out.

implicit-function-theorem.name: Implicit function theorem (local existence/sign of the branch root through gamma = 0)

source.located: Classical theorem: Cauchy (analytic case, first rigorous proof) and U. Dini (real variables, 1876; Lezioni di Analisi Infinitesimale vol. 1, Pisa 1907, pp. 197-241); no arXiv copy of either. Exact modern statement read in O. R. B. de Oliveira, 'The implicit and the inverse function theorems: easy proofs', arXiv:1212.2066v1 (2012), Theorem 1 (one equation, p. 5) and Theorem 2 (system, pp. 6-7). The function the tree applies it to was read at source in GMMPS arXiv:2604.01047v1: (4.17)-(4.18) p. 48, Thm 4.16 p. 58, (5.1)-(5.3) pp. 59-60, 5.3 p. 62.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text: 1212.2066 pp. 1-10 in full; 2604.01047 pp. 1, 33, 40, 48-52, 58-60, 62. Cauchy and Dini are NAMED-NOT-READ (restated in 1212.2066). Krantz-Parks (2002) is NAMED-NOT-READ; 1212.2066 p. 2 restates that the Krantz-Parks induction proof 'does not establish the local uniqueness of the implicit solution'.

implicit-function-theorem.published_statement: de Oliveira 1212.2066 Theorem 1 (p. 5): 'Let F : Omega -> R be of class C^1 in an open set Omega inside R^n x R and (a, b) be a point in Omega such that F(a, b) = 0 and dF/dy(a, b) > 0. Then, there exist an open set X, inside R^n and containing a, and an open set Y, inside R and containing b, satisfying the following. For each x in X there is a unique y = f(x) in Y such that F(x, f(x)) = 0. We have f(a) = b. Moreover, f : X -> Y is of class C^1 and df/dx_j(x) = -F_{x_j}(x, f(x)) / F_y(x, f(x)).' Theorem 2 (pp. 6-7) is the same statement for F in C^1(Omega; R^m) with dF/dy(a, b) invertible. For m = 1 the sign condition > 0 in Theorem 1 loses nothing, since F can be replaced by -F.
published_hypotheses: H1 Omega open in R^n x R (here n = 1: x = alpha~^S_1, y = gamma)
H2 F of class C^1 on Omega
H3 F(a, b) = 0 at the base point
H4 dF/dy(a, b) != 0 (stated as > 0 in Theorem 1; invertible in Theorem 2)
THE CONCLUSION IS LOCAL: X and Y exist but have no stated size; uniqueness holds only inside Y; the theorem says nothing about zeros outside Y or about complex zeros
hypothesis_drift: H2 IS STRENGTHENED AND SATISFIED (linstab.py:959-960, 'F_S smooth near (0,0)'). Smooth implies C^1. This was checked, not assumed: F_S is affine in alpha (R4), and J is real-analytic on (-inf, 4m^2) (GMMPS (4.18) excludes only [4m^2, inf)). J(0), J'(0) and J''(0) are finite (R1). In effect there is no drift.

H4 IS KEPT, BUT THE APPLICATION USES CONDITIONS IT DOES NOT STATE (linstab.py:959-960). F_S'(0)(1-6xi)^2 kappa = 12 + kappa m^2/(24 pi^2) was re-derived. For this to be > 0 you need kappa > 0, m > 0 and xi != 1/6. z3 proves positivity under exactly those conditions, and a control shows kappa < 0 can flip the sign. m > 0 is stated at linstab.py:122. kappa > 0 and xi != 1/6 are left implicit (at xi = 1/6, F_S is undefined). All three hold in GMMPS's setting, so they are named here, not counted as dropped.

A WORDING DISCREPANCY IN THE CONCLUSION, NOT A REFUTATION (linstab.py:165-166, 345-346, 367-369; LEDGER.md:49). The tree says the branch zero 'exists iff alpha~^S_1 != 0'. The IFT actually gives a branch zero f(alpha) for every alpha in X, alpha = 0 included, with f(0) = 0. What follows from the IFT together with F_S(alpha,0) = -b_0 is that the branch zero is NONZERO iff alpha != 0 (R4, R5). The tree itself records gamma = 0 as an exact root at alpha = 0 (linstab.py:168-169, 961), so the meaning it intends is the accurate one; the literal word 'exists' is not accurate.

LOCALITY IS KEPT (linstab.py:164, 346-347, 367). To get from 'alpha near 0' to the physical alpha = 1/(64 pi^2), the tree uses an intermediate-value bracket at |b_2| <= 1e100 (linstab.py:636-661, 973-976), not the IFT. Measured here (R8): at GMMPS's point the IFT branch reaches the physical alpha iff b_2 >= -B*, with B* = F_1^2/(4 F_0) = 8.62e120 in m = 1 units. This holds for xi = 0 and for xi = 1/3; the two values coincide because B* scales as 1/(6(1/6 - xi)^2). Every b_2 > 0 is covered, and the tree's 1e100 bracket lies inside B*.

THE WORD 'grows' ADDS A DEPENDENCE, NAMED HERE (linstab.py:166, 963). The IFT gives only the SIGN of the root: f'(0) = -2 kappa m^4/(1 + kappa m^2/(288 pi^2)) < 0. Because F_S is affine in alpha, f is nonzero everywhere on X except at 0, so the sign is constant on each side of 0 throughout X, not just to first order. That a negative root is a growing mode is a separate result: GMMPS's pole term in (4.31) and Thm 4.16 (p. 58). The simple-zero condition that pole term needs is supplied by F_gamma != 0 along the branch.

THE SCOPE OF UNIQUENESS IS KEPT (linstab.py:173-180). The tree does not claim the 'only if' for growth in general. An extension computed here (R6): the winding number on |gamma| = 0.2 is 1, so there is exactly one zero in that complex disk and no complex-conjugate pair near the branch.

ADJACENT, NOT THIS KEY (belongs to the GMMPS Thm 4.16 entry). linstab.py:136 and 190 paraphrase Thm 4.16's growth clause as '(for Z strictly inside (-4m^2, 0))'. At source (p. 58) that interval belongs to the DECAY clause; the GROWTH clause reads 'Z subset (-4m^2, inf), with some gamma in Z, gamma > 0', in Q's variable. The tree's conclusion that the alpha = 0 root lies outside Thm 4.16 still holds under the source's own wording.

The evidence: every check of its application here (R2-R4, R6) is symbolic and exact. What the classical statement does lack is a size for X and Y. For this application that size was computed here: the neighbourhood reaches the physical alpha = 1/(64 pi^2) iff b_2 >= -8.6e120 (m = 1 units), and the tree's bracket lies inside it. The data the application uses were moved and do not move the conclusion (R9): alpha~^S_1 (contested between GMMPS and AMM), Lambda and H0 (the Planck vs distance-ladder tension). The contested alpha~^S_1 only decides which side of the conditional applies, and the tree leaves that open. M's hypothesis finds nothing here.

'LOCALLY' is kept at every use, and the 'only if' for growth in general is not claimed. The IFT slope reproduces the tree's first-order formula exactly and does not depend on xi. The sign holds on all of X, not only to first order. The numerics agree (27/27 PASS), and no moved datum moves the conclusion. planck-scale-validity-limit.published_statement: Burgess gr-qc/0311082 p.4: predictions 'must be made within the context of a low-energy expansion, in powers of E/M ... What plays the role of the heavy scale M in the case of quantum gravity? It is tempting to identify this scale with the Planck mass, M_p^-2 = 8 pi G ..., and in some circumstances this is the right choice. But as we shall see M need not be M_p'. p.25-26: amplitudes suppressed by (E/M_p)^2, and by (E/4 pi M_p)^2 per loop; 'the weakness of the graviton's coupling follows only from the low-energy approximations, E << M_p and E << m'. p.35: validity needs the wavelength 'very small compared with the local radius of curvature'. p.46: leading quantum corrections 'controlled by the ratio l_p^2/r^2, where l_p = (G hbar/c^3)^1/2 ~ 1e-35 m ... At face value it is only for separations comparable to the Planck length that quantum gravity effects become important.' Garay gr-qc/9403008, abstract: 'The existence of a fundamental scale, a lower bound to any output of a position measurement, seems to be a model-independent feature of quantum gravity'. p.2: 'we set hbar = c = 1, so that the only dimensional constant is Planck's length l_* = sqrt(G); also, irrelevant numerical factors are ignored' ... 'the distance between two events will have a minimum uncertainty of the order of Planck's length. This conclusion, which has been reached by means of rather crude arguments'. p.3 (Mead, restated): Delta x >~ max(1/Delta p, l_*^2 Delta p) >~ l_*. p.4: 'these uncertainty relations are low-energy approximations to what the full theory of quantum gravity would give'. p.17: 'notions ... based on a metric structure lose their meaning at the Planck's scale'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Burgess): GR plus matter is treated as a low-energy EFT. The control parameter is (E/M)^2, where M is the lightest heavy scale integrated out. M = M_p (reduced, M_p^-2 = 8 pi G) holds only 'in some circumstances'; M 'need not be M_p'.
H2 (Burgess p.35-38): short-wavelength modes are much shorter than the local curvature radius; backgrounds vary slowly ('nice slice'); time-dependent backgrounds need adiabatic vacua.
H3 (Burgess p.49-50): all-orders power counting is NOT demonstrated for general curved spaces. The breakdown scale is an estimate, 'not in serious doubt' but not proved.

H4 (Garay p.2-4): quantum mechanics, special relativity and GR are combined through thought experiments; numerical factors of order one are ignored; the bound is 'of the order of' l_*, from 'rather crude arguments' that are themselves low-energy approximations.
H5 (Garay abstract, p.17): 'seems to be a model-independent feature'. This is a claim about approaches to quantum gravity, not a measured fact; no datum at the Planck scale is used.

planck-scale-validity-limit.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. What the authors had: hbar, c and G, dimensional analysis, and thought experiments (Mead 1964 as Garay restates it; Burgess's power counting). What they lacked, and what no one has yet: any measurement at or near l_P. The location of the breakdown is an extrapolation by construction (Garay p.2, 'rather crude arguments'; Burgess p.49-50, curved-space power counting 'not yet given'). The only numerical input that could have moved, G, has not moved (CODATA 2018 = 2022), and it cannot move the crossovers in Planck units at all, because R/l_P depends only on Lambda. Evidence on the missing datum, in each direction: (a) toward a LOWER breakdown energy (larger length): Burgess p.4, 'M need not be M_p'. If so, the tree's sub-Planckian crossovers sit even further outside the framework and the refusal gets stronger. (b) toward NO breakdown (a UV completion within QFT): not read here because the later-literature search was unavailable, so this direction is OPEN. So the authors did lack data, and the gap is real and will not close soon. None of the data that can be obtained moves the tree's conclusion. The datum that cannot be obtained could move only the words 'outside the domain of the theory' and 'exactly', not the rough location of the crossovers.
planck-scale-validity-limit.grade_evidence: As published (Burgess gr-qc/0311082 p.4, 25-27, 46; Garay gr-qc/9403008 p.2-4, 17), the extrapolation says semiclassical GR+QFT is expected to lose control at separations 'comparable to' or 'of the order of' l_P. Numerical factors are ignored, the scale M 'need not be M_p', and the curved-space power counting is not demonstrated. The tree's crossover_is_sub_planckian holds in every Planck convention tried, and at the crossovers the required curvature is itself at the Planck scale (l_P^2 G rho/c^4 = 1.056 and 0.732). So the tree's central claim STANDS to within an order-one factor: the Ford-Roman and Casimir crossovers lie where the framework cannot be trusted. The grade is NARROWED for four reasons. (i) The tree uses a sharp boundary and a band test [0.1, 10] that depend on a convention it never names. Under the reduced Planck length Burgess uses, two of the three crossovers fall outside the band (0.0614 and 0.0738), and the z3 window [26.46, 2513] excludes Lambda = 9.98. (ii) It says 'exactly where', while the sources say 'of the order of' and 'need not be M_p'. (iii) It states the boundary with no status word, though the sources call it an estimate. (iv) It rules out an EFT cutoff at a few l_P, where Fliss et al. treat a Planckian cutoff as inside the EFT; their own condition |8 pi G xi phi^2| = 2.518 xi at the tree's cutoff rules it out only for xi >~ 0.40. No datum has moved (G and l_P are unchanged in CODATA 2022). This is not WRONG: nothing here refutes the tree's structural finding, and the spread of 10.26 is exact whatever Lambda is.

fewster-teo-sec7-candelas-schwarzschild.published_statement: Not quoted from source in this stage. As transcribed by the tree's DOCKET 62 read and not re-read here: F&T Sec. 7 evaluates their static-spacetime bound (2.12) for a massless, minimally coupled scalar in the Boulware (static) vacuum, on the Schwarzschild exterior r > 2M, for a static observer. It uses Candelas' asymptotic mode sums (7.4)/(7.5), which split the modes into outgoing ('up', from the past horizon) and ingoing ('in', from past null infinity) families, with greybody (horizon transmission) coefficients B_l(w) in (7.6). Proper time enters through (7.7), tau_0 = |g_tt|^{1/2} t_0. The bound (7.8) has a (1-2M/r)^{-1} pole and goes arbitrarily negative at the horizon. (7.10) is the comparison form, stated to lie 'between 9/64 and 1/4' of Pfenning & Ford's Schwarzschild bound, because its (tau_0/r)^2 coefficients are 16/9 of Pfenning-Ford's. gr-qc/9406053#escapes.published_statement:
Sec. IX: 'Their true value is not so much that they actually rule out topology change, but rather that they allow us to pinpoint what modifications we have to make in our general framework so as to allow it. A popular modification ... is to abandon the Lorentzian framework altogether and to use a Euclidean path integral formalism. But even within the general Lorentzian framework there are still several interesting possibilities.'

A] Dropping causal compactness: Tipler Thm 5 '(in the closed universe case) ... if topology change occurs via a non-compact interpolating spacetime, then it contains (under some mild additional assumptions) a singularity (in the sense of an incomplete timelike geodesic) or a point at infinity'. A singularity specifically follows 'only under the significant additional assumption' of an upper bound on timelike lengths. 'The presence of points at infinity is still a highly undesirable feature.'

B] Weakening the curvature constraints: 'This would not affect the presence of causality violations, but it might permit topology change as a dynamical process.' Either alter Einstein's equation ('such an alteration would have to be fairly severe'), or allow 'violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are, for example, based precisely on large violations of the energy condition.'

C] Degenerate metrics: 'allow the metric to vanish or to become degenerate at isolated points and to use these kinds of singularities in order to get topology change ... even in standard general relativity (couched in first-order language) Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed. So, this might well prove to be the correct approach to describing topology change.' Borde adds that the usual causal structure 'will not necessarily be well-defined'.

Sec. VIII: 'If we were satisfied with metrics that are only continuous ... S1 and S2 need not be diffeomorphic, even if causality violations are forbidden.'
published_hypotheses: Borde's list is framed as non-exhaustive: 'several interesting possibilities' inside the Lorentzian framework, plus the Euclidean route outside it. The routes are offered as modifications that 'allow' topology change, not as a proof that every way out fails.

Every escape is measured against the paper's framework: a smooth, non-degenerate, time-oriented Lorentz metric on a causally compact interpolating manifold. 'All of these comments are valid only under the assumptions of this paper.'

A] rests on Tipler Thm 5: closed-universe case, non-compact interpolant, 'mild additional assumptions'. The conclusion is a singularity OR a point at infinity. A singularity specifically needs an upper bound on timelike lengths, and Yodzis shows a conformal rescaling can push it to infinity.

B] keeps causal compactness, so Theorem 1's causality violation remains. B has two sub-routes: (1) alter Einstein's equation ('fairly severe'); (2) keep Einstein's equation and violate the energy conditions enough to break Theorem 3's assumption (ii).

C] allows the metric to degenerate at isolated points ('these kinds of singularities'). Borde places C 'within the general Lorentzian framework', cites Horowitz doing it in first-order standard GR, and notes the usual causal structure is not necessarily well-defined there.
'Singularity' means the standard incomplete-geodesic definition.

em-stress-energy-energy-conditions.published_statement: Energy conditions, as Fewster 1208.5399 p.4 restates Hawking-Ellis. WEC: T_ab u^a u^b >= 0 for all timelike u. NEC: the same for all null u. DEC: T_ab u^a v^b >= 0 for all future-pointing timelike u and v, so every observer sees a causal energy-momentum flux. SEC: T_ab u^a u^b - (1/2) T g_ab u^a u^b >= 0. The classical electromagnetic field obeys WEC and DEC (p.6: 'DEC also holds ... and the same is true for the electromagnetic field'), and NEC follows. The same source records that the QUANTIZED EM field violates WEC between Casimir plates (p.9), and that QFT violates all the classical pointwise conditions (abstract).
published_hypotheses: H1 classical field: T_ab is the classical Maxwell tensor F_ac F_b^c - (1/4) g_ab F^2. Fewster's p.6 statement sits among the classical-field examples, and his p.1 and p.9 say the quantized field violates WEC.
H2 linear (Maxwell) Lagrangian -F. The Casimir argument on p.9 depends on the EM stress tensor being conformally invariant (traceless).
H3 the conditions are pointwise statements about the EM stress-energy ALONE. The matter that sources or confines the field has its own T_ab and is not covered.

H4 (definitional) WEC/NEC/DEC as stated for an arbitrary T_ab. The eigenvalue forms rho >= 0, rho + p_i >= 0 and rho >= |p_i| apply to Hawking-Ellis type I only. That is standard, but it is not quoted in the restatement read here; it is re-derived below, by z3 for WEC/NEC and numerically for DEC.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/em-stress-energy-energy-conditions.out). Part A (sympy, exact, every F_ab): T_00 = (E^2+B^2)/2, |T_0i| = |ExB|, trace 0, and the identity T_00^2 - |T_0i|^2 = ((E^2-B^2)^2 + 4(E.B)^2)/4 >= 0. Because the identity holds for all E and B, it holds in every frame, which gives WEC and DEC for every classical field and NEC by limit. 12,000 random (F,u,v) give T_ab u^a v^b >= 0. The characteristic polynomial of T^a_b is (lam^2 - L^2)^2, which is em_is_ordinary's eigenstructure. The null field is nilpotent (type II) and passes NEC on 2,000 random null k. Part A6 (z3): the definitional WEC/NEC are equivalent to charge.py's algebraic forms for type I (the negation is unsat; the vacuity guard passes). The type-I DEC form agrees with the flux definition on 300 random cases. Part B (sympy, general L(F)): T_ab k^a k^b = -L_F w.w with w.w >= 0, so NEC holds iff L_F <= 0. For pure B: rho = -L, p_par = L, p_perp = L - B^2 L_F. Part C (mpmath): the proper-time one-loop EH form was NOT read at source. It was used only after it reproduced the weak-field coefficient (ratio 0.99994) and the strong-field leading log (ratio 0.99942). At B/B_crit = 1, 22.65 (1e11 T), 226.5, 1e4 and 1e8, L_F = -0.99993, -0.99877, -0.99716, -0.99425 and -0.98712, and rho > 0 with a positive DEC margin throughout. The leading-log NEC boundary is at ln(B/B_crit) of about 1291 (the Landau-pole scale). My first draft had an index-placement bug in w.k; it failed its check and was fixed before the recorded run.

em-stress-energy-energy-conditions.lacked_data: The published result is a THEOREM about the classical Maxwell tensor. Its conclusion uses no measured number, so no datum can move it; it is re-derived here exactly for every F_ab. What the 1973 statement leaves unsaid is its domain. (i) Fields above B_crit = 4.414e9 T: magnetar fields near 1e11 T came after 1973 (that history is not read here), and above B_crit the QED effective Lagrangian replaces the linear one. Within one-loop Euler-Heisenberg (form not read at source, but internally consistent), NEC, WEC and DEC still hold at the tree's 1e11 T with L_F = -0.99877, and the sign change is at ln(B/B_crit) of about 1291. So the strong-field data does NOT change the conclusion for any field the tree names. (ii) Quantum states and conducting boundaries do violate the pointwise conditions (Casimir, READ in Fewster p.9). That was known in theory before 1973, so it is not data the authors lacked. It is a hypothesis the tree drops. Net: no evidence that the authors' data were inaccurate or incomplete in a way that moves this result.

For every classical Maxwell field, T_00 >= 0 and T_00^2 - |S|^2 = ((E^2-B^2)^2 + 4(E.B)^2)/4 >= 0 in every frame, so WEC, DEC and NEC hold (sympy identity plus 12,000 numeric cases). charge.py's definitions agree with the ones read at source (z3). Nothing in the result is WRONG and no datum moves it. The grade is NARROWED because the tree applies it to a larger class than it covers. (1) spec.py:190 DOES[1] and specthm SR1 claim NEC/WEC/DEC 'everywhere' for a positive-MASS lens, but the only check cited, spec.py:305 calling charge.em_is_ordinary() (charge.py:155-162), is a constant about EM stress-energy, not lens matter. (2) The tree drops the 'classical field' hypothesis, although the source read here records WEC violation by the quantized EM field (p.9). (3) The tree drops 'EM stress-energy alone': spec.py:99-101's 'everywhere' for a sustained field includes the confining matter, which faces 3.98e27 Pa at 1e11 T. The drop of 'linear Maxwell' at 22.7 B_crit was computed not to move the conclusion within one-loop QED, conditional on an unread EH form. The narrowing is in how the tree uses the result. The tree's lensing conclusion is not shown false; it is shown to be unsupported by this particular check.

gr-hyperbolicity-causal-propagation.published_statement: Low gr-qc/9812067, restating Wald Ch.10 and Hawking-Ellis Ch.7. Thm 2.4 takes an initial data set (Sigma,h,K,J,rho) whose matter u obeys a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system A^a nabla_a u + B u = c (eq. 2.2), with T depending only on u and g. It then states: (1) there is a unique smooth maximal development, globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface i(Sigma); (2) if two data sets agree on S, then D(i(S)) is isometric in the two developments; (3) g depends continuously on the data. Cor 3.1/4.1: if the data change only inside K = J^+(p) cap Sigma, D(i(Sigma\K)) stays isometric, and 'no gravitational influence propagates faster than light'. Sec.4: with ray cones inside the light cones, 'one cannot construct a warp drive which has the effect of making it possible to travel faster than light'. Thm 4.2 adds the DEC: 'In the absence of exotic matter, it is impossible to construct a warp-drive.' Kontou-Sanders p.12: a symmetric-hyperbolic Einstein-matter system has a unique maximal globally hyperbolic solution depending continuously on the data, and no energy condition is needed on T_ab. T_ab = 0 on O subset Sigma implies T_ab = 0 on D(O).

gr-hyperbolicity-causal-propagation.lacked_data: The result is a theorem, and no measured number enters it; only the matter model's principal part (H2) does. The authors lacked a measurement of the speed of gravity. GW170817 supplied it in 2017, -3e-15 <= (v_gw-c)/c <= 7e-16, which confirms speed c and moves the tree's floor by less than 1e-14 (C8). That is evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result. They also lacked any established model of the exotic matter the corridor needs, and that is still missing. Classical exotic fields with a causal principal part leave the theorem unchanged (C7). For quantum sources, well-posedness is not established (2604.01047). A superluminal matter sector would lower the floor (C6). So the missing data do not overturn the theorem, but whether H2 holds for whatever would actually build the corridor is still OPEN. The later correction on the DEC (Earman, Geroch, Wong) applies to Low's Thm 4.2 step, which the tree does not use.

linearised-weak-field-metric.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 ch.6: in harmonic gauge, Box hbar_mu_nu = -16 pi G T_mu_nu (6.22). 'it is straightforward to derive the weak-field metric for a stationary spherical source such as a planet or star ... h_00 = -2Phi (6.24), where Phi is the conventional Newtonian potential, Phi = -GM/r. gr-qc/9304008.published_statement: v1 p.5, quoted verbatim from the text layer: 'We propose that the extent to which the semiclassical approximation is violated can be measured by the dimensionless quantity Delta_{abmn}(x,y) = |(<:T_ab(x)T_mn(y):> - <:T_ab(x):><:T_mn(y):>)/<:T_ab(x)T_mn(y):>|. (3.1) ... If its components are always small compared to unity, then these fluctuations are small and we expect the semiclassical theory to hold. ... For simplicity, we will concentrate upon the coincidence limit, x -> y, of the purely temporal component ... Delta(x) = |(<:T00^2(x):> - <:T00(x):>^2)/<:T00^2(x):>|. (3.2) The local energy density fluctuations are small when Delta << 1, which we take to be a measure of the validity of the semiclassical theory. Note that we have used normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state to define the various operators.' p.11-12: (3.43) Delta' = (<:T00^2:> - rho^2)/rho^2 = (1/8)[(rho+xi1+xi2+xi3)^2 + ...]; (3.44) Delta' = Delta/(1-Delta), Delta = Delta'/(1+Delta'). Sec. V: curved space 'will require a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such spacetimes, which has not yet been developed'; averaging 'introduces an arbitrary length or time scale'.
published_hypotheses: H1 PROPOSAL, not derivation: 'We propose that the extent to which the semiclassical approximation is violated can be measured by' Delta. It is motivated by Ford (1982) on graviton emission. No theorem bounds the error of G = 8 pi G <T> by Delta.
H2 The full measure is (3.1): all components, at two points x and y. The theory is expected to hold 'if its components are always small', which is a sufficiency-type expectation.
H3 Delta(x) in (3.2) is a reduction of (3.1) made 'for simplicity': the coincidence limit and the 00 component only.
H4 Every operator, including the quartic :T00^2:, is normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, on a flat spacetime background.
H5 (3.2) has an absolute value. (3.44) tacitly assumes <:T00^2:> >= rho^2 and <:T00^2:> > 0.

H6 The examples use a massless scalar in flat spacetime, in single-mode number-state superpositions, squeezed states and the Casimir vacuum. The Casimir bound (3.45) assumes a diagonal <:d_A phi d_B phi:> and the Wick condition phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0 (vacua).

gr-qc/9304008.lacked_data:
The result is a definition plus a proposed criterion, with no empirical input. No measured datum was lacking and none has moved. What KF lacked in 1993 was theory, and they said so themselves.
(a) Curved-space renormalisation of quartic products. Perez & Sudarsky (2026) have since supplied it by the OPE. They find squeezed vacua fail the criterion and agree 'in general lines' with KF. This is evidence that having it does not overturn KF's qualitative conclusion.
(b) A principled averaging scale. The tree says the corridor has its own (fluctuation.py:110-113).
(c) A derivation of Delta as the actual error of G = 8 pi G <T>. None has appeared. Instead the criterion was refined by back-reaction stability (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer 2004, citing Hu-Phillips) or replaced by linear response (Anderson et al. 2002), under which flat space is stable although its Gaussian states have Delta of order 1.
That supports M's suspicion in one narrow sense: the validity criterion is incomplete. It ignores back reaction, and it is sign-blind, condemning thermal radiation at Delta = 2/5 (C7). It is no evidence that the definition or any flat-space value is wrong. Every internal identity checks exactly (C1, C4, C5), and the printed discrepancies are algebra or typography against v1, not missing data.

The definition stands exactly as READ. (3.2), its Minkowski normal ordering, its 00 coincidence reduction, (3.44), the coherent-state zero, and the Gaussian, Casimir and thermal values all re-derive (24/24).
It is NARROWED against the tree's use on two counts, each shown here:
(1) The tree drops the absolute value of (3.2). Its closed form 1 - rho^2/<:T^2:> (fluctuation.py:39, 230, 237, 281) is KF's Delta only where <:T00^2:> >= rho^2, and that fails in KF's own vac+2 state at rho > 0 (+0.9428 vs -0.9428, C2d-e; the case is reachable, C3c). The absolute value is inactive on rho < 0 (C3a-b) and on every zero-mean Gaussian state (C5c). So T1, T2, the Casimir 6/7, the thermal 2/5 and KF_CLAIM_NEGATIVE_MEANS_DELTA_GT_1 = False all stand (C3d).
(2) The tree states a stronger status than the source gives. KF propose Delta as 'a measure' for the reduced component of (3.1). 'Semiclassical gravity's error term is Delta' (fluctuation.py:101-102) and 'Kuo & Ford's measure of that equation's error' (ledger.py:751-752) upgrade it. gr-qc/9304008-quartic-renormalisation.published_statement: KF gr-qc/9304008 v1 Sec. V, verbatim from the saved excerpt: 'The analysis in this paper was restricted to a flat spacetime background. In this case, the expectation values of quartic operators which appear in the dimensionless measure of the fluctuations, Delta, or in the Langevin equation, Eq.(4.27), may be defined in terms of normal ordered products. nuclear-saturation-density.lacked_data: M's hypothesis was tested here. Because the tree cites no source, what the original authors had cannot be attributed, and the history of the datum was not read. The data that came later is parity-violating electron scattering (PREX/PREX-2, 2020-21), which measured the weak-charge (neutron) density. The snippet values of 0.148-0.150 fm^-3 sit 6-8% below 0.16. This is data the earlier analyses lacked. Evidence that it does not change the conclusion: the conclusion is linear in n0 and stays over threshold for any n0 above 1.4e-3 fm^-3, a margin of more than 100x, so 398x and 114x become about 368x and 106x. The discrepancies that were found are in the tree, not in outside physics. First, the 'everywhere there is a nucleus' figures are heavy-nucleus figures: light nuclei, whose sizes CODATA measures, have mean densities of 0.14-0.59 n0. Second, the tree carries two inconsistent constants, 2.676e17 and 2.3e17. Third, under H2 the literal 'two orders' fails at the tree's own 2.3e17. None of these comes from earlier physicists lacking data.
nuclear-saturation-density.grade_evidence: Computed in the rederive script (exit 0). The verdict the datum carries is that ordinary nuclear matter displaces the vev beyond eps_det. It holds for every plausible n0: the break-even values, 4.0e-4 and 1.4e-3 fm^-3, are more than 100x below any quoted value. It also holds for every nucleus tested with CODATA 2022 radii; the lowest is the deuteron at 57x (H1) and 16.5x (H2). So the grade is neither DATA-DEPENDENT nor WRONG. It is not STANDS because the tree uses the datum on a wider class than it holds for. address.py:191-196 applies '398 or 114 TIMES ... everywhere there is a nucleus' and 'two orders over threshold' to every nucleus, against its own coarse-grained-mean hypothesis at :297-303. The deuteron's mean density is 0.14 n0 and alpha's is 0.59 n0, so those figures hold for heavy-nucleus interiors only. Under H2, 'two orders' is literally true only for n0 >= 0.1401. One discrepancy is recorded and not repaired: the tree's two constants, 2.676e17 and 2.3e17, differ by 16%. n0 itself was not read at source, so the grade is built on a parameter scan and on CODATA radii.

1407.0164.published_statement: Abstract p.1: 'The absolute frequencies of both transitions are also presented, each with a relative standard uncertainty of 6 x 10^-16 ... mu-dot/mu = 0.2(1.1) x 10^-16 year^-1 ... alpha-dot/alpha = -0.7(2.1) x 10^-17 year^-1.' p.1: 'the first direct measurement of the ratio between the E3 and E2 optical transition frequencies in 171Yb+, with fractional uncertainty 3 x 10^-16.' p.1: absolute frequencies 'are now limited by Cs primary standards.' p.3: 'nu_E3/nu_E2 = 0.932 829 404 530 964 65(31)'. The Table I totals (x1e-16) are E2 6.13, E3 5.79 and ratio 3.36. p.4: 'r-dot/r = (A_1 - A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1 - B_2) mu-dot/mu. The sensitivity coefficients A_i ... are: A_E3 = -5.95 [34], A_E2 = 0.88 [35], and A_Cs = 2.83 [36]. Dependence on mu-dot arises through the nuclear magnetic moment and is negligible for optical transitions (the sensitivity coefficient B_E3 = B_E2 = 0). As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38], an AFM history can also be interpreted to set constraints on mu-dot/mu (B_Cs = -1).' Also p.4: mu = m_p/m_e, and the limits hold 'on the assumption of local position invariance and that any time-variation is linear'.
published_hypotheses: H-MU: mu = m_p/m_e (p.4).
H-LIN: frequencies respond linearly to the constants, r-dot/r = (A_1-A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1-B_2) mu-dot/mu (p.4). This is a power-law dependence alpha^A mu^B.
H-AOPT: A_E3 = -5.95, A_E2 = 0.88 and A_Cs = 2.83 are atomic-structure calculations taken from refs [34]-[36] (1999-2008). They are not measured in this paper.
H-BOPT: B_E3 = B_E2 = 0 because an optical transition's mu-dependence 'is negligible' (p.4). This is an approximation, not an identity.
H-GCS: B_Cs = -1 rests on the premise that 'the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38]' (p.4).
H-LPI: the mu-dot and alpha-dot limits assume local position invariance and linear time variation (p.4).

H-BUDGET: the 3e-16 and 6e-16 are the Table I totals (3.36, 6.13 and 5.79 x1e-16), from the systematics plus statistics over 105 h (E2) and 81 h (E3) in Feb-Mar 2014. gauss-law-closed-universe-zero-charge.published_statement: This was not read at source. Search-summary wording, which is NAMED-NOT-READ and is not quoted as source: 'On a compact space the total electric charge must be zero. This is a consequence of the Gauss constraint.' Read verbatim in arXiv:2503.18963v1 p.7: 'In the extended Reissner-Nordstrom geometry, the total charge can be similarly calculated as an integral on a two-surface at infinity. After applying Stokes' theorem, the resulting integrand d*F ... vanishes identically ... The charge is nowhere to be localized!' The mathematical content re-derived here: on a compact Riemannian 3-manifold without boundary, the integral of div E over dV is 0 for a globally defined E. With div E = rho (massless U(1), untwisted bundle), the integral of rho over dV is 0.
published_hypotheses: H1: the spatial slice is compact without boundary. This means compactness, not positive curvature, so the flat T^3 qualifies.
H2: the Maxwell (massless-photon, exact U(1)) Gauss constraint div E = rho holds on the whole slice.
H3: E is a single-valued global section of the untwisted bundle, with no charge-conjugation holonomy.
H4: 'total charge' means the source integral of rho over dV, not the flux through a non-bounding 2-cycle. That flux can be nonzero (charge without charge).

Not required (checked by hand, and point charges numerically in D3): smooth rho, since point charges are handled distributionally. Absence of monopoles, since div B = rho_m also integrates to zero and a theta term adds theta*div B, which integrates to zero too. Orientability, since the divergence theorem is stated with a density.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 (massless photon) at permute.py:126-130, :337-340, :344 and :560-563, which say only 'Gauss's law'. Under a Proca photon mass, a uniform net charge on T^3 is an exact solution: A0 = rho0/m^2 and E = 0 (D5).

OVERSTATED at permute.py:130 ('Not approximately, not by observation -- FORCED, by topology') and :562. The conclusion also needs m_gamma = 0. Observation bounds the photon mass below 1e-18 eV but cannot establish zero.

DROPPED H3 (untwisted bundle) at permute.py:338-339. A C-antiperiodic E on a compact boundaryless space carries net charge q (D6). z3 finds total charge 2 on a C-twisted lattice (D7). This is the mechanism of C* boundary conditions (Lucini et al. arXiv:1509.01636, NAMED-NOT-READ).
H4 is implicit and consistent with the tree: pair.py:82-86 records charge without charge, and D4 confirms a zero source integral with flux Q.

magsail-drag-law.published_statement: Gros 2017 (READ): eq. (1) 'd/dt(m_tot v) = -(A(v) n_p v)(2 m_p v)' for fully reflected incoming particles. Eq. (8) 'A(v) = A_c [log(I/(beta I_c))]^3, v < (cI)/I_c', with A_c = 0.081 pi R^2 and I_c = 1.55e6 A, fitted to non-relativistic Lorentz-force trajectory integrations (eq. 4) 'over two orders of magnitude'. A(v) 'vanishes altogether when I < beta I_c'. Eq. (11) gives a finite stopping distance x_max = (1/0.081) log^-2(v0 I_c/(cI)) m_tot/(4 m_p n_p pi R^2), and eq. (19) at the optimal current gives x_max = 3.1 m_tot/(m_p n_p pi R^2). On Zubrin-Andrews, Gros writes that previous estimates 'have been rather on the optimistic side'; that a power-law area 'would be inconsistent with the existence of a critical current I_c'; and that Z-A's 159 kA at c/10 'would be right on the point where protons are not reflected at all'. Gros's restatement of the Z-A bow-shock pressure balance (eq. 31): n_p m_p v^2/2 = (2B)^2/(2 mu0) ~ 2 B0^2 R^6/(mu0 z^6), 'clearly only a rough estimate'.

magsail-drag-law.lacked_data: As far as READ here, Zubrin-Andrews lacked two things. First, particle-level simulations for the dilute limit. Gros 2017 supplied these and found a velocity-dependent area with a critical-current cutoff, 4x smaller than Andrews-Zubrin's at the same parameters; he calls the source of the difference 'unclear'. Second, the modern ion census (Crawford 2011: 0.05-0.21 cm^-3 locally, 0.005-0.04 in the Local Bubble). Does having that data change the conclusion? Evidence both ways. It does NOT overturn momentum braking: Gros still gets finite stopping distances and a feasible slow 1.5 t mission. It DOES change magnitudes: the tree's floor (constant A, n = 1, coefficient 1) is not a distance to rest. With Gros's law at the tree's own mass and speed, the stop takes 12,335 AU at n = 1 and about 123,000 AU (1.95 ly) at n_p = 0.1, against the printed 810 AU. At 0.87 c no source model applies at all, so the high-beta row is unsupported rather than refuted, and the tree's own verdict 'ISM braking is a low-beta technology' survives. The Z-A-versus-Gros difference is a live disagreement between models, not a refutation of Z-A, whose paper is unread here.
magsail-drag-law.grade_evidence: F = rho v^2 A (coefficient 1, constant A, total proton density) is a generic ram-drag form and is internally correct under its stated hypotheses. Its arithmetic reproduces (2001.638 AU), and its floor label is TRUE under its own constant-A hypothesis: the exact solution has no finite stop and the relativistic forms diverge too. The label is also true under the pressure-balance law, where the true distance is 3L. But every READ magsail law holds on a smaller class than the tree uses: the area depends on velocity, only ions count (0.05-0.21 cm^-3, not 1), full reflection carries a factor 2, and the physics is non-relativistic with A = 0 unless I > beta x 1.55e6 A. So the 0.87 c row is outside every source's domain. Under Gros's law the floor label depends on how A is read: it holds for the bare area (x_max = 6.17 L at a = 1) and fails for the initial effective area (x_max = 0.5 L at a = 1). Not WRONG: nothing published is refuted, and the tree's formula is not contradicted under its own hypotheses. The 810 AU / 2.6 ly prose figures are a tree-internal discrepancy, recorded and not graded. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the ion density has not moved since 2011 (the tree drops that hypothesis rather than using an outdated datum), and the Z-A-versus-Gros disagreement is not something the tree uses.
magsail-drag-law.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: a READ source giving magsail drag with a constant area and coefficient 1, against total density, valid up to 0.87 c. None was found. To WRONG: a contradiction computed under the tree's own hypotheses (none; the constant-A floor is proven), or a READ result that momentum braking cannot stop a craft at 0.048 c. To OPEN: evidence that the cached 1707.02801v3 text differs from the published paper. Reading Zubrin-Andrews 1991 directly, or a post-2018 relativistic or kinetic magsail study, could narrow this further or change the coefficient. A relativistic reflection model would decide the 0.87 c row.

si-astro-constants-c-g-msun-ly.published_statement: CODATA 2022 Table XXXII: 'speed of light in vacuum c 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact'; 'Newtonian constant of gravitation G 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, 2.2 x 10^-5'. Sec. I.B.11: '...the 2022 and 2018 recommended values of G are therefore identical.' IAU 2015 B3 Recommends 3: '1 (GM)^N_sun = 1.327 124 4 x 10^20 m^3 s^-2', exact, and to be read as 'conversion factors only ... not as the true solar properties'. Recommends 5: 'if SI masses are explicitly needed, they should be expressed in terms of (GM)_object/G, where the estimate of the Newtonian constant G should be specified in the publication'. Noting 3: G is 'one of the least precisely determined constants, whereas the error in the product GM_sun is five orders of magnitude smaller'.
published_hypotheses: c is exact by the 1983 definition of the metre. This is a definition, not a hypothesis.

G is the weighted mean of 16 mutually inconsistent measurements, with data closing 31 Dec 2018 and unchanged through 31 Dec 2022. The uncertainties were multiplied by an expansion factor of 3.9 so that every normalized residual is <= 2 (largest before expansion: BIPM-14 7.75, JILA-18 -6.80). u_r = 2.2e-5.
(GM)^N_sun is an exact conversion constant, given to the precision within which its TCB and TDB values agree. The source says explicitly that it is not the true solar property.
IAU 2015 B3 defines no nominal solar mass in kg. An SI solar mass is (GM)/G, inherits G's uncertainty, and must state which G was used.
ly is neither a CODATA nor an IAU-B3 quantity. c x Julian year is exact given c and the Julian-year convention, which is NAMED-NOT-READ here.

(2) Huang-Lee, arXiv 1706.03732v3 (CMP 2020): Theorem 1 and Corollary 4 pp.1-3, history p.2, Remark 2.11 p.7.

positive-mass-theorem.published_statement: EHLS 1110.2087 Theorem 1: 'Let 3 <= n < 8 and let (M, g, k) be an n-dimensional asymptotically flat initial data set that satisfies the dominant energy condition. Then E >= |P|.' History, p.2: 'In the time-symmetric case [k = 0], we have that P = 0 and the dominant energy condition becomes the assumption that the scalar curvature of g is nonnegative. [Schoen-Yau] proved the time-symmetric case in dimension three in two articles from 1979 and 1981 ... In 1981 ... the general case k != 0 in dimension three ... E >= 0 by solving Jang's equation. Later, E. Witten discovered a completely different proof that E >= |P| in dimension three.' Rigidity (Huang-Lee p.2): in the time-symmetric case, 'if E = 0, then (M, g) is isometric to Euclidean space'. For general data E = |P| implies E = |P| = 0: proved by Beig-Chrusciel in 1996 (3D, spin) and by Huang-Lee in 2020 (n <= 7; for n = 3 embedding in Minkowski also needs tr k = O(r^-s), s > 2).
published_hypotheses: n = 3 (Schoen-Yau, Witten; spin is automatic for orientable 3-manifolds); 3 <= n < 8 in EHLS
complete C^2_loc metric g, C^1_loc k, no boundary
asymptotic flatness of type (p,q,q0,alpha): (g - delta, k) in W^{2,p}_{-q} x W^{1,p}_{-1-q}, q in ((n-2)/2, n-2), mu and J decaying like r^{-n-q0}
dominant energy condition mu >= |J| on the slice, with mu = (1/2)(R_g - |k|^2 + (tr k)^2); for k = 0 this is R_g >= 0
E_ADM is a flux integral of the metric's fall-off (EHLS Def.3), not a field-equation quantity
the rigidity clause is a separate theorem (Schoen-Yau for k = 0; Beig-Chrusciel 1996; Huang-Lee 2020)
no empirical data enter

positive-mass-theorem.lacked_data: The theorem takes no measured input. It is an implication from completeness, asymptotic flatness and the DEC to E >= |P|, with rigidity at equality. Later work added mathematics, not data: proofs without spin (EHLS 2016), proofs in all dimensions (Schoen-Yau 2017, named not read), general-data rigidity (Beig-Chrusciel 1996, Huang-Lee 2020), and an extra regularity hypothesis for the 2016 statement. None of this moves the smooth, static 3+1 case the tree uses, and the recomputation here (C1-C4) agrees with the source. The physical assumption the authors made without measuring it is the DEC, and quantum fields were already known to violate it (Casimir). That violation does not falsify the theorem. It puts a configuration outside the theorem's scope, and every configuration on this board is outside it, by the board's own account (certify.py section 2, overturn.py:212-213, concentric.py:51-53, pair.py:124-129). So M's hypothesis gets no support from this result. What is missing is not data the authors lacked but a hypothesis the tree drops at phase1.py:397-399 and concentric.py:7-8. The literature is genuinely incomplete in one place: the averaged-condition positivity results meant to cover the quantum regime (PSW 1993) are unpublished and have a recorded gap, and the rigorous D>=4 version gives nothing at M=0. The tree does not cite that line of work.
positive-mass-theorem.grade_evidence: The theorem as published stands: statement and hypotheses were read via EHLS and Huang-Lee, the re-derivation agrees (C1-C4), and no datum enters. It is graded NARROWED because the tree applies it beyond its class, in three places. (1) phase1.py:397-399 and concentric.py:7-8 drop the DEC and treat negative ADM mass as forbidden outright. C2 exhibits complete, regular, AF static data with E_ADM < 0 and R_g < 0 that the theorem does not forbid; z3 C4(i) confirms the case is consistent; 2408.00154 p.4 says the same in print. This exclusion carries phase1's ranking and the_winner(). (2) The 'never in danger / nothing to object to' uses (certify.py:161-164, overturn.py:217 and 679-680, concentric.py:49-50 and 271-273) are true but vacuous, because every configuration on the board violates the DEC. So they cannot tell the concentric corridor from a bare negative mass (C4 ii, iv, v). (3) phase1.py:195-197 and 537-539 ('no energy condition violated with M_ADM = 0') are contradicted by the rigidity clause for static, complete, compactly supported configurations. hep-th/0402058.name: Bousso, 'Flat space physics from holography' (hep-th/0402058v2, 14 Aug 2004; JHEP 0405:050): the Bekenstein bound S <= 2 pi M R / hbar contains no Newton constant and remains nontrivial at G = 0

source.located: arXiv hep-th/0402058v2 (UCB-PTH-04/02, dated 14 Aug 2004). All 12 pages were returned: abstract p.1, Sec 2.1 p.4, Sec 2.2 pp.5-6, Sec 3 pp.7-8, Sec 4 pp.9-10, references pp.10-11. The journal reference JHEP 0405, 050 (2004) is as Casini 0804.2182 cites it in ref [7].

hep-th/0402058.published_statement:
Abstract (p.1): 'In flat space, the covariant entropy bound reduces to the Bekenstein bound. The latter does not contain Newton's constant and cannot operate via gravitational backreaction.'

Sec 2.2 (p.5): 'In its original form, the bound states that the entropy S of any weakly gravitating matter system obeys S <= 2 pi M R/hbar, (2.2) where M is the total gravitating mass of the matter and R is the radius of the smallest sphere that barely fits around the system. The absence of Newton's constant in Bekenstein's bound is notable. It renders Eq. (2.2) independent of the strength of gravity, G, in its regime of validity. In particular, the bound remains nontrivial when gravity is turned off completely (G = 0).'

Weak-gravity condition, eq (2.3): M << R/G.

Sec 2.1 (p.4): the covariant bound A/4G hbar becomes 'more lenient as G -> 0, and trivial for G = 0'.

Eq (3.2): S <~ M R/(l_Pl^2/G), which 'involves only the combination l_Pl^2/G'.

p.8: 'our understanding of the Bekenstein bound is still imperfect... quite sensitive to the precise definition of the entropy'.

p.10: an example that precisely saturates the bound 'is an important outstanding problem.'
published_hypotheses: H1 WEAKLY GRAVITATING matter system, M << R/G (eq 2.3). The G-independence is asserted 'in its regime of validity' (p.5), and the derivation 'applies only in weakly gravitating regions' (p.3).
H2 M is the total gravitating mass and R is the radius of the smallest sphere that barely fits around the system (p.5).
H3 hbar is the constant held fixed. The source writes the bound in hbar-form (2.2). In its own axiomatic form (3.2), with l_Pl primitive, the bound reads S <~ M R G/l_Pl^2.

H5 Entropy is the log of the number of Fock-space states compatible with the boundary conditions (p.2). The source says the bound is sensitive to how entropy is defined and assumes a rigorous formulation exists (p.8).

H6 (derivation only, not the quoted claim) The generalized covariant entropy bound is taken as an axiom. Sec 3 is a simplified argument good to factors of order one; the rigorous derivation is ref [17], hep-th/0210295.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1 (weakly gravitating, 'in its regime of validity'). bounds.py:309-312 quotes the two phrases without this qualifier, and the canonical entry's only hypothesis is 'S <= 2 pi R E'. DOCKET.md:193-195 does the same. The quotes themselves are verbatim.
