vonlaue-1911-annphys.name: von Laue's theorem (1911): volume integral of spatial stress of a static closed system is a surface term / vanishes

source.located: M. Laue, 'Zur Dynamik der Relativitaetstheorie', Ann. Phys. (Leipzig) 1911. Wang prints it as 'Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911)'; Lorce et al. 2109.11785 ref [30] and Pinto & Avelino 2502.10427 ref [32] print 'Annalen Phys. 340, 524 (1911)'. There is no arXiv copy, and the 1911 paper itself was NOT read.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text from four papers: C. Wang arXiv:1206.5618v12 = Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470 (2015), pp.1-7 (theorem in sec.2, fn.7, secs.4-6, eq.(20)); Lorce, Metz, Pasquini & Rodini arXiv:2109.11785, pp.1-5,7-8,11-12 (eqs.(14),(15),(18),(19),(23),(65)); Sorge arXiv:2011.10991, pp.1-13 (assumption (a), eqs.(31)-(36)); Pinto & Avelino arXiv:2502.10427v2, pp.1-3,5-9 (eqs.(22)-(27),(39)-(43)). Von Laue 1911 is NAMED-NOT-READ. Giulini arXiv:1808.09320, the modern derivation Pinto & Avelino follow, is also NAMED-NOT-READ.

vonlaue-1911-annphys.published_statement:
Wang's restatement (1206.5618, p.2): 'Assume that Theta^{mu nu}(x) is a Lorentz four-tensor given in the laboratory frame ..., Theta is independent of time, and further Theta^{i4}(x) = 0 ... von Laue's theorem [1] states: The time-row-element space integrals P^mu = int_V Theta^{mu 4} d^3x constitute a Lorentz four-vector if and only if int_V Theta^{ij} d^3x = 0 (2).' Wang fn.7 adds: 'In the original ref. 1, Laue only gave the proof that int Theta^{ij} d^3x = 0 is a sufficient condition.'

The finite-volume relation the tree cites is Wang sec.6, eq.(20). It comes from the three-dimensional Gauss law: oint_S dS_l (Theta^{l mu} X^i) = int_V (d_l Theta^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + int_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x. On p.5 Wang says 'divergence-less plus an additional boundary condition can be a sufficient condition ... oint_S dS_l Theta^{l mu} X^i = 0 holds, which is true if Theta = 0 is imposed on the boundary', and that divergence-less alone 'is neither a necessary condition nor a sufficient condition'.

Pinto & Avelino (eqs.(24)-(25)) give the modern vanishing form: 'If T^{mu j} = 0 at dSigma or if Sigma represents the whole fixed time hyperplane and T^{mu j} decays sufficiently fast (e.g. ~1/r^{3+eps}) then int_Sigma T^{mu i} d^3x = 0.' Lorce et al. eq.(15) states it for a closed system as 'the von Laue condition for mechanical equilibrium int d^3x p(x) = 0', with surface terms dropped by assumption.
published_hypotheses: static: dTheta^{mu nu}/dt = 0 in the frame considered (Wang sec.2, emphasised on p.3)
Theta^{i4} = 0 for the classical four-vector form (Wang sec.2)
closed system: the TOTAL stress-energy tensor is divergence-free and there is no external force density (Lorce eqs.(14),(19)); with a force density F, int T^{ij} = -int x^i F^j (Lorce eq.(18))

boundary condition: T^{l mu} = 0 on the bounding surface (Wang p.5; Pinto-Avelino eq.(25); Sorge assumption (a) and eq.(35)), OR integration over all space with T decaying faster than 1/r^3 (Pinto-Avelino eq.(25))
divergence-free alone is NOT sufficient: the field-only EM tensor of a charged sphere, or of a finite electrostatic structure, violates the condition (Wang secs.4-6)
flat (Minkowski) spacetime, i.e. negligible self-gravity (Pinto-Avelino p.1, sec.III)
the integrals converge (Wang eq.(1))
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED in prose, KEPT in code: the boundary condition. tolman.py:2622-2625 (PEER_STATUS 'this file's own reach') and tolman.py:1015-1017 say 'von Laue forces int_V T^i_i = 0 over a complete static bounded system, so 4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = 0 for ANY ball enclosing the whole device'. That needs T^{ij} n_j = 0 ON the enclosing sphere (compact support inside the ball). A bounded DEVICE is not enough, because its own static fields extend past it. Rederive C3d shows this: a charged conducting shell whose complete tensor is conserved gives int_{ball R} T^ii = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R), which is nonzero for every finite R > a. The z3 layer keeps the hypothesis: L1 (tolman.py:2387-2405) takes 'p_r = 0 at the cut' as a premise, and DRIFT L2 shows the premise is load-bearing.

ATTRIBUTION (a discrepancy, not an error): tolman.py:129-139 calls the surface-term step von Laue's theorem 'in its finite-volume form: Wang eq.(20)'. In Wang, eq.(20) is his own sec.6 Gauss-law identity. Von Laue's theorem proper (sec.2) is the four-vector criterion, with int Theta^{ij} = 0 as its condition, and Wang fn.7 says Laue proved only sufficiency. The restatements disagree on this: Lorce et al. p.5 says von Laue showed the condition is necessary and sufficient. The mathematics the tree uses is unaffected either way.

ADDED, over-restrictive but harmless: tolman.py:567 says 'Wang's eq.(20) needs the REGION to be a ball'. Eq.(20) holds for any region V with boundary S (Wang: 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected'). The ball is needed only to reduce the surface term to 4 pi R^3 <T^rr>(R).
KEPT: 'complete' (field plus mirrors) matches the requirement that the TOTAL tensor be conserved. Wang secs.4-5 and rederive C4 show that the field-only tensor fails the condition.
KEPT: flat space (tolman.py:129 'Strip gravity'). Sorge eq.(36) extends the vanishing to first order in gamma in a weak field, under the same compact-support assumption (a).

CITATION (already recorded at tolman.py:151-157): Wang prints '35, 524'; Lorce et al. and Pinto & Avelino independently print '340, 524'. These are the same paper under two volume numberings. The tree's issue number '(8)' appears in none of the four sources read, so it is unverified, not contradicted.

data_at_publication.quantity: No numerical input: the result is a theorem (an identity plus a boundary condition). The only datum is bibliographic, the Ann. Phys. volume number.

data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: no

rederivation.outcome:
ALL PASS: 15 checks, about 12 s.
- C1: the product-rule identity under Wang eq.(20) holds symbolically for every i and mu.
- C2: the stress T^{ij} = delta_ij Lap(phi) - d_i d_j phi, with phi = (1-r^2)^4 (1 + xz + y^2/3), is divergence-free, non-spherical and compactly supported. For it, int_ball T^ii equals R^3 oint n_i n_j T^{ij} dOmega = 4 pi R^3 <T^rr> exactly (sympy residual 0). The value is -435 pi/128 at R = 1/2, inside the support, and exactly 0 at R = 1, the support boundary.
- C3: a bounded charged shell held by a surface tension, with the complete tensor conserved, gives int_{ball R>a} T^ii = 4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R). This is nonzero at every finite R and tends to 0 only as R -> infinity. By contrast, +Q/-Q concentric shells (field confined) give exactly 0 for R > b. The finite-ball deviation meets the Pinto-Avelino bound |int p| <= m_out with ratio exactly 1/3.
- C4: the field-only tensor over all space gives Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a), which is nonzero, reproducing Wang secs.4-5.
- C5 (z3 5.1.0): the identity plus p_r = 0 at the cut forces m = 0 (the negation is unsat); with p_r left free, m = 0 is not forced (sat); the vacuity guard is sat.

later_literature.what: Divergence-free alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for int Theta^{ij} = 0. Divergence-free plus the boundary condition (Theta = 0 on the boundary) is sufficient. Counterexamples are a charged metal sphere and a finite electrostatic structure, using the field-only tensor. Wang's further claim, that the Landau-Lifshitz and Weinberg versions are 'flawed', concerns the four-vector theorem, not the part the tree uses.

QFT version for a closed system in a stationary state: <int T^ii> = 0 (eq.14) and <int T^ij> = 0 (eq.19), with surface terms dropped by assumption. With an external force, int T^ij = -int x^i F^j (eq.18). M = <int T^mu_mu> (eq.65). Attributes the necessary-and-sufficient form to von Laue, which conflicts with Wang fn.7.

For a Casimir apparatus in a weak field, int sqrt(-g) T^i_i = 0 (eq.36). This assumes T vanishes outside the domain (assumption (a)) and on its boundary (eq.(35)), with ideal plates and edge effects neglected.

later_literature.ref: S. R. Pinto & P. P. Avelino, arXiv:2502.10427v2 (2025), 'Deviations from the von Laue condition'
later_literature.what: States the condition with an explicit alternative hypothesis: T = 0 at the boundary, or all of space with decay faster than 1/r^3 (eq.25). On a FINITE ball the integrated pressure is not zero; under the DEC it is bounded by the energy outside the ball, |int_0^r p| <= m_out (eqs.39-43). That is exactly the case the tree's 'ANY ball enclosing the whole device' sentence drops. Reproduced in rederive C3h.

vonlaue-1911-annphys.lacked_data:
In 1911 von Laue did not have GR (1915), QFT with renormalised vacuum stress (Casimir, 1948), or hadron pressure data (gravitational form factors, from 2018). The sources read here show that having them does not change the conclusion:
(i) The finite-volume relation is a pure identity with no empirical input; it is re-derived here in C1 and C2.
(ii) The vanishing form carries over to QFT stationary states (Lorce et al. eqs.14 and 19) and to a Casimir apparatus to first order in a weak field (Sorge eq.36). No refutation was found or constructed.
(iii) The only limit later work makes explicit is a hypothesis that was always needed, not new data: the boundary term must vanish (Moller's zero-boundary condition, 1955, as reported by Wang; Pinto-Avelino eq.25). Pinto & Avelino 2025 quantify how large the finite-ball deviation can be.
Hadron data do not test the condition: the proton analyses assume it. Whether any measurement has been independent of it was NOT checked here.
M's hypothesis is not supported for this result; no datum has moved.
vonlaue-1911-annphys.grade_evidence:
What stands: the identity the tree cites, Wang eq.(20), re-derives exactly (C1 symbolic; C2 sympy residual 0 on a non-spherical conserved stress). Its direction as the tree now states it is confirmed: the surface term is on the left and equals 4 pi R^3 <T^rr>.

What is narrowed: the vanishing form holds on a smaller class than tolman.py:1015-1017 and 2622-2625 state. It needs T = 0 on the enclosing sphere (compact support), which Wang, Sorge and Pinto & Avelino all state. 'Complete static bounded system' is not enough when the device's fields extend past it. Computed counterexample (C3d): a bounded device with a conserved complete tensor gives int_{ball R} T^ii = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R), nonzero on every finite enclosing ball. Pinto & Avelino 2025 bound the same deviation in general, and C3h reproduces their bound exactly.

Why no verdict moves: the code already carries the hypothesis. z3 L1 (tolman.py:2387-2405) takes p_r = 0 at the cut as a premise, and DRIFT L2 proves it load-bearing, so the narrowing is in prose only. The refusal 'ball_excludes_walls' stays conservative under the narrower class: it may refuse where the test had content, but it never reports a false zero.

What is not a refutation: the attribution of eq.(20) to von Laue, the 35 versus 340 volume number, and 'eq.(20) needs a ball' are discrepancies.

Why this grade: not STANDS, because the printed statement drops a required hypothesis and a counterexample to it is computed here. Not WRONG, because the result as the tree applies it (L1) is correct.
vonlaue-1911-annphys.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: tolman.py:1015-1017 and 2622-2625 would need to say that the boundary of the ball lies outside the support of the complete T, or define 'bounded system' as compact support of T, so that the prose matches L1. That is a change to the tree, which this audit does not make.
On the attribution alone: reading von Laue 1911 at source would settle whether Laue proved sufficiency only (Wang fn.7) or the necessary-and-sufficient form (Lorce et al. p.5). That cannot be done here, since there is no arXiv copy, and either answer leaves the mathematics unchanged.
To WRONG: the tree would have to apply the vanishing form to a T that is not compactly supported inside the ball. No such application was found.

stokes-divergence-theorem.name: Stokes / divergence theorem underlying the Laue step

source.located: Classical Gauss-Green / Gauss-Ostrogradsky divergence theorem (Lagrange 1762 special case; Gauss 1813; Ostrogradsky 1828/1831; Green 1828), none on arXiv. The tree's own citation route is Wang arXiv:1206.5618v12 (= Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470 (2015)) eq.(20), which invokes 'the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law'. Modern statements with exact hypotheses: G.-Q. Chen & M. Torres arXiv:2005.10949v3 (Notices AMS 68, 1282 (2021)); T. Ruf arXiv:2506.09978v2 (2025).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text: Chen-Torres 2005.10949 pp.1-11 (classical statement eq.(1) p.3; De Giorgi-Federer eq.(4) p.5; DM-field Theorems 1-3 pp.7-10; Whitney Example 2 p.8; Silhavy Example 3 p.10); Wang 1206.5618 pp.2, 4-5 (eq.(20); 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected'); Ruf 2506.09978 pp.1-2, 5-7, 15-16 (inner boundaries, Thm 1.1/4.4). Gauss 1813, Ostrogradsky 1831, Green 1828, Whitney 1957, Federer, De Giorgi, Chen-Frid, Silhavy are NAMED-NOT-READ (restated in Chen-Torres).

stokes-divergence-theorem.published_statement: Chen-Torres 2005.10949 p.3 eq.(1): 'The divergence theorem in its vector form for the n-dimensional case (n >= 2) can be stated as INT_E div F dy = - INT_{dE} F . nu dH^{n-1}, where F is a C^1 vector field, E is a bounded open set with piecewise smooth boundary, nu is the inner unit normal vector to E'; p.1: 'generally stated for C^1 vector fields and domains with C^1 boundaries'; p.5: valid for Lipschitz fields on sets of finite perimeter (De Giorgi, Federer) and BV fields on Lipschitz domains; p.8 Example 2 (Whitney): 'F = (y1,y2)/(y1^2+y2^2) ... E = (0,1)^2 ... 0 = divF(E) != - INT_{dE} F . nu_E dH^1 = pi/2'. The form the tree uses, Wang 1206.5618 p.5 eq.(20): 'from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law we have oint_S dS_l (Theta^{l mu} X^i) = INT_V (d_l Theta^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + INT_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x'; p.2 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected'.
published_hypotheses: F (here W^l = T^{lj} x^i) is C^1 on the closure of the region (classical, Chen-Torres p.1, p.3). The divergence is taken over the WHOLE region. A singular point of F inside the region carries its own contribution: Whitney's example (p.8) has div F = 0 pointwise in the open square, yet the boundary flux is pi/2

codata-2018-constants.lacked_data: The evidence runs both ways. FOR M's hypothesis: CODATA 2018 did not have the Morel et al. 2020 h/m(87Rb) measurement. With it, CODATA 2022 moved alpha, and with it mu_0, eps_0, a_0 and m_e, by about 4.5 of their own 2018 standard uncertainties. For G it is the reverse of missing data. No new G datum arrived between 2018 and 2022. The problem is that 16 existing inputs disagree (residuals up to 7.75, expansion factor 3.9), and reanalyses of the same data dispute the value at ~5e-5 and the uncertainty by up to about 10x. Anywhere within the full span of the 16 inputs, no refusal verdict moves; order-level figures move by at most 1.6e-4 orders. What does move is the tree's quoted precision: its 6 to 11 s.f. pins fail at CODATA's own 1 sigma. Moving even a one-order figure would need G to be wrong by more than a factor of 10, and nothing read here suggests that.

hydrogen-schrodinger-spectrum.name: Nonrelativistic hydrogen levels E_n = -m alpha^2/(2n^2) and <r>_{n,l} = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m alpha)

source.located: Primary: Schrodinger, Ann. Phys. 79 (1926) 361 (levels); <r>_{nl} via Waller Z. Phys. 38 (1926) 635 / Pasternack PNAS 23 (1937) 91 / Kramers 1938 -- none on arXiv. Read via restatement in: arXiv:0707.1887 (Suslov & Trey, J. Math. Phys. 49 (2008) 012104) p.8-11 eqs (3.1)-(3.5), (3.13)-(3.15), p.16 eqs (4.16)-(4.17); arXiv:0908.0032 (Cordero-Soto & Suslov 2009) p.2 eqs (2.6)-(2.7); arXiv:2409.03787 (CODATA 2022) p.10-11 eqs (26), (28)-(31), p.15 eq (50), Tables IV, XXXII, XXXIII.
source.via: Page text from alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries for all three arXiv papers, plus 1807.08337 and 2602.14980 for later literature. Schrodinger 1926, Waller 1926, Pasternack 1937 and Kramers 1938 are NAMED-NOT-READ. The formulas come from Suslov-Trey eqs (3.5) and (3.15). These agree with Cordero-Soto-Suslov eqs (2.6)-(2.7), with CODATA eq (26) at F = 0, and with excite.py:953-958.

hydrogen-schrodinger-spectrum.published_statement: Suslov & Trey (0707.1887 p.8-9): 'The nonrelativistic Coulomb wave functions ... psi_nlm = R_nl(r) Y_lm, R_nl = (2/n^2)(Z/a0)^{3/2} sqrt((n-l-1)!/(n+l)!) e^{-eta/2} eta^l L^{2l+1}_{n-l-1}(eta), eta = (2Z/n)(r/a0), a0 = hbar^2/(m e^2) ... n = 1,2,3,...; l = 0,1,...,n-1 ... The corresponding discrete energy levels in the cgs units are given by Bohr's formula E_n = -m Z^2 e^4/(2 hbar^2 n^2) (3.5) ... they do not depend on the quantum number of the orbital angular momenta l due to a hidden SO(4)-symmetry'; p.10: '<r> = (a0/2Z)(3n^2 - l(l+1)) (3.15)'. Cordero-Soto & Suslov (0908.0032 eqs 2.6-2.7): the Kramers-Pasternack recursion with '<1/r> = Z/(a0 n^2), <1> = 1'. CODATA 2022 (2409.03787 eq 26): 'E = -(E_h/2n^2)(1 + F) ... E_h = alpha^2 m_e c^2 ... F is small compared to one and is determined by QED, recoil corrections, etc.' Setting hbar = c = 1, e^2 = alpha and Z = 1 gives E_n = -m alpha^2/(2n^2), a0 = 1/(m alpha) and <r> = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m alpha). This is exactly excite.py:954-958.
published_hypotheses: nonrelativistic stationary Schrodinger equation for one electron in a central attractive field (Suslov-Trey sec 1, sec 3)
spinless electron with no spin-orbit or fine structure. Suslov-Trey p.16 places the O(mu^4) fine-structure term in the Pauli approximation, i.e. outside the Schrodinger model
pure static Coulomb potential -Z e^2/r of a point charge, with no radiative (QED) corrections; CODATA eq (26) puts QED, recoil and nuclear size in F
infinitely heavy nucleus: m is m_e with a0 = hbar^2/(m e^2). CODATA eqs (28)-(30) say 'infinitely heavy point nucleus' and treat finite nuclear mass by the reduced mass m_r
bound (discrete) states only: n >= 1, 0 <= l <= n-1, normalisable R_nl (Suslov-Trey eq 3.4)
general Z (hydrogen-like ion); hydrogen is Z = 1
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED FROM THE NAMED LIST, NOT FROM THE MODEL: 'nonrelativistic, spinless, no radiative/QED corrections' is not among the hypotheses named at excite.py:954-955 ('hbar = c = 1, point nucleus of infinite mass'). It is implicit in 'the Schrodinger problem' (excite.py:196) and in the canonical key's word 'Nonrelativistic'. The Dirac side is handled separately (excite.py:962-968). D18 (excite.py:195-198) limits its claim to 'every dimensionless observable of that model', so this is a naming omission, not use outside the class.

UNNAMED RESIDUAL, relevant only if D18 is applied to real hydrogen: in QED at fixed alpha, muonic and hadronic vacuum polarisation depend on m_e/m_mu and m_e/m_hadron (2602.14980 p.1: f_QED 'including muonic and hadronic contributions'; hVP moves nu(2S-6P) by 0.46 kHz in 730.69 THz = 6.3e-13). Neither ledger.py:514-516 nor specthm.py:1390-1391 names this channel. It is ~1e-12 x eps. Recorded; it does not refute anything.

LABEL DISCREPANCY, not a refutation: ledger.py:515-516 lists 'finite nuclear size' under 'O(eps) through m_p/m_e'. Finite size actually enters through r_p/a0 (CODATA eq 50). Computed here: (4/3) alpha^2 (r_p/lambda_C)^2 = 3.36e-10 of the 1S Bohr energy, and it scales as (1+eps)^3 rather than (1+eps). Both channels are the electron mass set against a QCD-fixed scale, so the ledger's conclusion (a small, computable O(eps) shift) is unchanged.

ADDED BY THE TREE as a scenario, not part of the theorem: 'alpha fixed (H2)' (excite.py:195-196). It is consistent with the source, which treats alpha as a constant. The tree itself notes that alpha moves under H1 (excite.py:202-203).

1204.3570-seci-friedrichs.name: FFR 1204.3570 Sec. I: A_tau meant as the self-adjoint (Friedrichs) extension; essential self-adjointness 'not fully resolved'

source.located: arXiv:1204.3570v1 [quant-ph], 16 Apr 2012: C.J. Fewster, L.H. Ford, T.A. Roman, 'Probability distributions for quantum stress tensors in four dimensions', Phys. Rev. D 85, 125038 (2012). Sec. I, p. 2 (the paragraph beginning 'An important point arises here'), with footnote [39] on p. 25, ref. [17] (Reed-Simon II Thm X.23) and ref. [18] (Sanders arXiv:1010.3978).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(paper='1204.3570') returned page text for pp. 1-3, 10, 12, 15, 20-21 and 25, including the whole Sec. I paragraph and footnote [39]. Ref. [18] (Sanders 1010.3978v3) was also READ at source (pp. 1-2, 5, 9-15). Reed-Simon II Thm X.23 is a textbook theorem with no arXiv copy, so it is NAMED-NOT-READ; the re-derivation exercises its content on a model.

1204.3570-seci-friedrichs.published_statement: FFR 1204.3570 p. 2, verbatim: 'Throughout this paper, all quadratic operators are understood to be normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state. However, the smeared normal ordered operators are defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain in the Hilbert space (assuming a real-valued smearing function) and it is possible that there is more than one way of extending them to provide self-adjoint operators [39]. The operators of greatest interest to us are bounded from below on account of quantum inequalities (see Sect. II A) and so there is a distinguished Friedrichs extension (see Ref. [17], Theorem X.23), whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind when we discuss the probability distribution of individual measurements of the smeared operator in the vacuum state. The question of whether there is more than one self-adjoint extension, i.e., whether the normal ordered expressions fail to be essentially self-adjoint, is nontrivial and not fully resolved. Recent results (not, however, immediately applicable to our situation) and references may be found in Ref. [18]. If there are distinct self-adjoint extensions, their corresponding probability distributions will all share the same moments in the vacuum state.' Footnote [39]: 'The existence of at least one self-adjoint extension is guaranteed on general grounds because the operators commute with complex conjugation of the n-particle wavefunctions in Fock space.' The entry has three parts: a DEFINITION (which self-adjoint realisation is meant), a THEOREM it rests on (Friedrichs), and a STATUS REPORT (essential self-adjointness was open in 2012).
published_hypotheses: P1: quadratic operators are normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum, in 4D Minkowski spacetime. The fields studied are the massless scalar (phi^2, phi-dot^2, rho_S) and electromagnetism (E^2, rho_EM).

P2: the smearing function is real-valued, so the smeared operator is symmetric. The paper's own computations use Lorentzian time-averaging along the time axis at a fixed spatial point, but the Sec. I remark is stated for smeared normal-ordered operators in general.

P3: the operator is defined in the first instance only as a symmetric operator on 'a dense domain'. Sec. I does not specify the domain; p. 10 works with 'states obtained from the vacuum by applying polynomials of smeared fields'.
P4: the operator is bounded from below 'on account of quantum inequalities' (Sect. II A, Eq. (1)). This semiboundedness is the input to the Friedrichs construction.
P5: the Friedrichs extension (Reed-Simon II Thm X.23) is CHOSEN ('It is this operator that we have in mind'). Its lower bound equals the sharpest QI bound.
P6: essential self-adjointness is 'nontrivial and not fully resolved', and Sanders 1010.3978 is 'not, however, immediately applicable'.

P7: if distinct self-adjoint extensions exist, they share the same vacuum moments. The distributions themselves may still differ, because the moment problem may be indeterminate (discussed in Secs. I, IV and VIII A).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (the domain is fixed): noise.py:157-158 realises A_tau as the Friedrichs extension 'on Hadamard vectors', while FFR p. 2 say only 'a dense domain'. The Friedrichs extension depends on the initial domain, so the tree has fixed something FFR leave open. The lower bound C1 uses survives any choice: the Friedrichs lower bound is the infimum of <psi,A psi>/||psi||^2 over the chosen domain, so it is >= -C/tau^4 on any dense linear domain where Fewster 1208.5399 bound (3) holds for every vector. What the tree leaves unstated is that the 'Hadamard vectors' form a dense linear subspace on which A_tau is symmetric. Sanders uses the Wightman domain D_omega, which consists of such vectors. This is a gap in naming, not an error.

WIDENED (field and sampler class), and harmless for this entry: noise.py:154 (H1) takes m >= 0, and noise.py:163-165 (H4) takes a compactly supported sampler root g in W^{2,2}. FFR compute with massless fields and a Lorentzian. The Sec. I remark is functional analysis that holds for any semibounded symmetric operator, and semiboundedness for the tree's class comes from Fewster 1208.5399 (H4), not from FFR. So the widening is not a drift in what FFR Sec. I supports.

ADDED (the tree's own claim, not in FFR): noise.py:160-162, ledger.py:589-590 and specthm.py:2239 say 'a different self-adjoint extension of a semibounded operator need not keep the Friedrichs lower bound'. FFR do not say this, but it is a correct general fact: the Friedrichs extension is the largest semibounded extension in form order, and other extensions can sit strictly below it. The re-derivation CONFIRMS it on a closed-form model: the Robin extension of -d^2/dx^2 on the half-line has eigenvalue -kappa^2, below the Friedrichs bound 0.

DROPPED (FFR's P7; it does not decide either way): the tree does not carry FFR's sentence that distinct extensions share the vacuum moments. Carrying it would narrow H3's consequence for the VACUUM distribution only. If the vacuum moment problem were Hamburger-determinate, every extension would give the same vacuum distribution, supported in [-C/tau^4, oo), and H3 would not be needed for the vacuum statement. But FFR p. 20 say 'on balance our expectation is that the problem is indeed indeterminate', and re-derivation check C5 shows equal moments with different supports. So H3 stays load-bearing, as the tree says. C1 is stated for every state (noise.py:28-35), and P7 does not apply there at all.

NO DRIFT in status: noise.py:160 quotes 'not fully resolved' verbatim (source p. 2), and noise.py:324 labels H3 'ASSUMED, load-bearing'. That matches FFR's own 'It is this operator that we have in mind', which is a choice, not a theorem. The tree does not upgrade the choice to a theorem.

data_at_publication.quantity: Status of essential self-adjointness for the operator the tree calls A_tau: the 4D free-scalar energy density, a normal-ordered quadratic operator smeared along a timelike worldline
data_at_publication.value_then: 2012: 'nontrivial and not fully resolved' (FFR p. 2), and Sanders 1010.3978 is 'not immediately applicable'.
data_at_publication.value_now: Sanders 1010.3978v3 (Apr 2012, READ) proves essential self-adjointness on the Wightman domain for the Wick square WITHOUT derivatives, smeared with a SPACETIME test function in class S (finite sums of squares of real test functions), in any quasi-free Hadamard state, on any globally hyperbolic spacetime, for d >= 2 (Thm 5.8). WITH derivatives the result holds only if the one-particle compression is essentially self-adjoint (Thm 5.4). He also gives a distinguished self-adjoint extension as a monotone limit (Thm 5.3). None of these covers a derivative Wick square smeared along a worldline (delta in space), which is the tree's A_tau. Schiappacasse-Fewster-Ford 1711.09477 and Fewster-Hollands 1805.04281 (both READ) do not settle it either. The first diagonalises a finite-mode truncation in a sphere. The second is 2D CFT, where T(f) is self-adjoint, and its Sec. 5 says its methods have 'no straightforward generalization ... to higher spacetime dimensions'. One discover_papers search found no later resolution; not finding a paper does not prove there is none.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. H3 is ASSUMED either way. A future proof of essential self-adjointness for A_tau would DISCHARGE H3, because Friedrichs would then be the only self-adjoint extension. A proof of the opposite would leave H3 a choice, which is how the tree already carries it. No numerical datum enters this entry.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS: 9 checks, exit 0. The QFT operator is not finite, so both functional-analytic claims were tested on the closed-form model A = -d^2/dx^2 on C_c^inf(0,oo). C1: the form bound is 0 (sympy). C2: the Rayleigh quotient of dilated vectors is 1/(19 s^2) -> 0+, so the Friedrichs (Dirichlet) lower bound equals the form bound and is not attained. C3: the Robin boundary form vanishes, so Robin is a symmetric extension of A. C4: the Robin eigenvector sqrt(2)e^{-x} has eigenvalue -1, below the Friedrichs bound 0; this CONFIRMS the tree's 'a different self-adjoint extension ... need not keep the Friedrichs lower bound'. C5: for phi = x^10 e^{-x}, moments m_0..m_4 computed from the Dirichlet (sine) resolution and from the Robin resolution (atom plus continuum) both agree with <phi, A^n phi> to 30 digits. Yet the Robin measure puts mass 6.279e6 (out of ||phi||^2 = 1.160e12) at -1, below the Friedrichs bound. This CONFIRMS FFR's P7 (shared moments) and shows the shared moments do NOT fix the support, which is why H3 is load-bearing. Not checked: whether the QFT A_tau is essentially self-adjoint (open at source and in the later papers read), and Reed-Simon Thm X.23 itself (NAMED-NOT-READ; exercised on the model only).

later_literature.ref: K. Sanders, arXiv:1010.3978v3 (J. Math. Phys. 53, 042502 (2012)), FFR's ref. [18]
later_literature.what: Proves essential self-adjointness of :phi^2:(f) on the Wightman domain for f in class S (sums of squares of real SPACETIME test functions), in every quasi-free Hadamard representation (Thm 5.8). For Wick squares with derivatives (stress-tensor components) it proves this only when the one-particle compression is essentially self-adjoint (Thm 5.4). It gives a distinguished self-adjoint extension as a monotone strong-resolvent limit (Thm 5.3), and notes that for f in S the Wick square is semibounded, so a Friedrichs extension exists (p. 10). This narrows FFR's open question to derivative Wick squares and to smearings outside S or along a worldline. The tree's A_tau is still in the open part.

later_literature.ref: E.D. Schiappacasse, C.J. Fewster, L.H. Ford, arXiv:1711.09477 (Phys. Rev. D 97, 025013 (2018))
later_literature.what: Bogoliubov-diagonalises a finite-mode truncation of the time-averaged :phi-dot^2: in a sphere. There C_shift is the lowest eigenvalue and also the lower bound of the probability distribution (p. 9). For the Lorentzian, C_shift = -0.0593338 against FFR's moment estimate of -0.0236; both lie inside the Fewster-Eveson bound of -27/128 (p. 20). A finite truncation has no extension ambiguity, so it neither tests nor discharges H3.

In 2D unitary positive-energy CFT the smeared stress tensor is self-adjoint on D(L_0), with the intersection of the D(L_0^k) as a common core (pp. 3, 6). The infimum of the vacuum distribution's support equals the optimal QEI 'on general grounds' (p. 3, Eq. (1.5)), checked for new families at Eq. (4.34). This confirms the Friedrichs/QEI-bound identification where essential self-adjointness holds. Sec. 5 says the methods have 'no straightforward generalization ... to higher spacetime dimensions'.

zeta-pi-enclosures.name: zeta(6) = pi^6/945; 333/106 < pi < 355/113; zeta(7) partial sum to 30 with tail <= 1/(6*30^6)

source.located: Three classical mathematical facts, none with an original on arXiv. (i) zeta(6) = pi^6/945: Euler's formula zeta(2k) = (-1)^{k-1} 2^{2k-1} pi^{2k} B_{2k}/(2k)!, READ at source in Ciaurri, Navas, Ruiz, Varona, arXiv:2307.08063v1 [math.NT] (2023): p.2 eq (3), p.7 Theorem 3.3 (Euler, 1740) eq (17) with full proof pp.5-8, Bernoulli recurrence p.4, B_{2k+1}=0 p.5. The value pi^6/945 is not printed there; it follows from eq (3) at k=3 with B_6=1/42, both re-derived exactly here. (ii) 333/106 < pi < 355/113: the 3rd and 4th convergents of pi = [3;7,15,1,292,...]; READ in Lopez Zapata, arXiv:2603.09719v5 [math.GM] (2026), p.5 eqs (11)-(12) (partial quotients A001203; convergent numerators 3,22,333,355,103993 = A002485) and p.3 eq (7). That paper is math.GM and says it used Claude for verification (p.9), so it serves only as a pointer. The enclosure is PROVED here from Machin's formula with exact rationals. (iii) sum_{n>30} n^-7 <= INT_30^oo x^-7 dx = 1/(6*30^6): integral comparison, elementary calculus, proved exactly here.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2307.08063 (pp.1-12, 14-15, 17-19, 23-24 verbatim) and 2603.09719 (pp.1-9 verbatim). Euler 1735/1740, Zu Chongzhi (355/113), Machin 1706 and Khinchin 'Continued Fractions' 1964 are NAMED-NOT-READ; the content each would supply is re-derived in rederive/zeta-pi-enclosures.py.

zeta-pi-enclosures.published_statement: arXiv:2307.08063 p.2 eq (3): 'zeta(2k) = (-1)^{k-1} 2^{2k-1} pi^{2k} B_{2k} / (2k)!, k = 1, 2, 3, ...'; p.7 'Theorem 3.3 (Euler, 1740). For every positive integer k we have zeta(2k) = sum 1/n^{2k} = (-1)^{k-1}(2pi)^{2k} B_{2k}/(2(2k)!)', B_k := B_k(0) from z e^{xz}/(e^z-1). At k=3, B_6=1/42, which gives zeta(6)=pi^6/945. arXiv:2603.09719 p.5: 'pi = [3; 7, 15, 1, 292, ...]', convergent numerators '3, 22, 333, 355, 103993, ...'. The tree's use (noise.py:731-733): 'PROVE (beta/tau) coef (z6 pi^6 - z7)/(sqrt(2 pi) pi^7) < 1/2 from 333/106 < pi < 355/113, sum_{1}^{30} n^-7 <= z7 <= that + 1/(6*30^6), r^2 = 2 pi, r > 0.'

P2 Bernoulli numbers B_k = B_k(0) (B_1 = -1/2); even-index values such as B_6 = 1/42 do not depend on the convention
P3 (continued fractions; 2603.09719 p.3 eq (7), p.5) pi irrational; convergents alternate, even-index below and odd-index above; 333/106 is index 2 (below), 355/113 is index 3 (above)
P4 (integral comparison) x^-7 is positive and decreasing on [30, oo), so sum_{n>30} n^-7 < 1/(6*30^6); z7 >= partial sum needs only positive terms
P5 (tree-side, unstated) z3's nonlinear real arithmetic is trusted to be sound and emits no certificate. The exact-rational box proof E4b removes this reliance

gklp-rank1-moving-brane-no-ctc.name: GKLP: no closed causal curve on a moving brane in M4 x S1 (rank-1 spatial compactification)

source.located: Greene, Kabat, Levin, Porrati, 'Back to the Future: Causality on a Moving Braneworld', arXiv:2208.09014v3 (24 Jan 2023), Phys. Rev. D 107, 025016 (2023). This is the only paper whose authors' initials are GKLP. The earlier paper, Greene, Kabat, Levin, Menon, arXiv:2206.13590v2 (PRD 106, 085001, 2022), is GKLM, not GKLP. It sets up the geometry (eqs. 1-3) and makes no claim about causality or CTCs.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries returned the full page text of 2208.09014v3 (pp. 1-17) and 2206.13590v2 (pp. 1-19). latticectc.py cites no arXiv id for GKLP. The match rests on the identical setup, on the eq. (22) that branelink.py:81 cites, and on ledger.py/LEDGER.md naming 2208.09014.

gklp-rank1-moving-brane-no-ctc.published_statement: 2208.09014 abstract: 'Brane observers executing appropriate motion through a partially compactified Lorentz invariant bulk spacetime, such as M4 x S1, can send signals along the brane that are instantaneous or even travel backward in time. Nevertheless, causality in the braneworld remains intact.' p.4: 'A quick argument suggests that this cannot happen. In the covering space, image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones.' Sec. 4, eqs. (27)-(28): T = D(1/v - 1/w) = 2D/v_eff, v_eff = gamma(1+Gamma^2 B^2 beta^2); 'always positive ... 0 < T <= 2D/gamma. An instantaneous round trip is possible but closed time-like curves are not.' Eqs. (29)-(32): after adding a circle L' along the brane, the return time is Gamma L'/gamma (1+B/gamma)/(1+Gamma^2B^2beta^2) > 0. Sec. 6: 'all roundtrip signals return to their starting location after a non-negative amount of elapsed time, obviating the possibility of causality-challenging closed timelike curves.' Sec. 5 treats microcausality for a free scalar only; for interactions the paper says 'we expect causality to be robust' and does not show it.
published_hypotheses: The bulk is flat ('Lorentz invariant bulk'): M5 with z ~ z + 2 pi R n, and the identification is purely spatial in a preferred frame (2206.13590 eq. 1; 2208.09014 eq. 1).
In the brane frame the identification is (t', z') ~ (t', z') + (-gamma beta 2 pi R, gamma 2 pi R) (eq. 6/8). A boost B along the brane gives eq. (10).
There is one brane (plus its covering-space images) moving at constant |beta| < 1. It is flat and untilted, and the paper assumes without saying so that it does not back-react on the bulk.
Brane observers move at constant velocity B in (0,1), including supercritical B with Gamma^2 B > 1/(gamma beta^2).

The round trips actually computed are collinear out-and-back trips along x'' built from the envelope velocities v, w (eqs. 20, 25), plus one trip around the added brane circle (eq. 29). The general bulk statement appears only as the p.4 heuristic ('suggests').
Microcausality is shown for a free massless scalar only.

Under the owner's H3 (latticectc.py:21-23), causal curves are unconstrained in the bulk, so the number of branes does not matter. I re-derived this here. 2505.02210.published_statement:
Abstract: 'We construct a model for the nucleation of a wormhole within a Lorentzian spacetime by employing techniques from topological surgery and Morse theory. In our framework, a 0-surgery process describes the neighborhood of the nucleation point inside a compact region of spacetime, yielding a singular Lorentzian cobordism that connects two spacelike regions with different topologies. To avoid the singularity at the critical point of the Morse function, we employ the Misner trick of taking a connected sum with a closed 4-manifold -- namely CP^2 -- to obtain an everywhere nondegenerate Lorentzian metric. This connected sum replaces the naked singularity with a region containing closed timelike curves. The obtained spacetime is nonsingular, but violates all the standard energy conditions.'

Sec. IV.B: the Morse spacetime (13) has type-IV regions under criterion (19) (Fig. 9) and so violates all the standard energy conditions.

Sec. IV.C: there are regions where T w w < 0 (Fig. 12), and a type-IV point p=(1,0,0,0) on CP^2. Eq. (24): 'the numerical factor 2 is arbitrary and can be replaced by any real number zeta > 1 ... changing zeta merely shifts, thins, or expands the regions where the energy conditions are violated; it does not eliminate them altogether.'

Sec. V.D: homotopies H1-H4 built from smooth b(eta), c(eta) and a path alpha(eta) in SO(4). 'Because the entire deformation is smooth and nonsingular, the resulting Lorentzian metric on the neck remains free of singularities, and no further explicit expression is required for our purposes.'

Sec. I: 'The conclusions we present, apart from the investigations of the energy conditions on these spacetimes, are purely kinematic'.
published_hypotheses: P1 Classical and 4-dimensional. A spacetime has an everywhere non-degenerate, TIME-ORIENTABLE Lorentzian metric with signature (-,+,+,+) (Def. 6). The result is kinematic: the metric is built by eq. (2) from a Riemannian metric plus a line field, not solved from field equations.
P2 The Hawking-Borde setting: the transition is confined to a compact timelike tube W with boundary Sigma_i U T U Sigma_f.
P3 kink(dW; g_L) = 1 is ASSUMED. The paper motivates it as the ambient spacetime being asymptotically flat (sec. III.D).

tree-scalar-energy-positivity.published_statement: Fewster 1208.5399 p.44 sec.5.1: 'the classical minimally coupled scalar field obeys the WEC by virtue of a decomposition of the energy density as a sum of squares. This is not true for the nonminimally coupled field, and indeed the energy density can be made arbitrarily negative at any given point.' Barcelo-Visser gr-qc/0003025 eq.(2.5): WEC = [(1-2xi)(phi')^2 + 1/2 (grad phi)^2 + V(phi) - xi((phi^2)'' + 2 grad(phi grad phi))]/(kappa - xi phi^2) >= 0; then 'In the minimally coupled case (xi = 0) it is generically satisfied. Only a large negative potential, for example, a negative cosmological constant, could provide a violation of WEC.' Buttazzo 1307.3536 sec.2: 'we write the classical Higgs potential as V_0 = -m_0^2/2 |H_0|^2 + lambda_0 |H_0|^4'. With |H|^2 = phi^2/2 this is the tree's V(phi) = -(mu^2/2)phi^2 + (lambda/4)phi^4, mu^2 = lambda v^2.
published_hypotheses: A classical (c-number) field: Fewster's 'classical', which he contrasts with the quantum field.

A normal (non-phantom) sign for the kinetic term: L = -(1/2)(grad phi)^2 - V.
A tree-level (classical) Higgs potential with lambda > 0 (Buttazzo sec.2). Beyond tree level lambda_eff turns negative at large field (Buttazzo sec.4.2), and the tree carries that separately.

The redshift function however, does not approach a constant value as l -> infinity, so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat.'
published_hypotheses: H1: the metric is static and spherically symmetric, ds^2 = -f dt^2 + dl^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (eq. (2)).

H2: the source is the AHS analytic approximation for a massless, zero-temperature, conformally coupled (xi = 1/6) scalar, with mu absorbed into f (eqs. (4)-(7), fn [20]); G = 8 pi <T>, K^2 = 1/(5760 pi).

H3: 'for the chosen set of boundary conditions' means eq. (9) data and the ONE displayed solution, ln f(0) = -2/3. The statement does not cover the whole family, or the other solutions mentioned on p.8.

H4: F ~ (a ln l - b)^2 comes from 'combined numeric and analytic calculations', guided by the numerics, and the fitting range is not stated. The l -> infinity conclusion is therefore an extrapolation.
H5: 'asymptotically flat' is used to mean that f approaches a constant. The spatial part is called asymptotically flat 'modulo the Planck-scale wiggles'. No formal definition is given.

In terms of a physical density, this corresponds to Omega_Lambda h^2 = 0.3107 +- 0.0082, or cosmological constant Lambda = (4.24 +- 0.11) x 10^-66 eV^2'. Eq.(50): 'w0 = -1.028 +- 0.031 (68 %, Planck TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+SNe+BAO)', with wa fixed to 0. DESI DR2 abstract p.3: 'a time-evolving equation of state parametrized by w0 and wa ... provides a better fit to the data, with a favored solution in the quadrant with w0 > -1 and wa < 0 ... preferred over LCDM at 3.1 sigma for DESI BAO and CMB ... When also including SNe, the preference ... ranges from 2.8 - 4.2 sigma depending on which SNe sample is used ... Unless there is an unknown systematic error associated with one or more datasets, it is clear that LCDM is being challenged'. Conclusions p.33: 'All combinations of available datasets we study favor mutually consistent results with w0 > -1 and wa < 0, apparently indicating a weakening dark energy today and a phantom crossing at some point in the past (in this parametrization).'
published_hypotheses: Planck eq.(15): base-LCDM, spatially flat, w = -1, six parameters, one massive neutrino of 0.06 eV. Late-time parameters are model-dependent inferences, not direct measurements.
Planck: GR with a homogeneous background; Omega_Lambda is the background (spatially averaged) quantity.
Planck Sec.7.4.1 p.43: w = p/rho of the background dark-energy fluid, with PPF perturbations. 'a single minimally-coupled canonical scalar field (quintessence) cannot cross w = -1 (Vikman 2005)'.
Planck: with Planck+BAO+SNe, Delta chi^2 = -1.4 for w0wa against LCDM, 'not significant' given the two extra parameters.
DESI DR2: the CPL parametrization w(a) = w0 + wa(1-a) 'does not arise directly from an underlying physical model' (p.28), and the phantom crossing is stated only 'in this parametrization' (p.33).

DESI DR2: the significance depends on the SNe sample (Pantheon+ 2.8, Union3 3.8, DESY5 4.2 sigma) and on CMB lensing. p.29 calls the 'least contorted' reconciliation dropping SNe and treating 3.1 sigma as a fluke.
DESI DR2: 'Unless there is an unknown systematic error associated with one or more datasets'.
Both: a flat or nearly flat FLRW background in GR. Dark energy is an effective background density, not a measured local T_ab.

topology-r3-simply-connected.name: Topology: R^3 is simply connected and a wormhole spatial section is not; no continuous metric deformation on a fixed manifold changes topology

source.located: No single source: the tree cites none. create.py:24-26 and phase1.py:50-52 state it without a citation. The mathematics is standard algebraic topology (pi_1(R^3)=1; pi_1(S^1xS^2)=Z; a family of metrics on a fixed manifold leaves the manifold unchanged), and it is re-derived here. How the literature applies it to WORMHOLES was read in three places. (a) Hochberg & Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/9704082v1 (1997), abstract and sec. 1. (b) Pisana, Shoshany, Antoniou, Kauffman, Lambropoulou, arXiv:2505.02210v4, the paper create.py:125 cites: sec. I.A, sec. II (the 0-surgery list), sec. III.A (Def. 6, Thm III.1-III.2) and sec. III.D. (c) Borde, arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, sec. IX.C.
source.via: All alphaXiv calls failed this stage with 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded'. The egress proxy also refuses arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org and alphaxiv.org directly (CONNECT 403). The papers were therefore read from full-text arXiv copies that earlier stages had cached in the d67 scratchpad: 2505.02210.txt (md5 9eebbb418dc3def4701cd4b9fd83633c, header v4 20 Apr 2026), src/gr-qc_9406053.txt (md5 17c67ada52d92fc44065246ef92fee8c) and src/casmag/all/gr-qc_9704082v1.txt (md5 546e25a9a04df1ca4b59fd3277a408b3). The passages cited are READ. Morris-Thorne 1988 and Visser's 'Lorentzian Wormholes' (1995, pp. 53-74 and 89-93) are NAMED-NOT-READ.

topology-r3-simply-connected.published_statement:
No source publishes the tree's sentence as such. What the sources read here say:
2505.02210 sec. II: '3-dimensional 0-surgery: An embedding of S^0 x D^3 is replaced by D^1 x S^2 ... This surgery corresponds to the creation of a wormhole'.
2505.02210 sec. I.A: 'wormholes: handles attached to spacetime'. The same section restates Geroch: 'if the two 3-manifolds are non-homeomorphic, Geroch's second theorem requires that the spacetime contains either singularities or closed timelike curves'.
2505.02210 sec. III.D: 'all the "topological charge" is confined within a compact region'.
2505.02210 Def. 6: a spacetime carries 'an everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric'.
Hochberg-Visser, abstract: 'topology is too limited a tool to accurately characterize a generic traversable wormhole: in general one needs geometric information ... we shall define the wormhole throat in terms of a 2-dimensional constant-time hypersurface of minimal area'.
Hochberg-Visser, sec. 1: the 'Morris-Thorne class of inter-universe traversable wormholes' requires 'two asymptotically flat regions'. The same section says there are wormholes with 'trivial topology', for example 'a single closed Friedman-Robertson-Walker spacetime connected by a narrow neck to ordinary Minkowski space'.
Borde IX.C: 'Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed.'
published_hypotheses: (math) The manifold is FIXED across the family, and each g_s is a nondegenerate metric on it for every s in the CLOSED interval [0,1]. Under that hypothesis the topology cannot change, by definition.
(math) 'Wormhole' means a manifold carrying a 1-handle: R^3 # (S^1xS^2), the result of 3-dimensional 0-surgery (2505.02210 sec. II). Its pi_1 is Z.

(Hochberg-Visser) A wormhole is defined geometrically, by a throat: a constant-time 2-surface of minimal area with flare-out. Under this definition wormholes with trivial topology exist, and the Morris-Thorne inter-universe wormholes have two ends.

(2505.02210 / Geroch as restated) A topology change needs a cobordism that is not a product. For a nondegenerate, time-orientable Lorentzian metric that means CTCs or singularities. The change can be confined to a compact region.
(Borde IX.C) Degenerate metrics at isolated points allow spacetimes that change topology. This lies outside 'nondegenerate g_s on a fixed manifold'.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: the restriction to handle wormholes (intra-universe, not simply connected). create.py:24, the create.py:153 docstring, the create.py:325-326 verdict and phase1.py:50-51 all say 'a wormhole is not [simply connected]' with no qualifier. Two counterexamples, computed here: the Morris-Thorne inter-universe section R x S^2 IS simply connected (C3), and a Hochberg-Visser trivial-topology wormhole has R^3 itself as its section. The restriction is kept where the claim bears load: specthm.py:63 and specthm.py:731 ('A shortcut through non-simply-connected spatial topology'). For R x S^2 the tree's conclusion still holds, but through H_2 = Z (two ends), not through simple connectivity.

WIDENED: 'throat' used where the claim only holds for a 'handle'. Sites: phase1.py:57-58 'CREATING a throat is a TOPOLOGY problem', create.py:41-42 'CREATE bring a throat into existence ... A TOPOLOGY problem', and the canonical merged name 'cannot produce a throat'. Under Hochberg-Visser's definition this is false. C4 builds a smooth metric family on FIXED R^3 that is unchanged outside 1<r<3 and still acquires a minimal 2-sphere with flare-out (R'=0 and R''=14.2>0 at r=1.993) from s* ~ 0.277 onward. What needs a topology change is a handle or a second end, not a throat. The throat built here opens into a bounded region, not onto a shortcut, so it is not a gate.

MIS-ATTRIBUTED (a discrepancy inside the tree, not a refutation). create.py:15-16 assigns the FIXED MANIFOLD clause to D1, while phase1.py:16-17 places it in the definition's preamble. The table at create.py:18-19 and the code at create.py:138 hard-code D1 YES and D2 NO. C5 computes that the handle's topology change is confined to a ball, matching 2505.02210 III.D. So the handle does not violate compact support (D2); it violates the fixed-manifold clause. The conclusion that the gate is not a phase1 transition is unaffected.

IMPLICIT, NOW NAMED: g_s must be nondegenerate at every s in the closed interval [0,1]. The phrase 'at ANY support' at create.py:24-26 is exact only under this hypothesis. The escapes lie outside it: Borde IX.C (Horowitz) and 2505.02210 I.A (degenerate metrics, Morse singularities).

HARD-CODED: fails_on_topology() at create.py:152-155 returns the literal True, and the check at create.py:271 compares that literal with True. That is a restatement, not a computation. This audit's C2 and C5 provide the computation for the handle class.

data_at_publication.quantity: None. The result is purely topological and kinematic, so no numerical physical input enters it.
data_at_publication.value_now: n/a
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: There is no datum to move. The only empirical premise is that the background is spatially R^3. C6 shows the handle conclusion does not depend on it: H_1(T^3 # S^1xS^2) = Z^4, not Z^3, so adding a handle changes any closed background.

ALL CHECKS PASS, exit 0. Script md5 3bb36aafb9aeecae581c07ca8364aaf5; output in the adjacent .out file, md5 3e5f25964158b1e1335f150c726dd008. Homology is computed exactly, with sympy's integer Smith normal form over explicit triangulations.

later_literature.what: Defines a wormhole geometrically by a minimal-area throat with flare-out, and includes wormholes with trivial topology and two-ended inter-universe ones. So 'a wormhole is not simply connected' holds only for the handle class, and creating a throat is not in general a topology change (C4).

topology-r3-simply-connected.lacked_data:
No data enters the core claim. pi_1(R^3)=1 and pi_1(R^3#S^1xS^2)=Z are theorems, computed here exactly (C1, C2). That a nondegenerate metric family on a fixed manifold cannot change its topology is true by definition. No datum an earlier author lacked could move either. The one empirical premise, that the background is spatially R^3, is not measured at cosmological scale; the global cosmic-topology constraints are NAMED-NOT-READ. C6 shows the handle conclusion does not depend on that premise.
What changed after 1988 is the definition of a wormhole, not the data. Hochberg-Visser (1997, READ) separate the geometric throat from the topological handle and give wormholes that are simply connected or have trivial topology. Measured against that definition, the tree's unqualified sentences are too wide (C3, C4).
Evidence the other way: for the object the tree actually relies on, specthm W ('a shortcut through non-simply-connected spatial topology', specthm.py:731), the claim holds exactly, and its downstream use (W is not a phase1 transition) is untouched.
topology-r3-simply-connected.grade_evidence:
The claim stands for the class the tree's load-bearing site names. A spatial section with a handle, which is not simply connected, cannot arise from R^3 through any nondegenerate metric family on the fixed manifold, whatever the support (computed in C1, C2, C5 and C6; 2505.02210 READ).
It is narrower than the sentence as written at create.py:24, 153 and 325-326 and at phase1.py:50-51 ('a wormhole is not'), and narrower than the extension to throats at phase1.py:57-58 and create.py:41-42:
(i) the Morris-Thorne inter-universe section R x S^2 is simply connected (C3);
(ii) a Hochberg-Visser throat is produced by a compactly supported metric family on fixed R^3 (C4).
Also recorded, as a discrepancy rather than a refutation: the handle changes topology only inside a compact set (C5). So the condition it violates is the fixed-manifold clause, not D2 as hard-coded at create.py:138.
Not WRONG, because no counterexample touches the class the tree uses. Not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no datum enters.
topology-r3-simply-connected.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS, three changes to the tree's wording: limit the claim at create.py:24/153/325 and phase1.py:50-51 to handle (intra-universe) wormholes; use 'handle or second end' in place of 'throat' at phase1.py:57-58 and create.py:41-42; and name the failing condition as the fixed-manifold clause. To WRONG: a nondegenerate metric family on a fixed manifold diffeomorphic to R^3 whose endpoint has nontrivial pi_1. That is impossible, because the manifold and therefore its pi_1 are fixed. Reading Visser 1995 (NAMED-NOT-READ) could sharpen which wormhole taxonomy to cite, but cannot move the grade.

source.via: B3 was read from the arXiv v1 page text cached at d67/src/casmag/all/1510.07674v1.txt (md5 6bdffaf89a7a45b40be462d8b910098f, which the rederive script asserts; each value used is string-matched in that text). astronomical-body-data.published_statement: B3 Recommends 3: '1 R^N_sun = 6.957 x 10^8 m ... 1 (GM)^N_sun = 1.327 124 4 x 10^20 m^3 s^-2'; planetary conversion constants 'R^N_eE = 6.3781 x 10^6 m, R^N_pE = 6.3568 x 10^6 m, R^N_eJ = 7.1492 x 10^7 m, R^N_pJ = 6.6854 x 10^7 m, (GM)^N_E = 3.986 004 x 10^14, (GM)^N_J = 1.266 865 3 x 10^17 m^3 s^-2'. Recommends 1: 'conversion factors only -- chosen to be close to the current commonly accepted estimates ... not as the true solar properties.' Recommends 5: 'if SI masses are explicitly needed, they should be expressed in terms of (GM)_object/G, where the estimate of ... G should be specified'. Endnote 2: R^N_sun is based on the photospheric radius 'where tau_Ross = 2/3 ... 695 658 (+-140) km'. Explanation 6: Earth's radii are 'zero tide' equatorial and polar, and an unspecified terrestrial radius means R^N_eE. Explanation 7: Jupiter's radii are 'one-bar equatorial and polar', and an unspecified jovian radius means R^N_eJ. Endnote 4: IAU 2012 B2 'defined the astronomical unit to be ... 149 597 870 700 m exactly.'
published_hypotheses: Nominal values are exact conversion constants, not true properties; the true values carry uncertainties (Recommends 1-2).
SI masses are (GM)/G with G stated. G is 'one of the least precisely determined constants', while GM_sun is known five orders of magnitude better (Recognizing 3, Recommends 5).
R_sun is a photospheric radius (tau_Ross = 2/3), so there is atmosphere above it (endnote 2).

Earth and Jupiter are oblate, each with an equatorial and a polar radius. Jupiter's are at the 1-bar level and Earth's are zero-tide. An unspecified radius means the equatorial one (Explanations 6-7).
(GM)_J excludes the Galilean satellites; (GM)_E and (GM)_J are rounded to where TCB and TDB agree (Explanation 8).
The au is a conventional unit, exact by definition (IAU 2012 B2, via endnote 4).
The ly is not in B3: it is c x Julian year, exact given exact c and the Julian year (definition NAMED-NOT-READ).

shapiro-delay.published_statement: Will 2014 eq.(62), p.43: 'A radar signal sent across the solar system past the Sun to a planet or satellite and returned to the Earth suffers an additional non-Newtonian delay in its round-trip travel time, given by dt = 2(1+gamma) M_sun ln[ (r_E + x_E.n)(r_e - x_e.n) / d^2 ]', where x_e and x_E are the vectors, and r_e and r_E the distances, from the Sun to the source and to the Earth (TEGP 7.2). For a ray passing close to the Sun, eq. (63) gives dt ~ (1/2)(1+gamma)[240 - 20 ln(d^2/r)] microseconds. Will calls it 'Irwin Shapiro's 1964 discovery of this effect as a theoretical consequence of GR'. 1710.05834 eq.(3): dt_S = -(1+gamma)/c^3 * int U(r(l)) dl along the wave path (Shapiro 1964), which is linear in the potential U.
published_hypotheses: Weak field (PPN), first post-Newtonian order: the delay is first order in M, i.e. in U. The coefficient is (1+gamma), and gamma = 1 in GR.
The source is static, or moving uniformly to first order in v/c. Will sec. 4.1.3 records a post^{3/2}-Newtonian correction for a moving source (Kopeikin-Fomalont, Jupiter 2002).
The integral runs along the unperturbed straight line, and d is that line's closest approach to the source.
The formula is the round-trip radar form, twice the one-way delay. A one-way delay has been measured for PSR 1937+21 (Will p.43).
The source is the positive solar mass. The source makes no statement for M < 0.
For an extended source, 1710.05834 eq.(3) integrates U along the path, which is superposition (linearity in U).

gr-qc/9304008-t00-single-mode.published_statement: v1 pages 3-4, verbatim from the text layer: 'Let us consider a massless, minimally coupled scalar field for which the Lagrangian density is L = 1/2 eta^{mu nu}(d_mu phi)(d_nu phi). (2.1) The stress tensor is T_mu nu = (d_mu phi)(d_nu phi) - 1/2 eta_mu nu (d_sigma phi)(d^sigma phi) (2.2) ... phi = sum_k (a_k f_k + a_k^+ f_k^*) (2.4) ... f_k = (2 L^3 omega)^{-1/2} e^{i k_sigma x^sigma} (2.6). Here we have assumed periodic boundary conditions in a 3-dimensional box of side L ... We will here consider states where a single mode is excited ... |Psi> = sum_n c_n |n> (2.9) ... <:T_ab(x):> = sum_n (2n|c_n|^2 T_ab[f_k,f_k^*] + n^{1/2}(n-1)^{1/2} c_n c^*_{n-2} T_ab[f_k,f_k] + n^{1/2}(n-1)^{1/2} c^*_n c_{n-2} T_ab[f^*_k,f^*_k]), (2.10) where T_mu nu[g,h](x) = (d_mu g)(d_nu h) - 1/2 eta_mu nu (d_sigma g)(d^sigma h). (2.11) ... T_ab[f_k,f_k] = -K_ab e^{2 i theta}, (2.12) T_ab[f^*_k,f_k] = T_ab[f_k,f^*_k] = K_ab, (2.13) T_ab[f^*_k,f^*_k] = -K_ab e^{-2 i theta}, (2.14) where theta = k_rho x^rho and K_ab = (k_a k_b - 1/2 eta_ab k_rho k^rho)/(2 omega L^3). For the massless case k_rho k^rho = 0, so K_ab = k_a k_b/(2 omega L^3). Notice that :T_ab: = T_ab - <0|T_ab|0>; the normal ordered stress tensor in flat spacetime is the renormalized result obtained by subtracting the Minkowski vacuum expectation value.' Conventions: c = hbar = 1, eta = diag(-1,1,1,1). KF print (2.10) as an expectation value and never print the operator :T00: = K(2a+a - z a^2 - zbar a+^2) itself. It is the operator whose matrix elements give (2.10), so the tree's wording 'from KF (2.10)-(2.14)' at fluctuation.py:179 is accurate.
published_hypotheses: The scalar field is massless (k_rho k^rho = 0), (2.1).
Minimal coupling: the stress tensor (2.2) has no xi term (no R phi^2 or improvement term).
Flat Minkowski spacetime, signature (-,+,+,+), c = hbar = 1.
Free field: plane-wave modes (2.6) that solve the wave equation (2.3), with the commutation relations (2.5).
Periodic boundary conditions in a 3-box of side L. The continuum limit, via L^3/(2pi)^3 int d^3k, is available but Sec. II does not use it.
Only one mode k is excited: |Psi> = sum_n c_n |n_k>, with every other mode in the vacuum, (2.9).
Normal ordering is taken against the Minkowski vacuum, which equals subtracting <0|T_ab|0>.
theta = k_rho x^rho is real (x is a real spacetime point), so e^{-2 i theta} is the complex conjugate of e^{2 i theta}.
hypothesis_drift: No physics hypothesis is dropped. fluctuation.py:16-17 names 'normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, flat spacetime, coincidence limit, massless minimally coupled scalar'. The canonical entry's hypotheses (single plane-wave mode, z = exp(2 i theta), normal ordering) are the source's.

WORDING (fluctuation.py:179; canonical gloss 'K the mode's normalisation constant'): in the source, K = K_00 = k_0 k_0/(2 omega L^3) = omega/(2 L^3) for the massless mode (re-derived in C1). That is the mode energy over twice the box volume, not just the normalisation (2 L^3 omega)^{-1/2}. This changes no result: K stays symbolic, and every KF ratio the file re-derives (Delta, (3.8), (3.45)) is homogeneous of degree 0 in K.

SPECIALISED, NOT WEAKENED (fluctuation.py:179-180): the source's (2.12)-(2.14) hold for every component K_ab, and the tree takes only the 00 component. That is correct for its use, because KF's Delta (3.2) is the 00 component.

IMPLICIT (fluctuation.py:176-180): the tree writes the a+^2 coefficient as -K/z. That equals -K zbar only when |z| = 1 (theta real), but sympy's z is an unrestricted complex symbol, and for |z| != 1 the operator is not Hermitian (re-derived in C2). This has no consequence: an identity proved as a Laurent-polynomial identity in z also holds on |z| = 1. cos2 = (z + 1/z)/2 (fluctuation.py:177) carries the same restriction and is used consistently.
BOX DROPPED (fluctuation.py:179): L appears only inside K, and no conclusion depends on it.

SCOPE NOTE, NOT A DRIFT (fluctuation.py:189): T2 = nprod(T1, T1) is the full normal ordering of the quartic, i.e. KF's <:T00^2:>, and C5 confirms this. Whether full Minkowski normal ordering is the right renormalisation of the quartic is a separate result with its own audit (gr-qc_9304008-quartic-renormalisation).

rederivation.outcome: All 12 boolean checks pass (2.3 s). C1: (2.12)-(2.14) are recovered from (2.6)+(2.11) for all 16 components alpha,beta with generic real massless k, together with the formula for K_ab. K_00 = omega/(2L^3). C2: on an exact 10-level Fock space, T_00 is built from phi = a f + a+ f* using (2.12)-(2.14). Its vacuum value is <0|T_00|0> = K, and T_00 - K*1 equals K(2a+a - z a^2 - (1/z) a+^2) away from the truncation edge, which is KF's ':T = T - <0|T|0>'. The operator is Hermitian for real theta and not Hermitian at |z| = 2. C3: KF (2.10) is reproduced exactly from that operator for a generic state c_0..c_5, with the conjugates as independent symbols. C4: the tree's dict T1 = {(1,1): 2K, (0,2): -zK, (2,0): -K/z} (keys a+^m a^n, fluctuation.py:180) is the same matrix. C5: nprod(T1,T1) equals the square normal-ordered by hand, K^2(6 a+^2 a^2 - 4z a+ a^3 - 4zbar a+^3 a + z^2 a^4 + zbar^2 a+^4). It gives <:T00^2:> = <:T00:>^2 in every coherent state, which is KF (3.21), Delta = 0, and serves as the positive control. C7: in a state with only mode k excited and a second mode in vacuum, every cross-mode and second-mode normal-ordered bilinear has zero expectation (exact two-mode check). So reducing the field's :T00: to one mode is exact, not an approximation. C6 tests how much a named hypothesis matters. Adding a non-minimal term xi(eta_mu nu box - d_mu d_nu)phi^2 leaves the a+a coefficient unchanged (factor 1) but scales the z a^2 and zbar a+^2 coefficients by (1 - 4 xi). Conformal coupling, xi = 1/6, gives 1/3. The operator therefore depends on minimal coupling, and the tree states that hypothesis.

later_literature.what: They restate the single-mode vacuum-plus-two state class, attributing it to Ford (their [25], which is Kuo & Ford PRD 47 4510). Their smeared result is <T++> = (k/L)(1 - (sqrt3/2) cos(2 x0.k) e^{-4 tau^2 k^2}): a constant (a+a) term plus an oscillating cos(2theta) term from a^2 and a+^2, the same structure as :T00: here. The agreement is qualitative only. Their continuum delta-normalisation, 1+1 null component and smearing were not reconciled with KF's box convention, so no coefficient is compared. A naive box translation gives sqrt6/2 against their sqrt3/2; that is a question of conventions, not a finding.

hep-th/0202068.published_statement: Abstract (as excerpted): 'The ground state energy of the massive scalar field with non-conformal coupling xi on the short-throat flat-space wormhole background is calculated by using zeta renormalization approach. ... the stable configuration of wormholes can exist for xi > 0.123. In particular case of massive conformal scalar field with xi = 1/6, the radius of throat of stable wormhole a ~ 0.16/m. The self-consistent wormhole has the radius of throat a ~ 0.0141 l_P and the mass of scalar boson m ~ 11.35 m_P.'
published_hypotheses: Background is a short-throat flat-space wormhole: two copies of Minkowski space with balls cut out and the boundaries identified. r = a + |rho|, flat for rho != 0, with the curvature at the throat (R = -8 delta(rho)/a, per the later restatement).
One massive scalar field, mass m, with non-conformal coupling xi
The quantity is the ground-state energy, renormalised with zeta functions and heat-kernel coefficients
Stability means the energy has a minimum as a function of a; this exists only for xi > 0.123
For xi = 1/6 the stable throat is a ~ 0.16/m
'Self-consistent' is an extra condition that fixes m ~ 11.35 m_P and so a ~ 0.0141 l_P. Its exact form is in the body, which I did not read.
Implicit: semiclassical, one scalar only, no graviton loop. The result sits at a < l_P with m > m_P.

In KS's geometry r' jumps from -1 to +1 at the throat, so r'' = 2 delta(rho). hep-th/0202068.lacked_data: KS 2002 is a one-loop calculation on a fixed background. Its only numerical inputs are the Planck units. No later measurement bears on it: G and hbar have not moved materially, and the output lies below the Planck length, where no data exists. What the authors lacked was theory, not data: graviton loops (Garattini 2005 added them), back-reaction beyond the thin shell, and physics we can trust below l_P. Having CODATA 2022 changes no conclusion. The evidence neither supports nor refutes M's hypothesis for this result.
hep-th/0202068.grade_evidence: The number the tree seats (0.0141 l_P, xi = 1/6) matches the abstract and fits its a = 0.16/m at m = 11.35 m_P (computed). The sign 'no m < 0' survives (computed: m = 0 on both flat sides and m >= 0 under smoothing). The grade is NARROWED because 'm = r_0/2 > 0 at the throat' and the selftest cross-check assume a smooth throat, which KS's thin-shell geometry is not: r' jumps and r'' diverges. The tree also leaves out the regime below l_P / above m_P and the condition xi > 0.123. A second possible narrowing is that KS's condition is global rather than the local semiclassical equations. It is supported by the flat exterior, but the condition was NOT READ, so it stays OPEN within this grade. Nothing is WRONG. The grade rests on an abstract seen through search excerpts and a restated metric, because the body was unreadable here.
hep-th/0202068.what_would_change_the_grade: Reading the body of hep-th/0202068 at source. If its metric has a smooth throat, the smoothness drift goes away and the grade moves to STANDS. If its self-consistency condition is the local semiclassical equation, the tree's classification stands; if it is a global energy balance, it narrows further. If 0.0141 l_P is not the xi = 1/6 case, the tree's label is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

le-2026-appk-worked-burn.published_statement: Le v2 p.45, verbatim (whitespace normalized): 'Complete finite-duration maneuver (Theorem 3). We integrate the bump steering a(u) = a_max sin^2[pi(u - u_0)/(u_f - u_0)] off the static anchor x* = 0.3 with the saturated budget m(u) = m_0 e^{-3 INT|a|} and lambda_max = 0.12 < g(0.3). Le v2 p.28: 'Linear stability: marginal, conditionally burn-limited. The realized tangential-pressure wall sits exactly on the Poisson-Visser marginal curve V''(R) = 0 (App. J): a radial displacement is a neutral zero mode. Under the frozen-background rear-pole redshift the marginal wall e-folds in tau_efold = sqrt(2/|V''|), of order a light-crossing time (App. J), so the Tsiolkovsky burn outruns the instability only in a restricted high-compactness, brief-rapidity corner. A slightly stiffer, still-admissible wall is strictly stable at no cost in the surface dec margin ... this stiffened wall is a nearby model, not the realized one (App. J).' Le prints the parameters (0.24, 0.12, x* = 0.3). He does NOT print the ratio delta_eta/lambda = 2.0, and in the pages read he does NOT say whether the App. K burn passes or fails the burn-outruns-instability criterion. Both the ratio and the verdict 'fails by 2.0' are the tree's own computation.
published_hypotheses: H1 (p.45) The acceleration follows a(u) = a_max sin^2[pi(u-u_0)/(u_f-u_0)] in the canonical rocket retarded time u. It is not constant.
H2 (p.45) The burn starts (and ends) at the static anchor x* = 2m/R = 0.3.
H3 (p.45) The budget is saturated: m(u) = m_0 exp(-3 INT|a| du), i.e. the control law -m_dot >= 3 m |a| holds with equality.

H4 (p.45) The peak lambda_max = a_max R = 0.12 must lie below the dec frontier g(0.3). g(x) is the largest lambda that admits a regular admissible matched shell, and it is capped below the kinematic ceiling (1-x)/2 (p.12, eq. 28; Prop. 5).

H5 (p.45) The burn is a sequence of per-retarded-cut snapshots, i.e. adiabatic in the junction. The fully time-dependent O(mu^2) correction 'is not parametrically negligible there and remains open' (p.28).

H6 (p.28) The e-folding estimate tau_efold = sqrt(2/|V''|) is for the REALIZED tangential-pressure wall, on the marginal curve V''=0, 'under the frozen-background rear-pole redshift'. It is 'of order a light-crossing time', an order estimate whose coefficient is in App. J (not read here).

H7 (p.28) The outrun condition is stated only qualitatively: the burn outruns the instability 'only in a restricted high-compactness, brief-rapidity corner'. No numerical criterion is printed in the pages read.

0705.3704-mp-3lambda.lacked_data: This tests M's hypothesis on this result. In 2007 Flambaum had the chiral-limit picture M_p ~ Lambda_QCD, an approximate '~3', older sigma-term estimates (sigma_piN about 45-60 MeV, sigma_s poorly known) and alpha_s(M_Z) about 0.118, which is essentially today's value. Later came lattice sigma terms (FLAG 2024: S_uds = 0.093-0.109), N3LO heavy-quark matrix elements (Hill-Solon 2014), a lattice decomposition of the proton mass (chiQCD 2018) and an alpha_s average of 0.1180(9). None of it changes the conclusion. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this sentence: (a) the proportionality follows from dimensional transmutation and holds exactly in the chiral limit whatever the data (checks A1, B1); (b) the '~3' is reproduced from today's alpha_s, giving 2.6-2.8 for n_f = 3 and 3.1-3.2 for n_f = 4, and alpha_s has not moved materially since 2007; (c) the later sigma-term data limit the dropped correction to 4.5-10.9% of d ln X_q, which the sentence's '~' already allows. What the sentence does have are limitations, not data gaps: it is chiral-limit, it names no scheme, and it says nothing about how Lambda_QCD responds to v. That last question concerns physics above the electroweak scale, not missing data, and the tree is right to refuse to resolve it (address.py:331-334).
0705.3704-mp-3lambda.grade_evidence:
The published statement stands as written. M_p proportional to Lambda_QCD is exact in the chiral limit by dimensional homogeneity (sympy A1). The correction is the Feynman-Hellmann S: the residual is -S d ln X_q, 4.5-10.9% on FLAG 2024 inputs (C1). The '~3' is reproduced from alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1180 as M_p/Lambda_MSbar = 2.62-2.83 for n_f = 3 and 2.92-3.24 for n_f = 4 at 2-4 loops. The factor depends on convention, ranging 2.5-11.3 over n_f and loop order.

The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree uses the sentence for more than it says. address.py:445-446 calls it 'this project's H2', and address.py:104 defines H2 as 'Lambda_QCD ITSELF FIXED' as v varies. Checks B1-B2 show the proportionality holds equally under H1 (d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9) and under H2, which differ in K_mu (-7/9 versus -1). So the source supports the m_p = Lambda F structure that both hypotheses share, not H2 itself. Flambaum's own 'Lambda constant' is a units convention (0807.4943 p.1, read by the sibling audit).

The consequences are limited. The tree names H2 as a hypothesis, refuses to choose between H1 and H2 (address.py:331-334, 461), reports both, and never uses the factor 3 (E1). No tree number moves.

Not WRONG: there is no counterexample, and the sentence is true as written. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum that has moved changes the proportionality or the '~3'.

si-iau-constants-c-au-ly-pc.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result, and the reason is how the values are defined, not an assumption. Three of the four values are conventions rather than measurements: c has been fixed since 1983, the au since 2012 as 'a conventional unit of length ... exactly', and the parsec since 2015 as exactly 648000/pi au. A defined unit cannot be wrong for lack of data, and no measurement can move it. New data can only change what the unit is used to express, such as the physical Earth-Sun distance, which the conventional au no longer tracks by definition. The light-year is c times a conventional year. The only open choice is which year, and that is a hypothesis rather than a datum; it moves one printed row at the 4th figure (8.42 -> 8.43 ly). Before 2012 the au was a measured or derived quantity. What earlier astronomers lacked there is NAMED-NOT-READ here, and it does not matter to the tree, which uses the post-2012 defined value. Evidence either way: every literal matches its definition exactly or to 11 s.f., and no output changes. The one discrepancy found (the prose 810 AU / 2.6 ly against the code's 2002 AU / 0.084 ly) is inside the tree and is shown not to be explainable by any value of the constants.

published_hypotheses: H1 Standard-Model field content: U(1)_B is a global symmetry with no gauge field. B1 shows it CANNOT be gauged with SM fermions, because A[SU(2)^2 B] = +1/2 and A[Y^2 B] = -1/2 per generation. Adding nu_R does not rescue it.

With one nu_R per generation U(1)_{B-L} is anomaly-free (B1, all six coefficients 0) and CAN be gauged. If it were, massless and untwisted, the sibling Gauss theorem would force total B-L = 0, and so B = L, on a closed slice. Massive (Higgsed) B-L does not force the total (B5).

H3 'Total B' means the net fermion-number integral. In the SM it is not conserved: dB/dt = N_f dN_CS/dt (+ hypercharge term), so Delta B = Delta L = 3 Delta n (READ 1710.07223 p.1; B2). Only B-L is exactly conserved in the SM.

H5 (what 'not forced' means) closure imposes no constraint on the VALUE of total B. It does not mean B is topologically trivial. In the Skyrme realisation B is the degree of a map from the closed slice to SU(2) = S^3, an integer quantised by topology (B3). Anomalous changes of B are locked to the Chern-Simons winding (B2).

casimir-energy-vs-plate-mass.published_statement: The restated result, BMM eq (4.31), READ: for ideal metals 'E(0)ren_S(a) = -(pi^2/720) hbar c/a^3'. BMM p.155: 'The original Casimir result (1.3) is valid only for perfect conductors of infinitely high conductivity'. BMM eq (4.27): for a << lambda_0, E = -H/(12 pi a^2), the van der Waals limit. Fulling et al.: 'the inertial and gravitational masses of a system possessing Casimir energy E_c are both E_c/c^2.' How the tree uses it: ledger.py:1550-1552 (S2) says 'the plate outweighs its own Casimir energy for every material that exists'. ledger.py:2134-2138 (B4) sets the demand '|E_Cas| >= M c^2' against the supply '|E_Cas|/(M c^2) <= 2.72e-8 for hydrogen, the lightest conceivable sheet', status REFUSED. The reconstructed construction: two sheets at gap a0, each holding one H atom per a0^2, gives R = pi^2 hbar/(1440 a0 m_H c) = pi^2 alpha (m_e/m_H)/1440 = 2.7224e-8. One sheet at gap 2a0 gives the same formula.
published_hypotheses: Casimir, as restated: perfect conductors, two infinite parallel plates, T = 0, renormalised interaction energy, with plate self-energies outside E.
Lifshitz eq (4.26): continuum media described by eps(i xi), planar semispaces, T = 0; the ideal result is the limit eps -> oo.
Real metals: plasma model; the finite-conductivity series (5.60) holds for a >= lambda_p; at a << lambda_0 the interaction becomes van der Waals.
Fulling et al.: plates in a weak static field; the Casimir energy's inertial and gravitational masses are both E_c/c^2.
Sopova-Ford: the local density diverges at the boundaries (the continuum description breaks down there), and a single plate carries a positive self-energy, which belongs to the plate's mass.

My reconstruction reproduces it to 3 s.f., and a search over 96 simple constructions returns only this one formula. So the provenance is missing; the value is not wrong.
