casimir-energy-vs-plate-mass.lacked_data: Casimir in 1948 had no measurement and assumed perfect conductors. Lifshitz theory, measurement (Bressi 2002, 15%) and the E/c^2 gravitation result (Fulling 2007) all came later. Computed here: every later datum pushes |E_Cas| down, never up. The effects are finite conductivity (x0.20 at a = delta0), the van der Waals crossover, and the passivity bound (z3). The CODATA 2018 to 2022 update moves R by -6.7e-10. So nothing the originators lacked could lift the ratio toward 1, and the evidence runs against M's hypothesis for this result. What the tree lacked is different: it never recorded its construction, and its qualifiers outrun its number. Positronium (1.25e-5) and the tree's own nuclear density (7.43e-4) both exceed 2.72e-8, while staying below 1. The conclusion could move only through a medium that breaks H-PASSIVE (gain, |r| > 1), or a reflecting gap below 0.7% of the constituents' reduced Compton wavelength. Nothing read here shows either exists, and nothing rules them out, so both are recorded as named hypotheses.
casimir-energy-vs-plate-mass.grade_evidence: The refusal's conclusion, |E_Cas| < M c^2 (B4 REFUSED, no gap), is re-derived with a large margin. 2.7224e-8 reproduces under both CODATA vintages. The ideal formula is proved an upper bound on the Lifshitz energy for passive pairs (sympy + z3, vacuity-guarded). Casimir energy gravitates as E/c^2 (READ). The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS for three reasons. (1) The construction is recorded nowhere, and no instrument owns the literal (ledger.py:2136). (2) '<= 2.72e-8' needs hypotheses the tree drops: H-CONTINUUM, H-GAP-GE-SPACING, spacing >= a0 and site mass >= m_H. That is ordinary atomic matter, not 'the lightest conceivable sheet' (positronium gives 1.25e-5) and not 'every material that exists' (nuclear density gives 7.43e-4). (3) It also needs H-PASSIVE, H-PLANAR-INFINITE and H-T0. B4's verdict does not move: every case computed stays below 1 by at least 3.1 orders. It is not WRONG, because no counterexample to the conclusion exists here; the over-reach is a discrepancy in the number and its qualifier. The later-literature leg is OPEN because of the quota.
casimir-energy-vs-plate-mass.what_would_change_the_grade: It becomes STANDS if the tree records its construction and scopes B4 to 'site mass >= m_H, spacing >= a0, continuum, passive, T = 0', or replaces the figure with the general bound pi^2 hbar/(1440 d m c). It becomes WRONG only if some real material shows |E_Cas| >= M c^2, for example a gain medium with |r| > 1, or a mirror gap below 0.7% of the constituents' reduced Compton wavelength. It becomes DATA-DEPENDENT only if the refusal came to hinge on the third digit. A later paper exhibiting Casimir energy comparable to the apparatus's rest energy would reopen it.

gaia-dr3-proxima-distance.published_statement: The Gaia EDR3 (= DR3) parallax of Proxima Centauri is 768.066539187357 +- 0.049872905 mas at epoch J2016.0 (2104.14972 Table 1; 2512.08533 Table 2 gives '768.067 +- 0.050'). 2208.00211, abstract: 'The Gaia DR3 catalogue contains the same source list, celestial positions, proper motions, parallaxes ... already present in ... Gaia EDR3'. Sec. 3.2: 'the astrometry in Gaia DR3 is unchanged from Gaia EDR3'. Sec. 2: the catalogue is 'based on data collected over a 34-month time interval'. Sec. 3.3: 'the global parallax bias for Gaia DR3, as measured from quasars, is -17 uas ... varies as a function of magnitude, colour, and celestial position'. L21 Sec. 8: the bias 'should be subtracted from the value (parallax) given in the Archive', so the catalogue value is uncorrected, and 'Beyond the non-clamped interval 1.72 > nu_eff > 1.24 ... all results are in any case quite uncertain'. No source read states the distance 4.2465 ly. It is the tree's own inversion 1/parallax, which re-derives to 4.2464599 ly (J2016.0).
published_hypotheses: H1: a five- or six-parameter astrometric solution under the standard model of uniform linear barycentric motion, fitted to 34 months of data (2208.00211 Sec. 2-3). Proxima's solution type was not READ.
H2: the reference epoch is J2016.0 (TCB) in the Gaia-CRF3 frame, aligned to ICRF3 (2208.00211 Sec. 3.2; 2104.14972 Table 1).

H3: catalogue parallaxes carry an uncorrected zero-point bias (global quasar median -17 uas) that depends on G, colour and ecliptic latitude, plus angular covariances of ~26 uas RMS (2208.00211 Sec. 3.3; L21).
H4: the L21 zero-point recipe is 'provisional and indicative' and 'quite uncertain' outside 1.24 < nu_eff < 1.72 um^-1 (L21 Sec. 2.2, 8).
H5: the published 0.0499 mas is the formal catalogue uncertainty.
H6 (the tree's own step): distance = 1/parallax. This is safe when sigma/plx << 1; here sigma/plx = 6.5e-5 and the inversion bias is ~4e-9.

gaia-dr3-proxima-distance.lacked_data:
What DR3 had: 34 months of data, no extended mission, and a zero-point calibrated only for 1.24 < nu_eff < 1.72, a range Proxima lies outside.

What came later:
- An independent 13-year HST parallax (2512.08533) agrees within 1.2-1.7 sigma. It directly tests the colour-systematic worry for this very red star and finds nothing.
- Refined zero-point maps (2605.31402) change bright-star corrections by a few uas.
- Gaia DR4 (66 months, expected precision gain x1.4 per 2208.00211 Sec. 14) has not been READ.

Evidence either way: the datum did move once when more data arrived (DR2 -> DR3, -0.46 mas, 6e-4 relative, 2 sigma of DR2), so M's premise holds historically at the 4th figure. But the tree's conclusions are orders of magnitude (2.72e13 Msun, 48.92 orders, 5.42e42 kg). A later release would change one only by moving the parallax by a large fraction of itself, and every independent measurement READ agrees to <= 6e-4.

So missing data does not change the conclusion. It changes only the 4th-5th figures the tree prints. What the tree lacks is not data but hypotheses the datum carries: sigma, the J2016.0 epoch and the zero-point.

alcubierre-1994-metric.name: Alcubierre drive metric (tanh top-hat shape, Eulerian energy density eq 19); neither static nor spherically symmetric

source.located: M. Alcubierre, 'The warp drive: hyper-fast travel within general relativity', Class. Quantum Grav. 11 (1994) L73-L77; arXiv:gr-qc/0009013 (posted 2000, text of the 1994 paper)

Cross-read: Barzegar-Buchert-Vigneron arXiv:2602.16495 eqs (3.44)-(3.48) and Sec IV A (Error 1); Santiago-Schuster-Visser arXiv:2105.03079 eqs (2.11)-(2.12), (4.9), Sec 7.1, App. A.

alcubierre-1994-metric.published_statement: gr-qc/0009013 eq (8): ds^2 = -dt^2 + (dx - v_s f(r_s) dt)^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, with alpha = 1, beta^x = -v_s(t) f(r_s(t)), gamma_ij = delta_ij (eqs 2-5), v_s(t) = dx_s(t)/dt, r_s(t) = [(x - x_s(t))^2 + y^2 + z^2]^(1/2). Eq (6): f(r_s) = [tanh(sigma(r_s+R)) - tanh(sigma(r_s-R))]/[2 tanh(sigma R)], 'with R > 0 and sigma > 0 arbitrary parameters'. Eq (7) is the sigma -> infinity top-hat limit. Eq (19): T^{mu nu} n_mu n_nu = alpha^2 T^00 = (1/8pi) G^00 = -(1/8pi)(v_s^2 rho^2 / 4 r_s^2)(df/dr_s)^2, rho^2 = y^2+z^2. The paper then says: 'The fact that this expression is everywhere negative implies that the weak and dominant energy conditions are violated. In a similar way one can show that the strong energy condition is also violated.' Figure 1 uses sigma = 8 and R = v_s = 1. The tree's scope sentence ('the Alcubierre drive is neither [static nor spherically symmetric]') is not in the paper. It is a property of eq (8), and E5 checks it.
published_hypotheses: General relativity with G = c = 1. The metric is PRESCRIBED and T_mu_nu is read off as G_mu_nu/8pi; there is no matter model.
3+1 form with unit lapse (Eulerian observers are geodesic), flat spatial slices gamma_ij = delta_ij, and a shift only along x.
The bubble centre moves on an arbitrary trajectory x_s(t), and v_s(t) = dx_s/dt. The bubble velocity and the shift amplitude are the SAME function (eq 3 and the definition under it).
f is the specific tanh form (6) with arbitrary R > 0 and sigma > 0. The physical discussion (tidal forces, eqs 14-17) assumes large sigma and R << d << D.
The energy density is stated only for the Eulerian observers n^mu = (1/alpha)(1, -beta^i) (eqs 18-19). The SEC violation is asserted, not shown.
Global hyperbolicity is claimed from positive-definiteness of gamma_ij alone (text after eq 1). BBV 2602.16495 Error 1 shows this argument is incomplete.

alcubierre-1994-metric.lacked_data: No measured datum enters this result. It is a prescribed metric plus its Einstein tensor, and eq (19) re-derives exactly for a generic shift (E1), so no later measurement can move it. What the author lacked in 1994 was later analysis, not data. (i) An explicit NEC proof (Alcubierre-Lobo; SSV): it strengthens the energy-condition conclusion. (ii) A correct global-hyperbolicity argument: BBV Error 1 shows the 1994 argument is incomplete, but the tree does not rest on that sentence. (iii) The Type IV character of the stress tensor: the tree measures it itself, and it carries over to the true moving bubble (E6b). Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: every part the tree uses re-derives exactly. Evidence for it, on a smaller scale: the source's global-hyperbolicity sentence is incomplete, and its SEC claim was unproved in 1994 (it was later proved true).
alcubierre-1994-metric.grade_evidence: The source itself holds as the tree needs it. Eqs (6), (8) and (19) re-derive exactly (E1), and the scope claims at certify.py:181-183 and nonstatic.py:240-242 are correct (E5; SSV App. A agrees). The grade is NARROWED because of how the tree uses it. (a) The tree codes a frozen bubble (typefour.py:138, twist.py:174): x_s is held fixed while v_s = 0.5, which contradicts the source's v_s = dx_s/dt. This is immaterial for eq (19) and for every anec.py number, which are identical on the moving bubble to rel 1e-9. It is material for typefour.py's printed tensor table, where 6 of 7 points change, though the Type IV verdict survives. (b) anec.py's 'every ray' headline rests on one parameter point and five forward fixed-y curves, and only y = 0 is a null geodesic (E7). On that ray the affine ANEC integral is negative (-0.0772 moving), so the violation is confirmed on one genuine geodesic; the opposite-directed axis ray is positive. Nothing is WRONG: no computed contradiction of the source, and none of any number the tree prints.
alcubierre-1994-metric.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the frozen-bubble hypothesis (or recomputes with d_t = -v_s d_x, which leaves anec.py unchanged) and restates anec.py's headline as an ANEC violation on the axis null geodesic at sigma = 8, R = 1, v_s = 0.5, with the off-axis curves described as non-geodesic T_kk integrals. To WRONG: a computed contradiction of eq (19), or a positive affine ANEC integral on every complete null geodesic through the moving bubble. Neither was found. A Killing-algebra proof that no SO(3) acts would close the symmetry sub-claim, which was checked here only for rotations about the bubble centre.

acoustic-metric-analogue.name: Acoustic (analogue-gravity) metric in PG form, -c_s^2 dt^2 + (dr - v dt)^2 + r^2 dOmega^2, for rho/c_s constant; acoustic horizon at |v| = c_s

source.located: M. Visser, 'Acoustic black holes: horizons, ergospheres, and Hawking radiation', Class. Quantum Grav. 15 (1998) 1767, arXiv gr-qc/9712010v2 (15 Dec 1997). Read: Theorem p.3, eqs (4),(28),(29) p.8, (35) p.10, (44)-(45) p.13, sec 7 (49)-(53) pp.14-15, sec 8 (54)-(57) p.16, (59)-(65) p.18. Cross-read: Barcelo-Liberati-Visser, 'Analogue gravity', Living Rev. Rel., arXiv gr-qc/0505065v4 (2024). Unruh 1981 (PRL 46, 1351) is pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ; it is known here only through Visser's and the Living Review's restatement.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9712010 (page text pp.1-27) and on gr-qc/0505065 (pp.13-43, 74-75)

acoustic-metric-analogue.published_statement: Visser 1998, Theorem (p.3): 'If a fluid is barotropic and inviscid, and the flow is irrotational (though possibly time dependent) then the equation of motion for the velocity potential describing an acoustic disturbance is identical to the d'Alembertian equation of motion for a minimally coupled massless scalar field propagating in a (3+1)-dimensional Lorentzian geometry.' Eq (29): ds^2 = (rho_0/c)[-c^2 dt^2 + (dx^i - v_0^i dt) delta_ij (dx^j - v_0^j dt)]. Sec 7, on PG Schwarzschild: 'the constant time spatial slices are completely flat'. Setting rho and c constant with v = sqrt(2GM/r) 'is incompatible with the continuity equation'. The best achievable is c = 1 with rho ~ r^{-3/2} (eq 53), which is 'conformal to the Painleve-Gullstrand form of the Schwarzschild geometry but not identical to it'. Sec 8, canonical acoustic black hole: rho and c constant, v = c r0^2/r^2, eq (55). Eq (35): g_tt = -[c^2 - v^2], so any supersonic region is an ergo-region. p.13 / eq (45): 'The acoustic event horizon forms once the radial component of the fluid velocity exceeds the speed of sound'. p.21: the horizon is where v_perp = c, and 'it is essential that we use the natural Newtonian time coordinate'.
published_hypotheses: H1 barotropic fluid (rho = rho(p)); Visser notes this is weaker than Unruh's isentropic assumption
H2 inviscid; viscosity adds a term that is not of d'Alembertian form (Visser eq 106)
H3 locally irrotational flow (a velocity potential on an atlas of patches); distributed vorticity takes the wave equation outside the d'Alembertian form (Living Review 2.11.3)
H4 linearised fluctuations about a background (rho_0, p_0, psi_0)
H5 the background itself solves continuity and Euler, with pressure, Newtonian gravity and an arbitrary gradient-derived external body force, all fixed with no back-reaction (Visser eqs 5-7)
H6 (3+1) dimensions: the conformal factor is rho/c only for d = 3, and (rho/c)^{2/(d-1)} in general (Living Review eq 130)
H7 horizons are defined with the lab (Newtonian) time; the ergosurface |v| = c and the horizon v_perp = c are distinct, and coincide only for flow normal to the surface
H8 non-relativistic fluid; the relativistic acoustic metric reduces to rho/c when p << rho (Living Review eqs 161-163)

rederivation.outcome: All 24 checks pass (exit 0), plus one recorded discrepancy. (1) Visser eq 29 with rho = k c is exactly k[-c^2 dt^2 + (dr - v dt)^2 + r^2 dOmega^2], with c = c(r) allowed. (2) On lab slices W = 1 exactly and the slice 3-Ricci scalar is 0. In general W = 1 + r d/dr log sqrt(rho/c), which matches drivensource.py:211. (3) g_tt = 0 at v^2 = c^2, and radial null speeds are v +- c. Misner-Sharp gives 1 - 2m/R = 1 - v^2/c^2, so for radial flow the acoustic horizon is the marginally trapped surface 2m = R. The identity W^2 = 1 - 2m/R + U^2 holds with U = v/c. (4) Swirl separates the ergosurface from the horizon. (5) The canonical acoustic black hole satisfies continuity, has its horizon at r0, and eq (57) re-derives through Visser's eq (62). (6) rho/c constant with varying rho is lawful. (7) The eq 53 background has W = 1/4. (8) A lawful inhomogeneous background has W = 1 + alpha/2 > 1. (9) Milne slicing gives W = cosh(chi). DISCREPANCY, not a refutation: eq (56), with its +/- matched to eq (55), leaves a cross term 2c r0^2/r^2. Visser's eq (62) gives the opposite sign, so (56) reads as a sign misprint in arXiv v2. acoustic-metric-analogue.lacked_data: In 1997 Visser had the Newtonian fluid equations and Unruh's 1981 construction; no analogue horizon had been built. Later came laboratory sonic horizons in water-wave and BEC experiments (cited in 2106.03960, NAMED-NOT-READ here). Later work also showed that real media are dispersive, so the acoustic metric holds only in the long-wavelength hydrodynamic limit. That adds a hypothesis; it does not correct the result. None of this changes the conclusion the tree uses, and the reason is computed: W = 1 on lab slices for rho/c constant, and the horizon at |v| = c for radial flow, are exact algebraic properties of the background metric with no measured input. Dispersion changes what propagates on the geometry, not the geometry of the slices. Later theory moved a neighbouring claim instead: Visser's 'impossible to be identical to Schwarzschild' is contested by 2106.03960, using inhomogeneous rho/c. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this item: no datum was missing. The tree's use is narrower than it reads because of theory, not data: W = cosh chi on Milne slices of the same geometry, and W = 1 + alpha/2 in the inhomogeneous case. Both are computed here.
acoustic-metric-analogue.grade_evidence: What stands, computed: with rho/c_s constant, Visser's eq 29 is exactly the tree's line element. Its lab slices are exactly flat (3-Ricci scalar 0), so W = 1 exactly. The tree's inhomogeneous formula W = 1 + r d/dr log sqrt(rho/c_s) is exact. For radial flow the horizon is at |v| = c_s and coincides with the marginally trapped surface 2m = R. No datum can move any of this. What narrows it is four hypotheses the tree relies on but does not write at the owner site. (a) The lab-time foliation behind 'THE ANALOGUE CANNOT EXHIBIT CONTRACTION AT ALL' (drivensource.py:209-210): the tree's own nonstatic.py:209-215 says W depends on the slicing, and Milne slicing of the same geometry gives W = cosh chi. (b) Purely radial flow, for horizon = |v| = c_s. (c) The continuity constraint on v. (d) Visser's H1-H4, which appear at wavecorridor.py:30-33 but not in the owner. It is not WRONG: nothing fails inside the stated scope, and the rho/c-constant scope is written at drivensource.py:204 and 268-269. Against over-reading it the other way: the lab foliation is the physically distinguished one (Visser p.21), and the tree refused the inhomogeneous case, which is where W > 1 lives. The source's eq (56) sign misprint is recorded as a discrepancy and does not touch the tree.
acoustic-metric-analogue.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: scope the owner sentence to 'lab-time slices, rho/c_s constant, radial flow'. That is a wording change; every computation already agrees. To WRONG: a lawful rho/c-constant radial background with W != 1 on lab slices. That is impossible, because the slice metric is identically k(dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2) (rederivation section 2). A radial flow whose horizon is not at |v| = c_s would also do it. DATA-DEPENDENT is unavailable, because no measured constant enters. Reading the CQG print of Visser 1998 would settle whether the eq (56) sign error appears only on arXiv.

bekenstein-bound.name: Bekenstein bound S <= 2 pi R E/(hbar c), 'saturated by black holes' (bounds.py) and evaluated for a 70 kg body at R = 1 m (massform.py)

source.located: J. D. Bekenstein, Phys. Rev. D 23, 287 (1981), which has no arXiv copy. Read through Bekenstein's own restatement, arXiv quant-ph/0404042v1 (Found. Phys. 35, 1805 (2005)), Eq. (1) p.1 and pp.1-3, 6, 8. The saturation clause is restated in Bousso, arXiv hep-th/0203101v2 (RMP 74, 825) Sec. II.B pp.8-10. G-independence is from Bousso, hep-th/0402058v2 p.5. The proven form is from Casini, arXiv 0804.2182v3, pp.1-8.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on quant-ph/0404042, hep-th/0203101, hep-th/0402058, 0804.2182, 2309.07436, 1804.10623 and 2602.03606. Bekenstein 1981 itself is NAMED-NOT-READ. Longo-Xu 1802.07184 and Longo 2409.14408 are NAMED-NOT-READ; they are restated in Page 1804.10623 p.9 and in Hollands-Longo-Morsella 2602.03606 Prop. 2.1.

bekenstein-bound.published_statement: Bekenstein, quant-ph/0404042 p.1: 'the entropy of a complete physical system in asymptotically flat D = 4 spacetime, whose total mass-energy is E, and which fits inside a sphere of radius R, is necessarily bounded from above: S <= 2 pi E R / hbar c. (1)'. Further, 'E is to be interpreted as the gravitating energy of the system', and 'the universal bound is relevant only for weakly self-gravitating isolated physical systems'. Saturation, Bousso hep-th/0203101 p.9: 'A Schwarzschild black hole in four dimensions has R = 2E. Hence, its Bekenstein entropy, S = A/4 = pi R^2, exactly saturates the Bekenstein bound (Bekenstein, 1981). In D > 4, black holes come to within a factor 2/(D-2) of saturating the bound.' No G, hep-th/0402058 p.5: 'The absence of Newton's constant ... remains nontrivial when gravity is turned off completely (G = 0).' Proven form, Casini 0804.2182 p.6: the vacuum-subtracted entropy is at most the vacuum-subtracted modular energy, which is the positivity of relative entropy. For a half-space it approaches (1) with lambda = 2 pi.
published_hypotheses: COMPLETE system: E is the total gravitating energy, including rest energy, walls and ground-state energy (quant-ph/0404042 pp.1, 2, 8)
WEAKLY SELF-GRAVITATING and isolated (quant-ph/0404042 p.1; hep-th/0203101 pp.6, 8)
asymptotically flat, D = 4

R is the radius of the smallest circumscribing sphere, on an almost-Euclidean slice. There is no consensus on R or on the coefficient (Casini p.3; quant-ph/0404042 p.1 gives 'a larger numerical coefficient' under quantum buoyancy)
not valid inside black holes or for large pieces of the universe (quant-ph/0404042 pp.1-2)
SATURATION holds for Schwarzschild in D = 4 with R taken from the horizon area. This extrapolates the bound to a strongly gravitating spherical object (hep-th/0203101 pp.9-10)

PROVEN FORM (Casini 2008 / Longo-Xu / Longo 2025 / HLM 2026): S is the vacuum-subtracted entropy or vacuum relative entropy, E is the vacuum-subtracted modular energy, and R is the half-width or the distance to the Rindler boundary. The proof holds in flat, fixed geometry

bekenstein-bound.lacked_data: Bekenstein in 1981 lacked no measured datum; the bound's only inputs are hbar and c. He lacked three things that came later: a definition of S, E and R in QFT (Casini 2008, Longo-Xu 2018, Longo 2025); the quantum-buoyancy objection (Unruh-Wald 1982), which he answers with a larger coefficient; and a resolution of the species problem. Having them does change the bare 1981 form: Page 1804.10623 shows violations under naive definitions, and the proven version bounds redefined quantities. It does not change the tree's conclusions. First, K = 0 rests on the Schwarzschild identity, which is algebraic (rederive A). Second, G = 0 is confirmed at source (Bousso; Hayden-Wang p.1). Third, massform's instance is complete and weakly gravitating (2GM/c^2R = 1e-25), with x ~ 1e45, far outside every published counterexample regime, and massform already declines to read the figure as a capacity. Fourth, 'it bounds by energy; it supplies none' holds in every formulation read. What the later reading removes is only the generalisation 'saturated by black holes'.
bekenstein-bound.grade_evidence: massform.py uses the bound as published: E = Mc^2, R = 1 m, read as an upper bound and not as a capacity. Its figures all re-derive (1.8038e45, 1.58e45, 7478, 0.134 mm), and no moved datum moves them. The narrowing is bounds.py's clause 'saturated by black holes' (bounds.py:315, :49, :97). At source this holds only for Schwarzschild in D = 4 (hep-th/0203101 p.9). Computed here, it fails for Reissner-Nordstrom (r+/2M < 1 when Q != 0), depends on the choice of R for Kerr, and gives 2/(D-2) for D > 4. The saturating object is also outside the weak-gravity hypothesis, which the tree does not carry (quant-ph/0404042 p.1; hep-th/0203101 pp.6, 9-10). No pin moves: K = 0 needs one saturating case, and Schwarzschild is one. G = 0 is confirmed at source. The S = 0 / B = 1 coding discrepancy is recorded separately and is not part of this grade.

integral-monotonicity.name: Monotonicity of an integral: u < 0 throughout implies INT 4 pi r^2 u dr < 0

source.located: No arXiv source exists for this. It is a textbook theorem of Lebesgue integration: for measurable f >= 0, INT_E f = 0 implies f = 0 a.e. on E, so a u that is negative a.e. and has r^2 u in L^1 gives INT u < 0. The textbook statement (e.g. Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis, Thm 1.39(a)) is NAMED-NOT-READ. The physics form, monotonicity and positivity of the Misner-Sharp mass starting from a regular centre, was READ at source in Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', gr-qc/9408002 (1994, revised 1995).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9408002, reading: Prop 5 (monotonicity, p.8); Prop 6 (positivity, p.9: 'By Proposition 5, since E = 0 at a regular centre'); eq (21), the explicit integral; eq (32a) E' = 4 pi r^2 rho r' (p.12); Prop 9, E = (4/3) pi r^3 T00 + O(r^4) at a regular centre; the regular centre defined on p.4 ('E = O(r^3) at a regular centre'). The tree's G2 is Prop 6 with the sign flipped: u < 0 stands where Hayward has the DEC.

integral-monotonicity.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002, Prop 5: 'If the dominant energy condition holds on an untrapped sphere, E is non-decreasing (respectively non-increasing) in any outgoing (respectively ingoing) spatial or null direction.' Prop 6: 'If the dominant energy condition holds on an untrapped spatial hypersurface with regular centre, then E >= 0 on the hypersurface. Proof. By Proposition 5, since E = 0 at a regular centre.' Eq (32a), perfect fluid: E' = 4 pi r^2 rho r'. Analysis form (NAMED-NOT-READ): u measurable, r^2 u in L^1(0,R), u < 0 a.e. on (0,R], R > 0 => INT_0^R 4 pi r^2 u dr < 0.
published_hypotheses: spherical symmetry (Hayward assumes it throughout)
regular centre: g^-1(dr,dr) - 1 = O(r^2), hence E = O(r^3) -> 0 at r = 0 (Hayward p.4)
a sign condition on the source over the whole region (Hayward: the DEC, T_{+-} >= 0 and T_{--} >= 0; analysis form: u < 0 a.e.)
untrapped hypersurface, outgoing direction: the areal radius increases along the path, r' > 0 in eq (32a)
analysis form: u measurable and r^2 u integrable on (0,R]; strictness needs u < 0 on a set of positive measure
implicit in E(R) = INT E': E absolutely continuous along the hypersurface (Hayward integrates eq (21) without stating this and assumes smoothness)
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED IN THE CANONICAL ENTRY, CARRIED BY THE TREE. The entry lists only 'integrable u on the ball'. Getting m(R) = INT_0^R 4 pi r^2 u dr also needs m(0+) = 0 (regular centre) and m absolutely continuous. tolman.py:931-936 (refusal 3) names exactly this: 'r^3 p_r must be absolutely continuous on (0, R] with a limit at 0'. So the tree does not drop the hypothesis, but refusal 5 (tolman.py:940-942) relies on refusal 3 without cross-referencing it. This audit shows the hypothesis is load-bearing: m(r) = -r + 2 Cantor(r) has m' = -1 < 0 a.e. and m(0) = 0, yet m(1) = +1 > 0 (rederive layer C).

'THROUGHOUT' IS LOAD-BEARING, AND THE TREE KEEPS IT (tolman.py:590, 'u < 0 THROUGHOUT implies m < 0'). With only u <= 0, m = 0 is reachable (DRIFT Z1). With one positive cell, m > 0 is reachable (DRIFT Z2). Witnesses W3/W4 at tolman.py:580-588 already show that u(R) < 0 at a single radius is neither necessary nor sufficient. No drift.

DROPPED BUT SATISFIED BY THE CHART. Hayward's orientation hypothesis (untrapped, r' > 0 in eq 32a) is not stated by the tree. The tree works in the static areal-radius chart ds^2 = -e^{2Phi}dt^2 + e^{2Lambda}dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (tolman.py:309-313), where r is itself the coordinate, so r' = 1, and V8 computes dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 u. The chart absorbs the hypothesis. It would matter only at a throat, where r is non-monotone, and the tree handles that case separately (tolman.py:325-337, the Phi' = 0 wormhole branch).

INTERNAL DISCREPANCY IN THE TREE, NOT IN THE SOURCE (recorded, not repaired). tolman.py:590-591 and 940-942 say G2 'is machine-checked only on the power-law family where the integral is algebraic'. But tolman.py:2235-2241 says the G2/G3 rows 'contain NO variable u and no power law' and that the integral's sign 'is ASSERTED in the hypothesis as s*A < 0 and is nowhere established here'. The z3 rows (tolman.py:2256-2260) agree with the second reading: A is a free real and s*A < 0 is given, not derived. So the docstrings claim more machine-checking than exists, in the tree's favour. The power-law case is true, and it is now checked outside the tree (rederive layer S): INT_0^R 4 pi r^2 (-a r^k) dr = -4 pi a R^{k+3}/(k+3) < 0 for every k > -3.

rederivation.outcome: All rows pass; exit 0. Layer S (sympy): for the power-law family u = -a r^k, the closed form -4 pi a R^{k+3}/(k+3) is verified and negative at k = -5/2, -2, -1, 0, 1, 7/3 and 5. The general antiderivative is -4 pi a r^{k+3}/(k+3), and its centre term goes to 0 exactly when k > -3. At k = -3 and k = -4 the integral diverges, so the regular centre fails. Layer N (numeric, 20 digits): five non-algebraic negative choices of u all give INT < 0: exp, an atan-type case, the oscillatory -(2+sin 1/r), the unbounded but integrable -log(1+1/r), and -exp(-r^2)(1.5+cos 40r). Layer Z (z3): the finite simple-function version is unsat for n = 1..10 (w_i > 0, u_i < 0 and SUM w_i u_i >= 0 cannot all hold), and the hypothesis set alone is sat, so the check is not vacuous. DRIFT Z1: with u <= 0, SUM = 0 is sat. DRIFT Z2: with one u_i > 0, SUM > 0 is sat. Layer C (numeric): the Cantor counterexample m = -r + 2C(r) has m(0) = 0 and m(1) = +1, with slope -1 on removed intervals of total measure 1, so the a.e. version fails without absolute continuity. Layer P: the route through an everywhere-differentiable m and the mean value theorem needs no integrability; this is stated, not machine-checked. The general Lebesgue theorem itself is not machine-checked here: Lean and Coq cannot be installed (elan and opam are blocked) and z3 has no integral. What was checked is the finite z3 version plus the sympy and numeric instances.

integral-monotonicity.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not reach this result. It is a theorem of real analysis with no empirical input, so no datum found later, or now, can move it. The evidence either way: every checked instance of the re-derivation agrees, and the finite z3 version discharges for n = 1..10. Each way the conclusion can fail is exhibited here, and each breaks a hypothesis the tree already names: u <= 0 only, one positive cell, m not absolutely continuous, or a non-integrable centre (k <= -3). The relevant hypotheses are 'throughout' (tolman.py:590) and the regular centre plus absolute continuity (tolman.py:931-936). The gap the tree has is internal, not external: the power-law case its docstrings call machine-checked (tolman.py:590-591, 940-942) is not encoded in any row (tolman.py:2235-2241, 2256-2260). That is a discrepancy in the docstrings, not an error in the cited theorem.
integral-monotonicity.grade_evidence: The statement as used (tolman.py:590, 940-942, 2256-2258: u < 0 throughout (0,R] => m < 0) is the textbook strict monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral plus the fundamental theorem of calculus under a regular centre. Its GR form, with the sign flipped, is Hayward gr-qc/9408002 Props 5-6, read at source. Where each hypothesis lives: integrability in the canonical entry; regular centre and absolute continuity in the tree's refusal 3 (tolman.py:931-936); 'throughout' at tolman.py:590; areal-radius orientation absorbed by the static chart (tolman.py:309-313). The re-derivation agrees: sympy on the power-law family, five non-algebraic numeric cases, the z3 finite version for n = 1..10 with a non-vacuity check and two drift rows, and the Cantor counterexample showing absolute continuity is needed. No datum enters. Recorded separately and not graded against the source: the tree's docstrings claim a power-law machine-check that its z3 rows do not contain.
integral-monotonicity.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree's use turned out to depend on any of: negativity only a.e. with m not absolutely continuous; a u whose r^2 u is not integrable at the centre (k <= -3); or a chart where the areal radius is non-monotone (a throat). None of these was found at the owner lines. WRONG only on a counterexample that meets every hypothesis (u < 0 on (0,R], r^2 u in L^1, m(0+) = 0, m absolutely continuous) and still has m(R) >= 0, which the theorem rules out. 1206.5618.name: C. Wang, 'von Laue's theorem and its applications', arXiv:1206.5618v12 = Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470-1476 (2015), eq. (20): the Gauss-law identity oint_S dS_l (Omega^{l mu} X^i) = int_V (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x. tolman.py uses it in its divergence-free form, traced on a sphere.

source.located: arXiv:1206.5618v12, the version alphaXiv serves. Its text layer carries the journal pagination Can. J. Phys. 93: 1470-1476 (2015), doi 10.1139/cjp-2015-0198 (received 26 Mar 2015, accepted 15 Jun 2015). Eq. (20) is on journal p. 1474, Sect. 6. First arXiv submission 2012. The tree cites both the arXiv id and the CJP reference.
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) returned the whole paper. answer_pdf_queries re-read pp. 1-7. Both are text layers of the same PDF, and the Greek letters and operators in the displayed equations are lost. The operators in eq. (20) were recovered from the paper's own glyph use: in footnotes 8/9 (p. 1472) the same two glyphs can only mean '=' and '+'. The product rule printed just above (20), and Wang's own following sentence ('from (20), with d/dt=0 and d_nu Omega^{mu nu}=0 => d_l Omega^{l mu}=0 ... we have int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x = 0' when the boundary term vanishes), fix the form. So the operators are an inference from the text layer, not a glyph read. Re-derivations C1/C2 confirm the recovered form exactly.

1206.5618.published_statement: Sect. 6, p. 1474: 'From differential rules, we have d_k(Omega^{k mu} X^nu) = (d_k Omega^{k mu}) X^nu + Omega^{nu mu} ... where k, mu, nu = 1, 2, 3, and 4. With dOmega/dt = 0 => dOmega/dX^4 = 0 taken into account, from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law we have  oint_S dS_l (Omega^{l mu} X^i) = int_V [(d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i] d^3x + int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x   (20)  (i, l = 1, 2, 3 for left-divergence and row-four-vector)'. Eq. (21) is the transposed form, and Wang notes 'If Omega^{mu nu}(x) is symmetric, (20) and (21) are the same.' Then: '... from (20), with dOmega/dt = 0 and d_nu Omega^{mu nu} = 0 => d_l Omega^{l mu} = 0 taken into account we have int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x = 0' (when the boundary term vanishes). Sect. 2: 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected.' Metric diag(-1,-1,-1,+1), index 4 = time. Ref. [1]: 'M. von Laue. Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911).'
published_hypotheses: Omega^{mu nu}(x) is a four-tensor in the laboratory frame and need not be symmetric; index 4 = time; metric diag(-1,-1,-1,+1)
time-independent: dOmega/dt = 0, so the 3-divergence d_l Omega^{l mu} equals the 4-divergence
V is any spatial domain with closed boundary S and can be multiply connected; no ball, no shape and no symmetry of the source is required

eq. (20) itself does NOT assume divergence-free: the term int_V (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i is kept. Divergence-free is the specialization Wang applies afterwards, to the left divergence (first index contracted)

implicit, stated only as 'from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law': Omega^{l mu} X^i must be regular enough on the closure of V for the divergence theorem (C^1, or distributional with integrable divergence and no interior singular sources)
Omega^{i4} = 0 is a hypothesis of Wang's von Laue theorem, NOT of eq. (20)
hypothesis_drift: STATEMENT FORM, not a content drift -- tolman.py:131-133 quotes as 'eq. (20)' the divergence-free specialization, oint_S dS_l(Theta^{l mu} X^i) = int_V Theta^{i mu}. The published (20) keeps the term int_V (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i. The tree names 'divergence-free' as a hypothesis, so nothing is dropped, and this is the same step Wang takes in Sect. 6. C1b shows the hypothesis is load-bearing: the residual without it is 28 pi R^5/15.

ADDED, and stronger than the source in the conservative direction -- tolman.py:566-567 says 'Wang's eq. (20) needs the REGION to be a ball'. The source allows any V, even a multiply connected one (p. 1471). Only the tree's own trace step needs a sphere centred on the origin of X^i (X^i = R n^i). This is a discrepancy about what the cited equation needs, not a narrowing, because the tree only uses balls. C2 verifies (20) on a cube.

WEAKENED AT THIS SITE, CARRIED ELSEWHERE -- tolman.py:567 says 'THE SOURCE MAY BE ANYTHING' and leaves Gauss-theorem regularity throughout V implicit in 'divergence-free'. The tree names regularity elsewhere: tolman.py:1198 lists 'regular_centre' and 'ball_excludes_walls', and tolman.py:547-549 refuses the Coulomb field and any ball enclosing a mirror. But regular_centre (tolman.py:931-936) is a CENTRE condition. A non-spherical source (F5/F6) needs regularity THROUGHOUT V, so an off-centre point singularity is not excluded. C5 computes the failure: on a shell the identity is exact, but on a ball around a Coulomb charge LHS = -q^2/(8 pi R) and RHS = +infinity. Proposed named hypothesis: SOURCE-REGULAR-THROUGHOUT-V. No tree site violates it.

UNSTATED, HARMLESS -- (20) is the LEFT-divergence form. For a non-symmetric tensor the second-index form (21) differs, and C7 shows that left-divergence-free does not give it. The tree's Theta is a symmetric stress-energy tensor and tolman.py:131-138 does not state symmetry, but no site uses a non-symmetric tensor.

CONVENTION, NOT DRIFT -- Wang's signature is diag(-1,-1,-1,+1), where T^r_r = -T^{rr}. In the tree's mostly-plus convention T^r_r = T^{rr} = p_r (tolman.py:135), so the tree's reading is correct in its own convention (C8). The upper spatial block is the pressure tensor in both: Wang Sect. 4 has T^{ii} = 0.5 eps0 E^2 = W_em.

LABEL DISCREPANCY -- tolman.py:128-130 calls eq. (20) 'von Laue's theorem ... in its finite-volume form'. In Wang, the theorem is the four-vector criterion, eqs. (1)-(3), and (20) is a Sect. 6 lemma. The content the tree takes (the volume stress integral is a surface term) is what (20) says. Giulini 1808.09320 eqs. (18)-(19) and Pinto-Avelino 2502.10427 eq. (24) give it the same role.

later_literature.ref: D. Giulini, arXiv:1808.09320 (2018), Sect. 1.5 eqs. (18)-(20), Theorem 1
later_literature.what: States the same identity independently: the product rule plus Gauss's theorem for a conserved, stationary T gives int_Sigma T^{mu n} d_n phi = int_{dSigma} T^{mu n} phi nu_n. Taking phi = x^m gives the tree's short form. It makes two points explicit. First, stationarity is enough and Laue's T^{0m}=0 is not needed for this step, which matches the tree. Second, the boundary term vanishes only if T = 0 on the boundary or falls off faster than 1/r^3. In the tree's finite-radius use the boundary term is kept and is the quantity read.

later_literature.ref: D. Giulini, arXiv:1808.09320, footnote 5 (p. 13), on Wang CJP 93, 1470 (2015)
later_literature.what: Calls Wang's derivation 'logically incomplete'. The third line of Wang's eq. (6) changes the integration hyperplane from t'=const to t=const, which does not follow from t-independence without local conservation (a 'petitio principii'). This contests Wang's Sect. 2 necessity proof and, by extension, his verdict that the Landau-Lifshitz and Weinberg versions are 'flawed'. Giulini Sect. 1.6 instead explains those examples as violating Laue completeness. It does NOT touch eq. (20), the only part the tree uses. The tree should not import Wang's other claims.

Eq. (24) restates the identity int_Sigma T^{mu i} d^3x = int_{dSigma} T^{mu j} x^i n_j dS for a time-independent, divergence-free T, in signature (-,+,+,+) as the tree uses. Eq. (42) bounds the finite-radius residual, |

_r/_r| <= m_out/(m - m_out), but only under the dominant energy condition. The tree does not assume DEC, so the bound does not transfer to the tree's DEC-violating sources.

1206.5618.lacked_data: M's hypothesis has no purchase on this result, and the evidence runs against it. Eq. (20) is the product rule plus the three-dimensional divergence theorem, applied to a time-independent tensor. It takes no measured input, so there is no datum Wang (2012 arXiv / 2015 CJP) could have lacked. The evidence: it is re-derived exactly here on a ball and on a cube, for generic tensors and for a non-constant non-spherical divergence-free one (16/16 checks), and Giulini (2018, eqs. 18-19) and Pinto & Avelino (2025, eq. 24) restate it independently. Later work adds scope, not data. Giulini makes the boundary and fall-off conditions and the stationarity-versus-staticity distinction explicit, and contests Wang's separate Sect. 2 necessity proof, which the tree does not use. The limits that matter to the tree are hypotheses, not data: regularity throughout V (C5), time-independence (C6), symmetry and index order (C7) and sign convention (C8). Each is now a named hypothesis with a computed failure case.
1206.5618.grade_evidence: What the tree uses (tolman.py:131-138) is the divergence-free, time-independent form ∮ dS_l Θ^{lμ}X^i = ∫_V Θ^{iμ}, traced on a sphere to 4πR³⟨T^r_r⟩(R) = ∫_V Θ^{ii}. That is the specialization of the published eq. (20) that Wang himself makes in Sect. 6. It was READ at source (v12 = CJP 93, 1470), with the surface integral on the LEFT as the tree's repair note says. It is machine-checked exactly (16/16, including a vacuity guard showing the divergence-free hypothesis carries weight) and has no data input. The downstream fixtures that rest on it (F3, W5, the factor 9) recompute exactly. Recorded without changing the grade: (1) tolman.py:566-567 over-states what (20) needs ('a ball'), in the conservative direction. (2) tolman.py:567 'SOURCE MAY BE ANYTHING' leaves regularity throughout V implicit. The tree names it as regular_centre / ball_excludes_walls / the Coulomb refusal (tolman.py:1198, 547-549), but only as a centre condition. No site applies the identity to a source that violates it; the non-spherical witnesses are constant-stress. (3) The 'von Laue's theorem' label and the status wording at tolman.py:145-146 vs 2522-2523 are discrepancies, not errors. (4) Giulini 2018 fn. 5 contests Wang's other claims; the tree does not rest on them. Why STANDS and not NARROWED: the class the tree actually uses (balls; symmetric, time-independent, regular, conserved sources) lies inside the source's class.
1206.5618.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any tolman.py site, or a peer that imports SOURCE_SPHERICITY_IS_LOAD_BEARING=False, applies the Laue route to any of: a source with an interior singularity (including an off-centre one, which regular_centre does not exclude); a non-integrable stress; a force-carrying wall inside the ball (all C5); a time-dependent source (C6); or a non-symmetric tensor contracted on its second index (C7). A discrepancy only, with no grade change, if the arXiv version the prior-art pass read numbers the identity differently from v12/CJP (not checkable here, because alphaXiv serves v12 only), or if a glyph-level read of (20) contradicts the operator recovery (C1/C2 make that very unlikely). WRONG would need a counterexample to the divergence theorem under its hypotheses, which is not expected.

sm-higgs-potential-tree.published_statement:
Buttazzo et al. 1307.3536:
- eq.(6): "we write the classical Higgs potential as V0 = -(m0^2/2)|H0|^2 + lambda0|H0|^4".
- eq.(10)-(11): "m^2_OS = 2 lambda_OS v^2_OS, M_h^2 = 2 lambda_OS v^2_OS, or lambda_OS = G_mu M_h^2/sqrt2".
- Table 1: the tree-level threshold is lambda = M_h^2/2V^2, with V = (sqrt2 G_mu)^(-1/2).
- Table 3: lambda(M_t) is 0.12917 at LO, 0.12774 at NLO and 0.12604 at NNLO.
- p.3: "the Higgs vacuum does not reside in the configuration of minimal energy, but in a metastable state".

Martin 1205.3365:
- eq.(13): "V(Phi) = V0 + (lambda/4)(Phi^2 - v^2)^2".
- eq.(21): "V(<Sigma>=v) = -m^4/(4 lambda) ... Clearly, this is because we have chosen V0 = 0".
- eq.(48): "rho_vac = -(1/4) m_H^2 v^2", where his v is 246/sqrt2 GeV.
- eq.(58): "rho^EW_vac ~ -1.2 x 10^8 GeV^4 ~ -10^55 rho_cri".
- p.11: "in absence of gravity, only differences of energy can be detected".

2503.11548 p.4: "Only a direct measurement of the Higgs field self-coupling interaction can determine the shape of the Higgs field potential."
published_hypotheses: The potential is classical (tree-level); loop corrections enter only through MS-bar threshold corrections and the effective potential (1307.3536 eqs.(25)-(26), App. C)
The potential has the renormalizable SM quartic form -m^2|H|^2/2 + lambda|H|^4, which fixes the self-couplings by M_h and v
lambda is identified on-shell through M_h and G_mu at tree level; the MS-bar lambda(mu) differs from it at loop level (Table 3)
V0 = 0 is a choice of zero; only energy differences are observable without gravity (1205.3365 eq.(21), p.11)
v is taken from muon decay, v = (sqrt2 G_mu)^(-1/2)
Flat spacetime and fixed couplings are assumed for the tree relation; lambda runs negative at field values around 10^10-10^11 GeV

The data fix only v (from G_F) and V''(v) = m_h^2. kappa_lambda is bounded only to (-1.2, 7.5) (CMS, as quoted by 2503.11548 p.2), and the quartic coupling is unmeasured. No file in research/warp-drive names this; a grep for trilinear, kappa_lambda or self-coupling finds 0 hits. sm-higgs-potential-tree.lacked_data:
Higgs and Weinberg did not know m_h, so they did not know lambda. The tree does not rely on their data: it uses post-2012 inputs, and moving m_h across 124.80-125.46 GeV changes every figure by less than 0.6% and changes no verdict. The one-loop correction to the depth is about +6%, and again no verdict moves.

Evidence against the hypothesis: no measurement contradicts the SM potential. The SM value kappa = 1 lies inside the measured interval, and the metastability results concern field values of 1e10-1e11 GeV, not 0..v.

Evidence for a narrower form of the hypothesis: the self-couplings are STILL unmeasured. Only v and m_h^2 are fixed; kappa_lambda is known only to (-1.2, 7.5) and the quartic not at all. Measuring them would change three things the tree reads off the SM shape: the depth and its sign, V''(0)/V''(v), and the stability edge (Part E, exact). It would not change D15 or D20's leading source/field -> 2/eps law, because both depend only on V''(v). So the missing datum is the self-coupling, and it is still missing today, not only in 1964.
sm-higgs-potential-tree.grade_evidence:
Every SM identity and number the tree uses re-derives exactly (35/35 checks). No datum that has moved changes a verdict: m_h 125.13 vs 125.20 and the one-loop +6.6% both leave the verdicts intact.

The grade is not STANDS because the tree drops a hypothesis its sources state. The sources are explicit that the quartic shape between 0 and v is untested: the data fix only v and m_h^2, and kappa_lambda is bounded only to (-1.2, 7.5). No tree file names this. On a family of potentials with the same v and m_h, the depth is (m_h^2 v^2/8)(3-kappa)/2, so its sign flips for kappa > 3, inside the allowed interval. V''(0)/V''(v) and the stability edge also move with kappa. Several readings therefore hold only for potentials with SM self-couplings, not on the data:

spectral-theory-friedrichs-rayleigh-ritz.name: Friedrichs extension keeps the form lower bound; Rayleigh-Ritz places the spectrum above the form bound (operator theory)

source.located: Two classics were not read directly (NAMED-NOT-READ): Friedrichs, Math. Ann. 109 (1934) 465-487, 685-713, and Reed-Simon Vol. II Thm X.23. Read instead: (1) Gesztesy & Sukhtaiev arXiv:2504.11718 (2025), Sec. 2, Thm 2.2, Eqs. (2.13)-(2.21), which restate the Friedrichs extension; (2) Fewster, Ford & Roman (FFR) arXiv:1004.0179 note [18], which gives Rayleigh-Ritz (a)=>(b), spectral support (b)=>(c) and (c)=>(a); (3) FFR arXiv:1204.3570 Sec. I p.2 and Sec. VIII.A; (4) Sanders arXiv:1010.3978v3 (2012).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2504.11718 (pp.1,3-5,7-10), 1204.3570 (pp.1-3,9-10,12,15,19-20,25) and 1010.3978 (pp.1-2,5,9-15). 1004.0179 note [18] came from the stage transcript src/1004.0179-note18.txt (alphaXiv full text, 2026-09-26).

spectral-theory-friedrichs-rayleigh-ritz.published_statement: Friedrichs, as restated in 2504.11718 Sec. 2: take S densely defined, symmetric and bounded below. Then the form q_S(f,g) = (f,Sg) on dom(S) is closable. Its closure Q_S corresponds to a self-adjoint extension S_F of S, with dom(Q_S) = dom(S_F^{1/2}) (2.18)-(2.19). S_F >= 0 when S >= 0 (2.14), and (S+cI)_F = S_F + cI (2.21), so S >= -Q gives S_F >= -Q. Among the non-negative extensions S_F is the largest: S_K <= S~ <= S_F (Thm 2.2), and ker S_K = ker S* (2.11). Rayleigh-Ritz, in FFR 1004.0179 note [18]: for A self-adjoint, three statements are equivalent: (a) <psi|A psi> >= -Q for all normalised psi in D(A); (b) sigma(A) is contained in [-Q, oo); (c) supp mu_psi is contained in [-Q, oo). "(a) => (b) is the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle; (b) => (c) because measurements always give values in the spectrum." FFR 1204.3570 p.2: the smeared normal-ordered operators are "defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain ... there is a distinguished Friedrichs extension (see Ref. [17], Theorem X.23), whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind ... whether the normal ordered expressions fail to be essentially self-adjoint, is nontrivial and not fully resolved."
published_hypotheses: F1 (Friedrichs): S is densely defined
F2 (Friedrichs): S is symmetric
F3 (Friedrichs): S is bounded below on dom(S). Restated for S >= 0, with the shift rule (2.21) giving any lower bound
F4 (scope of the conclusion): S_F keeps the bound, and other self-adjoint extensions need not (S_K <= S_F; for S >= eps > 0 with nonzero deficiency, 0 is in sigma(S_K))
R1 (Rayleigh-Ritz): A is self-adjoint and the form bound holds on D(A), equivalently on the form domain
R2 (support): mu_psi is the spectral measure of A in the state psi, i.e. the distribution of individual measurement results
P1 (FFR 1204.3570 Sec. I): the smearing is real-valued, so the operator is symmetric on a dense domain, and it is semibounded by the QEI
P2 (FFR 1204.3570 Sec. I): the physical observable is taken to be the Friedrichs extension; essential self-adjointness is 'not fully resolved'
hypothesis_drift: NONE DROPPED. F1-F3 are present at noise.py:157-159 (H3: the smeared Wick-ordered operator on Hadamard vectors is dense, symmetric for the real sampler g^2, and semibounded by Fewster (3)). F4 is carried in substance at noise.py:160-162, noise.py:324 (H3 'ASSUMED, load-bearing'), ledger.py:590 and specthm.py:2239. FFR's 'not fully resolved' is quoted correctly at noise.py:160 and 324.

ATTRIBUTION COMPRESSED (not an error): noise.py:172-173 cites 'Fewster (3)' for the bound on 'every psi in the form domain'. Fewster (3) covers Hadamard states, i.e. the dense domain. Carrying the bound to the whole form domain is done by the Friedrichs form closure (2504.11718 (2.15), (2.17)-(2.19)), which H3 supplies. The inequality survives form-norm limits, so the statement is correct; only the citation puts two steps under one name.

WORDING, EQUIVALENT: noise.py:158-159 says 'its lower bound is the form bound'; FFR 1204.3570 p.2 says 'coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound'. These are the same thing. The tree uses Fewster's non-optimal -C/tau^4 only as a containment (noise.py:29-31, 174-175) and never as inf sigma. No over-claim.

DOMAIN WORDING: noise.py:158 says 'Hadamard vectors'; FFR say 'a dense domain'; Sanders says 'the Wightman domain' D_omega. Vector states in D_omega are Hadamard, as Sanders' proof of Thm 5.3 uses. No drift.

NOT BORROWED, RECORDED: FFR 1204.3570 Sec. VIII.A says the distribution's lower bound 'is independent of any concerns about uniqueness'. The tree does not use this to weaken H3 and keeps H3 load-bearing, which is the more careful reading. A non-Friedrichs extension can sit below the form bound, as the Krein and Robin counterexamples in the rederivation show.

rederivation.outcome: 18 PASS, 0 FAIL (exit 0). Rayleigh-Ritz in finite dimensions: z3 finds no 2x2 or 3x3 real symmetric matrix with an eigenvalue below a form bound that holds at its eigenvector (unsat). (c)=>(a) is unsat for a 4-atom measure. sympy gives RQ = lambda_min = 2 - sqrt2 exactly. On S = -d^2/dx^2 on C_c^oo(0,1), with form bound pi^2: the Friedrichs (Dirichlet) extension has ground RQ = pi^2 exactly, so it keeps the bound. Compactly supported trials give RQ 13.709, 10.852, 10.066, all above pi^2 and falling toward it (form closure). The Krein extension has ker S* = span{1, x}, so 0 is in its spectrum and it loses the bound. Robin extensions have eigenvalues -2.3821 (kappa=1), -25.6403 (kappa=5), -2500.0 (kappa=50) and about -1e8 (kappa=1e4); the ODE holds exactly and the boundary residual is at most 1.4e-41. Finite differences agree (9.869592; -25.640). So H3's caveat is real: extensions of one semibounded operator can have lower bounds that are zero, negative, or arbitrarily negative. Clamped sampler: mu_1 = 4.730040744862704026 and C = 3.169857938310468. Galerkin Rayleigh-Ritz values 504, 504, 500.584681, 500.563908 are monotone and never fall below mu_1^4 = 500.563902.

later_literature.what: Proves the Wick square :Phi^2:(f) essentially self-adjoint on the Wightman domain when f is a finite sum of squares of real spacetime test functions (class S), in any quasi-free Hadamard state and any d >= 2 (Thm 5.8). With derivatives (the energy density) it proves self-adjointness only if the one-particle compression is self-adjoint (Thm 5.4), and that is not shown for the stress tensor. It does not reach the tree's A_tau, which has derivatives and is smeared along a worldline rather than by a spacetime test function. FFR's open question is narrowed, not closed, for A_tau.
Restates the Friedrichs construction, its extremality S_K <= S~ <= S_F (Krein 1947), the shift rule (2.21), and ker S_K = ker S*. The theorem is unchanged.
Derives quantum inequalities from operator product expansions, which bears on the semiboundedness input F3 in wider settings. Found by discover_papers; not read and not used.

spectral-theory-friedrichs-rayleigh-ritz.lacked_data: No datum enters this result. Friedrichs (1934), Krein (1947) and Rayleigh-Ritz are theorems about operators on Hilbert space with no measured input, and the rederivation (18/18) found nothing that moves them. By FFR's own account (1204.3570 p.2), what was missing in 2012 was not data but a proof: whether the time-smeared normal-ordered energy density is essentially self-adjoint. Sanders (2012 v3) settles this for the Wick square but not for the worldline-smeared energy density. So M's hypothesis takes a non-empirical form here. A proof of essential self-adjointness would discharge H3 and leave C1 unchanged. A proof against it would not falsify C1, which is stated for the Friedrichs extension, but it would reopen H6's choice of physical observable, because other extensions can sit arbitrarily far below the form bound. Evidence against 'the old math is wrong': the 2025 restatement is identical, and the result re-derives here both in finite dimensions (z3) and on an explicit unbounded operator.
spectral-theory-friedrichs-rayleigh-ritz.grade_evidence: The statement as used (noise.py:29-31, 172-177) matches the source. The Friedrichs extension of a densely defined symmetric operator bounded below by -Q keeps that bound (2504.11718 (2.14), (2.18)-(2.21)). Rayleigh-Ritz and spectral support then put the spectrum and every mu_psi in [-Q, oo) (FFR 1004.0179 note [18]). F1-F3 are present. The dependence on the choice of extension, and FFR's 'not fully resolved', are carried as the named, load-bearing, ASSUMED H3 (noise.py:157-162 and 324, ledger.py:590, specthm.py:2239), and C1 is claimed only for the Friedrichs extension. Nothing is dropped, so NARROWED does not apply. The rederivation agrees (18/0), including the Krein and Robin counterexamples that justify the H3 caveat. There is no datum, so DATA-DEPENDENT does not apply, and no computed contradiction, so WRONG is not available. Two wording points are attribution, not error: the form-domain step is cited to Fewster (3) though it is the Friedrichs closure, and 'form bound' means the same as FFR's 'sharpest QEI bound'. Whether A_tau is essentially self-adjoint is still open in the literature read here, but that openness belongs to H3, which the tree already marks ASSUMED.

2505.02210-energy-conditions.published_statement: Sec. IV.B (after eq. 19): 'Using the tetrad (18a)-(18c), the test reduces to checking the sign of r^8 + 4r^6 - 2(z^4 + 6z^2 - 4)r^4 - 4(5z^4 + 2z^2 - 2)r^2 + (z^4 - 2z^2 - 2)^2. This expression is positive, zero, or negative, corresponding to types I, II, and IV, respectively. These regions are shown in Fig. 9. Thus, the spacetime (13), having regions where the stress-energy tensor is type IV, violates all the standard energy conditions. We stress that this does not mean that the violations originate solely from the type IV region; energy-condition violations also occur in the type I and type II regions.' Fig. 9 caption: '...the energy-condition violations associated with type-IV regions occur on the critical level set.' Sec. IV.C: 'considering the vector field w^mu in (21), which is timelike by construction, we find regions where T_mu nu w^mu w^nu < 0 ... (evaluated at x = t = 0) is shown in Fig. 12.' And: 'we merely argue for the existence of type-IV regions ... we consider the event p = (1, 0, 0, 0) in the U1 chart. With our specific numerical choice of tetrads, we found that the stress-energy tensor T_ab at p has complex eigenvalues ... So T_ab should be of Hawking-Ellis type IV. Because the classification varies continuously, an extended region must exist in which the tensor remains of type IV.' After (24): 'changing zeta merely shifts, thins, or expands the regions ... it does not eliminate them altogether. Nonetheless, we expect that, with an appropriate choice of zeta and a suitable starting Riemannian metric, one might ... remove such regions completely -- at least for the Morse spacetime M.' cauchy-schwarz-lagrange-identity.name: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality via the Lagrange identity

source.located: Cauchy, Cours d'Analyse (1821), Note II, Th. XVI eq. (30) p.373 (the inequality) and eq. (31) p.374 (the identity for general n, proved by expansion). Lagrange 1773, Nouv. Mem. Acad. Roy. Berlin 85-128 (the n = 3 case). Neither has an arXiv copy.
source.via: Read the restatements at alphaXiv with answer_pdf_queries. Kichenassamy, arXiv:2504.19543, p.3: eq. (2) restates Cauchy's general-n identity with Cauchy's page and equation numbers. p.4: eq. (4) restates Lagrange's n = 3 case. p.7: the integral form. Labropoulou et al., arXiv:2312.03478: Th. 1 (p.3), Prop. 3 eq. (9) (p.6) and Appendix Proof 1 (p.12) give the double-sum proof for real vectors. Cauchy 1821 and Lagrange 1773 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ.

cauchy-schwarz-lagrange-identity.published_statement: Cauchy 1821, as restated in arXiv:2504.19543 eq. (2): for real a_1..a_n and b_1..b_n, (a1 b1 + ... + an bn)^2 + sum_{i<j} (ai bj - aj bi)^2 = (a1^2 + ... + an^2)(b1^2 + ... + bn^2). From this, (sum a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum a_i^2)(sum b_i^2). Cauchy wrote it for square roots and with the strict signs, per footnote 14 and p.7 of the restatement. Modern form, arXiv:2312.03478 Th. 1: 'Let x, y in R^n. Then |x . y| <= ||x|| ||y||. The equality holds iff x and y are collinear.' Appendix Proof 1 there: sum_{i,j}(x_i y_j - x_j y_i)^2 = 2(sum x_i^2)(sum y_i^2) - 2(sum x_i y_i)^2, and the left-hand side is a sum of squares of real numbers.
published_hypotheses: The entries are REAL numbers. The sum-of-squares step needs real squares.
Finitely many entries, any n >= 1. Cauchy proves general n; Lagrange 1773 covers n = 3 only.
The inner product is the standard positive-definite Euclidean dot product on R^n (arXiv:2312.03478 Prop. 2).
Going from the squared form to |x.y| <= ||x|| ||y|| takes a square root and needs ||x||, ||y|| >= 0. Both sources leave this implicit.
hypothesis_drift: NONE DROPPED on reality. latticectc.py:292-293 declares x0:3 and y0:3 with real=True, so the tree uses real Euclidean spatial vectors, which is exactly the source's hypothesis. Rederive L3 shows the hypothesis matters: over C without conjugation, x = (1, i) and y = (1, 0) give bilinear |x|^2|y|^2 = 0 < (x.y)^2 = 1.

WHAT THE OWNER CHECKED vs WHAT IT CLAIMS. latticectc.py:284 claims 'in any dimension', but :286 and :292-297 check the Lagrange residual only at d = 3. The published theorem holds for every n, and rederive L1 (n = 1..12) and L2 (symbolic n) close this gap. chain_to only ever handles 4-vectors (:277, range(4)), so the owner's d = 3 check already covers everything the tree computes.

UNCHECKED STEP IN THE OWNER, now checked here. The owner combines the squared Lagrange residual (:297) with a z3 lemma that assumes 'dot <= a b' with a, b >= 0 (:298-300). Two steps between them were not machine-checked: the square root, and identifying a^2 = |x|^2 and b^2 = |y|^2 (both stated only in the docstring, :286-288). Rederive L4 proves the square-root step in z3 and shows it fails without a, b >= 0.

NAMING DISCREPANCY, not a content drift. latticectc.py:30, :286 and :358 call the general-d identity 'the Lagrange identity'. Per arXiv:2504.19543 pp.3-4, Lagrange 1773 gave only n = 3; the general-n form is Cauchy 1821 eq. (31). Calling it Lagrange's identity is conventional. Recorded, not repaired.

The Lagrange identity is a polynomial identity, and the inequality follows for real entries because real squares are non-negative. No measurement, physical constant or extrapolation enters. Cauchy in 1821 had everything the conclusion needs. His proof by expansion is redone here exactly (L1, L2) and by machine (L4, L5). Later work widened the scope (Bunyakovsky 1859 integrals, Schwarz 1885 abstract form, Hermitian and operator versions); none of it corrected the result. The residual is exactly 0 for n = 1..12 and for symbolic n, and no datum can move a polynomial identity. The only hypothesis that could fail is that the entries are real, and it holds in the tree (real=True).

2604.01047#setting-thm1.2.published_statement: Thm 1.2 (p. 11): 'For any choice of past-compact smooth tensor S_ab(x) and for any symmetric past-compact smooth function Xi(x,y), there exists unique past-compact solution (omega~_1, h~_ab) of the Cauchy problem for the linearised semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations [(1.8) with zero data on Sigma_-eps] for any time t in [0, infinity). For any nontrivial choice of the sources S_ab and Xi, the solution h~_ab grows exponentially in time, but it can be bounded from above by the conformal rescaling of the Minkowski metric using a universal factor H, i.e. h~_ab <= e^{-Ht} eta_ab.' Thm 4.14 (p. 53): 'For a_i in (-infinity, 4m^2) and for any choice of past-compact smooth source S supported in the future of Sigma_-eps, the equation phi + W_ret(phi) = S ... admits a unique smooth and past-compact solution phi, supported in the future of Sigma_-eps.' Prop. 2.4 (p. 19): 'Let h_ab in Gamma_pc(T*R^n (x)_s T*R^n). Then, there is exactly one vector field X~_a in Gamma_pc(T*R^n), which makes the trace-reversal h-bar_ab divergence-free.'

plummer-enclosed-mass.published_statement: Not read at source (see source.via). This is the standard Plummer (1911) model as galpy 1.12.0 restates it (PlummerPotential.py:18-20, 74, 156) and as re-derived here. Potential: Phi(r) = -GM/sqrt(r^2+a^2). Density: rho(r) = (3M/4 pi a^3)(1 + r^2/a^2)^(-5/2). Enclosed mass: M(<r) = M r^3/(r^2+a^2)^(3/2) = M (1 + a^2/r^2)^(-3/2). The fraction outside r is therefore 1 - (1 + (a/r)^2)^(-3/2), which matches linstab.py:548-551 exactly.
published_hypotheses: H1 Newtonian gravity: the mass is the flat-space Poisson source, rho = lap(Phi)/(4 pi G). This is Plummer's setting. The M(<r) relation needs nothing more than Gauss's law applied to the potential.

This equation expresses the conservation of energy in the presence of a gravitational field.' Hotta 1101.3954 p.16: 'After completion of the protocol, the total energy of the field is equal to E_A - E_B. Therefore, the input energy E_A is not smaller than the output energy E_B: E_A >= E_B, because the total energy does not become negative. Note that the positive local energy +E_A of the field in region A compensates for the negative local energy -E_B of the field in region B.' p.40: 'the total energy must be nonnegative'. published_hypotheses: H-EOM: every matter source obeys its equations of motion; d_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 follows 'for any individual source of matter' from them (Carroll p.37).

In Noether's theorem this is invariance of the action; in GR it is a timelike Killing vector or asymptotic flatness (ADM). nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 is local only (Carroll p.114). From Noether, NAMED-NOT-READ here; computed in C6.
H-ISO: the system is isolated and energy is counted over all of it, sender included. In Hotta p.16 the output E_B is balanced by an input E_A infused at a different site.

H-POS: the Hamiltonian is bounded from below and the total energy is nonnegative (Hotta pp.16, 40; Kontou-Sanders p.27). In classical GR the corresponding condition is the dominant energy condition (EHLS Thm 1). Local energy density may be negative, and is unbounded below at a point (Kontou-Sanders p.22).
H-REST: a body of rest mass M has energy >= Mc^2 in any inertial frame, with equality at rest (Einstein 1905, NAMED-NOT-READ).

einstein-quadrupole-formula-rod.published_statement: From the restatement, L02 p6 eq. 3.75, with G and c restored: P = (G/5c^5) < dddQ_ij dddQ_ij >. Q_ij is the traceless mass quadrupole. The rod coefficient 2/45 is not printed in the source read; it follows from substituting mu R^2 -> M l^2/12, and it was re-derived here.

einstein-quadrupole-formula-rod.lacked_data: Einstein (1918) had no gravitational-wave data at all: no binary pulsar (1974), no double pulsar (2003), no interferometer detection (2015). Evidence against that gap changing the conclusion: (a) the formula is a closed-form theorem of linearised GR whose only empirical input is G, and it was re-derived here; (b) every later measurement read agrees with the leading-order flux, namely Hulse-Taylor to within 0.5% (Will 2014) and the double pulsar as the tightest Newtonian-order bound (GWTC-5.0 p.15); (c) G has moved 3.3e-5 since CODATA 2014 and is unchanged from 2018 to 2022. Evidence the other way: every confirmation is for a gravitationally bound astrophysical source, and no laboratory, stress-supported source has ever been detected. The rod case therefore rests on the theorem, not on a measured rod. It is, however, the case the linearised derivation covers most directly, and at v/c ~ 1.7e-5 the post-Newtonian corrections are about 1e-5. Einstein's own historical coefficient errors are NAMED-NOT-READ and play no part in the grade.

topology-change-vs-metric-change.published_statement: Nothing published states the tree's sentence as such. What Borde gr-qc/9406053v1 states, verbatim. Thm 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' Thm 3 (dim >= 3, null generic + half-integral null convergence): 'Then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected.' Reinhart/Sorkin as quoted: 'If n is even, then M admits such a field if chi(M) = 0'. Misner/Geroch: 'If N = M#V, then chi(N) = chi(M) + chi(V) - 2'. Tipler, as Borde restates him: 'if topology change occurs via a non-compact interpolating spacetime, then it contains (under some mild additional assumptions) a singularity ... or a point at infinity.' Every conclusion is about the interpolating manifold M (whether it is a product), not about a pair of endpoint topologies.
published_hypotheses: M is an interpolating spacetime: connected smooth manifold with boundary S1 u S2 (u a compact timelike tube T), carrying a smooth everywhere non-degenerate Lorentz metric with S1 and S2 spacelike [Borde II.A]
time-oriented [Thm 1, Thm 3, Corollary]
causally compact (automatic for compact M). For an open universe, M is the causally compact region of an externally simple spacetime [Borde 1160-1210]
Thm 1 assumes no field equation, no energy condition and no completeness
Thm 3 adds dim >= 3, the null generic condition (i) and the half-integral null convergence condition (ii)
Tipler Thm 5 (as restated): closed-universe case, non-compact M, topology change occurs, 'some mild additional assumptions' that are not named (Tipler NOT READ)

The antecedent of Thms 1 and 3 is not 'topology change'. Their conclusion is 'M = S1 x [0,1]', so they constrain every non-product M, including one whose two ends are the same manifold, and they are silent exactly when M is a product

source.located: A. Escriva, 'A new approach for simulating PBH formation from generic curvature fluctuations with the Misner-Sharp formalism', arXiv:2504.05813v3 [astro-ph.CO], 28 Nov 2025 (v1 8 Apr 2025). Section 2, p.3-5: eqs. (2.1)-(2.5), (2.12); p.12 (type-II Gamma < 0).

2504.05813.published_statement: p.3-4: 'we need to consider a perfect fluid with the energy-momentum tensor T^{mu nu} = (p + rho) u^mu u^nu + p g^{mu nu} (2.1), and with the following spacetime metric in spherical symmetry: ds^2 = -A(r,t)^2 dt^2 + B(r,t)^2 dr^2 + R(r,t)^2 dOmega^2 (2.2) ... we have chosen zero-shift vector beta^i = 0 (comoving threading) ... u^t = 1/A and u^i = 0 ... (comoving slicing).' '(1/A) dR/dt = D_t R = U(r,t), (1/B) dR/dr = D_r R = Gamma(r,t) (2.3), where D_t and D_r are the proper time and distance derivatives.' 'The Misner-Sharp mass M(r,t) is introduced as M(R) = int_0^R 4 pi Rt^2 rho dRt (2.4), which is related with Gamma, U and R through the constraint: Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R) (2.5)'. p.5: 'where Gamma is called the generalised Lorentz factor, which includes the gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy per unit mass.' p.12, same paper: 'we observe the throat-neck structure in the areal radius R, which causes the function Gamma to take negative values'. Also p.12: 'when Gamma < 0, the integrand in Eq. (2.4) (4 pi Rt^2 rho Gamma B), taken over the comoving radial coordinate r includes a locally "negative mass" component'. Units G = c = 1.
published_hypotheses: H1 spherical symmetry, with metric (2.2) diagonal in (t, r)
H2 zero shift beta^i = 0 ('comoving threading'), so that D_t = (1/A) d_t is the derivative along the slice normal
H3 perfect fluid (2.1) and comoving slicing u^t = 1/A (no radial energy flux in these coordinates)
H4 M defined by the integral (2.4) from R = 0, which implies a regular centre; when R is non-monotonic the integral is taken over r with integrand 4 pi R^2 rho Gamma B (p.12)

misner-sharp-1964.name: Misner-Sharp mass identity Gamma^2 - U^2 = g^ab d_aR d_bR = 1 - 2m/R (Misner & Sharp 1964, via Hayward gr-qc/9408002 eq. (27))

source.located: C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964), no arXiv copy. Restated by S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', PRD 53, 1938 (1996), arXiv gr-qc/9408002v2: eq.(4) p.4, eqs.(23)-(28) pp.11-12, eqs.(31)-(35) pp.12-13, Prop.1 p.4, App.B p.19, ref.[4] p.22. An independent second restatement: A. Escriva arXiv:2504.05813v3 eqs.(2.2)-(2.5), (2.24), refs.[50],[57] = MS 1964. Later context: Maeda & Nozawa arXiv:0709.1199v4 eq.(2.7), ref.[6].
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9408002 plus get_paper_content fullText. The extracted text had lost its Greek letters; they were recovered by decoding the TeX OML font bytes (0x15=lambda, 0x10=zeta, 0x1C=tau). pi and rho decode to physically correct places, which validates the map. Also answer_pdf_queries on 2504.05813 and 0709.1199. Misner & Sharp 1964 and Hernandez & Misner 1966 are NAMED-NOT-READ: the arxiv.org e-print fetch got a proxy 403.

misner-sharp-1964.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002 p.4 eq.(4): 'The Misner-Sharp spherically symmetric gravitational energy ... may be defined in units G = 1 by E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) = (1/2) r + e^f r d+r d-r = (1/2) r + (1/4) e^f r^3 theta+ theta-. The form actually given by Misner & Sharp is derived in Section IV. Note that E is an invariant. Indeed, the only invariants of the metric and its first derivatives are functions of r and E.' pp.11-12 eqs.(23)-(27): coordinates (tau, zeta) with g(d_tau,d_zeta) = 0, g(d_tau,d_tau) = -1, 'Define a function lambda by e^lambda = g(d_zeta,d_zeta)', ds^2 = r^2 dOmega^2 + e^lambda dzeta^2 - dtau^2 (26), '1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda}(r')^2 - rdot^2 (27) which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4], with different notation.' Prop.1: trapped iff E > r/2, marginal iff E = r/2, untrapped iff E < r/2. App.B: E is the Kodama charge. Escriva 2504.05813 eqs.(2.3),(2.5): U = (1/A) dR/dt, Gamma = (1/B) dR/dr, Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R), attributed to MS [57] in the general-lapse comoving metric.
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry, 'assumed implicitly in the Propositions' (Hayward p.2).
r is the areal radius (area 4 pi r^2), r > 0 (Hayward p.3).
The spacetime is time-orientable (Hayward p.3). This is needed for the SIGNS of theta^pm, not for E.
Units G = 1, c = 1.
Definition (4) uses no field equation. The Einstein equations with no cosmological constant enter only in the variation formulas (10)-(11) and (28).
Form (27) is written in a lapse-1, zero-shift gauge adapted to a spatial hypersurface Sigma (eqs.23a,b). For (27) and (28) the gauge is needed only on Sigma.
Misner & Sharp's own setting: adiabatic perfect fluid, comoving coordinates, general lapse (Hayward p.12; Escriva eqs.2.1-2.3).
The enclosed-integral form E = int 4 pi r^2 rho r' dzeta (eq.33) needs a regular centre. The definition does not.
hypothesis_drift: DISCREPANCY IN A QUOTATION (a misprint, not a refutation). driven.py:56-58 quotes Hayward eq.(27) as 'e^{-chi}(r')^2'. The v2 text prints e^{-lambda}, where lambda is the metric function of eq.(24); the coordinates are (tau, zeta) and no chi appears in eqs.(23)-(27). Reading chi as a coordinate would make the equation false (rederive C11b, residual nonzero). The tree's working identity is correct: driven.py V3 (driven.py:571-574) and foliation.py V1 (:637-640) use e^{-2Lambda}, which is Hayward's form at lambda = 2 Lambda, Phi = 0 (C2b, residual 0). foliation.py:381-383 and :875-876 cite the equation by number only. Recorded, nothing repaired.

BROADENED, and supported: lapse-1 gauge to general lapse. Hayward's (27) uses the lapse-1 gauge; driven.py:145, foliation.py:632 and nonstatic.py:26 use e^{2Phi}. driven.py:65-66 translates correctly. Checked: C1 (any diagonal lapse), C1b (with a shift), C5a-c (Schwarzschild gives E = M in the Schwarzschild, Lemaitre and Painleve-Gullstrand charts). The diagonal 'general metric' is without loss of generality locally.

Where there is no regular centre, m encloses nothing: throatmass.py's own throat (m = r_0/2, the marginal case of Prop.1) and M < 0 Schwarzschild are examples. A wording drift; it moves no verdict.

misner-sharp-1964.lacked_data: Tested for this result, M's hypothesis finds nothing. The identity has no empirical input: it is the definition 1 - 2m/R = g^ab d_aR d_bR plus 2-metric algebra, so no datum Misner & Sharp could have lacked bears on it. It was re-derived from scratch here: residual 0 in 10 forms and 3 Schwarzschild charts, with vacuity guards. What 1964 lacked was conceptual, not data: the Kodama vector (1980), Hayward's invariant and trapping formulation with E as the Kodama charge (1994-96), the Lambda and higher-curvature generalisations (2008), and the exotic geometries where m < 0 or no regular centre occurs. Each of these reproduces the identity unchanged. The only moved-datum candidate anywhere in the tree's use is G in the SI exchange rate, and CODATA 2022 left G identical to 2018. The evidence against M's hypothesis is complete for this result. Later work sharpens only the tree's 'enclosed' gloss (it needs a regular centre, EFE and Lambda = 0), which is recorded as a drift.
misner-sharp-1964.grade_evidence: The statement was read in Hayward eqs.(4) and (27) and in Escriva eq.(2.5): exactly the tree's Gamma^2 - U^2 = g^ab dR dR = 1 - 2m/R, attributed to MS 1964 by two independent restatements. On hypotheses, the tree uses the source's own class (spherical symmetry plus areal radius), with untrapped, U = 0 and H_EFE named where they are used. Its broader use (general lapse, general matter) was machine-checked (C1, C1b, C5, C7). The re-derivation agrees, 24/24 with vacuity guards. No datum enters, and G is unchanged in CODATA 2022. Four discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and none moves a verdict: (i) driven.py:58 misprints Hayward's e^{-lambda} as e^{-chi}; (ii) 'enclosed' at ledger.py:337, 367 is an added gloss; (iii) Lambda = 0 is unstated at throatmass.py:235 and tolman.py:705; (iv) foliation.py:857 ONLY_INVARIANT leaves out the discrete sign invariants.
