1208.5399.name: Fewster, 'Lectures on quantum energy inequalities' (arXiv:1208.5399v1, 27 Aug 2012; AEI Golm lectures, March 2012), Sec. 1.3. It covers the flat worldline QEI Eq.(3), the duration bound Eq.(4) rho >= -C/tau^4 (C ~ 3.17), and the a priori Casimir-plate bound T00 >= -C/(2l)^4 with the '3-7%' ratio. Merged here: 1208.5399-eq4 and Fewster-Thompson 2301.01698 eq.(1.4).

source.located: arXiv:1208.5399v1 [gr-qc], C.J. Fewster (York), pp.10-14 (Secs. 1.3, 1.4), 24-29 (Secs. 2.4-2.5), 44-46 (Secs. 5.1, 5.3). Merged key: arXiv:2301.01698v2 [hep-th], Fewster & Thompson (2023), p.2 eq.(1.4). Also read for comparison: gr-qc/9908073v2, Fewster & Teo (2000).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries returned page text for 1208.5399 (pp.1-3, 10-15, 24-27, 29, 44, 46-47), for 2301.01698 (pp.1-4, 7-9, 12, 15, 18, 27) and for gr-qc/9908073 (pp.1-4, 7, 12-16, 18). Every quotation is from that page text. Two sources were not read here and are marked NAMED-NOT-READ: Fewster-Pfenning math-ph/0602042 (ref [31], the stated basis of the Casimir a priori bound) and Fewster-Eveson gr-qc/9805024 (ref [22], the original derivation of Eq.(3)).

1208.5399.published_statement: p.10: 'In the m = 0 case, the bound simplifies, and actually gives a bound valid for all m >= 0: INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' This holds 'for any smooth compactly supported g, and all Hadamard states w' of the Klein-Gordon field in 4-dimensional Minkowski space. The notes that follow say: 'the right-hand side is state-independent. The bound is known not to be optimal. ... remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R) ... does not apply to ... discontinuous g.' p.11: 'Suppose that <T00>_w < rho for some interval t in [t0, t0+tau] ... the left-hand side can be minimized over g, to give the minimum eigenvalue of the operator d^4/dt^4 on [t0,t0+tau], with boundary conditions at each end corresponding to vanishing of the function and its first derivative. The upshot is that rho >= -C/tau^4, (4) where the numerical constant C ~ 3.17.' p.13: 'Consider a region between Casimir plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime and an inertial trajectory parallel to the plates. Let l be the distance ... to the nearest plate ... no experiment conducted along the trajectory in a time interval of less than 2l can possibly know about the existence of the plates ... [as the energy density is supposed constant along the trajectory] (4) gives an a priori bound T00 >= -C/(2l)^4 ~ -3.17/(2l)^4 = -0.20/l^4. By comparison, the known value of the Casimir energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field is T00 = -pi^2/(1140 L^4) - (pi^2/(48 L^4))(3 - 2cos^2(pi z/L))/cos^4(pi z/L) which ranges between 3-7% of the bound as z varies in [-L/2, L/2].' p.14: 'There remains an interesting question as to why the Casimir energy density is a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound.' 2301.01698 p.2 eq.(1.4) gives the same -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''|^2 by Parseval, for the massless field on an inertial worldline, all Hadamard states, and real compactly supported smooth g.
published_hypotheses: P1: free real scalar field with minimal coupling; Eq.(3) holds for every mass m >= 0
P2: four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with no boundaries
P3: averaging along an inertial worldline (Eq.(15) adds lower-order acceleration terms; 2301.01698 eq.(1.8) covers stationary worldlines)
P4: all Hadamard states; the right-hand side does not depend on the state
P5: g real, smooth and compactly supported; also valid for g in W^{2,2}(R); fails for discontinuous g

P6: Eq.(4) needs <T00> < rho (rho constant) throughout an interval of duration tau at the point, with the sampler in C0^oo of that open interval. The infimum is the least eigenvalue of d^4/dt^4 with clamped ends (footnote 7, Fewster-Teo). C is printed only as 'C ~ 3.17'.
P7: 'The bound is known not to be optimal' (said of Eq.(3); Eq.(4) inherits it)

P8: Casimir a priori bound: plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime, an inertial trajectory parallel to them, and l the distance to the nearer plate. A causality window (duration < 2l) licenses the Minkowski QEI, following Fewster-Pfenning [31]. The energy density is taken as constant along the trajectory, and the bound applies to all stationary Hadamard states.
P9: the Casimir comparison is for the massless minimally coupled scalar. The passage does not state a boundary condition; the printed form is the Dirichlet one.
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION (not an error): Fewster prints only 'C ~ 3.17' and the clamped-eigenvalue description. He does not print C = mu_1^4/(16 pi^2) or cos(mu_1)cosh(mu_1) = 1. The tree credits the closed form to 'Fewster 1208.5399 Eq. (4)' at noise.py:80-83, specthm.py:921-925 and bounds.py:270-273. The closed form is the tree's own computation and it is correct: re-derived here, mu_1 = 4.730040744862704026 and C = 3.169857938310468. achievable.py:232-240 words it correctly.

DROPPED in one use: bounds.py:60-66 and casimir_fraction_of_bound (bounds.py:340-366) take the 3-7% and conclude 'CASIMIR DOES NOT SATURATE IT', then code FORD_ROMAN_K_IS_WRONG = True (bounds.py:324; ledger W2). The a priori bound is built on Eq.(3), which Fewster says 'is known not to be optimal' (p.10), and on a 2l window fixed by causality rather than by optimisation. So 3-7% shows non-saturation of THIS bound only. It says nothing about how far Casimir is from the sharp bound. bounds.py never mentions optimality (grep 'optimal': no hit); the caveat appears only at achievable.py:256, for the corridor use.

RELABEL: bounds.py:55-66 frames the withdrawn claim as 'Casimir is the Ford-Roman bound saturated' and withdraws it using Fewster's bound. Fewster's C comes from the Fewster-Eveson INT g''^2 form with the clamped sampler, not from Ford-Roman's Lorentzian -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4). The canonical names also say 'Ford-Roman / Fewster'. The Ford-Roman bound itself rests on gr-qc/9510071 (bounds.py:67-70), which is a different key.

DISCREPANCY CARRIED: Fewster's text layer prints the Casimir constant as pi^2/(1140 L^4). The standard Dirichlet scalar value is pi^2/(1440 L^4), re-derived here two ways (zeta mode sum; the periodic a = 2L image family). The tree copies 1140 at bounds.py:347 and bounds.py:350. The midpoint fraction moves from 6.7597% to 6.7028%, and '3-7%' still holds. The selftest pin near(mid, 0.0682, rel 1e-2) at bounds.py:557 passes with 1140 (|rel| 0.0088) but would fail with 1440 (|rel| 0.0172). This is a misprint, recorded, not a refutation.

NAMED, NOT DROPPED: the tree applies the Minkowski/inertial bound on the curved corridor as H_flat 'ASSUMED' (specthm.py:900-985; noise.py H2 'FAILS ON THE CORRIDOR, b/l_G = 61.237'; achievable.py:257,370). Fewster's licence for importing a flat QEI (Sec. 1.3) is the causality window, and nothing comparable is supplied for the corridor, so ASSUMED is the right label. ledger.py:409 labels D7 THEOREM: it is a theorem in Minkowski space, and for the corridor only under H_flat, which ledger.py:406-411 names.

ADDED BY OWNER, NAMED: the owner applies the bound pointwise and sums over the core under staticity, with T = b/c (achievable.py:242-249, bounds.py:270-282, specthm H_static). Eq.(4) is a statement at one point on one inertial worldline. The owner names this as an extra hypothesis (bounds.py:280-282).
TREE NARROWER THAN SOURCE (harmless): achievable.py:363-372 and specthm H_M0 restrict Eq.(4) to massless fields, but Eq.(3) holds for all m >= 0. noise.py H1 'm >= 0' matches the source.

EXTENSION, NAMED: ledger.py:406-411 says 'STATE-INDEPENDENT over Hadamard states, so no branch of any decomposition escapes it'. The source's state-independence is over Hadamard states of this free minimally coupled field only. The escape route is named (O1), and bounds.py:283-285 cites Sec. 5.1 on nonminimal coupling (READ p.44).

SCOPE OF 'OPTIMAL': fewsterteo.py:41-42 calls C_F the constant at the 'OPTIMAL COMPACTLY SUPPORTED sampler'. That is true for the Eq.(3) functional (the Galerkin check converges down onto mu_1^4 from 504). But Eq.(3) is itself not optimal. For the corridor this is conservative. For the Casimir ratio it cuts the other way: the true ratio to the sharp bound is at least 3-7%.

1208.5399.lacked_data: No data was missing, because Eq.(3)/(4) is a theorem of free QFT in Minkowski space with no measured input. C is a pure number from an eigenvalue problem. Re-derived here, it is 3.16985793831, in agreement with the printed 'C ~ 3.17'. The constants the tree adds downstream have not moved: hbar and c are exact, and G is unchanged from CODATA 2018 to 2022. So nothing moves 71.256. Evidence the other way was also found. First, the source has a misprint: the Casimir constant 1140 should be 1440. It moves the midpoint ratio by 0.057 points and leaves '3-7%' intact, but the tree copied it and its selftest pin 0.0682 is tuned to it. Second, the source says itself where it is incomplete: 'The bound is known not to be optimal', and why the Casimir density is 'a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound' is left as an open question. What could change the conclusion is a sharper QEI in the plate geometry, which is a mathematical gap, not a data gap. For this result, M's hypothesis is not supported in the 'lacked data' form. It is supported in the narrower 'incomplete' form, exactly where the author says so.
1208.5399.grade_evidence: Eq.(3)/(4) as used for the corridor stands. The statement and its hypotheses match the tree's use, the non-Minkowski application is carried as the named hypothesis H_flat, and the constant re-derives exactly (checks A1-A10). The grade is NARROWED because of the Sec. 1.3 Casimir use. bounds.py:60-66, 340-366 and 557-562 turn '3-7% of Fewster's a priori bound' into 'CASIMIR DOES NOT SATURATE [Ford-Roman]' (FORD_ROMAN_K_IS_WRONG, ledger W2). They leave out what Fewster states on p.10: 'The bound is known not to be optimal'. Sitting at 3-7% of a valid but non-optimal bound shows non-saturation of that bound only; the distance to the sharp QEI floor is not measured. Calling Fewster's bound 'Ford-Roman' narrows it again. Two discrepancies are recorded, and neither is a refutation. The printed 1140 (correct value 1440) is copied at bounds.py:347,350; it leaves '3-7%' intact, but bounds.py:557's pin 0.0682 passes only with the misprint. The closed form for C is credited to Fewster's Eq.(4), which prints only 'C ~ 3.17'; the value itself is right. No computation contradicts Fewster, so WRONG does not apply. No datum has moved, so DATA-DEPENDENT does not apply.
1208.5399.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: bounds.py's Casimir withdrawal says the ratio is relative to Fewster's a priori bound, which is known not to be optimal (or restates the claim as 'Casimir is 3.2-6.8% of a valid a priori QEI bound'), and keeps the Ford-Roman label separate. The 1140/1440 misprint stays recorded either way. To WRONG, for the withdrawal only and not for Eq.(4): a sharp, boundary-aware QEI in the Dirichlet-plate geometry, read at source, that the Casimir density saturates. Reading Fewster-Pfenning math-ph/0602042 would upgrade the causality-window step from read-via-Fewster to READ, and could not change Eq.(4).

bousso-covariant.name: Bousso covariant entropy bound (lightsheets)

source.located: R. Bousso, 'A Covariant Entropy Conjecture', hep-th/9905177v3 (JHEP 07 (1999) 004) is the primary. It was read alongside: Bousso, 'The holographic principle', hep-th/0203101v2 (RMP 74 (2002) 825); Flanagan-Marolf-Wald, hep-th/9908070v4 (PRD 62 (2000) 084035); Bousso-Casini-Fisher-Maldacena, 1404.5635v2.

bousso-covariant.published_statement: hep-th/9905177 p.9-10, verbatim: 'Covariant Entropy Conjecture. Let M be a four-dimensional space-time on which Einstein's equation is satisfied with the dominant energy condition holding for matter. Let A be the area of a connected two-dimensional spatial surface B contained in M. Let L be a hypersurface bounded by B and generated by one of the four null congruences orthogonal to B. Let S be the total entropy contained on L. If the expansion of the congruence is non-positive (measured in the direction away from B) at every point on L, then S <= A/4.'  The units are given on p.5: 'We set hbar = c = G = k = 1'. FMW's abstract restates it with units restored as 'S <= A/4G hbar'. On status, review p.19: 'There is no fundamental derivation of the covariant entropy bound ... The resulting entropy bound can be saturated, but no example is known where it is exceeded.'
published_hypotheses: H1: Einstein's equation holds in a four-dimensional spacetime (D dimensions in review Sec. V.E). Source: hep-th/9905177 p.9.

H2: the dominant energy condition holds for matter (1999, p.9; fn.3 suggests causal energy flow may be enough). The review works with the null energy condition plus the causal energy condition, and requires excluding 'unphysical matter content, such as large negative energy' (p.4, Sec. V.D.1).
H3: the spacetime is inextendible and has no naked (null or timelike) singularities (p.9).
H4: L is a NULL hypersurface generated by one of the four null congruences orthogonal to B. Bousso says 'we must use null hypersurfaces' and that the spacelike version fails (p.6; review p.19).
H5: expansion theta <= 0 at every point of L, measured away from B. A generator is terminated where theta would turn positive (caustics), or at a boundary or singularity (pp.10-12).
H6: the geometry is approximately classical and the matter entropy on L can be defined (fluid, or the FMW mode rule). The species problem carries over (review Sec. V.C-V.D).

H7 (status): it is a conjecture. It has been proven only under FMW's classical entropy-current hypotheses, which include the NEC, and for a vacuum-subtracted von Neumann entropy in free fields at weak gravity without the NEC (BCFM 1404.5635).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1/H2/H3/H6: bounds.py:50 and bounds.py:316 carry only the note 'lightsheets', and the canonical hypotheses are only 'light-sheets' and 'A/4G on RHS'. Einstein's equation, the energy condition (DEC in 1999, NEC plus causal in the review), the no-naked-singularity condition and the classical-regime condition are all absent. On a warp board this matters: NEC-violating matter is outside the 1999 statement. Only BCFM's weak-gravity version drops the NEC. The load-bearing pin (bounds.py:459) does not depend on H2.
DROPPED H7 (status): bounds.py:316 has status word 'none', while the source prints that the bound is a conjecture with no fundamental derivation (review p.19; BCFM p.2).

CHANGED H4 (null to spacelike/region): bounds.py:195 and bounds.py:316 code Z = 2 'spacelike / region'. Z's own definition (bounds.py:29-31) puts null at Z = 1. The source's defining move is the null hypersurface; the spacelike bound fails (hep-th/9905177 p.6; review Sec. IV). Re-coding Z 2->1 in memory leaves cells at 8 and empties the Z = 2 gravity list. Recorded, not repaired.

The source prints 'can be saturated, but not exceeded' (1999 abstract and Sec. 7; review pp.19, 27, 33, where 'S/A approaches 1/4 from below'). FMW are more guarded (pp.9-10): they do not show saturation, only 'within a factor of order unity'. These are worst-case limits, not an exact saturating system of the kind Schwarzschild is for Bekenstein. K = 1 can be defended but is not what the source asserts. Re-coding K 1->0 moves saturated 4 -> 5, cells stay 8. Recorded, not repaired.

NOT A DRIFT: S = 0. The right-hand side depends only on the area of B, which is held fixed (review Sec. V.C.2).

Exactly one row has G = 1, as bounds.py:459 pins. Recorded, not repaired.

bousso-covariant.lacked_data:
In 1999 Bousso had classical GR, the dominant energy condition, S_BH = A/4, and FRW and collapse solutions with worst-case entropy estimates.

What he lacked, and what came later:
(a) A sharp definition of entropy on a null segment. BCFM 2014 supplied one, and it CONFIRMS the bound in weak gravity even without the NEC.
(b) The full weight of generic quantum NEC violation. This NARROWS the reach of the 1999 statement (FMW 2000), but in BCFM's regime the light-sheet condition protects the bound anyway.
(c) Higher-curvature and higher-dimension quantum corrections. These break the QUANTUM generalization in d >= 5 (Fu-Koeller-Marolf, contested by Leichenauer), not the classical 4D bound.
(d) Newer measured constants. G and hbar moved by less than 1e-3 and 2e-7 relatively. The tree uses only whether G appears, so nothing moves.

Evidence either way: no later datum or paper read here refutes the classical 4D bound under its stated hypotheses. The one claimed violation read (1412.2618) is outside FMW's hypotheses by its authors' own Sec. VIII. The missing data changed the bound's STATUS and SCOPE, not the conclusion the tree draws from it.
bousso-covariant.grade_evidence:
The load-bearing use STANDS. bounds.py:458-459 says Bousso 'genuinely has A/4G in its statement'. That is true at source (FMW abstract; BCFM abstract) and was re-derived: dS/dG is nonzero, the bound becomes trivial as G -> 0, and Bekenstein has no G. No moved datum moves it: CODATA 2022 G equals the 2018 value, and the density shifts by -2e-4.

The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS for two reasons.
1. The tree's row drops named hypotheses of the published statement: Einstein's equation, the DEC (or NEC plus causal), no naked singularities, and a classical regime with definable entropy. It also drops the bound's status as a conjecture proven only under FMW's classical hypotheses or in BCFM's weak-gravity regime.
2. Two slots are coded differently from the source. Z = 2 'spacelike / region' (bounds.py:195, 316) is given to a bound whose defining feature is a NULL hypersurface. K = 1 'not known saturated' stands against the source's printed 'can be saturated, but not exceeded', which is a worst-case/limit claim, so K = 1 is contestable rather than wrong.

These are discrepancies, recorded and not repaired; none is a refutation. Measured costs: Z 2->1 empties the Z = 2 gravity list with cells at 8; K 1->0 moves saturated 4 -> 5.

For a warp board, the hypothesis that matters most is H2: the 1999 statement assumes the DEC and so says nothing about NEC-violating matter. The only proof without the NEC (BCFM) is weak-gravity and for free, or argued interacting, fields.
bousso-covariant.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the dropped hypotheses (Einstein's equation, DEC or NEC plus causal, classical regime, conjecture status) at bounds.py:316, and either brings Z and K into line with the source (Z = 1, null) or states why it departs. To WRONG: a counterexample to the classical 4D bound that meets every published hypothesis (DEC, Einstein's equation, theta <= 0 light-sheet, definable entropy), or a demonstration that the GR right-hand side carries no G. None was found. To OPEN: if 'lightsheets' in the tree means something other than the published S on L. To DATA-DEPENDENT: only if the 1/4 normalisation moved. It is fixed by T_H and the first law.

2011.10991.name: Sorge, eq. (36): int_V sqrt(-g) T^i_(C) i = 0 for a complete Casimir apparatus

source.located: F. Sorge, 'Quasi-local Casimir energy and vacuum buoyancy in a weak gravitational field', arXiv:2011.10991v1 [gr-qc], 22 Nov 2020; eqs (29)-(40), sec. 6; appendix eqs (64)-(72)
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true): the whole paper was read, 20 pp. including references. Only v1 was read. The acknowledgment thanks referees, so a journal version exists and was not read. Following the tree's precedent, the discrepancies below must not be quoted against the journal version until it is read.

2011.10991.published_statement: Sec. 6 starts from the equilibrium equation f_nu + nabla_mu T^mu_(C) nu = 0 (31) in the Fermi metric ds^2 = (1+2 gamma z)dt^2 - dx^2 - dy^2 - dz^2 (30). The weight is identified as F_z = int_V sqrt(-g) f_z = m gamma = gamma int_V sqrt(-g)[T^t_t - T^i_i]_(C) (32). Sorge then writes: 'The first and the last term cancel each other [at the O(gamma) order]' (34)->(35); 'The last term is zero, since it can be converted to a surface integral on the boundary dV of the cavity volume, where T^mu nu_(C) = 0. The second term is zero, as the cavity does not exchange energy and momentum with the surroundings. As a consequence int_V d^3x sqrt(-g) T^i_(C) i = 0. (36)'. On p.11: 'such cancellation basically relies on the virial theorem [2]'. His boxed conclusion: 'if (according to the Equivalence Principle) the gravitational and inertial (quasi-local Tolman) mass associated to the field quantum vacuum coincide, then the quasi-local mass value is related solely to the T^t_(phi) t component'.
published_hypotheses: H1 weak static field, first order in gamma only: Fermi metric (30), rotations neglected, O(|x|^2) dropped, gamma uniform over the apparatus
H2 the apparatus is a test system: T_(C) has a negligible effect on the background (assumption (c); eq. (27))
H3 compact support: T^mu nu_(C) = 0 on and outside the boundary dV (assumption (a); eq. (29)). This is what removes int d_j T^j_z in (35)
H4 stationarity: int d_t T^t_z = 0 (no exchange with the surroundings; footnote 1)
H5 the apparatus is held at rest by an external non-gravitational force density f_nu (31), so it is not a closed system
H6 the premise (32): weight = gamma x the quasi-local Tolman mass, justified by the Equivalence Principle. Eq. (36) is derived from this premise
H7 complete apparatus: T_(C) = T_(phi) + T_(cav) (38). T_(cav) is never modelled
H8 model: massless minimally coupled scalar field with Dirichlet parallel plates, L << sqrt(A), edge effects neglected. The derivation of (36) does not use the form of the field
H9 the cancellation is attributed to the virial theorem (Landau-Lifshitz [2], Carlip [55], Ohanian [10]), not proved independently
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (the premise), tolman.py:167-169 'proves int_V sqrt(-g) T^i_(C) i = 0 for the apparatus (his eq. 36)'. Sorge derives (36) from conservation plus the premise (32), and his own statement of the result is conditional. Re-derived here: conservation alone gives F_z = gamma int sqrt(-g) T^tt. Adding (32) gives exactly int sqrt(-g) T^i_i = 2 gamma int sqrt(-g) z T^tt. The conclusion survives at O(gamma^0) because flat-space von Laue supplies it independently (machine-checked). So 'proves' overstates Sorge's logic, and the content actually rests on von Laue, which tolman.py already cites through Wang 1206.5618 eq. (20).

DROPPED (the order in gamma), tolman.py:171-172 ('4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = 0 identically') and :2608-2609 ('returns exactly zero'). Eq. (36) enters (35) multiplied by gamma, so it is established only at O(gamma^0). The O(gamma) remainder depends on the frame and on how the apparatus is held: a column hung vs supported gives +/- gamma M h/2. Its relative size gamma h/c^2 is 1.1e-22 to 1.1e-16. In the tree's own flat test-field setting von Laue is exact, so the drift is in citing a weak-field O(gamma) paper for an exact zero. No conclusion moves.

WEAKENED (what 'complete' means), tolman.py:170-171 'for a COMPLETE apparatus -- field plus mirrors'. Something must hold the plates apart against the Casimir attraction, and Fulling et al. hep-th/0702091 p.3 say so explicitly. Checked: the EM field alone has int sum_i T^ii = E_total != 0, so the struts or frame must carry -E_total. This is a naming gap in the tree's gloss. The refusal is unaffected.

WIDENED (the refusal's stated ground), tolman.py:173-174, :549 ('any ball enclosing a mirror : REFUSE (Sorge eq. 36, section 1)'), :1016-1017, :2974. Eq. (36) and von Laue cover only a region containing the whole support. On a ball that contains one mirror but cuts through the apparatus, int T^i_i is generally nonzero (shown: -27pi/8, -24/35, -2097152/688905). The refusal is still correct, but for a cutting ball its ground is unmodelled wall stress, not a vanishing integral. A refusal makes no claim, so nothing is over-represented in either direction.
ADDED (a different field), tolman.py:2607-2609 applies this scalar-field result to the EM apparatus in switch.py. This is harmless: the derivation of (36) never uses the scalar Lagrangian.

PARAPHRASE, tolman.py:167-168 'attributes a Tolman mass to a Casimir cavity'. The abstract says 'to a massless scalar field confined to a Casimir cavity'. The quotation 'basically relies on the virial theorem' (tolman.py:169-170) is verbatim from p.11.

SOURCE-SIDE DISCREPANCY, not the tree's: Sorge's eq. (33) prints (1/sqrt(-g)) d_mu T^mu_z where the correct form is (1/sqrt(-g)) d_mu(sqrt(-g) T^mu_z). Checked: the difference is d_j((sqrt(-g)-1)T^j_z), which is a total derivative, so it does not reach (36). This is a display discrepancy in v1, not an error. The journal version was not read.

C shows that, given conservation, (36) is algebraically equivalent to the premise F_z = gamma m_Tolman. Sec. static-spherical-radial-metric.name: Radial metric of a static spherically symmetric spacetime, g_rr = 1/(1-2m(r)/r)

source.located: Classic textbook form, no single originating paper. Read at source in two arXiv papers that state it exactly: (a) S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', PRD 53, 1938 (1996), arXiv gr-qc/9408002v2, p.4 eq.(4): 'The Misner-Sharp spherically symmetric gravitational energy ... may be defined in units G = 1 by E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr))' ... 'Note that E is an invariant'; p.3: 'The area of a symmetric sphere is 4 pi r^2, so that r is the areal radius'; p.12 eq.(27): '1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda}(r')^2 - rdot^2, which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4]'. (b) M. Visser, 'Dirty black holes: Entropy versus area', PRD 48, 583 (1993), arXiv hep-th/9303029v2, p.3 eq.(3): 'In any static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat spacetime the metric g_L may without loss of generality be cast into the form ds^2 = -e^{-2phi(r)}(1 - b(r)/r) dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - b(r)/r) + r^2(dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2)', with b(infinity) = 2GM and eq.(5) b' = 8 pi G rho r^2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9408002v2 (pp.1-4, 7-10, 12-13, 16-17, 19, 21) and hep-th/9303029v2 (pp.1-17, the whole paper). Misner & Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964) is NAMED-NOT-READ: it has no arXiv copy, and its form is quoted by Hayward eq.27. Combining (a) with the static diagonal form in (b): g^{rr} = 1/g_rr and E = (r/2)(1 - g^{rr}) give g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r) with m = E. Re-derived symbolically (C1a).

static-spherical-radial-metric.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002 eq.(4): 'E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr))' in units G = 1, 'an invariant', where r is the areal radius (area 4 pi r^2). Prop.1: a sphere is trapped iff E > r/2, marginal iff E = r/2, untrapped iff E < r/2. p.8: 'E may be negative, as in the negative-energy Schwarzschild solution'. Prop.6: 'If the dominant energy condition holds on an untrapped spatial hypersurface with regular centre, then E >= 0'. Visser hep-th/9303029 eq.(3): 'In any static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat spacetime the metric may without loss of generality be cast into the form ds^2 = -e^{-2phi}(1 - b/r)dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - b/r) + r^2 dOmega^2'; eq.(5): b' = 8 pi G rho r^2; 'This metric has putative horizons at values of r satisfying b(r_H) = r_H.' With b = 2m (G = 1) this is the tree's radial part dr^2/(1 - 2m(r)/r), and the proper radial length on a t = const slice is dl = dr/sqrt(1 - 2m/r).
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry: a warped product with round spheres of area 4 pi r^2, r the areal radius (Hayward p.2-3).
Static: a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector, so the metric is diagonal in (t, r) and the t = const slices are orthogonal to the Killing vector (Visser eq.3).
r usable as a coordinate: dr != 0, i.e. away from marginal spheres where 2m = r (Visser: 'putative horizons at b(r_H) = r_H'). In the static region 1 - 2m/r > 0.
Asymptotic flatness (Visser eq.3). It is used only to set phi(infinity) = 0 and identify b(infinity) = 2GM, not for the local form of g_rr.
Units: G = 1 (Hayward); c = 1 (Visser keeps G explicit, b = 2Gm).

No energy condition is needed for the definition. E < 0 is explicitly allowed (negative-energy Schwarzschild); E >= 0 follows only under the dominant energy condition plus an untrapped slice with a regular centre (Hayward Prop.6).

static-spherical-radial-metric.lacked_data:
This result is a definition plus an exact identity (Hayward eq.4 evaluated on Visser's static diagonal form). It is not a measurement or an extrapolation, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. C1a holds as an identity in m(r) and Phi(r) for every profile, and no physical constant enters the L3 ratio, which depends only on |m|/r1 and r2/r1.

Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: two 2026 papers (2608.09963, 2601.03077), written with about thirty more years of data and formalism, use the same form unchanged, and no measurement since 1964 bears on it.

Evidence that something was incomplete: the gap is in the tree's statement of the result, not in the external result. The slicing hypothesis (C6) and the constant-m ansatz (drift 1) were both left unnamed. Neither changes the conclusion, because the static-slice bound is proved for arbitrary m(r) (C3, C4, C7).

Real dependence on new data would arise only outside the result's hypotheses. One case is a theory other than GR, where g^{rr} = 1 - 2m/r still defines m geometrically but m is no longer the gravitational energy (cf. 2601.03077 Sec.6, Lovelock). The other is a non-static configuration, where Hayward eq.(27) adds rdot^2.
static-spherical-radial-metric.grade_evidence:
The published statement (Hayward eq.4: invariant, G = 1; Visser eq.3: static spherical, 'without loss of generality') gives g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r) on the static region, with m the Misner-Sharp mass. C1a re-derives this symbolically as an identity, and C1b re-derives m' = 4 pi r^2 rho from a freshly computed Einstein tensor.

The tree's three listed hypotheses (static, spherical, areal r; G = c = 1; 2m/r < 1, automatic for m < 0) are exactly the source's, minus asymptotic flatness, which the local identity does not use.

The tree's numbers are reproduced to every printed digit by a closed form (C2), and the tree's own routine agrees with it (C8).

The tree's L3 conclusions, which rest on this result, come out stronger, not weaker. 'The logarithm is the best case' and 'the return falls monotonically' are proved here for arbitrary profiles m(r), not just the constant-m sample (z3 + sympy: (s-1)^2 (s+2) >= 0, and f(x)/x = 2/(s(s+1))). No datum enters.

Two things are recorded, not repaired:
(i) A wording discrepancy: overturn.py:92-94 and 401 say 'ansatz-free ... no shell', while the code fixes m constant on [r1, r2], which means vacuum there (drift 1).
(ii) An unnamed but load-bearing hypothesis: the length is measured on the slice orthogonal to the Killing vector. On a boosted slice even flat space shows a 'deficit' (C6: 26.66 over [1, 200]).

Neither narrows the external result, whose statement already specifies the static t = const radial part, and neither moves the tree's conclusion.

1206.2942-phi.published_statement: p.4: 'The transition from symmetric to broken phase in the SM can be characterized by the vacuum expectation value (VEV) of the Higgs field H = (H+, H0)^T that transforms as (1, 2, 1/2) under SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y. A field basis can always be chosen such that only the real component of H0 develops a non-zero expectation value. Thus, we will write phi/sqrt(2) = <H0> . (1) The symmetric phase corresponds to phi = 0 and the broken phase to phi != 0. Note that (in unitary gauge) the masses of the W+- and Z0 weak vector bosons and the fermions are proportional to phi.'
published_hypotheses: Standard Model with one Higgs doublet H ~ (1,2,1/2). The sentence is framed 'in the SM' (p.4).
phi is the homogeneous vacuum expectation value, phi/sqrt(2) = <H0>, in a basis where only Re H0 has a vev (eq. 1).
Unitary gauge. This is stated, as a parenthetical.
Implicit and never stated: tree level with renormalisable Yukawas, so m_f = y_f phi/sqrt(2). The review itself warns on p.8 that the vev of the one-loop effective potential is gauge-dependent.
Implicit: 'the fermions' means the SM fermions whose Dirac masses come from Yukawas. Neutrino masses are not discussed in any page read.

Convention note, not a hypothesis: eq. (1) gives phi = sqrt(2)<H0> ~ 246 GeV, but eq. (20) on p.9 uses v(0) = 174 GeV = <H0>. The paper uses two normalisations; this is not an error. The tree uses 246.22 GeV, which is consistent with eq. (1).

1206.2942-phi.lacked_data: In June 2012, three weeks before the discovery, the authors had no Higgs boson and no coupling data. Their sentence is a structural statement about the SM Lagrangian, not an inference from data. Later data confirm kappa = 1 for W and Z (about 5%) and for t, b and tau (7-12%), and the muon is emerging. For the statement as published, the new data change nothing: nothing contradicts it and the re-derivation agrees. For the payload's fermions e, u and d, the missing data are STILL missing. kappa_e is bounded only to below 262, and kappa_e = 0 is not excluded. kappa_u and kappa_d are assumed, not measured. But the tree's 'm_e is 100% Higgs, subtract exactly 1' (address.py:514) and 'what the Higgs gives the fermions' (excite.py:145-147) rest on an SM prediction for exactly the particles no experiment has tested yet. Against over-reading this: every Yukawa that has been measured agrees with kappa = 1, and a large kappa_e needs fine-tuned cancellation (2501.07628 p.5). For caution: 2501.07628 exhibits models consistent with all current data that have kappa_e around 265-925. Two tree results move: K_mu, one-for-one with kappa_e, and the H2 stable-matter f, in proportion to kappa_l. Three do not move: C5, D27 and C2.

source.located: The result has three parts, and each has its own source. (a) The exact GR parent: K. Read in S. Antoci's English translation, arXiv:physics/9912033v1: eqs (2), (10), (29)-(30), (35), (40) and sec. 7 remarks 2 and 4, pp.1-9. (b) The weak-field redshift: C.M. Will, arXiv:1403.7377v1 (Living Rev. Relativ. 17 (2014) 4), sec. 2.1.3 eqs (5)-(6) p.12 and eq (30) p.28. (c) The Newtonian interior field is Newton's shell theorem (Principia 1687). 0802.0658-sec3.2.published_statement: p.10 (after Eq. 3.12): 'The noise kernel is defined in terms of the unrenormalized stress-tensor operator T_ab[g;x) on a given background metric g_ab, thus a regulator is implicitly assumed on the right-hand side of Eq. (3.11). However, for a linear quantum field the above kernel - the expectation function of a bi-tensor - is free of ultraviolet divergences because the regularized T_ab[g;x) differs from the renormalized T^R_ab[g;x) by the identity operator times some tensor counterterms, see Eq. (3.6), so that in the subtraction (3.12) the counterterms cancel. Consequently the ultraviolet behavior of <T_ab(x) T_cd(y)> is the same as that of <T_ab(x)><T_cd(y)>, and T_ab can be replaced by the renormalized operator T^R_ab in Eq. (3.11); an alternative proof of this result is given in Ref. [7, 8]. The noise kernel should be thought of as a distribution function, the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions.' Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'the noise kernel is finite for y != x ... When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur.' p.25: Phillips-Hu's expression 'holds for x != y without recourse to renormalization of the Green function, showing that N(x,y) is always finite for x != y (and off the light cone for massless theories).'
published_hypotheses: H-lin: a LINEAR (free) quantum field (p.10, 'for a linear quantum field'; the scalar field with coupling xi, Eqs. (3.4)-(3.5)).

H-ct: the regularized and renormalized stress operators differ by a c-number, T^R_ab = T_ab + F^C_ab * I, where F^C are local functionals of the metric that depend on the regulator (Eq. 3.6, p.8). This is true for a linear field. It is not true for interacting fields, where the composite-operator counterterms are operators.
H-had: physically acceptable (Hadamard) states, for which <psi|T^R_ab|phi> is finite (p.8).

H-sep: the finiteness statement is for separated points x != y (and off the light cone for massless fields, p.25). At coincidence the kernel has meaning 'only in the sense of distributions' (p.10), and pointwise 'divergences do occur' (p.29).
H-reg: a regulator is implicit (dimensional regularization in Secs. 3-4, point separation in Sec. 5).
H-qf, needed only by the ALTERNATIVE route of Sec. 5.2.1 and not by the Sec. 3.2 argument: a free field in a state that obeys Wick's theorem (quasi-free), Eqs. (5.20)-(5.21).

future-causal-cone-convex.name: The future causal cone of Minkowski space is closed under addition (reduction lemma)

source.located: Textbook theorem with no single originating paper, and the tree cites no source (status_word 'none (re-derived: sympy + z3)'). The standard statement is O'Neill, Semi-Riemannian Geometry (1983) Prop. 5.30, cited and restated by Lange-Lytchak-Samann arXiv:2009.08834v2 sec. 6 pp.12-13. The axiomatic form is Minguzzi arXiv:1709.06494v4 (Rev. Math. Phys. 31, 1930001 (2019)): p.11 Def. 2.1-2.2, Example 2.1, and p.87 sec. 3.1 (polar cone, (C^o)^o = C).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text. From 2009.08834v2: pp.5-6 conventions; pp.12-13, where C+ = {<v,v> >= 0, v_t > 0} and the reversed triangle inequality (6.1) and reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality are cited as [O'N83, Prop. 5.30]; p.14, 'all chords of a timelike curve are timelike'. From 1709.06494v4: pp.1, 5, 11, 13, 15, 19-22, 87, 89. O'Neill 1983 and Hawking-Ellis 1973 are NAMED-NOT-READ because they are only restated. Two attempts to read Minguzzi's Living Reviews 'Lorentzian causality theory' by title both resolved to 2009.08834, so it was not read.

future-causal-cone-convex.published_statement: 2009.08834 pp.12-13: 'vectors u, v in C+ in the positive causal cone C+ = {v = (v_t, v_x) in R x R^n | <v,v> >= 0, v_t > 0} of the standard Minkowski space ... satisfy the reversed triangle inequality (6.1) |u + v| >= |u| + |v| as well as the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality <u,v> >= |u||v|, see e.g. [O'N83, Prop. 5.30].' Closure under addition follows directly: (u+v)_t > 0 and <u+v,u+v> = |u|^2+|v|^2+2<u,v> >= 0. 1709.06494 p.11: 'All our cones will be closed and convex'. Example 2.1 there: the causal cones C_x = {y in T_xM\{0} : g(y,y) <= 0, y future directed} of a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold form a cone structure, so the Lorentzian causal cone is admitted as a closed, sharp, convex cone.
published_hypotheses: A single real vector space carrying a nondegenerate Lorentzian quadratic form, either a tangent space or flat R^{1,n}. The statement is pointwise and algebraic.
A time orientation, with both vectors in the SAME (future) cone. The result fails across cones.
The cone as the sources define it excludes the origin (v_t > 0; 1709.06494 p.11).
Any finite dimension n+1 >= 2.
A round (quadratic) cone. Beyond the round case Minguzzi takes convexity as a defining property of every admitted cone rather than deriving it.

no-communication-theorem.name: No-communication (no-signalling) theorem

source.located: Classics: P. H. Eberhard, Nuovo Cimento B 46, 392 (1978), and Ghirardi, Rimini & Weber, Lett. Nuovo Cimento 27, 293 (1980). Neither has an arXiv copy. Read through exact restatements: G. C. Ghirardi, arXiv:1305.2305 (2013), sec. 4 eq.(12), pp.13-14, which is the GRW proof restated by its first author; and Peres & Terno, Rev. Mod. Phys. 76, 93 (2004), arXiv:quant-ph/0212023, sec. II.E eqs.(9)-(11), pp.8-9.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1305.2305 and quant-ph/0212023. Eberhard 1978 and GRW 1980 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ: only their restatements were read. The tree cites no source for the theorem; it only names it (transit.py:318, ledger.py:452 and 605).

no-communication-theorem.published_statement: Peres-Terno (quant-ph/0212023 pp.8-9): a sufficient condition for 'no instantaneous information transfer' from a distant intervention is [A_mu_m, B_nu_n] = 0 (eq.9), where A and B are Alice's and Bob's Kraus matrices. Bob's probability 'irrespective of what Alice found', p_nu = sum_mu tr(sum B A rho A^+ B^+) (eq.10), reduces through sum_mu E_mu = 1 to p_nu = tr(sum_n B rho B^+) (eq.11), 'whence all expressions involving Alice's operators have totally disappeared.' Ghirardi 2013 (1305.2305 p.13, eq.12): under no action, a unitary evolution, or an ideal or non-ideal NONSELECTIVE measurement on S(2), 'the reduced statistical operator of subsystem S(1) does not change in any way whatsoever.' p.14: under SELECTIVE measurements the distant physics 'is actually changed', but the change depends on the outcome, and using it needs 'subluminal communication'.
published_hypotheses: H1 Linear quantum mechanics: operations are linear, completely positive Kraus maps rho -> sum A rho A^+ (Peres-Terno eq.6), with Born-rule probabilities.

H2 The intervention is NON-SELECTIVE, i.e. trace-preserving and summed over Alice's outcomes (sum_mu E_mu = 1; Peres-Terno eq.10->11, Ghirardi eq.12). A selective update does change the distant conditional state (Ghirardi p.14).
H3 The operations are local: Alice's and Bob's Kraus operators commute (Peres-Terno eq.9, stated as SUFFICIENT). In finite dimensions this is the tensor product H_A (x) H_B with A (x) I.
H4 There are no closed causal loops (Peres-Terno p.9: 'we assume that there are no closed causal loops').

H5 The content is non-relativistic (Peres-Terno sec. III.D: 'Replace superluminal by supersonic and the argument is exactly the same'). The speed of any actual signal is set by the carrier's dynamics (sec. III.C). The theorem forbids signalling BY the entanglement; it does not itself set c.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED WORDING (H2), transit.py:17-18 and :176, 'invariant ... under EVERY operation A can perform': the theorem covers every NON-SELECTIVE local operation. A selective (post-selected) operation moves B's conditional state; check C4a gives rho_B -> |0><0|. The file's own teleportation step relies on exactly this, so the omission is in the wording, not in the physics.

INSTRUMENT SAMPLES LESS THAN IT CLAIMS, transit.py:97-110: only U (x) I on one Bell pair is sampled (6 draws with seed 7, 40 draws with seed 101). no-communication-theorem.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the 1978/1980 authors had was finite-dimensional linear QM with Kraus operations. The theorem is an algebraic identity with no empirical input, so no later measurement can move it inside its hypotheses; C1 re-derives it exactly. Three things came later. (i) Sorkin 1993 found the weak point in the measurement model for QFT regions, not in the identity. Fewster-Verch closed it by adding axioms, without overturning the theorem. (ii) Gisin / Simon-Buzek-Gisin showed linearity is necessary, and experiment now bounds one class of nonlinearity at |eps_gamma| < 4.7e-11, consistent with zero. (iii) Donnelly-Giddings showed that the commuting-subsystem structure the theorem assumes cannot be defined in perturbative gravity. Evidence either way: nothing read here shows entanglement signalling in linear QM with local non-selective operations. Nothing here shows that H1, H3 and H4 hold in the gravitational or CTC settings the board also considers. So missing data does not change the conclusion within the class. It matters only at the class boundary, and those limits must be named as hypotheses, not treated as refutations.

Non-selectivity is missing from 'EVERY operation' (transit.py:17-18,176), and C4a shows a selective operation moves rho_B. no-communication-theorem.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names H1-H4 at transit.py:17-18/176 and at D13/D23, and limits 'proved' to that class. 1802.08257.published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'Since the ACA observations do not show any quiescent excess emission, we conclude that there is no need to invoke the presence of a dust belt at 1-4 AU. We also posit that the slight excess flux density of 101+-9 uJy observed in the 12-m observations compared to the photospheric flux density of 74+-4 uJy extrapolated from infrared wavelengths may be due to coronal heating from continual smaller flares ... If this is true, then the need for warm dust at ~0.4 AU is also removed.' Sec 4.2 (p.6): 'It is clear from our analysis that the entirety of the 1.3 mm emission detected by the ACA results from the short duration stellar flare. No emission is detected above a 3 sigma level during quiescence ... When averaged together with the remaining ~19 hours of non-detections, this transient event appeared as the ~340 uJy source detected by Anglada et al. (2017). Without the detection of a quiescent excess, there is no need to posit the cold belt at 1-4 AU.' ... 'the number of sources with flux density > 150 uJy that are expected within the ACA primary beam (FWHM ~39") is 13+10-8, a not insignificant number. In addition, Proxima Centauri sits close to the Galactic plane (latitude -2 deg) in a region of high background cirrus.' Sec 5 (p.7): the flare 'does not immediately impact the claim of an outer belt at ~30 AU', but background sources and cirrus 'suggest that caution should be used in over-interpreting this marginal result.' Sec 1 (p.1): 'Late M-type stars ... have long pre-main sequence phases during which the stellar luminosity can change significantly'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (data): the 2017 Jan 21 - Apr 25 ALMA 12-m (2 SBs, 41 antennas) and ACA (13 SBs, 8-11 7-m antennas) Band 6 data of programme 2016.A.00013.S. These are the same data Anglada et al. 2017 used; nothing new was observed.

H2 (sensitivity): 'no quiescent excess' holds at the ACA sensitivity: first-12 image rms 68 uJy/beam, no source above 3 sigma, a ~2 sigma central peak, and 30-s binning for short flares (p.3). A quiescent point source of ~100 uJy 'would not have been detected' (p.3).
H3 (parsimony, not exclusion): the belt conclusion is 'no need to posit/invoke'. The evidence for the belt is removed; the paper does not claim to exclude a belt below its sensitivity.
H4 (photosphere): the 74+-4 uJy at 1.3 mm is an extrapolation of the Ribas et al. 2017 SED model, not a measurement.

H5 (conditional, coronal): the 12-m ~30 uJy excess 'may be' / 'could also be plausibly explained by' / is 'likely' due to continual small flares (by analogy with AU Mic). The 0.4 au warm dust is removed only 'if this is true'.

H6 (background): the 13+10-8 figure uses 1.3 mm differential counts (Carniani et al. 2015) over 'the ACA primary beam (FWHM ~39")'; neither the integration area nor the formula is stated. A second contamination source is Galactic (latitude -2 deg, high cirrus) and is not quantified.
H7 (outer belt): the ACA visibilities 'do not adequately cover the short spatial frequencies' needed to measure the total disk flux, and the flare 'does not immediately impact' the 30 au claim.

1802.08257.lacked_data:
M18 had exactly the data A17 had; its result came from re-analysing those data in time, not from new data. Five things M18 lacked, and what came later:
(1) The mm flare rate. Burton 2025 measured it and recovered the Mar 24 event, which confirms the flare attribution.
(2) Second-scale time resolution of the 'quiescent' 2017 ACA data. Burton finds short flares on Feb 1 and Mar 19. This narrows M18's 'no source above 3 sigma' to its 30-s binning and makes 'no quiescent excess' stronger, not weaker.
(3) A direct 1.3 mm photospheric measurement. It is still missing: the 74 uJy is an extrapolation, so the coronal reading stays conditional, as both M18 and the tree say.
(4) Deeper source counts. ASPECS 2020 lowers the expected background, and 13+10-8 is not reproduced under the literal beam area. That moves a number the tree quotes, not a conclusion.
(5) Deep dust data on the 30 au belt. The 34 h 2019 ACA campaign exists, but no dust analysis of it was found or read here, so that question is OPEN.
Net: the later data do not move this result's conclusions; they reinforce the flare attribution. The one overreach is the tree's own gloss 'WITHDRAWN', which the data support only as 'no longer evidenced, disfavoured at ~2 sigma at A17's flux'.

IS WITHDRAWN', WITHDRAWN_BY_SOURCE = True) turn the source's 'no need to posit', stated at first-12 rms 68 uJy, into a withdrawal. 1802.08257.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: reword the flag to the source's scope ('not evidenced; disfavoured ~2 sigma at A17 flux'), or find a READ deep upper limit (for example from the 2019 ACA campaign) that excludes a 1-4 au belt. To WRONG (only for the quoted background figure): M18's area or method is stated and gives ~1-2 rather than 13; even then the tree's 'marginal' conclusion survives. lodders-2003-condensation-temperatures.name: Lodders (2003) 50% condensation temperatures at 1e-4 bar

source.located: K. Lodders, 'Solar System Abundances and Condensation Temperatures of the Elements', ApJ 591, 1220-1247 (2003), Table 8. Not on arXiv; the primary was not read here. Read through three arXiv restatements: (a) Lodders, Palme & Gail 2009, arXiv:0901.1149, sec. 3.4.1.4 p.5 and Table 1 p.6 ('Table 1 lists the calculated 50% condensation temperatures at a nebular total pressure of 10^-4 bars taken from [03L]'); (b) Lodders & Fegley 2023, arXiv:2301.03674, pp.40-44 (CONDOR method; restates the 2003 Cl 948 K, Br ~546 K, I 535 K, Ca 1517 K and updates them); (c) Wang, Lineweaver & Ireland 2019, arXiv:1810.12741, p.12 and p.15 (restates the definition, 1e-4 bar, C 40 K, O 180 K, Mg 1330 K, Si 1310 K). The update used for DATA is Lodders, Fegley, Mezger & Ebel 2024, arXiv:2411.01362, Table 1 pp.5-6 (log P = -2, -4, -6, -8).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0901.1149, 2301.03674, 1810.12741, 2411.01362 (two calls) and 2509.03724. The title query for Lodders 2003 resolved to 2301.03674, which confirms there is no arXiv copy of the 2003 paper. The 2003 primary is NAMED-NOT-READ.

lodders-2003-condensation-temperatures.published_statement: As restated in 0901.1149 p.5 (from [03L]): 'A convenient measure of volatility is the condensation temperature. These temperatures are calculated by assuming thermodynamic equilibrium between solids and a cooling gas of solar composition. Major elements condense as minerals while minor and trace elements condense in solid solution with the major phases. The temperature where 50% of an element is in the condensed phase is called the 50% condensation temperature. Condensation temperatures depend on total pressure. Table 1 lists the calculated 50% condensation temperatures at a nebular total pressure of 10^-4 bars taken from [03L].' Table 1 values the tree uses, with host phases: P 1229 K in schreibersite (confirmed only indirectly, through LF23's update to 1264 K); N 123 K (NH3.H2O); O 180 K ('rock + ice'); H 182 K (no host phase listed); C 40 K (CH4.7H2O + CH4 ice); Li 1142 K (forsterite+enstatite); Ta 1573 K; Au 1060 K (Fe-alloy); Hg 252 K; Br 546 K and I 535 K (Cl-apatite); In 536 K; Tl 532 K. 1810.12741 p.12: '50% condensation temperatures are estimated from where 50% of the element passes from gaseous to solid phase, either directly as elements, compounds, or as substitutions into condensing phases at a total pressure of 10^-4 bar.'
published_hypotheses: H1 thermodynamic EQUILIBRIUM between solids and a cooling gas (0901.1149 p.5; 2301.03674 p.40 'mass balance and mass action'); for C and N 'complete chemical equilibrium' (2411.01362 p.5), i.e. no kinetic inhibition of CH4/NH3 formation (Lewis & Prinn 1980)
H2 a gas of SOLAR composition (Lodders 2003 abundances); the values are properties of that gas, not of an arbitrary reservoir
H3 a fixed nebular TOTAL PRESSURE of 1e-4 bar; 'Condensation temperatures depend on total pressure' (0901.1149 p.5); 2411.01362 p.28: 'a total pressure of 10^-4 bar is model specific'

H4 the stated HOST PHASE for each element, with ideal solid solution for most traces (non-ideal only for As, Au, Cu, Ga, Ge, Sb in Fe alloy, 2411.01362 p.40); Br and I by an assumed substitution into apatite, since no thermodynamic data existed (2301.03674 p.42)
H5 the thermodynamic data available at the time (JANAF 4th ed., Robie & Hemingway 1995; sodalite from Wellman 1969; 2301.03674 pp.40,44)

H6 for H and O (and the noble gases) the tabulated value is not a 50% condensation of the element into rock. Only a tiny fraction of H condenses in water ice or hydrous minerals, and anhydrous rock holds too little O for 50% (2411.01362 p.4). The 2003 H value of 182 K carries no host phase in 0901.1149 Table 1

H7 the use as a volatility RANK is qualitative: 'Plots of normalized elemental abundances versus 50% condensation temperatures (volatility trends) are qualitative indicators' (2411.01362 abstract point 5)
hypothesis_drift: KEPT: H3, the pressure. stockgate.py:330 carries 'at 1e-4 bar' in the table header.
KEPT, qualitatively: H7. stockgate.py:738-751 regime_of() uses T_c only as a threshold on the binder element. The authors themselves call this kind of rank use qualitative (2411.01362 abstract (5)).

The authors' own boundaries at 1e-4 bar are refractory > 1300-1360 K, moderately volatile 1300-660 K and highly volatile < 660 K (2411.01362 p.2). The 500 K figure is Wang et al. 2019's category boundary (1810.12741 Fig.4 caption), not Lodders'. Measured: the four regime labels hold for any cut in (139 K, 1029 K], and moving the cut to 660 K changes Finding G's refractory mass by -0.001 %.

DROPPED H2/H3 at stockgate.py:182-184: 'Retaining volatiles is a statement about formation temperature, hence orbital radius' and 'THE SNOW LINE IS THEREFORE THE SELECTOR'. The source's T_c are equilibrium temperatures of a solar gas at one fixed pressure, and no T(a), P(a) disc map is part of the result. 2411.01362 p.28 says T and P varied with radial distance, height and time, and pp.4/30 call the depletion mechanism (partial condensation vs. partial sublimation) 'moot'. The step to an orbital radius is the owner's. The tree already concedes this downstream, at formation.py:271-279: 'REFUSED to compute a radius: it would use a nebular T_c outside its pressure hypothesis'.

lodders-2003-condensation-temperatures.grade_evidence:
What STANDS (computed):
- The tree's table is a faithful transcription of Lodders 2003: 53 values match a restatement read here. The restatements disagree among themselves on Mg, Si and Zr; that is unresolved and makes no difference.
- Both load-bearing uses survive every later datum. The regime labels are unchanged under the 2024 table and at log P = -2 to -8, with a cut window of (139 K, 1029 K]. Finding G moves by -0.25 % (refractory) and -0.09 % (rock+ice).

What is NARROWED (read):
- At stockgate.py:182-184 the tree goes from a nebular T_c ranking to 'formation temperature, hence orbital radius' and 'THE SNOW LINE IS THEREFORE THE SELECTOR'. That step drops the source's fixed-pressure, solar-gas and equilibrium hypotheses. The source supplies no disc T(a), P(a). Its authors call 1e-4 bar 'model specific' and the depletion mechanism 'moot'. The tree itself concedes this at formation.py:271-279.
- Lesser narrowings: H, He and O are labelled as 50 % temperatures, which the source's later account denies for H. The values are the superseded 2003 edition, cited correctly but not flagged as revised.

Why not WRONG: nothing here refutes Lodders 2003. The updates are revisions by the same authors on new data, not demonstrated errors. The owner's '99.06 %' against a computed 99.05 % is a rounding discrepancy, recorded and not repaired.
lodders-2003-condensation-temperatures.what_would_change_the_grade: To reach STANDS: restate stockgate.py:182-184 as conditional on a formation-epoch disc model, as formation.py already does, or find a read source that gives T(a), P(a) at the destination. To become DATA-DEPENDENT: a revision would have to drop T_c(P) below the cut (a fall of more than 529 K from its 1e-8 bar value) or raise T_c(N) above it. No source read here shows either. Reading the ApJ primary would settle the Mg and Zr disagreements between restatements; since both elements are above 1300 K, the result cannot move a conclusion.

In the hypothesis of Proposition 3.1 and by the principle of general local covariance, the fixed value of alpha_1 gives that the values taken by alpha~^S_1 and alpha~^TT_1 are alpha~^S_1 = 1/(64 pi^2), alpha~^TT_1 = 0.'

S half of the proof: the metric is rescaled conformally, g = Omega^2 eta with Omega^2 = (1 + W f_n chi_nu)^2. p. 40: 'general local covariance and ... perturbative agreement imply that some renormalisation constants are already fixed by their background value'.

2604.01047#thm3.6.grade_evidence:
SCOPE: the grade is for the S half, alpha~^S_1 = 1/(64pi^2), as a consequence of Prop. 3.1 plus general local covariance, with perturbative agreement as the matching. The TT half (alpha~^TT_1 = 0) STANDS (C6). Prop. 3.1's alpha_1 STANDS (C1-C2); its [w_1]/[v_1] notational discrepancy is recorded.

THE CONTRADICTION, computed from the paper's own formulas:
(i) The late region is Omega^2 eta with constant Omega = 1+W and mass m. It is isometric to Minkowski by the dilation, with the same m, and the paper's own convergence step puts the state in the vacuum there.
(ii) General local covariance then gives <T_g> = 0 exactly, at every order in W, by Prop. 3.1: Omega^2 H_g(m, mu) = H_eta(Omega m, Omega mu), checked symbolically and to all orders.
(iii) The printed (3.21) is identically T_eta(Omega m, mu), the value with mu frozen, and it is nonzero.
(iv) With 0 on the left of the p. 37 comparison '-4/(64pi^2) m^2 dm^2 = -8 alpha~^S_1 m^4 W', alpha~^S_1 = 0. The printed 1/(64pi^2) m^4 is exactly dT_vac/d log mu^2.

A consistency check points the same way. F_S(0) = -b_0 is proportional to alpha~^S_1 (linstab.py:158). A nonzero value therefore gives a nonzero zero-momentum response to a constant rescaling, where the exact covariant response is zero.

This is NOT a misprint: C3 reproduces 1/(64pi^2) from (3.21) exactly. The fault is in what (3.21) computes.

LIMITS:
- p. 36 ((3.22)) and Prop. 3.3 were not read (quota). The right-hand side of the comparison is taken as printed on p. 37.
- If (3.22) carries a compensating background-parametrix term, then 1/(64pi^2) is a non-covariant bookkeeping constant and the physical zero-momentum coefficient still vanishes. The tree's use -- the constant that sets b_0 and GMMPS's reported mode -- is contradicted under either reading.
- This grade does not say AMM is right in general.
- It does not touch the roots near -b_1/b_2 set by the free alpha~^S_3 and alpha~^TT_4.
- It does not adjudicate the physical renormalisation condition beyond what the general local covariance GMMPS invoke implies.

sm-yukawa-bl-charges.published_statement: NOT QUOTED: the source could not be read here. What follows is what the tree attributes and what this stage re-derived. Take the SM with its standard field content and a renormalizable (dimension <= 4) Lagrangian. Every gauge-invariant Yukawa term (Qbar H d_R, Qbar H~ u_R, Lbar H e_R) carries B = L = 0, so B and L are accidental global symmetries at the classical and perturbative level. Each is violated non-perturbatively by the SU(2) (and U(1)_Y) anomaly; B - L is anomaly-free under the SM gauge fields. Standard attribution, NAMED-NOT-READ: Weinberg 1979 finds that the first B- or L-violating operators allowed by SM gauge symmetry are at dimension 5 (LLHH, Delta L = 2) and dimension 6 (four-fermion, Delta B = Delta L).
published_hypotheses: SM gauge group SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1)_Y, with the standard chiral field content Q, u_R, d_R, L, e_R per generation and one Higgs doublet (as re-derived)
Renormalizability: only operators of mass dimension <= 4. Standard, and NAMED-NOT-READ in the source; what happens when it fails is computed here
B = 1/3 per quark, L = 1 per lepton, H neutral. These are assignments, not data
Perturbative or classical level only: B and L each have SU(2)^2 and Y^2 anomalies (computed here as 1/2 and -1/2 per generation), so B + L is violated non-perturbatively
No right-handed neutrino in the minimal SM. Adding one is computed here to be harmless for the Yukawa claim
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (unnamed): renormalizability, i.e. mass dimension <= 4. massform.py:2451 gives C3 the status 'THEOREM (perturbative SM)'. massform.py:486-488, :171-172, :719 and :2918 state 'no Higgs coupling carries B or L' under the hypotheses 'perturbative SM field content and B, L assignments (_Q table)' plus H-BL. 'SM' implies dimension <= 4 but the tree never names it, and it matters. The dimension-5 Weinberg operator (eps L H)(eps L H) is gauge-invariant: hypercharge 0, SU(2)-invariant to 2.5e-14 under 200 random SU(2) matrices, and non-vanishing. It carries Delta L = 2, so it is a Higgs coupling that carries L (rederive (2c), (3)).

WEAKENED BUT COVERED: B, the half every refusal uses. No Higgs-bearing operator carries B at dimension 5, and none of the dim-6 psi^2 phi^3 structures does; the dim-6 B-violators are four-fermion with no Higgs. Higgs-bearing B-carriers first appear at dimension 7: 8 psi^4 H structures, all with Delta B = -Delta L (rederive (2e)). All 18 Higgs-bearing B/L carriers at dims 5-7 violate B - L, so the tree's NAMED H-BL (massform.py:832-833) excludes them. At dimension 8 there are B - L-CONSERVING Higgs-bearing B carriers: 18 structures, e.g. H H+ L Q Q Q = (H+H) x QQQL (rederive (2g)). H-BL does not exclude those; only dimension <= 4 does.

GENERALISED, HOLDS: the tree goes from 'every Yukawa term' (massform.py:2049-2053, three terms) to 'no Higgs coupling' (massform.py:487-488). At dim <= 4 the only other Higgs couplings are |D H|^2 and V(H); the phi^4 enumeration gives H H H+ H+. Neither contains fermions, so both carry B = L = 0 trivially. The three listed terms are exactly the complete set of gauge-invariant psi psi phi structures (rederive (2)). Flavour indices do not matter because B and L are the same for every generation.

UNNAMED BUT HARMLESS: the minimal content has no nu_R (_Q at massform.py:2047-2048; H-FLAV at :834 assumes massless neutrinos, for the flavour sub-count only). Adding nu_R adds the Dirac Yukawa L H nc, with B = L = 0 (rederive (2b)). The Majorana bare mass nc nc carries L = -2 but contains no Higgs, so C3 survives it as a statement about Higgs couplings. H-BL does not survive it, but that belongs to a different key.

RETAINED CORRECTLY: 'perturbative'. B and L each have SU(2)^2 anomaly 1/2 and Y^2 anomaly -1/2 per generation. The two are equal, so B - L is free of SM-gauge anomalies and B + L is not (rederive (4)). The tree prices the anomaly route separately (S11, massform.py:512-560), so there is no drift. Recorded but outside this key: grav x (B - L) = -1 per generation without nu_R (rederive (4)). That bears on H-BL, not on C3.

One completion the data allow is the dim-5 Weinberg operator, and it is a Higgs coupling carrying Delta L = 2 (computed here: gauge-invariant and non-vanishing). READ in D. Gerosa & C. Owen, 'Gravitational waves from compact binaries', GGI Florence PhD class 2026, lecture notes L01_gwpropagation.pdf pp.3-5 (md5 09606aaa58c39b05a4abab3d75b23152) and L03_binaries1.pdf pp.2-3 (md5 ba3f262e3b8feb57c07f5a7f94d30566). Fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/dgerosa/gwbinaries_florence_2026/main/lectures/ and saved under scratchpad d67/src/gwflux/. The notes say their equation numbers follow Maggiore's book. They are handwritten with no text layer, so they were read as rendered page images (L01_p3-5.png, L03_p2-3.png).

gw-energy-flux-strain.published_statement: Gerosa L01 p.5, in units G = c = 1, eq. (1.153): 'dE/(dA dt) = +t^00 = (1/32 pi) <hdot^TT_ij hdot^TT_ij> = (1/16 pi) <hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2>'. Boxed and labelled 'GW energy flux': dE/dt = (r^2/32 pi) \int dOmega <hdot^TT_ij hdot^TT_ij>. It is derived from t^00 (1.135-1.136), t^0r (1.146) and the far-field form h^TT_ij = (1/r) f_ij(t - r/c). With G and c restored: F = c^3/(16 pi G) <hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2>. L03 p.2 (Maggiore 3.330-3.336) treats a rotating quadrupole: h_+ ~ (1+cos^2 theta)/2 cos(2 w_s t_ret) and h_x ~ cos theta sin(2 w_s t_ret). It notes face-on gives circular polarisation and edge-on gives linear polarisation in h_+. The emission pattern is dP/dOmega proportional to [((1+cos^2 theta)/2)^2 + cos^2 theta], and 'Emission is largest in the direction perpendicular to the orbital plane'. The single-amplitude form F = c^3 w^2 h^2/(16 pi G) that the tree uses is not printed in the source read. It follows from (1.153) only when h^2 = <h_+^2 + h_x^2>.
published_hypotheses: Linearised GR about a background with a separation of scales: lambda-bar << L_B, or f_GW >> f_B (L01 pp.2-3)
Short-wave (Isaacson) averaging over a length lbar with lambda-bar << lbar << L_B; t_mu_nu is defined only as that average (L01 p.3, eqs. 1.122-1.130)
Evaluated away from the source: T_mu_nu = 0 there and nabla ~ partial (L01 p.4)
Far zone: h^TT_ij = (1/r) f_ij(t - r/c) + O(1/r^2), i.e. outgoing radiation with r >> lambda (L01 pp.4-5)
TT gauge, with two polarisations h_+ and h_x (L01 p.4)
Four spacetime dimensions and a massless spin-2 field moving at c (implicit in the retarded time t - r/c)
For the angular pattern: quadrupole (slow-motion) approximation, with the source rotating in the x-y plane at w_s and radiating at 2 w_s (L03 p.2)

source.located: This is classical engineering mechanics with no single arXiv source. The thin-ring hoop balance gives sigma = rho v^2 (textbook rotating-disc elasticity: Timoshenko & Goodier; Stodola's constant-strength disc; Genta, Kinetic Energy Storage 1985, shape factor K). The candidate arXiv restatement is arXiv:2103.05224, 'A review of flywheel energy storage systems: state of the art and opportunities'.
source.via: Not read at source. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers all returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded' (four attempts). arxiv.org and alphaxiv.org are EGRESS_BLOCKED for both WebFetch and curl (403 CONNECT). The only contact with a restatement is a WebSearch result summary. It attributes to arXiv:2103.05224 the sentence 'If all the mass of a rotor is concentrated at the rim, the maximum tip speed is (sigma/rho)^(1/2)', plus thin rim K = 0.5 and Laval disc K = 1. That is a search-engine paraphrase, not page text, so it is not counted as READ. Because the result is closed-form continuum mechanics, it was re-derived in full here with sympy from force balance and the Lame equations. The audit rests on that re-derivation. The step-(5) discover_papers call also hit the quota, so no later work was read.

rotor-burst-speed.published_statement: Not quoted at source (NAMED-NOT-READ). The classical content, as re-derived here: take a thin rim, with all mass at radius R and only uniaxial hoop stress, spinning at tip speed v = omega R. Its hoop stress is sigma_h = rho v^2, so it fails once v exceeds sqrt(sigma/rho), and R does not appear in that limit. The search-summary paraphrase of arXiv:2103.05224 reads: 'If all the mass of a rotor is concentrated at the rim, the maximum tip speed is (sigma/rho)^(1/2)'. The rim hypothesis sits inside the sentence itself.
published_hypotheses: All mass is concentrated at the rim: a thin rim, radial thickness << R. This is stated in the restated sentence itself.
The hoop stress is uniaxial; radial and axial stresses are neglected.
The material is linear elastic and the rotation quasi-static: no vibration, creep or fatigue, and non-relativistic speeds.
sigma is the strength of the rim material in the hoop direction.

Other geometries carry different factors: a uniform disc has v_max = sqrt(8 sigma/((3+nu) rho)); a constant-strength (Stodola/Laval) disc has K = 1, and the same argument puts no ceiling on its tip speed.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED at warpfolder.py:117-118. The sentence 'A rotor asked to exceed sqrt(sigma/rho) does not spin; it disassembles.' states the thin-rim limit as if it held for every rotor. Re-derived here: a uniform solid disc reaches 1.557 sqrt(sigma/rho) (nu = 0.3). A constant-stress Stodola disc, h = h0 exp(-rho omega^2 r^2/2 sigma), closed by a thin rim of section A = R h0 sigma e^{-rho v^2/2 sigma}/(rho v^2 - (1-nu) sigma), satisfies equilibrium and compatibility at any v > sqrt((1-nu) sigma/rho). The sentence holds for a thin rim, not for all rotors.

source.located: This is a standard textbook computation with no single arXiv source. This key covers only the Einstein-equation matching, not Fewster & Teo gr-qc/9812032.

elementary-flatness-regular-axis.published_statement: NOT QUOTED VERBATIM (the source was not read; see source.via). The content, as restated by the search summariser and re-derived here: take an axis, meaning the fixed-point set of the axial Killing vector xi, whose orbits close with period 2 pi. The axis is free of a conical singularity iff lim_axis (grad X)^2/(4X) = 1, with X = xi.xi. Equivalently, circumference / (2 pi x proper radius) -> 1 for small loops about the axis. This is a NECESSARY condition for the metric to be regular at the axis (C^2, locally flat tangent structure), not a sufficient one.
published_hypotheses: a spacelike Killing vector xi with closed orbits, normalised so the orbit period is 2 pi (NAMED from restatement; not read verbatim)
a non-empty axis: the set where xi = 0, a timelike 2-surface (NAMED; not read verbatim)

the condition is imposed as a limit ON the axis and concerns only the norm of xi. It says nothing about the other metric functions (Phi and Psi here). Computed in A1: the invariant quantity involves only X = k^2 W^2 and g^{rr}.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: the 2 pi period of phi. See axial.py:33 (the metric, 'W^2 dphi^2', period unstated) and axial.py:186 (HYPOTHESES[0] 'regular axis: W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 1'). With period 2 pi k the no-cone condition is k W'(0) = 1 (computed in B1: lim C/(2 pi rho) = k W'(0)). W'(0) = 1 with k = 1/2 leaves a deficit of pi (B3). The same convention sits inside axial.py:187 ('W -> r, so W' -> 1') and inside the deficit/excess reading of axial.py:121-135. It is a coordinate convention. The conical term W'(0) - W'(inf) = (k W'(0) - k W'(inf))/k vanishes for every k once both normalisations are stated period-invariantly (D2), so O4 is unaffected. But W'(0) = 1 is the elementary-flatness condition ONLY under the unstated k = 1.

DROPPED: the axis end of the other boundary term. axial.py:43-46 says 'A REGULAR AXIS gives W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 1 ... Psi' -> 0 fast enough that W Psi' -> 0. Both boundary terms vanish'. But the condition W Psi' -> 0 is stated (axial.py:45, 187) only at infinity. At the axis the boundary term is lim_{r->0} W Psi', which elementary flatness does not control (A1: the EF quantity does not contain Psi). Making it vanish needs Psi' = o(1/r) at the axis. COMPUTED consequence: this is not load-bearing for the SIGN. E1 (Psi = a log(r/(1+r)), so W Psi' -> a != 0) gives INT_eps 8 pi u W -> -inf, with values -0.0307, -0.4405, -0.8549 at eps = 1e-2, 1e-4, 1e-6 (each step about a^2 ln 100). E2 (Psi' ~ r^{-1/2}, so W Psi' -> 0) keeps the equality exactly. By hand, checked numerically on E1 and E2: with W ~ r, if lim W Psi' != 0 then INT W Psi'^2 diverges logarithmically and the weighted energy is -inf. So 'INT 8 pi u W <= 0' survives wherever the integral exists, and only the EQUALITY form needs the dropped condition.

WEAKENED NAME (the tree's label claims too much; this does not narrow the theorem). axial.py:43 and 186 call W(0) = 0, W'(0) = 1 a 'REGULAR AXIS'. Elementary flatness is necessary but not sufficient for regularity. E3 (W = r + b r^2 e^{-r^2}) satisfies both conditions, yet its (r,phi) Gaussian curvature -W''/W ~ -2b/r diverges at the axis (E3a). The theorem's equality still holds there to 1e-10 (E3b), so the theorem is true on a LARGER class than 'regular axis'. The label claims more regularity than the hypothesis supplies, and nothing downstream depends on the extra regularity (specthm.py:606-608 builds H_axial as '; '.join(axial.HYPOTHESES)).

ORIENTATION, made explicit here but not a drift: the invariant condition gives W'(0)^2 = 1 (A2). W'(0) = +1 follows from W > 0 off the axis, which axial.py uses implicitly because W is a circumferential radius.

casimir-effect-magnitude.published_statement: Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007 p.10: '[the] spacetime obtained by periodically identifying Minkowski space along the z-direction. The ground state of the massless, minimally coupled scalar field on this (globally hyperbolic) spacetime has renormalized stress tensor <T_ab> = (pi^2/(90 L^4)) diag(-1, 1, 1, -3) (24) where L is the periodicity length. It is readily verified that the (A)NEC is violated along any null geodesic with a nonzero z-component of velocity, i.e., for those which wind around the compact direction. On the other hand, the (A)NEC is obeyed along complete null geodesics with zero velocity in the z-direction ... null geodesics which wind round the cylinder are not achronal.' p.11: 'distant interactions or boundary conditions apparently do not help to produce ANEC violations. For example, Casimir plates would not seem to be useful to support a wormhole ... because of the need to get through the plate.' Kuo-Ford gr-qc/9304008 eqs.(3.32)-(3.33): '... = -(zeta(4)/(pi^2 L^4)) diag[1,-1,-1,3] ... we have excluded the n = 0 term, since it is just the contribution from the Minkowski vacuum. Since zeta(4) = pi^4/90, <:T_00(x):> = -pi^2/(90 L^4).' GJW 1608.05687 sec. 5 (the tree's context, prose only): 'the negative ANE could be understood as coming from the Casimir effect associated to the cycle in space ... Of course, the effect would be enhanced if the signals sent between the black holes were directed and amplified (otherwise the Casimir energy would be extremely tiny if the black holes were far apart).'
published_hypotheses: H1 field content: ONE free, massless, real scalar (minimally coupled; in flat space without boundaries the conformal improvement adds nothing since <phi^2> is constant). Other fields change the coefficient (EM: 2 dof).

H2 geometry: flat Minkowski space with ONE periodic spatial identification of length L, infinite and homogeneous in the transverse directions; the density is UNIFORM. No wormhole, no curvature, no throat.
H3 state: the ground (vacuum) state of the identified spacetime, zero temperature; renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski (n = 0) term.

H4 the negative quantity is the energy density T_00 = -pi^2/(90 L^4); the null-null component is -4 pi^2/(90 L^4) along geodesics that wind the compact direction and ZERO along null geodesics transverse to it (FOP p.10); ANEC is violated only on non-achronal (winding) geodesics.

H5 semiclassical: <T_ab> is an expectation value; Kuo-Ford's paper is precisely about the fluctuations around it, which are not small in general (their abstract: semiclassical theory 'a good approximation only when the fluctuations in the stress tensor are small').

H6 (GJW context) the flat-space Casimir reading of the cycle is a discussion-section remark with no computation; GJW state the undirected effect is 'extremely tiny' at large separation and that directing/amplifying the signals would enhance it.

casimir-effect-magnitude.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The formula is a theorem of free QFT on a flat identified spacetime, and the only numerical inputs are hbar, c (exact since 2019) and G (22 ppm); the tree's constants are current and CODATA 2022 moves the gain by 6e-10 relative. No experiment measures a periodic-identification Casimir density, and the plate-force measurements (sibling audit) confirm the Lifshitz/ideal framework, with every real-material correction REDUCING |rho|. So for this result the authors lacked no DATUM that changes the conclusion: evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis on the data side. What was missing in 2016 (GJW remark) was a CONSTRUCTION, not data: GJW named 'directed and amplified' signals without quantifying them, and the tree quantified only the undirected single-scalar version. MMP (2018) and Butcher (2014) supply constructions whose negative energy does not follow the single-length pi^2/(90 L^4) law; that is a hypothesis the tree's model drops (H2), not an inaccuracy in the older mathematics. Neither construction reaches metre-scale separation with Standard Model content (MMP: d below the electroweak length; Butcher: static wormhole not stabilised, metre-long throat has radius ~6e-25 m), so having the later results narrows the class the tree's number describes without overturning the tree's metre-scale refusal.

The TREE'S USE is broader than the result: (1) phase1.py:403-404 quotes the figure without its model hypotheses -- one free scalar, flat transversely infinite uniform density, a single length D, cycle 2D -- and gjw.py:94-100 reads the resulting Planck landing as independent evidence when it is forced by the single-length model (D4); later literature (Butcher 2014, MMP 2018, read) shows Casimir-type sources with two lengths or 2D-reduced modes that escape that law, so '4.39e71 short' holds for the undirected flat-cycle scalar model, not for Casimir support as a class. (2) DISCREPANCY: energy density divided into a T_kk threshold; the winding-direction T_kk is 4|rho| (gain 1.097e71 D^2). (3) DISCREPANCY: the figure is attached to the 'Casimir corridor' (plate model, gain 2.193e71 at 1 m) though computed for GJW's cycle. None is WRONG: every named variant stays at 5e70-3.5e72 at 1 m (check F1), the metre-scale refusal is not overturned by any construction read (MMP's SM embedding stops below 2e-19 m), and phase1's ranking does not depend on the number (Lambda None).

adm-mass-definition.published_statement: EHLS 1110.2087v2 Def. 3: 'If (M, g, k) is asymptotically flat, one can define the ADM energy E and the ADM momentum P as E = 1/(2(n-1)omega_{n-1}) lim_{r->inf} int_{|x|=r} sum (g_ij,i - g_ii,j) nu^j dH^{n-1} ...'. McCormick 2401.05128v1 Def. 2.2: the same flux, and 'By the work of Bartnik [10] and Chrusciel [26] it is now well-known that the ADM mass is well-defined and independent of the diffeomorphism phi used to define it ... asymptotic flatness alone is not sufficient to ensure that the ADM mass is in fact finite, however with the additional assumption that scalar curvature is integrable it turns out to be the case.' For n = 3 the prefactor is 1/(16 pi). With g_ij = (1 - 2 Phi) delta_ij this gives E = lim r^2 Phi'(r) (derived here, C1). So E equals the coefficient of the 1/r tail of Phi exactly when the SPATIAL metric carries the same Phi as g_tt.
published_hypotheses: H1: an asymptotically flat end. There is a compact K and a chart M\K ~ R^3\B in which g - delta = O(r^-tau), dg = O(r^-tau-1), d^2g = O(r^-tau-2), with tau > 1/2 (McCormick Def. 2.1; EHLS Def. 3 has the weighted-Sobolev form).
