cauchy-schwarz.name: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality SUM G_AB^2 >= (tr G)^2/4 on a 4x4 symmetric matrix

source.located: Classic sources: Cauchy, Cours d'analyse (1821), Note II (the discrete form); Bunyakovsky (1859, the integral form); Schwarz (1885). None of the originals has an arXiv copy.
source.via: I did not read the originals (NAMED-NOT-READ). I read two arXiv restatements from alphaXiv page text cached at scratchpad/d67/src/casmag/all/. (i) arXiv:2312.03478v2, Sec. 2.2, Theorem 1: 'Let x, y in R^n. Then |x . y| <= ||x|| . ||y||. The equality in CBS inequality holds if and only if the vectors x and y are collinear.' (lines 295-305, md5 dc2a9a33e63238cbff44859bdccb8a25). (ii) arXiv:2504.19543v1, p.2 eq.(1): Bunyakovsky's 'well-known inequality' (a1^2+...+an^2)(b1^2+...+bn^2) > (a1b1+...+anbn)^2, which refers to Note II of Cauchy's 1821 lectures (md5 6d3233c32b77bed54ca672061737dfc8). In this stage I tried answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers, and all three returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded'. The Kuo & Ford paper the tree applies this to (gr-qc/9304008) was read earlier in DOCKET 67 (src/gr-qc_9304008.note). The result is pure finite real algebra, so a complete exact proof is given here and nothing depends on the unread originals.

cauchy-schwarz.published_statement: For real a, b in R^n: (SUM a_i^2)(SUM b_i^2) >= (SUM a_i b_i)^2, i.e. |a.b| <= ||a|| ||b||, with equality iff a and b are collinear (2312.03478 Thm 1; Cauchy 1821 Note II as restated in 2504.19543 eq.(1), which prints the strict form). The tree's form follows in two steps. Take a = diag(G) and b = (1,1,1,1) to get (tr G)^2 <= 4 SUM_A G_AA^2. Then SUM_A G_AA^2 <= SUM_AB G_AB^2, because off-diagonal squares of real entries are nonnegative.
published_hypotheses: a and b are real vectors in finite-dimensional R^n; the tree uses n = 4 and b = (1,1,1,1)
the inner product is the standard Euclidean one, and the squares are squares of real numbers
equality holds iff a and b are collinear; the extra off-diagonal step has equality iff G_AB = 0 for A != B
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, harmless (it narrows the tree's class to a subset of the theorem's): 'G symmetric'. fluctuation.py:293 encodes g[A,B] as g[min,max]. The inequality holds for every real 4x4 matrix, symmetric or not: z3 proves the non-symmetric case, and the sympy identity covers general real n x n. The tree's G is symmetric anyway, so this has no effect.

KEPT, and it matters: 'G real' (fluctuation.py:75). With complex entries and the unconjugated SUM G_AB^2, the inequality FAILS; z3 finds a counterexample with complex symmetric G and real trace. Recorded here so the hypothesis stays named.

ATTRIBUTION COMPRESSION, not a drift. fluctuation.py:75 says 'Cauchy-Schwarz gives SUM G_AB^2 >= (tr G)^2/4', which combines two steps. Cauchy-Schwarz proper gives only the diagonal bound; dropping the off-diagonal squares is a separate trivial step that needs real entries. The z3 proof at fluctuation.py:297 covers the combined statement, so nothing is lost.

The constant depends on dimension: the 1/4 is 1/n with n = 4 components (3+1 D). The tree states this correctly: 4x4 at fluctuation.py:75-79, the 2/n floor at noise.py:104-106, and T1 failing under smearing at noise.py:97.

APPLICATION hypotheses are in the file header but missing from local labels. rho = (1/2) tr G holds only for a massless, minimally coupled scalar in flat spacetime, normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum (fluctuation.py:15-17). Two local statements drop that qualifier: fluctuation.py:70-71 ('For ANY zero-mean quasifree (Gaussian) state') and the check label at fluctuation.py:472 ('for every zero-mean Gaussian state'). For a massive field the trace runs over n = 5 components, and the same Cauchy-Schwarz argument gives only Delta' >= 2/5. z3 shows that 1/2 fails as a bound on 5x5 matrices (SAT) and proves 2/5. Whether a physical massive state actually goes below 1/2 is not shown here.
rho != 0 is needed to form Delta'. The tree says so at fluctuation.py:91; the check here assumes tr G != 0.

rederivation.outcome:
ALL PASS, 23 checks, exit 0.
(1) Exact sum-of-squares identity (sympy expands the difference to 0) for general real n x n, n = 2 to 5: n SUM G_AB^2 - (trG)^2 = SUM_{A<B}(G_AA-G_BB)^2 + n SUM_{A!=B} G_AB^2. At n = 4 this completely proves the inequality and its equality case: every term vanishes iff G = (trG/4) I = (rho/2) I.
(2) Lagrange identity for the Cauchy-Schwarz step itself.
(3) Delta = Delta'/(1+Delta') is increasing, so Delta' >= 1/2 is equivalent to Delta >= 1/3.
(4) Controls built from rho and p_i alone reproduce the tree's printed values: thermal Delta' = 2/3; Casimir Delta' = 6 (Delta = 6/7); the same value with the sign flipped, so the bound is sign-blind; a single null mode gives Delta' = 2, Delta = 2/3.
(5) z3 checks, run independently of the tree's code: the symmetric case, the equality case and the non-symmetric case are all proved; the constant 1/4 is sharp; the equality case is attainable (vacuity guard); complex entries break the bound; 5x5 gives only 2/5.
The tree's own fluctuation.py --selftest also passes T1, T1-equality and the vacuity guard.

The tree itself shows T1 does not survive smearing: once K is not 4x4 there is no 1/2 floor (thermal counterexample, Hoelder bound plus z3). This narrows where the inequality can be applied, not the inequality.

cauchy-schwarz.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result, and the evidence is direct: the result uses no measured datum. It is a polynomial identity over the reals, with 4 SUM G_AB^2 - (tr G)^2 written explicitly as a sum of squares (checked exactly in sympy), so there is nothing Cauchy, Bunyakovsky or Schwarz could have lacked that would change it. Only the tree's application can move, and it moves through named physical hypotheses rather than data: rho = (1/2) tr G for a massless, minimally coupled scalar; n = 4; Wick factorisation, which needs a zero-mean quasifree state; flat spacetime with Minkowski normal ordering; and evaluation at a point rather than smeared. For a massive field the Cauchy-Schwarz route alone gives 2/5 instead of 1/2. That is a change of field content, not of data.
cauchy-schwarz.grade_evidence: The statement as used (fluctuation.py:75-79) is a special case of the Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz inequality, as restated in arXiv:2312.03478 Thm 1 and 2504.19543 eq.(1), plus the trivial off-diagonal step. It is re-derived exactly: the sum-of-squares identity proves both the inequality and the equality case G = (rho/2) I, and z3 independently proves both, confirms the 1/4 is sharp and confirms the equality case is attainable. The only hypothesis drift is an added symmetry assumption the theorem does not need, which is harmless. No data enter. The application scope (massless minimal scalar, n = 4, rho != 0, pointwise only) is stated in the tree's header and in noise.py; it is recorded above so that T1's local label is read with fluctuation.py:15-17's qualifier.
cauchy-schwarz.what_would_change_the_grade: Nothing about the inequality can change it, because it is a closed polynomial identity. T1 as physics is a separate question, and its standing would change if the result were quoted outside its hypotheses: a massive field (Cauchy-Schwarz alone then gives 2/5), non-minimal coupling, smeared observables (noise.py already shows failure) or rho = 0. Reading Cauchy 1821 at source would move read_status from READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT to READ, but not the grade.

1607.05280.published_statement: Abstract: 'We present an approximate time-dependent metric in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates for an evaporating nonrotating black hole as a first-order perturbation of the Schwarzschild metric, using the linearized backreaction from a realistic approximation for the stress-energy tensor for the Hawking radiation in the Unruh quantum state.' p.8: 'we solve Eq. (53) up to relative corrections of the order of 1/mu^2'. Eq. (64): f(z) = alpha z^2/(16 pi (1-z)). p.21: 'linearized backreaction from the stress-energy tensor ... in the unperturbed spacetime ... a very good approximation everywhere near to and everywhere outside the event horizon when the mass is large in Planck units.' p.17: the conformal scalar is 'Type IV everywhere outside the horizon' for Bardeen's fits [64] and [65] and for Visser's k3 = 0 fit. Spin 1 is Type IV only for 0<z<0.04374 [64] or 0<z<0.06151 [65], and the authors are 'not certain' it is Type IV anywhere. No read page gives a mass-function sign or any m < 0.
published_hypotheses: H1 first-order (linearized) perturbation of Schwarzschild; relative corrections O(1/mu^2) (p.1, p.8, p.21)
H2 <T> evaluated on the UNPERTURBED Schwarzschild background (eq. 31; p.21); not iterated to a fixed point
H3 spherically symmetric Unruh state
H4 massless emission only: mu' = -alpha/mu^2, alpha ~ 3.7474e-5 (photons+gravitons), valid when mu >> 1/m for all massive particles (p.2)
H5 mass large in Planck units; v << -1, u < 0 (Fig. 1, p.21)
H6 slowly evolving: orthonormal <T> = mu0^-4 x f(z) (eq. 36)
H7 mass infinite at u -> -inf; for a hole formed at M0, valid for mu(u) < M0
H8 Type IV for the conformal scalar rests on numerical fits (Bardeen, Visser); spin 1 is undecided because of the disputed k3 z^3 term
H9 gauge g(1) = h(1) = 0; trace = conformal anomaly beta xi z^6 (not the full graviton trace)

source.located: The explicit coefficient formula S(zeta)|0> = (cosh r)^{-1/2} sum_k (-e^{i delta} tanh r)^k sqrt((2k)!)/(2^k k!) |2k> is a textbook quantum-optics result. Its classic sources are D. Stoler, PRD 1, 3217 (1970); H.P. Yuen, PRA 13, 2226 (1976); C.M. Caves, PRD 23, 1693 (1981); R. Loudon & P.L. Knight, J. Mod. Opt. 34, 709 (1987); and Gerry & Knight (2005). None of them is on arXiv, and the owner cites no source. The paper the owner is auditing, Kuo & Ford arXiv:gr-qc/9304008 v1 (1993), supplies the convention the formula must match (eqs 3.9-3.17, citing Caves 1981 as its ref [8]) and the qualitative Fock statement.

squeezed-vacuum-fock-expansion.published_statement: This statement is not quoted from any page read in this stage. The standard statement, in Kuo-Ford's convention (KF 3.11 and 3.16, both READ): for S(zeta) = exp[(zeta* a^2 - zeta a+^2)/2] with zeta = r e^{i delta}, S(zeta)|0> = (cosh r)^{-1/2} SUM_k (-e^{i delta} tanh r)^k sqrt((2k)!)/(2^k k!) |2k>. KF print verbatim (p.8) that the squeezed vacuum is 'a superposition of states containing even numbers of particles', and that 'we may also take delta = 0, as this is simply a choice of phase'. The tree's form (fluctuation.py:427) is cs[2k] = (-t)^k sqrt((2k)!)/(2^k k!)/sqrt(cosh r) with t = tanh r, which is the delta = 0 instance.
published_hypotheses: H1 single bosonic mode, [a, a+] = 1, Fock vacuum a|0> = 0

(14): 'Delta Lambda/Lambda = R Delta alpha/alpha + (2/27)(3 Delta v/v + Delta h_c/h_c + Delta h_b/h_b + Delta h_t/h_t)'. Footnote 1: 'In supersymmetric models, additional thresholds related to squark and gluino masses would affect this relation.' b_0(n_f) = 11 - 2n_f/3 (Gross-Wilczek/Politzer 1973, restated in Hill-Solon eq. 109). Set Delta alpha = Delta h = 0 and this is exactly the tree's Lambda_3 = Lambda_6^(7/9)(m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27), with d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9.
published_hypotheses: One-loop running: 1/alpha_s(mu) = (b_0/2 pi) ln(mu/Lambda), with b_0(n_f) = 11 - 2n_f/3 for SU(3) and n_f Dirac quarks in the fundamental. No b_1 or higher term.

Leading-order decoupling: alpha_s is continuous at each heavy threshold mu = m_Q. In MSbar at one loop this is exact only at mu = m_Q; at any other mu the one-loop decoupling log ln(mu^2/m^2)/(6 pi) applies.
The scale mu lies between m_t and 'some unification scale', and the coloured content in that interval is the Standard Model's. Footnote 1: extra coloured thresholds change the relation.
Heavy-quark masses are m_Q = h_Q v, and the variation is split into Delta h_Q and Delta v.
The high-scale coupling variation is tied to Delta alpha by a GUT-dependent R. The R-term is zero when alpha_s is held fixed at the high scale, which is the tree's H1.
The light quarks u, d, s lie below every heavy threshold, so hadronic scales are described by the n_f = 3 theory.

qcd-one-loop-beta-threshold-matching.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3 (1973) is group theory multiplied by a one-loop coefficient. It uses no measured datum, so nothing measured since (alpha_s, the quark masses, the LHC's null result on new coloured states) can move it; C_A = 3 and T_F = 1/2 are recomputed here exactly. The one-loop threshold chain (Coc et al. 2007) also uses no datum: 7/9 and 2/27 are ratios of b_0 values. What the authors left out was higher-order QCD, and that was a choice, not missing data: two-loop running and the O(alpha_s^3) decoupling constants (CKS 1997) already existed in 2007. What came later is the O(alpha_s^3) heavy-quark matrix elements (Hill-Solon 2014) and the current alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1180(9). Having them does change the number: d ln Lambda_3/d ln v is 0.235 to 0.238, not 2/9 'EXACTLY'. That is +5.8% at NNLO (numerical RG here) and +7.3% at N3LO (Hill-Solon). It does not change the conclusions resting on the number: K_mu stays O(1) and negative, and the order-of-magnitude densities are unmoved. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the one-loop value needs no data and is reproduced exactly by two routes, and the refinements are stable to within 0.1% over the alpha_s band. Evidence for it, in a weak form: the one thing that could really move the one-loop sum is the particle content between m_t and the high scale. That is an assumption about physics nobody has measured, not a measured value, and the tree drops it without saying so.

thin-shell-conservation-law.name: Surface energy conservation for the thin shell: sigma' = -(2/R)(sigma + p), m_s' = -8 pi R p

SAME CONFIGURATION AS THE TREE: Pitre, Schneider & Poisson, arXiv:2604.05980v1 (2026), p.8, 'no matter inside and outside the shell ... D_b S^ab = 0 is compatible with' the Israel condition (Israel eq 21). THE TREE'S TARGET OBJECT: Le, arXiv:2606.22531v3, p.2. thin-shell-conservation-law.published_statement: Poisson-Visser p.2, for a thin shell with Schwarzschild vacuum on both sides: sigma = -(1/4 pi)[K^theta_theta], p = (1/8 pi)([K^tau_tau] + [K^theta_theta]) (8); sigma = -(1/2 pi a) sqrt(1-2M/a+adot^2) (11); p = (1/4 pi a)(1 - M/a + adot^2 + a addot)/sqrt(1-2M/a+adot^2) (12). 'It is easy to check that these imply energy conservation: d/dtau(sigma A) + p d/dtau A = 0, (13) where A = 4 pi a^2.' Then 'sigmadot = -2(sigma+p) adot/a (15). If we choose a particular equation of state, in the form p = p(sigma), then we can formally integrate the conservation equation and obtain ln(a) = -(1/2) INT dsigma/(sigma+p(sigma)) (16)', and '[sigma(a) a]' = -(sigma+2p) (21)'. Ishak-Lake p.2: the transparency condition [G^alpha_beta n_alpha u^beta] = 0 (6); m = m(R) (12) 'is precisely the condition that guarantees (6) at equilibrium ... For timelike Sigma then our assumptions require static embeddings in the neighborhood of Sigma.' PSP 2026 p.8, for Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside with no matter on either side: D_b S^ab = 0 holds.
published_hypotheses: H1: a thin (distributional) shell whose surface stress comes from the jump [K_ij] via the Lanczos/Israel condition (PV eqs 3-8; PSP eq 2.10b)
H2: spherical symmetry

H3: VACUUM on both sides, so no flux crosses the shell. PV derive (13) for Schwarzschild/Schwarzschild; PSP p.8 says 'no matter inside and outside'; IL eq (6) requires transparency with static embeddings (eq 12). The general Israel identity carries a flux term otherwise.
H4: (13) is the tau (energy) component of D_b S^ab = 0; in spherical symmetry the theta (Euler) component is satisfied identically
H5: for the integrated form (16), a barotropic EOS p(sigma). PV do NOT assume it is linear; they linearise only through beta^2 = dp/dsigma at sigma0 (eq 23)
H6: sigma + p != 0 where (16) is inverted. IL sec. II.D treats Upsilon = 8 pi R^2 (sigma+P) = 0 (the domain wall) as a separate case
hypothesis_drift: KEPT, WIDENED LEGITIMATELY (unequal masses). PV derive (13) only for two equal-M Schwarzschild exteriors (a wormhole). wall.py:222-224 uses Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside. Re-derived here from the Israel condition for arbitrary static vacuum f_in, f_out: the law holds identically in (R, Rdot, Rddot, M_in, M_out) (checks 1a, 1b). PSP 2026 p.8 states it for exactly this configuration. Citing PV for the unequal-mass case is a widening PV do not print, not an error.

KEPT, AND NAMED BY THE TREE (vacuum on both sides, H3). wall.py:222-223 says 'Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild outside', and wall.py:198-200 says 'Not the flux-coupled dynamic stability of the RADIATING shell ... What is closed here is the frozen-background linear radial mode'. The hypothesis carries real weight. Le 2606.22531v3 p.2 matches his shell with 'flux-source balance laws ... with an external crossing flux, mandatory here because the exterior radiation is emitted at the shell'. So m_s' = -8 pi R p is exact for the static anchor (wall.py:125) and NOT for Le's radiating shell, which the tree states itself.

ADDED, AND STATED (linear EOS, wall.py:225-227 and 316-317). PV integrate for a general p(sigma). The tree takes p = p0 + beta^2 (sigma - sigma0) globally to get its closed form. This loses nothing for V, V', V'' at R0 or for the linear period. The closed form also needs A = 1 + beta^2 != 0 without saying so. At beta^2 = -1 the solution is logarithmic, sigma0 - 2(sigma0+p0) ln(R/R0) (check 4d), and wall.sigma_of_R raises ZeroDivisionError (check 4e). wall.py never calls it there, since every beta^2 it uses is >= 0.

SCOPE WEAKENED IN A DOWNSTREAM CLAIM, not in the external result (wall.py:205-216 BONUS; the box is at wall.py:215, 'ANY STRICTLY STABLE WALL AUTOMATICALLY HAS AN UNBOUNDED DOMINANT-ENERGY BASIN'). The claim is exact within the linear-EOS model (checks 6a-6d; z3). But strict stability is fixed by beta^2 at sigma0 alone, while the basin depends on the EOS along the whole curve. Check 8a is a counterexample outside that model: x = 0.3 and beta^2 = 0.5 (stable, and the linear basin is unbounded), with a quadratic term c = 400 added to the EOS. sigma - p then first goes negative at R/R0 = 1.2085, while sigma + p stays > 0. The box does not repeat its linear-EOS hypothesis. Whether an actual orbit of that shell reaches that radius is NOT checked.

potential-exact-linear-cost.published_statement: Buttazzo 1307.3536 eq.(6): 'V0 = -(m0^2/2)|H0|^2 + lambda0|H0|^4'. Martin 1205.3365 eq.(13): 'V(Phi) = V0 + (lambda/4)(Phi^2 - v^2)^2', with V0 the classical offset. The minimum at Phi = 0 has energy V0 + lambda v^4/4; at Phi = v it is V0. Substituting Phi = v(1+eps) gives [V - V0]/(lambda v^4/4) = eps^2(2+eps)^2. That is the tree's identity, with |V_min| read as the depth lambda v^4/4 = m_h^2 v^2/8. The identity is printed in no source; it is a one-line consequence of the printed potential. Moffat 2503.11548 p.4: 'Only a direct measurement of the Higgs field self-coupling interaction can determine the shape of the Higgs field potential.'
published_hypotheses: H-TREE: the classical (tree-level) potential (Buttazzo eq.6). The radiatively corrected potential is not a pure quartic, and MS-bar lambda(M_t) is 0.12604 at NNLO against 0.12917 at LO (Table 3).

unimodular-gravity-classical-equivalence.published_statement: Verbatim from the restatement, arXiv:2603.14718v1 p.2: "the determinant of the spacetime metric is required to remain fixed throughout the manifold, sqrt(-g) = eps_0. This constraint reduces the full diffeomorphism invariance of GR to volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and leads to trace-free field equations in which the cosmological constant does not appear as a free parameter of the action. Instead, the divergence of the traceless field equations yields the relation R_{;nu}/4 = 8 pi G (T^{mu nu}_{;mu} - T_{;nu}/4), (1) which in general allows for a varying Lambda. Only if the conservation of the energy-momentum tensor T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0 is additionally imposed does the cosmological constant reduce to a constant of integration, and the full Einstein equations with a fixed Lambda are recovered. This structure implies that Unimodular Gravity and GR, while sharing the same classical field equations under this additional assumption, are known to differ at the quantum and perturbative levels." On the cosmological constant problem (p.2), Smolin's quantisation shows "vacuum energy contributions of the form g^{ab} C decouple from the gravitational dynamics, providing a concrete mechanism addressing the first cosmological constant problem." Field equations (p.5, eqs.12-15): R_mu nu - (R/4) g_mu nu = kappa (T_mu nu - T g_mu nu/4), equivalently G_mu nu + Lambda(R,T) g_mu nu = kappa T_mu nu with Lambda = (R + kappa T)/4.
published_hypotheses: H1 (defining): sqrt(-g) = eps_0 is fixed and non-dynamical, and the symmetry group is reduced to volume-preserving diffeomorphisms (2603.14718 p.2).
H2: only the trace-free part of Einstein's equations holds, eq.(12) (p.5).

H3 (load-bearing, 'additionally imposed'): T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0. Without it eq.(1) 'in general allows for a varying Lambda'. With it, Lambda is an integration constant and GR with a fixed Lambda is recovered (p.2).

H4 (scope): the equivalence is of the classical field equations only. The theories 'differ at the quantum and perturbative levels' (Bufalo et al. 2015, Fabris et al. 2023), and the perturbative discriminator operates 'when standard conservation laws are not imposed' (p.2).
H5 (implicit and standard; checked here, not stated in the restatement): the result is d_nu Lambda = 0, so Lambda is constant on each connected component of spacetime.

rederivation.outcome: All 13 exact symbolic checks pass (0 FAIL, sympy 1.14.0). C1: nabla^mu(R_mu nu - R g_mu nu/4) = d_nu R/4 holds identically on the general time-dependent spherical metric, which gives the restatement's eq.(1). C2: G + Lambda g - kappa T is identically the trace-free equation once Lambda := (R + kappa T)/4, matching eq.(15); with nabla.T = 0, Lambda is constant on a connected domain. C3, the witness that H3 is load-bearing: in flat FLRW with dust the trace-free system reduces to one equation, kappa rho = -2 dH/dt. With a = t^{1/2} this gives rho = 1/(kappa t^2) > 0, nabla^mu T_mu t = 1/(2 kappa t^3) != 0 and Lambda(t) = -1/(4t^2), and G_tt + Lambda0 g_tt = kappa T_tt requires Lambda0 = -1/(4t^2), so no constant Lambda works. C4, the static wormhole metric of 2603.14718 eq.(2): the trace-free system has rank 2 in (rho, p_r, p_t) and the Einstein system rank 3, agreeing with the p.5 count. Radial conservation takes the TOV form, and when the trace-free equations hold, d_r Lambda = kappa x TOV, so conservation holds exactly when Lambda is constant. C5, minimally coupled scalar: nabla^mu T_mu nu = (Box phi - V') d_nu phi. The first run failed C4c because of an index-normalisation error in this script (it multiplied by g_rr); after the fix all checks pass. Script md5 73b39856b23adf680f94ce0f1c1bed02. Output is in rederive/unimodular-gravity-classical-equivalence.out.

unimodular-gravity-classical-equivalence.lacked_data: This result has no measured input, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. Its content is an identity (the contracted Bianchi identity, C1) plus one hypothesis (H3), and the identity is re-derived here exactly and agrees; no later datum can move an identity. What the tree lacked is a hypothesis, not data: conservation, which the source itself calls 'additionally imposed'. Restoring it does not change the conclusion for the tree's use, because ordinary Lagrangian matter conserves T whenever its own equations hold (C5), so within the tree's classical scope the equivalence it quotes is exact. It does change how far the statement reaches: UG admits solutions with non-conserved sources and a varying Lambda(t) that GR with a constant Lambda does not (the C3 witness). The CC sub-claim is a matter of interpretation, not data: Smolin's decoupling argument sits on one side, the free integration constant on the other. So no datum has moved; there is one dropped hypothesis, shown by computation, and one contested question flattened to a boolean.

The tree drops it at permute.py:149-151, 361-362 and 569-571, and in the copies at obstruct.py:281-282, index3.py:970-971 and CLAIMS.md:1103-1106. (b) The drop matters, and it is shown here: the C3 witness (flat FLRW, a = t^{1/2}, rho = 1/(kappa t^2) > 0) solves the UG equations with nabla.T != 0 and Lambda(t) = -1/(4t^2), and solves GR with a constant Lambda for no constant. (c) Where the source's hypotheses hold (classical theory, conserved T), every step of the re-derivation agrees (C1, C2, C4). C5 puts Lagrangian matter inside that class, so the tree's use is unaffected: it is context in obstruct.py's EXPANSION-IS-A-RELABELLING row, whose verdict rests on theta = 3 H_0 and not on UG. (d) The CC-problem boolean (permute.py:363) reduces a contested question to False, while the tree's prose 'reframes rather than removes' fits the literature. Not WRONG: nothing refutes the tree's use. Not STANDS: a hypothesis the source names is dropped. special-relativity-kinematics.published_statement: NOT QUOTED. The source could not be read in this run. This was computed instead (rederive A and B). On Minkowski spacetime ds^2 = c^2 dt^2 - dx^2, a clock on the inertial worldline x = beta c t accumulates proper time tau = t sqrt(1-beta^2) = t/gamma, where gamma = 1/sqrt(1-beta^2). Crossing a coordinate distance D at constant beta takes t = D/(beta c) and tau = D/(beta gamma c). The boost preserves the interval, and a clock at rest in the moving frame reads t' = t/gamma.
published_hypotheses: NOT QUOTED from source. The computed statement needs each of the following (rederive A-B). H1: spacetime is flat (Minkowski).
H2: the reference frame (the Earth frame) is inertial and at rest with respect to the destination.
H3: the clock's worldline is inertial at constant beta over the interval. Any non-inertial segment needs the clock hypothesis, tau = integral of sqrt(1-v^2/c^2) dt, as a further hypothesis.
H4: the invariant speed C of the Lorentz group equals the measured light speed c. Per LSV gr-qc/0107091 p.4 and p.10, as quoted by the sibling audit: 'tiny deviations ... are logically possible'.

painleve-gullstrand-lemaitre.published_statement: Martel-Poisson Sec. II. Radial timelike geodesics of Schwarzschild obey tdot = E~/f and rdot^2 + f = E~^2 (2.1), with E~ = 1/sqrt(1 - v_inf^2) (2.2). Specialising to E~ = 1 ('starting at infinity with a zero initial velocity') gives rdot = -sqrt(1-f) = -sqrt(2M/r). Then u_a = -d_a T with T = t + int sqrt(1-f)/f dr (2.3)-(2.5), and the metric becomes ds^2 = -dT^2 + (dr + sqrt(2M/r) dT)^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (2.7). In their words, 'the surfaces T = constant are intrinsically flat'. Hamilton-Lisle eqs (1)-(2): 'beta is the Newtonian escape velocity ... beta = (2GM/r)^(1/2) and t_ff is the proper time experienced by an object that free falls radially inward from zero velocity at infinity'; also 'inside the horizon, the infall velocity exceeds the speed of light'. Lemaitre chart (de Haro eqs 18, 28-29): trajectories with rdot = -sqrt(2MG/r) satisfy R - T = (2/3) r^{3/2}/sqrt(2MG), and ds^2 = dT^2 - (2MG/r) dR^2. The time coordinate is the same free-fall proper time as PG time.

painleve-gullstrand-lemaitre.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence runs both ways. The result is a closed-form statement about the exact Schwarzschild solution. No measured datum enters it, so none that came later can move it. What the 1921-22 authors lacked was interpretation, not data. Hamilton-Lisle (p.1) report that Painleve read the flat spatial metric as making redshift predictions 'pure imagination', while Gullstrand saw that observables do not depend on the choice of coordinates. Lemaitre in 1933 showed that r = r_s is only a coordinate singularity. That error was repaired within the theory without new data, and the tree uses the repaired form. Later work narrows the scope but corrects nothing: negative Misner-Sharp mass (Faraoni-Vachon 2020), and lapse != 1 or pressure (Nielsen-Visser; MP Sec. IV). Every step was re-derived symbolically here, 15/15 pass.

hernandez-misner-kinematics-boost-decomp.name: Boost decomposition of (U, Gamma) as standard Misner-Sharp-Hernandez kinematics

source.located: W. C. Hernandez & C. W. Misner, ApJ 143, 452 (1966), and C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964). Neither is on arXiv. The MSH formalism was read through arXiv restatements: Helou, Musco & Miller arXiv:1601.05109v6 (CQG 34, 135012, 2017) pp.3-6, 8-11, 30. Their p.3 footnote says MSH is 'a composite' of MS 1964, HM 1966 and May & White 1966. Also read: Faraoni, Ellis, Firouzjaee, Helou & Musco arXiv:1610.05822 (PRD 95, 024008) pp.5-8, 12-13; Escriva arXiv:2504.05813v3 (2025) pp.3-5, 12. The invariance was cross-read in Hayward arXiv:gr-qc/9408002v2 pp.3-4, 16.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1601.05109, 1610.05822, 2504.05813, gr-qc/9408002 and 2601.03077. HM 1966 and MS 1964 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ. The explicit two-observer boost U' = cosh w U + sinh w Gamma, Gamma' = sinh w U + cosh w Gamma was not found printed as-is in any source read. What the restatements do print: (i) U = D_t R and Gamma = D_r R, both in the fluid's comoving frame; (ii) Gamma^2 - U^2 = gradR.gradR = 1 - 2M/R; (iii) HMM eq.(15), dR/dtau = U + Gamma v; (iv) Faraoni eqs.(4.16)-(4.17), the comoving-vs-Kodama gamma_rel = (1 - U^2/Gamma^2)^-1/2 with |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|. The boost follows from (iii) plus time dilation (check C1).

hernandez-misner-kinematics-boost-decomp.published_statement: Helou-Musco-Miller 1601.05109 p.5, eqs.(3)-(6): 'In the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez approach, two basic differential operators are introduced D_t = (1/a) d/dt and D_r = (1/b) d/dr, representing derivatives with respect to proper time and radial proper distance in the comoving frame of the fluid ... U = D_t R ... Gamma = D_r R ... related to the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass M ... by the constraint equation Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R'. Eq.(9): 'M = (R/2)(1 - grad_a R grad^a R) with grad_a R grad^a R = Gamma^2 - U^2'. Eq.(15)-(16): '(1/a) dR/dt = dR/dtau = (U + Gamma v), where v = (b/a) dr/dt is the 3-velocity of the object ... measured with respect to the local comoving frame of the fluid.' Faraoni et al 1610.05822 p.5: 'all spherically symmetric foliations will produce the same apparent horizons (but this is not true of non-spherical foliations)'. Faraoni eqs.(4.16)-(4.17): 'u^a_(K) u_(C)a = -1/sqrt(1 - U^2/Gamma^2) = -gamma(v_rel) ... |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|'. Hayward gr-qc/9408002 p.4: 'Note that E is an invariant.'

perfect fluid (HMM eq.7). It is needed for the MSH evolution equations and for M as a volume integral of e, but NOT for the kinematic identity Gamma^2 - U^2 = gradR.gradR

nec-zero-rhs-saturation.name: NEC zero RHS saturated by vacuum and by EM field

source.located: No single paper. The pointwise NEC T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 is Hawking & Ellis (CUP 1973) sec. 4.3, which has no arXiv copy (NAMED-NOT-READ). What was read, at source: Kontou & Sanders arXiv:2003.01815 (2020): eq (26) and Table 1 (the NEC), Prop. 2.1, eq (15) (Maxwell/Proca stress tensor), eqs (36)-(37) and Table 2 (Maxwell/Proca: NEC holds for every off-shell configuration; traceless at n=4), eq (39) (non-minimal scalar breaks the NEC classically), and p.3 (every pointwise EC is violated by essentially any QFT, ref [7] = Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe 1965, NAMED-NOT-READ). Martin-Moruno & Visser arXiv:1702.05915 (2017): eq (2.6); type-I table p.6 (NEC <=> rho+p_i>=0); p.4 (non-null EM fields are type I); eq (2.13) (null dust T = f k k); eq (2.15) (electric or magnetic field: diag(mu,-mu,mu,mu)); p.10 (the Casimir vacuum violates all the standard conditions).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2003.01815 and 1702.05915 (page text quoted); Hawking-Ellis 1973 and Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe 1965 are NAMED-NOT-READ, restated in those two

nec-zero-rhs-saturation.published_statement: NEC: 'T_ab k^a k^b >= 0' for every null k (K&S eq 26; MM&V eq 2.6). For a type-I tensor this is rho + p_i >= 0 (MM&V p.6). Maxwell/Proca: the NEC holds 'for all off-shell configurations' (K&S Table 2), and the EM tensor is traceless at n=4 (K&S p.15). MM&V eq (2.15): an electric or magnetic field of energy density mu is diag(mu,-mu,mu,mu), so rho + p_1 = 0. Radiation is T = f k k (eq 2.13). K&S Prop 2.1: if S_ab eta^a xi^b is bounded below, its greatest lower bound is zero. Neither source uses the word 'saturates' here. Saturation, meaning T_kk = 0 at some nonzero null k, is the direct consequence of eqs (2.13) and (2.15) under the sources' own criterion, and this audit re-derives it.
published_hypotheses: Classical, pointwise condition: K&S p.3 says every pointwise EC is violated by essentially any QFT (EGJ, NAMED-NOT-READ); MM&V p.10 says the Casimir vacuum violates all of them

Holds only on a restricted classical matter class. K&S Table 2 has it hold for minimal Klein-Gordon with any V and for Maxwell/Proca; the non-minimal scalar (xi != 0) violates it even on-shell (eq 39)
Maxwell T_ab = F_ac F_b^c - (1/4) g_ab F^2 (K&S eq 15, m=0) in n = 4, where it is traceless
Non-null EM is Hawking-Ellis type I (MM&V p.4); null EM is type II null dust (eq 2.13)
Scale invariance (K&S Prop 2.1): an unnormalised infimum of 0 is trivial, so saturation means T_kk = 0 at a nonzero null k
'Vacuum' means T_ab = 0 (classical, or Minkowski renormalised). Casimir, Boulware, Hartle-Hawking and Unruh vacua VIOLATE the NEC (MM&V p.10)
hypothesis_drift: UNDER-CLAIM IN THE CANONICAL RESTATEMENT, not in the owner. The canonical entry says 'null EM field saturates'. bounds.py:43 and :295 say 'EM' without qualification, and the unqualified form is correct: EVERY Maxwell field saturates at every point, along its principal null direction(s). Non-null: MM&V eq 2.15, checked on 200 random fields (B1, 2.0e-14). Null: eq 2.13 (C1/C2). No effect on K=0.

DROPPED 'classical' AT A DIFFERENT SITE: bounds.py:88-90 (and the printed reading at :406) files the six G=0 bounds, the zero-RHS row among them, as 'statements about quantum field theory on a fixed background'. The pointwise zero-RHS NEC is violated in essentially every QFT (K&S p.3), by Casimir (MM&V p.10), and classically by the non-minimal scalar (K&S eq 39; check F1 gives T_kk = -2). No text at :43 or :295 says 'classical'. Saturation and K=0 are unaffected: the Minkowski vacuum keeps renormalised <T> = 0. Recorded as a discrepancy, not repaired.

IMPLICIT, SATISFIED: slot K ('known to be saturated', bounds.py:28) is undefined. By scaling, every NEC-satisfying T has unnormalised infimum 0 (G1), so saturation must mean attainment at a nonzero k. Vacuum attains it in every direction. EM attains it at every point along its PNDs. A minimal scalar with timelike gradient does not attain it (F2, min 0.49).

IMPLICIT: 'vacuum' at :43/:295 must mean T_ab = 0. Read as a general quantum vacuum, the claim would fail in the other direction, since those vacua violate the NEC (MM&V p.10). Under the reading consistent with the row being a bound that holds, no drift.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (17 checks), using sympy, z3 and numpy. (A) From the covariant F in (-,+,+,+): T_00 = (E^2+B^2)/8pi, trace 0, and T_kk = |E_perp + n x B|^2/4pi modulo |n|=1 (Groebner). This is a sum of squares, so the NEC holds for every Maxwell field. (B) For 200 random non-null F, both principal null directions are null and give T_kk/T_00 <= 2.0e-14. A null-sphere grid shows no negative value. (C) Plane wave: T = l l/4pi and T_kk(l) = 0. (D) A pure E field gives diag(mu,-mu,mu,mu), and rho+p_1 = 0. (E) z3: the negated identity is unsat; a non-null F with T_kk = 0 at some null k is sat. INFO: z3 asked directly for T_kk < 0 returns 'unknown', a solver limit that is evidence neither way. (F) The non-minimal scalar at xi=1 gives T_kk = -2 (the classical hypothesis is load-bearing). A minimal scalar with timelike gradient does not saturate (min 0.49). (G) Scaling triviality of an unnormalised infimum. (H) Tree zero row = (0,0,0,0,0,0) with K=0, counted in saturated().

For a normal-ordered free scalar, coherent states do not violate the NEC, while superpositions can (Theorems 2-5). Vacuum saturation carries into QFT, but the zero RHS is not a state-independent QFT bound.

gr-qc/0208045.published_statement: Abstract: 'We construct a particular class of quantum states for a massless, minimally coupled free scalar field which are of the form of a superposition of the vacuum and multi-mode two-particle states ... they can produce an arbitrarily large amount of negative energy in a given region of space at a fixed time. This class of states thus provides an explicit counterexample to the existence of a spatially averaged quantum inequality in four-dimensional spacetime.' Sec. III p.9: 'The first conclusion is the proof that there are no lower bounds on the spatially sampled energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field in four spacetime dimensions. ... S(F) = INT d^3x F(x) <:T00(x,t):> (42) at time t, where F(x) is a spatial sampling function. Let r0 be the characteristic width ... [or] the maximum width of F(x) in any direction.' p.10: 'Thus S(F) is unbounded below. However, this state satisfies the temporal quantum inequality, Eq. (1).' p.8: 'each state in this sequence will have the Hadamard form. By progressively increasing the values of Lambda ... we can make the energy density in our spatially sampled region as negative as we like.' p.10: 'The integration over all space removes the contribution of the rho2 term, leaving only the non-negative contribution of the rho1 term ... the compensating positive energy is arbitrarily far from the negative energy.' p.2: 'the total energy in any quantum state for a quantum field in boundary-free Minkowski spacetime must be non-negative ... <H> >= 0 (3), and <H> = 0 only in the vacuum state' (quoted as a known result, not proven in this paper). p.12 summary: 'we have shown that there are no purely spatially averaged quantum inequalities over bounded regions in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, even though the integral over all space is bounded. However, spacetime averaged quantum inequalities do exist.' p.10: 'it seems likely that one can construct similar counterexamples to spatial quantum inequalities in all spacetime dimensions greater than two' (a conjecture). p.12: 'The logarithmic divergences (of the energy density with the cutoff Lambda) are rather slow. We do not know whether it is possible to construct examples in Minkowski space with more severe divergences.'
published_hypotheses: H1 massless (m = 0), minimally coupled (xi = 0), free (non-interacting) real scalar field: abstract, Sec. II, and Sec. III p.9 'for the massless minimally coupled scalar field'
H2 four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, surface of constant time, no boundaries (Sec. I; <H> >= 0 is stated for 'boundary-free Minkowski spacetime')

gr-qc/0208045.lacked_data: No measured datum enters FHR. It is a construction in free QFT, so no later measurement can move it. What the authors lacked in 2002 was theory, not data. (a) A rigorous, non-asymptotic proof: the paper works at leading order. This audit's exact-integrand numerics confirm both ln Lambda coefficients (to 1.2e-8 and 1.1e-5), which is evidence FOR the conclusion. (b) Knowledge of other fields: still missing in what was read. Kontou-Sanders Table 3 leaves Maxwell and Dirac at '?', and says the spatial case 'usually' has no QEI. This cuts AGAINST M, because a field-specific spatial bound would be a refusal instrument, not a licence. (c) The UV completion. The divergence is only ln Lambda. If field theory stops at a physical cutoff (Freivogel-Krommydas raise this objection for the null analogue), FHR's family reaches at most K ln(Lambda r0)/r0^4 with K = 1.2554e-2. At r0 = 1 m with a Planck cutoff that is 0.988 hbar c/r0^4, about 104 times the Lorentzian temporal scale at t0 = r0/c. So supplying the missing UV datum would turn 'unbounded below' into a finite, log-enhanced ceiling for this family. That weakens ledger D6's 'THE MAGNITUDE AXIS CARRIES NO NO-GO' and does not help a warp. It does not reverse how bounds.py uses the result: whatever the cutoff, the massless minimally coupled scalar refutes a UNIVERSAL cutoff-free spatial bound. The board's actual refusal is priced on the duration axis (Fewster 1208.5399 Eq.(4)), and FHR's transient witness states obey that bound. The evidence in both directions is computed in the rederive script. Whether a cutoff restores a spatial bound in general is OPEN.
gr-qc/0208045.grade_evidence: The paper was READ in full at source, every quotation the tree uses matches it word for word, and the re-derivation of Sec. II-III agrees (28/28 checks, including exact-integrand numerics for both log coefficients). Even so, the tree states the result for a larger class than the paper proves. It drops the field restriction to the massless minimally coupled free scalar (bounds.py:31-32, 144-146, 211-216, 262-264; achievable.py:151-153; ledger.py:399-404). It drops state-independence where bounds.py's own S slot makes it load-bearing (bounds.py:262-264, 'FHR prove there cannot be one'). The use that matters most still STANDS: no UNIVERSAL spatial bound over a bounded region in 4D Minkowski can refuse the corridor, because one admissible field is a counterexample. The state-independence gap is partly closed here: bounds that depend on the state only through <H> also fail (computed at leading log). The grade is not WRONG: nothing refutes the theorem, and the 'lambda0 > r0' prose and the Eq.(5)/(10) cross-reference are discrepancies, not errors in the conclusion.
gr-qc/0208045.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners restore the dropped hypotheses (massless minimally coupled scalar, or 'no universal bound'; state-independent; Minkowski; Lambda -> oo), or cited proofs extending FHR to Maxwell, Dirac and massive fields and to curved Cauchy surfaces are READ (Helfer CQG 13 L129 is the named candidate for the curved case). classical-charge-radius-inside-body.name: Every charged body that exists has classical radius r_c = Q^2/2M no larger than its own radius a

source.located: No single source paper. The tree derives this itself in drivensource.py sec.4 and obligation E2, building on the classical charged-body and Reissner-Nordstrom literature. The external result that bears directly on the universal claim is Bonnor & Cooperstock, 'Does the electron contain negative mass?', Phys. Lett. A 139 (1989) 442, together with Cooperstock & Rosen 1989 and Herrera & Varela, Phys. Lett. A 189 (1994) 11. These are pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ. They are restated exactly in arXiv:0710.5619 (S. Bhadra, PhD thesis 2007) sec. 3.1-3.2.1, eqs (3.1),(3.5)-(3.7), pp. 34-36, and summarized on pp. 17-18 (with Ponce de Leon 1988 and Lopez 1992). The equality case (source boundary exactly at r = e^2/2m, zero bare mass) is restated in arXiv:1212.2920 (Burinskii 2013) eq (5), p.3, the Lopez bubble. Measured lepton sizes come from arXiv:2506.02450 (Bourilkov 2025) Table 1 and eq (3), which draw on L3 PLB 489 (2000) 81 and Bourilkov PRD 62 (2000) 076005.

classical-charge-radius-inside-body.published_statement: Bonnor-Cooperstock 1989, as restated in arXiv:0710.5619 p.36: 'any spherically symmetric distribution of charged fluid, irrespective of its equation of state, whose total mass, radius and charge correspond to the observed values of the electron, must have a negative energy distribution (at least for some values of the radial coordinate)'. The mechanism is in eqs (3.5)-(3.7). Match e^{-2lambda} = 1 - (1/r) int_0^r (8 pi rho + e^{-(nu+lambda)} E^2) r^2 dr to Reissner-Nordstrom at r = a. With m = 6.76e-56 cm, q = 1.38e-34 cm and a = 1e-16 cm, q^2/a^2 - 2m/a ~ 2e-36 > 0, so rho < 0 somewhere. Eq (3.1), M = m - q^2/2a, comes out negative, about -1e-52 cm. Ponce de Leon 1988 (restated p.21): repulsion 'always takes place in the interior of a charged perfect fluid sphere when its radius is less than the classical electron radius', but not necessarily for anisotropic spheres or charge sitting on the boundary. The tree's bound r_c <= a is the contrapositive of this result, since r_c <= a holds exactly when the Misner-Sharp mass at the surface, m_MS(a), is >= 0. The literature applies it to the electron in the opposite direction: the measured a is below r_c, so the interior must hold negative mass.
published_hypotheses: Classical Einstein-Maxwell (GR with linear Maxwell), static, spherically symmetric charged fluid (0710.5619 eqs 3.3-3.6)
Regular centre: the mass integral starts at r = 0 with no point singularity (eq 3.5)
Reissner-Nordstrom exterior matched at a sharp boundary r = a
Inputs: electron m and q in geometrized units, and the 1983 size bound a ~ 1e-16 cm (Quigg 1983)
Spin and magnetic moment are not modelled (0710.5619 p.35)

The tree's derivation (drivensource.py:144-150) uses flat-space accounting, M >= X/a, and holds 'whenever the body's own contribution to M is non-negative'. E2 (drivensource.py:426-429) states this as the hypothesis mu >= 0.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED at overturn.py:49-50 ('any body of charge Q and mass M >= 0') and at overturn.py:376 ('every charged body with mass >= 0'). The bound needs mu >= 0, the body's own mass excluding the electromagnetic field and including binding, as drivensource.py:149 and E2 at drivensource.py:429 say. Total mass M >= 0 is not enough: z3 returns sat with X=2, a=1, mu=-1, M=1, r_c=2. drivensource.py's own DRIFT guard (drivensource.py:430-433) is built to find exactly this counterexample.

ADDED at overturn.py:51, :262 and :318 ('for every charged body that exists'). This is an empirical universal over real bodies, and no owner measures it. drivensource.py has no table of bodies and gives no Q, M or a for any real body. The universal is declared, not computed.

DROPPED at overturn.py:48-53: 'a classical body with a sharp radius and a regular centre'. The derivation (drivensource.py:144-164) assumes such a body. Charged leptons have measured size bounds below r_c, so they fit only if mu < 0.

DROPPED, harmless: the gravitational binding in drivensource.py:146-152's M = mu + X/a. Re-derived exactly with the Israel junction condition for a thin shell: M - Q^2/2a = mu(2a-mu)/(2a), which is >= 0 on the normal branch 0 <= mu <= a (z3 unsat). The bound therefore survives in full GR. It fails only for mu > 2a, on the far sheet.
NOT STATED BUT EQUIVALENT: r_c <= a holds exactly when m_MS(a) = M - Q^2/2a >= 0 (z3 unsat on the negation). This is the identity Bonnor-Cooperstock use in the opposite direction.

ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0).
(A) E2 with mu >= 0: the negation is unsat.
(B) overturn.py's wording (M > 0 only): sat, with witness mu=-1, M=1, r_c=2a.

later_literature.ref: arXiv:0710.5619 (Bhadra 2007, restating Bonnor-Cooperstock 1989, Cooperstock-Rosen 1989, Herrera-Varela 1994, Ponce de Leon 1988)
later_literature.what: A charged sphere with the electron's observed m, q and size bound must contain negative energy density. Its interior rest mass is about -1e-52 cm. This is the tree's identity read in reverse, and it refutes 'every charged body that exists' for the electron under the classical reading.
Lepton radius upper limits at 95% CL: electron 2.8e-19 m, muon 2.4e-19 m, tau 4.0e-19 m. This is the moved datum: the electron's r_c is 5000 times its bound.

The flat-interior Kerr-Newman electron source has its boundary exactly at r = e^2/2m (eq 5). This is the zero-bare-mass equality case derived at drivensource.py:157-160, and it sits in tension with the measured size bounds.

A classical electron at R = 1e-20 m: M = 28,234.7 + 42,351.3 - 70,585.5 MeV (eq 13). The part not due to the electromagnetic field is -42,351 MeV, so mu < 0 is how a classical electron smaller than r_c is built. Classical and QED results agree only for r >> R. The electron has MR << 1.
Nonlinear electrodynamics plus GR with WEC gives regular charged solitons with positive mass smaller than the classical radius. This drops the tree's linear-Maxwell hypothesis.

classical-charge-radius-inside-body.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis, tested on this result. The external physics did not lack data. The conditional statement (mu >= 0 implies r_c <= a, which is the same as m_MS(a) >= 0) re-derives exactly, now also in full GR. The data that matters is the pointlike electron. Its size bound was about 1e-18 m by 1983 and 2.8e-19 m by 2000, and Bonnor-Cooperstock 1989 used it to reach the opposite conclusion for the electron. The data gap is on the tree's side: it asserts 'every charged body that exists' with no table of bodies.

Evidence for the tree: every composite charged body checked satisfies the bound, by 2 to 11 orders of magnitude.

Evidence against: under the classical reading the electron (ratio 5032) and the muon (28) violate it. Better data has moved the electron ratio from 1.4e3 to 5.0e3, further from the tree.

Whether this reopens L2 is not decided here. The electron's region r < 1.41 fm lies inside its Compton wavelength (386 fm), where QED and mass renormalization apply, not a classical Reissner-Nordstrom picture. So 'EMPTY' may survive, but by a quantum argument the tree does not make.
classical-charge-radius-inside-body.grade_evidence:
The conditional statement stands and is strengthened here: E2 is reproduced in z3, the result is re-derived exactly in GR for a charged thin shell on the normal branch, and r_c <= a is shown to hold exactly when m_MS(a) >= 0.

The tree uses it more widely than it holds, in two ways:
(1) overturn.py:49 and :376 weaken mu >= 0 to 'mass M >= 0'. That version has a counterexample (z3 sat).
(2) overturn.py:51, :262 and :318 extend it to 'every charged body that exists' with no data behind it. The measured electron (ratio 5032) and muon (28) violate it under the classical Einstein-Maxwell reading that the derivation itself uses. This is Bonnor-Cooperstock 1989, reproduced numerically here.

It holds on a smaller class: classical charged bodies whose mass, excluding the electromagnetic field and including binding, is non-negative. That class includes every composite body checked but not the charged leptons.

Why not WRONG: the conditional theorem is sound, and the lepton counterexample depends on treating a quantum pointlike particle as a classical body whose 'radius' is its form-factor bound.
Why not DATA-DEPENDENT: no plausible move in the data flips either half.
Tau and W+ are OPEN.
classical-charge-radius-inside-body.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: if overturn.py's hypothesis were restated as mu >= 0 (equivalently m_MS(a) >= 0) and its scope limited to classical composite bodies, naming the leptons as out of scope. WRONG: if M ruled that leptons are classical 'charged bodies that exist' and accepted their LEP form-factor bound as the radius. The electron would then be a counterexample to the claim as worded. OPEN on the lepton half: if M ruled that a classical radius is undefined when MR << 1. That removes the counterexamples, but leaves the universal claim unproven for leptons.

0705.3704.name: Flambaum 2007 review: (R1) M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD -> the tree's H2, f = d ln m_p/d ln v = S; (R2) eq. (9) Th-229 nuclear-clock enhancement 1e5 (2 da/a + 0.5 dX_q/X_q - 5 dX_s/X_s)(7 eV/w)

source.located: V.V. Flambaum, 'Variation of fundamental constants: theory and observations', arXiv:0705.3704v2 [physics.atom-ph], 21 Jun 2007 (8 pp.). R1 is on p.4 (sec. V, the last paragraph before 'VI. Microwave clocks'). R2 is p.5 sec. VII, eq. (9), with the energy data on p.5 at refs [51]-[53]. The author attributes eq. (9) to his Ref. [38] = PRL 97, 092502 (2006) = arXiv:physics/0604188, which was not itself read here.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0705.3704, which returned all 8 pages of v2 verbatim.

0705.3704.published_statement: R1 (p.4): 'The proton mass is proportional to Lambda_QCD (M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD), therefore, the measurements of the variation of the electron-to-proton mass ratio mu = m_e/M_p is equivalent to the measurements of the variation of X_e = m_e/Lambda_QCD.' R2 (p.5): 'As it is shown in Ref. [38] there is an additional very important advantage. The relative effects of variation of alpha and m_q/Lambda_QCD are enhanced by 5 orders of magnitude. A rough estimate for the relative variation of the 229Th transition frequency is dw/w ~ 10^5 (2 da/a + 0.5 dX_q/X_q - 5 dX_s/X_s) (7 eV/w) (9) where X_q = m_q/Lambda_QCD, X_s = m_s/Lambda_QCD, m_q = (m_u+m_d)/2 and m_s is the strange quark mass.' Energy context (p.5): 'A very narrow level (3.5+-1) eV above the ground state exists in 229Th nucleus [51] (in [52] the energy is (5.5+-1) eV, in [53] the energy is (7.6+-0.5) eV).'
published_hypotheses: R1-H1 A chiral-limit proportionality: M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD, with the quark-mass contributions to M_p not written. It is used to set d mu/mu = d X_e/X_e exactly (p.4; also the context of p.5 eq. 8).

R1-H2 Only dimensionless ratios are measurable, and X_e, X_q, X_s are defined in units of Lambda_QCD (p.4). Flambaum-Wiringa 0807.4943 p.1 states the convention outright: 'convenient to assume that Lambda_QCD is constant'.
R1-H3 The paper nowhere says Lambda_QCD is fixed while the Higgs vev varies. Its sec. V GUT models vary Lambda (dLambda/Lambda ~ 34 dalpha/alpha, called 'model dependent').
R2-H1 Eq. (9) is 'a rough estimate' taken from Ref. [38], a first-order linear response.
R2-H2 In 2007 the transition energy w is uncertain (3.5+-1, 5.5+-1 or 7.6+-0.5 eV). Eq. (9) is normalised to 7 eV and scales as 1/w.
R2-H3 X_q (m_q = (m_u+m_d)/2) and X_s are treated as independent parameters.
R2-H4 Implicit in the alpha coefficient: the isomer and ground state differ in Coulomb energy by 2e5 x 7 eV = 1.4 MeV.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (R1): address.py:446 calls Flambaum p.4 'this project's H2', and address.py:104 defines H2 as 'Lambda_QCD ITSELF FIXED'. Flambaum states a proportionality and a units convention. He does not say Lambda is physically fixed while v varies, and his own sec. V models vary Lambda. So 'Lambda fixed as v varies' is the tree's premise resting on this citation. The tree names that premise and refuses to choose between H1 and H2 (address.py:331-334), so this is an attribution drift, not a hidden hypothesis.

ADDED (R1): address.py:505-509 and excite.py:164-165 add the Feynman-Hellmann light-quark fraction S. Flambaum's statement is the S -> 0 limit of it. Checked in sympy: with Lambda fixed, d ln m_p/d ln v = S exactly, and K_mu = S - 1 goes to -1 at S = 0, which is Flambaum's mu == X_e. This improves on the source; it does not weaken it.

DROPPED-DATUM (R1): the headline S = 0.06 in excite.py:164-165 and 1542-1543 is sigma_piN/m_p alone. Under H2 every quark mass is proportional to v, so the strange sigma term also enters S = sum_q sigma_q/m_p (address.py:505). The strange term is in the scan (S_SCAN 0.09, address.py:449-452) but not in the headline figure.

WEAKENED-DATUM (R2): address.py:763 and 776-785 evaluate eq. (9) at omega = 7.0 eV, which sets the (7 eV/w) factor to 1. The transition is now measured at 8.355733554 eV, a factor of 0.8377. The tree does not flag this anywhere in address.py or excite.py.

ADDED (R2): address.py:281-282 and 766-773 set d ln X_q/d ln v = d ln X_s/d ln v (7/9 under H1, 1 under H2), where Flambaum keeps X_q and X_s independent. The tree names this premise. Under it the two terms partly cancel (0.5 - 5 = -4.5), and the X_s term carries 91% of the coefficient.

ADDED (R2): address.py:776-785 put the tree's own K_alpha(H1) into Flambaum's alpha term. That term is only 1.06e-3 of the bracket, so the alpha coefficient, which later data contradict, does not move the tree's figure.

0705.3704.lacked_data:
In 2007 Flambaum had the Th-229m energy only from gamma-ray differences (3.5, 5.5 or 7.6 eV). He had no measured isomer quadrupole moment or charge-radius difference, and his coefficients came from one rough model estimate. Three data have arrived since: w measured at 8.355733554 eV (2024); a measured-input K_alpha = 5900(2300), backed by theory giving 1e3-1e4 (2024-26); and sigma-term values of 59.1 vs 43.7 MeV for sigma_piN and 28.6 MeV for sigma_s.

Evidence against, or limiting it: the author called eq. (9) 'a rough estimate' and carried a factor-2.2 uncertainty in w, so this is an estimate overtaken by data, not an established result shown false. The X_q and X_s coefficients, which carry the tree's figure, are still unmeasured. The X_q estimates scatter in both directions (Flambaum-Wiringa is 3.3x higher), and no later X_s computation was found. R1 is unmoved: it is exact in the chiral limit, and the quark-mass correction is the S the tree already adds.

0802.0658-sec5.2.1.name: Hu & Verdaguer: divergences do occur in the coincidence limit

source.located: arXiv:0802.0658v1 [gr-qc] 5 Feb 2008, B.L. Hu & E. Verdaguer, 'Stochastic Gravity: Theory and Applications' (Feb 2008 update of the 2003 Living Review; Living Rev. Rel. 11 (2008) 3). The result is in Sec. 5.2.1 'Finiteness of Noise Kernel', p.29-30, Eqs. (5.17)-(5.22). Context read: Sec. 3.2 p.10 (Eqs. 3.11-3.13), Sec. 5 intro p.24-25, Sec. 5.2 p.27-28 (Eqs. 5.9-5.13), Sec. 5.2.2 p.30-32 (Eqs. 5.26-5.32), p.80. The Sec. 5.2.1 text comes from Phillips & Hu gr-qc/0010019v2 (PRD 63, 104001 (2001)): Sec. III.A p.9-10, Sec. II p.6, Sec. V p.18.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0802.0658 (two calls) returned pp.1, 8, 10, 24-32, 80, 84, 88, 92 verbatim. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/0010019 returned pp.1-2, 5-6, 9-10, 13, 15-16, 18. The Sec. 5.2.1 paragraph of the review is word for word Phillips & Hu 2001 Sec. III.A.

0802.0658-sec5.2.1.published_statement: 0802.0658 Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'Since T_ab(x) defined at one point can be ill-behaved as it is generally divergent, one can question the soundness of these quantities. But as will be shown later, the noise kernel is finite for y != x. ... From this we see that all possible divergences for y != x will cancel. When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur. The above procedure will allow us to isolate the divergences and obtain a finite result.' p.25: N(x,y) 'is always finite for x != y (and off the light cone for massless theories)'. The review takes 'a more modest goal ... and leave[s] the discussion of point-wise limit to a later date'. Sec. 3.2 p.10: 'The noise kernel should be thought of as a distribution function, the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions.' The primary source, Phillips & Hu gr-qc/0010019, says on p.6 'Of course, without use of a regularized Green function, the y -> x limit is divergent', and on p.18 'The noise kernel ... diverges as the pair of points are brought together, representing the "standard" ultraviolet divergence'.
published_hypotheses: H1: a free (linear) scalar field with mass m and curvature coupling xi; stress tensor from Eqs. (5.9)/(5.10), p.27-28

H2: Wick's theorem for the 4-point function, 'for the case of free fields which we are considering' (p.30, Eq. 5.20), so the state is quasi-free (Gaussian). N is called the 'vacuum expectation value' of the bi-tensor (abstract; Phillips & Hu p.2)
H3: the physically acceptable states are Hadamard states (Sec. 3.1, p.8). The 'finite result' comes from modified point separation, which subtracts a Hadamard ansatz (Phillips & Hu Sec. IV)
H4: the pairs (x,x') and (y,y') each lie in a Riemann normal neighbourhood; for y -> x all four points lie in one (p.30)
H5: for massless theories, finiteness at x != y needs x and y off the light cone (p.25)
H6: the sentence 'divergences do occur' is asserted, not demonstrated. The review defers the pointwise limit (p.25) and computes no divergence coefficient
hypothesis_drift: No load-bearing hypothesis is dropped. noise.py:206-207 applies the sentence to the coincidence limit of the linear-field noise kernel. The file keeps H1 elsewhere: noise.py:202 says 'for a linear field', and noise.py:222-224 excludes nonminimal coupling and interacting fields ('H1 is essential').

A paraphrase, not a drift (noise.py:206): the tree says the Sec. 3.2 quote 'is about SEPARATED points'. Sec. 3.2 never says 'separated points'. It says the counterterms cancel and then qualifies: 'the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions' (p.10). The paraphrase agrees with that qualification and with p.25 ('finite for x != y').

Omitted context (noise.py:206-207): the tree does not carry the source's next sentence, 'The above procedure will allow us to isolate the divergences and obtain a finite result'. That finite coincident result comes from Hadamard subtraction (Phillips & Hu Sec. IV, Eq. 4.10), which regularises the pointwise kernel. Leaving it out does not tilt the tree's case: it supports the tree's narrowing. The tree's own finiteness route, worldline smearing (Fewster Sec. 3.3), is a different argument and stays NAMED (noise.py:207-211, 275).
Not carried, and harmless: H4 and H5. Both concern finiteness at separated points, not the coincidence divergence the tree cites.
Status word is accurate: noise.py:206 says 'H&V Sec. 5.2.1 say' and does not claim H&V demonstrated the divergence. noise.py:371 records 'page text, Secs. 3.2, 5.2.1', which matches what was read.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS, exit 0; output saved as rederive/0802.0658-sec5.2.1.out. C1: a c-number counterterm F*I cancels in t = T - <T>, which is the Sec. 3.2 mechanism. C2: H&V's explicit functional, Eqs. (5.26) and (5.29)-(5.32) at R=0, m=0 and general xi, was evaluated on the Minkowski-vacuum Wightman function. It matches an independent Wick-theorem calculation of the connected <T_ab(x)T_cd(y)> from Eq. (5.9) exactly on 8 components. The term N~_c'd' is not printed on the pages read, so it was taken as the x<->y mirror of (5.31). C3: C_0000 = 3(30 xi^2 - 10 xi + 1)/(2 pi^4 r^8) at equal-time separation r, with the same coefficient over tau^8 along a timelike worldline. The quadratic's discriminant is -20, so the coefficient is nonzero for every real xi: 3/(2 pi^4) at xi=0 and 1/(4 pi^4) at xi=1/6. The pointwise limit y -> x therefore diverges, and r^-8 is not locally integrable, so the kernel exists only as a distribution. C4: with the Wightman i*eps rule, the worldline-smeared integral equals (1/7!) int_0^oo w^7 |f^|^2 dw, checked to 1e-15. It stays finite as eps -> 0, giving 1/105 for Gaussian sampling with tau = 1. Without i*eps the cut-off integral grows as delta^-7. Scope: flat space, vacuum state, m = 0 only. The curved Hadamard case follows from the universal Hadamard singularity; that argument is NAMED, not run. One discrepancy is recorded, not an error: the review's Eq. (3.11) has N = (1/2)<{t,t}> and its Eq. (5.17) has N = (1/8)<{t,t}>, a factor of 4, yet Sec. 5.2.1 calls its N 'the noise kernel introduced in Eq. (3.11)'. Sec. 5 follows the Phillips & Hu convention (their Eq. 1.3), and C2 confirms Sec. 5 is consistent with itself.

IV obtains a regularised coincident kernel by Hadamard subtraction. Eq. (1.3) fixes the Sec. 5 normalisation. This paper is older than the review; it was read because the sentence comes from it.

later_literature.what: For the coincident <T T> of a free scalar in Hadamard states, a state-independent subtraction is 'no longer sufficient'. There is a state-dependent divergent cross term, 2 C_uv (phi phi)_ren (their Eq. 5), and they renormalise it with the Hollands-Wald OPE, with coefficients going as 1/|sigma|^(8-i). This confirms that divergences occur at coincidence. It sharpens the tree's narrowing: the pointwise variance needs OPE renormalisation. It says nothing against a finite worldline-smeared variance.

The tree's finiteness claim concerns a timelike worldline (noise.py:207-210), where C4 shows the flat-vacuum case is finite. The remark is a caution against extending the claim to hypersurface smearing, not a contradiction.

0802.0658-sec5.2.1.lacked_data: No measured datum enters this result; it is a structural fact about the short-distance singularity of a free field's two-point function. What the review lacked was not data but a demonstration: H&V assert the divergence and defer the pointwise limit (p.25). This audit computes it for the flat massless vacuum: the coefficient 3(30 xi^2 - 10 xi + 1)/(2 pi^4) is nonzero for every real xi. Later work renormalises the coincident product and finds the divergence too, with extra state-dependent pieces (Perez-Sudarsky 2025/26, via the Hollands-Wald OPE). The evidence therefore goes against M's hypothesis for this result: nothing learned since moves it, and later work sharpens it. The only defect found is notational, a factor-4 normalisation mismatch between the review's Sec. 3.2 and Sec. 5. It is recorded as a discrepancy, not an error, and it cannot decide whether a limit diverges.

(5.17); (b) the tree's 'SEPARATED points' paraphrases the source's 'only in the sense of distributions'; (c) the check covers only the flat massless vacuum, and the curved Hadamard case is NAMED, not run.

That cannot happen if the leading Hadamard term is universal, but that argument is NAMED here, not computed. The grade would also narrow if the tree extended the sentence to interacting or nonminimal fields. WRONG would need a finite pointwise coincidence limit for a free field, and C3 computes the opposite.

quant-ph/bennett-1993-teleportation.published_statement: As restated in 1505.07831, pp.1-2: 'an unknown quantum state of a physical system is measured and subsequently reconstructed or reassembled at a remote location (the physical constituents of the original system remain at the sending location). This process requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication. Most importantly, it requires the resource of quantum entanglement.' The protocol: Alice and Bob 'share two qubits, A and B, prepared in a pure entangled state. In the ideal case, this is taken to be maximally entangled ... Alice is given another qubit a whose state rho is unknown ... Bell detection, which projects her qubits a and A into one of the four Bell states (P_k x I)|Phi> ... Bob's qubit B is simultaneously projected onto P_k^dag rho P_k ... Alice communicates the classical outcome k ... Bob applies P_k to recover the original input state rho', with F = 1 in the ideal case. 'Alice's input state is assumed to be unknown, otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation.' For finite d: 'Pauli operators P_k replaced by U_k and the classical channel involves distinguishing d^2 signals.' quant-ph/9511027, p.1: 'an arbitrary unknown qubit can be faithfully transmitted via a pair of maximally-entangled qubits (e.g. two spin-1/2 particles in a pure singlet state) previously shared between sender and receiver, and a 2-bit classical message'.
published_hypotheses: P1: the state is UNKNOWN to the sender (1505.07831 p.2; quant-ph/9511027 p.1). For a known state the task reduces to remote state preparation.
P2: a maximally entangled pure pair is PREVIOUSLY SHARED between sender and receiver. The original used a singlet (per quant-ph/9511027 p.1); any Bell pair is equivalent (1505.07831 p.1).
P3: a complete, ideal Bell measurement that distinguishes all four Bell states (1505.07831 p.2, and p.4 requirement (3)).
P4: a classical channel carries the 2-bit outcome (log2 d^2 bits for a d-level system) to the receiver, who applies the conditional unitary.
P5: ideal, noiseless operations give fidelity 1. With noise the fidelity is below 1 and purification is needed (quant-ph/9511027).
P6: standard linear quantum mechanics with the Born rule. It is implicit in all three restatements and stated in none. 'Excludes superluminal communication' is a theorem inside it.
P7: finite-dimensional systems. The original treats a qubit; the source's own generalisation covers any finite d.
hypothesis_drift: RESOURCE STATE (harmless): transit.py:91-95 uses |Phi+> with corrections [I, X, Z, ZX] in the Bell order [Phi+, Psi+, Phi-, Psi-]. The original used the singlet |Psi-> (quant-ph/9511027 p.1). The two differ by a local unitary, and rederive C1 and C2 show both return psi exactly on all four outcomes. Not a narrowing.

IDEALITY (named, consistent): the tree's hypotheses 'ideal noiseless Bell pair' and 'ideal Bell-basis measurement' (transit.py:91-95) match P2, P3 and P5. The prose at transit.py:20-22, 192-195 and 280 says EXACT/PERFECT without the word 'ideal', and TRANSIT_IS_EXACT = True (transit.py:150) holds only under P3/P5. Through a Werner resource of singlet fraction F the fidelity is (2F+1)/3 (C6). Measured fidelities are 0.831 +- 0.009 (quant-ph/9710013 p.8), >= 0.83 at 143 km (1505.07831 Fig.2) and 0.80 +- 0.01 at up to 1400 km (1707.00934).

UNKNOWN STATE (consistent): H_tele (specthm.py:1188, 1206) carries P1. specthm.py:1212 says a KNOWN state can be re-prepared rather than teleported, which matches 1505.07831 p.2 on remote state preparation. No drift.

SCALE (covered by the source): the tree applies the result to the reconstruction specification (ledger.py:1357-1372, specthm.py:1170-1222), an object's state, while transit.py runs d = 2 only. The source's own finite-d generalisation (1505.07831 p.2) covers this: d^2 outcomes, 2 log2 d classical bits and log2 d ebits (C7, checked numerically at d = 3). CLASSICAL_BITS_PER_QUBIT = 2 (transit.py:140) is correctly per qubit. No drift.

ADDED, OVERSTATED (tree prose): 'NO WORLDLINE CROSSES ANYTHING' (transit.py:21-22, 192-195). The source says only that the physical constituents of the original system stay at the sending location (1505.07831 p.1) and that classical communication is required. Bob's half of the pair and the two classical bits do cross the distance at <= c. transit.py says so itself at lines 46-50 and 251-256 and records TRAVERSAL_IS_REMOVED = False at line 154. This is an internal inconsistency in the tree's wording, and the constant is the correct statement. A discrepancy, not a refutation.

ADDED, MIS-NAMED (tree prose): 'CONSERVATION LAW' (transit.py:24, 213, 221, 283). The fall in Alice|Bob entanglement from 1 ebit to 0 is computed true here (C4: the state after measurement is a product). The principle at work is LOCC non-increase of entanglement (quant-ph/9511027 p.4), not conservation: after the measurement Alice's own two qubits hold one ebit locally. The conclusion 'one pair, one transit' stands; only the name is imprecise.

ASSERTED, NOT COMPUTED (tree code): CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER = 0.0 (transit.py:139) and A's S = 1 bit (transit.py:230, 342, from entropy2 of a hard-coded I/2) are constants in transit.py, not computed from the state after measurement. Computed here (C4), both are true.

ADVANTAGE BY CONSTRUCTION (tree code): advantage_over_light(D) = arrival_time(D) - D/c, with arrival_time(D) = D/c (transit.py:145-146), so it is identically 0 (C9). The word 'provably' (transit.py:44, 249) is earned by the no-signalling computation (C3, C5, C8, and transit.py's own section 3) together with an assumption the tree leaves unnamed: classical signals travel at <= c (special relativity). A real channel arrives no earlier than D/c, so the true advantage is <= 0.
COUNT WORDING: 'twelve trials' (transit.py:21, 280) means 3 trials x 4 outcomes in report(). The selftest runs 5 x 4 = 20. Wording discrepancy only.
UNNAMED IN BOTH: P6 (linear QM with the Born rule). The tree's 'provably' holds within it. Under nonlinear modifications of QM, entanglement can signal (Gisin 1990, Polchinski 1991; NAMED-NOT-READ).
ATTRIBUTION: transit.py names the mechanism (lines 10-13, 276) but cites no paper for it.

quant-ph/bennett-1993-teleportation.lacked_data: The result is a finite-dimensional theorem of linear quantum mechanics and uses no measured input, so no moved datum can shift it. What the 1993 authors lacked was any experiment. The experiments that followed (Boschi 1997: 0.831; Ma 2012: >= 0.83 at 143 km; Ren 2017: 0.80 at up to 1400 km) confirm it at the fidelities noise models predict, (2F+1)/3 (C6). None shows signalling, and each needed the entangled half distributed in advance, which is the tree's own point that the corridor must be traversed. Only a failure of P6 (linear QM with the Born rule) could overturn the no-signalling part. The tree does not name P6, and nothing checked here tests it. The papers showing nonlinear-QM signalling (Gisin 1990, Polchinski 1991) are NAMED-NOT-READ. As far as can be checked here, M's hypothesis that earlier physicists lacked data does not change this result: the later data confirms it and does not contradict it.
quant-ph/bennett-1993-teleportation.grade_evidence:
The tree uses the result under the source's hypotheses: an unknown state, an ideal Bell pair, an ideal Bell measurement and 2 classical bits per qubit. These match the restatements (1505.07831 pp.1-2; quant-ph/9511027 p.1). A symbolic re-derivation for a general state confirms every point the tree relies on (C1-C8). No datum enters, and later experiments confirm the protocol. The rows that rest on it (R11, Rec, M-S1A-P5, D23) use the constants IT_IS_A_MOVE_NOT_A_COPY, CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE, CARRIES_SUBSTANCE = False, BEATS_LIGHT = False and TRAVERSAL_IS_REMOVED = False, and each is correct under the source. The discrepancies are recorded here, not repaired, and all of them are in the tree's own prose or code, not in the external result:
- 'NO WORLDLINE CROSSES ANYTHING' (transit.py:21-22, 192-195) contradicts the file's own lines 46-50 and 251-256 and the constant at line 154.
- 'CONSERVATION LAW' (lines 24, 213, 221, 283) should be LOCC monotonicity.
- CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER and A's entropy are hard-coded constants, though both compute true here.
- The advantage over light is 0 by construction (lines 145-146).
- 'Twelve trials' means 3 trials x 4 outcomes.
- Linear QM and the c limit on classical signals are not named.
None of these narrows the result as used.
quant-ph/bennett-1993-teleportation.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if a dependent row were read as claiming exact transfer without the ideality hypothesis (real fidelity is (2F+1)/3 < 1, measured at 0.80-0.83), or if the 'no worldline crosses' prose were cited as a finding in place of the TRAVERSAL_IS_REMVED = False constant. WRONG only if a failure of linear QM or of no-signalling were shown experimentally; none is known. OPEN covers only the exact wording of the 1993 PRL, which was not read here. Three independent restatements and the re-derivation agree on the protocol itself.

1802.08257-pms-luminosity.name: MacGregor et al. 2018 sec. 1: late M dwarfs have long pre-main-sequence phases with significant luminosity change

source.located: M. A. MacGregor, A. J. Weinberger, D. J. Wilner, A. F. Kowalski, S. R. Cranmer, 'Detection of a Millimeter Flare from Proxima Centauri', arXiv:1802.08257v1 [astro-ph.EP], 22 Feb 2018 (ApJL, accepted 2018 Feb 5); sec. 1 Introduction, p.1, paragraph 1, sentence 2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1802.08257 returned all 7 pages verbatim. The Proxima-specific size of the effect was READ in Ribas et al. 2016, arXiv:1608.06813v2 (Table 1, sec. 2, 4.1, 4.4), and Barnes et al., arXiv:1608.06919v2 (sec. 2, 3.1, 4.3). Hayashi 1981 is NAMED-NOT-READ: it is restated in Johnston et al. 2025, arXiv:2508.20291, sec. 1.

1802.08257-pms-luminosity.published_statement: 1802.08257 p.1 sec. 1: 'Late M-type stars, in particular, have long pre-main sequence phases during which the stellar luminosity can change significantly, as well as high stellar activity throughout their entire lifetimes (e.g., Hawley et al. 1997; Shkolnik et al. 2014; France et al. 2016).' The same page says 'Proxima Centauri (spectral type M5.5V)'. The sentence is introductory background. The paper computes nothing about pre-main-sequence luminosity; its results are the 1.3 mm flare and the reinterpretation of the dust belts.
published_hypotheses: The claim is about a class: 'Late M-type stars' in general. It does not name Proxima, a mass, an age or an evolutionary-track model.
The claim is qualitative: a 'long' PMS phase and a luminosity that 'can change significantly'. It gives no magnitude, no timescale and no direction.

The only support is an 'e.g.' citation string (Hawley 1997; Shkolnik 2014; France 2016), shared with the activity clause of the same sentence. None of the three is an evolutionary-track paper by title, so the PMS clause has no citation of its own.
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION (not dropped or weakened, but over-weighted): formation.py:275-277 quotes the sentence verbatim and correctly, and 'read at source' is true. The canonical entry's kind 'measurement' overstates it, though: in 1802.08257 it is background MacGregor et al. neither measured nor computed. The evidence that actually carries the Proxima claim is Ribas et al. 2016 and Barnes et al. 2016/2018, both READ here.

CLASS TO INSTANCE: the tree's hypothesis 'late M dwarf (Proxima Cen) evolutionary history' (formation.py:275-279) applies a class statement to one M5.5V star, which sits at the early edge of 'late M'. The step is supported: Barnes et al. call Proxima 'a late-type M dwarf host', and both Ribas 2016 sec. 1 and Barnes sec. 2 compute a large PMS luminosity decline for Proxima itself (PMS about 1 Gyr; the habitable zone reaches b after 169 +- 13 Myr).

Nothing the tree needs is missing from the source. The refusal at formation.py:277-279 needs only that the formation-epoch luminosity differed significantly from today's, which is what the sentence says. The tree adds no magnitude of its own.

DISCREPANCY inside the source, not load-bearing: the in-text 'Shkolnik et al. 2014' corresponds to the reference-list entry 'Shkolnik, E. L. & Barman, T. S. 2014, AJ 148, 64', which has two authors. This is a citation misprint, recorded here and not a refutation.
