rederivation.outcome: All asserts pass. (1) Ribas Table 1's R and Teff reproduce L = 0.00155 Lsun (ratio 1.0000). (2) S_now = L/a^2 = 0.659 S_earth, against 0.65 READ. (3) With the orbit fixed, the habitable-zone entry times READ at source give L(90 Myr) = 2.28 L_now and L(200 Myr) = 1.37 L_now. (4) Checked in sympy: at constant Teff, L scales as (R/R0)^2, and an irradiation-only snow line (proportional to L^(1/2)) scales as R/R0. (5) The Hayashi snow line at present L is 0.106 au. Using only READ numbers, the snow line was at least 0.160 au (1.51 times) even at 90 Myr. At disc epochs, a stellar radius of 0.3-1.2 Rsun gives 2.1 to 8.5 times; that radius range is read off a figure and is not a READ number. The evolutionary tracks themselves were not recomputed; their outputs are READ.

later_literature.what: For Proxima specifically: 'Proxima's luminosity changed considerably during its early evolution, after Proxima b had already formed.' The habitable zone swept inward, and b entered it at ~90 or ~200 Myr (Baraffe 2015 tracks at 0.123 Msun, interpolated; no interpolated mass matches R, L and Teff at the same time).

An independent track family (Yonsei-Yale, [Fe/H] = +0.3, 0.12 Msun) gives a PMS phase of about 1 Gyr and has the habitable zone reach b after 169 +- 13 Myr. The model's L was rescaled down by ~20% to match today, which lowers L at every age and so is conservative for the claim. The paper also says: 'ignored the high luminosities that late M dwarfs have during planet formation'.

later_literature.ref: Mulders et al. 2015 (ApJ 807, 9), as restated in Ribas et al. 2016 sec. 2
later_literature.what: 'Viscous heating is the main heat source for the inner parts of protoplanetary disks. The location of the snow line is therefore determined not by the star but by the disk.' So the stellar luminosity of any epoch does not fix the formation snow line on its own, which makes formation.py:273-274's demand for the formation-epoch disc T(a), P(a) stronger.

Low-mass PMS stars dim as they approach the main sequence, so the disc cools and its snow lines move inward. The paper restates Hayashi's a_ice = 2.7 (L/Lsun)^(1/2) au and notes that accretion luminosity can equal or exceed the photospheric luminosity early on. It models 1-2.4 Msun stars only, so it is used here for the mechanism and the scaling, not for Proxima's numbers.

1802.08257-pms-luminosity.lacked_data: In 2018 MacGregor et al. gave this sentence as background and had no data of their own on it. The inputs it rests on already existed: Baraffe 2015 tracks, and Proxima's L, R and Teff (used in Ribas 2016 and Barnes 2016). Three things were uncertain then and still are. Low-mass tracks cannot fit Proxima's R, L and Teff at the same time (Ribas 4.1; Barnes 3.1, a ~20% L offset put down to metallicity and unmodelled magnetic effects). The initial PMS radius is not known. Accretion luminosity during the disc phase is not included. On whether filling these gaps would change the conclusion: each one changes the size of the effect, not its sign. Two independent track families both give a PMS phase of about 1 Gyr and a habitable zone that sweeps past b at 90-200 Myr. Barnes's downward rescaling of L keeps the decline. Magnetic inflation would slow the contraction and lengthen the PMS phase, and accretion adds heat. Neither weakens the claim. The missing data would not change the conclusion the tree uses: the luminosity then differed significantly from today's. M's hypothesis is not borne out for this result.
1802.08257-pms-luminosity.grade_evidence: The statement was READ verbatim at 1802.08257 p.1 sec. 1, and formation.py:275-277 quotes it exactly. The tree uses it for Proxima, a late M star whose PMS luminosity differed significantly from today's, to refuse a snow-line radius computed from present luminosity. That use falls inside the source's class. Two independent track computations, both READ, confirm it for Proxima itself: from Ribas's entry times the luminosity at 90 Myr was at least 2.28 L_now (computed here), and Barnes gives a PMS phase of about 1 Gyr. The rederivation script passes, and no datum that has since moved changes the conclusion. Three things are recorded without changing the grade. (a) The canonical entry calls this a 'measurement', which overstates the source: MacGregor et al. give it as background with an 'e.g.' citation, so the evidence really lies in Ribas and Barnes. (b) The in-text 'Shkolnik et al.' does not match the two-author 'Shkolnik & Barman' in the reference list. (c) Later literature, Ribas citing Mulders 2015, says the viscously heated disc, not the star, sets the inner snow line. That strengthens the refusal.
1802.08257-pms-luminosity.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if a credible track family gave Proxima a short PMS phase, with its luminosity at disc epochs within tens of percent of today's; none is known here. DATA-DEPENDENT if a revised age, mass or metallicity for Proxima moved its habitable-zone entry before the disc dispersed (under ~10 Myr), which would remove the READ floor from step 3. OPEN only if the source sentence could not be read, and it was read.

covering-space-lift-flat-quotient.name: Closed curves in a free translation-lattice quotient lift to curves from p to p + V, V in L (covering-space lifting). With the reduction lemma this gives: a closed causal curve exists in R^{1,d}/L iff L contains a nonzero causal vector.

source.located: There is no single source paper. The lift is the path-lifting and deck-transformation property of covering maps (Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Prop. 1.30 and Prop. 1.40). Hatcher has no arXiv copy and is NAMED-NOT-READ. Its physics restatement for spacetime quotients was READ in two papers: Hubeny, Rangamani & Ross, arXiv:hep-th/0307257v3 (2003), Sect. 2.2 and 5.2; and Greene, Kabat, Levin & Porrati (the GKLP of latticectc.py:23,35), arXiv:2208.09014v3, pp. 1-3. Also READ: arXiv:2206.13590v2 Sect. 2.1, for the covering-space image picture, and Minguzzi arXiv:1709.06494v4 Def. 2.13 and 2.23, for the definitions of causal and stably causal.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-th/0307257, 2208.09014, 2206.13590 and 1709.06494, each returning page text. The lemma is read only as HRR and GKLP apply it. HRR Sect. 5.2: 'we will identify some point q ... with the point p. But q is in the future of p ... thus giving us a CTC'. HRR Sect. 2.2: a time function on M/G pulls back to a G-invariant one. GKLP p. 3: 'In the covering space, image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones.'

covering-space-lift-flat-quotient.published_statement:
Topology (Hatcher Prop. 1.30, NAMED-NOT-READ, restated in the papers read): every path lifts uniquely through a covering map once its initial point is fixed. For X = X~/G under a properly discontinuous action, a loop at [x] lifts to a path from x to g x with g in G, and G = pi_1(X) when X~ is simply connected.

HRR hep-th/0307257 Sect. 5.2: identifying p with a point q in its future gives a CTC. HRR Sect. 2.2: 'M/G is itself stably causal iff there exists a time function tau on M such that L_xi tau = 0'.

GKLP 2208.09014 p. 3: no CTC arises because identified image points are mutually outside each other's light cones.

The tree's combined form, latticectc.py:25-26: '(a) A closed causal curve exists in the quotient IFF L contains a nonzero causal vector.'
published_hypotheses: Covering-space action: the group acts properly discontinuously. For translations of R^{1,d} this is the same as L being a discrete subgroup; acting freely is not sufficient.
Paths are continuous, and the lift is unique once its initial point is fixed.
The covering space is simply connected, so that the deck group equals pi_1. R^{1,d} is simply connected.
HRR Sect. 2.2: M is stably causal and G is generated by a Killing vector. The pull-back proof does not use that restriction.
HRR Sect. 5.2: the identified point q lies in I+(p). This is a sufficient condition, stated for the plane wave.

GKLP: flat M^4 x S^1 with one spatial identification (rank 1). The argument on p. 3 is offered as a 'quick argument'; the detailed no-CTC result (Sect. 4) is computed for round-trip signals on the brane.
hypothesis_drift: latticectc.py:21 and :112-118 read 'rank-n TRANSLATION lattice L acting freely'. This is a wording issue, not a narrowing. Every nonzero translation acts freely, so 'acting freely' adds nothing. The hypothesis the lift actually needs is that L is discrete, and only the word 'lattice' carries it. 2411.04268.published_statement: From FLAG 2024 Sec.10.4.4, as transcribed by the sibling audit's at-source read and by massform.py:1314-1350. Eq.(447): 'N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 : sigma_piN = 60.9(6.5) MeV'. Eq.(448): 'N_f = 2 + 1 : sigma_piN = 42.2(2.4) MeV'. Eq.(449): 'N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 : sigma_s = 41.0(8.8) MeV'. Eq.(450): 'N_f = 2 + 1 : sigma_s = 44.9(6.4) MeV'. p.273: 'there is now a 2.7 sigma difference between the N_f = 2 + 1 and N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 FLAG averages. This is unlikely to be due to the inclusion of charm quarks in the sea. The control of excited-state contributions remains an issue ... If this constraint is relaxed then a sigma term of around 42 MeV is obtained.' p.274: 'The N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 lattice average is in agreement with Hoferichter et al. [1035] ... while there is some tension, at the level of around three standard deviations, with the lattice average for N_f = 2 + 1.' p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses.' The definition is sigma_q = m_q <N|qbar q|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q (Feynman-Hellmann). On the charm term, p.275 gives sigma_c = 107(22) MeV from ETM 19.
published_hypotheses: sigma_q = m_q dM_N/dm_q is a first derivative (Feynman-Hellmann), taken at the physical point with the QCD coupling and scale held fixed (Eqs.431-433 and 446).

The isospin-symmetric limit is defined with the neutral pion (about 135 MeV). The Roy-Steiner value 59.1(3.5) MeV is in the charged-pion convention, and converting between the two shifts sigma_piN by 3.1(5) MeV.
The averages use only results that pass the FLAG quality criteria. The N_f = 2+1 error was inflated by about 10% because chi^2/dof = 1.23.
sigma_s(2+1+1) comes from a single study: MILC 12C's <N|ss|N> multiplied by the FLAG m_s average.
Control of excited states (N pi, N pi pi) 'remains an issue' and 'the averages may change'. FLAG does not attribute the 2.7 sigma split to charm in the sea.
'Shift in M_N due to nonzero quark masses' is the first-order reading of sigma. FLAG does not claim that sigma equals the finite difference M_N - M_N(m_q = 0).

newtonian-grav-binding.name: Gravitational binding of order G M/(R c^2) negligible at payload scale

source.located: There is no single paper behind this. The external content is Newton's law of gravitation and the Newtonian self-energy of a bound body, U = -k G M^2/R (k = 3/5 for a uniform ball; k = 3/(5-n) for a polytrope, from Chandrasekhar 1939, 'An Introduction to the Study of Stellar Structure', ch. IV), plus the value of G from CODATA. The CODATA 2022 paper is arXiv:2409.03787 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga).
source.via: All three alphaXiv tools (answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content, discover_papers) returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded' this session. The egress proxy refuses arxiv.org (curl CONNECT 403; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED). So the self-energy formula was not read at any source. It was RE-DERIVED here from Newton's law: sympy gives k = 3/5 and k = 3/4 exactly, and Lane-Emden numerics for n = 1.5 and n = 3 agree with 3/(5-n) to within 5e-3. The value of G was READ from the CODATA 2022 table shipped in scipy 1.17.1 (scipy.constants._codata, _current_codata = 'CODATA 2022'): G = 6.67430e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, u = 1.5e-15. That table is a machine copy of the NIST values, not the CODATA paper itself.

newtonian-grav-binding.published_statement: Textbook and Chandrasekhar form, restated here, NOT read at source, and re-derived: a self-gravitating body of mass M and radius R has gravitational potential energy U = -k G M^2/R, with k = 3/5 for uniform density and k = 3/(5-n) for a polytrope of index n < 5. Hence |U|/(M c^2) = k G M/(R c^2). The tree uses only the order-of-magnitude form G M/(R c^2) and leaves out k ('No shape factor is claimed', massform.py:2093).
published_hypotheses: HN1 Newtonian (weak-field) gravity. It holds when G M/(R c^2) << 1, and post-Newtonian corrections are O((G M/R c^2)^2).

HN2 A single self-gravitating body with a definite mass distribution. k depends on the density profile: 3/5 uniform, 3/4 for n=1, 6/7 for n=1.5, 3/2 for n=3, and it diverges as n -> 5 or as the mass concentrates to a point.
HN3 G = 6.67430(15)e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2. CODATA 2018 and CODATA 2022 give the same value.
HN4 R is the physical radius of the body, i.e. the scale over which its mass is spread.
hypothesis_drift: SUBSTITUTED R (weakens HN4). The R used is R_BEKENSTEIN_M = 1.0 m, the radius H-R sets for the Bekenstein comparison (massform.py:2010 and 2094; H-R is defined at massform.py:830-831). It is not the physical size of a 70 kg body. At water density a 70 kg body is a ball of radius 0.256 m, giving |U|/Mc^2 = 1.22e-25 (2.35 times the tree's figure), or a cylinder 1.75 m tall and 0.113 m in radius, giving 8.2e-26 (1.57 times, by Monte Carlo). The worst case under a density cap, a ball at osmium density, gives 3.45e-25 (6.6 times). So the printed 5.2e-26 under-states the realistic ratio by a factor of 1.6 to 6.6. The order of magnitude holds and 'negligible' is unaffected. This is recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation.
k DROPPED, and the tree says so openly: 'No shape factor is claimed' (massform.py:2093) and 'of order' (massform.py:494). That is honest as written, and the tree does not claim an exact figure.

The SCOPE qualifier carries weight and is present: 'negligible at payload scale' (massform.py:496; H-AME at massform.py:827-829; D28 at massform.py:2880-2881). The same ratio is 2.1e-6 for the Sun and 0.17 for a 1.4 Msun neutron star of radius 12 km. At that compactness gravitational binding does make matter lighter per baryon than 56Fe, so H-AME is false beyond payload scale, and the tree does not use it there. No drift.

H-AME's literal wording, 'no bound state carries baryon number more cheaply' (massform.py:493), is false on its own for every self-gravitating lump, which is lighter per baryon by |U|/B. The tree names the exception in the same sentence ('Gravitational binding could, but ...', massform.py:494) and folds it into H-AME at massform.py:827-829. It is named, not dropped.

NOT ADDRESSED, a hypothesis the tree does not state: the mutual gravitational binding between the payload and the B units of antibaryon number that are 'held apart' at separation d. It is of order G M^2/d, so at most 5.2e-26 Mc^2 for d >= 1 m. It grows without bound as d -> 0, but then the antimatter is not held apart. This is not drift in the claim as worded; it is a gap in scope.

clamped-beam-eigenproblem.name: Clamped-beam (Euler-Bernoulli) fundamental: g'''' = mu^4 g, clamped ends, cos(mu) cosh(mu) = 1, INT (g'')^2 = mu_1^4 INT g^2

source.located: Classic: the clamped-clamped Euler-Bernoulli beam frequency equation cos(mu)cosh(mu) = 1 (Rayleigh, Theory of Sound, 1877). There is no arXiv copy, so the classic is NAMED-NOT-READ. The form the tree relies on is restated in C.J. Fewster, 'Lectures on quantum energy inequalities', arXiv:1208.5399v1 (2012), pp.10-11, Eqs. (3)-(4) and footnote 7. Its rigorous Sobolev backing is Fewster & Teo, gr-qc/9908073 (PRD 61, 084012, 2000), Thm 3.2, Lemma 3.1 and footnote 7.

clamped-beam-eigenproblem.published_statement: 1208.5399 p.10: 'INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' ... 'The bound is known not to be optimal.' ... 'it remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R)'. p.11: 'Suppose that <T00>_w < rho for some interval t in [t0, t0+tau] of time. Then, for any g in C0^oo((t0,t0+tau)) ... <g|g''''>/<g|g> >= -16pi^2 rho ... the left-hand side can be minimized over g, to give the minimum eigenvalue of the operator d^4/dt^4 on [t0,t0+tau], with boundary conditions at each end corresponding to vanishing of the function and its first derivative. The upshot is that rho >= -C/tau^4, (4) where the numerical constant C ~ 3.17.' The classic content was not read and is derived here: the clamped eigenfunctions of d^4/dt^4 on [0,1] are g = cosh(mu t) - cos(mu t) - sigma(sinh(mu t) - sin(mu t)), with sigma = (cosh mu - cos mu)/(sinh mu - sin mu) and eigenvalue mu^4, where mu is a positive root of cos mu cosh mu = 1. The least root is mu_1 = 4.73004...
published_hypotheses: S1: the operator is d^4/dt^4 on a bounded interval (length tau, or [0,1] after scaling), in its self-adjoint clamped realisation, g = g' = 0 at both ends. Sources: 1208.5399 p.11; gr-qc/9908073 Thm 3.2, form domain W^{2,2}_0(I).

S2: the minimisation runs over g in C0^oo of the OPEN interval (p.11). The infimum is the least eigenvalue, and it is NOT attained in C0^oo, because the minimiser has g''(0) = 2 mu^2 != 0. Attaining it needs W^{2,2}_0: the p.10 remark, and gr-qc/9908073 Lemma 3.1 (C0^oo(I) is a form core).
S3: g is real-valued. Eq. (3) is written with g(t)^2, and the Parseval step uses the evenness of |ghat|^2 (2301.01698 eq. (1.4)).
S4: C is the optimal-sampler constant of an inequality that is itself 'known not to be optimal' (p.10). It is not a sharp QEI constant.
S5 (classic): the operator is the fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli one, with no shear or rotary-inertia terms. This is irrelevant here, because the tree uses the pure eigenproblem as mathematics.

weak-field-lens-focal-length.published_statement: Not read at source. The statement below is the textbook form, and it is what was re-derived here. A ray passing mass M at impact parameter b in the weak field is deflected toward the mass by alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b). Rays at impact parameter b from a source at infinity therefore cross the axis at f = b/alpha = b^2 c^2/(4GM). Because f grows with b, the lens has a focal line, not a focal point. For the Sun at b = R_sun the published focus is about 547.8 AU (Toth & Turyshev; search summary only).

reissner-nordstrom-repulsive-region.published_statement: Hamilton & Lisle, gr-qc/0411060v2, Sec II.B, p.5: 'the mass M(r) = M - Q^2/(2r) interior to r ... the mass M at infinity, less the mass ... Q^2/(2r) contained in the electric field ... r_+- = M +- (M^2 - Q^2)^{1/2} (21). The inflow velocity beta hits the speed of light at the outer horizon r_+, reaches a maximum velocity between the outer and inner horizons, slows back down to the speed of light at the inner horizon r_-, and slows all the way to zero velocity at the turnaround radius r_0 = Q^2/2M (22) ... The RN solution describes the geometry of empty space surrounding a classical point charge of infinitesimal size, and as such consists of a gravitationally repulsive singularity of infinite negative mass sheathed in an electric field containing an infinite positive mass.' Faraoni & Vachon 2006.10827v2: in the RN inner region, which has negative quasilocal mass, 'gravity becomes repulsive, a massive test particle with zero initial velocity cannot overcome this repulsion', and this happens 'in any region with negative Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass'. Khuri-Weinstein 1307.5499 Thm 2, restating GHHP83: Einstein-Maxwell initial data with a strongly asymptotically flat end that satisfy the charged DEC mu_0 >= |J| + |rho| (eq 2) have m >= |Q|. McCormick 1907.07967 p.14: 'Clearly we can write down initial data with very small mass density and very large charge density, and then one should not expect this inequality to hold'; the bound needs (3.16) R(g) - 2|E|^2 >= 4|div E|.
published_hypotheses: Reissner-Nordstrom electrovac: source-free Maxwell field on r > 0, static and spherically symmetric, geometric Gaussian units (Hamilton-Lisle Sec II.B)
the ordering r_0 = Q^2/2M < r_- <= r_+ presupposes real horizons, i.e. |Q| <= M (eq 21: 'a spherical black hole of mass M and charge Q')
r = 0 is a singular centre ('repulsive singularity of infinite negative mass'); r < r_0 is exactly where the Misner-Sharp interior mass is negative
'repulsive' means negative Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass (Faraoni-Vachon): an E = 1 radial observer cannot enter; this is exactly f > 1, i.e. Phi > 0

Q <= M (GHHP via KW13 / McCormick) needs complete Einstein-Maxwell data with a strongly asymptotically flat end AND the charged DEC mu_0 >= |J| + |rho| (matter energy density dominates charge density)
positivity for a horizonless body (Hayward Prop 6) needs the DEC, an untrapped hypersurface and a REGULAR centre; 'the energy can be negative if the above assumptions do not hold'

The bound holds only for data whose matter density dominates its charge density (KW13 eq 2, McCormick 3.16). Ordinary matter violates this (C9: 1 kg carrying 1 nC has Q/M = 11.6; the electron has 2.04e21), and so does a static Israel shell with positive rest mass and Q/M = 16.67 (C6). lyapunov-inequality.published_statement: NOT QUOTED (source not read). The standard modern form, as re-derived here: if u'' + q(t) u = 0 on [a,b] has a non-trivial solution with u(a) = u(b) = 0, then (b - a) * INT_a^b q+(t) dt > 4, where q+ = max(q,0). The constant 4 is best possible and is never attained. Lyapunov's own 1892 statement is commonly reported for continuous q (often q >= 0). The sign-indefinite q+ form and the refinement INT (t-a)(b-t) q+ > b - a are commonly credited to later authors (Wintner / Hartman, c. 1951). That credit is NOT verified here.
published_hypotheses: A scalar, linear, second-order ODE u'' + q u = 0 with one unknown function. This is the standard form; it was not read at source.

q is real-valued. The classical statement (as commonly reported) takes q continuous; the modern statement takes q in L^1, with Caratheodory solutions (u in C^1, u' absolutely continuous). The L^1, sign-indefinite case is re-derived here.
u is non-trivial with two zeros a < b. They need not be consecutive: the claim reduces to consecutive zeros inside [a,b], because shrinking the interval only lowers (b-a) INT q+.
The conclusion is strict (>), and the constant 4 is sharp but never attained. Re-derived here: a centred-slab family gives 5.92, 4.61, 4.17, 4.054, 4.0053, 4.00005, falling toward 4 from above.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED/WEAKENED, continuity to piecewise constant: seatindex.py:139-141. slab() is DISCONTINUOUS (q = m on [c,c+l], outside in {0,-5,-20} elsewhere), while the classical statement is commonly given for continuous q. This is not a defect. The L^1, sign-indefinite form is re-derived here: the proof steps symbolically in [1], and 600 random discontinuous mixed-sign profiles in [3], of which 493 seat, with 0 violations and a minimum b*INT q+ of 4.338.

lyapunov-inequality.lacked_data: Lyapunov's inequality is a theorem about a linear ODE and uses no measured datum. There is nothing measured it could have lacked, and no datum has moved: the constant 4 is exact, and it and its sharpness are re-derived here. What the APPLICATION was missing was a term, not data. The reduction u'' = -q u with q = 4 pi T_kk drops shear and Weyl, which is a modelling choice in transit.py and not an error of Lyapunov's. Putting the Weyl tidal data back changes the picture in two ways, and both are shown here. (a) The scalar bound no longer excludes seating: composite.py's vacuum seats have scalar numbers of 0.012 and 0.011, which the tree had already found and struck. (b) The matrix bound, with q replaced by lambda_max(T)+, remains necessary and is satisfied at those seats (5.07 and 4.87, both above 4). So 'Lyapunov does not cover Weyl' is true only of the scalar form. The evidence does not favour M either: nothing here shows the classical result to be inaccurate or wrong. Within its hypotheses it is exact, strict and sharp, and it holds on the tree's discontinuous, sign-indefinite potentials.
lyapunov-inequality.grade_evidence: Re-derived here, the theorem stands as mathematics. It is strict, its constant 4 is sharp and never attained, and it holds for L^1 sign-indefinite q, which includes the tree's discontinuous slabs. The tree's code applies it correctly and conservatively: it uses L in place of b-a, excludes on '<=' as a strict inequality requires, and none of its 12 exterior cells seats under either of two integrators. The grade is NARROWED because the result holds only for the SCALAR, Ricci-only equation, and Weyl focusing seats with q = 0: composite.py's actual seats have a scalar number of 0.011-0.012. The tree records this narrowing (seatindex.py:41-60 and :169-184), but the unqualified reading survives at seatindex.py:19-21, :70, :315 and :400-401, and at paper/CLAIMS.md:273 and :311. The source was not read (NAMED-NOT-READ), so the grade rests on re-derivation, not on a reading. It is not WRONG: there are 0 violations across 600 scalar and 300 matrix profiles, and the proof algebra checks symbolically. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no datum enters.
lyapunov-inequality.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the residual sites (seatindex.py:19-21, :70, :315, :400-401; CLAIMS.md:273, :311) carry the 'BY RICCI FOCUSING' qualifier, or the tree adopts the matrix form with lambda_max(T)+, which covers Weyl. That would also need a reading of Lyapunov 1892, or of an exact survey restatement, confirming the hypotheses. To WRONG: a non-trivial solution with two zeros and (b-a) INT q+ <= 4. The proof in [1] rules this out, and none turned up in 600 trials. A source reading that limits Lyapunov's own statement to continuous q >= 0 would change who is credited with the L^1 form, but not the grade, since that form is re-derived here.

gr-qc/9304008-eq2.16.published_statement: v1 p.4, verbatim from the text layer: '|Psi> = 1/sqrt(1+eps^2) (|0> + eps|2>), (2.15) where |0> is the vacuum state satisfying a|0> = 0, and |2> = (1/sqrt2)(a+)^2|0> is the two particle state. Here we take eps, the relative amplitude of the two states, to be real for simplicity. For this state, <:T_ab(x):> = <Psi|:T_ab(x):|Psi> = eps/(1+eps^2) { sqrt2 (T_ab[f_k,f_k] + T_ab[f*_k,f*_k]) + 2 eps (T_ab[f_k,f*_k] + T_ab[f*_k,f_k]) } = K_ab eps/(1+eps^2) (2 eps - sqrt2 cos(2 theta)). (2.16)'. The definitions it uses are (2.12)-(2.14): T[f,f] = -K e^{2i theta}, T[f*,f] = T[f,f*] = K, T[f*,f*] = -K e^{-2i theta}, with theta = k_r x^r and K_ab = (k_a k_b - 1/2 eta_ab k^2)/(2 omega L^3). p.6: 'From Eq.(2.16), it follows that the condition for the expectation value of energy density to be negative is cos(2 theta) > sqrt2 eps.'

gr-qc/9304008-eq2.16.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result. (2.16) is a closed-form Fock-space expectation value with no empirical input: no measured constant and no extrapolated datum. Kuo & Ford had everything the result needs in 1993 (the commutator, the box mode, the state), and both their middle line and their general formula (2.10) are exact (C3, C4). The discrepancy is an algebra or transcription slip between two consecutive printed lines of v1, a dropped overall 2, not a consequence of missing data. More data would change nothing. On whether the slip matters: it leaves the sign of rho and the condition cos2th > sqrt2 eps unchanged (z3 C6). It would halve rho and change any Delta built from it (C7). (3.8) follows from neither line (C8) and is a separate key. Whether PRD 47, 4510 carries the 2 is NAMED-NOT-READ.
gr-qc/9304008-eq2.16.grade_evidence: The tree uses two flags and a ratio, all scoped to v1: KF_216_MIDDLE_IS_EXACT = True, KF_216_FINAL_IS_EXACT = False, and final/exact = 1/2 (fluctuation.py:33-35, 139-140, 384-386). An independent derivation reproduces all three, both from exact Fock matrices and from KF's own (2.10) (C2-C4), and recovers (2.12)-(2.14) from (2.11) (C1). z3 shows the two printed lines agree only where rho = 0 (C5; vacuity guard SAT). The tree calls this a discrepancy ('A dropped 2'), not a refutation, against v1 only. That is the weight M's rule sets: a misprint is a discrepancy, not WRONG. KF's physical content in (2.16) is exact and unaffected: the sign is indefinite, the negativity comes from the cross term, and the condition is cos2th > sqrt2 eps (z3 C6). None of the hypotheses the tree drops moves the claim, and no datum exists that could. Three named residuals bound the grade without lowering it. (a) The v1 text layer is assumed faithful: the page image was not viewed, and this stage read a cached harvest because alphaXiv was over quota. (b) The journal version is unread. (c) The later-literature discover_papers call failed on quota, so no later restatement of the absolute coefficient was found; that absence is not a finding.
gr-qc/9304008-eq2.16.what_would_change_the_grade: Two things could change it, and nothing computable could, because the 1/2 is an identity. First, a v1 page image showing a leading '2' before K_ab in the final line would make the discrepancy a text-extraction artefact, and the grade would move to OPEN. Second, reading PRD 47, 4510 would only re-scope the finding: if the journal prints the 2, the slip is v1-only, as the tree already scopes it.

2007.14311.published_statement: Theorem 5.1 (v2 p.14), verbatim apart from extraction artefacts: 'Consider an Einstein static universe of radius a > 0, a cosmological constant Lambda in R and a free scalar quantum field of mass m >= 0 and scalar curvature coupling xi in R such that c := m^2 a^2 + 6 xi - 1 > -1. Fix renormalisation constants alpha_1..alpha_5, beta_1..beta_3 in R and define Y_1 (93), Y_2 (94) ... in terms of R = 6/a^2 and the numbers defined in (131), (133), (86), (87) and (90). Then the set S_qf of symmetric quasi-free states omega that solve the semi-classical Einstein equation (1) is in bijective correspondence with sequences {a_n}_{n>=0} subset R_{>=0} such that m^2 sum a_n = Y_1 (95), sum a_n l_n^2/a^2 = Y_2 (96), where the correspondence is given by Theorem 3.1.' Corollary 5.2 covers S, the set of all solutions with a symmetric two-point distribution, quasi-free or not: (1) S contains the ground state iff Y_1 = Y_2 = 0; (2) for m = 0, S is nonempty iff Y_2 >= Y_1 = 0; (3) for m > 0, S is nonempty iff Y_1 = Y_2 = 0 or m^2 Y_2 >= (m^2 + xi R) Y_1 > 0; (4) more than one solution implies infinitely many; (5) S is a singleton iff it contains the ground state. Intro: 'ultra-static spacetimes with maximally symmetric spatial slices ... spatially compact ... Evidence against 'lacked data': 2/3 and 4/5 are re-derived exactly from the anisotropic TOV equation (A3, A4), and wall.py's arithmetic on them is confirmed symbolically (D1-D6). What later work adds concerns the WIDER class: numerical Einstein-Vlasov thin shells reach 8/9 (Andreasson; Ames-Andreasson-Logg 2016/2019; restated in Dadhich 2025 p.7). That moves one auxiliary claim, wall.py:553, which becomes false for the general window since 8/9 > x* = 0.8437. It does not refute 2/3. Whether Le states 2/3 as a cluster bound or as an existence window cannot be settled here, because the source is unread.
einstein-vlasov-limit-2-3.grade_evidence: (1) Both numbers re-derive exactly as Einstein-CLUSTER bounds (sympy, 26/26 PASS): v < 1 on circular geodesics iff 2m/r < 2/3, and DEC holds iff 2m/r <= 4/5. There is no misprint, no arithmetic error and no moved datum; beta^2_crit(2/3), beta^2_crit(4/5) and x* = 0.8437418926 are all confirmed. (2) The tree calls 2/3 'the Einstein-Vlasov limit' (wall.py:29) and 'the Vlasov window' (wall.py:553), which drops the p_r = 0 / circular-orbit hypothesis. The general Einstein-Vlasov limit is 8/9 (Dadhich 2025 p.7, READ restatement of numerics), and wall.py's own counter-rotating thin shell runs to 8/9 (wall.py:83). On that class the check at wall.py:553 flips. (3) The finite-width window 4/5 is used as the realizability domain for a thin-shell stability criterion whose own windows, 8/9 and 24/25, both exceed x*. So 'strict stability available everywhere the wall is realizable' (wall.py:37-40 and 683; restatus.py:155) holds only under the named hypothesis that realizability means the finite-width window x < 4/5. It does not hold on the thin-shell class the criterion is computed for; wall.py:554 already records this for 24/25. Not WRONG: nothing refutes 2/3 or 4/5 for their own class, and 4/5 < x* stands. Caveat: Le arXiv:2606.22531 is NAMED-NOT-READ, so whether Le's own statement carries the narrower hypothesis is OPEN. The grade rests on computation plus the READ restatement, not on Le's text.
einstein-vlasov-limit-2-3.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: reading Le arXiv:2606.22531 and finding both (a) that his 2/3 is defined for a class the tree's wording legitimately covers, and (b) that he proves the thin-shell idealisation is realizable only where the finite-width wall is (x < 4/5). feynman-hellmann-sigma-term.published_statement: FLAG 2024 (2411.04268v3 p.260): 'The matrix elements of the scalar operator qq with flavour q give the rate of change in the nucleon mass due to nonzero values of the corresponding quark mass. This relationship is given by the Feynman-Hellmann theorem ... sigma_piN = m_ud <N|uu + dd|N> (431), sigma_s = m_s <N|ss|N> (432), sigma_c = m_c <N|cc|N> (433)'. p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses'. Eq.(446): sigma_piN = m_ud dM_N/dm_ud. Coc et al. 2007 (astro-ph/0610733v2 p.4): strange gives '~0.19 Delta m_s/m_s' and u, d give '~0.052 Delta m_q/m_q. This implies that Delta m_p/m_p ~ 0.76 Delta Lambda/Lambda + 0.24 (Delta h/h + Delta v/v) (11)'. Eq.(13): 'Lambda = mu (m_c m_b m_t/mu^3)^(2/27) exp(-2 pi/(9 alpha_s(mu))) for mu > m_t'. Eq.(14): Delta Lambda/Lambda = R Delta alpha/alpha + (2/27)(3 Delta v/v + Delta h_c/h_c + Delta h_b/h_b + Delta h_t/h_t). Hoferichter et al. 2015, eq.(24): 'sum_{q=u,...,t} f_q^N = 2/9 + 7/9 (f_u^N + f_d^N + f_s^N) = 0.305 +- 0.009'. Flambaum 2007 p.4: 'The proton mass is proportional to Lambda_QCD (M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD)'. Hill-Solon eq.(39): the heavy-quark matrix element is a series in alpha_s/pi whose O(alpha_s^0) term is (1/(3 beta_0))(2 - 2 lambda), where lambda is the sum of the light-quark scalar matrix elements. Hill-Solon p.15: 'poorly convergent alpha_s(m_c) expansion'.
published_hypotheses: FH-1: an isolated, non-degenerate eigenvalue of a Hermitian H(lambda) with a normalised eigenstate. The nucleon is the lowest state in its channel, so this holds (machine-checked here, check B).
FH-2 (FLAG eq.(446)): sigma_q is a first-order derivative at the physical point, m_q dM_N/dm_q, of renormalized operators. m_q qq is RG invariant, so sigma_q does not depend on the scheme.
HOM-1 (Coc eqs.(11)-(12)): QCD only. m_p depends on Lambda and the quark masses alone, and the mass dimension is repaired with powers of Lambda. QED and weak contributions to m_p are left out.

HOM-2 (implicit in any homogeneity statement; derived in check C): the quark masses held fixed while Lambda varies are RG-invariant masses. If m_q(mu0) is held fixed at a scale mu0 fixed in GeV, the coefficient becomes 1 - S(1 + gamma_m(mu0)).
HOM-3 (Coc eq.(11), Hoferichter eq.(24), Hill-Solon lambda): the light set is u, d, s, the flavours of the theory whose scale is Lambda_3. So S = (sigma_piN + sigma_s)/m_N.

H1-1 (Coc eqs.(13)-(14), Hoferichter eq.(24), SVZ via Hill-Solon eq.(39)): one-loop running with continuous leading-order matching at each heavy threshold; c, b and t treated in the heavy-quark limit; Standard Model coloured content between m_t and the high scale (Coc footnote 1).
H1-2 (Coc eq.(14)): m_Q = h_Q v at fixed Yukawa. The tree's H1 is Coc's case Delta alpha = 0, Delta h = 0.
H2 (Flambaum p.4): Lambda_QCD fixed and M_p proportional to it. Flambaum sets S -> 0; the tree keeps S.

feynman-hellmann-sigma-term.lacked_data: The identities themselves (Feynman-Hellmann, homogeneity, the full-theory Euler relation) lack no data: they are exact and no datum can move them (checks A, B, D). What the published numerical forms lacked: Coc et al. 2007 had no lattice sigma_s and used B_s = 1.5, giving S = 0.24. Today S_uds is 0.093-0.111, so their 0.76 becomes 0.89-0.91. That datum moved by a factor of 2.2-2.6, which supports M's hypothesis in its weak form. SVZ and the one-loop 2/9 lacked the O(alpha_s^1..3) decoupling coefficients and the Hill-Solon series; with them the H1 value rises 4.8% at S = 0.06. Evidence either way on the conclusion, computed with address.py's own functions: no quantity that rests on this result changes sign, and each moves by less than 5% (6.8% at the valence row). K_mu < 0 holds exactly for S < 1 at leading order, and beyond it whenever sum f_q < 1 (currently about 0.32-0.33). So the new data narrow the exactness of the H1 formula and move the published S, but refute nothing. The strong form of M's hypothesis is not supported for this result.
feynman-hellmann-sigma-term.grade_evidence: The core step is exact under its hypotheses and machine-checked (sympy A and B): Feynman-Hellmann plus homogeneity gives d ln m_p/d ln Lambda = 1 - S. It matches FLAG eqs.(431)-(433) and (446) and Coc 2007 eq.(11), both read at source. The tree's H1 and H2 forms, all its printed numbers and its own functions are reproduced (check D). The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree does not name three hypotheses. (1) 2/9 + 7S/9 is the leading-order evaluation of the exact sum_{u..t} f_q; beyond leading order f(0.06) is 0.28177, not 0.26889 (address.py:99-104 and 816-822 carry no LO qualifier). (2) The result is QCD only: the electromagnetic part of m_p is dropped at address.py:100. (3) Which quark mass is held fixed is unstated (check C), though the tree's use satisfies it. It is not WRONG: no counterexample exists. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT: the moved or contested inputs change numbers only. K_mu < 0 holds exactly for S < 1, |K_H2/K_H1| = 9/7, and no quantity resting on the result flips sign or moves more than 7%. Recorded as discrepancies, not repaired: '0.229' is a truncation, and S_MID omits sigma_s (see sibling sigma-term-scan).
feynman-hellmann-sigma-term.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree states the leading-order qualifier on 2/9 + 7S/9 (or carries the full sum_{u..t} f_q) and names the QCD-only and RG-invariant-mass hypotheses. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a conclusion that turned on S or on the beyond-LO shift; none does. To WRONG: a sum_{u..t} f_q >= 1 (which would flip the sign of K_mu), or a degenerate nucleon level that breaks Feynman-Hellmann; no source read shows either. OPEN does not apply, because every step is closed-form and checked here.

qnec-integrates-to-anec.published_statement: BFKLW 1509.02542 p.2 (as READ in the sibling audit): 'the right hand side can have any sign ... By integrating the QNEC along a null generator, we can obtain the ANEC, in situations where the boundary term S'_out vanishes at early and late times.' The QNEC, eq (2.2): <T_kk(p)> >= hbar/(2 pi sqrt(h(p))) delta^2 S_out/delta lambda(p)^2. This is the diagonal (delta-function) coefficient of the second functional derivative, at a point on a stationary null surface where the expansion and shear vanish. BFKW 1706.09432 eq (1.3) gives the integrated per-generator form: Q_-(A,B;y) = INT_{dA}^{dB} dx^- <T_--> - (1/2pi) dS(B)/dx^-(y) + (1/2pi) dS(A)/dx^-(y) >= 0, in flat space with locally stationary cuts.
published_hypotheses: H1: the boundary term S'_out vanishes at early AND late times. BFKLW state this as a CONDITION ('in situations where'), not as a consequence.
H2: the generator belongs to a stationary null surface of a FIXED background with no dynamical gravity (BFKLW p.4). BFKW work in flat space only; CF use Minkowski Rindler cuts.
H3: <T_kk> is the renormalised expectation value in a quantum STATE of a QFT in the proved class, and S_out is that state's entanglement entropy outside the cut.

H4: S''_out is the DIAGONAL coefficient of the second functional derivative. The per-generator integral that yields [S'] is BFKW eq (1.3), with S' the local first variation at the two cuts, not the FTC of an ordinary second derivative.
H5: an affine parameter along the generator, and locally stationary cuts (vanishing expansion and shear; BFKW K^+_ij = 0).
H6: CF additionally assume the state has finite averaged null energy.

qnec-integrates-to-anec.lacked_data: No empirical datum enters this step. It is FTC applied to a proved inequality plus a boundary condition on the state, and hbar/2pi is exact, so no physicist 'lacked data' that would move it, and none has moved. What BFKLW (2015) lacked was a general handle on the boundary term, hence 'in situations where'. Later work filled that from the other side: FLPW and HKT (2016) proved flat-space ANEC directly, and CF (2018) showed QNEC and ANEC are equivalent for Minkowski Rindler cuts. Later literature therefore CONFIRMS the conclusion in its class. The evidence the other way concerns the tree's use. R2 and R3 show the boundary condition carries the whole conclusion and is not implied by the inequalities, and the tree asserts it on a curved background with a classical T and no state. The tree's own anecscope.py:24-27 concedes curved-space ANEC is false in general. R4 shows the only escape route, [S'] != 0, would need a Planck-density entropy gradient (1.3-2.0 times S_BH per bubble radius), outside every fixed-background proof. More data would not change the step. A curved-space theorem or a computed state would change the tree's use.

sphaleron-instanton-and-collider-dispute.lacked_data:
The datum most plausibly missing is the Higgs mass. BLRRT (2003), the prevalent numerical result, used M_H = M_W (p.3, READ), nine years before m_H was measured. TW (2015), FFS (2016) and KM (2020) all postdate the measurement.

Evidence:
- Computed here: the measured m_H raises the barrier by 5.2 % (B from 1.8208 to 1.9163).
- BLRRT assert that their exponent depends 'very weakly' on m_H, but give no computation for it.
- Matchev-Verner 2025 (READ) say the physical m_H has 'important implications' for collider signatures, but do not quantify the collision exponent.
- No recomputation of the exponent at the physical m_H was read.

So whether this datum moves BLRRT's '30 sphaleron masses' is unknown, with no evidence either way beyond the 5 % shift. The other data were computed and do not move anything: alpha_W shifts the exponent by 2.7 of ~161 decades, and m_W shifts E_sph by 0.1 % or less.

Evidence against M's hypothesis being the operative issue: by every side's own words the dispute is limited by method, not data. BLRRT say 'not proven rigorously'; KM say 'no rigorous proof' and name an 'assumption'; FFS work at 'leading order of the WKB approximation'; TW17 speak of 'assumptions based on intuitions' and call their figure a 'guesstimate'. The one experimental datum (CMS, 0.021) lies above both sides' figures. No datum examined changes the tree's conclusion, which is CONTESTED with nothing refused on it.

schwarzschild-1916.name: Schwarzschild metric (static corner g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r) and PG witness)

source.located: K. Schwarzschild, Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin 1916, 189-196; English translation arXiv:physics/9905030 (Antoci & Loinger), pp.1-7. Lemaitre 1933 slicing and Painleve 1921 / Gullstrand 1922 NAMED-NOT-READ, restated in Hamilton & Lisle arXiv:gr-qc/0411060 eqs.(1)-(4),(7) and Lehmkuhl arXiv:2508.00034 p.5 fn.c, p.12, note 32
source.via: Schwarzschild 1916 READ in translation (physics/9905030 pp.1-7: conditions 1-4, eqs (4),(5),(9)-(14), Sec.5 uniqueness, Sec.6 numerics). The PG/Lemaitre slicing the tree actually evaluates is not in the 1916 paper: READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (gr-qc/0411060 eq.1; 2508.00034 note 32), and re-derived here directly (E6).

schwarzschild-1916.published_statement: physics/9905030 eq.(14): 'the line element that forms the exact solution of Einstein's problem: ds^2 = (1 - alpha/R)dt^2 - dR^2/(1 - alpha/R) - R^2(dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2), R = (r^3 + alpha^3)^(1/3). The latter contains only the constant alpha that depends on the value of the mass at the origin.' Sec.5: 'The uniqueness of the solution resulted spontaneously through the present calculation.' Sec.6: 'alpha/r is nearly equal to twice the square of the velocity of the planet'.
published_hypotheses: field equations (eq.4) hold 'everywhere, with the exception of the point x1 = x2 = x3 = 0' -- vacuum R_mn = 0, origin excluded
equation of the determinant |g_mn| = -1 (eq.5) -- unimodular coordinate condition, a gauge choice
condition 1: all components independent of time (static)
condition 2: g_rho4 = 0 exactly
condition 3: spherical symmetry
condition 4: asymptotic flatness, g -> diag(-1,-1,-1,+1)
Sec.3 item 4: continuity except at x1 = 0, fixing rho = alpha^3 (eq.13); the manifold is r in (0,inf) <=> R in (alpha,inf)
sign of alpha not derived: 'alpha depends on the value of the mass'; alpha > 0 enters only via the Newtonian identification alpha/r ~ 2v^2
hypothesis_drift: LABEL CONFLATION in the canonical entry, not in the owner: the entry calls 'the static corner g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r)' the Schwarzschild metric and lists 'vacuum' as its hypothesis. driven.py:182-183 calls it 'certify.py's metric', and certify.py:114-116 correctly writes it as the general static spherical form with m = m(r). E5 computes rho = m'/(4 pi r^2): it is Schwarzschild ONLY where m' = 0. The static corner rests on the Misner-Sharp definition (misner-sharp-1964-mass-function), not on Schwarzschild 1916, and 'vacuum' does not hold there in general.

V6 IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A CHECK OF THE METRIC (driven.py:182-183 'verified as a residual in V6'; driven.py:577-581): V6 defines m_s := (r/2)(1 - e^{-2Lambda}) and then tests e^{2Lambda} = 1/(1 - 2m_s/r). True as stated, but what it verifies is the inversion of the mass-function definition, not any property of Schwarzschild's solution. A discrepancy of description, not an error.

schwarzschild-1916.lacked_data: What Schwarzschild lacked in January 1916: (i) the knowledge that R = alpha is a coordinate singularity (Lemaitre 1933, Finkelstein 1958, via 2508.00034); (ii) the matter-sourced field equations he used a month later (2312.01865 Sec.9); (iii) any strong-field observation. Would having them change the conclusion? On the evidence here, no. The local metric is re-derived exactly from his own equations (E2) and from covariant R_mn = 0 (E1), with no numerical input. (i) enlarges the domain without altering the metric, and the tree checks the enlarged domain directly (E6). No datum enters the solution; the paper's only numbers are illustrative (E7). The one place later knowledge matters to the tree is the domain: driven.py's '|U| > 1 at every R < r_s' uses a region the 1916 paper excluded, and that claim rests on Lemaitre's extension and the tree's own computation, not on the 1916 paper. Observational tests of the exterior were not read at source here and are not claimed. They bear on whether nature realises the solution, not on whether it solves the equations, and solving the equations is all the tree uses.

frobenius-theorem-hypersurface-orthogona.name: Frobenius theorem: a unit timelike field with u_[a d_b u_c] = 0 is hypersurface orthogonal (the normal of a foliation)

source.located: Frobenius, 'Ueber das Pfaffsche Problem', J. Reine Angew. Math. 82 (1877) 230-315: pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Wald (1984) App. B Thms B.3.1/B.3.2: book, NAMED-NOT-READ. Read via restatement: (i) Yao, arXiv:2004.07288, Prop 1.1 pp.1-2 gives the classical theorem exactly: a smooth involutive subbundle has a LOCAL regular parametrisation near each p, and 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles'. Prop 1.11 p.4 is the Lipschitz version (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007). p.30 says a rank-1 distribution is automatically involutive. (ii) Ellis & van Elst, gr-qc/9812046, Sec 2.4 p.12: 'When the vorticity vanishes: The fluid flow is hypersurface-orthogonal, and there exists a cosmic time function t such that u_a = -g(x^b) nabla_a t'. (iii) Gourgoulhon, gr-qc/0703035, pp.23 and 44. (iv) Carroll, gr-qc/9712019, pp.78 and 164-165.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2004.07288, gr-qc/9812046, gr-qc/0703035 and gr-qc/9712019. No arXiv source was found that prints the twist form u_[a nabla_b u_c]=0 verbatim. Its equivalence with involutivity of ker u and with zero vorticity was machine-checked here (C4), not read.

frobenius-theorem-hypersurface-orthogona.published_statement: Yao arXiv:2004.07288 Prop 1.1 (restating Frobenius 1877): 'Let M be an n-dimensional smooth manifold and let V be a smooth subbundle of TM with rank r ... Suppose V is involutive. Then for any p in M there is a neighborhood Omega ... and a smooth regular parameterization Phi(u,v): Omega -> M such that Phi(0)=p, and ... dPhi/du^1..dPhi/du^r form a basis of V_Phi(u,v)'. It adds that 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles with C^1-regular parameterization'. Ellis-van Elst gr-qc/9812046 p.12: 'When the vorticity vanishes: 1. The fluid flow is hypersurface-orthogonal, and there exists a cosmic time function t such that u_a = -g(x^b) nabla_a t'. For V = ker u, with u a nowhere-zero 1-form: involutive <=> u^du = 0 <=> u_[a nabla_b u_c] = 0 (checked here, C2 and C4).
published_hypotheses: u (equivalently ker u) nowhere vanishing; automatic for a unit timelike field

REGULARITY: smooth (Frobenius 1877 as restated), or C^1 (the classical extension), or Lipschitz with a.e./set-valued involutivity (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007), or log-Lipschitz with distributional involutivity (Yao 2020 Thm 1.4)
LOCALITY: the conclusion holds on a neighbourhood of each point (u = f dtau there). A global time function whose level sets are the leaves is not asserted
C^{1,1} or smoother manifold; a torsion-free connection when the condition is written with nabla

frobenius-theorem-hypersurface-orthogona.lacked_data: Frobenius (1877, after Deahna 1840 and Clebsch 1866) is a theorem of differential topology. It has no numerical or measured input, so its authors could not have lacked data and no datum can have moved since. Later work (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007, Yao 2020, 2025-26) only extends it to weaker regularity and contradicts nothing. The one place the tree goes further than the source is a dropped regularity hypothesis ('w arbitrary'), shown by a counterexample here (C7), not a gap in data. That hypothesis does not reach any dependent. M's hypothesis therefore does not apply to this result: having all data now available leaves the conclusion as used unchanged.
frobenius-theorem-hypersurface-orthogona.grade_evidence: The theorem, as the dependents use it, stands. The twist was re-derived: V5's 0/64 reproduces, and the result holds for any (t,r) 1-form on any warped product. The twist form <=> zero vorticity <=> involutivity was machine-checked. The conclusion (dtau proportional to u', diagonal adapted chart) was built numerically on Schwarzschild with residuals of about 1e-9. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree's prose drops two of the source's hypotheses. (1) Regularity: 'For ANY rapidity field w(t,r)' (:105), 'w arbitrary' (:111) and 'EVERY SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD' (:113) fail for continuous non-Lipschitz w. C7 gives a spherically symmetric unit timelike u' that is the normal of no foliation, because three leaves pass through one point. The true class is C^1 or Lipschitz w. (2) Locality: :116-118 omits 'locally' (C8). Neither narrowing moves a dependent: ledger D2, specthm D2/K0/R1 and :144 need one smooth w per point and only a local foliation. This is a discrepancy of scope in the prose, not an error in the computation, which is itself C^1. Nothing was repaired.
frobenius-theorem-hypersurface-orthogona.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the sentences at foliation.py:105/:111/:113/:116 read as restricted to C^1 (or Lipschitz) w and to a neighbourhood of each point; the computation already assumes this. To WRONG: a C^1 spherically symmetric unit timelike field with nonzero twist, or one that is not locally a foliation normal. C2 rules both out, since the twist vanishes identically for every differentiable A(t,r)dt+B(t,r)dr. To OPEN: nothing; the result was checkable here and was checked.

1208.5399-sec5.1.published_statement: 1208.5399 Sec. 5.1 (p.44): 'The corresponding quantum theory was discussed in [29] for the case of Minkowski space. It was found that the nonminimally coupled field can sustain large negative energy densities for long periods of time. ... we may tensor together as many of these one-particle states as we wish, with respect to which the energy density is additive (as this is a free theory). Thus states of arbitrarily negative energy density can be sustained over arbitrarily large spacetime volumes.' p.45: 'However, there is a cost. The overall energy of these states is positive, and grows more rapidly than the scales characterising the negative energy density effect produced. ... one can establish QEI bounds for the nonminimally coupled field that are state-dependent [29].' Sec. 5.2 (p.45), first bullet: 'One cannot expect state-independent QEIs to hold; as mentioned, these can even fail in the nonminimally coupled theory. ... However, it is possible that modified QEIs hold.' The same section also says QEIs 'hold in a large class of conformal field theories in two dimensions'. PRIMARY, FO 0708.2450 p.8: 'to any bounded subset O of Minkowski space and arbitrary constant rho_0 > 0 there is a Hadamard state in which the expected energy density is less than -rho_0 throughout O. In particular any smearing rho_quant(f) with a non-negative compactly supported distribution f is unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states.' FO conclusion, p.20: '(at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space) the non-minimally coupled scalar field with xi > 0 admits states with arbitrarily large negative energy density over arbitrarily large bounded spacetime regions. Thus [it] cannot obey QEIs ... in which there is a state-independent lower bound.'
published_hypotheses: H1 free (not self-interacting) real scalar field. Tensor-product additivity of the energy density uses this ('as this is a free theory').
H2 coupling xi > 0 (FO Sec. 3). The sign enters through eq.(29), rho(0,0) = -xi(2 kappa)^4/(3 pi^2). 1208.5399 Sec. 5.1 does not state the sign.
H3 massless field (FO Sec. 3; conclusion 'at least for massless fields'). The scaling step, eq.(27), uses masslessness.
H4 four-dimensional Minkowski space ('for the case of Minkowski space'). Not proved on a curved background.
H5 Hadamard states, with energy density normal-ordered relative to the Minkowski vacuum.

H6 the quantity shown unbounded below is any smearing of the energy density against a non-negative compactly supported f. The state-dependent QEI (FO Thm 4.2/4.3) is proved for timelike geodesics and 0 < xi <= 1/4.
H7 energy cost: the witness states' total energy grows faster than the negative-energy scale (FO eq.(34)).

H8 (Sec. 5.2 clause) for interacting fields the source says 'one cannot expect' state-independent QEIs. This is an expectation, not a theorem, and is hedged by the 2D CFT counterexample and by 'modified QEIs' possibly holding.

1208.5399-sec5.1.lacked_data: The result is a free-field construction, not a fit to data. No measured input could have moved it. The 2007/2012 authors lacked later results, not data, and the two clauses the tree merges come out differently. (a) NMC clause: nothing later contradicts it. Fliss-Rolph 2025 restate it, and the construction re-derives exactly here. Its limits are the scope FO themselves print (massless, 4D Minkowski, xi > 0). The xi < 0 case is closed here by computation; the massive and curved-background cases remain OPEN. More data would not change it. (b) Interacting clause: in 2012 'not so much is known', and the author stated a hedged expectation. Later work filled that gap: the massive-Ising state-independent QEI (2013), which holds because interaction breaks the tensor additivity behind Sec. 5.1, and the transversely-integrated null QEIs for interacting CFTs (2025). So M's hypothesis holds in the narrow sense that the expectation, read as a blanket rule, is now too strong. It was never a theorem, and nothing later settles the generic 4D timelike case either way; it is OPEN, not reversed. Neither development helps a warp corridor. The NMC escape carries FO's energy cost, and the interacting-field QEIs that were found are bounds that hold, i.e. they constrain.

gr-qc/0209036.name: Fewster & Roman, Null energy conditions in quantum field theory (PRD 67 044003): no quantum inequalities along null geodesics in 4D Minkowski, and a timelike-worldline QNEI in globally hyperbolic spacetimes

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0209036v2 (dated Sept 10 2002, revised Nov 25 2002; arXiv stamp 26 Nov 2002), ESI 1205. Journal reference Phys. Rev. D 67, 044003 (2003), as cited by 2003.01815 ref.[101], 2111.05772 ref.[16], 2510.26247 ref.[47] and 2108.06068 ref.[28]. Each of these citations adds '[Erratum: Phys. Rev. D 80, 069903 (2009)]'.

gr-qc/0209036.published_statement:
Abstract (verbatim): 'For the quantised, massless, minimally coupled real scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski space, we show (by an explicit construction) that weighted averages of the null-contracted stress-energy tensor along null geodesics are unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states. Thus there are no quantum inequalities along null geodesics in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. This is in contrast to the case for two-dimensional flat spacetime, where such inequalities do exist. ... the renormalized expectation value of the stress energy tensor evaluated in these states satisfies the averaged null energy condition (as expected) ... However, we also show that in any globally hyperbolic spacetime the null-contracted stress energy averaged over a timelike worldline does satisfy a quantum inequality bound (for both massive and massless fields).'

Theorem II.1: '<rho(f)>_omega is unbounded from below as omega varies over the class of Hadamard states', where <rho(f)> = INT f(lambda) <:T_ab: l^a l^b>(lambda l) dlambda.

Theorem III.1 (globally hyperbolic spacetime, free Klein-Gordon field of mass m >= 0, Hadamard states, normal ordering relative to a Hadamard reference state omega_0, g smooth, real and compactly supported): INT <:T_ab: l^a l^b> g^2 dtau >= -INT_0^inf (dalpha/pi) Fhat(alpha,-alpha). In 4D Minkowski for a massless field this becomes -((v.l)^2/12 pi^2) INT g''^2 dtau (III.10), and for a Gaussian g it is -(v.l)^2/(64 pi^2 tau0^4) (III.13).
published_hypotheses: H1 field: quantised, FREE, massless, MINIMALLY COUPLED real scalar. For the massive case the paper says only 'our results generalise directly' / 'we expect this result to hold for massive fields as well', which is asserted, not proven.
H2 spacetime: four-dimensional MINKOWSKI. Curved spacetime gets only 'no reason to believe that a null worldline QNEI is any more likely to exist in curved spacetime', which is not proven.

H3 states: Hadamard. The counterexample family is the vacuum plus a multimode two-particle state, with momenta cut at Lambda0/alpha inside a cone of half-angle arccos(1-alpha) about l, and it converges to the vacuum in norm.

H4 sampling: f is smooth, nonnegative and compactly supported with INT f = 1, taken along an affinely parametrised null geodesic, so the average runs over a FINITE null segment. Lambda0 is chosen so that Re fhat >= 0 on [-2Lambda0, 2Lambda0], and 2nu+3/2 < sigma < 2nu+2.
H5 renormalisation: normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum.

H6 ANEC consistency: the paper shows its states obey ANEC in the lim-inf form (II.36) through a formal distributional limit ('may also be confirmed by a more careful analysis', which it does not give). It attributes ANEC to Klinkhammer (a dense set of Fock states) and to Wald-Yurtsever (a large subclass of Hadamard states), both in Minkowski.

H7 timelike QNEI (Thm III.1): globally hyperbolic spacetime, FREE minimally coupled Klein-Gordon field with m >= 0, Hadamard states, g smooth and compactly supported, and a bound that depends on the Hadamard reference state omega_0. The proof is only cited ('identical to' Fewster CQG 17 1897 (2000)).

H8 interacting fields: only a heuristic, the Buchholz-Verch/Woronowicz remark that in d > 2 no nontrivial observables are localised on a bounded null segment, which 'could provide a general argument'. It is not a theorem.

Known in 2002: QWEIs for free fields, the 2D null QEI, the FHR spatial no-go and ANEC for free fields in flat space. Not yet known: SNEC (2018), DSNEC (2021), ANEC for general QFTs in Minkowski (2016-17), the Fewster-Osterbrink nonminimal no-go (2007) and the QNEC proofs.

gr-qc/0209036.lacked_data:
This is a theorem with no empirical input, so no datum the authors lacked can have moved it; every step was re-derived. What they lacked in 2002 were later theorems, and those cut both ways.

For the result: the no-go now covers free scalars in every d > 2 (2108.06068). There is a general finite-segment argument beyond free fields (2510.26247). Kontou-Sanders 2020 restate it unchanged.

Against reading it broadly:
(i) The unboundedness needs arbitrarily high momenta. With a UV cutoff it becomes a finite, cutoff-dependent bound (SNEC). That is a choice of hypothesis, not a measurement.
(ii) Interacting CFTs admit state-independent QNEIs on transversely integrated finite null regions (2510.26247).
(iii) Thm III.1 fails for nonminimal coupling (Fewster-Osterbrink).

None of this refutes the paper as stated. (i)-(iii) limit how far the tree may carry it. The authors' own 2009 Erratum remains unread.

morris-thorne-1988-throat.published_statement:
As restated in Lobo 0710.4474:
- Metric (1): ds^2 = -e^{2Phi(r)} dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - b(r)/r) + r^2 dOmega^2, with Phi and b 'arbitrary functions'.
- The throat is the minimum r_0 of r, 'where b(r_0) = r_0'. Also: 'for the wormhole to be traversable it must have no horizons ... Phi(r) must be finite everywhere'.
- Flare-out (10): d^2r/dz^2 = (b - b'r)/(2b^2) > 0 at or near the throat, and 'at the throat ... b'(r_0) < 1'.
- Field equations (26)-(28): rho = b'/(8 pi r^2), and tau = -p_r = [b/r^3 - 2(1 - b/r)Phi'/r]/(8 pi).
- At the throat (29)-(31): rho(r_0) = b'(r_0)/(8 pi r_0^2); tau(r_0) = 1/(8 pi r_0^2); p(r_0) = (1 - b'(r_0))(1 + r_0 Phi'(r_0))/(16 pi r_0^2).
- (32)-(33): b = 2m, with m(r) = r_0/2 + int 4 pi rho r'^2 dr' (the 'effective mass').
- (39): with '(1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0 at the throat', flare-out gives tau_0 > rho_0 (exotic matter, NEC violated).
- (40): Phi = 0 is a 'specific class of particularly simple solutions' (e.g. the catenary b = r_0^2/r).
Hochberg-Visser eq (68) quotes the MT throat tension tau = 1/(8 pi G r_0^2).
published_hypotheses: General relativity, G_mu_nu = 8 pi T_mu_nu. MT print G and c; the restatement sets G = c = 1.
Static, spherically symmetric metric of form (1) with arbitrary Phi(r) and b(r). The stress-energy is read off from the metric; there is no matter model.
Throat: the minimum radius r_0, with b(r_0) = r_0. The proper radial distance l(r) is finite everywhere.
No horizon: Phi finite everywhere (traversability). At the throat, (1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0.
Flare-out: (b - b'r)/(2b^2) > 0 at or near the throat, i.e. b'(r_0) < 1 for a non-degenerate throat. MT's wording is 'at or near the throat'.
Asymptotic flatness, with two asymptotically flat regions. This is MT's global setting.
Phi' = 0 is NOT a general hypothesis. It is one special class of solutions (Lobo eq 40).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, and not needed: 'Phi' = 0 at the throat'. Sites: tolman.py:1439 docstring, tolman.py:1785 label 'V18a a throat has Phi' = 0', and the canonical hypothesis list. MT do not require it. Lobo eq (31) keeps Phi'(r_0) free, and eq (57) bounds it rather than setting it to zero. The re-derivation (R4a) finds 4 pi r^3 p_r + m = r(r - b)Phi' exactly. So at b(r_0) = r_0 the tree's V18 holds for ANY finite Phi'(r_0) (R4b, R4c). It holds even when Phi'(r_0) diverges with Phi finite (R4d). The tree therefore states its result on a smaller class than it actually holds on. As a sentence about MT throats in general, this is a discrepancy, not an error in V18.

DROPPED, harmless for the claim: flare-out b'(r_0) < 1. It is in the entry's name but not in its hypotheses, and V18/V18a never use it. Counter-check: at the equator of the Einstein static universe (Phi' = 0, b = (8 pi rho_0/3) r^3, b(r_e) = r_e), 4 pi r^3 p_r = -m holds and b'(r_e) = 3 > 1 (R6a-d). That surface is a maximal sphere, not a flare-out throat.

MISLABEL, a discrepancy and not WRONG: tolman.py:539-541 says 'THE FLARE-OUT CONDITION IS NOT THIS IDENTITY; IT IS THE SAME QUANTITY WITH THE OPPOSITE SIGN', and the tolman.py:2990 selftest says 'so the flare-out condition is NOT this identity'. The quantity 4 pi r_0^3 p_r = -m is the THROAT condition b(r_0) = r_0 read through G^r_r (Lobo eq 30 with m = b/2). MT's flare-out is the separate inequality b'(r_0) < 1, equivalently tau_0 > rho_0 (Lobo eqs 10, 39). The tree's conclusion, that m = +4 pi r^3 p_r cannot hold at a throat, is true (z3 Z1 returns unsat for any Phi'). Only the name 'flare-out' is attached to the wrong condition.

morris-thorne-1988-throat.lacked_data:
This result is neither a measurement nor an extrapolation from data. It is an identity of the Einstein tensor for ansatz (1): 8 pi p_r = -b/r^3 + 2(1 - b/r)Phi'/r, evaluated at b(r_0) = r_0.

The only constants involved are G and c, and the tree sets both to 1. Restoring SI moves the magnitude by at most 5.5e-4 fractionally across every G input in CODATA 2022. It moves no sign and no identity.

What came later is structural, not data. Hochberg-Visser 1997 generalised the throat to any static geometry and recovered MT's throat tension as a special case, without the normal redshift gradient. The anti-throat literature makes explicit that b = r without flare-out is a maximal sphere. Neither changes the conclusion. Both confirm that the tree's throat values hold on a larger class than the tree states.

Evidence against M's hypothesis here: there is no datum the authors could have lacked. Evidence for 'incomplete': MT's throat is defined only in the static, spherical, asymptotically flat class, and 'at or near the throat' leaves degenerate throats to later work. That is a scope limit, and the tree's use (static, spherical, local at r_0) stays inside it.
morris-thorne-1988-throat.grade_evidence:
The tree's statement is: at an MT throat, p_r(r_0) = -1/(8 pi r_0^2), m = r_0/2 > 0, and 4 pi r_0^3 p_r = -m, opposite in sign to m = 4 pi r^3 p_r. This agrees with MT as restated (Lobo eqs 30, 32-33; Hochberg-Visser eq 68). It is re-derived independently from the metric (sympy, 21/21 pass) and machine-checked (z3 Z1 unsat with guard Z2 sat; Z3 unsat). No datum enters it.

The hypothesis drift runs in the conservative direction. The tree adds Phi' = 0, which is not needed (R4a-d), so it claims less than is true.

Two wording discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and neither is a refutation:
1. tolman.py:1785 and :1439 say 'a throat has Phi' = 0'. That is inaccurate for MT throats in general (Lobo eqs 31, 57).
2. tolman.py:539-541 and :2990 call the throat relation 'the flare-out condition'. MT's flare-out is b'(r_0) < 1, equivalently tau_0 > rho_0. The ESU equator (R6) shows the identity holding where flare-out fails.

The dependent tree conclusions survive:
- The section-1 non-find (b) reason holds, and more directly: m(r_0) = r_0/2 > 0 at every throat (z3 Z3).
- The W4/section-2 withdrawal rests on the computed G^r_r, not on MT, so it is unaffected.
morris-thorne-1988-throat.what_would_change_the_grade:
NARROWED if a use in the tree needs flare-out or a true minimum of r rather than b(r_0) = r_0 alone. Also NARROWED if some other file treats 'Phi' = 0 at the throat' as a general property of MT wormholes and draws a conclusion from it, such as zero radial tidal force at every throat, which Lobo eq 57 contradicts.

WRONG only if someone exhibited an MT-form metric with b(r_0) = r_0, Phi finite and (1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0 at r_0, but p_r(r_0) != -1/(8 pi r_0^2). R4a's exact identity rules this out.

Reading MT 1988 at source would upgrade read_status to READ. It could change the grade only if MT's printed throat tension differed from the two independent restatements.

modified-gravity-effective-stress.name: In f(R), scalar-tensor, Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet and higher-curvature theories the field equations rearrange to G = 8 pi T^matter + T^effective

source.located: Primary: Sotiriou & Faraoni, 'f(R) theories of gravity', Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 451 (2010), arXiv:0805.1726v4. It gives the metric f(R) field equations in eq (6), the effective-stress rearrangement in eqs (10)-(12) with the text on p.6, the Palatini form in eq (28), the Brans-Dicke omega=0 form in eq (55) and the energy-condition caveat on p.17. Supporting sources, all read at source: Lobo & Oliveira arXiv:0909.5539 (PRD 80, 104012, 2009), eqs (2)-(21); Bronnikov, Skvortsova & Starobinsky arXiv:1005.3262 (2010), which restates Bronnikov-Starobinsky gr-qc/0612032 (JETP Lett. 85, 1, 2007), itself NAMED-NOT-READ; Glavan & Lin arXiv:1905.03601 p.1; Guerses, Sisman & Tekin arXiv:2004.03390 p.1-4; Capozziello, Lobo & Mimoso arXiv:1407.7293, eqs (26)-(33). The tree cites no source for this result, so the audit uses the canonical review statement.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0805.1726, 0909.5539, 1005.3262, 1905.03601, 2004.03390, 1407.7293 and 2609.18475. Page text was returned and is quoted.

modified-gravity-effective-stress.published_statement: Sotiriou-Faraoni 0805.1726 p.6: 'it is possible to write the field equations in the form of Einstein equations with an effective stress-energy tensor composed of curvature terms moved to the right hand side. This approach is questionable in principle ... but, in practice, it has been proved to be useful in scalar-tensor gravity.' Eq (10): G_mn = kappa T_mn/f'(R) + g_mn[f - R f']/(2f') + [nabla_m nabla_n f' - g_mn box f']/f'. Eq (11): G_mn = (kappa/f')(T_mn + T^(eff)_mn), with the text 'positivity of G_eff (equivalent to the requirement that the graviton is not a ghost) imposes that f'(R) > 0'. On eq (12): 'The effective energy density derived from it is not positive-definite and none of the energy conditions holds.' p.17: energy conditions on T^(eff) are 'not very meaningful'. Scalar-tensor eq (55): G = (kappa/phi)T - gV/(2phi) + (1/phi)(nabla nabla phi - g box phi). Palatini eq (28): the source 'includes derivatives of the stress-energy tensor'. EGB: 'In D = 4 the Gauss-Bonnet invariant is a total derivative ... vanishing identically in D = 4, but not in D >= 5' (1905.03601 p.1); 'for D = 4, the H_mn tensor vanishes identically' (2004.03390 p.1). Lobo-Oliveira abstract: 'the matter threading the wormhole satisfies the energy conditions, so that it is the effective stress-energy tensor containing higher order curvature derivatives that is responsible for the null energy condition violation.' Bronnikov-Skvortsova-Starobinsky abstract: 'in cases where a wormhole is obtained, the effective gravitational constant G_eff is negative in some region of space, i.e., the graviton becomes a ghost'. Their p.6, on Lobo-Oliveira eqs (25) and (31): 'F_R is negative over some range of R for matter satisfying the weak energy condition'.
published_hypotheses: METRIC f(R) (SF eq 5-6): matter is MINIMALLY coupled to g, so nabla T = 0 (SF p.5). With a curvature-matter coupling, nabla T != 0 (1407.7293 eq 32-33).
The rearranged matter coupling is kappa/f'(R), not kappa (SF eq 11). T_eff in eq (12) is built from f, R and derivatives of f' only in that 1/f' normalisation.
f'(R) > 0 is the non-ghost / positive-G_eff condition and f'' > 0 is the Dolgov-Kawasaki condition (SF p.6, p.16). The scalar-tensor equivalence needs f'' != 0 (SF p.12).
SCALAR-TENSOR: T_eff is built from the scalar phi and V(phi), with coupling kappa/phi (SF eq 55). The non-ghost conditions are f(Phi) > 0 and l(Phi) > 0 (1005.3262 eq 2).
PALATINI f(R): the effective source contains the matter trace and its derivatives (SF eq 28).

EINSTEIN-GAUSS-BONNET: H_mn != 0 only for D >= 5 and vanishes identically in D = 4. A 4D effect needs a scalar coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term (EsGB) or the alpha/(D-4) limit, and that limit is contested (2004.03390).
The rearrangement is an interpretation, not a physical source: 'questionable in principle' (SF p.6); energy conditions on T_eff are 'somewhat misleading' (1407.7293 p.5).

Negativity under normal matter as published (Lobo-Oliveira) assumes a static spherical metric, constant redshift Phi' = 0, an anisotropic fluid and specific shape functions. Its examples have F = f' < 0.

NO-GO (Bronnikov-Starobinsky, restated in 1005.3262): if matter respects the NEC, there are no static, twice-asymptotically-flat wormholes in scalar-tensor theory with f > 0 and l > 0 everywhere, nor in F(R) with F_R > 0 everywhere.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED (coupling), overturn.py:237. The tree writes G = 8 pi T^matter + T^effective. SF eqs (10)-(11) have kappa T/f'. The 8 pi form needs kappa(1/f'-1)T moved into T^effective, so T^effective then contains the matter tensor. Check A2 shows this exactly. overturn.py:239 'T^effective is built from curvature' is therefore false in the tree's own normalisation unless f' = 1. This is a discrepancy of presentation, not of existence: the rearrangement itself is an identity (check A).

DROPPED (scalar-tensor content), overturn.py:234-239. The tree says 'built from curvature'. SF eq (55) and 1407.7293 eq (47) build it from phi, its derivatives and V(phi). In Palatini f(R) (SF eq 28) it is built from the matter trace and its derivatives. Check A3 confirms eq (55) = eq (10).

DROPPED (dimension), overturn.py:234-235. The tree lists Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet without D >= 5. A 4D effect needs EsGB or the contested Glavan-Lin limit.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS, exit 0, about 15 s. (A) SF eq (6) is equivalent to eqs (10)-(12) identically on a general static spherical metric with arbitrary F(r) and f(r). (A2) In the 8 pi form, T_eff = kappa T(1/F - 1) + kappa T_eff^SF/F exactly. (A3) Eq (55) equals eq (10). (B) On exact rational curvature jets, H_mn = 0 exactly in D=4 on 3 random jets whose Gauss-Bonnet scalar is non-zero; H != 0 in D=5; trace H = -(D-4)/2 GB exactly. (C) Lobo eqs (14), (15) and (16)-(18) verified. On (16)-(18), H = 0 identically. (10)-(12) are invariant under rho -> rho - l, p -> p + l for any l(r), so (16)-(18) are fixed only by the trace eq (3) with f_R = F. ex.(31): F = -1, rho = r0^2/r^4 > 0, rho_eff + p_eff = -2r0^2/r^4 < 0, f = -R. ex.(25): F <= -1 and T = 0. (D) With Phi'=0, rho = f/2 - box F; on eq (16), rho = F rho_eff. (E) f = R - 2 Lambda gives effective density Lambda. Two source discrepancies are recorded, not treated as refutations. (1) Lobo eq (34) as extracted, at alpha = -1, gives df/dR = -5 where eq (31) requires -1; this is PDF extraction or a misprint. (2) For ex.(25), f from trace eq (3) (their eq 29, f = -RF) fails df/dR = F, with residuals 12.56, 0.685 and 0.0757 at r/r0 = 1.25, 2, 3. So their rho(16) is not the density of a metric-f(R) solution. Enforcing f = int F dR shifts rho (0.815 -> 2.278 at r = 1.25 r0) but leaves rho + p_r invariant. Neither discrepancy moves the tree's claim.

modified-gravity-effective-stress.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. For this result the evidence is that no missing data matters. The rearrangement is an exact identity (check A), and a negative effective term exists at the identity level (check E), so no datum the 2007-2010 authors lacked could change either. What came later was theorems and critiques that narrow the use, not data: the Bronnikov-Starobinsky no-ghost wormhole theorem, the 4D Gauss-Bonnet vanishing with its contested limit (2019-2020), and the minimal-coupling caveat (2015). Later observational bounds, such as the 2017 gravitational-wave speed mentioned in 1905.03601 p.3 and the solar-system f(R) bounds in SF sec V, limit the size of T_eff in the regimes they probe. They were not read numerically here and cannot move an identity. So the incompleteness M suspects is real, but it sits in the tree's restatement (8 pi coupling, 'built from curvature', EGB without D >= 5, no-ghost condition dropped), not in the published result.
modified-gravity-effective-stress.grade_evidence: The published result stands as published. The rearrangement G = (kappa/f')(T + T_eff) is an exact identity (check A). Its scalar-tensor form is SF eq (55) (check A3). An effective term can be negative: SF p.6, check E, and the re-derived Lobo-Oliveira construction (check C). The tree's use (overturn.py:234-241) holds on a smaller class than it states, for four reasons. (i) With coefficient 8 pi, T^effective contains kappa(1/f'-1)T^matter (check A2). For scalar-tensor theories it is built from phi, and for Palatini f(R) from the matter trace. (ii) EGB gives T^effective = 0 identically in D=4 (check B; 1905.03601 and 2004.03390 p.1). (iii) 'Any higher-curvature theory' needs minimal matter coupling (SF p.5; 1407.7293). (iv) The tree drops the f' > 0 no-ghost hypothesis. For the wormhole use it is load-bearing: 1005.3262 shows such wormholes need G_eff < 0 somewhere, and both published WEC-respecting f(R) examples have F < 0 (check C iii). In the Phi'=0 class on Lobo's eq (16), rho = F rho_eff (check D). The grade is not WRONG, because nothing refutes 'an effective term can be negative where matter is not'; check E is a ghost-free instance, though it is GR + Lambda. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no datum enters. The two Lobo-Oliveira discrepancies are recorded as discrepancies and do not move the grade.
modified-gravity-effective-stress.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates the result with coupling kappa/f' (or says T^effective includes the matter shift), names D >= 5 or a scalar-GB coupling for EGB, names minimal coupling, and names f' > 0 as a hypothesis that the L2 break must meet or explicitly waive. To WRONG: only an error in the identity itself; check A excludes that on the static spherical class, and a general-metric check would close it everywhere. The EGB sub-clause becomes OPEN if the tree means the Glavan-Lin 4D theory, which is contested. The no-ghost narrowing lifts if someone exhibits a ghost-free higher-curvature static configuration with NEC-respecting matter and a negative Misner-Sharp mass coming from T_eff. The Lambda < 0 example (check E) is ghost-free but is GR + Lambda, so it does not count.
