dlnlambdaqcd-dlnv-2-9.published_statement: Coc et al. 2007, eq. (13): 'Lambda = mu (m_c m_b m_t / mu^3)^(2/27) exp(-2 pi/(9 alpha_s(mu)))', 'for mu > m_t up to some unification scale in the standard model'. Eq. (14): 'Delta Lambda/Lambda = R Delta alpha/alpha + (2/27)(3 Delta v/v + Delta h_c/h_c + Delta h_b/h_b + Delta h_t/h_t)'. With Delta alpha = 0 (the tree's H1) and Delta h = 0 this gives d ln Lambda/d ln v = 3 x 2/27 = 2/9. Footnote 1: 'In supersymmetric models, additional thresholds related to squark and gluino masses would affect this relation.' Beyond LO, Hill-Solon eq. (39): <O'_Q>/m_N = (1/(3 beta_0^(nf))){2 - 2 lambda} + (alpha_s^(nf+1)(mu_Q)/pi)(1/(3 beta_0^(nf)))^2 {57/2 - 321 lambda/2 + 8 n_f} + O(alpha_s^2). Hill-Solon eq. (61): f_c = 0.083 - 0.103 lambda = 0.073(3) + O(alpha_s^4, 1/m_c), with a 'poorly convergent alpha_s(m_c) expansion'.
published_hypotheses: One-loop running with b_0(n_f) = 11 - 2n_f/3. The exp(-2 pi/(9 alpha_s)) form of eq. 13 is the one-loop solution.
alpha_s is continuous at each heavy-quark threshold mu = m_Q (leading-order decoupling).
mu > m_t up to some unification scale, with Standard-Model particle content in between. Footnote 1 says SUSY thresholds would change the relation.
Heavy-quark masses are m_Q = h_Q v, and each variation is split into Delta h and Delta v.
Delta alpha_s at the high scale is tied to Delta alpha through a GUT-dependent R (R = 36 is assumed). The h, v, Lambda relation is called 'quite robust'.
For the beyond-LO series (Hill-Solon): MSbar heavy-quark mass, mu_Q = m_Q, O(1/m_Q) power corrections neglected, QCD only.

dlnlambdaqcd-dlnv-2-9.lacked_data: Coc et al. did not use higher-order QCD. That was a choice, not missing data: the LO result needs no measured input, and the O(alpha_s^3) decoupling constants already existed in 1997. Three things came later: Hill-Solon's O(alpha_s^3) f_Q (2014), lattice charm sigma terms (±30%), and sigma-term values that are still contested. With them, the number changes by a computed few per cent: the heavy sum is 6.2% higher, f(H1) is 4.8% higher, |K_mu| is 1.8% lower and the H1 density is 4.6% lower. The conclusions resting on it do not change. K_mu stays O(1) and negative for every S (-0.755 to -0.679), D20, S6 and S7 are unmoved, and the shift is stable under every varied datum. sm-higgs-doublet-gauge-structure.published_statement: Maas 1712.04721 p.18-19 (sec. 3.2): 'Since the potential is, by construction, a function of gauge-invariant quantities only, so are the minima given by gauge-invariant conditions. I. e., phi^dagger phi = f^2 (35) ... In the standard model case (33), this condition takes the form X = v alpha, with v = f and alpha an arbitrary SU(2) matrix, since alpha^dagger alpha = 1. This also shows that the minimum is manifestly invariant under both, gauge transformations and custodial transformations.' p.19: 'In the standard-model case the Higgs field is in the fundamental representation of SU(2), and the only group-invariant from which an invariant potential could be built is phi^dagger phi.' p.2 (sec. 1.3): 'v, in contrast to the parameter f of the Lagrangian (3), is dependent on the gauge. In fact, it is possible to construct gauges ... in which <phi> = 0 always holds.' p.63 (sec. 4.7.1): 'The Higgs field transforms like phi -> g phi = exp(i alpha(y)) phi under a hypercharge gauge transformation.' Cohen et al. 2008.08597 p.11: H = (1/sqrt2)(phi1 + i phi2, phi3 + i phi4) <=> phi-vec = (v0 + h) n-vec (2.7); 'At zero-derivative order, there is only one O(4)-symmetric building block: |H|^2 = (1/2) phi.phi = (1/2)(v0 + h)^2 (2.8)'.
published_hypotheses: Higgs field in the fundamental (doublet) representation of SU(2)_L, with a U(1)_Y hypercharge phase exp(i alpha Y) (Maas eq. (31)-(33), p.63; Cohen et al. eq. (2.7))
a single Higgs doublet (Maas p.2 'the simplest case ... a complex doublet'; multi-doublet potentials with several minima on different orbits are treated separately, Maas p.18 and sec. 3.9)

the potential is a polynomial (renormalizable) function of gauge-invariant combinations only (Maas p.2, p.18 'For simplicity, only this polynomial case will be considered'); Cohen et al. work at zero-derivative order and assume custodial O(4) (footnote 3, p.4)
classical / tree level: 'the minima' are field configurations; at the quantum level the vev is gauge-dependent (Elitzur; Maas sec. 1.3, 3.6)
the transformation is a (global or local) gauge transformation acting on every charged field at once; a space-time-dependent element generates derivative terms (Maas eq. (31), minimal coupling)

sylvester-2x2-gram-signature.name: Signature of the induced form on a 2-plane from its Gram determinant (Sylvester's criterion / law of inertia / binary quadratic forms), as used in latticectc.py (c) for D21

source.located: Classic sources: Sylvester 1852 (law of inertia and the leading-minor criterion) and the discriminant of binary quadratic forms (Lagrange/Gauss). None has an arXiv copy, so all are NAMED-NOT-READ. Read instead through two arXiv restatements. (1) Zhang & Ding, arXiv:2501.00894v1 [math.RA] (2025), p.2, Theorem 1: '(i) A symmetric matrix is PD if and only if all of its leading principal minors are positive. (ii) A symmetric matrix is PSD if and only if all of its principal minors are nonnegative.' The paper covers real matrices only, credits (ii) to Prussing (1986), and warns that the leading-minor test has been misapplied to the PSD case. (2) R. Lopez, arXiv:0810.3351v2 [math.DG]: pp.2-3 define a subspace as spacelike, timelike or lightlike when its induced metric is positive definite, of index 1, or degenerate. Prop 1.3 (p.3): a plane in E^3_1 is timelike iff it contains a timelike vector. p.39: 'W = EG - F^2. The surface is spacelike if W > 0 and it is timelike if W < 0'. The proof of Thm 1.1 (p.5) uses the discriminant of <u+lambda v, u+lambda v> = 0.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2501.00894 (pages 1-18) and on 0810.3351 (pages 1-5, 9, 11, 15, 22-23, 29, 31, 39, 51, 53). The Sylvester 1852 and Gauss/Lagrange originals are NAMED-NOT-READ.

sylvester-2x2-gram-signature.published_statement: Zhang-Ding 2501.00894, p.2, Thm 1(i): a real symmetric matrix is positive definite iff all its leading principal minors are positive. For the 2x2 matrix [[A,H],[H,C]] that means A > 0 and AC - H^2 > 0. Lopez 0810.3351, p.3 Prop 1.3 and p.39: in E^3_1 a vector plane is timelike (index 1) iff it contains a timelike vector. Its first fundamental form W = EG - F^2 is spacelike when W > 0, timelike when W < 0, and degenerate/lightlike when W = 0 (p.3, type (3)).
published_hypotheses: Sylvester (read via 2501.00894): the matrix is real and symmetric, and the inequalities are STRICT. The leading-minor test decides only positive definiteness; positive semidefiniteness needs all principal minors (Prussing 1986).
Lopez: the ambient space is E^3_1 (index 1, two spatial dimensions), and the object is a vector plane of dimension exactly 2.
Lopez: the causal character of a subspace is defined by its induced metric: positive definite, index 1, or degenerate.
hypothesis_drift: WIDENED dimension (latticectc.py:40-47, 126-127, 232). The source I read states the result in E^3_1, but the tree uses R^{1,d}: the witness is in R^{1,3} and the census is in R^{1,2}. The law of inertia covers the extension, and I re-derived it here. z3 finds no 2-plane with A<0 and AC-H^2>0 in R^{1,1}, R^{1,2} or R^{1,3}. The scalar z3 checks hold in every dimension. The signed Cauchy-Binet identity was checked symbolically for d = 1 to 4. By hand, for any d: a negative-definite 2-plane would have to meet the t=0 hyperplane, where the form is positive definite. The drift is harmless.

SCOPE of rank (latticectc.py:40, '(c) n >= 2: with Gram entries A, C, H'). The 2x2 Gram test is a statement about rank exactly 2. I built a rational rank-3 example in R^{1,3} in which all three 2-spans are spacelike, yet -3g1+2g2+2g3 has norm -242/9, so it is timelike. The leading minors of the full 3x3 Gram are 106/9, 1675/12 and -46591/36, so Sylvester applied to the full Gram catches it. No computation in the tree applies the 2x2 test at n >= 3 (every check is rank 2: latticectc.py:232-243, 381-393). LEDGER.md:44 (D21) states the rank >= 2 case in terms of 'the span', which is correct when the full Gram is used.

ADDED but not needed: 'exact rational Gram entries'. The rational point m/n exists for real entries too, because the interval between the roots is open and nonempty (checks A3 and A4). Exactness is a property of how the tree verifies the result, not a hypothesis of the theorem.

UNSTATED CONSEQUENCE of that rational hypothesis. If A and H are rational and H^2 = AC, then Q(-H,A) = A(AC-H^2) = 0, so a degenerate span always holds a null lattice vector. Example: g1=(0,1,0), g2=(1,1,1); then g2-g1=(1,0,1) is null, which by (a) gives a closed causal curve that is not timelike. The boundary example at latticectc.py:54-58 correctly needs an irrational s. As a result, 'exactly when the span is spacelike' at LEDGER.md:44 is exact except on the measure-zero set of degenerate spans. This is a discrepancy of phrasing, recorded and not repaired.
A>0 is redundant (latticectc.py:40, 196-197). In R^{1,d}, AC-H^2>0 already forces A>0 (check C1). In the timelike branch, A>0 only rules out the trivial case where g1 is itself causal.
The PSD pitfall named in 2501.00894 p.2 is not incurred. span_kind (latticectc.py:189-198) uses the strict test and puts det = 0 in its own 'degenerate' class.

source.located: arXiv:0802.0658v1 [gr-qc], 5 Feb 2008, B. L. Hu & E. Verdaguer, 'Stochastic Gravity: Theory and Applications' (Feb 2008 update of the 2003 Living Reviews review). Eqs. (3.11)-(3.13) are on p.10 (Sec. 3.2), (3.14)-(3.17) on pp.11-12, (4.11) on p.20 and (5.17) on p.29 (Sec. 5.2.1).

0802.0658-eq3.13.published_statement: From p.10, Sec. 3.2: 'N_abcd[g;x,y) = (1/2) <{t_ab[g;x), t_cd[g;y)}>, (3.11) ... t_ab = T_ab - <T_ab>. (3.12) ... The bi-tensor N_abcd is real and positive semi-definite, as a consequence of T^R_ab being self-adjoint. ... Let us now introduce a Gaussian stochastic tensor field xi_ab[g;x) defined by the following correlators: <xi_ab[g;x)>_s = 0, <xi_ab[g;x) xi_cd[g;y)>_s = N_abcd[g;x,y), (3.13) where <...>_s means statistical average. The symmetry and positive semi-definite property of the noise kernel guarantees that the stochastic field tensor xi_ab ... is well defined. Note that this stochastic tensor captures only partially the quantum nature of the fluctuations of the stress-energy operator since it assumes that cumulants of higher order are zero.' In the paper, xi then sources the Einstein-Langevin equation (3.14) for a linear perturbation h of a background that solves the semiclassical equation (3.7). Its purpose is set by (3.16)-(3.17): the stochastic two-point correlations of h equal the symmetrized quantum two-point correlations, to leading order in 1/N.
published_hypotheses: The spacetime (M, g_ab) is globally hyperbolic and four-dimensional (p.7).
The matter is a real FREE (linear) scalar field of mass m with curvature coupling xi, action (3.1): 'we just assume a scalar field for simplicity'.
N is defined in a general state |psi> with self-adjoint renormalized T^R_ab (Eq. 3.11). The vacuum is a special case; the abstract's 'vacuum expectation value' refers to that case.
N has no UV divergence at separated points for a linear field (p.10). The coincidence limit has meaning only as a distribution (pp.10, 12); Sec. 5.2.1 says divergences occur in that limit.
N is real, symmetric and positive semi-definite, which is what makes the field in (3.13) well defined.
The field is GAUSSIAN: all cumulants above second order are set to zero. This is the stated reason it 'captures only partially the quantum nature'.
The background g_ab solves the semiclassical Einstein equations (3.7), and xi lives on that background independently of h.
The theory works to linear order in the metric perturbation h (Eq. 3.14).
For N fields the correlator is 1/N times one field's noise kernel. The correspondence (3.17) holds to leading order in 1/N.

Scope of use: (3.13) is used only for two-point symmetrized correlations of h ((3.16)-(3.17)) and the Feynman-Vernon identity (4.11). The paper makes no claim about the one-point law or tail probabilities of T_ab.
hypothesis_drift: Not a drift, it matches: noise.py:133-134 says 'N = <{t,t}>/2 is the FULL connected variance'. That is Eq. (3.11) verbatim, and for a real sampler N(f,f) = <t(f)^2> = Var_psi[T(f)] exactly.

A normalisation discrepancy in the literature, recorded and not repaired, with no effect on the tree: the same source's Eq. (5.17) (p.29) writes 8N = <{t,t}>, and Bates 1305.3755 Eq. (4)/(7b) writes N = <{t,t}> with no 1/2. The tree follows (3.11) and in any case uses the variance directly (K_F from formula (V), checked against FFR 1204.3570 Table I).

The reason clause of the caveat is left out at noise.py:169-171: the tree quotes 'captures only partially the quantum nature' verbatim but not 'since it assumes that cumulants of higher order are zero'. This is not a drift in content, because the tree's H6/C1 split (noise.py:22-34, 162-171) states a stronger fact.

An added reading, which the tree discloses: noise.py:46-53 and 344-360 read the one-point law of the smeared xi_00 as the probability of a density outcome, erfc(z/sqrt2)/2. H&V make no one-point or tail claim. The tree labels this 'a different reading of distribution, NOT H6' and calls it a 'surrogate' (noise.py:46-48, 166-171, 293-296).

teleportation-two-classical-bits.name: Teleportation requires 2 classical bits per qubit; without them B is maximally mixed (Bennett, Brassard, Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres & Wootters, PRL 70, 1895 (1993); the lower bound as restated by Bennett et al. 2001 and proved for exact schemes by Werner 2001)

source.located: Primary: C.H. Bennett, G. Brassard, C. Crepeau, R. Jozsa, A. Peres, W.K. Wootters, 'Teleporting an unknown quantum state via dual classical and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen channels', Phys. Rev. Lett. 70, 1895 (1993). It predates quant-ph and has no arXiv copy, so the paper itself is NAMED-NOT-READ. Restatements READ at alphaXiv: (i) Pirandola, Eisert, Weedbrook, Furusawa, Braunstein, 'Advances in quantum teleportation', arXiv:1505.07831v1 pp.1-2 (the protocol and its hypotheses); (ii) Bennett, DiVincenzo, Shor, Smolin, Terhal, Wootters, 'Remote State Preparation', arXiv:quant-ph/0006044v5 (PRL 87, 077902 (2001)) p.1 (the statement that 2 bits are necessary); (iii) R.F. Werner, 'All teleportation and dense coding schemes', arXiv:quant-ph/0003070v1 (J. Phys. A 34, 7081 (2001)), Thm 1 and its corollary, pp.5-7 (the d^2 lower bound for exact schemes, proved).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1505.07831, quant-ph/0003070 and quant-ph/0006044; the page text they returned was read. Every statement attributed below to Bennett 1993 is quoted from these restatements, which cite it as their ref. [2]/[BB]/[1].

teleportation-two-classical-bits.published_statement: Protocol, from Pirandola et al. 2015 restating Bennett et al. 1993 (pp.1-2): Alice and Bob 'share two qubits, A and B, prepared in a pure entangled state. In the ideal case, this is taken to be maximally entangled ... Alice is given another qubit a whose state rho is unknown. She then performs ... Bell detection, which projects her qubits a and A into one of the four Bell states (P_k x I)|Phi> ... Bob's qubit B is simultaneously projected onto P_k^dag rho P_k. In the last (feed-forward) step ... Alice communicates the classical outcome k ... to Bob, who then applies P_k to recover the original input state rho. Note that Alice's input state is assumed to be unknown, otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation.' Also: 'This process requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication.' NECESSITY, from Bennett et al. 2001 (p.1): 'Two bits of forward classical communication and one ebit of entanglement ... per teleported qubit are both necessary and sufficient, and neither resource can be traded off against the other.' BOUND FOR EXACT SCHEMES, from Werner 2001 (pp.6-7): 'no teleportation ... scheme exists with n < d^2 ... a corollary of Theorem 1', where n is the number of classical signals and d the input dimension. Every tight scheme has a pure maximally entangled resource, unitary corrections and a complete von Neumann measurement.
published_hypotheses: H1: the sender does not know the input state (it is arbitrary, and may be part of a larger entangled system). Pirandola et al. 2015, p.2: 'otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation'.

H2: exact (F = 1) teleportation needs one pure, maximally entangled pair per qubit. A partially entangled pure two-qubit resource teleports perfectly 'if and only if' it is maximally entangled (2506.18577 p.2, citing Li-Li-Guo 2000).
H3: a complete Bell measurement with four outcomes. Incomplete Bell detection makes the protocol post-selected or probabilistic (Pirandola et al. 2015, p.4).

H4: 'Necessary 2 bits' has two meanings. For an exact single-shot scheme with a d x d resource, at least d^2 signals are needed (Werner Thm 1, tight case). As an asymptotic rate, 2 classical bits per qubit are needed however much entanglement is shared beforehand (quant-ph/0006044 p.1).

H5: classical communication runs forward only, over an ordinary channel. The theorem says only that classical communication is required. That the channel is limited to <= c comes from relativity, not from this theorem.
H6: linear quantum mechanics, in which local operations on a shared state cannot signal (the no-communication theorem).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (H1, input unknown to the sender) at transit.py:140 'CLASSICAL_BITS_PER_QUBIT = 2', with the selftest label 'classical bits required per qubit' at :335 and transit.py:37-39 and :209-210. The 2-bit requirement is proved only for an input the sender does not know. If the sender knows the state (remote state preparation, RSP), the asymptotic cost is 1 bit per qubit (quant-ph/0006044 p.1). For known equatorial states 1 bit is exactly enough (Pati 1999); rederivation N3 reproduces this with fidelity 1.000000000000000. The tree's 'object in transition' (transit.py:57-60) never says whether the sender knows its state. The count therefore narrows. The refusal built on it does not: RSP still needs at least 1 bit per qubit 'by causality', and without that bit B's averaged state is still I/2 (N3, deviation 5.6e-16).

DROPPED (H4, the derivation) at transit.py:140 and :335. The lower bound is hard-coded, and the selftest compares the constant with itself, which proves nothing. The number is still correct under H1-H3. N1 rederives it from a reference system R: I(R;B_out) <= I(R;B) + log2 k = log2 k, and exact teleportation needs I(R;B_out) = 2, so k >= 4. The standard protocol meets the bound exactly (I(R;BM) = H(M) = 2.000000000000). Werner 2001's corollary proves the same bound. The fault is in the evidence the tree gives for the number, not in the number.

NARROWED IN WORDING (H2), in the entry name 'without them B is maximally mixed' and transit.py:37 'EXACTLY I/2'. B is exactly I/2 only with a maximally entangled resource. With c0|00>+c1|11>, sympy check S2 gives diag(c0^2, c1^2). That is still independent of the input, so 'zero information' holds for every resource. The tree's own protocol uses a Bell pair (transit.py:89), so its instance is correct; only the general reading of the sentence goes too far.

OVERSTATED (interpretation) at transit.py:38-39, :209-210 and paper/CLAIMS.md:4620, 'The state does not exist at the far end until two classical bits arrive'. The theorem says B's state averaged over Alice's unknown outcome carries no information. On each individual outcome, B's qubit is in the state P_k^dag rho P_k (S1 confirms each branch is exactly sigma_m psi). Recorded as a difference of description, not of number.

IMPORTED (H5), correctly flagged by the canonical entry, at transit.py:38-39 and :138-141. The '<= c' comes from relativity. advantage_over_light(D) = arrival_time(D) - D/C_SI with arrival_time(D) = D/C_SI, so it is zero by definition (N4). The four '0.000' rows (transit.py:246-251, selftest :340-341) therefore restate the <= c assumption; they are not a measurement against light. index3.py:1366 rightly says the refusal is proved, but the proof is no-communication plus the <= c assumption, not the printed numbers.
FAITHFUL: b_state_without_bits (transit.py:129-136) computes exactly the quantity the theorem is about. S1 gives exactly I/2 for a symbolic input, so the 1.1e-16 at :37 is float rounding.
FAITHFUL: teleport() (transit.py:113-126) gives four outcomes at p = 1/4 each, and the Pauli corrections restore psi exactly, confirmed symbolically in S1.

S1 (sympy, exact, symbolic input): each outcome has p = 1/4, the Pauli corrections restore psi exactly, and rho_B with the bits withheld is exactly I/2, whatever the input. This inequality chain is a proof, not a numerical fit. later_literature.what: Perfect qubit teleportation through partially entangled two-qutrit channels. The classical message needs at least 2 bits (Shannon entropy), reaching 2 only when the channel reduces to a Bell pair. Consistent with 2 bits as the floor.

later_literature.ref: Sohail, A.K. Pati et al., 'Teleportation of quantum coherence', arXiv:2302.11499 (2023)
later_literature.what: One classical bit cannot perfectly teleport even the l1-coherence of an arbitrary unknown qubit. It works only for partially known states (equatorial or polar circles).

later_literature.ref: A.K. Pati, quant-ph/9907022; H.-K. Lo, quant-ph/9912009
later_literature.what: Remote state preparation for special ensembles, and Lo's conjecture. Used here only as restated in quant-ph/0006044; the equatorial protocol is reproduced in N3.

teleportation-two-classical-bits.lacked_data: Testing M's hypothesis that earlier physicists lacked data: Bennett et al. 1993 is a theorem of finite-dimensional quantum mechanics, and its conclusion depends on no measured quantity. The tree's only numbers are a float-rounding residual, an integer, and c, which is exact by definition. Three things came after 1993. (a) The optimality proof for exact schemes (Werner 2001) confirms 2 bits for an unknown input. (b) Remote state preparation (Pati 1999, Lo 1999, Bennett et al. 2001) lowers the cost to 1 bit per qubit when the sender knows the state. That is a real narrowing, discovered later. (c) Experiments with real-time feed-forward (reviewed in 1505.07831) report no arrival without the classical message. Weighing both directions: later knowledge changes the count for known inputs from 2 to 1, and changes nothing in the tree's refusal. The refusal needs only two things. First, no-signalling: B's averaged state does not depend on the input until the message arrives, which is rederived exactly here for every resource (S1, S2) and for RSP (N3). Second, the classical channel travelling at no more than c (H5, audited under the c entry). Changing the conclusion would take a violation of no-signalling in linear quantum mechanics. Nothing in the literature read here shows one, and none is presumed.
teleportation-two-classical-bits.grade_evidence: The theorem holds as stated, and the tree's instance reproduces exactly. S1 gives rho_B = I/2 identically for a symbolic input, so the tree's 1.1e-16 is rounding. There are four outcomes at p = 1/4 and fidelity 1 after correction. The 2 bits are rederived as a lower bound that the standard protocol meets exactly (N1), matching Werner 2001's n >= d^2. The narrowing has two parts. (1) The tree says '2 classical bits required per qubit' (transit.py:140, :335) without the hypothesis that the sender does not know the input. For known states, remote state preparation needs 1 bit per qubit asymptotically and exactly 1 for equatorial states (N3). (2) 'Exactly I/2' needs a maximally entangled resource (S2), although 'zero information' holds for any resource. Neither narrowing reaches the conclusion the tree rests on this result (advantage 0, and the consumers D23, R11, Rec): every protocol, RSP included, still needs at least 1 classical bit, and until it arrives B's state does not depend on the input. Three further discrepancies are recorded but not graded: the selftest's 2-bit check compares the constant with itself; the advantage over light is zero by definition; and 'the state does not exist at the far end' says more than the theorem does. The grade is not WRONG, because nothing refutes the source, and not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no measured quantity enters it.
teleportation-two-classical-bits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: transit.py:140/:335 names H1 ('for an input the sender does not know; a known state needs only 1 bit per qubit via RSP, still at least 1 by causality') and names the maximally-entangled condition for 'exactly I/2'. Showing that the tree's use case requires an unknown input would also do it. To WRONG: an exact scheme that teleports arbitrary unknown qubits with fewer than 4 classical signals, or a protocol in which B's state before the message depends on the input. To DATA-DEPENDENT: an experiment showing such input dependence. None is known in the literature read here. Reading PRL 70, 1895 itself would raise the read status but is not expected to change the grade.

1711.00578.published_statement: Abstract: 'a belt of dust orbiting around it at distances ranging between 1 and 4 au, approximately ... about 40 K ... The estimated total mass, including dust and bodies up to 50 km in size, is of the order of 0.01 Earth masses ... Our data also show a hint of warmer dust closer to the star. We also find signs of two additional features ... which still require further observations to be confirmed: an outer extremely cold (about 10 K) belt at about 30 au ... and a compact 1.3 mm source at ~1.2 arcsec'. Sec 3.2: the ACA source measures 340+/-60 uJy against a 74+/-4 uJy photosphere, with '~200 uJy of dust emission spread over a belt ... ~1.3-4 au'. The dust mass is (m_dust/M_E) = 0.5 (S/Jy)(T/K)^-1 (d/pc)^2 (nu/230 GHz)^-2 with kappa = 2 cm^2/g, and T_d = 278 L^0.25 r^-0.5, giving T_d ~ 40 K and m_d ~ 4e-6 M_E. 'The 1.3 mm continuum emission traces dust grains with um to cm sizes'. The size law has index -3.5 (Tanaka 1996), and 'if the primordial size distribution connects smoothly with the collisional cascade ... m_tot ~ m_dust (D_max/D_dust)^0.5 ... D_dust ~ 1 cm ... m_tot ~ 2200 m_dust (D_max/50 km)^0.5 ... m_tot ~ 1e-2 M_E'. Warm component: 'it might be possible' that ~30 uJy of dust sits at ~0.4 au, with T_d ~ 90 K, m_dust ~5.5e-7 and m_tot ~1e-3 M_E. Sec 3.3: 30 au belt, 1.7 mJy, 10 K, m_dust 1.4e-4 and m_tot 0.33 M_E, 'marginal'. Sec 1: Proxima b m_p sin i = 1.3 M_E at 0.05 au, cited from Anglada-Escude 2016.
published_hypotheses: H1: the ACA flux above the photosphere (~270 uJy) is steady thermal dust emission. The stellar term is the Ribas 2017 photospheric model (74 uJy) plus negligible non-thermal emission; all epochs are combined and no time-variability analysis is reported.
H2: the ~200 uJy the 12-m array misses is spread over more than ~7 beams, so it sits at radii ~1-3 arcsec (~1.3-4 au).
H3: the dust opacity is kappa_nu = 2 cm^2/g at 230 GHz (Beckwith 2000), the emission is optically thin, and the Rayleigh-Jeans form holds (implicit).
H4: T_d = 278 (L/Lsun)^0.25 (r/au)^-0.5 (Wyatt 2008), with L = 0.0015 Lsun (Ribas 2017) and d = 1.3 pc (van Leeuwen 2007).
H5: 1.3 mm continuum traces um-cm grains; D_dust ~ 1 cm.
H6: the collisional-cascade equilibrium size distribution has index -3.5 (Tanaka 1996).
H7: the primordial size distribution connects smoothly with the cascade (Wyatt & Dent 2002).
H8: the extrapolation runs to D_max ~ 50 km, with m_tot scaling as (D_max/50 km)^0.5.

H9: the authors state that their 'data are insufficient for a proper modeling', so the masses are rough estimates. The 0.4 au component is a 'hint'; the 30 au belt and the 1.2 arcsec source are 'marginal'.
H10: Proxima b m_p sin i = 1.3 M_E at 0.05 au is imported from Anglada-Escude 2016, not measured in this paper.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (formation.py:283-285, 443): the tree names only the -3.5 size law and the 50 km cap. It drops H3 (kappa = 2 cm^2/g, optically thin, Rayleigh-Jeans), H4 (the T_d law, L and d), H5's D_dust ~ 1 cm and H7 (the smooth connection). The ~0.01 M_E depends on all of these, not on the size law alone. The tree only reports the number and then withdraws it, so this is not an over-claim.

The paper uses 'marginal' only for the 30 au belt and the 1.2 arcsec source; for the warm dust it says 'hint' and 'might be possible'. MacGregor 2018 sec 4.2 paraphrases both as 'marginal detections'. This is a citation and wording discrepancy; there is no change of substance.

1711.00578.lacked_data: M's hypothesis is SUPPORTED for this result, with a qualification. Anglada et al. had the relevant data: all 13 ACA sessions at integration level. They combined all epochs and did not analyse them over time. They also lacked the knowledge that M dwarfs flare strongly at millimetre wavelengths. MacGregor 2018 reports the first mm flare from Proxima and notes that M-dwarf mm flares were 'not previously well-studied'; Burton 2025 finds 463 in ~50 h. Having this datum changes the conclusion for the 1-4 au belt and its ~0.01 M_E: there is no quiescent excess, and a flare-only reading reproduces the combined ACA flux (computed here: 261-312 uJy against 334 +/- 48). It plausibly changes the 0.4 au component, since MacGregor's coronal reading is conditional. It does not change the 30 au belt, which was marginal before and remains marginal. Evidence the other way: 'no need to posit' is not a demonstrated absence. A fainter belt below the quiescent ACA limit (rms 68 uJy/beam) is not excluded, and nothing read here gives a belt-mass upper limit. The extrapolation itself (H3-H8) is not refuted by any datum read. It re-derives, apart from one unused v1 discrepancy, and its inputs d and L moved by less than 2%. The failure is in the observational premise H1, not in the size-law mathematics. The tree already marks the belt WITHDRAWN (formation.py:458) and does not rest D25 on it, so D25 stays OPEN/UNDETERMINED. The one stale datum the tree carries from this paper is Proxima b's 1.3 M_E, now 1.07 M_E, which does not move its threshold comparison.
1711.00578.grade_evidence: The published conclusion, a 1-4 au belt of ~0.01 M_E including bodies up to 50 km, moves with a datum that has moved. Re-analysis of the same ACA data shows the excess it rests on (H1) is a ~1 min flare with no quiescent excess (MacGregor 2018 sec 3.2, 4.2, READ); Burton 2025 (READ) confirms that such flares are common. The 0.4 au component is contested and the 30 au belt remains marginal. The extrapolation arithmetic re-derives (rederive A-C, E), apart from one v1 discrepancy in the warm-dust mass (2.8e-7 recomputed against 5.5e-7 printed), which the tree does not use. The grade is not WRONG because nothing read shows the belt absent. It is not STANDS because a moved datum moves the conclusion. NARROWED is not the primary grade because the tree uses the result as reported-then-withdrawn (formation.py:286-290, 458) and rests nothing on the 0.01 M_E. It does drop H1, H3, H4, H5 and H7 from its one-line statement (formation.py:283-285) and mis-sites the 0.4 au component, citing 'abstract, 3.3' where the source is sec 3.2 and calls it a 'hint'.
1711.00578.what_would_change_the_grade: To WRONG: a deep quiescent ALMA, far-IR or JWST limit, read at source, below the ~200 uJy assigned to 1-4 au. None was found. To STANDS for the belt: a confirmed steady mm excess at 1-4 au in data with the flares removed, for example the 2019 campaign's 34 h of ACA data or the 2021 12-m data. For the 30 au belt: an independent detection, or identification of the peaks as background sources. Reading the ApJL 850 L6 journal version would settle whether the warm-dust mass discrepancy is in the record. On the tree side, correcting formation.py:284-285's citation and naming H1, H3 and H4 would bring the statement exactly to source. Updating PROXIMA_B_MSINI_EARTH to 1.07 would change no verdict.

2604.01047#spectral-j.published_statement: (4.5), p.41: K_0[phi] = Box INT_{4m^2}^inf rho(M) G^M_ret(phi) dM, with rho(M) = (1/(16 pi^2)) sqrt(1 - 4m^2/M) (1/M). (3.12)-(3.13), pp.27-28: K_0 = Box INT varrho(M)/M G_ret dM, where varrho is 'the positive-defined spectral density' (1/(16 pi^2)) sqrt(1-4m^2/M) Theta(M-4m^2). So rho = varrho/M. (4.17), p.48 (Prop 4.10): 'the Stieltjes transform of the density rho(M) given in (4.5)', J(z) := INT_{4m^2}^inf rho(M)/(M-z) dM = (1/(8 pi^2)) (1/z - (4m^2 - z) m arccsc(2m/sqrt z) / (m sqrt(4m^2 - z) z^{3/2})), z in D. (4.18): D = {Im z != 0, or Im z = 0 and Re z < 4m^2}. The source does not state J(0). Lemma 4.13's proof uses the positivity of rho verbatim. The source does not state that J is monotone.
published_hypotheses: H1: a free real Klein-Gordon scalar of mass m > 0 with curvature coupling xi, on Minkowski (R^4, eta).
H2: the Poincare-vacuum (Hadamard) two-point function. rho is the Kallen-Lehmann density of G_+^2, a one-loop free-field quantity.
H3: rho is supported on M >= 4m^2, the two-particle threshold.
H4: J is defined on D, the plane cut along [4m^2, inf). The closed form (4.17) is claimed on all of D.
H5: Lemma 4.13's use of J (not J itself) needs a_1, a_2 in (-inf, 4m^2) strictly, per Prop 4.12.

Added by the tree, verified here: 'J monotone' (linstab.py:639, 752). GMMPS do not state it. It follows from rho >= 0 on M >= 4m^2 and is computed here (check C6).

Added by the tree, verified here, but its guard is not written down: the bracket bound 4J(0)/(4+|g|) <= J(g) <= J(0) (linstab.py:638-639, 652, 752, 770). It holds only for g <= 0 (z3, check C7), and the lower bound fails for g in (0, 4m^2) (the C7 control). The docstrings write M/(M+|g|), which quietly assumes g < 0. Every call site satisfies the guard (linstab.py:805, 810, 973, 976, 983), and no call passes alpha < 0.
Implicit in the tree, satisfied: m > 0 is not named at linstab.py:155-164 or 578-586, but the tree works in m = 1 units. J(0) ~ 1/m^2 diverges as m -> 0, so the massless case is outside this result.
H2 (free field, vacuum state, one loop) is not restated at the owner's lines. The tree uses J only inside GMMPS's own (5.3)/(5.4), so this is not a drift in use.

2604.01047#spectral-j.lacked_data: No empirical datum enters (4.5) or (4.17). They are a closed-form one-loop free-field density in m and its Stieltjes transform, so the authors could not have lacked data in the measurement sense, and the result is exact for every m > 0. Evidence for: the printed closed form matches the defining integral on the whole cut plane to 1e-34 or better; the source's two separately printed forms, (4.17) and Prop 4.5's L(K), agree; and the normalisation matches the independent 2002 AMM computation. Evidence against: none found. What the result cannot carry is model content, not data. It is a free-field, vacuum-state, one-loop quantity with m > 0 (H1, H2). An interacting or holographic field, or the massless limit (J(0) ~ 1/m^2), falls outside it. These are named hypotheses, not missing data, and the tree uses J only inside GMMPS's own setting.

icrp-23-reference-man.lacked_data: In 1975 ICRP 23 lacked in vivo whole-body data for women and for non-Western populations: it carries no Reference Woman elemental data, and in vivo Reference Woman estimates only came in 1990. It also predates the anatomical review that became ICRP 89 (2002) and the ICRP 110 (2009) tissue set. The source itself is not shown wrong. Nothing here contradicts 780 g of P for the defined 1975 male, and its table could not be read. The tree's D25 conclusion does move with the later data: on ICRP 110 bulk the photosphere binder becomes Li (1752) and the CI binder becomes C (9.02). The evidence cuts the other way on scale. The magnitudes move by at most 1.2x (1911 -> 1752; 10.70 -> 9.02), so the order-of-magnitude conclusions survive. Part of the move also comes from a different reference population, which is a choice of hypothesis rather than a correction of ICRP 23. So the older data were incomplete for the class the tree uses ('adult'), and which element binds, though not the scale, depends on which data are taken.

effective-mass-band-curvature.name: Effective mass as band curvature; negative m* quasiparticles carry positive energy (and: 'effective negative mass' in BECs/metamaterials is dispersion curvature, not T_00; negative-index metamaterials concern the refractive index)

source.located: The definition m* = hbar^2/(d^2E/dk^2) is textbook solid-state physics (semiclassical band model: Ashcroft & Mermin 1976 ch.12; Kittel), with no arXiv copy: NAMED-NOT-READ. The two papers the tree cites for the phenomenon are arXiv:2204.04041, 'Negative-mass exciton polaritons induced by dissipative light-matter coupling in an atomically thin semiconductor', Wurdack, Yun, Katzer, Truscott, Knorr, Selig, Ostrovskaya, Estrecho (Nature Communications 2023, s41467-023-36618-6), and arXiv:1801.04779, 'Negative-mass effects in spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates'. Web-search result titles and snippets corroborate both identities (id -> title -> subject). Neither body was read.
source.via: Every read route was refused this session. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries x2, get_paper_content x2 and discover_papers x1 all returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded', including one retry after other work. curl to export.arxiv.org, ar5iv, semanticscholar, core and europepmc gave 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. WebFetch of arxiv.org, nature.com and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov gave EGRESS_BLOCKED. WebSearch (titles and snippets) was the only route left, and it is used only to confirm that the cited ids are the papers the tree says they are. Everything graded here rests on the re-derivation, which was computed here, not on a reading.

effective-mass-band-curvature.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE (see source.via). What the re-derivation shows from the definition alone, and what is therefore graded: (i) m* = hbar^2 (d^2E/dk^2)^-1 is a property of the dispersion E(k). Semiclassically dv/dt = F/m*, so m* < 0 inverts the acceleration response to a force, and on an inverted band the group velocity points against k. (ii) Nothing in (i) fixes the sign of the energy or of T_00. Search snippets for 2204.04041 (secondary, not a reading): 'dissipative coupling between ... excitons and photons in an optical microcavity can lead to the formation of exciton polaritons with an inverted dispersion of the lower polariton branch and hence a negative mass'; 'the propagation direction of the negative-mass polaritons is opposite to their momentum'; the samples are monolayer WS2 in planar microcavities. Snippet for 1801.04779: negative effective masses are realised 'by engineering the dispersion relation', with two effective-mass parameters (propagation and diffusion).
published_hypotheses: SEMICLASSICAL BAND MODEL (textbook, NAMED-NOT-READ): a quasiparticle wavepacket in a medium with a single-band dispersion E(k), narrow in k, under a slowly varying force. m* is then defined locally in k: a tensor in general, a scalar for an isotropic band.

2204.04041 (from snippets only): DISSIPATIVE (non-Hermitian) exciton-photon coupling in a microcavity containing a monolayer of WS2 produces the inversion. The negative mass is a property of the real part of a complex eigen-dispersion.
1801.04779 (from snippets only): negative mass by dispersion engineering in a spin-orbit-coupled BEC, with TWO effective-mass parameters (propagation and diffusion) that need not share a sign.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (all three owners; candidates.py:52): 'A quasiparticle with m* < 0 still carries POSITIVE energy' needs a REFERENCE: energy measured from a stable ground state (the band minimum), or the absolute energy including rest energy. Computed here (rederive C3, negative control): once the zero of E is moved, E < 0 occurs with m* < 0 AND with m* > 0, so the curvature fixes neither sign. Measured from a band minimum, the excitation energy is >= 0 at every k whatever the sign of m* (C2, z3 UNSAT). The tree never names the reference. For the polariton the absolute energy is ~2 eV > 0, so the claim holds there. In a population-inverted medium the 'relative to the ground state' reading is not available.

DROPPED (achievable.py:57, achievable.py:439, ledger.py:1543): 'it does not gravitate'. This is true of m* as a QUANTITY, since m* does not enter the gravitating source (C6). It is false of the QUASIPARTICLE, whose energy E gravitates as E/c^2 whatever the sign of m* (C6: 3.57e-36 kg for a 2 eV polariton). candidates.py:56-58 keeps the right qualifier, 'the gravitational source is the full stress-energy of the cavity, the excitons and the field, and that is positive'. achievable.py and ledger.py S1 drop it.

ASSERTED, NOT COMPUTED (candidates.py:56-58, carried into candidates.py:447 'no EC is violated' and candidates.py:490-491): the positivity of the total stress-energy of cavity + excitons + field is asserted, not computed. effective_mass_violates_an_energy_condition() returns the constant False, and the selftest (candidates.py:533-534) checks that constant against a literal False. It is a declared boolean, not a computation. The conclusion is correct on the hypothesis that the medium and field are ordinary matter and radiation satisfying the classical WEC, and the tree should name that hypothesis rather than assert the result.

WEAKENED (achievable.py:58-59, 441): 'negative-index metamaterials ... are about the refractive index, not the energy density'. This is correct, but the positive energy density it implies needs the dispersive (Brillouin) energy density, u ~ d(w eps)/dw |E|^2 + d(w mu)/dw |H|^2, in a low-loss, quasi-monochromatic band. The naive eps|E|^2 + mu|H|^2 IS negative where eps, mu < 0. Computed here (C5): u is positive throughout the eps<0, mu<0 band of a Drude-Lorentz medium, and the Landau-Lifshitz passive-medium inequality (NAMED-NOT-READ) forces d(w eps)/dw >= 1 (z3 UNSAT). The tree does not state the low-loss, dispersive-formula hypothesis.
UNVERIFIED WORD (candidates.py:40, 536): 'switchable'. It does not appear in the snippets seen for 2204.04041, and the paper body was not read. Recorded as unverified, not as wrong.

NOT A DRIFT, RECORDED: candidates.py:44-45 and index3.py:1172 cite arXiv:1801.04779 for negative-mass effects in SOC BECs. The id resolves (search result title) to 'Negative-mass effects in spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates', so the citation is correct as to identity. Per snippet, that paper separates TWO effective-mass parameters where the tree uses one scalar m*. This is a simplification of scope with no effect on the KIND verdict.

effective-mass-band-curvature.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The effective-mass definition is a kinematic identity of the semiclassical band model: a definition, not a measurement. No datum the original authors lacked could move it, and C1-C3 re-derive it from E(k) alone. The data that came LATER are the realisations (negative-mass polaritons, 2022/2023; negative mass in SOC BECs, 2017-2018) and the analysis of the gravitational mass of sound waves (2018-2019). Evidence either way: the later realisations CONFIRM the tree's reading. They are dispersion engineering (search snippets: 'inverted dispersion', 'engineering the dispersion relation'), and C4 shows an inverted branch with Re E ~ 2 eV > 0. The sound-wave work is the one later datum that bears on a phrase the tree uses. It indicates that quasiparticles DO couple to gravity, with a sign unrelated to m*. That contradicts 'does not gravitate' taken of the quasiparticle, is itself contested (1903.04770), and on no reading supplies T_00 < 0. Later data therefore do not move the KIND conclusion, though they do narrow the wording. None of this comes from reading the paper bodies: the assessment rests on snippets plus computation and is marked as such.
effective-mass-band-curvature.grade_evidence: The load-bearing claim is re-derived and machine-checked here (rederive C1-C3 and C5; z3 UNSAT twice, vacuity guard SAT): m* is band curvature, not T_00, so a negative m* supplies no negative energy density and fails KIND (candidates.py:447, 486-491; ledger.py S1; achievable.py NOT_EXCEPTIONS). The KIND verdict is untouched. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree states the claim more broadly than what holds, on three computed counts. (1) 'm* < 0 still carries POSITIVE energy' (candidates.py:52) holds only relative to a stable ground state, or as absolute energy including rest energy. C3's negative control shows the curvature fixes no sign, and the tree never names the reference. (2) 'It does not gravitate' (achievable.py:57, 439; ledger.py:1543) is true of m* as a quantity and false of the quasiparticle, whose energy gravitates as E/c^2 (C6). candidates.py:56-58 keeps the qualifier; the other two owners drop it. (3) 'Negative-index metamaterials ... not the energy density' holds under the dispersive (Brillouin) energy density in a low-loss band (C5), a hypothesis the tree does not state. Also recorded: effective_mass_violates_an_energy_condition() is a hard-coded False checked against itself (candidates.py:490-491, 533-534). It is declared, not computed, and it is correct on the hypothesis that the medium and field satisfy the classical WEC. The grade is not WRONG: nothing computed here or seen in any snippet is a counterexample to the KIND refusal. 2102.06824.published_statement:
Abstract (p.1): 'We present the first general model for subluminal positive-energy, spherically symmetric warp drives; construct superluminal warp-drive solutions which satisfy quantum inequalities; provide optimizations for the Alcubierre metric that decrease the negative energy requirements by two orders of magnitude ... any warp drive, including the Alcubierre drive, is a shell of regular or exotic material moving inertially with a certain velocity. Therefore, any warp drive requires propulsion. We show that a class of subluminal, spherically symmetric warp drive spacetimes, at least in principle, can be constructed based on the physical principles known to humanity today.'

Sec 3.1 (pp.9-10): eq 6 is w(r) = (1-(r/Lambda)')/(8 pi r^2). 'for purely positive energy spacetimes, Lambda(r) > 1 in the outside region D_out ... Schwarzschild'. 'any non-trivial truncated spherically symmetric warp drive must contain regions where the energy density is negative'. 'for a subluminal warp drive based on non-exotic matter, the time inside the drive can only pass more slowly than it does for a remote Minkowski observer comoving with the drive. For scale, an Earth-mass shell of 10 meter radius will slow down the rate of time by a small fraction of 4e-4.'

Sec 5.2 (p.18): 'the only type of modification to the internal spacetime that is achievable with purely positive energy for spherically symmetric warp drives is slowing down the rate of time inside the craft'. The general axisymmetric positive-energy case is left among the 'important open questions'.

Sec 5.3 (pp.18-19): 'flattening the shape by a factor of 10 would lead to proportionally smaller energy requirements'. The optimal shape f = min(r0/r_s, 1) 'reduces the energy requirement for a similarly sized Alcubierre drive by about a factor of three' (App. A.3, eq A.7: E = -(v_s^2/12) Int_{r0}^inf r_s^2 f'^2 dr_s).

Sec 5.4 (p.19): 'it is possible to construct non-trivial warp drive solutions with purely positive energy ... our work suggests a method of constructing such objects based on fully understood laws of physics.'
published_hypotheses: H1 General warp drive (sec 2.1, p.4): an asymptotically flat vacuum region D_out encloses a compact curved region D_warp of spherical topology, which encloses a flat passenger region D_in. The spacetime is stationary, with a global Killing field xi aligned with the 4-velocity of the inner boundary.

H2 Positive-energy class (sec 3.1, p.9): spherical symmetry, meaning an SO(3) whose orbits are orthogonal to xi. B-M state this is possible 'only for class I and IV spacetimes, i.e., subluminal warp drives'.

cosmic-string-deficit-angle-8pigmu.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE this pass, so nothing is quoted. Re-derived here with sympy (10/10 PASS): (i) Exact, nonlinear case. Take a static, straight string core with T^t_t = T^z_z, which is boost invariance along the axis (Psi' = 0 in the tree's metric), and define mu = INT u dA = 2 pi INT_0^R u W dr. The exterior is a flat cone with deficit angle exactly 8 pi G mu, for either sign of mu. Checked on the uniform cores W = r0 sin(r/r0) with u = +1/(8 pi r0^2), and W = r0 sinh(r/r0) with u = -1/(8 pi r0^2). The cone closes at G mu = 1/4. (ii) Linearised case with general stress (energy per length mu, tension tau): deficit = 4 pi G (mu + tau). This equals 8 pi G mu only when tau = mu.
published_hypotheses: NOT READ AT SOURCE. These are the hypotheses under which the formula was re-derived here.
H1: the string is static, straight and infinite (cylindrical symmetry, translation invariance along z).
H2: tension equals energy per unit length, T^z_z = T^t_t (boost invariance along the string). 'Deficit = 8 pi G mu' needs this. Without it the linear deficit is 4 pi G (mu + tau).

H3: mu is the proper integral INT u dA over a smooth core, and the thin limit is taken of smooth sources. A conical singularity is not itself a distributional source (Geroch-Traschen 1987, NAMED-NOT-READ).
H4: the exterior is vacuum. The formula is exact beyond linear order for boost-invariant cores (re-derived B+/B-). The general-stress formula is weak-field only (re-derived D).

contracted-bianchi-identity.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 p.81: 'R_{rho sigma mu nu} = -R_{sigma rho mu nu} allows us to write this result as nabla_[lambda R_rho sigma] mu nu = 0 . (3.88) This is known as the Bianchi identity. (Notice that for a general connection there would be additional terms involving the torsion tensor.) ... An especially useful form of the Bianchi identity comes from contracting twice on (3.87): 0 = g^{nu sigma} g^{mu lambda}(nabla_lambda R_{rho sigma mu nu} + nabla_rho R_{sigma lambda mu nu} + nabla_sigma R_{lambda rho mu nu}) = nabla^mu R_{rho mu} - nabla_rho R + nabla^nu R_{rho nu} , (3.93) or nabla^mu R_{rho mu} = (1/2) nabla_rho R . (3.94) (Notice that, unlike the partial derivative, it makes sense to raise an index on the covariant derivative, due to metric compatibility.) If we define the Einstein tensor as G_{mu nu} = R_{mu nu} - (1/2) R g_{mu nu} , (3.95) then we see that the twice-contracted Bianchi identity (3.94) is equivalent to nabla^mu G_{mu nu} = 0 . (3.96)'. p.117: '... simply take the metric of your choice, compute the Einstein tensor G_{mu nu} for this metric, and then demand that T_{mu nu} be equal to G_{mu nu}. (It will automatically be conserved, by the Bianchi identity.)' p.118: T_{mu nu} = -Lambda g_{mu nu} 'is automatically conserved by metric compatibility'.
published_hypotheses: The connection is Christoffel (Levi-Civita), meaning torsion-free AND metric-compatible. Torsion: 'for a general connection there would be additional terms involving the torsion tensor' (p.81). Metric compatibility: needed to raise the index through nabla in the contraction (p.81, note after 3.94).

The identity is DIFFERENTIAL. (3.88) is the second Bianchi identity, which is closely related to the Jacobi identity for [[nabla,nabla],nabla] (3.89). It does not follow from the algebraic symmetries alone.
The metric is smooth enough for nabla R to exist classically: third derivatives of g enter nabla G, so C^3 is sufficient. The source leaves this implicit.
No field equation is assumed for (3.96) itself. The conservation consequence needs G = 8 pi G T, optionally with -Lambda g, which metric compatibility conserves on its own.
What comes out is LOCAL covariant conservation nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 (4.23), not an integral energy law in general. Carroll p.37 notes that gravitational energy has no sensible local tensor.
Holds in any dimension: the contraction does not use n = 4.

schwarzschild-radius-collapse-criterion.published_statement: Schwarzschild 1916 interior (physics/9912033): inside a homogeneous incompressible sphere, eq.(35) ds^2 = ((3 cos chi_a - cos chi)/2)^2 dt^2 - (3/kappa rho0)[dchi^2 + sin^2 chi dOmega^2], with rho0 + p = rho0 2 cos chi_a/(3 cos chi_a - cos chi) (eq.30). The 'radius measured outside' is P_o = sqrt(3/kappa rho0) sin chi_a, and eq.(40) gives alpha/P_o = sin^2 chi_a, alpha = (kappa rho0/3) P_o^3. 'At the center of the sphere velocity of light and pressure become infinite when cos chi_a = 1/3 ... Hence there is a limit to the concentration, above which a sphere of incompressible fluid can not exist.' 'a sphere of given gravitational mass alpha/2k^2 can not have a radius measured from outside smaller than: P_o = alpha. For a sphere of incompressible fluid the limit will be 9/8 alpha. (For the Sun alpha is equal to 3 km, for a mass of 1 gram is equal to 1.5 . 10^-28 cm.)' Hayward (gr-qc/9408002), with E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)): 'Proposition 1: trapping. A metric sphere is trapped if and only if E > r/2, marginal if and only if E = r/2, and untrapped if and only if E < r/2. Proof. By definition.' The gloss adds that 'the ratio E/r controls the formation of black and white holes, and trapped spheres generally'. The textbook form the tree uses: a uniform ball of areal radius l has M = u (4/3) pi l^3/c^2 and is (marginally) trapped iff 2GM/c^2 >= l.
published_hypotheses: classical GR, Einstein's field equations with no cosmological constant (1916: kappa = 8 pi k^2)
spherical symmetry (1916 Sec.3; Hayward: 'assumed implicitly in the Propositions')
1916 interior: STATIC equilibrium, isotropic perfect fluid of CONSTANT density rho0 ('incompressible'), regular centre with finite positive central pressure, p = 0 and C^1 matching at the surface
the radius in the criterion is the AREAL radius ('radius measured from outside'), not the proper radius
the mass in the criterion is the gravitational (Schwarzschild / Misner-Sharp) mass alpha/2k^2, not the 'substantial mass' over proper volume (eq.41, 43: the two differ)

schwarzschild-radius-collapse-criterion.lacked_data: In 1916 Schwarzschild had the field equations and the Newtonian limit. Everything that came later is theory: horizons (Lemaitre 1933, Finkelstein 1958), trapped surfaces (Penrose 1965), quasi-local mass (Misner-Sharp 1964), a collapse solution (Oppenheimer-Snyder 1939). The later black-hole observations (LIGO 2015, EHT 2019) are NAMED-NOT-READ and test the exterior geometry, not this criterion. The later work changed the wording, not the number. The criterion is the dimensionless 2Gm/(c^2 R) >= 1, and no measured datum enters the tree's ratio 2 pi^2/3 (sympy R1c: no free symbols). Later work sharpens it two ways, both computed here: (i) it is a TRAPPING criterion, a trapped sphere can be past-trapped (a white hole, R5), and black-hole formation needs Penrose plus censorship; this narrows 'is a black hole' to 'is trapped, hence not static' (R4), which is all the verdict needs; (ii) the stricter static bound 8/9 was already in the 1916 paper and raises the tree's ratio to 3 pi^2/4 (R6d). Evidence either way: no datum the author lacked moves the conclusion. What moves it are the tree's own defining choices (ball radius = Sturm length, T_kk = u), R6.
schwarzschild-radius-collapse-criterion.grade_evidence: The external result stands as published and is re-derived. Schwarzschild's 1916 uniform ball has gravitational mass exactly (4 pi/3) rho0 R^3 in the areal radius (R2c). A sphere is trapped iff 2Gm/(c^2 R) > 1 (Hayward Prop.1, READ; identity checked R4c). The tree's ratio 2 pi^2/3 is exact and matches spec.seat_over_collapse at four scales (R1, R7), and no datum moves it. It is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class, and with a stronger conclusion, than it holds on: (1) the 'black hole IFF' at specthm.py:612-613 is false both ways, shown by computation (R5), though not load-bearing; (2) spec.py:46-47 and specthm.py:1837 say 'black hole' where the result gives 'trapped'; what is proved without extra hypotheses is 'not static' (R4, z3), and that suffices for SR2; (3) l must be the areal radius and M the Misner-Sharp mass, which spec.py:39-41 does not state; (4) spec.py:39 ('ANY') and :47 ('always') exceed H_ball: an l/2 ball with T_kk = 2u gives 0.8225, not trapped (R6b, flat-chord approximation); (5) the criterion is spherical only, since off symmetry it is the unproven hoop conjecture (Dain), which the tree already routes to S-3. None of this refutes SR2 on its stated ball-of-radius-l hypothesis: every material row there is trapped (min 3.29), and the 9/8 bound makes it stricter (7.40). Caveat: live alphaXiv was unavailable (quota), so the sources were READ from cached alphaXiv extractions.
schwarzschild-radius-collapse-criterion.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates H_collapse as a one-directional trapping criterion on the areal radius ('trapped, hence not static'), and restricts spec.py:39/47 'ANY'/'always' to H_ball, or computes the l/2-ball and T_kk/u cases and shows them trapped. To WRONG: a regular, spherically symmetric, static configuration with 2Gm/(c^2 R) >= 1 in areal R (R4 shows this is impossible), or an error in the ratio arithmetic (R1/R7 reproduce it exactly). Reading Penrose 1965 and a censorship result at source would upgrade 'trapped => black hole' from NAMED to READ without moving the grade. 0708.2450-thm4.2.published_statement: FO p.10, verbatim: 'Theorem 4.2. Let omega_2^0 be the two-point function of a reference Hadamard state for the non-minimally coupled scalar field with coupling constant xi in [0, 1/4], defined on a globally hyperbolic spacetime with smooth metric. Furthermore, let gamma be a time-like geodesic parametrised in proper time tau and let f in D(R, R). On the set of Hadamard states, we then find (rho_quant o gamma)(f^2) >= -Q_xi(f), (44) where Q_xi(f) = Qt_A^xi(f) 1 + xi (:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_B[f]) + xi (:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_C^xi[f]), (45) with Qt_A^xi(f) = int_0^oo dalpha/pi [ phi*(rho1^ omega_2^0)(f_alpha, f_alpha) + 2 xi alpha^2 phi* omega_2^0 (f_alpha, f_alpha) ], (46) and Q_B(f) and Q_C^xi(f) are functions in D(R, R) given by Q_B[f](tau) = 2 (d_tau f(tau))^2, (47) Q_C^xi[f](tau) = f(tau)^2 ( R_mn gamma^m gamma^n - (1/2)(1 - 4 xi) R )(tau). (48) Furthermore Qt_A^xi(f) and Q_B[f] are non-negative. This result follows from the previous discussion by discarding manifestly positive terms. We remark that Qt_A^xi(f) depends on the reference state and that for xi = 0, we recover results known for minimal coupling [5]. Moreover, Q_C^xi(f) vanishes if the region of interest is Ricci-flat.' rho_quant is normal ordered: <G_quant>_Psi = [sum D_i :omega_2^Psi:]_c, :omega_2^Psi: = omega_2^Psi - omega_2^0 (eq. 6).

Evidence FOR the theorem as published: 22/22 checks here, covering (7)=(8), (9)=(10)-(14), the exact-derivative smearing step producing (47)-(48), the z3 range proof, an independent MTW derivation of (48) on a curved metric, and the Minkowski reduction to Fewster-Eveson. FO's successors supply none of these. M's hypothesis is therefore not supported for this result: it is incomplete in named ways (range, geodesic, difference type), not inaccurate.

weak-field-isotropic-metric-and-newtonia.published_statement: Will 2014 (arXiv:1403.7377) p.28: 'in this limit, the spacetime metric g predicted by nearly every metric theory of gravity has the same structure. It can be written as an expansion about the Minkowski metric (eta_mu nu = diag(-1,1,1,1)) in terms of dimensionless gravitational potentials ... in imitation of the Newtonian gravitational potential U(x,t) = int rho(x',t)|x-x'|^-1 d^3x' (30).' p.29: 'The "order of smallness" is determined according to the rules U ~ v^2 ~ Pi ~ p/rho ~ eps ... (we use units in which G = c = 1) ... A consistent post-Newtonian limit requires determination of g_00 correct through O(eps^2), g_0i through O(eps^3/2), and g_ij through O(eps).' Box 2 p.31: 'g_00 = -1 + 2U - 2 beta U^2 - 2 xi Phi_W + ... + O(eps^3), ... g_ij = (1 + 2 gamma U) delta_ij + O(eps^2).' Table 2 p.29: gamma 'How much space-curvature produced by unit rest mass?' value in GR 1; beta 'How much nonlinearity in the superposition law for gravity?' value in GR 1. p.43: round-trip delay 'delta t = 2(1 + gamma) M_sun ln(...) (62)'; Cassini 2003 'gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3) x 10^-5'. TREE'S USE (phase1.py:70-81): 'For a static metric in isotropic form, g_tt = -e^{2Phi}, g_ij = e^{-2Phi} delta_ij, a payload at rest at A has four-velocity u = e^{-Phi} d/dt ... d(A,B) = int e^{-Phi} dl THE TRANSITION QUANTITY ... t(A,B) = int e^{-2Phi} dl THE PROPULSION QUANTITY. ONE Phi, TWO EXPONENTS, RATIO EXACTLY 2 (unified.py measured 1.9940 to 2.0229 over both signs of Phi).' SI conversion (phase1.py:364-366): 'Delta d = (G/c^2) M Lambda' as G_SI * M_kg / C_SI**2 * lam(b, a, Rs).
published_hypotheses: W1 (Will p.26) metric theory: symmetric metric, test bodies on geodesics, special-relativistic non-gravitational physics in local Lorentz frames (EEP)
W2 (Will p.28) slow-motion, weak-field limit: expansion about Minkowski in potentials of graded smallness

hypothesis_drift: SIGN CONVENTION (implicit, not an error): with g_tt = -e^{2Phi} the Newtonian identification is Phi = -U = -GM/(c^2 r) (C3a/b). The canonical entry's name writes 'Phi = G M/(c^2 r)'. phase1 is internally consistent because its M is the MAGNITUDE of a NEGATIVE core mass: phi_device = +m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/max(r,R_s) with m > 0 (phase1.py:261-263), 'everything above needs M < 0' (phase1.py:204), and contraction_law takes a positive M_kg (phase1.py:364-366). The negative-mass hypothesis is therefore carried by prose at phase1.py:204 and specthm.py:641 ('m < 0 locally'), not by the sign of contraction_law's argument. Recorded as a labelling discrepancy in the canonical name, not a refutation.

SINGLE-Phi EXPONENTIAL FORM (ADDED as an ansatz, which the canonical hypotheses already say): Will's W4 fixes g_ij only through O(eps). The tree's e^{-2Phi} fixes the O(Phi^2) term of g_ij at coefficient 2; exact Schwarzschild in isotropic coordinates (Ricci-flat, C3e) has 3/2 (C3d), while g_00 agrees through O(U^2) (beta = 1, C3c). For non-constant Phi the ansatz's Einstein tensor has G_ij purely quadratic in grad Phi and G_tt = e^{4Phi}(2 lap Phi - |grad Phi|^2) (C4b-d): it is an exact GR vacuum solution for no non-constant Phi, and it demands stresses of O(Phi^2). Inside W3 (p/rho = O(eps)) this is consistent; it is a definition of the tree's device metric, not a claim about GR's strong field (phase1.py:67-69).

'RATIO EXACTLY 2' (WORDING, already bounded by the canonical hypothesis): exact for the EXPONENTS by construction; for the SAVINGS the exact identity (1-e^{-2Phi}) = (1-e^{-Phi})(1+e^{-Phi}) makes the ratio 1 + e^{-Phi} = 2 - Phi + Phi^2/2 - ..., equal to 2 only at Phi = 0 (C2a-c). The owner prints both 'EXACTLY 2' and the measured 1.9940-2.0229 side by side (phase1.py:79-80), and the selftest carries rtol 5e-3 at m = 2e-2 (phase1.py:461); the measured values correspond to effective Phi = 6.0e-3 and -2.26e-2 (C2d/e). Consistent, first order. In PPN terms the ratio is (1+gamma)/gamma, so it also carries the hypothesis gamma = 1 (W6), which phase1 does not state.

WEAK FIELD DROPPED AT THE PRICE FIGURES (the one narrowing): contraction_law is the first-order (weak-field) law Delta d = m Lambda. phase1.py:180-181 and its selftest phase1.py:508-510, and index3.py:673, apply it to contract a 4 ly corridor by 1 % (2.57e10 M_sun) and by 50 % (1.28e12 M_sun). Lambda as used is the FULL-CROSSING integral (C6), so the endpoints lie outside the shell, R_s <= L/2; then the peak potential on the ray is Phi_max ~ m/b >= (Delta d/L) e^2/2 for ANY choice of R_s/b (C8a), and = 40.06 (Delta d/L) at the tree's R_s/b = 200. At 50 %: Phi_max >= 1.85 for any geometry, 19.93 at the tree's -- not weak field; the exact ansatz contraction int(1-e^{-Phi}) at the m the linear law demands is 80.6 b against the 200 b required (ratio 0.403, C8c). At 1 %: Phi_max = 0.399 at the tree's geometry, exact ansatz contraction 0.944 of the linear law (C8d) -- the weak-field law is ~6 % optimistic there, beyond the 1e-3 selftest tolerance printed on the figure. What GR (rather than the ansatz) gives at Phi ~ 20 is not computed here and is OPEN.

gamma = 1 FOR A NEGATIVE-MASS SOURCE (hypothesis carried, not stated): Will's data (W7) are all positive-mass solar-system sources. In GR the linearised field equations are linear in T, so gamma = 1 is predicted for either sign; but no measurement of gamma exists for a negative-mass source, since none is known. phase1 needs M < 0 (phase1.py:204).

raychaudhuri-jacobi-null-focusing.published_statement:
Kontou-Sanders (2020), eq.(17), verbatim: 'For a null congruence with tangent field k^a, parametrized by affine parameter lambda, the expansion theta = nabla_a k^a satisfies dtheta/dlambda = -R_ab k^a k^b - sigma_ab sigma^ab + omega_ab omega^ab - theta^2/(n-2)', where 'n is the spacetime dimension, sigma_ab is the shear tensor and omega the vorticity'. They add: 'Unless otherwise noted, we will consider irrotational congruences, meaning that the rotation tensor vanishes'; the equation 'is derived from the trace of the geodesic deviation equation'; 'For theories that obey Einstein's equation we may rewrite these energy conditions by eliminating the stress tensor in favour of the Ricci curvature tensor'.

Wall (2010), eq.(7): '-dtheta/dlambda = (1/2) theta^2 + sigma_ab sigma^ab + 8 pi G T_ab k^a k^b'. Footnote 14: 'the classical background Raychaudhuri Eq. (7) can take over ... to show the existence of the conjugate point'. Abstract: the positivity theorems 'fail once the linearized graviton field is quantized, because then the renormalized shear squared term in the Raychaudhuri equation can be negative'.

Gao-Wald (2000), eqs.(11)-(13), re-quoted: d^2A/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta; G = sqrt(det A); 'the Raychaudhuri equation yields G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]'. Conjugate points are the zeros of G.

The tree's u'' = -q u, q = 4 pi T_kk, u(0) = 0 is this equation with sigma = omega = 0, n = 4 and R_kk = 8 pi T_kk (G = c = 1).
published_hypotheses: H1 Null geodesic congruence, affinely parametrised (Kontou-Sanders eq.17; Gao-Wald eq.11).
H2 Irrotational (omega_ab = 0). Otherwise +omega^2 enters with a DEFOCUSING sign (eq.17). This is automatic for the congruence from a point (A|p = 0): measured twist |B01 - B10| <= 3.2e-12 (S4).
H3 Spacetime dimension n. The coefficient is 1/(n-2), so the tree's 1/2, and hence its 4 pi, hold at n = 4 only (S1, S2: q = 8 pi T_kk/(n-2)).
H4 Einstein's equation (classical GR), used to replace R_kk by 8 pi G T_kk / c^4. Lambda and the trace term drop because g_kk = 0 (S2, exact in n = 4, 5, 6).
H5 sigma_ab sigma^ab >= 0. This is true classically, as a sum of squares of a real spatial tensor. Wall 0910.5751: the RENORMALISED shear-squared can be negative once gravitons are quantised.

H6 Shear is sourced by the Weyl tensor through the Jacobi (Sachs) equation. Setting sigma = 0 is EXACT only where the Weyl (traceless tidal) part vanishes along the ray (S3a). Otherwise G = sqrt(det A) obeys G'' = -(1/2)(sigma^2 + R_kk)G <= -(R_kk/2)G, which is a comparison inequality, not the scalar equation (S3b, S4).
H7 Point initial data u(0) = 0, u'(0) = 1, i.e. conjugate points to a point. A surface-orthogonal congruence has focal-point data u(0) = 1, u'(0) = theta_0/2 instead.

raychaudhuri-jacobi-null-focusing.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis, tested for this result.

The reduction is a geometric identity (the trace of the Jacobi equation, re-derived exactly in S1 and S4) plus Einstein's equation contracted on a null vector (S2). Its only empirical inputs are the GR coupling and G, and neither has moved: CODATA 2022 = 2018, and no deviation from GR was found in what this docket read.

Raychaudhuri 1955 lacked the null form with shear, but Sachs 1961 already carried sigma^2, so nothing in the classical identity was waiting on data. What came later and matters is theoretical, not a datum: quantised gravitons make the renormalised shear-squared sign-indefinite (Wall 2010). That narrows H5 only in a regime the tree does not use.

Evidence against M's hypothesis here: the outside result is exact, and every moved or re-checked datum leaves the tree's conclusions where they were.

Where there is inaccuracy, it is in the TREE's leftover wording, not in the outside physics. Three printed sentences (seatindex.py:70, :315, :400-401) state the Ricci-only exclusion without the shear hypothesis that the same file names at :47-50, and the tree's own composite.py measures the counterexample. No external result is shown wrong.
raychaudhuri-jacobi-null-focusing.grade_evidence:
The external result STANDS as published:
- The null Raychaudhuri equation reduces to u'' = -(R_kk + sigma^2 - omega^2)/(n-2) u, re-derived symbolically (S1).
- R_kk = 8 pi T_kk is exact including Lambda and the trace term (S2).
- Gao-Wald eq.(13) is verified numerically with O(h^2) convergence (S4).
- The tree's q = 4 pi T_kk, u(0) = 0, turn = next zero is exact under omega = 0 (automatic for point data), n = 4, GR, and a zero Weyl part along the ray (S3a).
- No datum moves anything: G, c and the GR coupling are unchanged, and replacing the 1e35 Pa nuclear-density reference with saturation (2.41e34 Pa) leaves 'below nuclear beyond ~100 km' intact.

The TREE's use is NARROWED, and this is shown, not presumed. The shear hypothesis that the canonical entry lists and seatindex.py:47-50 names is dropped at seatindex.py:70, :315 and :400-401. Those sites still print 'never seats' / 'nothing seats whatever the shape' below Lyapunov, yet the full Jacobi equation seats there: S3c gives a vacuum conjugate point at pi/sqrt(w) = 5.236 with Lyapunov number 0, and S3b finds 49 of 200 such profiles. Every verdict that rests on the Sturm (sufficiency) direction survives shear: in S3b the full zero comes later in 0 of 141 cases.

Minor discrepancies, recorded:
- n = 4, Einstein's equation, twist-free and k^0 = 1 normalisation are used without being named.
- T_COEFF is printed as 9.5054e43 but computes to 9.5053e43 (7.9e-6 relative, a last-digit discrepancy).
- seatindex.py:14 cites transit.py for a reduction that now lives in achronal.py:44-50 and turnseat.py:26-30.

Not WRONG: no published statement is contradicted. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no moved datum moves the conclusion. Not STANDS: a hypothesis of the result is dropped at printed verdict sites.

gr-qc/9506083.published_statement: PV eq (17): 'adot^2 = -V(a); V(a) = 1 - 2M/a - [2 pi sigma(a) a]^2. This single dynamical equation completely determines the motion of the wormhole throat.' Eq (15): sigma_dot = -2(sigma+p) adot/a. Eq (23): beta^2 = dp/dsigma, 'a useful parameter related to the equation of state'. Eq (27): V''(a0) = -2 a0^-2 [2M/a0 + (M^2/a0^2)/(1-2M/a0) + (1+2beta0^2)(1-3M/a0)]. Eq (28)-(29): 'at this order of approximation ... for V''(a0) > 0 the wormhole is stable, while for V''(a0) < 0 perturbations can grow (at least until the nonlinear regime is reached). Thus the wormhole is stable if and only if' (29) holds. Stable regions (35)-(36): I, beta0^2 >= 3/2+sqrt3 with a0- < a0 < a0+; II, beta0^2 <= -1/2 with a0 > a0-. Unstable for all a0 when -1/2 < beta0^2 < 3/2+sqrt3. Sec IV: 'there is no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound'.
published_hypotheses: H1: two copies of Schwarzschild with the SAME mass M, glued at r = a > 2M. This is a symmetric thin-shell wormhole, so sigma0 < 0 (exotic matter).
H2: an infinitesimally thin shell, with the Lanczos/Sen/Israel junction (eqs 3-8) and G = c = 1.
H3: only spherically symmetric (radial) perturbations, a -> a(tau).
H4: vacuum on both sides, so the conservation law (13)/(15) is exact.
H5: a barotropic EOS p = p(sigma). Only its slope beta0^2 at the static point enters V''(a0).
H6: an ASSUMED static solution related by (18)-(19), with V(a0) = V'(a0) = 0.
H7: the analysis is linear ('at this order of approximation'). V'' = 0 is not classified, and nonlinear behaviour is not addressed.
H8: beta is a parameter, not asserted to be a sound speed. There is no microphysical model of the matter.
hypothesis_drift: CONFIGURATION / ATTRIBUTION (a discrepancy, not a refutation). PV treat only the symmetric wormhole (H1). The tree cites PV for two formulas that are not in PV: the two-mass V = 1 - 2M_out/R - [dM/m_s - m_s/2R]^2 (stability.py:40-42), and V = 1 - [m_s/2R + m/m_s]^2 for Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside (wall.py:222-225, 327-330). The two-mass form is Ishak-Lake eq (5) with the MEAN mass (credited there to Lake 1979). The Minkowski/Schwarzschild shell is the configuration of Brady-Louko-Poisson 1991 (PV's ref [6]) and LeMaitre-Poisson 2019. Both formulas are re-derived here from the Israel junction and hold exactly. What the tree takes from PV is the method.

Nothing since 1995 moves that mathematics: Ishak-Lake 2002 generalise it, Eiroa et al. 2024 use it unchanged, and PSP 2026 reproduce the equivalent radial criterion exactly. pinamonti-siemssen-flrw-existence.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE. What follows is from web-search summaries of the abstracts, not quotations from the papers. [1309.6303] Flat cosmological spacetimes with a massive, conformally coupled scalar field. Initial conditions at finite time give a state with finite stress-tensor expectation values. The paper proves existence and uniqueness of local solutions, for the metric and the matter field together. Local solutions extend until the scale factor becomes singular or the Hubble function reaches a critical value H_c = 180 pi/G. [1001.0864] Local (and, per one summary, global) existence for a massive conformally coupled scalar on flat FLRW, solving for the state and the Hubble function together in an integral-functional equation. [2007.14665] Existence and uniqueness on flat FLRW for a massive scalar with arbitrary coupling xi. The problem is recast as a fixed point on a Banach space, giving short-time existence and uniqueness by the Banach fixed point theorem. [1809.03812] Existence in cosmological spacetimes without the conformal-coupling restriction and with the full renormalisation freedom, treated as an infinite-dimensional dynamical system.

The estimates of d and u masses are not without controversy ... there are even suggestions that the u quark could be essentially massless. ... We have normalized the MSbar masses at a renormalization scale of mu = 2 GeV. Results quoted in the literature at mu = 1 GeV have been rescaled by dividing by 1.35.' counter-rotating-shell-kinetic-model.name: Counter-rotating (Einstein-Vlasov) shell: sigma = n mu gamma, p = n mu gamma v^2/2, angular-momentum conservation u = gamma v ~ 1/R

source.located: The tree names no source, and says so: 'marked RECONSTRUCTED because no member or paper states it in this form' (wall.py:77-78; docstrings wall.py:399-410). The ingredients are classical and NAMED-NOT-READ: the Einstein cluster (Einstein, Ann. Math. 40, 922 (1939); every particle on a circular orbit, p_r = 0) and thin shells of counter-rotating collisionless particles (pre-arXiv literature, not identified by title here). The Lanczos/Israel junction the model rests on is audited separately (israel-lanczos-poisson-visser-thin-shell, STANDS). Read at source text: (i) N. Dadhich, arXiv:2504.00064v2 p.7, restating the Einstein-Vlasov numerics of Ames, Andreasson & Logg (arXiv:1603.05404, 1803.11224; NAMED-NOT-READ): 'as the limiting compactness M/R -> 4/9 is approached, the shell becomes infinitely thin ... in the limit, p_r/rho -> 0 and 2p_t/rho -> 1 ... particle velocity attains the value, v^2 = 8/9. All these are, however, numerical results.' (ii) Pitre, Schneider & Poisson, arXiv:2604.05980v1, cached text line 459: their shell 'is taken to be a perfect fluid', so it is not kinetic. Their sec. X restates LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 (NAMED-NOT-READ): 'radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2'. (iii) The sibling audit einstein-vlasov-limit-2-3 (rederive B1-B6): the Lanczos shell is exactly the thin limit of an Einstein cluster.
source.via: No paper stating the kinetic shell model could be read in this stage. alphaXiv discover_papers and answer_pdf_queries both returned 'assistant quota exceeded'. arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, www.alphaxiv.org and inspirehep.net are all refused by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403). Only two files mention counter-rotating or Vlasov thin shells: 2504.00064v2.txt (Dadhich) and 2606.22531v3.txt (Le, line 1643). 2604.05980v1.txt (md5 9916ebc75c7859da12c37c59acc4458f) is about a perfect fluid. The result is a closed-form computation, so I re-derived it in full from first principles instead: sympy plus an independent equation-of-motion test. The grade rests on that re-derivation.
