counter-rotating-shell-kinetic-model.published_statement: No published statement was read. The tree states the model at wall.py:79-86: 'sigma = n mu gamma and p = n mu gamma v^2/2, so p/sigma = v^2/2 -- and the junction ALREADY fixes p_0/sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4s), so v^2 = (1-s)/(2s) is set by x alone. Under a radial perturbation each particle conserves its angular momentum, so u = gamma v ~ 1/R ... beta^2_vlasov(x) = u^2 (3u^2 + 4) / ( 2 (1 + u^2)(3u^2 + 2) ). It has a ceiling of 1/2 as u -> infinity, and the model itself expires at v = 1, which is x = 8/9.' Its conclusion, wall.py:97-100: 'SO THE STRUCTURAL FIX IS REAL BUT CONDITIONAL: counter-rotating matter clears the threshold only for x < 0.46898, and the margin is widest at LOW compactness, tending to exactly 4/3 as x -> 0.' The closest external statement read is Dadhich 2504.00064v2 p.7, restating Ames-Andreasson-Logg: Einstein-Vlasov configurations approach 2M/R -> 8/9 as infinitely thin shells with p_r/rho -> 0 and 2p_t/rho -> 1. That is exactly the tree's model at its expiry: for a single-speed 2D gas 2p/sigma = v^2, which reaches 1 at x = 8/9.
published_hypotheses: (tree, wall.py:79-83) A thin (distributional) shell with Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside. The static equilibrium is fixed by the Lanczos junction p_0/sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4s), with s = sqrt(1-x) and x = 2M/R.

(tree, wall.py:79-81) Collisionless particles move tangentially, with directions isotropic on the 2-sphere and one common speed v (sigma = n mu gamma has a single gamma). This is the monoenergetic-|L| hypothesis.
(tree, wall.py:81-82) Under a radial (spherically symmetric) perturbation each particle conserves its angular momentum: u = gamma v = L/R.
(tree, wall.py:83, 434-436) The model is valid only while v < 1, i.e. x < 8/9.

(tree, wall.py:97-100, 414-427) Stability is judged by the radial criterion beta^2_vlasov > beta^2_crit(x). The criterion is audited separately; here it was also tested without using beta^2_crit (K5).
(read, Dadhich p.7, restating AAL) Static, spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov. The thin-shell limit is a numerical result.

(read, PSP sec. X, restating LeMaitre-Poisson 2019) A barotropic shell is radially stable in the Newtonian limit iff Gamma >= 3/2. This is a statement about a fluid. The kinetic shell obeys it because its equation of state is barotropic along the L-conserving sequence (K4).
hypothesis_drift: The single-speed hypothesis is unstated, and the conclusion is widened to the whole class. wall.py:98-99 says 'counter-rotating matter clears the threshold only for x < 0.46898'. That number holds only when every particle shares one speed (wall.py:79 'sigma = n mu gamma'; the canonical entry lists only 'isotropic tangential directions'). Computed in K7a: the thin limit of an Einstein cluster has the same Lanczos statics (checked at x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 to 2e-6), and every particle in it sits on its own circular geodesic. Its speeds spread over v^2 in [0, x/(2(1-x))]. With each particle conserving its own L, its crossover is x = 0.447387, not 0.468977, and its margin at x = 0.3 is 1.133151, not 1.144558. Two-speed mixtures with the same statics give 0.445357 and 0.430510 (K7b). Mixtures with most rest mass at rest fall below 0.1 (K7c), but those are not realizable as particles that each hold their own orbit. What the stated class drops: the monoenergetic-|L| hypothesis.

The '4/3 exactly as x -> 0' limit (wall.py:88, 98-99, 430-431, 606-611) is 2/(3/2): the Newtonian Gamma = 2 of a 2D gas against the Gamma = 3/2 threshold (PSP sec. X, restating LeMaitre-Poisson). It needs non-relativistic particle speeds, and a single speed guarantees that (v^2 ~ x/4). For any fixed speed distribution the limit still holds (K7a; K7c at x = 1e-6). How fast the margin approaches it depends on the distribution: with rest fraction 0.999 the margin is 1.259 at x = 1e-3 and 0.939 at x = 1/6.

Radial perturbations only. The model's beta^2 is defined by a spherically symmetric perturbation (wall.py:81). wall.py:119-128 imports the l >= 2 instability of Pitre-Schneider-Poisson and calls their configuration 'LE'S STATIC ANCHOR EXACTLY'. But PSP's shell is a perfect fluid (2604.05980v1, cached line 459). Nothing read here establishes that the l >= 2 instability carries over to a collisionless counter-rotating shell. That fluid-to-kinetic transfer at wall.py:124-125 is added without being stated. It sits next to this key rather than inside it.

A labelling discrepancy, cross-referenced to audit einstein-vlasov-limit-2-3. wall.py:29 and wall.py:245 call x = 2/3 the 'Einstein-Vlasov limit'. The file's own 'counter-rotating (Einstein-Vlasov) shell' (wall.py:77) expires at 8/9 (wall.py:83). K2 confirms 8/9 for the single-speed model. The sibling audit showed 2/3 is where the outermost particle of the thin-limit cluster reaches v = 1. This is a label, not an arithmetic error.

Provenance. 'no member or paper states it in this form' (wall.py:77-78) could not be tested, because no literature search was possible here. The Einstein-Vlasov thin-shell endpoint the model expires at is published (Dadhich p.7, restating AAL).

counter-rotating-shell-kinetic-model.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. The model uses no measured datum. Every quantity is a closed-form function of the compactness x, and every one was re-derived exactly (K1-K6). That includes the equation-of-motion test that never uses beta^2_crit and reproduces the crossover to 1e-9. So there is no missing measurement that could move this result, which is evidence against M's hypothesis for this entry. What the model does leave out is a microstate input: how the particles' speeds are distributed. The tree gives every particle one speed. The natural alternative with the same statics is the thin limit of an Einstein cluster, where each particle sits on its own circular geodesic. It gives a crossover of 0.447387 instead of 0.468977 (4.6% lower) and a margin of 1.133 instead of 1.145 at x = 0.3. That input moves the number but none of the conclusions the tree draws from it. x = 0.3 stays stable, x = 2/3 and x = 4/5 stay unstable, and the x -> 0 limit stays 4/3. designpoint.py:160-161 checks that 1/6 is below the crossover, and that still holds (1/6 < 0.447).
